**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 9, verses 1–2 (part 1 of 3)**

**On the interpretation of His saying, ﴿A declaration of freedom from the Allah and His Messenger, to those among the polytheists with whom you made a covenant (1). So travel freely in the land for four months, and know that you cannot escape Allah, and that Allah will humiliate the disbelievers (2).﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His majesty be exalted, ﴿A declaration of freedom from Allah and His Messenger﴾, he means: this is a declaration of freedom from Allah and His Messenger.

"Bara'ah" (براءة, declaration of freedom) is in the nominative, governed by an omitted element, which is "hadhihi" (هذه, "this"), as in His saying, ﴿A surah which We have sent down﴾ [Surah al-Nur: 1], where "surah" is in the nominative governed by an omitted "hadhihi." If someone said that "bara'ah" is in the nominative governed by the pronoun referring back to it in His saying ﴿to those with whom you made a covenant﴾, treating it as definite, which raises what follows it, since it has become definite through its complement, which is His saying ﴿from Allah and His Messenger﴾, and the meaning of the statement becomes: the freedom from Allah and His Messenger to those among the polytheists with whom you made a covenant [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "براءة" instead of "البراءة", and the context requires what I have confirmed, God willing.]] — this would be an acceptable view whose soundness is not refuted. However, the first opinion is more pleasing to me, because it is the habit of the Arabs to omit, for whatever is visibly present, whether indefinite or definite, that demonstrative: "this" and "this" (fem.). So when they see a good thing they say, "Good, by Allah!" and when they see a bad thing they say, "Bad, by Allah!", meaning: this is good, by Allah, and this is bad, by Allah. That is why I chose the first opinion.

And He said: ﴿A declaration of freedom from Allah and His Messenger to those with whom you made a covenant﴾, and the meaning is: to those among the polytheists with whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made a covenant, because covenants between the Muslims and the polytheists were the covenant of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Only the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), or someone who concluded it on his command, would undertake to conclude them. But He addressed the believers with that because they knew its meaning, and that the covenants of the Prophet (ﷺ) with his community were their covenants, since they were content with all his actions concerning them, and submitted to his covenants on their behalf. So his covenant over them became like their covenants over themselves. That is why He said: ﴿to those among the polytheists with whom you made a covenant﴾, because of the covenant and pact of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

* * *

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have differed concerning those to whom Allah and His Messenger declared freedom from the covenant that existed between him and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) among the polytheists, and he permitted them to travel in the land for four months.

Some of them said: They are two categories of polytheists. One of them: the term of their covenant between him and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was less than four months, and they were given four months of travel. The other of them: the term of his covenant was without a fixed limit, so it was cut short to four months so that he could take counsel for himself; after that he would be at war with Allah, His Messenger and the believers, and he would be killed wherever he is found, and taken captive, unless he repents.

Mention of those who said that:

16356. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, as commander over the pilgrimage in the year nine, to conduct the pilgrimage of the people, while the people of polytheism were in their own places regarding their pilgrimage. Abu Bakr set out with the Muslims who were with him, and the "Surah of Bara'ah" was revealed to annul what existed between the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the polytheists of the covenant that they had been upon between him and them: that no one who came to the House should be prevented, and that no one should be feared in the sacred month. That was a general covenant between him and the people of polytheism. Between that there were covenants between the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and tribes of the Arabs, "special" (khasa'is) until a named term, [[ "khasa'is" means that they were specific to them, not to others.]] So it was revealed concerning him and those among the hypocrites who stayed behind from him at Tabuk, and concerning the statement of those among them who said such things. Allah exposed in it the secrets of people who used to conceal other than what they displayed: some of them were named to us, and some were not named to us. So He said: ﴿A declaration of freedom from Allah and His Messenger to those with whom you made a covenant among the polytheists﴾, that is, to the people of the general covenant from among the polytheists of the Arabs = ﴿So travel freely in the land for four months﴾, up to His saying: ﴿that Allah is free from the polytheists, and His Messenger﴾, that is, after this proof. [[The report: 16356 — Sirah Ibn Hisham 4: 188.]]

* * *

Others said: Rather, Allah, may He be exalted, gave respite of four months of travel to those among the polytheists who had a covenant between them and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). As for whoever did not have a covenant from the Messenger of Allah, his term was fifty nights, which is twenty days of Dhu al-Hijjah and all of Muharram. They said: This was so because the term of those who had no covenant extended to the passing of the sacred months, as Allah said: ﴿So when the sacred months have passed, kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 5], the verse. They said: The proclamation of "Bara'ah" was on the day of the greater pilgrimage, and that is the day of sacrifice according to one group, and according to others it is the day of Arafat, and that is fifty days. They said: As for the postponement of the four months, it was only for the people of the covenant between them and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), from the day "Bara'ah" was revealed. They said: It was revealed at the beginning of Shawwal, so the end of their term was the passing of the sacred months. Some who held this view said: The beginning of the postponement was one for both groups — I mean the one who had a covenant and the one who had no covenant — except that the term of the one who had a covenant was four months, and the term of the one who had no covenant was the passing of the sacred months, which is the end of Muharram.

Mention of those who said that:

16357. Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿A declaration of freedom from Allah and His Messenger to those among the polytheists with whom you made a covenant. So travel freely in the land for four months﴾, he said: Allah set the term for those who made a covenant with His Messenger at four months, during which they may travel wherever they wish. And He set the term for the one who had no covenant as the passing of the sacred months, from the day of sacrifice to the passing of Muharram, which is fifty nights. When the sacred months have passed, He commanded him to lay down the sword against those who had made a covenant.

16358. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When ﴿A declaration of freedom from Allah﴾ was revealed, up to ﴿and that Allah will humiliate the disbelievers﴾, it means: a declaration of freedom from the polytheists who had a covenant on the day "Bara'ah" was revealed. He made the term of those who had a covenant before "Bara'ah" was revealed four months, and commanded them to travel in the land for four months. And He made the term of the polytheists who had no covenant before "Bara'ah" was revealed the passing of the sacred months, and the passing of the sacred months was from the day it was proclaimed as "Bara'ah" until the passing of Muharram, and that is fifty nights: twenty of Dhu al-Hijjah and thirty of Muharram = ﴿So when the sacred months have passed﴾ up to His saying: ﴿and sit in ambush for them at every place of ambush﴾, meaning: no polytheist has any covenant or protection from the time "Bara'ah" was revealed and the sacred months passed. The term of the polytheists who had a covenant before "Bara'ah" was revealed was four months from the day it was proclaimed as "Bara'ah," until the tenth of the beginning of Rabi' al-Akhir, and that is four months.

16359. Narrated to me on the authority of al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His saying: ﴿A declaration of freedom from Allah and His Messenger to those with whom you made a covenant among the polytheists﴾: Before "Bara'ah" was revealed, he made a covenant with some polytheists from Mecca and others, then "Bara'ah" was revealed: a declaration of freedom from Allah to everyone among the polytheists who had made a covenant with you. Indeed I annul the covenant that is between you and them, and I give them a term of four months during which they may travel freely in the land wherever they wish. The term of those who had no covenant between them and the Prophet (ﷺ) was the passing of the sacred months, from the day it was proclaimed as "Bara'ah." It was proclaimed on the day of sacrifice, so it was twenty of Dhu al-Hijjah and Muharram thirty, making fifty nights. So Allah commanded His Prophet that when Muharram passed, he should lay the sword against those who had no covenant between them and the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), killing them until they enter Islam. And He commanded that whoever had a covenant, when four months had passed from the day of sacrifice, he should also lay the sword against them, killing them until they enter Islam. Thus the term of those with no covenant between them and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was fifty nights from the day of sacrifice, and the term of those who had a covenant between them and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was four months, from the day of sacrifice until the tenth of the remaining days of the month of Rabi' al-Akhir.

16360. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿A declaration of freedom from Allah and His Messenger﴾, up to His saying: ﴿and give the good news to those who disbelieve of a painful punishment﴾, he said: It was mentioned to us that Ali proclaimed the call, and Abu Bakr was appointed over the pilgrimage, may Allah's mercy be upon both of them. That was the year in which the Muslims and the polytheists performed the pilgrimage, and the polytheists did not perform the pilgrimage after that year. His saying: ﴿those among the polytheists with whom you made a covenant﴾, up to His saying: ﴿until their term﴾, he said: They are the polytheists of Quraysh, with whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made a covenant at the time of al-Hudaybiyah, and four months of their term remained after the day of sacrifice. Allah commanded His Prophet to fulfil their covenant until their term, and for those with no covenant, the passing of Muharram, and he cast to every person with a covenant his covenant back, and commanded fighting them until they bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and nothing from them would be accepted but that.

* * *

Others said: The beginning of the postponement for the polytheists of four months, and its end for all of them, was one time. They said: Its beginning was the day of the greater pilgrimage, and its end was the end of the tenth of the remaining days of Rabi' al-Akhir.

Mention of those who said that:

16361. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿A declaration of freedom from Allah and His Messenger to those among the polytheists with whom you made a covenant﴾, he said: When this verse was revealed, he was freed from the covenant of every polytheist, and no one was made a covenant after it except those who had already made one, and he gave to each their term = ﴿So travel freely in the land for four months﴾, for whoever's covenant entered it, from the tenth of Dhu al-Hijjah, Muharram, Safar, the month of Rabi' al-Awwal, and the tenth of Rabi' al-Akhir.

16362. Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, saying: Abu Ma'shar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi and others narrated to us, saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Abu Bakr as commander over the season in the year nine, and he sent Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with both of them, with thirty or forty verses of "Bara'ah," and he recited them to the people, giving the polytheists a term of four months to travel freely in the land. He recited "Bara'ah" to them on the day of Arafat, giving the polytheists a term of twenty of Dhu al-Hijjah, Muharram, Safar, the month of Rabi' al-Awwal, and ten of Rabi' al-Akhir. He recited it to them in their dwellings, and said: No polytheist shall perform the pilgrimage after this year of ours, and no one shall circumambulate the House naked.

16363. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿So travel freely in the land for four months﴾: twenty of Dhu al-Hijjah, Muharram, Safar, Rabi' al-Awwal, and ten of Rabi' al-Akhir. That was their covenant that existed between them.

16364. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿A declaration of freedom from Allah and His Messenger﴾, to the people of the covenant: Khuza'ah, and Mudlij, and whoever among them or others had a covenant. [[In the manuscript: "ومن كان له أو غيرهم", and in the printed edition: "ومن كان له عهد من غيرهم"; I have corrected it as you see.]] The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned from Tabuk when he had finished, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intended the pilgrimage, then said: Polytheists come and circumambulate naked, so I do not like to perform the pilgrimage until that no longer happens. So he sent Abu Bakr and Ali, may Allah's mercy be upon both of them, and they went among the people at Dhu al-Majaz, and at their marketplaces where they used to trade, and at all the seasons, and they announced to the companions of the covenant that they should be safe for four months, which are the consecutive months: twenty from the end of Dhu al-Hijjah until ten remaining days of Rabi' al-Akhir, after which they have no covenant. And he announced to all the people the declaration of war unless they believed.

16365. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid concerning His saying: ﴿A declaration of freedom from Allah and His Messenger to those with whom you made a covenant among the polytheists﴾, he said: The people of the covenant are Mudlij, and the Arabs with whom he made a covenant, and whoever had a covenant. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came back from Tabuk when he had finished with it, and intended the pilgrimage, then said: Polytheists come to the House and circumambulate naked, so I do not like to perform the pilgrimage until that no longer happens. So he sent Abu Bakr and Ali, may Allah's mercy be upon both of them, and they went among the people at Dhu al-Majaz, and at their marketplaces where they used to trade, and at the whole season, and they announced to the companions of the covenant that they should be safe for four months, which are the sacred months that have passed, consecutive: twenty from the end of Dhu al-Hijjah until ten remaining days of Rabi' al-Akhir, after which they have no covenant. And he announced to all the people the declaration of war unless they believed. So all the people believed at that time, and no one traveled freely. And he said: When he returned from al-Ta'if, he went straight away from that, and then he went out to Tabuk, after he had come to Medina.

* * *

Others said, from among those who said: "The beginning of the term for all the polytheists and its end was one": Its beginning was the day "Bara'ah" was revealed, and the end was the passing of the sacred months, which is the end of Muharram.

Mention of those who said that:

16366. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri: ﴿So travel freely in the land for four months﴾, he said: It was revealed in Shawwal, so these four months are: Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, and Muharram.

* * *

Others said: The postponement of the four months given by Allah to the polytheists for travel was only for the one who had a covenant between him and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of a term less than four months. As for the one who had a covenant with a term more than four months, he commanded (ﷺ) that his covenant be completed for its term.

Mention of those who said that:

16367. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, who said: Al-Kalbi said: The four months were only for the one who had a covenant between him and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) less than four months, so four months were completed for him. As for the one who had a covenant of more than four months, he is the one whose covenant he commanded to be completed, and He said: ﴿So complete their covenant for them until their term﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 4].

* * *

Abu Ja'far, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The most correct of these opinions is the statement of the one who said: The term which Allah granted to the people of the covenant among the polytheists, and in which He permitted them to travel by His saying: ﴿So travel freely in the land for four months﴾, is only for the people of the covenant who backed up (zahara) against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and broke their covenant before the end of its term. As for those who did not break their covenant and did not back up against him, Allah, may His majesty be exalted, commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to complete the covenant between him and them until its term, by His saying: ﴿except those among the polytheists with whom you made a covenant, who have not failed you in anything nor backed anyone against you; so complete for them their covenant until their term. Indeed Allah loves the righteous﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 4].

If someone supposes that the saying of Allah, may His mention be exalted: ﴿So when the sacred months have passed, kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 5] indicates something contrary to what we have said about that, since it would imply that the obligation on the believers was to kill every polytheist after the passing of the sacred months [[In the printed edition: "ينبئ عن أن..." and Abu Ja'far has repeatedly used "على" with "ينبئ"; I have kept it as in the manuscript, which is permissible since it includes the meaning of "يدل" (indicates).]], then the matter is contrary to what he supposed. That is because the verse that follows it demonstrates the soundness of what we have said [[In the printed edition: "تنبئ عن صحة"; I have kept what is in the manuscript.]], and the error of what the one who supposed that the passing of the sacred months would permit killing every polytheist, whether or not he had a covenant from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), held. That is His saying: ﴿How can there be for the polytheists a covenant with Allah and with His Messenger, except those with whom you made a covenant at the Sacred Mosque? So as long as they remain upright toward you, remain upright toward them. Indeed Allah loves the righteous﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 7]. These are polytheists, and Allah commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers to remain upright toward them in their covenant, so long as they remain upright toward them by not breaking their treaty and not backing their enemy against them.

Then after that, Abu Ja'far said: The widely transmitted reports from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) show that when he sent Ali, may God have mercy on him, with the declaration (Bara'ah) to the people with whom he had covenants, he commanded him, among what he commanded, to proclaim among them: "Whoever has a covenant between himself and the Messenger of God (ﷺ), his covenant extends to its term." This is the clearest evidence for the soundness of what we have said. God did not command His Prophet (ﷺ) to breach the covenant of a people with whom he had made a covenant for a fixed term, when they remained faithful to their covenant by not breaking it. He only set a deadline of four months for those who had breached their covenant before the deadline was announced, or for those whose covenant had no fixed term. As for the one whose covenant had a defined term and who had not made breaking it his own choice, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was commanded to fulfill his covenant until its term ended. With this he sent his herald to proclaim among the people of the pilgrimage season from among the Arabs.

16368. Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, he said: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Qays narrated to us, from Mughirah, from al-Sha'bi, who said: Muharrir ibn Abi Hurayra narrated to me, from Abu Hurayra, who said: I was with Ali, may God have mercy on him, when the Prophet (ﷺ) sent him to proclaim. Whenever his voice grew hoarse, I would proclaim in his place. [Editor's note: "Sahila sawtuhu" means his voice became hoarse, which is the same as al-bahh. It has another, similar meaning in the hadith of Umm Ma'bad describing the Messenger of God, may my father and mother be ransomed for him (ﷺ), where she said: "And in his voice there is sahal" (with two fathas), which is like hoarseness in the voice, so it is not sharp and high-pitched.] I asked: What were you proclaiming? He said: Four things: No naked person shall circumambulate the Ka'bah; whoever has a covenant with the Messenger of God (ﷺ), his covenant extends to its term; no one shall enter Paradise except a believing soul; and no polytheist shall perform the Hajj after this year of ours. [Editor's note: The report 16368 was transmitted by Abu Ja'far through three chains, and its takhrij will come later. "Qays" is Qays ibn al-Rabi' al-Asadi, whom Ahmad and others regarded as weak in transmission, and his previous mentions were numerous, the last being no. 12802. "Mughirah" is Mughirah ibn Miqsam al-Dabbi, trustworthy, from whom the whole group narrated; he was mentioned many times before, the last being no. 11340. "Muharrir ibn Abi Hurayra" is a trustworthy Successor (tabi'i) who transmitted few hadiths, mentioned previously in no. 2863. This report is weak in its chain because of the weakness of Qays ibn al-Rabi'.]

16369. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Affan narrated to us, he said: Qays ibn al-Rabi' narrated to us, he said: al-Shaybani narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi, who said: Muharrir ibn Abi Hurayra informed us, from his father, who said: I was with Ali, may God be pleased with him, and he mentioned something similar, except that he said: "And whoever has a covenant between himself and the Messenger of God (ﷺ), his covenant extends to its term." [Editor's note: This is the second chain of the hadith of Muharrir ibn Abi Hurayra. "Affan" is Affan ibn Muslim ibn Abd Allah al-Saffar, whom the whole group narrated from; he narrated from Qays ibn al-Rabi', and there is some criticism of him. His biography was given at no. 5392. "Al-Shaybani" is Abu Ishaq al-Shaybani, Sulayman ibn Abi Sulayman, the Imam, mentioned many times, the last being no. 12489. The defect of this chain is the weakness of Qays ibn al-Rabi'. However, al-Hakim transmitted it in al-Mustadrak 2:331 through the route of Shu'bah, from Sulayman al-Shaybani, and said: "This hadith has a sound chain but they did not include it," and al-Dhahabi agreed. See the following note.]

Abu Ja'far said: Shu'bah also transmitted this hadith and differed from Qays regarding the term.

16370. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, both saying: Uthman ibn Umar narrated to us, he said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Mughirah, from al-Sha'bi, from Muharrir ibn Abi Hurayra, from his father, who said: I was with Ali when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent him with the declaration to the people of Makkah, and I kept proclaiming until my voice became hoarse. I asked him: What were you proclaiming? He said: We were commanded to proclaim: No one shall enter Paradise except a believer; and whoever has a covenant between himself and the Messenger of God (ﷺ), its term is four months. When the term expires, God is free of the polytheists and His Messenger; no naked person shall circumambulate the House; and no polytheist shall perform the Hajj after this year. [Editor's note: This is the third chain. "Uthman ibn Umar ibn Fares al-Abdi" is trustworthy, and the whole group narrated from him; he was mentioned many times, including no. 5458 and others. This report, through Shu'bah from Mughirah, was transmitted by Ahmad in his Musnad, no. 7964, and by al-Nasa'i in his Sunan 5:234. Al-Hakim transmitted it in al-Mustadrak 2:331 through another route, from al-Nadr ibn Shumayl, from Shu'bah, from Sulayman al-Shaybani, and said: "This hadith has a sound chain, but they did not include it," and al-Dhahabi agreed; see the previous note. Ibn Kathir discussed it fully in his Tafsir 4:111, and in al-Tarikh 5:38, and he said in al-Tarikh: "This chain is good, but there is an odd element in the statement of the narrator that whoever had a covenant was given a term of four months. Some have held this view, but the correct position is that whoever had a covenant is given a term up to its end, however long it may be, even if it exceeds four months. For one who had no term at all, the deferral is four months. There remains a third category: one whose term ends in less than four months from the day of the deferral. This may be attached to the first category, so his term extends to its end, however short. It may also be said that he is given a deferral of four months, because he has a better claim than one who had no covenant at all." See the explanation of the report in Musnad Ahmad.]

Abu Ja'far said: I fear that this report contains an error by its transmitter regarding the term, because the reports are widely transmitted contrary to it, besides Qays's disagreement with Shu'bah on this very hadith, as I have explained.

16371. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith al-A'war, from Ali, may God have mercy on him, who said: I was commanded with four things: that no polytheist shall come near the House after this year; that no man shall circumambulate the House naked; that no one shall enter Paradise except every Muslim soul; and that every person with a covenant be fulfilled in his covenant. [Editor's note: "Al-Harith al-A'war" is al-Harith ibn Abd Allah al-Hamdani, very weak; he was mentioned many times before, see no. 174. Therefore its chain is weak. It will come with another chain, no. 16374.]

16372. Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, he said: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Israil narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Zayd ibn Yuthay', who said: Surah Bara'ah was revealed, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent it with Abu Bakr, then he sent Ali and took it from him. When Abu Bakr returned he said: Has anything been revealed about me? He said: No, but I was commanded to deliver it myself or a man from my family. So he (Ali) set out for Makkah, [Editor's note: "He set out" refers to Ali, may God have mercy on him,] and he stood among them and proclaimed four things: that no polytheist shall enter Makkah after this year; that no naked person shall circumambulate the Ka'bah; that no one shall enter Paradise except a Muslim soul; and whoever has a covenant between himself and the Messenger of God, his covenant extends to its term. [Editor's note: The two reports 16372 and 16373 are the hadith of Zayd ibn Yuthay', which he will transmit through three routes: this one, the one following it, and then no. 16379. "Zayd ibn Yuthay'", or "Uthay'" with diminutive form in both, is a trustworthy Successor who transmitted few hadiths; mentioned before in no. 15737. This report was transmitted by Ahmad in his Musnad no. 594, through the route of Sufyan from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, and its chain is sound. al-Tirmidhi transmitted it in the Book of Hajj, in the chapter on what has come concerning the disapproval of circumambulating naked, and said: "There is also a report from Abu Hurayrah on this subject." Abu Isa said: "The hadith of Ali is good." By the hadith of Abu Hurayrah he means what preceded at nos. 16368–16370. He also transmitted it in the Book of Tafsir and said: "This is a good, sound hadith." Ahmad also transmitted in the Musnad of Abu Bakr no. 4 a similar, longer hadith from Zayd ibn Yuthay', from Abu Bakr.]

16373. Ibn Wakic narrated to us, he said: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Zakariyya, from Abu Ishaq, from Zayd ibn Yuthay', from Ali, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) sent me when Surah Bara'ah was revealed, with four things: that no naked person shall circumambulate the House; that no polytheist shall come near the Sacred Mosque after their year this year; whoever has a covenant between himself and the Messenger of God (ﷺ), it extends to its term; and that no one shall enter Paradise except a Muslim soul. [Editor's note: See the note on the previous report.]

16374. Ibn Wakic narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith, from Ali, may God have mercy on him, who said: I was sent to the people of Makkah with four things, and then he mentioned the hadith. [Editor's note: See the note on report 16371.]

16375. Ibrahim ibn Sa'id al-Jawhari narrated to us, he said: Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Sulayman ibn Qarm narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn Abbas: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent Abu Bakr with Surah Bara'ah, then he followed him with Ali and took it from him. Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, has something been revealed about me? He said: "No. You are my companion in the cave and at the Pool; no one shall deliver on my behalf except me or Ali!" What he sent Ali with was four things: no one shall enter Paradise except a Muslim soul; no polytheist shall perform the Hajj after this year; no naked person shall circumambulate the House; and whoever has a covenant between himself and the Messenger of God (ﷺ), it extends to its term. [Editor's note: "Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Marwazi" was narrated from by the whole group; he was mentioned many times before, the last being no. 15338. "Sulayman ibn Qarm ibn Mu'adh al-Taymi" is trustworthy, though some accused him of extremism in Shi'ism; see no. 9163. "Al-Hakam" is al-Hakam ibn Utaybah, mentioned many times. This report was transmitted by al-Tirmidhi in the Book of Tafsir, through another route, from Abbad ibn al-Awwam, from Sufyan ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hakam ibn Utaybah, similarly, and he said: "This is a good, strange hadith from this route, from the hadith of Ibn Abbas."]

16376. Ibn Wakic narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Khalid, from Amir, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) sent Ali, may God have mercy on him, and he proclaimed: "Beware, no polytheist shall perform the Hajj after this year; no naked person shall circumambulate the House; no one shall enter Paradise except a Muslim soul; and whoever has a covenant between himself and the Messenger of God (ﷺ), its term extends to its end; and God is free of the polytheists and His Messenger."

16377. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from Hakim ibn Hakim ibn Abbad ibn Hanif, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Husayn ibn Ali, who said: When Surah Bara'ah was revealed upon the Messenger of God (ﷺ), he had sent Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God have mercy on him, to lead the Hajj for the people. It was said to him: O Messenger of God, if only you had sent someone to Abu Bakr! He said: "None shall deliver on my behalf except a man from my family!" Then he called Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God have mercy on him, and said: "Go out with this account from the beginning of Bara'ah, and proclaim to the people on the day of sacrifice when they gather at Mina: no unbeliever shall enter Paradise; no polytheist shall perform the Hajj after this year; no naked person shall circumambulate the House; and whoever has a covenant with the Messenger of God (ﷺ), it extends to its term." Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God have mercy on him, set out on the she-camel of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), al-Adba', and caught up with Abu Bakr al-Siddiq on the road. When Abu Bakr saw him he said: "Are you a commander or one who is commanded?" He said: "One who is commanded." Then they both went on, may God have mercy on them both. Abu Bakr led the people in the Hajj, while the Arabs, at that time and in that year, were in their traditional places of Hajj that they had followed in the Jahiliyyah. When the day of sacrifice came, Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God have mercy on him, stood and proclaimed to the people what the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had commanded him, saying: "O people, no one shall enter Paradise except a Muslim soul; no polytheist shall perform the Hajj after this year; no naked person shall circumambulate the House; and whoever has a covenant with the Messenger of God (ﷺ), it is his until its term." After that year no polytheist performed the Hajj, and no naked person circumambulated the House. Then they both came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ). This was from Bara'ah concerning those among the polytheists who had a general covenant, and those with a term up to the appointed end. [Editor's note: Ibn Hisham, al-Sirah 4:190, 191. "Hakim ibn Hakim ibn Abbad ibn Hanif al-Ansari" is trustworthy, though some spoke about him, to the point that Ibn Sa'd said: "He narrated few hadiths, and they do not use his hadith as proof." His biography was given in no. 11741.]

16378. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: When these verses were revealed up to the end of forty verses, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent them with Abu Bakr and appointed him to lead the Hajj. When he had traveled and reached the tree at Dhu al-Hulayfah, he sent Ali after him and took them from him. Abu Bakr returned to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, may my father and mother be your ransom, has something been revealed about me?" He said: "No, but none may deliver on my behalf except someone other than me, or a man from my own family. Are you not content, O Abu Bakr, that you were with me in the cave, and that you are my companion at the Pool?" He said: "Yes, O Messenger of God!" Abu Bakr continued leading the pilgrims, while Ali proclaimed Bara'ah. He stood on the day of Adha and said: "No polytheist shall come near the Sacred Mosque after this year; no naked person shall circumambulate the House; whoever has a covenant between himself and the Messenger of God (ﷺ), his covenant extends to its term; and these are days of eating and drinking; and God will not admit anyone into Paradise except one who is a Muslim." They said: "We disavow your covenant and the covenant of your cousin, except for stabbing and striking!" The polytheists returned, blaming one another and saying: "What are you doing, when Quraysh has embraced Islam?" So they embraced Islam.

16379. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Zayd ibn Yuthay', from Ali, who said: I was commanded with four things: that no polytheist come near the House after this year; that no naked person circumambulate the House; that no one enter Paradise except a Muslim soul; and that every person with a covenant be fulfilled in his covenant. Ma'mar said: Qatadah also said it. [Editor's note: See the note on reports 16372 and 16373.]

Abu Ja'far said: These reports and their like confirm what we have said, and that the period of four months was only for those we have described. As for the one whose covenant had a known term, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and the believers have no right to breach it or to support their enemies against them. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) fulfilled his covenant until its term, by God's command to him. The apparent meaning of the revelation supports this, and the reports from the Messenger (ﷺ) are widely transmitted to that effect.

As for the four months, they were the deadline for those we mentioned. Their beginning was the day of the Greater Hajj, and their end was the completion of ten days of Rabi' al-Akhir. Thus they were four consecutive months, granted to the people of the covenants whose situation we described, during which they could travel through the land, going wherever they wished, with no Muslim confronting them with war, killing, or plunder.

Someone might say: If the matter is as you described, what is the meaning of His words: ﴿So when the sacred months have passed, kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ (Surah al-Tawbah: 5)? You know that their passing refers to the passing of the sacred month of Muharram, and you claim that the deferral granted by God and His Messenger to those people was four months, but between the day of the Greater Hajj and the end of the sacred months there are about fifty days. Where are the fifty days in relation to the four months?

It is said: the expiry of the sacred months was only the term for those polytheists who had no covenant with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), while the four months were for those who had a covenant, either for an unspecified term, or for a specified term which they had violated. By their violation, they became like those whose treachery is feared, and so it was due that the covenant be cast back to them on equal terms, except that they were given the four months to prepare for themselves and to seek refuge. Do you not see that Allah says to the people of the four months, describing them as people of covenant: ﴿A declaration of immunity from Allah and His Messenger to those among the polytheists with whom you made a covenant. So travel freely in the land for four months, and know that you cannot escape Allah﴾; and He describes those for whom the expiry of the sacred months was the term as people of polytheism, not people of covenant, saying: ﴿And a proclamation from Allah and His Messenger to the people on the day of the greatest pilgrimage that Allah is free of obligation to the polytheists, and so is His Messenger﴾, to the end of the verse, = ﴿except those among the polytheists with whom you made a covenant﴾, to the end of the verse? Then He said: ﴿When the sacred months have passed, kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾. So He commanded the killing of the polytheists who had no covenant after the expiry of the sacred months, and the fulfilment of the covenant of those who had a covenant, provided they had not broken their covenant by aiding against the believers and inflicting harm upon them through it.

If someone says: What is the evidence that the beginning of the term was the day of the greatest pilgrimage, and not that it began in Shawwal, as those who hold that view claim?

It is said to him: Those who hold that view claim that the term began from the time of the revelation of "Bara'ah" (Surat al-Tawbah), and that cannot be correct, because the one granted the period of travel has a term up to a specified time. If he does not know what has been granted to him, especially when there is a covenant he had before that which contradicts it, then he is like one who was not granted that, for when he does not know what is his in the term granted to him and what is upon him after it ends, he is in the same state as before the term was granted. It is well known that the people did not learn of what had been granted to them except when it was proclaimed to them at the season of pilgrimage. And when that is so, it is established that its beginning was as we have said, and its ending was as we have described.

As for His saying: ﴿So travel freely in the land for four months﴾, it means: travel in it, coming and going, secure and without fear from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his followers.

* *

It is said of it: "So-and-so travelled (sāḥa) in the land, travels (yasīḥu), a journey (siyāḥah), and [its verbal nouns] sayūḥan and sayaḥānan."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And know that you cannot escape Allah﴾, it says to the people of covenant, those who had a covenant with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) before the revelation of this verse: Know, O polytheists, that if you travel in the land, and choose that while you remain in disbelief in Allah, without acknowledging His oneness and affirming His Messenger = ﴿you cannot escape Allah﴾, meaning: you cannot frustrate Him by yourselves, for wherever you go and wherever you are on earth, you are within His grasp and authority; no minister will protect you from Him, and no fortress or refuge will stand between you and Him if He wills to punish you. [[See the explanation of "al-I'jaz" previously: 12:128 / 13:31.]] Except by faith in Him and His Messenger, and repentance from disobeying Him. That is, hasten to forestall His punishment by repentance, and leave off the travelling which will not benefit you.

As for His saying: ﴿And that Allah will disgrace the disbelievers﴾, it means: know that Allah humiliates the disbelievers, and brings them shame in this world and the Fire in the Hereafter. [[See the explanation of "al-Khizy" previously: 10:318, note 2, and the references there.]]

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 9, verses 1–2 (part 1 of 3)**

**On the interpretation of His saying, ﴿A declaration of freedom from the Allah and His Messenger, to those among the polytheists with whom you made a covenant (1). So travel freely in the land for four months, and know that you cannot escape Allah, and that Allah will humiliate the disbelievers (2).﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His majesty be exalted, ﴿A declaration of freedom from Allah and His Messenger﴾, he means: this is a declaration of freedom from Allah and His Messenger.

"Bara'ah" (براءة, declaration of freedom) is in the nominative, governed by an omitted element, which is "hadhihi" (هذه, "this"), as in His saying, ﴿A surah which We have sent down﴾ [Surah al-Nur: 1], where "surah" is in the nominative governed by an omitted "hadhihi." If someone said that "bara'ah" is in the nominative governed by the pronoun referring back to it in His saying ﴿to those with whom you made a covenant﴾, treating it as definite, which raises what follows it, since it has become definite through its complement, which is His saying ﴿from Allah and His Messenger﴾, and the meaning of the statement becomes: the freedom from Allah and His Messenger to those among the polytheists with whom you made a covenant [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "براءة" instead of "البراءة", and the context requires what I have confirmed, God willing.]] — this would be an acceptable view whose soundness is not refuted. However, the first opinion is more pleasing to me, because it is the habit of the Arabs to omit, for whatever is visibly present, whether indefinite or definite, that demonstrative: "this" and "this" (fem.). So when they see a good thing they say, "Good, by Allah!" and when they see a bad thing they say, "Bad, by Allah!", meaning: this is good, by Allah, and this is bad, by Allah. That is why I chose the first opinion.

And He said: ﴿A declaration of freedom from Allah and His Messenger to those with whom you made a covenant﴾, and the meaning is: to those among the polytheists with whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made a covenant, because covenants between the Muslims and the polytheists were the covenant of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Only the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), or someone who concluded it on his command, would undertake to conclude them. But He addressed the believers with that because they knew its meaning, and that the covenants of the Prophet (ﷺ) with his community were their covenants, since they were content with all his actions concerning them, and submitted to his covenants on their behalf. So his covenant over them became like their covenants over themselves. That is why He said: ﴿to those among the polytheists with whom you made a covenant﴾, because of the covenant and pact of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

* * *

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have differed concerning those to whom Allah and His Messenger declared freedom from the covenant that existed between him and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) among the polytheists, and he permitted them to travel in the land for four months.

Some of them said: They are two categories of polytheists. One of them: the term of their covenant between him and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was less than four months, and they were given four months of travel. The other of them: the term of his covenant was without a fixed limit, so it was cut short to four months so that he could take counsel for himself; after that he would be at war with Allah, His Messenger and the believers, and he would be killed wherever he is found, and taken captive, unless he repents.

Mention of those who said that:

16356. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, as commander over the pilgrimage in the year nine, to conduct the pilgrimage of the people, while the people of polytheism were in their own places regarding their pilgrimage. Abu Bakr set out with the Muslims who were with him, and the "Surah of Bara'ah" was revealed to annul what existed between the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the polytheists of the covenant that they had been upon between him and them: that no one who came to the House should be prevented, and that no one should be feared in the sacred month. That was a general covenant between him and the people of polytheism. Between that there were covenants between the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and tribes of the Arabs, "special" (khasa'is) until a named term, [[ "khasa'is" means that they were specific to them, not to others.]] So it was revealed concerning him and those among the hypocrites who stayed behind from him at Tabuk, and concerning the statement of those among them who said such things. Allah exposed in it the secrets of people who used to conceal other than what they displayed: some of them were named to us, and some were not named to us. So He said: ﴿A declaration of freedom from Allah and His Messenger to those with whom you made a covenant among the polytheists﴾, that is, to the people of the general covenant from among the polytheists of the Arabs = ﴿So travel freely in the land for four months﴾, up to His saying: ﴿that Allah is free from the polytheists, and His Messenger﴾, that is, after this proof. [[The report: 16356 — Sirah Ibn Hisham 4: 188.]]

* * *

Others said: Rather, Allah, may He be exalted, gave respite of four months of travel to those among the polytheists who had a covenant between them and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). As for whoever did not have a covenant from the Messenger of Allah, his term was fifty nights, which is twenty days of Dhu al-Hijjah and all of Muharram. They said: This was so because the term of those who had no covenant extended to the passing of the sacred months, as Allah said: ﴿So when the sacred months have passed, kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 5], the verse. They said: The proclamation of "Bara'ah" was on the day of the greater pilgrimage, and that is the day of sacrifice according to one group, and according to others it is the day of Arafat, and that is fifty days. They said: As for the postponement of the four months, it was only for the people of the covenant between them and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), from the day "Bara'ah" was revealed. They said: It was revealed at the beginning of Shawwal, so the end of their term was the passing of the sacred months. Some who held this view said: The beginning of the postponement was one for both groups — I mean the one who had a covenant and the one who had no covenant — except that the term of the one who had a covenant was four months, and the term of the one who had no covenant was the passing of the sacred months, which is the end of Muharram.

Mention of those who said that:

16357. Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿A declaration of freedom from Allah and His Messenger to those among the polytheists with whom you made a covenant. So travel freely in the land for four months﴾, he said: Allah set the term for those who made a covenant with His Messenger at four months, during which they may travel wherever they wish. And He set the term for the one who had no covenant as the passing of the sacred months, from the day of sacrifice to the passing of Muharram, which is fifty nights. When the sacred months have passed, He commanded him to lay down the sword against those who had made a covenant.

16358. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When ﴿A declaration of freedom from Allah﴾ was revealed, up to ﴿and that Allah will humiliate the disbelievers﴾, it means: a declaration of freedom from the polytheists who had a covenant on the day "Bara'ah" was revealed. He made the term of those who had a covenant before "Bara'ah" was revealed four months, and commanded them to travel in the land for four months. And He made the term of the polytheists who had no covenant before "Bara'ah" was revealed the passing of the sacred months, and the passing of the sacred months was from the day it was proclaimed as "Bara'ah" until the passing of Muharram, and that is fifty nights: twenty of Dhu al-Hijjah and thirty of Muharram = ﴿So when the sacred months have passed﴾ up to His saying: ﴿and sit in ambush for them at every place of ambush﴾, meaning: no polytheist has any covenant or protection from the time "Bara'ah" was revealed and the sacred months passed. The term of the polytheists who had a covenant before "Bara'ah" was revealed was four months from the day it was proclaimed as "Bara'ah," until the tenth of the beginning of Rabi' al-Akhir, and that is four months.

16359. Narrated to me on the authority of al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His saying: ﴿A declaration of freedom from Allah and His Messenger to those with whom you made a covenant among the polytheists﴾: Before "Bara'ah" was revealed, he made a covenant with some polytheists from Mecca and others, then "Bara'ah" was revealed: a declaration of freedom from Allah to everyone among the polytheists who had made a covenant with you. Indeed I annul the covenant that is between you and them, and I give them a term of four months during which they may travel freely in the land wherever they wish. The term of those who had no covenant between them and the Prophet (ﷺ) was the passing of the sacred months, from the day it was proclaimed as "Bara'ah." It was proclaimed on the day of sacrifice, so it was twenty of Dhu al-Hijjah and Muharram thirty, making fifty nights. So Allah commanded His Prophet that when Muharram passed, he should lay the sword against those who had no covenant between them and the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), killing them until they enter Islam. And He commanded that whoever had a covenant, when four months had passed from the day of sacrifice, he should also lay the sword against them, killing them until they enter Islam. Thus the term of those with no covenant between them and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was fifty nights from the day of sacrifice, and the term of those who had a covenant between them and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was four months, from the day of sacrifice until the tenth of the remaining days of the month of Rabi' al-Akhir.

16360. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿A declaration of freedom from Allah and His Messenger﴾, up to His saying: ﴿and give the good news to those who disbelieve of a painful punishment﴾, he said: It was mentioned to us that Ali proclaimed the call, and Abu Bakr was appointed over the pilgrimage, may Allah's mercy be upon both of them. That was the year in which the Muslims and the polytheists performed the pilgrimage, and the polytheists did not perform the pilgrimage after that year. His saying: ﴿those among the polytheists with whom you made a covenant﴾, up to His saying: ﴿until their term﴾, he said: They are the polytheists of Quraysh, with whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made a covenant at the time of al-Hudaybiyah, and four months of their term remained after the day of sacrifice. Allah commanded His Prophet to fulfil their covenant until their term, and for those with no covenant, the passing of Muharram, and he cast to every person with a covenant his covenant back, and commanded fighting them until they bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and nothing from them would be accepted but that.

* * *

Others said: The beginning of the postponement for the polytheists of four months, and its end for all of them, was one time. They said: Its beginning was the day of the greater pilgrimage, and its end was the end of the tenth of the remaining days of Rabi' al-Akhir.

Mention of those who said that:

16361. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿A declaration of freedom from Allah and His Messenger to those among the polytheists with whom you made a covenant﴾, he said: When this verse was revealed, he was freed from the covenant of every polytheist, and no one was made a covenant after it except those who had already made one, and he gave to each their term = ﴿So travel freely in the land for four months﴾, for whoever's covenant entered it, from the tenth of Dhu al-Hijjah, Muharram, Safar, the month of Rabi' al-Awwal, and the tenth of Rabi' al-Akhir.

16362. Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, saying: Abu Ma'shar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi and others narrated to us, saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Abu Bakr as commander over the season in the year nine, and he sent Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with both of them, with thirty or forty verses of "Bara'ah," and he recited them to the people, giving the polytheists a term of four months to travel freely in the land. He recited "Bara'ah" to them on the day of Arafat, giving the polytheists a term of twenty of Dhu al-Hijjah, Muharram, Safar, the month of Rabi' al-Awwal, and ten of Rabi' al-Akhir. He recited it to them in their dwellings, and said: No polytheist shall perform the pilgrimage after this year of ours, and no one shall circumambulate the House naked.

16363. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿So travel freely in the land for four months﴾: twenty of Dhu al-Hijjah, Muharram, Safar, Rabi' al-Awwal, and ten of Rabi' al-Akhir. That was their covenant that existed between them.

16364. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿A declaration of freedom from Allah and His Messenger﴾, to the people of the covenant: Khuza'ah, and Mudlij, and whoever among them or others had a covenant. [[In the manuscript: "ومن كان له أو غيرهم", and in the printed edition: "ومن كان له عهد من غيرهم"; I have corrected it as you see.]] The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned from Tabuk when he had finished, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intended the pilgrimage, then said: Polytheists come and circumambulate naked, so I do not like to perform the pilgrimage until that no longer happens. So he sent Abu Bakr and Ali, may Allah's mercy be upon both of them, and they went among the people at Dhu al-Majaz, and at their marketplaces where they used to trade, and at all the seasons, and they announced to the companions of the covenant that they should be safe for four months, which are the consecutive months: twenty from the end of Dhu al-Hijjah until ten remaining days of Rabi' al-Akhir, after which they have no covenant. And he announced to all the people the declaration of war unless they believed.

16365. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid concerning His saying: ﴿A declaration of freedom from Allah and His Messenger to those with whom you made a covenant among the polytheists﴾, he said: The people of the covenant are Mudlij, and the Arabs with whom he made a covenant, and whoever had a covenant. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came back from Tabuk when he had finished with it, and intended the pilgrimage, then said: Polytheists come to the House and circumambulate naked, so I do not like to perform the pilgrimage until that no longer happens. So he sent Abu Bakr and Ali, may Allah's mercy be upon both of them, and they went among the people at Dhu al-Majaz, and at their marketplaces where they used to trade, and at the whole season, and they announced to the companions of the covenant that they should be safe for four months, which are the sacred months that have passed, consecutive: twenty from the end of Dhu al-Hijjah until ten remaining days of Rabi' al-Akhir, after which they have no covenant. And he announced to all the people the declaration of war unless they believed. So all the people believed at that time, and no one traveled freely. And he said: When he returned from al-Ta'if, he went straight away from that, and then he went out to Tabuk, after he had come to Medina.

* * *

Others said, from among those who said: "The beginning of the term for all the polytheists and its end was one": Its beginning was the day "Bara'ah" was revealed, and the end was the passing of the sacred months, which is the end of Muharram.

Mention of those who said that:

16366. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri: ﴿So travel freely in the land for four months﴾, he said: It was revealed in Shawwal, so these four months are: Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, and Muharram.

* * *

Others said: The postponement of the four months given by Allah to the polytheists for travel was only for the one who had a covenant between him and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of a term less than four months. As for the one who had a covenant with a term more than four months, he commanded (ﷺ) that his covenant be completed for its term.

Mention of those who said that:

16367. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, who said: Al-Kalbi said: The four months were only for the one who had a covenant between him and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) less than four months, so four months were completed for him. As for the one who had a covenant of more than four months, he is the one whose covenant he commanded to be completed, and He said: ﴿So complete their covenant for them until their term﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 4].

* * *

Abu Ja'far, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The most correct of these opinions is the statement of the one who said: The term which Allah granted to the people of the covenant among the polytheists, and in which He permitted them to travel by His saying: ﴿So travel freely in the land for four months﴾, is only for the people of the covenant who backed up (zahara) against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and broke their covenant before the end of its term. As for those who did not break their covenant and did not back up against him, Allah, may His majesty be exalted, commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to complete the covenant between him and them until its term, by His saying: ﴿except those among the polytheists with whom you made a covenant, who have not failed you in anything nor backed anyone against you; so complete for them their covenant until their term. Indeed Allah loves the righteous﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 4].

If someone supposes that the saying of Allah, may His mention be exalted: ﴿So when the sacred months have passed, kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 5] indicates something contrary to what we have said about that, since it would imply that the obligation on the believers was to kill every polytheist after the passing of the sacred months [[In the printed edition: "ينبئ عن أن..." and Abu Ja'far has repeatedly used "على" with "ينبئ"; I have kept it as in the manuscript, which is permissible since it includes the meaning of "يدل" (indicates).]], then the matter is contrary to what he supposed. That is because the verse that follows it demonstrates the soundness of what we have said [[In the printed edition: "تنبئ عن صحة"; I have kept what is in the manuscript.]], and the error of what the one who supposed that the passing of the sacred months would permit killing every polytheist, whether or not he had a covenant from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), held. That is His saying: ﴿How can there be for the polytheists a covenant with Allah and with His Messenger, except those with whom you made a covenant at the Sacred Mosque? So as long as they remain upright toward you, remain upright toward them. Indeed Allah loves the righteous﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 7]. These are polytheists, and Allah commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers to remain upright toward them in their covenant, so long as they remain upright toward them by not breaking their treaty and not backing their enemy against them.

Then after that, Abu Ja'far said: The widely transmitted reports from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) show that when he sent Ali, may God have mercy on him, with the declaration (Bara'ah) to the people with whom he had covenants, he commanded him, among what he commanded, to proclaim among them: "Whoever has a covenant between himself and the Messenger of God (ﷺ), his covenant extends to its term." This is the clearest evidence for the soundness of what we have said. God did not command His Prophet (ﷺ) to breach the covenant of a people with whom he had made a covenant for a fixed term, when they remained faithful to their covenant by not breaking it. He only set a deadline of four months for those who had breached their covenant before the deadline was announced, or for those whose covenant had no fixed term. As for the one whose covenant had a defined term and who had not made breaking it his own choice, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was commanded to fulfill his covenant until its term ended. With this he sent his herald to proclaim among the people of the pilgrimage season from among the Arabs.

16368. Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, he said: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Qays narrated to us, from Mughirah, from al-Sha'bi, who said: Muharrir ibn Abi Hurayra narrated to me, from Abu Hurayra, who said: I was with Ali, may God have mercy on him, when the Prophet (ﷺ) sent him to proclaim. Whenever his voice grew hoarse, I would proclaim in his place. [Editor's note: "Sahila sawtuhu" means his voice became hoarse, which is the same as al-bahh. It has another, similar meaning in the hadith of Umm Ma'bad describing the Messenger of God, may my father and mother be ransomed for him (ﷺ), where she said: "And in his voice there is sahal" (with two fathas), which is like hoarseness in the voice, so it is not sharp and high-pitched.] I asked: What were you proclaiming? He said: Four things: No naked person shall circumambulate the Ka'bah; whoever has a covenant with the Messenger of God (ﷺ), his covenant extends to its term; no one shall enter Paradise except a believing soul; and no polytheist shall perform the Hajj after this year of ours. [Editor's note: The report 16368 was transmitted by Abu Ja'far through three chains, and its takhrij will come later. "Qays" is Qays ibn al-Rabi' al-Asadi, whom Ahmad and others regarded as weak in transmission, and his previous mentions were numerous, the last being no. 12802. "Mughirah" is Mughirah ibn Miqsam al-Dabbi, trustworthy, from whom the whole group narrated; he was mentioned many times before, the last being no. 11340. "Muharrir ibn Abi Hurayra" is a trustworthy Successor (tabi'i) who transmitted few hadiths, mentioned previously in no. 2863. This report is weak in its chain because of the weakness of Qays ibn al-Rabi'.]

16369. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Affan narrated to us, he said: Qays ibn al-Rabi' narrated to us, he said: al-Shaybani narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi, who said: Muharrir ibn Abi Hurayra informed us, from his father, who said: I was with Ali, may God be pleased with him, and he mentioned something similar, except that he said: "And whoever has a covenant between himself and the Messenger of God (ﷺ), his covenant extends to its term." [Editor's note: This is the second chain of the hadith of Muharrir ibn Abi Hurayra. "Affan" is Affan ibn Muslim ibn Abd Allah al-Saffar, whom the whole group narrated from; he narrated from Qays ibn al-Rabi', and there is some criticism of him. His biography was given at no. 5392. "Al-Shaybani" is Abu Ishaq al-Shaybani, Sulayman ibn Abi Sulayman, the Imam, mentioned many times, the last being no. 12489. The defect of this chain is the weakness of Qays ibn al-Rabi'. However, al-Hakim transmitted it in al-Mustadrak 2:331 through the route of Shu'bah, from Sulayman al-Shaybani, and said: "This hadith has a sound chain but they did not include it," and al-Dhahabi agreed. See the following note.]

Abu Ja'far said: Shu'bah also transmitted this hadith and differed from Qays regarding the term.

16370. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, both saying: Uthman ibn Umar narrated to us, he said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Mughirah, from al-Sha'bi, from Muharrir ibn Abi Hurayra, from his father, who said: I was with Ali when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent him with the declaration to the people of Makkah, and I kept proclaiming until my voice became hoarse. I asked him: What were you proclaiming? He said: We were commanded to proclaim: No one shall enter Paradise except a believer; and whoever has a covenant between himself and the Messenger of God (ﷺ), its term is four months. When the term expires, God is free of the polytheists and His Messenger; no naked person shall circumambulate the House; and no polytheist shall perform the Hajj after this year. [Editor's note: This is the third chain. "Uthman ibn Umar ibn Fares al-Abdi" is trustworthy, and the whole group narrated from him; he was mentioned many times, including no. 5458 and others. This report, through Shu'bah from Mughirah, was transmitted by Ahmad in his Musnad, no. 7964, and by al-Nasa'i in his Sunan 5:234. Al-Hakim transmitted it in al-Mustadrak 2:331 through another route, from al-Nadr ibn Shumayl, from Shu'bah, from Sulayman al-Shaybani, and said: "This hadith has a sound chain, but they did not include it," and al-Dhahabi agreed; see the previous note. Ibn Kathir discussed it fully in his Tafsir 4:111, and in al-Tarikh 5:38, and he said in al-Tarikh: "This chain is good, but there is an odd element in the statement of the narrator that whoever had a covenant was given a term of four months. Some have held this view, but the correct position is that whoever had a covenant is given a term up to its end, however long it may be, even if it exceeds four months. For one who had no term at all, the deferral is four months. There remains a third category: one whose term ends in less than four months from the day of the deferral. This may be attached to the first category, so his term extends to its end, however short. It may also be said that he is given a deferral of four months, because he has a better claim than one who had no covenant at all." See the explanation of the report in Musnad Ahmad.]

Abu Ja'far said: I fear that this report contains an error by its transmitter regarding the term, because the reports are widely transmitted contrary to it, besides Qays's disagreement with Shu'bah on this very hadith, as I have explained.

16371. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith al-A'war, from Ali, may God have mercy on him, who said: I was commanded with four things: that no polytheist shall come near the House after this year; that no man shall circumambulate the House naked; that no one shall enter Paradise except every Muslim soul; and that every person with a covenant be fulfilled in his covenant. [Editor's note: "Al-Harith al-A'war" is al-Harith ibn Abd Allah al-Hamdani, very weak; he was mentioned many times before, see no. 174. Therefore its chain is weak. It will come with another chain, no. 16374.]

16372. Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, he said: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Israil narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Zayd ibn Yuthay', who said: Surah Bara'ah was revealed, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent it with Abu Bakr, then he sent Ali and took it from him. When Abu Bakr returned he said: Has anything been revealed about me? He said: No, but I was commanded to deliver it myself or a man from my family. So he (Ali) set out for Makkah, [Editor's note: "He set out" refers to Ali, may God have mercy on him,] and he stood among them and proclaimed four things: that no polytheist shall enter Makkah after this year; that no naked person shall circumambulate the Ka'bah; that no one shall enter Paradise except a Muslim soul; and whoever has a covenant between himself and the Messenger of God, his covenant extends to its term. [Editor's note: The two reports 16372 and 16373 are the hadith of Zayd ibn Yuthay', which he will transmit through three routes: this one, the one following it, and then no. 16379. "Zayd ibn Yuthay'", or "Uthay'" with diminutive form in both, is a trustworthy Successor who transmitted few hadiths; mentioned before in no. 15737. This report was transmitted by Ahmad in his Musnad no. 594, through the route of Sufyan from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, and its chain is sound. al-Tirmidhi transmitted it in the Book of Hajj, in the chapter on what has come concerning the disapproval of circumambulating naked, and said: "There is also a report from Abu Hurayrah on this subject." Abu Isa said: "The hadith of Ali is good." By the hadith of Abu Hurayrah he means what preceded at nos. 16368–16370. He also transmitted it in the Book of Tafsir and said: "This is a good, sound hadith." Ahmad also transmitted in the Musnad of Abu Bakr no. 4 a similar, longer hadith from Zayd ibn Yuthay', from Abu Bakr.]

16373. Ibn Wakic narrated to us, he said: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Zakariyya, from Abu Ishaq, from Zayd ibn Yuthay', from Ali, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) sent me when Surah Bara'ah was revealed, with four things: that no naked person shall circumambulate the House; that no polytheist shall come near the Sacred Mosque after their year this year; whoever has a covenant between himself and the Messenger of God (ﷺ), it extends to its term; and that no one shall enter Paradise except a Muslim soul. [Editor's note: See the note on the previous report.]

16374. Ibn Wakic narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith, from Ali, may God have mercy on him, who said: I was sent to the people of Makkah with four things, and then he mentioned the hadith. [Editor's note: See the note on report 16371.]

16375. Ibrahim ibn Sa'id al-Jawhari narrated to us, he said: Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Sulayman ibn Qarm narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn Abbas: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent Abu Bakr with Surah Bara'ah, then he followed him with Ali and took it from him. Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, has something been revealed about me? He said: "No. You are my companion in the cave and at the Pool; no one shall deliver on my behalf except me or Ali!" What he sent Ali with was four things: no one shall enter Paradise except a Muslim soul; no polytheist shall perform the Hajj after this year; no naked person shall circumambulate the House; and whoever has a covenant between himself and the Messenger of God (ﷺ), it extends to its term. [Editor's note: "Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Marwazi" was narrated from by the whole group; he was mentioned many times before, the last being no. 15338. "Sulayman ibn Qarm ibn Mu'adh al-Taymi" is trustworthy, though some accused him of extremism in Shi'ism; see no. 9163. "Al-Hakam" is al-Hakam ibn Utaybah, mentioned many times. This report was transmitted by al-Tirmidhi in the Book of Tafsir, through another route, from Abbad ibn al-Awwam, from Sufyan ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hakam ibn Utaybah, similarly, and he said: "This is a good, strange hadith from this route, from the hadith of Ibn Abbas."]

16376. Ibn Wakic narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Khalid, from Amir, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) sent Ali, may God have mercy on him, and he proclaimed: "Beware, no polytheist shall perform the Hajj after this year; no naked person shall circumambulate the House; no one shall enter Paradise except a Muslim soul; and whoever has a covenant between himself and the Messenger of God (ﷺ), its term extends to its end; and God is free of the polytheists and His Messenger."

16377. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from Hakim ibn Hakim ibn Abbad ibn Hanif, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Husayn ibn Ali, who said: When Surah Bara'ah was revealed upon the Messenger of God (ﷺ), he had sent Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God have mercy on him, to lead the Hajj for the people. It was said to him: O Messenger of God, if only you had sent someone to Abu Bakr! He said: "None shall deliver on my behalf except a man from my family!" Then he called Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God have mercy on him, and said: "Go out with this account from the beginning of Bara'ah, and proclaim to the people on the day of sacrifice when they gather at Mina: no unbeliever shall enter Paradise; no polytheist shall perform the Hajj after this year; no naked person shall circumambulate the House; and whoever has a covenant with the Messenger of God (ﷺ), it extends to its term." Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God have mercy on him, set out on the she-camel of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), al-Adba', and caught up with Abu Bakr al-Siddiq on the road. When Abu Bakr saw him he said: "Are you a commander or one who is commanded?" He said: "One who is commanded." Then they both went on, may God have mercy on them both. Abu Bakr led the people in the Hajj, while the Arabs, at that time and in that year, were in their traditional places of Hajj that they had followed in the Jahiliyyah. When the day of sacrifice came, Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God have mercy on him, stood and proclaimed to the people what the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had commanded him, saying: "O people, no one shall enter Paradise except a Muslim soul; no polytheist shall perform the Hajj after this year; no naked person shall circumambulate the House; and whoever has a covenant with the Messenger of God (ﷺ), it is his until its term." After that year no polytheist performed the Hajj, and no naked person circumambulated the House. Then they both came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ). This was from Bara'ah concerning those among the polytheists who had a general covenant, and those with a term up to the appointed end. [Editor's note: Ibn Hisham, al-Sirah 4:190, 191. "Hakim ibn Hakim ibn Abbad ibn Hanif al-Ansari" is trustworthy, though some spoke about him, to the point that Ibn Sa'd said: "He narrated few hadiths, and they do not use his hadith as proof." His biography was given in no. 11741.]

16378. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: When these verses were revealed up to the end of forty verses, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent them with Abu Bakr and appointed him to lead the Hajj. When he had traveled and reached the tree at Dhu al-Hulayfah, he sent Ali after him and took them from him. Abu Bakr returned to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, may my father and mother be your ransom, has something been revealed about me?" He said: "No, but none may deliver on my behalf except someone other than me, or a man from my own family. Are you not content, O Abu Bakr, that you were with me in the cave, and that you are my companion at the Pool?" He said: "Yes, O Messenger of God!" Abu Bakr continued leading the pilgrims, while Ali proclaimed Bara'ah. He stood on the day of Adha and said: "No polytheist shall come near the Sacred Mosque after this year; no naked person shall circumambulate the House; whoever has a covenant between himself and the Messenger of God (ﷺ), his covenant extends to its term; and these are days of eating and drinking; and God will not admit anyone into Paradise except one who is a Muslim." They said: "We disavow your covenant and the covenant of your cousin, except for stabbing and striking!" The polytheists returned, blaming one another and saying: "What are you doing, when Quraysh has embraced Islam?" So they embraced Islam.

16379. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Zayd ibn Yuthay', from Ali, who said: I was commanded with four things: that no polytheist come near the House after this year; that no naked person circumambulate the House; that no one enter Paradise except a Muslim soul; and that every person with a covenant be fulfilled in his covenant. Ma'mar said: Qatadah also said it. [Editor's note: See the note on reports 16372 and 16373.]

Abu Ja'far said: These reports and their like confirm what we have said, and that the period of four months was only for those we have described. As for the one whose covenant had a known term, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and the believers have no right to breach it or to support their enemies against them. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) fulfilled his covenant until its term, by God's command to him. The apparent meaning of the revelation supports this, and the reports from the Messenger (ﷺ) are widely transmitted to that effect.

As for the four months, they were the deadline for those we mentioned. Their beginning was the day of the Greater Hajj, and their end was the completion of ten days of Rabi' al-Akhir.
