Thus they were four consecutive months, granted to the people of the covenants whose situation we described, during which they could travel through the land, going wherever they wished, with no Muslim confronting them with war, killing, or plunder.

Someone might say: If the matter is as you described, what is the meaning of His words: ﴿So when the sacred months have passed, kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ (Surah al-Tawbah: 5)? You know that their passing refers to the passing of the sacred month of Muharram, and you claim that the deferral granted by God and His Messenger to those people was four months, but between the day of the Greater Hajj and the end of the sacred months there are about fifty days. Where are the fifty days in relation to the four months?

It is said: the expiry of the sacred months was only the term for those polytheists who had no covenant with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), while the four months were for those who had a covenant, either for an unspecified term, or for a specified term which they had violated. By their violation, they became like those whose treachery is feared, and so it was due that the covenant be cast back to them on equal terms, except that they were given the four months to prepare for themselves and to seek refuge. Do you not see that Allah says to the people of the four months, describing them as people of covenant: ﴿A declaration of immunity from Allah and His Messenger to those among the polytheists with whom you made a covenant. So travel freely in the land for four months, and know that you cannot escape Allah﴾; and He describes those for whom the expiry of the sacred months was the term as people of polytheism, not people of covenant, saying: ﴿And a proclamation from Allah and His Messenger to the people on the day of the greatest pilgrimage that Allah is free of obligation to the polytheists, and so is His Messenger﴾, to the end of the verse, = ﴿except those among the polytheists with whom you made a covenant﴾, to the end of the verse? Then He said: ﴿When the sacred months have passed, kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾. So He commanded the killing of the polytheists who had no covenant after the expiry of the sacred months, and the fulfilment of the covenant of those who had a covenant, provided they had not broken their covenant by aiding against the believers and inflicting harm upon them through it.

If someone says: What is the evidence that the beginning of the term was the day of the greatest pilgrimage, and not that it began in Shawwal, as those who hold that view claim?

It is said to him: Those who hold that view claim that the term began from the time of the revelation of "Bara'ah" (Surat al-Tawbah), and that cannot be correct, because the one granted the period of travel has a term up to a specified time. If he does not know what has been granted to him, especially when there is a covenant he had before that which contradicts it, then he is like one who was not granted that, for when he does not know what is his in the term granted to him and what is upon him after it ends, he is in the same state as before the term was granted. It is well known that the people did not learn of what had been granted to them except when it was proclaimed to them at the season of pilgrimage. And when that is so, it is established that its beginning was as we have said, and its ending was as we have described.

As for His saying: ﴿So travel freely in the land for four months﴾, it means: travel in it, coming and going, secure and without fear from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his followers.

* *

It is said of it: "So-and-so travelled (sāḥa) in the land, travels (yasīḥu), a journey (siyāḥah), and [its verbal nouns] sayūḥan and sayaḥānan."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And know that you cannot escape Allah﴾, it says to the people of covenant, those who had a covenant with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) before the revelation of this verse: Know, O polytheists, that if you travel in the land, and choose that while you remain in disbelief in Allah, without acknowledging His oneness and affirming His Messenger = ﴿you cannot escape Allah﴾, meaning: you cannot frustrate Him by yourselves, for wherever you go and wherever you are on earth, you are within His grasp and authority; no minister will protect you from Him, and no fortress or refuge will stand between you and Him if He wills to punish you. [[See the explanation of "al-I'jaz" previously: 12:128 / 13:31.]] Except by faith in Him and His Messenger, and repentance from disobeying Him. That is, hasten to forestall His punishment by repentance, and leave off the travelling which will not benefit you.

As for His saying: ﴿And that Allah will disgrace the disbelievers﴾, it means: know that Allah humiliates the disbelievers, and brings them shame in this world and the Fire in the Hereafter. [[See the explanation of "al-Khizy" previously: 10:318, note 2, and the references there.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 3 (part 1 of 3):

The explanation of His saying: ﴿And a proclamation from Allah and His Messenger to the people on the day of the greatest Hajj that Allah is free of obligation to the polytheists, and so is His Messenger﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: and an announcement from Allah and His Messenger to the people on the day of the greatest Hajj.
* *
We have already explained the meaning of "al-adhan" (proclamation) earlier in this book, with its evidence. [[See the explanation of "al-adhan" above. ... Comment: ... and the references there.]]
* *
Sulayman ibn Musa used to say the following about this:
16380. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Sulayman ibn Musa al-Shami claimed that His saying ﴿And a proclamation from Allah and His Messenger﴾ means: "al-adhan" is the narratives, the opening of "Bara'a" (Surat al-Tawba) until its conclusion: ﴿And if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty﴾ [Surat al-Tawba: 28]. That makes twenty-eight verses. [[Report 16380: Sulayman ibn Musa al-Umawi al-Dimashqi, al-Ashdaq, the jurist of the people of Syria in his time. It passed as nos. 15654, 15655.]]
16381. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And a proclamation from Allah and His Messenger﴾: it is an announcement from Allah and His Messenger.
* *
The phrase ﴿And a proclamation from Allah﴾ is in the nominative case (raf') by coordination (atf) with His saying ﴿A declaration of disavowal from Allah﴾, as if He had said: "This is a declaration of disavowal from Allah and His Messenger, and a proclamation from Allah."
* *
As for His saying ﴿the day of the greatest Hajj﴾, there is disagreement among the scholars concerning it.
Some of them said: It is the day of 'Arafah.
Mention of those who said this:
16382. Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam narrated to us, saying: Abu Zur'a Wahb Allah ibn Rashid informed us, saying: Hayawa ibn Shurayh informed us, saying: Abu Sakhr informed us that he heard Abu Mu'awiya al-Bajali of the people of Kufa say: I heard Abu al-Sahba' al-Bakri say: I asked 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, about "the day of the greatest Hajj," and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Abu Bakr ibn Abi Quhafa, may Allah be pleased with him, to lead the people in Hajj, and sent me with him with forty verses of Bara'a. When he reached 'Arafah, he delivered a sermon to the people on the day of 'Arafah. When he finished his sermon, he turned to me and said: "Stand up, O 'Ali, and deliver the message of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ!" So I stood and recited to them forty verses of "Bara'a." Then we departed ["sadara 'an al-ma' wa al-bilad" means to return; "al-sadr" (with two fatha vowels) is the night of the people's return from 'Arafah to Mina; "sadar al-bayt" (with a damma on the sad and a shadda on the dal) means the pilgrims returning from their Hajj], until we came to Mina. I threw the pebbles at the Jamra, sacrificed the camel, then shaved my head, and I knew that the people of the gathering had not been present for Abu Bakr's sermon on the day of 'Arafah. So I began going around the tents ["al-fasatit" is the plural of "fustat," similar to a sarradiq but smaller, used by travellers] reciting it to them. That is why I suppose that you thought it was the day of sacrifice, while it is the day of 'Arafah. [[Report 16382: The explanation of this chain was given earlier at no. 5386. Abu Zur'a, Wahb Allah ibn Rashid al-Misri, appeared many times, the last at no. 11510 with its references there. In the printed edition here it read "Abu Zur'a and Wahb Allah ibn Rashid qalа" (two men), which is wrong; the manuscript has the same, except it wrote "qal" in the singular, placing the kunya before the name. The correct reading is what has been adopted. Hayawa ibn Shurayh appeared many times, the last at no. 11510. Abu Sakhr is Humayd ibn Ziyad al-Kharrat; Ahmad said "there is no harm in him," and Muslim narrated from him. He appeared at no. 4325 and elsewhere. Abu Mu'awiya al-Bajali is 'Ammar ibn Mu'awiya al-Duhni, as al-Tabari stated explicitly at no. 4325; he is trustworthy and appeared in several places. Abu al-Sahba' al-Bakri was explained at no. 5386. This is a sound chain.]]

Sahl ibn Muhammad al-Sijistani narrated to us, saying: Abu Jabir al-Harami narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn al-Ghaz al-Jarshi narrated to us, from Nafiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood at the Jamarat on the Day of Sacrifice during the Farewell Pilgrimage and said: 'This is the Day of the Greater Hajj.'"

[[Editor's note on 16447: "Sahl ibn Muhammad ibn ʿUthman al-Sijistani" is Abu Hatim, the grammarian, reciter, famous Basran. Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy (al-Thiqat). He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, and in Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/204. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 1/1/165, where no criticism is mentioned, Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/5, and Mizan al-iʿtidal 3: 95. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it from the report of al-Walid ibn Muslim, from Hisham ibn al-Ghaz. Then he narrated it from the report of Saʿid ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz, from Nafiʿ, with this chain. As for al-Hakim, he transmitted it in al-Mustadrak 2: 331 through Sulayman ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Dimashqi, from al-Walid ibn Muslim, from Hisham ibn al-Ghaz, and then said: "This is a hadith with a sound chain, though they [al-Bukhari and Muslim] did not transmit it in this form. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Murrah al-Hamdani, from a man of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood among us upon a red she-camel, split-eared [[al-mukhadramah: the one whose ear-tip is cut. [[Editor's note on 16448: "A man of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)" may have been ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, for Ibn Majah transmitted the report at length in his Sunan (1016, no. 3057), through Ismaʿil ibn Tawbah, from Zafir ibn Sulayman, from Abu Sinan, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud. 16449. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Saʿid narrated to us, saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr ibn Murrah informed me, saying: Murrah narrated to us, saying: A man of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) narrated to us, saying: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood among us," and he mentioned something similar.

[[Editor's note on 16450: "Ismaʿil ibn Abi Khalid al-Ahmasi" has passed several times. "His father" is Abu Khalid al-Ahmasi al-Bajali, who is biographed in al-Tahdhib. 16451. Yaʿqub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to me, from Hajjaj ibn Artah, from ʿAta', who said: "The Day of the Greater Hajj is the Day of Sacrifice."

16452. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿the Day of the Greater Hajj﴾: "It is the Day of Sacrifice, the day on which the one in ihram is released from its restrictions and the camels are slaughtered." Ibn ʿUmar used to say: "It is the Day of Sacrifice." My father used to say this too. And Ibn ʿAbbas used to say: "It is the Day of ʿArafah." I have not heard anyone say that it is the Day of ʿArafah except Ibn ʿAbbas. Ibn Zayd said: "The Hajj is lost by the loss of the Day of Sacrifice, and it is not lost by the loss of the Day of ʿArafah. If one misses the day, one has not missed the night; one stands [at ʿArafah] from the time between it and the rising of dawn."

16453. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: "The Day of al-Adha, the Day of the Greater Hajj."

16454. Sufyan narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, who said: "A man of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) narrated to me in this room of mine, I think he said: 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) addressed us on the Day of Sacrifice from a red split-eared she-camel, and said: "Do you know what day this is? This is the Day of Sacrifice, and this is the Day of the Greater Hajj."'"

[[Editor's note on 16454: See the note on no. 16448.]]

* *

Others said: The meaning of His saying ﴿the Day of the Greater Hajj﴾ is: the time of the Greater Hajj and its appointed period. They said: That is the days of Hajj entire, not one particular day.

Mention of those who said that:

16455. Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "﴿The Day of the Greater Hajj﴾: the time of Hajj, its days entire."

16456. Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: "The Greater Hajj is the days of Mina entire, and the gatherings of the polytheists when they were at Dhu al-Majaz, ʿUkaz and Majannah, when it was proclaimed among them: that the Muslims and the polytheists shall not gather after this year of theirs, that no one shall circumambulate the House naked, and that whoever has a treaty between himself and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), his treaty extends to its term."

16457. al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿUbayd narrated to us, saying: "Sufyan used to say: 'the Day of Hajj,' 'the Day of the Camel,' 'the Day of Siffin,' meaning: its days entire."

16458. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, concerning His saying ﴿the Day of the Greater Hajj﴾, he said: "The time of Hajj, that is, its days entire."

* *

Abu Jaʿfar [al-Tabari] said: The most correct of the sayings on this matter, in my view, is the saying of those who said: "The Day of the Greater Hajj is the Day of Sacrifice," because of the convergence of reports from a group of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that ʿAli proclaimed, on the Day of Sacrifice, what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had sent him with of the message to the polytheists, and recited the "Bara'ah" (Immunity/Disavowal) to them. This is together with the reports we have mentioned from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said on the Day of Sacrifice: "Do you know what day this is? This is the Day of the Greater Hajj."

Furthermore, "yawm" (day) is attributed to the meaning in which it occurs, as people say: "the Day of ʿArafah," which is the day on which people stand at ʿArafah; "the Day of al-Adha," which is the day on which they sacrifice; and "the Day of al-Fitr," which is the day on which they break the fast. Likewise "the Day of Hajj" is the day on which they perform Hajj. People perform Hajj and complete their rites on the Day of Sacrifice, because in the night following the day of the Sacrifice, standing at ʿArafah continues until dawn, and on its morning the acts of Hajj are performed. As for the Day of ʿArafah, although standing at ʿArafah occurs on it, the standing there is not lost before the rising of dawn of the night of the Sacrifice, and the whole Hajj is on the Day of Sacrifice.

* *

As for what Mujahid said, that "the Day of Hajj" is in fact its days entire: although that is permissible in the speech of the Arabs, it is not the most famous and well-known of its meanings in the speech of the Arabs. Rather, the more prevalent meaning of "day" among them is from sunset to its counterpart the next day. The interpretation of the Book of Allah must be carried according to the most famous and well-known usage of the speakers in whose tongue the Book was revealed.

* *

The interpreters differed concerning the reason why this day was called "the Day of the Greater Hajj."

Some of them said: It was so named because that was in a year in which the Hajj of the Muslims and the polytheists gathered together.

Mention of those who said that:

[The text ends here, as the passage continues in the next part.]

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 9, Verse 3 (Part 3 of 3)**

16459. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan, who said: "It was called 'al-Hajj al-Akbar' (the Greater Pilgrimage) because Abu Bakr performed the pilgrimage that he performed, and both Muslims and polytheists gathered during it. That is why it was called 'al-Hajj al-Akbar.' It also coincided with the festival of the Jews and the Christians."

16460. Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salama narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal, who said: "The day of the Greater Pilgrimage was the Farewell Pilgrimage. In it the pilgrimage of the Muslims, the Christians and the Jews gathered, and it had not gathered before it or after it."

16461. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan, who said concerning His words ﴿the day of the Greater Pilgrimage﴾: "It was only called 'al-Hajj al-Akbar' because Abu Bakr performed the pilgrimage on that day, and the covenants were annulled on it."

* * *

Others said: "al-Hajj al-Akbar" is the *qiran* (combining the pilgrimage and the lesser pilgrimage in one state of ihram), and "al-Hajj al-Asghar" is the *ifrad* (performing the pilgrimage alone).

Mention of those who said this:

16462. Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr al-Nahshali narrated to us, from Hammad, from Mujahid, who said: He used to say: "al-Hajj al-Akbar" and "al-Hajj al-Asghar." So "al-Hajj al-Akbar" is the *qiran*, and "al-Hajj al-Asghar" is the *ifrad* of the pilgrimage.

* * *

Others said: "al-Hajj al-Akbar" is the Hajj, and "al-Hajj al-Asghar" is the 'umrah (the lesser pilgrimage).

Mention of those who said this:

16463. Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata', who said: "al-Hajj al-Akbar" is the Hajj, and "al-Hajj al-Asghar" is the 'umrah.

16464. ...... He said: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, from Dawud, from 'Amir, who said: I said to him: "This is the Greater Pilgrimage, so what is the Lesser Pilgrimage?" He said: "The 'umrah."

16465. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from al-Sha'bi, who said: It used to be said: "al-Hajj al-Asghar" is the 'umrah performed in Ramadan.

16466. ...... He said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, who said: It used to be said: "al-Hajj al-Asghar" is the 'umrah.

16467. ...... He said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Asma', from 'Abdullah ibn Shaddad, who said: "The day of the Greater Pilgrimage" is the Day of Sacrifice (yawm al-nahr), and "al-Hajj al-Asghar" is the 'umrah.

16468. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, that the people of the Jahiliyyah used to call the 'umrah "al-Hajj al-Asghar."

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these opinions in my view is the statement of the one who said: "al-Hajj al-Akbar" is the Hajj, because it is greater than the 'umrah in that its actions exceed the actions of the 'umrah. It was therefore called "the Greatest" for this reason. As for "al-Asghar," it is the 'umrah, because its actions are fewer than the actions of the Hajj, and so it was called "the Lesser" on account of the deficiency of its actions compared to those of the Hajj.

* * *

As for His words ﴿that Allah is free from the polytheists, and so is His Messenger﴾, its meaning is: that Allah is free from the covenant of the polytheists, and His Messenger is too, after this pilgrimage.

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the speech is: an announcement from Allah and His Messenger to the people on the day of the Greater Pilgrimage that Allah and His Messenger are free from the covenant of the polytheists, as:

16469. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, concerning ﴿that Allah is free from the polytheists, and so is His Messenger﴾: that is, after the pilgrimage. [[Report: 16469 – Sirat Ibn Hisham 4: 188. This follows the earlier report no. 16356.]]

* * *

Concerning the interpretation of His words: ﴿But if you repent, it is better for you; and if you turn away, then know that you cannot escape Allah. And give tidings to those who disbelieve of a painful punishment﴾ (3).

Abu Ja'far said: The Exalted says: ﴿If you repent﴾, O polytheists, from your disbelief, and return to the affirmation of Allah's oneness and sincere worship of Him alone, without the deities and rivals, then returning to that is ﴿better for you﴾ than persisting in polytheism in this world and the Hereafter. ﴿But if you turn away﴾ means: if you turn your backs on faith in Allah and refuse anything but persistence in your polytheism. ﴿Then know that you cannot escape Allah﴾ means: be certain that you cannot put yourselves beyond Allah's reach, so that His painful punishment and His severe retribution will not befall you for your persistence in disbelief, just as He did to those before you among the people of polytheism by sending down His vengeance upon them and bringing His punishment swiftly upon their dwelling. ﴿And give tidings to those who disbelieve﴾ means: O Muhammad, inform those who denied your prophethood and opposed the command of their Lord ﴿of a painful punishment﴾ that will befall them.

16470. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, concerning His words ﴿If you repent﴾: he said: "You believe."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 4:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Except those with whom you made a treaty among the polytheists, then they have not failed you in anything and have not supported anyone against you, so complete for them their treaty until their term.⁠ Indeed, Allah loves the righteous.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may He be remembered, says: ﴿And an announcement from Allah and His Messenger to the people on the day of the greatest pilgrimage that Allah is free of obligation to the polytheists, and so is His Messenger﴾, except for the covenant of those with whom you made a treaty among the polytheists, O believers [see the explanation of "mu'ahada" (treaty) above, p. 21, note 2, and the references there]. ﴿Then they have not failed you in anything﴾, meaning, not failed to uphold your covenant which you made with them. ﴿And have not supported anyone against you﴾, meaning, against your enemy, by aiding them with their persons and bodies, nor with weapons, horses, or men [see the explanation of "muzahara" (support) above, vol. 2, p. 304]. ﴿So complete for them their treaty until their term﴾, meaning: fulfill for them the covenant you made with them, and do not wage war against them until the end of the term of the treaty between you and them [see the explanation of "itmam" (completion) above, vol. 13, p. 87, note 1, and the references there]. ﴿Indeed, Allah loves the righteous﴾, meaning: indeed, Allah loves those who fear Him by obeying Him, by performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions [see the explanation of "taqwa" (God-consciousness) above in the language indexes, under (w-q-y)].

16471 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿So complete for them their treaty until their term﴾, he said: until their appointed time.

16472 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿Except those with whom you made a treaty among the polytheists﴾, meaning: the specific covenant until the appointed term ﴿then they have not failed you in anything﴾, etc. [Report 16472 - Sirah of Ibn Hisham 2:188, which continues the earlier report no. 16469.]

16473 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: ﴿Except those with whom you made a treaty among the polytheists, then they have not failed you in anything and have not supported anyone against you﴾, etc. He said: They were the polytheists of Quraysh with whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made a treaty at the time of al-Hudaybiyah, and four months of their term remained after the Day of Sacrifice. So Allah commanded His Prophet to fulfill for them their covenant until its term, and for those without a covenant until the end of Muharram, and to dissolve the covenant with every party that had one, and commanded him to fight them until they testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and that nothing else from them would be accepted.

16474 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The term for those polytheists who had a covenant before the revelation of "Bara'ah" was four months, from the day the announcement of Bara'ah was made until the tenth of Rabi' al-Akhir, which makes four months. If the polytheists breached their covenant and supported an enemy, then they have no covenant. But if they fulfilled their covenant that was between them and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and did not support an enemy against him, then he was commanded to pay them their covenant and fulfill it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 5:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿So when the sacred months have passed, then kill the polytheists wherever you find them, and capture them, and besiege them, and sit in wait for them at every place of ambush. But if they repent, establish prayer, and give zakah, then let them go on their way. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (9:5)

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His praise be exalted, ﴿So when the sacred months have passed﴾, He means: when they have ended, elapsed and gone out.

* *

It is said of it: "We slakhna (stripped off) the month of such-and-such, nuslakhuhu salkhan and sulukhan," meaning: we came out of it. From this comes their saying: "a skinned sheep" (shah maslukhah), meaning: one stripped of its skin, removed from it. [See the explanation of "al-infisal" (withdrawal) above, 13:260.]

* *

By "the sacred months" is meant Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah and al-Muharram. [See the explanation of "al-ashhur al-hurum" (the sacred months) above, 3:575–579 / 9:456, 466 / 11:91, 94.]

What is intended in this passage is only the passing of Muharram alone, because the proclamation with the Bara'ah (Immunity) was on the Day of the Greater Pilgrimage. It is known that they had not granted respite for all the sacred months, and we have shown the correctness of this earlier. But since it was connected to the two other sacred months before it, and it was the third of them, and they are all connected to one another, it was said: ﴿So when the sacred months have passed﴾. The meaning of the speech is: when the three sacred months have passed, for those who have no covenant, or for those who had a covenant but broke their covenant by backing the enemies against the Messenger of Allah and his Companions, or whose covenant was until another known term.

* *

= ﴿Then kill the polytheists﴾, he says: then kill them. = ﴿wherever you find them﴾, he says: wherever you encounter them on the earth, in the sacred precinct and outside it, in the sacred months and outside the sacred months. = ﴿and capture them﴾, he says: and take them prisoner. = ﴿and besiege them﴾, he says: and prevent them from moving freely in the lands of Islam and from entering Makkah. = ﴿and sit in wait for them at every place of ambush﴾, he says: and lie in wait for them, pursuing them to kill or capture them. = "every place of ambush" means: every path and vantage point.

* *

It is on the pattern "mif'al", from the speaker's saying: "I watched (rasadtu) so-and-so, arsudu-hu rasdan," meaning: I kept watch over him.

* *

﴿But if they repent﴾, he says: if they return from what He forbade them of, namely associating partners with Allah and denying the prophethood of His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), [See the explanation of "repentance" (tawbah) above in the lexical indices, root (t-w-b).] to the Oneness of Allah and sincere worship of Him alone, without the gods and rivals, and acknowledging the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ). = ﴿and establish prayer﴾, he says: and perform what Allah has made obligatory upon them of prayer within its limits. = and give zakah which Allah has made obligatory upon them on their wealth to its people. [See the explanation of "establishing prayer" and "giving zakah" above in the lexical indices, roots (q-w-m) and (a-t-y).] = ﴿then let them go on their way﴾, he says: then leave them to move about in your cities and enter the Sacred House. = ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, toward whoever of His servants repents and turns back to His obedience after having been in disobedience, covering over his sin, merciful to him, that He would not punish him for his past sins before his repentance, after repentance. [See the explanation of "Forgiving" (ghafur) and "Merciful" (rahim) above in the lexical indices, roots (gh-f-r) and (r-h-m).]

* *

We have already mentioned the disagreement of those who differed concerning those who were granted respite until the end of the sacred months.

* *

The people of interpretation said in agreement with what we have said regarding its interpretation.

Mention of those who said that:

16475 – Abd al-A'la ibn Wasil al-Asadi narrated to us, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far al-Razi informed us, from al-Rabi', from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Whoever departs from this world upon sincerity to Allah alone, and worship of Him without associating anything with Him, departs while Allah is pleased with him. He said: Anas also said: It is the religion of Allah with which the Messengers came and which they conveyed from their Lord, before the chaos of discourses ["haraj al-ahadith" – excessive speech about them, disagreement of those who disagree, and confusion of their voices] and the divergence of desires. The confirmation of this in the Book of Allah, in the last of what Allah revealed, is that Allah said: ﴿If they repent, establish prayer and give zakah, then let them go on their way﴾. He said: Their repentance is the abandonment of idols, the worship of their Lord, the establishment of prayer and the giving of zakah. Then He said in another verse: "But if they repent, establish prayer and give zakah, then they are your brothers in religion" [Surah al-Tawbah: 11].

16476 – Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: ﴿So when the sacred months have passed, then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾, until the end of the verse. Qatadah used to say: Let go the way of those whom Allah has commanded you to let go, for people are of three kinds: a Muslim group upon whom is zakah, a polytheist upon whom is the jizyah, and a combatant who is safe in his trade among the Muslims when he gives the tithe of his wealth.

16477 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿So when the sacred months have passed﴾, and they are the four which I have enumerated for you, meaning: twenty days of Dhu al-Hijjah, Muharram, Safar, the first Rabi', and ten days of the second Rabi'.

* *

Those who held this view said: They were called "the sacred months" because Allah, mighty and majestic, made forbidden to the believers in them the blood of the polytheists, and attacking them except by a righteous cause. [In the printed and manuscript text: "wal-'arḍ lahum," which means "the approach to them."]

Mention of those who said that:

16478 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakr, that he informed him from Mujahid and Amr ibn Shu'ayb regarding His saying: ﴿So when the sacred months have passed﴾, that they are the four of which Allah said: ﴿So travel freely in the land﴾, he said: they are "the sacred ones" (al-Hurum), because they were given security in them so that they might travel through it. 

16479 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿A declaration of immunity from Allah and His Messenger to those with whom you made covenants among the polytheists. So travel freely in the land for four months﴾, he said: A term of four months was set for them, and He disavowed every polytheist. Then He commanded, when those sacred months had passed: ﴿So kill the polytheists wherever you find them, and capture them, and besiege them, and sit in wait for them at every place of ambush﴾, do not leave them to roam the lands or to go out for trade; restrict them afterward. Then He commanded forgiveness: ﴿But if they repent, establish prayer and give zakah, then let them go on their way. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

16480 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿So when the sacred months have passed﴾, meaning: the four which Allah granted as a term to the people of the general covenant among the polytheists, ﴿then kill them wherever you find them, and capture them, and besiege them, and sit in wait for them at every place of ambush﴾, the verse.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 6:

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿And if any one of the polytheists seeks your protection, grant him protection until he hears the words of Allah; then deliver him to his place of safety. That is because they are a people who do not know.﴾ (9:6)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Almighty Allah says to His Prophet: "And if any one of the polytheists, O Muhammad, whom I commanded you to fight and kill after the sacred months have passed, seeks your protection (yastajara) = [and] wants your safe-conduct (yasta'min) in order to hear the words of Allah from you, which is the Qur'an that Allah sent down to him = ﴿then grant him protection﴾, meaning: grant him safe-conduct until he hears the words of Allah and you recite them to him = ﴿then deliver him to his place of safety﴾, meaning: then send him back, after he has heard the words of Allah, if he refuses to become Muslim and does not take warning from what you have recited to him of the words of Allah so as to believe = "to his place of safety", meaning: to where he is safe from you and from those under your obedience, until he reaches his home and his people among the polytheists [[See the explanation of "al-amn" (safety) above, 13:420, note 1, and the references there.]] = ﴿That is because they are a people who do not know﴾, meaning: you do this with them, by giving them safe-conduct so that they may hear the Qur'an, and by returning them to their place of safety when they refuse Islam, because they are a people of ignorance who do not understand any proof from Allah, and do not know what would be theirs by believing in Allah had they believed, nor what burden and sin is upon them by abandoning belief in Allah.

* *

Something similar to what we have said on this has been said by the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil).

Those who said so:

16481 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿And if any one of the polytheists seeks your protection﴾, i.e., from those whom I commanded you to fight, ﴿then grant him protection﴾. [[The report 16481 is from Sirat Ibn Hisham 4:189, and it continues the preceding report no. 16480.]]

16482 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿grant him protection until he hears the words of Allah﴾. As for "the words of Allah", it is the Qur'an.

16483 - Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And if any one of the polytheists seeks your protection, grant him protection﴾. He said: A person comes to you and hears what you say and hears what has been revealed to you; he is secure until he comes to you and hears the words of Allah, and until he reaches his place of safety, where he came from. [[In the printed edition: "haythu ja'a", and the correct reading is from the manuscript.]]

16484 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, similarly.

16485 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Ya'qub related to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out on a campaign, met the enemy, and the Muslims brought out a man from the polytheists and pointed their spears at him. The man said: "Lower your weapons from me, and let me hear the words of Allah!" They said: "Testify that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, and renounce the rivals (al-andad), and disavow al-Lat and al-Uzza!" He said: "Then I call you to witness that I have done so."

16486 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿then deliver him to his place of safety﴾: "If what you recite to him and tell him does not agree with him, then deliver him." He said: "And this is not abrogated."

* *

They differed concerning the ruling of this verse, whether it is abrogated (mansukh) or not abrogated.

Some of them said: It is not abrogated. We have already mentioned the statement of the one who said so.

* *

Others said: It is abrogated.

Those who said so:

16487 - Ahmad ibn Ishaq related to us, saying: Abu Ahmad related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: ﴿So kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ — it was abrogated by: ﴿Then either free them as a favour or take ransom﴾. [Surat Muhammad: 4]

16488 - ...... He said: Sufyan related to us, from al-Suddi, the like of it.

* *

Others said: Rather, His saying ﴿So kill the polytheists﴾ was abrogated by His saying ﴿Then either free them as a favour﴾.

Those who said so:

16489 - Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: Ubayda ibn Sulayman related to us, from Ibn Abi Urwah, from Qatadah: ﴿Until, when you have subdued them, then tighten the bonds﴾ [Surat Muhammad: 4] — it was abrogated by His saying: ﴿So kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view in this matter, in my judgment, is the view of the one who said: "That is not abrogated." We have already shown that the meaning of "naskh" (abrogation) is the negation of a ruling that had been established by another ruling besides it. [[See what Abu Ja'far said on "naskh" repeatedly in the indexes of the book.]] No valid proof has been established that the ruling of Allah concerning the polytheists was obligatory killing in every case, and then abrogated by leaving them alive in exchange for ransom or as an act of grace. Since that is so, and since ransom, grace, and killing have continued to be part of the ruling of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning them from the first war he fought against them, which was from the day of Badr [[In the printed edition: "fa-kana al-fida'", which is an error; the editor did not read the manuscript well.]], it is known that the meaning of the verse is: "So kill the polytheists wherever you find them, and take them captive for killing, or grace, or ransom, and besiege them." And when this is its meaning, what we have said is correct, and not other than it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 7:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿How can there be a covenant with God and with His Messenger for the polytheists, except for those with whom you made a covenant at the Sacred Mosque? So long as they are upright towards you, be upright towards them. Indeed God loves the God-fearing (muttaqin).﴾ (7)

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: How, O believers in God and His Messenger, and in what sense, could there be for the polytheists who are disbelievers in their Lord a covenant and a pact with God and with His Messenger, by which they are to be kept to and left secure, moving freely about the lands? [See the explanation of "covenant" (ʿahd) and "treaty" (muʿahadah) above, p. 132, note 1, and the references there.] What is meant is: they have no covenant, and it is obligatory upon the believers to kill them wherever they find them, except those among them who gave a covenant at the Sacred Mosque. For God, majestic is His praise, commanded the believers to fulfil their covenant to them and to remain upright towards them in it, for as long as they remain upright towards the believers in it.

* *

The people of interpretation differed concerning those meant by His saying: ﴿except those with whom you made a covenant at the Sacred Mosque﴾.

Some said: they are a people from Judhaymah ibn al-Duʾayl.

Mention of those who said this:

16490 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding: ﴿How can there be a covenant with God and with His Messenger for the polytheists, except those with whom you made a covenant at the Sacred Mosque; so long as they are upright towards you, be upright towards them﴾: they are the Banu Judhaymah ibn al-Duʾayl. [Thus it comes here, "Banu Judhaymah ibn al-Duʾayl", and in no. 16491: "Judhaymah of Bakr of Kinanah". I do not know of "Judhaymah" among the "Duʾayl ibn Bakr ibn ʿAbd Manat ibn Kinanah"; rather the "Judhaymah of Kinanah" are: "Banu Judhaymah ibn ʿAmir ibn ʿAbd Manat ibn Kinanah", cousins of the "Duʾayl" and of "Bakr ibn ʿAbd Manat".

The Banu Judhaymah ibn ʿAmir ibn ʿAbd Manat are the people of al-Ghumaysa', upon whom Khalid ibn al-Walid fell after the conquest. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent ʿAli (may God be pleased with him) to rectify the error of Khalid ibn al-Walid, so he paid them the blood-money and the value of what had been seized of their property, to the extent that he paid them even the bowl of a dog. (See Ibn Hisham's Sirah 4: 70–73.)]

16491 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Muhammad ibn ʿAbbad ibn Jaʿfar regarding His saying: ﴿except those among the polytheists with whom you made a covenant﴾: he said: they are Judhaymah of Bakr of Kinanah. [The report 16491: see the earlier note. In the printed edition it read: "Bakr, from Kinanah", and I have confirmed what is in the manuscript.]

16492 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿How can there be for the polytheists﴾, those who were, they and you, under the general covenant, [In the printed edition and manuscript: "were they and you", and I have adopted what is in Ibn Hisham's Sirah.] that you should not frighten them and they should not frighten you within the sacred precinct and in the sacred month [In the printed edition: "that you should not prevent them and they should not prevent you from the Haram", differing from the manuscript, because he did not read it well. The correct reading is that of the manuscript, matching the Sirah.

As for his saying "in the sanctity" (fi al-hurmah), he means in Makkah, the sacred city, and all the rites of the Hajj. It is with a dammah on the ha' and a sukun on the ra'. It derives from "hurmah", that which is not lawful to violate. The lexicographical books have fallen short in establishing the word "hurmah" with this meaning that I have explained, though it is common in their reports with the meaning I mentioned; I have therefore affirmed it there. For this reason the editor supposed that when he wrote "min al-haram", "hurmah" does not come to mean "haram".] = ﴿a covenant with God and with His Messenger, except those with whom you made a covenant at the Sacred Mosque﴾. They are the tribes of Banu Bakr who had entered into the covenant of Quraysh and their pact on the day of Hudaybiyah, up to the term that existed between the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and Quraysh. None broke it except this clan of Quraysh and the Banu al-Duʾayl of Bakr. So He commanded the completion of the covenant for those of the Banu Bakr who had not broken their covenant, up to its term = ﴿So long as they are upright towards you﴾, the verse. [The report 16492: Ibn Hisham's Sirah 4: 189, continuing the earlier report no. 16481.]

* *

Others said: they are Quraysh.

Mention of those who said this:

16493 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn ʿAbbas said regarding His saying: ﴿except those with whom you made a covenant at the Sacred Mosque﴾: they are Quraysh.

16494 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿except those with whom you made a covenant at the Sacred Mosque﴾, meaning: the people of Makkah.

16495 - Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿except those with whom you made a covenant at the Sacred Mosque﴾, he says: they are a people between whom and the Prophet (ﷺ) there was a term, and it is not befitting for a polytheist to enter the Sacred Mosque, nor to give the jizyah to the Muslims. ﴿So long as they are upright towards you, be upright towards them﴾, meaning: the people of the covenant among the polytheists.

16496 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿except those with whom you made a covenant at the Sacred Mosque; so long as they are upright towards you, be upright towards them﴾: he said: these are Quraysh. The months that were set for them have been abrogated, and they betrayed them and did not remain upright, as God said. So a term of four months was set for them after the conquest, in which they might choose their affair: either to become Muslims, or to go to whatever lands they wished. He said: They embraced Islam before the four months, and before killing. [In the printed edition and manuscript: "wa-qabla wa-qabla", which has no sense; but in the manuscript it is unpointed, and the correct reading, God willing, is what I have adopted.]

16497 - Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah: ﴿except those with whom you made a covenant at the Sacred Mosque; so long as they are upright towards you, be upright towards them﴾, he said: it is the day of Hudaybiyah, [In the printed edition: "they are the people of Judhaymah", which is utterly corrupt. In the manuscript: "they are the day of Hudaybiyah", and the correct reading is what I have adopted. For when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) wrote the truce between himself and Quraysh in the year of Hudaybiyah, the Banu Bakr ibn ʿAbd Manat leapt forward saying: "We are within the pact and covenant of Quraysh", and Khuzaʿah leapt forward saying: "We are within the pact and covenant of Muhammad" (Ibn Hisham's Sirah 3: 332). Then after a while Banu Bakr and Quraysh combined against Khuzaʿah, who were allies of the Messenger of God, and that was one of the causes requiring the march to Makkah and its conquest. This is what the whole report indicates.] He said: they did not remain upright; they broke their covenant, that is, they aided the Banu Bakr, Quraysh's allies, against Khuzaʿah, the allies of the Prophet (ﷺ). [That is "his ally" (hilfuhu), meaning his confederate, with whom he has a covenant.]

* *

Others said: they are a people from Khuzaʿah.

Mention of those who said this:

16498 - Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿except those with whom you made a covenant at the Sacred Mosque﴾, he said: the people of the covenant from Khuzaʿah.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The view nearest to correctness in my judgment among these sayings is the view of him who said: they are some of the Banu Bakr of Kinanah, of those who remained upon their covenant, and had not entered into the breaking of what existed between the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and Quraysh of the covenant with Quraysh on the day of Hudaybiyah, when they broke it with their support of their allies, the Banu al-Duʾayl, against the allies of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) from Khuzaʿah.

* *

I say this view is the nearest of the sayings to correctness, because God commanded His Prophet and the believers to complete the covenant for those with whom they had made a covenant at the Sacred Mosque, so long as they remained upright in their covenant. We have shown that these verses were proclaimed by ʿAli in the ninth year of the Hijrah, one year after the conquest of Makkah. At that time there was no disbelieving Quraysh or Khuzaʿah in Makkah between whom and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) there was a covenant, so as to be commanded to keep faith with them as long as they remained upright in their covenant, for whoever of them was among the inhabitants of Makkah had already broken the covenant and been warred against before the revelation of these verses.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed God loves the God-fearing (muttaqin)﴾, its meaning is: indeed God loves whoever fears God and watches over Him in performing His obligations, fulfilling His covenant with those with whom he has made a covenant, avoiding His disobedience, and abstaining from betraying the covenants of those with whom he has made one.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 8:**

**On the interpretation of His words, ﴿How (can there be a covenant), when if they gain the upper hand over you, they will not observe regarding you any kinship tie or pact? They please you with their mouths, but their hearts refuse, and most of them are defiant wrongdoers﴾:**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His words, may His praise be exalted, He means: How can there be a covenant or pact for these polytheists, who broke their covenant, or for those among them who have no covenant with you, O believers, when ﴿if they gain the upper hand over you﴾, that is, overcome you, ﴿they will not observe regarding you any kinship tie or pact﴾.

* *

He suffices with "how" (kayfa) as an indication of the meaning of the speech, because what is intended by it has already been mentioned before it. This is what the Arabs do: when they repeat the particle after its meaning has passed, they permit omitting the verb, as the poet said: [[He is Ka'b ibn Sa'd al-Ghanawi.]]

*"You two told me that death is only in the towns, / so how (can it be), when this is a hillock and a sand dune?"* [[Al-Asma'iyyat: 99; Tabaqat Fuhul al-Shu'ara': 176; Amali al-Qali: 151; Jamharat Ash'ar al-'Arab: 135; and Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra': 1:424, and many others. It is among the most famous and noble elegies. Ka'b ibn Sa'd had a brother called Abu al-Mughawwar, who took up residence in a town where there was plague. They advised him to flee with his brother from the plague-stricken land, so that he might escape the calamities of death. But when he took him out into the desert, his brother died, and he grieved over him with the grief of a noble Arab.]]

Thus the verb after "how" was omitted, because what is meant after it has already been mentioned before it. The meaning of the speech is: "How could death be in the towns, when this is a hillock and a sand dune, in which none escapes death?"

* *

The commentators differed concerning the interpretation of His words, ﴿they will not observe regarding you any kinship tie or pact﴾.

Some of them said: its meaning is, "they will not observe God regarding you, nor any covenant."

Those who said this:

16499. Ibn Wakf' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿they will not observe regarding a believer any kinship tie or pact﴾ [Surat al-Tawbah: 10]: He said: "God."

16500. Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Sulayman, from Abu Mijlaz, regarding His words, ﴿they will not observe regarding a believer any kinship tie or pact﴾: He said: It is like His saying "Jibra'il," "Mika'il," "Israfil," as if he were saying: they add "Jabr," "Mika," and "Israf" to "Il," [[In the manuscript: "as if he were saying: yudaf Jabr," and in the manuscript also: "Jabr yudaf Jabr..." And in the manuscript also "Sraf" without an alif.]] meaning "servant of God." ﴿They will not observe regarding a believer any kinship tie or pact﴾, as if he were saying: they will not observe God.

16501. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to me, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿any kinship tie or pact﴾: They will not observe God, nor anything else.

* *

Others said: "al-Il" means kinship.

Those who said this:

16502. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words: ﴿they will not observe regarding a believer any kinship tie or pact﴾: He says: kinship and no covenant. And regarding His words: ﴿if they gain the upper hand over you, they will not observe regarding you any kinship tie or pact﴾: He said: "al-Il" means kinship, and "al-dhimma" means covenant.

16503. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿they will not observe regarding you any kinship tie or pact﴾: "al-Il" is kinship, and "al-dhimma" is covenant, meaning the people of covenant among the polytheists; He says: their pact.

16504. Ibn Wakf' narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiya and 'Abda narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: "al-Il" is kinship. [[Report 16504: In the printed edition: "from Hawshab, from al-Dahhak," differing from the manuscript; the manuscript is the correct version, and this chain has passed many times.]]

16505. Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from Salama ibn Kuhayl, from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿they will not observe regarding a believer any kinship tie or pact﴾: He said: "al-Il" is kinship, and "al-dhimma" is covenant.

16506. It was narrated from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿they will not observe regarding a believer any kinship tie or pact﴾: "al-Il" is kinship, and "al-dhimma" is the solemn pact.

16507. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿How (can there be a covenant), when if they gain the upper hand over you﴾: the polytheists ﴿will not observe regarding you﴾: covenant, nor kinship, nor solemn pact.

* *

Others said: its meaning is "the oath."

Those who said this:

16508. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿they will not observe regarding you any kinship tie or pact﴾: He said: "al-Il" is the oath, and "al-dhimma" is the covenant.

* *

Others said: "al-Il" is the covenant, but it was repeated because the two wordings differ, even though their meaning is one.

Those who said this:

16509. Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿il﴾: He said: a covenant.

16510. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: ﴿they will not observe regarding you any kinship tie or pact﴾: He said: they will not observe regarding you a covenant or a pact. He said: One of the two words is like its companion, like the pattern of "Ghafur" and "Rahim." He said: The word is one, but it is divided. He said: And the covenant is the "dhimma."

16511. Ibn Wakf' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from his father, from Khusayf, from Mujahid: ﴿and pact﴾: He said: the covenant.

16512. al-Harith narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Qays narrated to us, from Khusayf, from Mujahid: ﴿and pact﴾: He said: "al-dhimma" is the covenant.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these opinions is to say: God, may He be mentioned, informed about these polytheists whom He commanded His Prophet and the believers to kill after the sacred months had passed, and to besiege them and lie in wait for them at every place of ambush: that if they gained the upper hand over the believers, they would not observe "il" regarding them.

"Al-Il" is a term that comprises three meanings: covenant, pact, oath, and kinship, and it also means "God." Since the word encompasses these three meanings, and God did not single out one meaning from among them over another, the correct view is that it be generalized, just as He, may His praise be exalted, generalized its three meanings. So it is said: they will not observe regarding a believer God, nor kinship, nor covenant, nor solemn pact.

As evidence that it can mean "kinship," there is the saying of Ibn Muqbil:

*"The people have been corrupted by degenerate successors who came after them, / they severed the il and the roots of the womb."* [[From scattered verses, which I did not find collected in one place, and this verse I also did not find elsewhere. "Khuluf" is the plural of "khalf" (with fatha and then sukun), which is the remnant of evil and the wicked who follow those who preceded them. In the manuscript: "akhlafu" with an alif, and the correct reading is what is in the printed edition. "Al-a'raq" is the plural of "irq," and the irq of everything is its root from which it is established. It is said of it: "Its roots of good and roots of evil have overtaken him."]] meaning: they severed kinship. And the saying of Hassan ibn Thabit:

*"By your life, your il among Quraysh / is like the il of a young camel from the young of an ostrich."* [[His Diwan: 407; and al-Lisan (a-l-l). From verses in which he satirized Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib ibn Hashim, the cousin of the Messenger (ﷺ) and his foster brother, who was among those who resembled the Messenger of God (ﷺ). Abu Sufyan was among those who harmed the Prophet (ﷺ), mocked him, and harmed the Muslims; Hassan rose up against him and took from him everything he took. Then he embraced Islam at the conquest of Mecca, witnessed Hunayn, stood firm with those who stood firm with the Prophet of God, and continued holding the bridle of the mule of the Messenger of God, restraining it while the Messenger of God urged it on toward the unbelievers. Then Abu Sufyan, after that, did not lift his head toward the Messenger of God out of shame before him.

But among Hassan's satire against him, after the verse, is: *"For if you go to Quraysh / like a she-camel's fawn wandering in search of its mother,*

*and you are attached to them as an unworthy hybrid / as the slices are attached to the ... ,* [the rest]

*So do not boast of a people you are not of, / and do not be like the base ones, the Banu Hisham."*

"Al-Saqb" is the young of a she-camel at the moment of its birth. "Al-Ra'l" is the young of the ostrich. He means: your kinship among Quraysh is only like the kinship of the foal of the ostrich!]]

As for its meaning when it means "covenant," it is the saying of the speaker: [[I do not know who said it.]]

*"We found them liars in their il, / but the one with il and covenant does not lie."*

* *

Some of those who are attributed to knowledge of the speech of the Arabs among the Basrans have claimed that "il," "covenant," "solemn pact," and "oath" are one thing, and that "dhimma" in this place means the observance of one who has no covenant, and its plural is "dhimam." [[This is Abu 'Ubayda in Majaz al-Qur'an, 1:253.]]

* *

Ibn Ishaq used to say: By this verse is meant the people of the general covenant.

16513. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿How (can there be a covenant), when if they gain the upper hand over you﴾, that is: the polytheists who have no covenant until a term, from the people of the general covenant ﴿will not observe regarding you any kinship tie or pact﴾. [[Report 16513: Sirat Ibn Hisham 4:189; it follows the previous report numbered 16492.]]

* *

As for His words, ﴿They please you with their mouths﴾, He means: they give you, with their tongues, speech contrary to what they conceal for you in their souls of enmity and hatred [[See the interpretation of "Hatred has appeared from their mouths" 7:145-147; "they say with their mouths" 7:378; and "they said, 'We believe' with their mouths" 10:301-308.]] ﴿but their hearts refuse﴾, that is: their hearts refuse to submit to you, to confirm what they show you with their tongues. He, may His praise be exalted, warns the believers of their affair, and urges them to kill them and exterminate them wherever they are found in the land of God, and not to fall short in harming them with everything they are able to do. ﴿And most of them are defiant wrongdoers﴾, He says: most of them violate your covenant, break it, disbelieve in their Lord, and depart from His obedience. [[See the interpretation of "al-fisq" in the previous language indexes (f-s-q).]]

The discussion of His saying: ﴿They have bartered away the signs of God for a small price, and have barred [others] from His way. Evil indeed is what they have been doing.﴾ (9)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: His saying, may His praise be exalted, means: These polytheists, whom God has commanded you, O believers, to kill wherever you find them, have purchased, by abandoning their following of the proofs God presented against them from His evidences, a small gain, a little of the goods of this world. [[See the explanation of "ishtara" (to purchase, to barter) in what has preceded, 10:344, note 2, and the references there.

= And the explanation of "al-ayat" (the signs) in what has preceded in the language indexes, under (ayy).

= And the explanation of "al-thaman al-qalil" (a small price) in what has preceded, 10:344, note 2, and the references there.]]

* *

That is because they, as has been reported of them, had broken the covenant that existed between them and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) by means of a meal that Abu Sufyan ibn Harb had fed them.

16514 - Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿They have bartered away the signs of God for a small price﴾, he said: Abu Sufyan ibn Harb fed his allies and left the allies of Muhammad (ﷺ).

16515 - al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and have barred [others] from His way﴾, its meaning is: they prevented people from entering Islam, and they sought to turn the Muslims away from their religion [[See the explanation of "al-sadd" (barring, hindering) in what has preceded, 13:581, note 2, and the references there.

= And the explanation of "sabil Allah" (the way of God) in what has preceded in the language indexes, under (sabl).]] = ﴿Evil indeed is what they have been doing.﴾ His saying, may His praise be exalted, means: Indeed, these polytheists whose attributes have been described, their deed that they were doing was evil, in their purchasing disbelief in exchange for faith, and error in exchange for guidance, and their barring from the way of God those who believed in God and His Messenger, or those who wished to believe. [[See the explanation of "saa" (was evil) in what has preceded, 13:275, note 2, and the references there.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 10:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿They do not observe regarding a believer any pact of kinship or covenant. And those are the transgressors﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: These polytheists whom I have commanded you, O believers, to kill wherever you find them, do not show restraint regarding the killing of a believer, if they were to gain power over him. ﴿Any pact of kinship or covenant﴾ means: so do not spare them, O believers, just as they do not spare you if they gain power over you [[See the explanation of "il" and "dhimma" above, pp. 145–149.]]. ﴿And those are the transgressors﴾ means: those who exceed the limits against you, going beyond what is lawful for them to what is not, through wrongdoing and aggression. [[See the explanation of "i'tida'" above, 13:182, footnote 2, and the references there.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 11:

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿But if they repent, establish prayer, and give zakat, then they are your brothers in religion. And We detail the verses for a people who know.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, mighty is His praise, says: If these polytheists whom I have commanded you, O believers, to kill, return from their disbelief and their associating others with Allah, to belief in Him and His Messenger, and turn in obedience to Him, ﴿and establish prayer﴾, the prescribed prayer, performing it within its limits, ﴿and give zakat﴾, the obligatory alms, to its rightful recipients [[See the explanation of "repentance" (tawbah), "establishing prayer" and "giving zakat" in the lexical indexes under (t-w-b), (q-w-m), and (a-t-y).]], ﴿then they are your brothers in religion﴾, meaning: they are your brothers in the religion which Allah has commanded you, which is Islam. ﴿And We detail the verses﴾, meaning: and We make clear the proofs and evidences of Allah upon His creation [[See the explanation of "tafsil" (detailing) earlier, 13:252, footnote 1, and the references there. And the explanation of "ayat" (verses) in the lexical index under (a-y-y).]], ﴿for a people who know﴾, what has been made clear to them, so We explain it to them in detail, unlike the ignorant who do not comprehend Allah's clarification and His firm verses.

* *

Similar to what we have said on this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of those who said that:

16516 – Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿But if they repent, establish prayer, and give zakat, then they are your brothers in religion﴾, meaning: if they abandon al-Lat and al-Uzza, and testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah ﴿then they are your brothers in religion. And We detail the verses for a people who know.﴾

16517 – Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, from Layth, from a man, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿But if they repent, establish prayer, and give zakat﴾, he said: This verse has made sacred the blood of the People of the Qiblah.

16518 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: Prayer and zakat were made obligatory together, not separated. And he recited: ﴿But if they repent, establish prayer, and give zakat, then they are your brothers in religion﴾, and he refused to accept prayer without zakat. And he said: May Allah have mercy on Abu Bakr, how well he understood.

16519 – Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sharik narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Ubaydah, from Abdullah, who said: You were commanded to establish prayer and give zakat, and whoever does not give zakat has no prayer.

* *

It has been said: ﴿fa-ikhwanukum﴾ is in the nominative as the predicate of an implied subject, "fa-hum ikhwanukum" (then they are your brothers), since their mention had preceded, as He said: ﴿And if you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in religion﴾ [Surah al-Ahzab: 5], meaning: then they are your brothers in religion. [[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1:425.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 12:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And if they break their oaths after their covenant and attack your religion, then fight the leaders of disbelief; indeed, they have no oaths, so that they may desist.﴾ (9:12)

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: If these polytheists whom you made covenant with, from Quraysh, break their covenants after they contracted with you that they would not fight you nor assist anyone of your enemies against you [[See the explanation of "nakath" (breaking) above, 13:73.]] = ﴿and attack your religion﴾, meaning: and they disparage your religion, Islam, slandering it and defaming it [[In the printed edition: "fathalamuhu" (they corrupted it), but the correct reading from the manuscript is as given.]] = ﴿then fight the leaders of disbelief﴾, meaning: then fight the chiefs of disbelief in God [[See the explanation of "imam" (leader) above, 3:18.]] = ﴿indeed, they have no oaths﴾, meaning: indeed, the chiefs of disbelief have no covenant [[See the explanation of "yamin" (oath) above, 8:272, 273, 281.]] = ﴿so that they may desist﴾, meaning: so that they may cease from attacking your religion and from assisting against you. [[See the explanation of "intiha'" (desisting) above, 13:543, note 3, and the references there.]]

* *

In accordance with what we have said on this, the people of interpretation said, though they differed regarding those intended by "leaders of disbelief."

Some of them said: They are Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, 'Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, and their counterparts. Hudhayfah used to say: "It has not yet come to its people."

Mention of those who said they are those I have named:

16520- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And if they break their oaths after their covenant﴾, to: ﴿so that they may desist﴾, he meant the people of covenant among the polytheists; He named them "leaders of disbelief," and they are so. God says to His Prophet: If they break the covenant that is between you and them, then fight them, the leaders of disbelief, who have no oaths [[I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is purely correct; the printed edition corrected it thus, as it supposed: "fa-qatil a'immat al-kufr li-annahum la aymana lahu," adding and altering!!.]] = ﴿so that they may desist﴾.

16521- Harun related to us... Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And if they break their oaths after their covenant﴾, to: ﴿they may desist﴾; among the leaders of disbelief were Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, Umayyah ibn Khalaf, 'Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, Abu Sufyan, Suhayl ibn 'Amr, and they were the ones who plotted to expel him.

16522- Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿leaders of disbelief﴾: Abu Sufyan, Abu Jahl, Umayyah ibn Khalaf, Suhayl ibn 'Amr, and 'Utbah ibn Rabi'ah.

16523- Ibn WakI' and Ibn Bashshar related to us = Ibn WakI' said: Ghundar related to us = and Ibn Bashshar said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us =, from Shu'bah, from Abu Bishr, from Mujahid: ﴿then fight the leaders of disbelief; indeed, they have no oaths﴾, he said: Abu Sufyan is among them.

16524- Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And if they break their oaths﴾, to: ﴿they may desist﴾, these are Quraysh. He means: if they break their covenant which they made on Islam, and attack it, then fight them. [[In the printed edition: "fa-qatilu-hum" (then fight them), but I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

16525- It was narrated from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿then fight the leaders of disbelief﴾, meaning the heads of the polytheists, the people of Makkah.

16526- Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: ﴿then fight the leaders of disbelief﴾: Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, Umayyah ibn Khalaf, 'Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, Suhayl ibn 'Amr, and they are the ones who broke the covenant of God and plotted to expel the Messenger. It is not, by God, as those who interpret it, the people of doubtful innovations, fabrications against God and His Book, have construed it. [[" Al-Firan" (with kasra then fatha) is the plural of "firyah," meaning falsehood. By this he means the Kharijites, who use this verse as evidence for fighting those who oppose them among the people of the qiblah, and who thereby deem their blood and property lawful.]]

* *

Mention of the report from Hudhayfah with what we have mentioned from him:

16527- Ibn WakI' related to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, from al-A'mash, from Zayd ibn Wahb, from Hudhayfah: ﴿then fight the leaders of disbelief﴾, he said: Those of this verse have not yet been fought. [[Report 16527: Zayd ibn Wahb al-Hamdani al-Juhani, a Successor (tabi'i) of the mukhadram category, who heard 'Umar, 'Abd Allah, Hudhayfah, and Abu al-Darda'. The group (al-jama'ah) narrated from him. Passed as number 4222.

This report was narrated by al-Bukhari at length (Fath 8:243), with a different wording, by way of Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Zayd ibn Wahb who said: "We were with Hudhayfah..."

See the following report and the one after it.]]

16528- Ahmad ibn Ishaq related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Habib ibn Hassan related to us, from Zayd ibn Wahb who said: I was with Hudhayfah, when he recited this verse: ﴿then fight the leaders of disbelief﴾, and said: Those of this verse have not yet been fought. [[Report 16528: a repetition of the preceding report; see its takhrij there. "Habib ibn Hassan" is "Habib ibn Abi al-Ashras," and he is "Habib ibn Abi Hilal," munkar al-hadith, abandoned. Ibn Hibban said: "Extremely munkar al-hadith; he had fallen in love with a Christian woman, and it was said that he became a Christian and married her. As for his going to the church for her sake, that is true." Yahya ibn Ma'in said: "He had two Christian slave-girls, and he used to go with them to the church."

Translated in al-Kabir 1/2/311, Mizan al-I'tidal 1:209, 211, and Lisan al-Mizan 2:167, 170.]]

16529- Abu al-Sa'ib related to me, saying: Al-A'mash related to us, from Zayd ibn Wahb who said: Hudhayfah recited: ﴿then fight the leaders of disbelief﴾, and said: Those of this verse have not yet been fought. [[Report 16529: a repetition of the two preceding reports.]]

16530- Ibn WakI' related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Sufyan and Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Silah ibn Zufar: ﴿indeed, they have no oaths﴾, they have no covenant. [[Report 16530: Silah ibn Zufar al-'Absi is a trustworthy Successor. The group narrated from him; he is mentioned in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 2/2/322, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/446.

See number 16533, raised to 'Ammar ibn Yasir, and number 16534, raised to Hudhayfah.]]

16531- Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿And if they break their oaths﴾, he said: Their covenant.

16532- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And if they break their oaths﴾, their covenant which they made on Islam.

16533- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Silah, from 'Ammar ibn Yasir, regarding His saying: ﴿they have no oaths﴾, he said: They have no covenant. [[Report 16533: a repetition of report 16530, raised to 'Ammar ibn Yasir. "Silah" is Silah ibn Zufar al-'Absi as before.]]

16534- Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd al-Muharibi related to me, saying: Abu al-Ahwas related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Silah ibn Zufar, from Hudhayfah regarding His saying: ﴿then fight the leaders of disbelief; indeed, they have no oaths﴾, he said: They have no covenant. [[Report 16534: a repetition of the two preceding reports, raised to Hudhayfah.]]

* *

As for "nakth" (breaking), its origin is annulment; it is said of it: "So-and-so broke the strands of his rope," if he unravelled them. [[See the explanation of "nakth" above, p. 153, note 2, and the references there.]]

* *

And "al-ayman" is the plural of "al-yamin" (oath). [[See the explanation of "yamin" above, p. 154, note 3, and the references there.]]

* *

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of His saying: ﴿indeed, they have no oaths﴾.

The reciters of the Hijaz, Iraq, and others recited it: ﴿إِنَّهُمْ لا أَيْمَانَ لَهُمْ﴾, with a fatha on the alif of "aymaan," meaning: they have no covenants, according to what we have mentioned of the interpretation of the people of interpretation regarding it.

* *

And it is related of al-Hasan al-Basri that he used to recite it: ﴿إِنَّهُمْ لا إِيمَانَ لَهُمْ﴾, with a kasra on the alif, meaning: they have no Islam.

* *

It may also be directed toward this recitation a meaning other than this. That is, that by reciting it thus he intended: they have no security = that is, do not grant them safe-conduct, but kill them wherever you find them = as though he intended the verbal noun from the saying of the speaker: "I granted him security, so I grant him security (uminuhu) with faith (iman)." [[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1:425.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct reading in this matter, which I do not permit reciting otherwise, is the recitation of whoever recited with a fatha on the "alif," not a kasra, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on reciting it so, and the rejection of its opposite; and due to the consensus of the people of interpretation on what I have mentioned, that its interpretation is: they have no covenant; and "al-aymaan," which carries the meaning of covenant, can only be with a fatha on the "alif," because it is the plural of "yamin," which was upon a pact that existed between those who had made a truce.
