**The interpretation of His saying:** ﴿Will you not fight a people who broke their oaths and resolved to expel the Messenger, and it was they who began [the hostility] against you the first time? Do you fear them? Yet God has more right that you should fear Him, if you are believers.﴾ (9:13)

Abu Ja'far said: He, may He be exalted, says to the believers in God and His Messenger, urging them to fight their enemies among the polytheists: ﴿Will you not fight﴾, O believers, ﴿these polytheists who broke the covenant between you and them, who attacked your religion, and who backed your enemies against you?﴾ [[See the explanation of "al-nakth" (breaking of oaths), p. 157, note 2, and the references there.]] = ﴿and resolved to expel the Messenger﴾ from among them, so that you would expel him. [[See the explanation of "al-hamm" (resolve) above, 9:199 / 10:100.]] = ﴿and it was they who began [the hostility] against you the first time﴾, by fighting. That refers to their act on the day of Badr. It has also been said that it refers to their fighting the allies of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) from Khuza'ah. = ﴿Do you fear them?﴾ That is, do you fear them for your own selves, so that you abandon fighting them out of fear for yourselves from them? [[See the explanation of "al-khashyah" (fear) above, 10, 344, note 1, and the references there.]] = ﴿Yet God has more right that you should fear Him﴾, meaning: God has more right over you that you fear His punishment for abandoning jihad against them, and that you beware of His wrath upon you, than these polytheists, who possess no harm or benefit for you except by God's permission. = ﴿if you are believers﴾, meaning: if you acknowledge that the fear of God is more fitting for you than fear of these polytheists for your own selves.

* *

Those of the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

16535. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: ﴿Will you not fight a people who broke their oaths﴾, after their covenant = ﴿and resolved to expel the Messenger﴾, meaning: they resolved to expel him, so they expelled him = ﴿and it was they who began [the hostility] against you the first time﴾, by fighting.

16536. Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and it was they who began [the hostility] against you the first time﴾: He said: It is the fighting of Quraysh against the allies of Muhammad (ﷺ).

16537. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, similarly.

16538. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

16539. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: God commanded His Messenger to fight the polytheists from among those who broke the special covenant [[In the printed edition and the manuscript the word "al-khass" (special) is omitted; I have restored it from Ibn Hisham.]] and those of the general covenant who were among the people, after the four months which He set as a term for them, unless one of them transgresses therein and is thereby killed for his hostility. [[In the printed edition: "illa an ya'udu fiha 'ala dinihim fayuqbal ba'd thumma qal", which is a meaningless phrase. In the manuscript: "illa an ya'udu fiha 'ala dinihim fayuqtal bi'da'ihi, fa-qal", in which there is severe corruption. The word "ya'udu" is a corruption of "ya'du", and "'ala dinihim" should be "'ad minhum" (one of them transgresses), and the text has been badly miscopied. The correct reading is from the Sirah of Ibn Hisham.]] Then he said: ﴿Will you not fight a people who broke their oaths and resolved to expel the Messenger﴾, to His saying: ﴿and God is Aware of what you do﴾.

[Narration: 16539 – Sirat Ibn Hisham 4: 191. It follows the earlier narration numbered 16377.]

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Fight them, and Allah will punish them at your hands, and disgrace them, and give you victory over them, and heal the breasts of a believing people﴾ (9:14).

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, He says: Fight them, O believers in Allah and His Messenger, these polytheists who broke their oaths and violated their covenants between you and them, and expelled the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from among them. ﴿Allah will punish them at your hands﴾, meaning: Allah will kill them at your hands. ﴿And disgrace them﴾, meaning: and humiliate them through capture and subjugation [[See the explanation of "al-ikhza" (disgracing) above, p. 112, footnote 1, and the references there.]]. ﴿And give you victory over them﴾, meaning: and grant you triumph and dominance over them. ﴿And heal the breasts of a believing people﴾, meaning: and cure the ailment of the breasts of a people who believe in Allah and His Messenger, by killing these polytheists at your hands, and by your humiliating and subduing them. That ailment is the resentment they held in their hearts against them because of the harm and hardship they inflicted upon them.

* *

It has also been said: By His words ﴿and heal the breasts of a believing people﴾, Allah meant the breasts of Khuza'ah, the allies of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. This is because the Quraysh had broken the covenant between them and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ by aiding Bakr against them.

Mention of those who said this:

16540. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Waki' narrated to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, regarding this verse: ﴿and heal the breasts of a believing people﴾, he said: Khuza'ah.

16541. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Muhammad al-'Anqazi narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi: ﴿and heal the breasts of a believing people﴾, he said: Khuza'ah; He heals their breasts from Bani Bakr.

16542. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, the like of it.

16543. Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿and heal the breasts of a believing people﴾, Khuza'ah, the allies of Muhammad ﷺ.

16544. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Raja' narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, from 'Abd Allah ibn Kathir, from Mujahid: ﴿and heal the breasts of a believing people﴾, he said: the allies of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from Khuza'ah.

16545. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 15:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And He will remove the rage of their hearts. And Allah turns in forgiveness to whom He wills. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, mighty and majestic is He, says: And He will remove the grief (wajd) from the hearts of these believing people of Khuza'ah, [[See the explanation of "al-idhhab" (removal) above, 12:126, note 3, and the references there.]] over these people who broke their oaths from among the polytheists, and remove their distress and anguish caused by the grief they felt over them, by their (the Banu Bakr's) assistance to them against the Khuza'ah. [[See the explanation of "al-ghayz" (rage) above, 7:215.]] As related:

16546. Ibn WakI' related to me, saying: Amr ibn Muhammad al-Anqazi narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And He will remove the rage of their hearts﴾: when the Banu Bakr killed them, and Quraysh aided them.

16547. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, the like of it, except that he said: and Quraysh aided them against them. [[In the printed edition: "wa a'anahum" (and aided them); in the manuscript: "wa a'lasahum"; the correct reading is what is established here.]]

* *

As for His words: ﴿And Allah turns in forgiveness to whom He wills﴾, it is a predicate of a new clause (khabar mubtada'), which is why it is in the nominative (raf'). The three imperatives before it are apocopated (majzum) in the manner of conditional (conditional-response) construction, as if He had said: "Fight them, for if you fight them, Allah will punish them at your hands, and disgrace them, and grant you victory over them." Then He began anew, saying: ﴿And Allah turns in forgiveness to whom He wills﴾, because fighting does not necessitate repentance for them from Allah, whereas it necessitates for them punishment from Allah, disgrace, the healing of the hearts of the believers, and the removal of the rage of their hearts. So that was made a conditional and a response (shart and jaza') upon fighting, while fighting did not necessitate repentance, so the statement was begun with it and put in the nominative.

* *

The meaning of the speech: Allah bestows His favour upon whom He wills of His disbelieving servants, and inclines him to repentance through His guidance of him; ﴿And Allah is Knowing﴾ of the inner secrets of His servants, and of who is fit for repentance so that He turns to him, and who among them is not fit for it so that He forsakes him; ﴿Wise﴾ in turning His servants from a state of disbelief to a state of belief by guiding whom He guides to that, and from a state of belief to a state of disbelief by forsaking those among them who turn away from His obedience and His monotheism, and other matters concerning them. [[See the explanation of "tab" (repent), "alim" (knowing) and "hakim" (wise) in the earlier lexical indexes (tawb), (ilm), (hukm).]]

The Discourse on the Interpretation of His Words: ﴿Or did you think that you would be left alone, while Allah has not yet known those among you who strove and did not take, besides Allah and His Messenger and the believers, any intimate (waliyjah); and Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾ (9:16)

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, mentioning to the believers whom He had commanded to fight these polytheists, who had broken their covenant that was between them and Him, by His saying: ﴿Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands﴾ (9:14), and so on, urging them to strive against them: ﴿Or did you think﴾, O believers [[See the explanation of "ḥasiba" previously, 12:388, note 3, and the references there.]] = that Allah would leave you without a trial by which He tests you, and without an examination by which He tests you, so that He may know the truthful among you in his religion from the liar in it = ﴿while Allah has not yet known those who strove﴾, meaning: Did you think you would be left without a test by which He makes known those of His allies who strive among you in His way, from those who neglect the command of Allah in that and are remiss? [[See the explanation of "jihad" previously, p. 77, note 2, and the references there.]] = ﴿and who did not take, besides Allah and His Messenger﴾, meaning: while Allah has not yet known those among you who strove, and those who did not take, besides Allah, or besides His Messenger, or besides the believers = ﴿any intimate (waliyjah)﴾.

* *

It is that which enters into the inside of something else. It is said of it: "Walaja fulān fī kadhā yalijuhu, fahuwa waliyjah" (a man entered into such-and-such, so he is an intimate). [[In the manuscript: "walaja fī fulān kadhā," and what is in the printed edition is better.]]

* *

What is meant by it in this place is: the inner circle (biṭānah) from among the polytheists. Allah forbade the believers to take as allies from among their enemies, from the polytheists, those to whom they would disclose their secrets = ﴿and Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾, meaning: Allah is All-Aware of what you do, of your taking, besides Allah and besides His Messenger and the believers in Him, allies and an inner circle, after He has already forbidden you from it. That is not hidden from Him, nor is any other of your deeds, and Allah will recompense you for that: if good, then good, and if evil, then evil.

* *

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said the same as what I have said regarding the meaning of "waliyjah."

Mention of those who said that:

16548- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿nor the believers, waliyjah﴾: one who takes him as an intimate from the authority of the polytheists.

16549- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', regarding ﴿waliyjah﴾: he said, "Entered (dakhala)."

16550- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Or did you think that you would be left alone﴾, to His saying: ﴿waliyjah﴾: He refused to leave them without purification (tamhis). And he recited: ﴿Or did you think that you would enter Paradise, while Allah has not yet known those among you who strove﴾ (3:142), and recited: ﴿Or did you think that you would enter Paradise while there has not yet come to you the example of those who passed away before you﴾ (2:214), the verses all of them. [[The beginning of this verse was not in the manuscript or the printed edition; its beginning was "walam ya'tikum..."]] He informed them that He would not leave them until He purifies them and tests them. And he recited: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. Do people think that they will be left alone because they say, "We believe," and they will not be tested?﴾ (29:1-2), meaning, they will not be tested, ﴿And We certainly tested those before them, so Allah will surely make known those who are truthful, and He will surely make known the liars﴾ (29:3). Allah refused except to purify.

16551- Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿waliyjah﴾: he said, "It is disbelief and hypocrisy" = or he said one of the two.

* *

It was said: ﴿Or did you think﴾, and it was not said "a-ḥasibtum," because it is an interrogative inserted in the middle of speech, so "am" was introduced into it to distinguish it from the initial interrogative. I have explained similar instances in more than one place in this book. [[See what has passed in the explanation of "am" at 2:492-494 / 3:97 / 4:287, 288, then see the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:426.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 17:

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah, bearing witness against themselves of disbelief. Those, their deeds have become worthless, and in the Fire they will abide eternally.﴾ (9:17)

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His mention, says: It is not fitting for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah while they bear witness against themselves of disbelief. That is to say: mosques are only maintained for the worship of Allah within them, not for disbelieving in Him. So whoever is a disbeliever in Allah, it is not his place to maintain the mosques of Allah.

* *

As for their bearing witness against themselves of disbelief, it is as follows:

16552 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, who said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words: ﴿It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah, bearing witness against themselves of disbelief﴾, he said: It is not fitting for them to maintain them. As for ﴿bearing witness against themselves of disbelief﴾, a Christian is asked, "What are you?" and he says, "A Christian." The Jew is asked, and he says, "A Jew." The Sabian is asked, and he says, "A Sabian." And the polytheist, when you ask him, "What is your religion?", he says, "A polytheist!" No one would say this except the Arabs.

16553 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, who said: Amr al-'Anqazi narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi: ﴿It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah﴾, he said: He says: It was not fitting for them to maintain them.

16554 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, who said: Amr narrated to us, from Asbat, from al-Suddi: ﴿bearing witness against themselves of disbelief﴾, he said: A Christian is told, "What are you?" and he says, "A Christian." A Jew is told, "What are you?" and he says, "A Jew." A Sabian is told, "What are you?" and he says, "A Sabian."

* *

As for His words: ﴿Those, their deeds have become worthless﴾, He says: their rewards have become null and departed, because they were not for Allah but were for Satan [see the explanation of "habita" (become worthless) earlier at 2:116, note 2, and the references there] = ﴿and in the Fire they will abide eternally﴾, He says: they will remain in it forever, neither living nor dead [see the explanation of "khulud" (abiding eternally) in the earlier language indexes (kh-l-d)].

* *

The readers differed regarding the recitation of His words: ﴿It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah﴾. The majority of readers of Medina and Kufa recited it as ﴿masajid Allah﴾ (mosques of Allah), in the plural. [In the printed edition: "in the plural (al-jam')", but I have retained what is in the manuscript; in this topic and what follows, all of it.]

* *

Some of the Meccan and Basran readers recited it as ﴿masjida Allah﴾ (the mosque of Allah), in the singular, meaning the Sacred Mosque.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: They all agree on the recitation of His words: [Abu Ja'far means that all the readers agree on the recitation of the following verse: "Only those maintain the mosques of Allah," in the plural, without any disagreement among them about this; therefore I have added the complete verse, whereas the printed and manuscript texts read only "mosques of Allah" without "Only those maintain".] ﴿Only those maintain the mosques of Allah﴾, in the plural, because when it is recited thus, it may carry the meaning of both the singular and the plural, for the Arabs sometimes take the singular to mean the plural and the plural to mean the singular, as in their saying: "He is wearing a worn-out garment" [see the Meanings of the Qur'an by al-Farra' 1: 426, 427].

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 18:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Only he who believes in Allah and the Last Day, establishes prayer, gives zakah, and fears none but Allah — it is those who may be among the guided.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is His mention, He says: ﴿Only he who maintains the mosques of Allah﴾, the one who affirms the oneness of Allah and devotes worship to Him alone, ﴿and the Last Day﴾, meaning: the one who believes in Allah's raising of the dead to life from their graves on the Day of Resurrection [[See the explanation of "the Last Day" in the earlier glossary of language (akhar).]] ﴿and establishes prayer﴾, the prescribed prayer, within its limits, and pays zakah, the obligatory charity due upon his wealth, to those to whom Allah has made it obligatory [[See the explanation of "establishing prayer" and "giving zakah" in the earlier glossary of language (qawm), (atā).]] ﴿and fears none but Allah﴾, meaning: he does not dread the punishment of anything for his disobedience to Him, other than Allah [[See the explanation of "khashyah" (fear) earlier, p. 158, note 3, and the references there.]] ﴿then it is those who may be among the guided﴾, meaning: it is fitting for those who have these characteristics that they be, in Allah's sight, among those whom Allah has guided to the truth and to hitting what is right. [[See the explanation of "ʿasā" (may/perhaps) earlier, vol. 13, p. 45, note 1, and the references there, and the explanation of "guidance" (ihtidāʾ) in the earlier glossary of language (hudā).]]

16555 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Only he who maintains the mosques of Allah is one who believes in Allah and the Last Day﴾, meaning: whoever affirms the oneness of Allah and believes in the Last Day, meaning: acknowledges what Allah has sent down. ﴿And establishes prayer﴾, meaning the five daily prayers. ﴿And fears none but Allah﴾, meaning: then he worships none but Allah. He said: ﴿Then it is those who may be among the...﴾, meaning: indeed those are the successful, like His saying to His Prophet: ﴿It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾ [Surah al-Isra: 79], meaning: your Lord will surely raise you to a praiseworthy station, which is the intercession. And every "ʿasā" in the Qur'an is obligatory.

16556 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, he said: Then he mentioned the statement of the Quraysh: "We are the people of the Sanctuary, the providers of the pilgrims, and the maintainers of this House, and no one is better than us!" So He said: ﴿Only he who believes in Allah and the Last Day﴾, meaning: your maintenance is not upon that. ﴿Only he who maintains the mosques of Allah﴾, meaning: whoever maintains them in their rightful manner ﴿who believes in Allah and the Last Day, establishes prayer, gives zakah, and fears none but Allah﴾, those are the ones who maintain them. ﴿It is those who may be among the guided﴾, and "ʿasā" from Allah is binding. [[The report: 16556 - Sirat Ibn Hisham 4: 192, and it follows the earlier report no. 16539.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 19:

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿Do you consider the providing of water for the pilgrims and the maintaining of the Sacred Mosque as equal to [the deeds of] one who believes in God and the Last Day and strives in the way of God? They are not equal in the sight of God, and God does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ (19)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: This is a rebuke from God, exalted is His remembrance, to a people who boasted of the water-providing (al-siqaya) and the custodianship of the House (al-sidana). So He, majestic is His praise, informed them that true merit lies in belief in God and the Last Day and striving in His way, not in what they boasted of, namely the custodianship and the water-providing. [[See the explanation of the terms of this verse in the lexical indices of earlier volumes.]]

* *

This is also what the reports transmitted and the interpretation of the interpreters agree upon.

Those who said this:

16557. Abu al-Walid al-Dimashqi Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salam narrated to me, from his grandfather Abu Salam al-Aswad, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir al-Ansari, who said: I was by the pulpit of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) with a group of his Companions. One of them said: "I would not mind if I did no deed after accepting Islam except giving water to the pilgrims!" Another said: "Rather, the maintaining of the Sacred Mosque!" Another said: "Rather, striving in the way of God is better than what you have said!" Umar ibn al-Khattab (may God be pleased with him) rebuked them and said: "Do not raise your voices by the pulpit of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) — and that was on Friday — but when I have prayed the Friday prayer I will enter upon the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and ask him about what you have differed over." He said: So he did, and God, blessed and exalted, revealed: ﴿Do you consider the providing of water for the pilgrims…﴾ up to His words: ﴿and God does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾

[[The report 16557: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Bakkar al-Qurashi al-Dimashqi, Abu al-Walid, a teacher of al-Tabari, has passed several times, the last being no. 11416.

And al-Walid ibn Muslim al-Qurashi al-Dimashqi, has passed several times, the last being no. 9071; the collectors of the six books narrated from him.

And Mu'awiya ibn Salam ibn Abi Salam Mamtur al-Habashi, Abu Salam al-Dimashqi; the collectors narrated from him. He narrated from his grandfather Abu Salam. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/1/335, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/383.

And Abu Salam al-Aswad, whose name is Mamtur, a trustworthy Successor, has passed as nos. 15654, 15655.

This report was narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (13:25, 26), by way of Abu Tawba, from Mu'awiya ibn Salam, from Zayd ibn Salam, that he heard Abu Salam say: "al-Nu'man ibn Bashir narrated to me," then he narrated it by way of Yahya ibn Hassan, from Mu'awiya, from Zayd, with the same.

Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir 4:131 and attributed it to Abu Dawud, but I could not find it in his Sunan.

al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 3:218 added its attribution to Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh.

It will come with another chain, no. 16560, by another route that is mursal.]]

16558. al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿Do you consider the providing of water for the pilgrims and the maintaining of the Sacred Mosque as equal to one who believes in God and the Last Day﴾. Al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib said when he was taken captive on the Day of Badr: "If you have preceded us in Islam, emigration and striving, we used to maintain the Sacred Mosque, give water to the pilgrims, and free the captives!" ["al-Ani": the captive.] God said: ﴿Do you consider the providing of water for the pilgrims…﴾ up to ﴿the wrongdoing people﴾, meaning that this was in polytheism, and I do not accept what was done in polytheism.

16559. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿Do you consider the providing of water for the pilgrims…﴾ up to ﴿the wrongdoing people﴾. That is because the polytheists said: "The maintaining of God's House and standing over the water-providing is better than one who believes and strives." They used to boast of the Sanctuary and act arrogantly, because they were its people and its maintainers. So God mentioned their arrogance and turning away, and said to the polytheists of the Sanctuary: ﴿My verses were recited to you, but you turned back on your heels, arrogant, talking nonsense about it by night﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 66-67], meaning that they acted arrogantly by the Sanctuary. He said "sāmiran" because they used to converse at night and abandon the Qur'an and the Prophet (ﷺ). So He preferred belief in God and striving alongside the Prophet of God (ﷺ) over the polytheists' maintaining of the House and their standing over the water-providing. Their maintaining of His House and serving it did not benefit them with God while they associated others with Him. God said: ﴿They are not equal in the sight of God, and God does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾, meaning: those who claimed they were the people of maintenance. God named them "wrongdoers" for their polytheism, so the maintenance availed them nothing.

16560. al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, that a man said: "I would not mind if I did no deed after Islam except giving water to the pilgrims!" Another said: "I would not mind if I did no deed after Islam except maintaining the Sacred Mosque!" Another said: "Striving in the way of God is better than what you have said!" Umar rebuked them and said: "Do not raise your voices by the pulpit of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) — and that was on Friday — but when he prays the Friday prayer we will enter upon him!" Then it was revealed: ﴿Do you consider the providing of water for the pilgrims and the maintaining of the Sacred Mosque…﴾ up to ﴿they are not equal in the sight of God﴾.

[[Report 16560: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir al-Ta'i, trustworthy, the collectors narrated from him; he narrated from Zayd ibn Salam ibn Abi Salam, and he related mursal reports from Abu Salam al-Habashi and others; this is from his mursal from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, or from Abu Salam. It has passed as nos. 9189, 11505–11507.]]

16561. al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Amr, from al-Hasan who said: It was revealed concerning Ali, al-Abbas, Uthman, and Shayba, who argued about it. Al-Abbas said: "I see myself only abandoning our water-providing!" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Remain at your water-providing, for in it there is good for you."

16562. ... He said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn Uyayna informed us, from Isma'il, from al-Sha'bi who said: It was revealed concerning Ali and al-Abbas, who argued about it.

16563. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: I was informed from Abu Sakhr who said: I heard Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi say: Talha ibn Shayba of Banu Abd al-Dar, al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib, and Ali ibn Abi Talib boasted. Talha said: "I am the owner of the House; its key is with me; if I wished, I would spend the night in it!" Al-Abbas said: "I am the owner of the water-providing and the one who oversees it, and if I wished I would spend the night in the mosque!" Ali said: "I do not know what you two are saying; I prayed toward the qibla six months before the people, and I am the owner of striving!" So God revealed: ﴿Do you consider the providing of water for the pilgrims and the maintaining of the Sacred Mosque…﴾, the whole verse.

16564. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan who said: When ﴿Do you consider the providing of water for the pilgrims﴾ was revealed, al-Abbas said: "I see myself only abandoning our water-providing!" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Remain at your water-providing, for in it there is good for you."

16565. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi regarding: ﴿Do you consider the providing of water for the pilgrims and the maintaining of the Sacred Mosque as equal to one who believes in God and the Last Day and strives in the way of God? They are not equal in the sight of God﴾. He said: Ali, al-Abbas, and Shayba ibn Uthman boasted. He said to al-Abbas: "I am better than you; I give water to the pilgrims of God's House!" Shayba said: "I maintain God's mosque!" Ali said: "I emigrated with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and strive with him in the way of God!" So God revealed: ﴿Those who believed and emigrated and strove in the way of God…﴾ up to ﴿lasting bliss.﴾

16566. Narrated from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿Do you consider the providing of water for the pilgrims…﴾, the verse: The Muslims turned to al-Abbas and his companions who had been captured on the Day of Badr, reproaching them for polytheism. Al-Abbas said: "By God, we used to maintain the Sacred Mosque, free the captives, screen the House, and give water to the pilgrims!" So God revealed: ﴿Do you consider the providing of water for the pilgrims…﴾, the verse.

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the speech, then, is: Do you consider, O people, the providing of water for the pilgrims and the maintaining of the Sacred Mosque as equal to the faith of one who believes in God and the Last Day and strives in the way of God? "They are not equal" — these and those — and their states and ranks are not equal in God's sight, because God, exalted, accepts no deed without belief in Him and in the Last Day. ﴿And God does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾ means: God does not grant success in righteous deeds to one who is a disbeliever in Him and denies His oneness.

* *

The placing of the noun in the position of the verbal noun in His words ﴿one who believes in God﴾ is because its meaning is known, as the poet said: [[I do not know who said it.]]

By your life, youths are not those whose beards have grown, but youths are every man who is generous.

So he made the predicate of "al-fityan" (youths) the word "an" (that), and this is like saying: "Generosity is only Hatim, and poetry is only Zuhayr."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 20:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Those who believed, emigrated, and struggled in the way of God with their wealth and their selves are greater in rank with God, and those are the victorious﴾ (20).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: This is a judgment from God between the groups of boasters. One of them boasted of providing water (al-siqayah) to pilgrims, another boasted of the custodianship (al-sidanah) of the Ka'bah, and another boasted of faith in God and struggle in His way. Almighty God says: ﴿Those who believed﴾ in God and affirmed His oneness (tawhid) from among the polytheists, ﴿and emigrated﴾ from the homeland of their people [[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1: 427.]], ﴿and struggled﴾ against the polytheists for the religion of God [[See the explanation of "hajara" (emigrated) earlier, p. 81, note 2, and the references there.]], ﴿with their wealth and their selves are greater in rank with God﴾, and higher in station with Him, [[See the explanation of "jahada" (struggled) earlier, p. 163, note 2, and the references there, and the explanation of "sabil Allah" (the way of God) earlier in the language indexes under (s-b-l).]] than the providers of water to pilgrims and the maintainers of the Sacred Mosque, who were polytheists in God. ﴿And those﴾, he says: those whom We have described, who believed, emigrated, and struggled, ﴿are the victorious﴾, with Paradise, saved from the Fire. [[See the explanation of "al-darajah" (rank) earlier, vol. 13, p. 389, note 1, and the references there.]]

**The discussion on the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying:** ﴿Their Lord gives them good tidings of mercy from Him, and approval, and gardens for them, in which is lasting bliss﴾ (9:21)

Abu Ja'far said: May He be exalted and remembered, says: Their Lord gives good tidings to these who believed, emigrated, and strove in the cause of God [[See the explanation of "al-fawz" (success) above, 11:286, footnote 1, and the references there.]], ﴿of mercy from Him﴾, that He has shown them mercy by sparing them punishment; ﴿and approval from Him﴾, that He is pleased with them for their obedience to Him and their fulfilment of what He imposed on them [[See the explanation of "al-tabshir" (giving good tidings) above, p. 131, footnote 4, and the references there.]]; ﴿and gardens﴾, meaning orchards [[See the explanation of "al-ridwan" (approval) above, 11:245, footnote 1, and the references there.]]; ﴿for them, in which is lasting bliss﴾, which does not cease or perish, but is constant and everlasting for them. [[See the explanation of "al-na'im" (bliss) above, 10:461–462, and the explanation of "muqim" (lasting) above, 10:293.]]

16567 – Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: When the people of Paradise enter Paradise, God, glorified is He, says: "I will give you something better than this." They say: "Our Lord, what could be better than this?" He says: "My approval." [[The report: 16567 – This report has passed before with its chain and wording, and its authenticity was established under number 651 (vol. 6, p. 262). In the printed edition it read "Abu Ahmad al-Musawi," a pure error; the editor did not read the manuscript well.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 22–23:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Abiding therein forever. Indeed, with Allah is a great reward﴾

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿Abiding therein﴾, remaining therein, meaning in the Gardens [[See the explanation of "al-khulud" (abiding) in the preceding lexical indexes (kh-l-d).]] = ﴿forever﴾, without end or limit [[See the explanation of "abadan" (forever) in the preceding volumes, 11:244, note 2, and the references there.]] = ﴿Indeed, with Allah is a great reward﴾, meaning: Indeed, with Allah, for these believers whom He, may His praise be exalted, has described with the description mentioned in this verse = ﴿reward﴾, recompense for their obedience to their Lord and their performance of the deeds He imposed upon them [[See the explanation of "al-ajr" (reward) in the preceding lexical indexes (a-j-r).]] = ﴿great﴾, and that is the bliss which He promised to give them in the Hereafter. [[See the explanation of "azim" (great) in the preceding lexical indexes ('-z-m).]]

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take your fathers and your brothers as allies if they prefer disbelief over faith. And whoever among you allies with them, then those are the wrongdoers﴾

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, says to the believers in Him and His Messenger: Do not take your fathers and your brothers as intimates and friends, to whom you confide your secrets and reveal to them the weak points of Islam and its people, and prefer to remain among them over emigrating to the Abode of Islam [[See the explanation of "wali" (ally, guardian) in the preceding lexical indexes (w-l-y).]] = ﴿if they prefer disbelief over faith﴾, meaning: if they choose disbelief in Allah over believing in Him and affirming His oneness = ﴿And whoever among you allies with them﴾, meaning: and whoever among you takes them as intimates instead of the believers, and prefers to stay with them over emigrating to the Messenger of Allah and the Abode of Islam [[See the explanation of "tawalli" (allying) in the preceding lexical indexes (w-l-y).]] = ﴿then those are the wrongdoers﴾, meaning: those among you who do that are the ones who have opposed the command of Allah, placing loyalty in other than its proper place, and disobeying Allah in His command. [[See the explanation of "zulm" (wrongdoing) in the preceding lexical indexes (z-l-m).]]

* *

It has been said: This was revealed as a prohibition from Allah to the believers against allying with their relatives who had not emigrated from the land of polytheism to the Abode of Islam.

Mention of those who said this:

16568- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the words of Allah: ﴿Have you made the providing of water for the pilgrims and the maintenance of the Sacred Mosque [equal to...]﴾, he said: They were commanded to emigrate, so al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib said: I give water to the pilgrims! And Talhah, brother of the Banu 'Abd al-Dar, said: I am the keeper of the Ka'bah, so we will not emigrate! Then it was revealed: ﴿Do not take your fathers and your brothers as allies﴾, up to His words: ﴿until Allah brings His command﴾, meaning the conquest, concerning His command to them to emigrate. All of this was before the conquest of Mecca.

The Interpretation of His words: "Say: If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your wives, your kindred, the wealth you have acquired, the commerce whose slackness you fear, and the dwellings with which you are pleased are dearer to you than Allah and His Messenger and striving in His way, then wait until Allah brings His command. And Allah does not guide the defiant people."

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The Blessed and Exalted says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: "Say," O Muhammad, to those who stayed behind from the migration to the abode of Islam and remained in the abode of polytheism: If remaining with your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your wives, and your kindred, and "wealth you have acquired" — that is, you have earned it [[See the explanation of "iqtiraf" (acquiring, earning) above in 12:76, 17:173, note 1, and the references there.]] — and "commerce whose slackness you fear" — by your leaving your land — and "dwellings with which you are pleased" — so that you dwell in them — are "dearer to you" than migrating to Allah and His Messenger, from the abode of polytheism, and than striving in His way, meaning: in supporting the religion of Allah which He has approved [[See the explanation of "jihad" above in 17:173, note 5, and the references there.

And the explanation of "the way of Allah" above in the lexical indexes (sabl).]] — "then wait" — that is, then wait and expect [[See the explanation of "tarabbus" above in 9:323, note 3, and the references there.]] — "until Allah brings His command," until Allah brings the conquest of Makkah. "And Allah does not guide the defiant people" — that is, Allah does not grant success in goodness to those who go out of His obedience and persist in disobedience. [[See the explanation of "guidance" above in the lexical indexes (hada), and the explanation of "fisq" above in the lexical indexes (fasaq).]]

* *

Those of the people of interpretation said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

16569. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "until Allah brings His command" — by the conquest.

16570. al-Qasim told us, he said: al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid: "then wait until Allah brings His command" — the conquest of Makkah.

16571. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, he said: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: "and wealth you have acquired and commerce whose slackness you fear" — he said: you fear that it will slacken so you sell it. "And dwellings with which you are pleased" — he said: these are the palaces and houses.

16572. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: "and wealth you have acquired" — he said: that you have obtained it.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 25 (part 1 of 2)**

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Certainly, Allah helped you on many occasions, and on the day of Hunayn, when your great number made you vain, but it availed you nothing, and the earth became constricted for you despite its vastness, then you turned back in retreat (25)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may He be remembered, says: ﴿Certainly, Allah helped you﴾, O believers, ﴿in places of battle where you prepared yourselves to meet your enemy, and in encounters where you and they met many times﴾, ﴿and on the day of Hunayn﴾. That is, He also helped you on the day of Hunayn.

* * *

Hunayn is a valley, as is reported, between Makkah and al-Ta'if. It is inflected (ujriya), because it is a masculine name for a masculine thing. Its inflection may also be omitted, when it is intended as the name of the town in which it lies [see Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1: 429]. From this is the saying of the poet [this is Hassan ibn Thabit]:

They helped their Prophet and strengthened his support
At Hunayn, on the day when the champions left one another to fend alone.

His words "tawakkul al-abtal" (the champions leaving one another alone) derive from the saying "tawakkala al-qawm" (the people left one another alone), when some of them rely on others and do not help one another in the narrow straits of war. It is reported in a hadith that he forbade "al-mawakala" (leaving one another alone), which is for each person to leave his companion to himself, so that he does not help him in what he intends. It leads to weakness, severance, and the corruption of affairs. May Allah protect us from all of that. [The verse is a single line of poetry.]

16573 - Abd al-Warith ibn Abd al-Samad narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: Aban al-Attar narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn Urwah narrated to us, from Urwah, who said: "Hunayn" is a valley beside Dhu al-Majaz. [The report 16572 is part of a letter of Urwah to Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan, which I have already takhrij'd, no. 16083. Al-Tabari also narrated it in his History, within a long report, 2: 125.]

* * *

﴿when your great number made you vain﴾. As is reported to us, they were on that day twelve thousand.

* * *

It is narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said on that day: "We shall not be defeated through lack of numbers."

* * *

It has been said: that was said by a man from among the Muslims, from the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

* * *

This is the word of Allah: ﴿when your great number made you vain, but it availed you nothing﴾, that is: your great number did not avail you anything. ﴿And the earth became constricted for you despite its vastness﴾, that is: the earth became narrow for you in its breadth.

* * *

The "ba'" here has the sense of "fi" (in), and the meaning is: the earth became constricted for you within its breadth and by its breadth. [See Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1: 430.]

* * *

It is said from this: "makan rahib" (a spacious place), meaning wide. The courtyards (al-rihab) were called "rihab" only for their spaciousness.

* * *

﴿then you turned back in retreat﴾, fleeing from your enemy in defeat. "Mudbirin" (in retreat): that is, you turned to them with your backs, and that is defeat. He, blessed and exalted, informs them that victory is in His hand and from Him, and that it is not by the multitude of numbers or the severity of force; that He gives victory to the few over the many when He wills, and leaves the many and the few to themselves, so the many are defeated. [In the printed edition: "and leaves the few, so the many are defeated." This was altered by bad judgment, which corrupted the sentence. He intended that Allah leaves the many and the few to themselves, so He does not give victory to the few, and the many defeat the few, according to the customary dominance of the many over the few.]

* * *

Those of the exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) have said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said so:

16574 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿Certainly, Allah helped you on many occasions and on the day of Hunayn﴾, up to ﴿and that is the recompense of the disbelievers﴾. He said: "Hunayn" is a water between Makkah and al-Ta'if, on which the Prophet of Allah fought Hawazin and Thaqif. Over Hawazin was Malik ibn Awf, brother of Banu Nasr, and over Thaqif was Abd Yalil ibn Amr al-Thaqafi. He said: It is mentioned to us that twelve thousand went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that day: ten thousand from the Muhajirun and the Ansar, and two thousand from the Tulaqa'. It is mentioned to us that a man said that day: "We shall not be defeated today through numbers!" He said: It is mentioned to us that the Tulaqa' fled from the people that day [the phrase "injafala al-qawm 'an ra'isihim" means they were terrified and dispersed from around him and fled quickly], and they left the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) alone until he dismounted from his grey mule. It is mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah said: "O Lord, give me what You promised me!" He said: Al-Abbas was holding the bridle of the Messenger of Allah's mule, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Call out, O company of the Ansar and O company of the Muhajirun!" He began to call the Ansar clan by clan, then he said: "Call the companions of Surat al-Baqarah!" He said: So the people came, one neck (i.e., all at once). ["Unuqan wahidan" means one whole body. It is said: "the people came 'unuqan 'unuqan" meaning group after group. It is said: "they are 'alayhi 'unuq" meaning they are a single front against him.] Then the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) turned, and behold, a band of the Ansar. He said: "Is there anyone with you other than yourselves?" They said: "O Prophet of Allah, by Allah, if you were to go to Barak al-Ghimad in Yemen, we would be with you." [See what has passed in the explanation of "Barak al-Ghimad", no. 15720.] Then Allah sent down His help, defeated their enemy, and the Muslims returned. He said: The Messenger of Allah took a handful of dust, or a handful of pebbles, and threw it into the faces of the disbelievers, and said: "May the faces be disfigured!" and they were routed. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gathered the spoils and came to al-Ji'ranah, he distributed there the spoils of Hunayn, and he won over some people, among them Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, al-Harith ibn Hisham, Suhayl ibn Amr, and al-Aqra' ibn Habis. The Ansar said: "The man has favoured his own people!" [In the printed edition: "hanna al-rajul ila qawmihi" (the man yearned for his people), which differs from the manuscript, and is without basis.] This reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), while he was in a leather tent, and he said: "O company of the Ansar, what is this that has reached me? Were you not astray, and Allah guided you? Were you not humbled, and Allah honoured you? Were you not such and such?" He said: Sa'd ibn Ubadah, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "Permit me to speak!" He said: "Speak." He said: As for your saying, "You were astray, and Allah guided you," we were so. "And you were humbled, and Allah honoured you," the Arabs know that no tribe of the Arab tribes was more protective of what was behind their backs than we were! Then Umar said: "O Sa'd, do you know whom you are addressing?" He said: "Yes, I am addressing the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By He in whose hand is my soul, if the Ansar were to take a valley and the people a valley, I would take the valley of the Ansar. Were it not for the emigration, I would have been a man of the Ansar." It is mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: "The Ansar are my stomach and my bag, so accept from their good-doers and overlook their wrongdoers." ["Al-karsh" is the vessel of perfume, and "al-'aybah" is a leather vessel in which goods and clothes are kept. He means: the Ansar are my intimates and the place of my secret; I trust them and rely upon them, and they are the most precious of what I keep.] Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O company of the Ansar, are you not content that the people return with camels and sheep, and you return with the Messenger of Allah to your houses?" The Ansar said: "We are content with Allah and His Messenger; by Allah, we only said that out of eagerness for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah and His Messenger affirm you and excuse you." [The report 16574 was narrated by Ibn Sa'd in abridged form in al-Tabaqat 4/1/11, 12.]

16575 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: It is mentioned to us that the mother of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who nursed him, or his foster-mother, from the Banu Sa'd ibn Bakr, came to him and asked him for the captives of the day of Hunayn. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I do not own them; I have only my share of them. But come to me tomorrow and ask me, with the people present with me, for when I give you my share, the people will give you theirs." She came the next day, and he spread a garment for her, and she sat upon it, then asked him, and he gave her his share. When the people saw that, they gave her their shares.

16576 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning ﴿Certainly, Allah helped you on many occasions﴾, to the end of the verse: that a man from among the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the day of Hunayn said: "O Messenger of Allah, we shall not be defeated today through lack of numbers!" He was pleased with the great number of people, and they were twelve thousand. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) marched, and they were left to the man's word, and they fled from the Messenger of Allah, except al-Abbas, Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith, and Ayman ibn Umm Ayman, who was killed that day before him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called out: "Where are the Ansar? Where are those who pledged allegiance under the tree?" The people returned, and Allah sent down the angels with victory, and they defeated the polytheists that day. That is His word: ﴿Then Allah sent down His tranquillity upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and sent down hosts you did not see﴾, to the end of the verse.

16577 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Kathir ibn Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib, from his father, who said: When the day of Hunayn came, the Muslims and the polytheists met, and the Muslims turned in flight that day. He said: I saw the Prophet (ﷺ), and no one was with him except Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib, who was holding the stirrup of the Prophet (ﷺ), not failing to hasten toward the polytheists. ["Al-gharz" is the stirrup of the mount, and "la ya'lu" means he does not fall short.] He said: I came until I took hold of his bridle, and he was on a grey mule of his. He said: "O Abbas, call out to the companions of the acacia tree!" I was a man with a loud voice, so I called out with my loudest voice: "Where are the companions of the acacia tree!" They turned like camels when they are gathered to their young, ["al-hashr" means gathering. In other sources: "as if their turning, when they heard my voice, was the turning of cows to their young." What is in Ibn Sa'd's Tabaqat agrees with the printed edition.] saying: "Here we are, here we are, here we are!" and the polytheists advanced. They met with the Muslims, and the Ansar called out: "O company of the Ansar!" Then the call was shortened to the Banu al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj, and they called out: "O Banu al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), sitting on his mule as one who stretches himself up, looked at their fighting, and said: "This is the time when the oven (al-watays) has become hot!" ["Al-watays" is a pit dug and kindled with fire, so that when it is heated, bread is baked and meat roasted in it. It is also called "al-ira", and this is from eloquent speech; this expression was not heard from anyone before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).] Then he took a handful of pebbles and threw them at them, and then said: "Retreat, by the Lord of the Ka'bah, retreat, by the Lord of the Ka'bah!" He said: By Allah, their affair kept turning back, and their edge grew blunt, until Allah defeated them. He said: It is as if I am looking at the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) riding after them on his mule. [Report 16577: "Kathir ibn al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib", the cousin of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), was born in the time of the Messenger of Allah and did not hear from him; he was a trustworthy Successor who narrated little. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/1/207, and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/2/153.

This report was narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad, no. 1775, through Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri; my brother Sayyid Ahmad has detailed its takhrij there, then no. 1776.

Muslim narrated it in his Sahih 12: 113, through Yunus, from al-Zuhri. He also narrated it again (12: 117) through Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, and through Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, from al-Zuhri.

al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak 3: 327, through Yunus, from al-Zuhri.

Ibn Sa'd narrated it in al-Tabaqat 2/1/112 = 4/1/11; the second through the route of Muhammad ibn Abd Allah, from his uncle, from Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri, and the first through Muhammad ibn Humayd al-Abdi, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri.

Then see the History of al-Tabari 3: 128, the report of Ibn Ishaq, and in the Sirah of Ibn Hisham 4: 87, 88.]

16578 - Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib: that they took six thousand captives that day. Then their people came afterwards as Muslims, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, you are the best of people and the most righteous of people, and you have taken our sons, our women, and our wealth!" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Among me are those whom you see! And the best speech is the most truthful. Choose: either your offspring and your women, or your wealth." They said: "We would not equate lineages with anything!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up and said: "These people came to me as Muslims, and we gave them the choice between the offspring and the wealth, and they did not equate lineages with anything. Whoever has any of them in his hand, and his soul is content to return it, let him do so; and whoever is not, let him give us, and let it be a loan upon us, until we obtain something, and we shall give it in its place." They said: "O Prophet of Allah, we are content and submit!" He said: "I do not know, perhaps among you are those who are not content, so command your chieftains to raise that matter to us." The chieftains raised to him that they were content and submitted. [Report 16578 was narrated by Ibn Sa'd in al-Tabaqat 2/1/112.]

16579 - Ali ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: Mu'ammal narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, saying: Ya'la ibn Ata' narrated to us, from Abu Hammam, from Abu Abd al-Rahman, meaning al-Fihri, who said: I was with the Prophet (ﷺ) in the battle of Hunayn. When the sun stood still, ["rakadat al-shams" means it became fixed, which is the time when the sun stands at midday,] I put on my armour, ["al-La'mah" is the coat of mail and the whole weaponry of war,] mounted my horse, and came to the Prophet (ﷺ), who was in the shade of a tree. I said: "O Messenger of Allah, the time of the midday journey has come." He said: "Indeed!" Then he called out: "O Bilal! O Bilal!" Bilal rose from under an acacia tree and came, as if his shadow were the shadow of a bird, and said: "Here I am, at your service, and my soul is your ransom, O Messenger of Allah!" The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Saddle my horse!" He brought out a saddle whose two sides were stuffed with palm fibre, having in them neither "ashar" nor "bataru". ["Al-ashar" is arrogance and pride, and "al-bataru" is excessive insolence in blessing, from little endurance of it.] He said: The Prophet (ﷺ) mounted, and we lined up against them, and we remained so through our day and our night. When the two cavalries met, the Muslims turned in retreat, as Allah said. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called out: "O servants of Allah, O company of the Muhajirun!" He said: The Prophet (ﷺ) leaned from his horse, took a handful of dust, and threw it into their faces, and they turned back in flight. Ya'la ibn Ata' said: Their sons told me, from their fathers, that they said: "None of us remained except that his eyes were filled with that dust." [Report 16579: Ya'la ibn Ata' al-Amiri al-Ta'ifi, trustworthy, passed as no. 2858, 11527, 11529.

Abu Hammam is Abd Allah ibn Yasar, who narrated from Amr ibn Huraith and Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Fihri. Trustworthy; biographed in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/202.

Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Fihri is a Companion whose name is disputed; he is biographed in al-Isabah, al-Tahdhib, Usd al-Ghabah 5: 245, 246, and al-Isti'ab: 676.

This report was narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad 5: 286, through Bahz, from Hammad ibn Salamah, and through Affan, from Hammad.

Ibn Sa'd narrated it in al-Tabaqat 2/1/112, 113, through Affan, from Hammad ibn Salamah.

Abu Dawud narrated it in his Sunan 4: 485, 486, no. 5233, through Musa ibn Isma'il, from Hammad, abridged.

Ibn Abd al-Barr narrated it in al-Isti'ab 676, without an isnad.

Ibn al-Athir narrated it in Usd al-Ghabah through Musa ibn Isma'il, from Hammad.

al-Haythami took it out in Majma' al-Zawa'id 6: 181, 182, and said: "al-Bazzar and al-Tabarani narrated it, and its narrators are trustworthy."]

16580 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard al-Bara', when a man from Qays asked him: "Did you flee from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the day of Hunayn?" Al-Bara' said: "But the Messenger of Allah did not flee. Hawazin were archers that day, and when we charged against them, they broke, and we fell upon the spoils, and they met us with arrows. I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on his white mule, and Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith was holding its bridle, and he was saying:

I am the Prophet, I do not lie;
I am the son of Abd al-Muttalib."

[The two reports 16580 and 16581 are the report of al-Bara' ibn Azib, which Muslim narrated through many routes in his Sahih 12: 117-121, and he narrated it through the route of Shu'bah, from Abu Ishaq, in 12: 121.

al-Bukhari also narrated it in his Sahih (al-Fath 8: 24) through many routes.]

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 25 (part 2 of 2):**

16581. Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Israʾil, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', who said: A man asked him, "O Abu ʿUmara, did you turn your backs on the day of Hunayn?" Al-Bara', while I was listening, said: "I bear witness that the Messenger of God did not turn his back that day, but Abu Sufyan was leading his mule." When the polytheists overwhelmed him, he dismounted and began to say:

*I am the Prophet, no lie,*
*I am the son of ʿAbd al-Muttalib.*

No one was seen that day to be stronger than he was.

16582. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Jaʿfar ibn Sulayman narrated to me, from ʿAwf al-Aʿrabi, from ʿAbd al-Rahman, the mawla (client) of Umm Barthan, who said: A man who had been among the polytheists on the day of Hunayn narrated to me, saying: "When we met, we and the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ), they did not stand firm against us for the length of a milking of a sheep. We drove them back, and as we were pursuing them, we came upon the owner of the white mule, and men with white faces and handsome features met us and said to us, 'May your faces be disgraced! Turn back!' So we turned back, and the people rode upon us, and it was as it was." [[Report 16582: "ʿAbd al-Rahman, mawla Umm Barthan" is ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Adam, the one in charge of the water-supply (siqaya). Umm Barthan used to treat people with perfumes. She found an abandoned boy, raised him until he grew up, and named him ʿAbd al-Rahman. He was commonly called "ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Umm Barthan," but he was called "ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Adam," being attributed to Adam, the father of all humanity (peace be upon him), because he was not known to have a father. He is trustworthy (thiqa). It has passed as no. 7145.
In the manuscript it reads "mawla Barthan," which is an error. See the following report, no. 19587, through another chain.
His saying "they did not stand firm against us for the length of a milking of a sheep" means: except for only as long as it takes to milk a sheep, a kinaya (figurative expression, i.e., euphemism) for a short time, just as one says "fawaq of a she-camel." The fawaq is the interval between two milkings, when one squeezes the udder and then releases it.
His saying "and it was as it was" means: the defeat that is known. In the hadith of Muʿawiya ibn ʿAta': "When Muʿawiya (may God be pleased with him) raised his head from the last prostration, it was as it was." They said: the subject of "kana" (was) is a pronoun referring to "the prostration," and "iyaha" is the predicate, meaning: "it was itself," i.e., he would rise from it and stand up for the next rak'a without sitting in the brief resting posture.]]

16583. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Yaʿqub, from Jaʿfar, from Saʿid, who said: "God reinforced His Prophet (ﷺ) on the day of Hunayn with five thousand angels, marked (for battle)." He said: "On that day God named the Ansar 'believers'." He said: "Then God sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and sent down hosts you did not see."

16584. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: "And (remember) the day of Hunayn, when your large numbers pleased you but availed you nothing," he said: "They were twelve thousand."

16585. Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Adami narrated to us, saying: Maʿn ibn ʿIsa narrated to us, from Saʿid ibn al-Sa'ib al-Ta'ifi, from his father, from Yazid ibn ʿAmir, who said: "When the Muslims were routed on the day of Hunayn, the Prophet (ﷺ) struck his hand on the ground and took from it a handful of dust. He turned with it toward the polytheists, who were pursuing the Muslims, threw it into their faces, and said: 'Turn back! May the faces be disgraced!'" He said: "So we turned back, and no one met anyone without wiping the dust from his eyes." [[Report 16585: Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Adami al-Kharraz, the teacher of al-Tabari, trustworthy and ascetic. It has passed as no. 4894.
Maʿn ibn ʿIsa al-Ashja'i al-Qazzaz, one of the imams of hadith, from whom the majority (of compilers) narrated. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/1/390, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/277.
Saʿid ibn al-Sa'ib al-Ta'ifi, trustworthy. It has passed as no. 15402.
His father al-Sa'ib ibn Abi Hafs al-Ta'ifi, trustworthy, biographed in al-Kabir 2/2/156, and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/245.
Yazid ibn ʿAmir al-Suwa'i, Abu Hajiz, a companion (sahabi), biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/2/316, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/281.
This report was narrated by al-Bukhari in his Tarikh 4/2/316, through Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir, from Maʿn ibn ʿIsa.
It was also narrated by Ibn al-Athir in Usd al-Ghaba 5: 115, 116.
al-Haythami cited it in Majma' al-Zawa'id (6: 182, 183) as two hadiths, as they appear here in the tafsir, and he said of the first and second: "Narrated by al-Tabarani, and its narrators are trustworthy."]]

16586. Through the same chain, from Yazid ibn ʿAmir al-Suwa'i, who said: He was asked, "O Abu Hajiz, what did you find of the terror that God cast into the hearts of the polytheists?" He said: Abu Hajiz was among the polytheists on the day of Hunayn, and he would take a pebble and throw it into a basin, and it would ring, and then he would say: "There was something like this in our bellies!" [[Report 16586: a repetition of the previous report, and its takhrij (sourcing) is there.]]

16587. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn ʿArafa narrated to us, saying: al-Muʿtamir ibn Sulayman narrated to me, from ʿAwf, who said: "I heard ʿAbd al-Rahman, mawla Umm Barthan, or: Umm Barthum," he said: "A man who had been among the polytheists on the day of Hunayn narrated to me, saying: 'When we met, we and the companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) on the day of Hunayn, they did not stand firm against us for the length of a milking of a sheep.'" He said: "When we had routed them, we began driving them from behind, until we came upon the owner of the white mule, and behold, it was the Messenger of God (ﷺ)." He said: "There, men with white faces and handsome features met us and said to us, 'May the faces be disgraced! Turn back!'" He said: "So we were routed, and they rode upon our necks, and it was as it was." [[Report 16587: "ʿAbd al-Rahman, mawla Umm Barthan, or Umm Barthum," with the nun changed to a mim, which has passed in report no. 16582. In the printed edition here it reads "or: Umm Maryam," which is a pure error, and a liberty taken with the manuscript's writing, which is unpointed.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 26:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Then Allah sent down His tranquillity upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and sent down hosts you did not see, and He punished those who disbelieved. That is the recompense of the disbelievers.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, He says: Then, after the earth had become constricted for you despite its vastness, and after you had turned your backs to the enemy in flight, Allah lifted the calamity that had descended upon you by sending down upon you His tranquillity, which is security and tranquillity.

* *

= We have already explained that it is an intensive form (fa'ila) derived from "sakun" (stillness) earlier in this book, in what suffices so that it need not be repeated here. [[See the explanation of "al-sakina" above: 3:66, 70 / 5:326-330.]]

* *

= ﴿And sent down hosts you did not see﴾: these are the angels, which I mentioned in the reports whose mention has already passed. = ﴿And He punished those who disbelieved﴾: that is, God punished those who denied His oneness and the message of His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), by killing, the taking captive of their families and offspring, the seizure of their wealth, and humiliation. = ﴿That is the recompense of the disbelievers﴾: that is, what We did to them of killing and taking captives. = ﴿The recompense of the disbelievers﴾: that is, it is the reward of the people who deny His oneness and the message of His Messenger. [[See the explanation of "al-jaza'" in the earlier linguistic indexes under (j-z-y).]]

16588 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And He punished those who disbelieved﴾, he said: He killed them by the sword.

16589 - Ibn Wakic related to us, he said: Abu Dawud al-Hafari related to us, from Ya'qub, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, regarding ﴿And He punished those who disbelieved﴾, he said: By defeat and killing.

16590 - Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words ﴿And He punished those who disbelieved; that is the recompense of the disbelievers﴾, he said: Those among them who remained.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 27–28:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Then Allah relents toward whom He wills after that, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (27)

Abu Ja'far said: May He be exalted and remembered, says: Then Allah bestows, by His grace, the success of repentance and turning back to Him after His punishment with which He punished those among them who perished by the sword; ﴿upon whom He wills﴾, that is, Allah relents toward whomever He wills of the living, turning him toward His obedience; ﴿and Allah is Forgiving﴾, to the sins of those among them and others who turn back and repent to Him; ﴿Merciful﴾, toward them, so He does not punish them after their repentance, nor hold them to account for it after they have turned back. [See the explanation of "tawbah" (repentance), "Ghafur" (Forgiving) and "Rahim" (Merciful) in the earlier lexical indexes under (t-w-b), (gh-f-r), and (r-h-m).]

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, the polytheists are only unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this, their year. And if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty if He wills. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Wise﴾ (28)

Abu Ja'far said: May He be exalted and remembered, says to the believers in Him and His Messenger, who affirmed His oneness: The polytheists are nothing but unclean (najas).

The interpreters differed regarding the meaning of "najas" (unclean), and the reason for which He named them thus.

Some of them said: He named them thus because they remain in a state of major impurity (janabah) and do not perform ghusl; so He said: they are unclean, and let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram, because one in a state of janabah should not enter the mosque.

Those who said this:

16591- Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, the polytheists are unclean﴾: I do not know that Qatadah said anything but: "Najas" is janabah.

16592- And with this chain, from Ma'mar, who said: It has reached me that the Prophet (ﷺ) met Hudhayfah, and the Prophet (ﷺ) took his hand. Hudhayfah said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am in a state of janabah!" He said: "Indeed, the believer does not become unclean."

16593- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed the polytheists are unclean﴾: that is, they are those in janabah.

* *

Others said: The meaning is: the polytheists are nothing but the filth (rijs) of a pig or a dog.

This is a report narrated from Ibn 'Abbas through a route other than Humayd, so we dislike mentioning it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this, their year﴾, it says to the believers: Do not allow them to approach al-Masjid al-Haram by entering the Haram. He only meant by this preventing them from entering the Haram, because if they entered the Haram they would have approached al-Masjid al-Haram.

* *

The interpreters differed regarding the meaning of this.

Some of them said something similar to what we have said.

Those who said this:

16594- Bishr and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: 'Ata' said: "The whole Haram is qiblah and masjid." He said: ﴿So let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram﴾ — He did not mean the mosque alone; He meant Makkah and the Haram. He said this more than once.

It is mentioned from 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz regarding this:

16595- 'Abd al-Karim ibn Abi 'Umayr narrated to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Amr narrated to us: that 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz wrote: "Prevent the Jews and Christians from entering the mosques of the Muslims," and in his prohibition he followed the saying of Allah: ﴿Indeed, the polytheists are unclean.﴾

16596- Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from al-Hasan: ﴿Indeed, the polytheists are unclean﴾, he said: Do not shake hands with them; whoever shakes hands with them should perform wudu'.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿after this, their year﴾, it means: after the year in which 'Ali, may Allah have mercy on him, proclaimed the declaration of immunity (Bara'ah), and that was the year Abu Bakr led the pilgrimage with the people, which is the ninth year after the Hijrah, as:

16597- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿So let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this, their year﴾, which is the year in which Abu Bakr performed the pilgrimage, and 'Ali, may Allah have mercy on them both, proclaimed the adhan, and that was nine years after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) migrated. The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) performed the Farewell Pilgrimage the following year, and he performed no pilgrimage before it or after it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And if you fear poverty﴾, it says to the believers: And if you fear destitution and need, by preventing the polytheists from approaching al-Masjid al-Haram — ﴿Allah will enrich you from His bounty if He wills﴾.

* *

It is said from this: 'ala ya'il 'aylatan wa 'uyulan, and from it is the saying of the poet: [He is Uhayhah ibn al-Jullah.]

And the poor man does not know when his wealth will come, and the rich man does not know when he will become poor.

[The verse was previously cited, its takhrij and explanation, in the earlier volume 7: 459; see also Majaz al-Qur'an 1: 255.]

It has been related from some that some Arabs say for poverty: "'ala ya'ulu," with waw. [See the explanation of "'ala" in the earlier volume 7: 548, 549.]

* *

It has been reported from 'Amr ibn Fa'id that he interpreted His saying ﴿And if you fear poverty﴾ as meaning: "And since you feared." And he said: The people had feared, and this is like the speaker's saying to his father: "If you are my father, then honour me," meaning: "since you are my father."

* *

This was said to them because the believers feared that the polytheists' cutting off from entering the Haram would cut off their trade, and harm would come to them through the cessation of that. Allah secured them against poverty and compensated them, in place of what they disliked being cut off from them, with something better for them, which is the jizyah. So He said to them: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah or the Last Day and do not prohibit what Allah and His Messenger have prohibited﴾, up to: ﴿humbled﴾.

* *

Others said: It refers to the abundant rain sent down upon them.

* *

The interpreters said things in agreement with what we have said regarding this.

Those who said this:

16598- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, the polytheists are only unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this, their year﴾, he said: When Allah expelled the polytheists from al-Masjid al-Haram, Satan cast grief into the hearts of the believers, saying: "From where will you eat, now that the polytheists have been expelled and the caravans have been cut off from you?" So Allah said: ﴿And if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty if He wills﴾, and He commanded them to fight the People of the Book, and enriched them from His bounty.

16599- Hannad ibn al-Sarri narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah regarding His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, the polytheists are only unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this, their year﴾, he said: The polytheists used to come to the House, bringing food with them, and they would trade in it. When they were forbidden to come to the House, the Muslims said: "From where will we get food?" So Allah revealed: ﴿And if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty if He wills﴾, and He sent down rain upon them, and their good increased until the polytheists were gone from them.

16600- Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Salih, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah: ﴿Indeed, the polytheists are unclean﴾, the verse — then he mentioned a report similar to Hannad's, from Abu al-Ahwas.

16601- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Mu'ammal narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Waqid, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: When this was revealed: ﴿Indeed, the polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this, their year﴾, it weighed heavily upon the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they said: "Who will bring us our food, and who will bring us our goods?" So this was revealed: ﴿And if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty if He wills﴾. [The two reports 16601 and 16602: "Waqid, mawla of Zayd ibn Khulaydah," is trustworthy, previously cited under no. 11450.]

16602- Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Waqid, mawla of Zayd ibn Khulaydah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: The polytheists used to come to them with trade, so this verse was revealed: ﴿Indeed, the polytheists are unclean﴾, up to His saying: ﴿poverty﴾ — he said: the poverty — ﴿Allah will enrich you from His bounty﴾.

16603- Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from his father, from 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi, who said: The Muslims said: "We used to profit from their trade and their sales," so this was revealed: ﴿Indeed, the polytheists are unclean﴾, up to His saying: ﴿from His bounty﴾.

16604- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: I heard my father — I think he said: Abu Ja'far informed us, from 'Atiyyah, who said: When it was said: "No polytheist shall perform the pilgrimage after this year!" they said: "We used to profit from their sales during the season." He said: So this was revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, the polytheists are only unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this, their year. And if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty﴾, meaning: by what escaped them of their sales.
