16605- Abu Kurayb and Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Abu Sinan, from Thabit, from al-Dahhak: ﴿And if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty﴾, he said: the jizyah.

16606- Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman and Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Abu Sinan, from Thabit, from al-Dahhak, who said: The polytheists were expelled from Makkah, and this weighed upon the Muslims, and they said: "We used to profit from them through trade and provisions." So Allah revealed: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah nor the Last Day﴾,

16607- It was narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿And if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty﴾: some Muslims used to be attached to the caravans. When "Bara'ah" was revealed, ordering the fighting of the polytheists wherever they were found and that they be waited for at every lookout, Satan cast into the hearts of the believers: "From where will you live, when you have been commanded to fight the people of the caravans?" So Allah knew what they knew and said: "Obey Me, carry out My command, and obey My Messenger, for I will surely enrich you from My bounty." Thus Allah guaranteed them that.

16608- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, the polytheists are unclean﴾, up to His saying: ﴿Allah will enrich you from His bounty if He wills﴾, he said: The believers said: "We used to profit from the merchants of the polytheists!" So Allah promised them that He would enrich them from His bounty, as compensation for them in that they would not let them approach al-Masjid al-Haram. This verse, together with the beginning of "Bara'ah" in recitation, and with its end in interpretation [in the printed edition: "from the beginning of Bara'ah... and from its end"; I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is correct], ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah nor the Last Day﴾, up to His saying: ﴿while they are humbled﴾, when Muhammad and his Companions were commanded to the expedition of Tabuk.

16609- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly.

16609m- Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: When Allah expelled the polytheists from al-Masjid al-Haram, this weighed upon the Muslims, for they used to bring goods from which the Muslims benefited. Then Allah, may He be exalted and remembered, revealed: ﴿And if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty﴾, so He enriched them through this tax (kharaj), the jizyah levied upon them, which they paid month by month and year by year. So no polytheist may approach al-Masjid al-Haram after their year in any circumstance, except the holder of the jizyah or the slave of a Muslim man.

16610- al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: Abu al-Zubayr informed us that he heard Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah say regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, the polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this, their year﴾: except one who is a slave or one of the People of Dhimmah.

16611- [Isnad omitted] 'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: ﴿So let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this, their year﴾, he said: except the holder of the jizyah, or a slave of a man from the Muslims.

16612- Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Jurayj, who said: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah say regarding this verse: ﴿Indeed, the polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram﴾: except one who is a slave, or one of the people of the jizyah.

16613- al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: ﴿And if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty﴾, he said: Allah enriched them with the jizyah levied month by month and year by year.

16614- Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: 'Abbad ibn al-'Awwam narrated to us, from al-Hajjaj, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir: ﴿Indeed, the polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this, their year﴾, he said: No polytheist or dhimmi may approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this year.

16615- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿Indeed, the polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this, their year. And if you fear poverty﴾, because the people said: "You will surely cut off our markets, and trade will perish, and what we used to gain from it in benefits will be gone!" [In the printed edition: "So it was revealed: And if you fear", which is not in the manuscript; the scribe slipped and skipped what he was copying from, and I have restored it from Ibn Ishaq's text in Ibn Hisham's Sirah.] Then Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty﴾, from a direction other than that, ﴿if He wills﴾, up to His saying: ﴿while they are humbled﴾. In this is a compensation for what you feared from the cutting off of those markets; so Allah compensated them for what was cut off from them of the matter of polytheism with what He gave them of the jizyah from the necks of the People of the Book. [The report 16615 is from Sirah Ibn Hisham 4: 192, 193, and continues the earlier report no. 16556.]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Wise﴾, its meaning is: Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what your souls, O believers, have been moved by, of fear of poverty, through preventing the polytheists from approaching al-Masjid al-Haram, and of other matters of the welfare of His servants; ﴿Wise﴾, in His management of them and His management of all His creation. [See the explanation of "'Alim" (Knowing) and "Hakim" (Wise) in the earlier lexical indexes under (ʿ-l-m) and (ḥ-k-m).]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 27–28:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Then Allah relents toward whom He wills after that, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (27)

Abu Ja'far said: May He be exalted and remembered, says: Then Allah bestows, by His grace, the success of repentance and turning back to Him after His punishment with which He punished those among them who perished by the sword; ﴿upon whom He wills﴾, that is, Allah relents toward whomever He wills of the living, turning him toward His obedience; ﴿and Allah is Forgiving﴾, to the sins of those among them and others who turn back and repent to Him; ﴿Merciful﴾, toward them, so He does not punish them after their repentance, nor hold them to account for it after they have turned back. [See the explanation of "tawbah" (repentance), "Ghafur" (Forgiving) and "Rahim" (Merciful) in the earlier lexical indexes under (t-w-b), (gh-f-r), and (r-h-m).]

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, the polytheists are only unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this, their year. And if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty if He wills. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Wise﴾ (28)

Abu Ja'far said: May He be exalted and remembered, says to the believers in Him and His Messenger, who affirmed His oneness: The polytheists are nothing but unclean (najas).

The interpreters differed regarding the meaning of "najas" (unclean), and the reason for which He named them thus.

Some of them said: He named them thus because they remain in a state of major impurity (janabah) and do not perform ghusl; so He said: they are unclean, and let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram, because one in a state of janabah should not enter the mosque.

Those who said this:

16591- Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, the polytheists are unclean﴾: I do not know that Qatadah said anything but: "Najas" is janabah.

16592- And with this chain, from Ma'mar, who said: It has reached me that the Prophet (ﷺ) met Hudhayfah, and the Prophet (ﷺ) took his hand. Hudhayfah said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am in a state of janabah!" He said: "Indeed, the believer does not become unclean."

16593- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed the polytheists are unclean﴾: that is, they are those in janabah.

* *

Others said: The meaning is: the polytheists are nothing but the filth (rijs) of a pig or a dog.

This is a report narrated from Ibn 'Abbas through a route other than Humayd, so we dislike mentioning it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this, their year﴾, it says to the believers: Do not allow them to approach al-Masjid al-Haram by entering the Haram. He only meant by this preventing them from entering the Haram, because if they entered the Haram they would have approached al-Masjid al-Haram.

* *

The interpreters differed regarding the meaning of this.

Some of them said something similar to what we have said.

Those who said this:

16594- Bishr and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: 'Ata' said: "The whole Haram is qiblah and masjid." He said: ﴿So let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram﴾ — He did not mean the mosque alone; He meant Makkah and the Haram. He said this more than once.

It is mentioned from 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz regarding this:

16595- 'Abd al-Karim ibn Abi 'Umayr narrated to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Amr narrated to us: that 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz wrote: "Prevent the Jews and Christians from entering the mosques of the Muslims," and in his prohibition he followed the saying of Allah: ﴿Indeed, the polytheists are unclean.﴾

16596- Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from al-Hasan: ﴿Indeed, the polytheists are unclean﴾, he said: Do not shake hands with them; whoever shakes hands with them should perform wudu'.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿after this, their year﴾, it means: after the year in which 'Ali, may Allah have mercy on him, proclaimed the declaration of immunity (Bara'ah), and that was the year Abu Bakr led the pilgrimage with the people, which is the ninth year after the Hijrah, as:

16597- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿So let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this, their year﴾, which is the year in which Abu Bakr performed the pilgrimage, and 'Ali, may Allah have mercy on them both, proclaimed the adhan, and that was nine years after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) migrated. The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) performed the Farewell Pilgrimage the following year, and he performed no pilgrimage before it or after it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And if you fear poverty﴾, it says to the believers: And if you fear destitution and need, by preventing the polytheists from approaching al-Masjid al-Haram — ﴿Allah will enrich you from His bounty if He wills﴾.

* *

It is said from this: 'ala ya'il 'aylatan wa 'uyulan, and from it is the saying of the poet: [He is Uhayhah ibn al-Jullah.]

And the poor man does not know when his wealth will come, and the rich man does not know when he will become poor.

[The verse was previously cited, its takhrij and explanation, in the earlier volume 7: 459; see also Majaz al-Qur'an 1: 255.]

It has been related from some that some Arabs say for poverty: "'ala ya'ulu," with waw. [See the explanation of "'ala" in the earlier volume 7: 548, 549.]

* *

It has been reported from 'Amr ibn Fa'id that he interpreted His saying ﴿And if you fear poverty﴾ as meaning: "And since you feared." And he said: The people had feared, and this is like the speaker's saying to his father: "If you are my father, then honour me," meaning: "since you are my father."

* *

This was said to them because the believers feared that the polytheists' cutting off from entering the Haram would cut off their trade, and harm would come to them through the cessation of that. Allah secured them against poverty and compensated them, in place of what they disliked being cut off from them, with something better for them, which is the jizyah. So He said to them: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah or the Last Day and do not prohibit what Allah and His Messenger have prohibited﴾, up to: ﴿humbled﴾.

* *

Others said: It refers to the abundant rain sent down upon them.

* *

The interpreters said things in agreement with what we have said regarding this.

Those who said this:

16598- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, the polytheists are only unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this, their year﴾, he said: When Allah expelled the polytheists from al-Masjid al-Haram, Satan cast grief into the hearts of the believers, saying: "From where will you eat, now that the polytheists have been expelled and the caravans have been cut off from you?" So Allah said: ﴿And if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty if He wills﴾, and He commanded them to fight the People of the Book, and enriched them from His bounty.

16599- Hannad ibn al-Sarri narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah regarding His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, the polytheists are only unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this, their year﴾, he said: The polytheists used to come to the House, bringing food with them, and they would trade in it. When they were forbidden to come to the House, the Muslims said: "From where will we get food?" So Allah revealed: ﴿And if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty if He wills﴾, and He sent down rain upon them, and their good increased until the polytheists were gone from them.

16600- Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Salih, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah: ﴿Indeed, the polytheists are unclean﴾, the verse — then he mentioned a report similar to Hannad's, from Abu al-Ahwas.

16601- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Mu'ammal narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Waqid, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: When this was revealed: ﴿Indeed, the polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this, their year﴾, it weighed heavily upon the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they said: "Who will bring us our food, and who will bring us our goods?" So this was revealed: ﴿And if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty if He wills﴾. [The two reports 16601 and 16602: "Waqid, mawla of Zayd ibn Khulaydah," is trustworthy, previously cited under no. 11450.]

16602- Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Waqid, mawla of Zayd ibn Khulaydah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: The polytheists used to come to them with trade, so this verse was revealed: ﴿Indeed, the polytheists are unclean﴾, up to His saying: ﴿poverty﴾ — he said: the poverty — ﴿Allah will enrich you from His bounty﴾.

16603- Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from his father, from 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi, who said: The Muslims said: "We used to profit from their trade and their sales," so this was revealed: ﴿Indeed, the polytheists are unclean﴾, up to His saying: ﴿from His bounty﴾.

16604- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: I heard my father — I think he said: Abu Ja'far informed us, from 'Atiyyah, who said: When it was said: "No polytheist shall perform the pilgrimage after this year!" they said: "We used to profit from their sales during the season." He said: So this was revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, the polytheists are only unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this, their year. And if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty﴾, meaning: by what escaped them of their sales.

16605- Abu Kurayb and Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Abu Sinan, from Thabit, from al-Dahhak: ﴿And if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty﴾, he said: the jizyah.

16606- Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman and Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Abu Sinan, from Thabit, from al-Dahhak, who said: The polytheists were expelled from Makkah, and this weighed upon the Muslims, and they said: "We used to profit from them through trade and provisions." So Allah revealed: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah nor the Last Day﴾,

16607- It was narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿And if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty﴾: some Muslims used to be attached to the caravans. When "Bara'ah" was revealed, ordering the fighting of the polytheists wherever they were found and that they be waited for at every lookout, Satan cast into the hearts of the believers: "From where will you live, when you have been commanded to fight the people of the caravans?" So Allah knew what they knew and said: "Obey Me, carry out My command, and obey My Messenger, for I will surely enrich you from My bounty." Thus Allah guaranteed them that.

16608- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, the polytheists are unclean﴾, up to His saying: ﴿Allah will enrich you from His bounty if He wills﴾, he said: The believers said: "We used to profit from the merchants of the polytheists!" So Allah promised them that He would enrich them from His bounty, as compensation for them in that they would not let them approach al-Masjid al-Haram. This verse, together with the beginning of "Bara'ah" in recitation, and with its end in interpretation [in the printed edition: "from the beginning of Bara'ah... and from its end"; I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is correct], ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah nor the Last Day﴾, up to His saying: ﴿while they are humbled﴾, when Muhammad and his Companions were commanded to the expedition of Tabuk.

16609- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly.

16609m- Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: When Allah expelled the polytheists from al-Masjid al-Haram, this weighed upon the Muslims, for they used to bring goods from which the Muslims benefited. Then Allah, may He be exalted and remembered, revealed: ﴿And if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty﴾, so He enriched them through this tax (kharaj), the jizyah levied upon them, which they paid month by month and year by year. So no polytheist may approach al-Masjid al-Haram after their year in any circumstance, except the holder of the jizyah or the slave of a Muslim man.

16610- al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: Abu al-Zubayr informed us that he heard Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah say regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, the polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this, their year﴾: except one who is a slave or one of the People of Dhimmah.

16611- [Isnad omitted] 'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: ﴿So let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this, their year﴾, he said: except the holder of the jizyah, or a slave of a man from the Muslims.

16612- Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Jurayj, who said: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah say regarding this verse: ﴿Indeed, the polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram﴾: except one who is a slave, or one of the people of the jizyah.

16613- al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: ﴿And if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty﴾, he said: Allah enriched them with the jizyah levied month by month and year by year.

16614- Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: 'Abbad ibn al-'Awwam narrated to us, from al-Hajjaj, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir: ﴿Indeed, the polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this, their year﴾, he said: No polytheist or dhimmi may approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this year.

16615- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿Indeed, the polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this, their year. And if you fear poverty﴾, because the people said: "You will surely cut off our markets, and trade will perish, and what we used to gain from it in benefits will be gone!" [In the printed edition: "So it was revealed: And if you fear", which is not in the manuscript; the scribe slipped and skipped what he was copying from, and I have restored it from Ibn Ishaq's text in Ibn Hisham's Sirah.] Then Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you from His bounty﴾, from a direction other than that, ﴿if He wills﴾, up to His saying: ﴿while they are humbled﴾. In this is a compensation for what you feared from the cutting off of those markets; so Allah compensated them for what was cut off from them of the matter of polytheism with what He gave them of the jizyah from the necks of the People of the Book. [The report 16615 is from Sirah Ibn Hisham 4: 192, 193, and continues the earlier report no. 16556.]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Wise﴾, its meaning is: Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what your souls, O believers, have been moved by, of fear of poverty, through preventing the polytheists from approaching al-Masjid al-Haram, and of other matters of the welfare of His servants; ﴿Wise﴾, in His management of them and His management of all His creation. [See the explanation of "'Alim" (Knowing) and "Hakim" (Wise) in the earlier lexical indexes under (ʿ-l-m) and (ḥ-k-m).]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 29:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah or the Last Day, and who do not forbid what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, and who do not adopt the religion of truth from among those who were given the Book, until they give the jizyah willingly while they are humbled﴾ (29).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may He be exalted, says to the believers in Him among the companions of His Messenger ﷺ: ﴿Fight﴾, O believers, the people ﴿who do not believe in Allah or the Last Day﴾, meaning: who do not affirm Paradise or Hell [[See the explanation of "the Last Day" in the earlier lexical indexes under (akhara).]] ﴿and who do not forbid what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, nor adopt the religion of truth﴾, meaning: who do not obey Allah with the obedience of truth, that is, they do not obey with the obedience of the people of Islam [[See the explanation of "din" (religion, obedience) in the earlier passages: 1:155, 3:571, 9:522.]] ﴿from among those who were given the Book﴾, and they are the Jews and the Christians.

* *

Every person who obeys a king or a ruler with authority is a debtor (dā'in) to him. It is said of this: "Fulan submitted to Fulan, so he yadinu lahu, dīnan (submits to him)." Zuhayr said:

"If you were to settle in the open land among the Banu Asad, under the religion (authority) of Amr, and Fadak came between us..."

[[Diwan: 183; Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1:286. It is from an excellent qasida in which he warned al-Harith ibn Warqa' al-Saydawi, of the Banu Asad, who had raided the Banu 'Abd Allah ibn Ghatafan, seized booty, and driven off Zuhayr's camels and his shepherd Yasar. (The verses follow in the original, as cited there.) "Jaww" is the name of many places in the Arabian Peninsula; this "Jaww" is here in the abodes of the Banu Asad. "Amr" is 'Amr ibn Hind ibn al-Mundhir ibn Ma' al-Sama'. "Fadak" is a well-known village in the Hijaz, frequently mentioned in the biographies.]] His saying ﴿from among those who were given the Book﴾ means: those who were given the Book of Allah, and they are the people of the Torah and the Gospel ﴿until they give the jizyah﴾. [[See the explanation of "al-iytaa'" (giving) in the earlier lexical indexes under (ata).]]

* *

"Al-jizyah" is the form (fi'lah) from "jazaa Fulan Fulanan ma 'alayhi", when he paid him what was due upon him, "yajziihi", and "al-jizyah" is like "al-qi'dah" and "al-jilsah".

* *

The meaning of the statement is: until they give the kharaj (tribute) from their necks, which they pay to the Muslims to ward off (harm) from them.

* *

As for His saying ﴿'an yad﴾ (from hand), it means: from his hand to the hand of the one who receives it from him.

* *

Thus the Arabs say of everyone who gives to one who overpowers him, whether he gives willingly or unwillingly: "He gave him 'an yadihi, and 'an yad (from his hand, from hand)." This is like their saying: "I spoke to him fa-man li-fam (mouth to mouth)," and "I met him kaffatan li-kaffatin [[It is said: "I met him kaffatan kaffatan" (with kaf vowelled, and the ta' in the accusative), when you face him directly, as if each of the two had restrained the other from passing beyond him and prevented him. See the detailed treatment under its root in Lisan al-Arab (kaff).]]," and likewise: "I gave him 'an yadin li-yadin."

* *

As for His saying ﴿and they are humbled﴾, its meaning is: and they are abased and subdued.

* *

One says of the lowly, contemptible person: "saghir."

[[See the explanation of "al-saghar" (humiliation) in the earlier passage, vol. 13: 22, note 2, and the references there.]]

* *

It is mentioned that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning his command to fight the Byzantines, and after its revelation the Messenger of Allah ﷺ campaigned in the expedition of Tabuk.

Those who said so:

16616 - Muhammad ibn 'Urwah narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah and the Last Day...until they give the jizyah 'an yad while they are humbled﴾, when Muhammad and his companions were commanded to the expedition of Tabuk.

16617 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly.

* *

The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of "al-saghar" (humiliation) which Allah intended in this place.

Some of them said: that he gives it while standing, and the receiver is seated.

Those who said so:

16618 - 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Bishr al-Naysaburi narrated to me, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Sa'd, from 'Ikrimah: ﴿until they give the jizyah 'an yad while they are humbled﴾, he said: that you take it while you are seated and he is standing. [[The report 16618: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Bishr ibn al-Hakam al-Naysaburi, Tabari's teacher, trustworthy, one of al-Bukhari's teachers, previously mentioned under no. 13805. In the printed edition it reads "from Ibn Sa'd," which is an error, contrary to the manuscript; see "Abu Sa'd" in the index of men.]]

* *

Others said: the meaning of His saying ﴿until they give the jizyah 'an yad while they are humbled﴾ is: from themselves, with their hands carrying it, while they are unwilling; and this is a saying transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas, through a chain that is open to scrutiny.

* *

Others said: their giving it is the humiliation.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 9, Verse 30:

Concerning the interpretation of His words: ﴿And the Jews say, "Ezra is the son of Allah," and the Christians say, "The Messiah is the son of Allah." That is their statement from their mouths; they imitate the saying of those who disbelieved before them. May Allah destroy them; how are they deluded?﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the one who said: ﴿Ezra is the son of Allah.﴾

Some of them said: It was one man, namely Finhas.

Those who said this:

16619. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr say concerning His words: ﴿And the Jews say, "Ezra is the son of Allah,"﴾ : "It was said by one man. They said his name was Finhas, and they said he is the one who said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich﴾ [Surah Al 'Imran: 181]."

Others said: Rather, it was the saying of a group of them.

Those who said this:

16620. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, the client of Zayd ibn Thabit, narrated to me, saying: Sa'id ibn Jubayr, or Ikrimah, narrated to me, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Salam ibn Mishkam came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Nu'man ibn Awfa, [[In the Sirah of Ibn Hisham: "Nu'man ibn Awfa Abu Anas, Mahmud ibn Dahya, and Shas..."]] and Shas ibn Qays, and Malik ibn al-Sayf, and they said: "How can we follow you when you have abandoned our qiblah, and you do not claim that Ezra is the son of Allah?" So Allah revealed concerning their statement: ﴿And the Jews say, "Ezra is the son of Allah," and the Christians say, "The Messiah is the son of Allah,"﴾ up to: ﴿how are they deluded?﴾ [[The report: 16620 – Sirah Ibn Hisham 2: 219.]]

16621. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas concerning His words: ﴿And the Jews say, "Ezra is the son of Allah,"﴾ . They only said he was the son of Allah because Ezra was among the People of the Book, and the Torah was with them. They acted upon it as much as Allah willed them to act, then they neglected it and acted by falsehood, and the Ark (al-tabut) was among them. When Allah saw that they had neglected the Torah and acted upon their desires, He lifted the Ark from them, caused them to forget the Torah, and its text was erased from their chests. Allah sent upon them a sickness that loosened their bowels, until a man would walk with his liver [falling out]. [[In the printed edition: "they acted upon it," and I have kept what is in the manuscript.]] They forgot the Torah, and it was erased from their chests, and Ezra was among them. They remained as long as Allah willed them to remain after the Torah had been erased from their chests, and Ezra had previously been among their scholars. Ezra called upon Allah and implored Him to return to him what had been erased from his chest of the Torah. While he was praying, imploring Allah, a light came down from Allah and entered his inner body, and what had gone from his inside of the Torah returned to him. He called out to his people, saying: "O people, Allah has given me the Torah and returned it to me!" He began to teach them [[In the printed edition: "fa'allaqa yu'allimuhum"; in the manuscript "fa'allaqa bihi yu'allimuhum"; I have preferred the correct form as set out. It is said "'allaqtu af'alu kadha" meaning "I began to do such-and-such," from the saying "'allaqa bi-l-shay'," if he clung to it. Yazid ibn al-Tuthriyyah said: "They clung around me, asking for hospitality, the camels..." meaning: they began (tafaqqa).]]. They remained as long as Allah willed, while he taught them. Then the Ark came down after that, after its departure from them. When they saw the Ark, they compared what was in it with what Ezra had been teaching them, and they found it identical. They said: "By Allah, this man Ezra was given nothing except that he is the son of Allah."

16622. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi concerning ﴿And the Jews say, "Ezra is the son of Allah,"﴾ : They only said that because the Amalekites prevailed over them, killed them, and took the Torah, and their surviving scholars departed, and they had buried copies of the Torah in the mountains. [[In the printed edition: "fa-dafanu", and I have kept the manuscript reading.]] Ezra was a youth who worshipped on the mountaintops, descending only on the day of a festival. The youth began to weep and say: "My Lord, You have left the Children of Israel without a scholar!" He continued weeping until the eyelids of his eyes fell off. He descended once for the festival, and when he returned he found a woman who had appeared to him at one of those graves, weeping and saying: "O my provider, O my clothier!" He said to her: "Woe to you, who used to feed you, clothe you, give you drink, or benefit you before this man?" [[In the printed edition they were all joined with "wa" conjunction; I have kept the manuscript.]] She said: "Allah!" He said: "Indeed Allah is living and has not died!" She said: "O Ezra, who used to teach the scholars before the Children of Israel?" He said: "Allah!" She said: "Then why do you weep for them?" When he realized he had been overcome in the dispute [[khasim: i.e., overcome in argument and debate]], he turned away, and she called after him: "O Ezra, when you rise tomorrow, go to such-and-such river, bathe in it, then come out and pray two rak'ahs. A old man will come to you; whatever he gives you, take it." When morning came, Ezra went to that river, bathed in it, came out, and prayed two rak'ahs. The old man came to him and said: "Open your mouth!" He opened his mouth, and he put into it something like a great burning coal, gathered like glass, three times. [[In the printed edition: "mujtami'an"; I have kept the manuscript and al-Durr al-Manthur. This part of the report requires examination regarding its soundness and meaning.]] Ezra returned, being among the most knowledgeable of people in the Torah, and said: "O Children of Israel, I have brought you the Torah!" They said: "O Ezra, you were not a liar!" He then tied a pen to each of his fingers, and wrote with all his fingers, and wrote the entire Torah. When the scholars returned, they were informed about the matter of Ezra; those scholars brought out their books of the Torah which they had buried in the mountains, and they were in buried jars [[khawabi, plural of khabiyah, the large jar]]. They compared them with Ezra's Torah and found them identical, and they said: "Allah gave you this only because you are His son!"

* *

The readers differed concerning the recitation of this.

The majority of the readers of Medina and some of the Meccans and Kufans recited: ﴿وَقَالَتِ الْيَهُودُ عُزَيْرُ ابْنُ اللَّهِ﴾ , without tanwin on "'Uzayr".

* *

Some of the Meccans and Kufans recited: ﴿عُزَيْرٌ ابْنُ الله﴾ , with tanwin on "'Uzayr". They said: it is a name treated as diptote, though it is foreign, because of its lightness. It is not, moreover, attributed to Allah, so it is like the statement of one who says "Zayd ibn Abd Allah," and "the son" is placed in the position of the predicate. Had it been attributed to Allah, the proper form, when "the son" is a predicate, would be inflection and tanwin; but how could it be, when it is attributed to other than his father?

As for those who omitted the tanwin on "'Uzayr," the "ba'" of "ibn" was quiescent with the quiescent tanwin, and two quiescent letters met, so the first of them was dropped, to avoid the burden of moving it. The rajaz poet said: [[I do not know who said it.]]

"You will certainly find me with the commander, dutiful, and with the spear, thrusting and repeatedly charging, when Ghutayf al-Sulami flees."

[[Nawadir Abi Zayd: 91; Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1: 431. Lisan (sahb), (da'as), (da'as) and others. Preceding it in al-Nawadir: "They came dragging iron, dragging... tawny-whiskered, seeking evil." In al-Nawadir: "dragging the blacks"; this is another transmission.]]

So he dropped the nun because of the quiescent letter that followed it.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two readings is the reading of the one who recites: ﴿عُزَيْرٌ ابْنُ اللَّهِ﴾ with tanwin on "'Uzayr," because the Arabs do not leave names without tanwin when "the son" is an adjective of the name, [and they do add tanwin when it is a predicate], as in their saying "This is Zayd ibn Abd Allah," where they intend to inform about Zayd that he is the son of Allah. They did not intend to make "the son" an adjective for him, since "the son" in this place is the predicate of "Ezra," because those whom Allah mentions as having said it were informing about "Ezra," that he is so, even though by their saying it they were lying against Allah and fabricators. [[This sentence in the manuscript read: "Because the Arabs' noun [...] when the son is an adjective of the name, like their saying, This is Zayd ibn Abd Allah, so they intended to inform about Zayd that he is the son of Allah." This is extremely disordered speech.

In the printed edition it was corrected to: "Because the Arabs do not make tanwin on names when the son is an adjective of the name, like their saying: This is Zayd ibn Abd Allah, so they intended to inform about Ezra that he is the son of Allah," which is also disordered.

I have kept the first editor's correction at the start of the sentence, then corrected the rest of the statement to agree with the manuscript, then added what is between the brackets, so that the speech is straight in a satisfactory manner. I have no doubt that the copyist dropped some of Abu Ja'far's words.]]

* *

= ﴿And the Christians say, "The Messiah is the son of Allah." That is their statement from their mouths; they imitate the saying of those who disbelieved before them﴾ , meaning the saying of the Jews: ﴿"Ezra is the son of Allah."﴾ He says: it resembles the saying of these people in lying against Allah and fabricating against Him, and in their attributing the Messiah to Allah as a son. It resembles the lie and fabrication of the Jews against Allah in their attributing Ezra to Allah as a son. [[In the printed edition: "the attribution of the saying of these..." – "like the lie of the Jews and their fabrication"; the editor misread "yushbihu," making it "nisbah," then added a kaf at the start of "kadhib" to make it fit, but it did not fit. His phrase "kadhib" is the object of "yushbihu." That is the meaning of "mudahah" as will follow.]] It is not fitting that Allah should have a son, glory be to Him; rather, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth; all are devoutly obedient to Him.

* *

Ahl al-ta'wil said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said this:

16623. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas concerning His words: ﴿imitate the saying of those who disbelieved before them﴾ : he says: they resemble.

16624. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah concerning His words: ﴿imitate the saying of those who disbelieved before them﴾ : the Christians imitated the saying of the Jews before them.

16625. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi concerning ﴿imitate the saying of those who disbelieved before them﴾ : The Christians imitate the saying of the Jews concerning "Uzayr."

16626. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj concerning ﴿imitate the saying of those who disbelieved before them﴾ : he says: the Christians imitate the saying of the Jews.

16627. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas concerning His words: ﴿imitate the saying of those who disbelieved before them﴾ : he says: they said the same as what the people of idols said.

* *

It has also been said that the meaning of this is: by their saying they imitate the saying of the idolaters who said: "al-Lat, al-'Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other."[[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1: 433.]]

* *

The readers differed concerning the recitation of this.

The majority of the readers of the Hijaz and Iraq recited: ﴿يُضَاهُونَ﴾ , without hamzah.

* *

Asim recited: ﴿يُضَاهِئُونَ﴾ , with hamzah, and this is the dialect of Thaqif.

* *

Both are two dialects: it is said "dahaytuhu 'ala kadhā udāhīhi mudāhāh" and "dahatūhu 'alayhi mudāha'ah," meaning: I agreed with him upon it and helped him.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct recitation in this is leaving out the hamzah, because it is the widely transmitted recitation among the readers of the cities, and the eloquent dialect.

* *

As for His words: ﴿May Allah destroy them﴾ , its meaning, as reported from Ibn Abbas, is:

16628. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas concerning His words: ﴿May Allah destroy them﴾ : he says: May Allah curse them. Everything in the Qur'an that says "qatl" means curse.

* *

Ibn Jurayj said concerning this:

16629. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj concerning His words: ﴿May Allah destroy them﴾ , meaning the Christians: a phrase from the speech of the Arabs.[[He means it is a phrase the Arabs say, not intending by it the meaning of "killing," as in their saying "taribat yadaka" (may your hands be dust), which does not mean the matter actually occurs.]]

* *

As for those knowledgeable in Arabic speech, they say its meaning is: "qatalahum Allah" (may Allah kill them). The Arabs say "qatā'aka Allah" and "qatā'aha Allah," meaning "qatalaka Allah" (may Allah kill you). They say: "qata'aka Allah" is milder than "qatalaka Allah."

They have also mentioned that they say: "shaqāhu Allah mā taqāhu," meaning: "ashqāhu Allah mā abqāhu" (may Allah make him wretched whatever He leaves him).

They said: the meaning of His words ﴿May Allah destroy them﴾ is like His words: ﴿Killed are the liars﴾ [Surah Adh-Dhariyat: 10] and ﴿Killed were the people of the trench﴾ [Surah Al-Buruj: 4], one expression that carries the meaning of wonder.

* *

If what they said is as they said, then it is from the rare speech that came contrary to analogy, because "fa'ala" (form III) barely comes as a verb except from two parties, as in their saying "khasamtu fulanan" (I disputed with so-and-so) and "qatalahu" (I fought him), and what is similar to that. They have claimed that their saying "'afaka Allah" (may Allah pardon you) is from this, and its meaning is "a'faka Allah" (may Allah pardon you), in the sense of supplication for one whom one supplicates for, that He pardon him from evil.

* *

As for His words: ﴿How are they deluded?﴾ , He says: In what direction are they being led away, and turned aside? And how are they being diverted from the truth? We have already explained this with its evidences earlier. [[See the explanation of "al-ifk" previously: 10: 486 / 11: 554.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 31:

The discussion of the interpretation (ta'wil) of His words: ﴿They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God, and the Messiah, son of Mary. Yet they were commanded only to worship one God; there is no god but Him. Glory be to Him above what they associate with Him.﴾ (9:31)

Abu Ja'far said: His saying, may His praise be great: The Jews have taken their rabbis (aḥbār), who are the scholars.

* *

I have already explained the interpretation of this with its evidences earlier in this book. Its singular is ḥabr, and ḥibr with a kasra on the ḥa' and ḥabr with a fatḥa. [See the explanation of "al-ḥabr" above: 6:543, 544 / 10:341, 448.]

Yunus al-Jarmi [see above 10:120, note 1 / 11:544, note 3 / 13:129, note 3 = 13:138, note 4], as reported from him, claimed that he had heard only ḥibr with a kasra on the ḥa', and he argued from the people's saying: "This is the ink of a ḥibr," meaning the ink of a scholar.

Al-Farra' mentioned that he had heard it as ḥibran and ḥabran, with the ḥa' pronounced with a kasra and with a fatḥa.

* *

And the Christians' "monks" (ruhbān), who are the people of the monasteries and those among them who exert effort in their religion [see the explanation of "al-ruhbān" above: 10:502, 503]. His saying, "and the Christians, their monks," is coordinated with His earlier words, "the Jews have taken their rabbis."

As related to us:

16630. Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Salamah, from al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿They have taken their rabbis and their monks﴾: he said, "Their reciters (qurrā') and their scholars."

* *

﴿As lords besides God﴾: meaning, masters for them besides God, whom they obey in disobedience to God, so that they make lawful what those masters have made lawful for them of what God has forbidden them, and forbid what those masters have forbidden them of what God has made lawful for them. As related to us:

16631. Al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Tahhan related to me, saying: 'Abd al-Salam ibn Harb al-Mala'i related to us, from Ghutayf ibn A'yan, from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd, from 'Adi ibn Hatim, who said: I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was reciting in Surat Bara'ah: ﴿They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God﴾. He said: "Indeed, they did not worship them, but they made lawful for them, and they made lawful accordingly."

[Footnote: The report 16631 is a ḥadīth of 'Adi ibn Hatim al-Ta'i, which Abu Ja'far transmitted by three paths, all following one another, all through 'Abd al-Salam ibn Harb, from Ghutayf ibn A'yan, from 16631 to 16633.

Al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Subay'i al-Tahhan, the teacher of al-Tabari, was judged trustworthy by Ibn Hibban, but Abu Hatim considered his narrations weak. He appeared above at 2892, 7863, 9153. In the printed and manuscript copies it was "al-Hasan ibn Yazid," which is an error.

'Abd al-Salam ibn Harb al-Mala'i al-Nahdi, the trustworthy memorizer, appeared at 1184, 5471, 12478.

Ghutayf ibn A'yan al-Shaybani al-Jazari, or "Ghudayf," was judged trustworthy by Ibn Hibban. al-Tirmidhi said: "He is not known in ḥadīth." al-Daraqutni weakened him. See Tahdhib al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/1/106, where no criticism is mentioned, and Ibn Abi Hatim included him under "Ghadif" with a ḍād, 3/2/55, where he also mentioned no criticism. "Ghudayf" will come at 16633.

Mus'ab ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas related from his father, 'Ali, 'Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, 'Adi ibn Hatim, Ibn 'Umar, and others. He was related from by Ghutayf ibn A'yan, and he is trustworthy; the group (of compilers) all related from him. He appeared at 9841, 11450.

This report is an abridgment of the one that follows, so consult the following takhrij.

Al-Tirmidhi related it through this same path from al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Kufi al-Tahhan in the Book of Tafsir, and said: "This is a good, strange ḥadīth. We do not know it except from the ḥadīth of 'Abd al-Salam ibn Harb, and Ghutayf ibn A'yan is not known in ḥadīth."

al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur 3:230, and attributed it additionally to Ibn Sa'd, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan. I did not find it in the printed Tabaqat of Ibn Sa'd, and its place in the Sunan of al-Bayhaqi escaped me.]

16632. Abu Kurayb and Ibn Waki' related to us, both saying: Malik ibn Isma'il related to us. [And] Ahmad ibn Ishaq related to us, saying: Abu Ahmad related to us; all of them from 'Abd al-Salam ibn Harb, who said: Ghutayf ibn A'yan related to us, from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd, from 'Adi ibn Hatim, who said: I came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) while there was a golden cross around my neck. He said: "O 'Adi, throw this idol from your neck!" So I threw it away. I came to him while he was reciting in Surat Bara'ah, and he recited this verse: ﴿They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God﴾. I said: "O Messenger of God, we do not worship them!" He said: "Do they not forbid what God has made lawful, so you forbid it, and make lawful what God has forbidden, so you make it lawful?" I said: "Yes." He said: "That is their worship!" The wording is that of Abu Kurayb's ḥadīth.

[Footnote: The report 16632 was transmitted through Malik ibn Isma'il, from 'Abd al-Salam ibn Harb, with the same wording, by al-Bukhari in al-Kabir 4/1/106. See the earlier takhrij.]

16633. Sa'id ibn 'Amr al-Sakuni related to me, saying: Baqiyyah related to us, from Qays ibn al-Rabi', from 'Abd al-Salam ibn Harb al-Nahdi, from Ghudayf, from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd, from 'Adi ibn Hatim, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) reciting Surat Bara'ah. When he recited, ﴿They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God﴾, I said: "O Messenger of God, indeed they did not pray to them!" He said: "You have spoken truly, but they made lawful for them what God had forbidden, so they made it lawful, and they forbade what God had made lawful for them, so they forbade it."

[Footnote: "Ghudayf" is Ghudayf ibn A'yan, and "Ghutayf," as mentioned in the takhrij of report 16631. In the manuscript it was "Hasif," and the printed edition made it "Ghutayf." The correct reading is what I have recorded, as I indicated in the note mentioned.]

16634. Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Abu al-Bakhtari, from Hudhayfah: that he was asked about His saying, ﴿They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God﴾: did they worship them? He said: "No. When they made something lawful for them, they considered it lawful, and when they forbade them something, they forbade it."

16635. Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Sufyan, from Habib, from Abu al-Bakhtari, who said: It was said to Abu Hudhayfah, and he mentioned something similar, except that he said: "But they made the forbidden lawful for them, so they considered it lawful, and they forbade the lawful for them, so they forbade it."

16636. Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun related to us, from al-'Awwam ibn Hawshab, from Habib, from Abu al-Bakhtari, who said: It was said to Hudhayfah: Have you seen the saying of God, ﴿They have taken their rabbis﴾? He said: "Indeed, they did not fast for them, nor did they pray to them. But when they made something lawful for them, they considered it lawful, and when they forbade them something that God had made lawful for them, they forbade it. That was their lordship."

16637. ...... He said: Jarir and Ibn Fudayl related to us, from 'Ata', from Abu al-Bakhtari, regarding ﴿They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God﴾, he said: They went to the lawful of God and made it unlawful, and they went to the unlawful of God and made it lawful, and they obeyed them in that. So God made their obedience their worship. And if they had said to them, "Worship us," they would not have done it.

16638. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to me, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Abu al-Bakhtari, who said: A man asked Hudhayfah, saying: "O Abu 'Abd Allah, have you seen His saying, ﴿They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God﴾: did they worship them?" He said: "No. When they made something lawful for them, they considered it lawful, and when they forbade them something, they forbade it."

16639. Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adi related to us, from Ash'ath, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords﴾: he said, "In obedience."

16640. Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying, ﴿They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God﴾: he says, "They made their obedience appear fair to them."

16641. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God﴾: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas said: "They did not command them to prostrate to them, but they commanded them to disobey God, and they obeyed them. So God named them lords for that."

16642. Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: Ibn Numayr related to us, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, regarding ﴿They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords﴾: he said: I said to Abu al-'Aliyah, "How was the lordship that existed among the Children of Israel?" He said: "[They did not revile our rabbis with anything that had passed.] 'What they commanded us, we obeyed; what they forbade us, we refrained from, deferring to their word.' And they used to find in the Book of God what they were commanded and what they were forbidden, but they sought counsel from men and cast the Book of God behind their backs."

[Footnote: The sentence placed between brackets here is from the manuscript, and I do not know what it is, but I have kept it as it came, so that perhaps someone may find the report elsewhere and correct it.]

16643. Bishr ibn Suwayd related to me, saying: Sufyan related to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abu al-Bakhtari, from Hudhayfah, regarding ﴿They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God﴾: he said: "They did not worship them, but they obeyed them in acts of disobedience."

[Footnote: "Bishr ibn Suwayd": I have not found anyone by this name. I fear it may be "Bishr ibn Mu'adh," the teacher of al-Tabari, from "Suwayd ibn Nasr al-Marwazi."]

* *

As for His saying, ﴿and the Messiah, son of Mary﴾: its meaning is: They took their rabbis and their monks, and the Messiah, son of Mary, as lords besides God.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿Yet they were commanded only to worship one God﴾: He means by it: The Jews and Christians who took the rabbis, the monks, and the Messiah as lords were commanded only to worship one object of worship, and to obey only one Lord, not many diverse lords. He is God, to whom belongs the worship of everything and the obedience of every creature, and who is due from all His creatures acknowledgment of His oneness and lordship. ﴿There is no god but Him.﴾ He, may He be exalted, says: Divinity is not fitting except for the One whom creation was commanded to worship, and whose obedience is incumbent on all servants. ﴿Glory be to Him above what they associate with Him.﴾ He says: Exalted and purified is God above what is associated with His obedience and lordship by those who say, "Ezra is the son of God," and those who say, "The Messiah is the son of God," and those who take their rabbis as lords besides God. [See the explanation of "subhan" above: 13:102, note 3, and the references there.]

The discourse on the interpretation of His words: ﴿They want to extinguish the light of God with their mouths, but God refuses except to perfect His light, even though the disbelievers dislike it﴾ [9:32].

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The Exalted says: those who take their rabbis and monks, and the Messiah, son of Mary, as lords want ﴿to extinguish the light of God with their mouths﴾, meaning that by denying the religion of God with which He sent His Messenger, and by turning people away from it with their tongues, they try to nullify it. It is the light that God set for His creation as illumination [[See the explanation of "extinguishing" above, 10: 458.]]. ﴿But God refuses except to perfect His light﴾, meaning His religion will prevail, His word will be made manifest, and the truth with which He sent His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) will be completed. ﴿Even though the disbelievers dislike it﴾, meaning God's completion of it, ﴿the disbelievers﴾, meaning those who deny it and reject it.

* *

The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) have said things similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

16644. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿They want to extinguish the light of God with their mouths﴾: he said, "They want to extinguish Islam with their speech."

The commentary on the words of Allah: ﴿He it is who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religion, even though the polytheists dislike it﴾ (33)

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may He be exalted and remembered, says: Allah is the One who refuses anything but the completion of His religion, even if its deniers and rejecters dislike it. ﴿He who sent His Messenger﴾, Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿with guidance﴾, meaning: with the clarification of Allah's obligations upon His creation and all that is incumbent upon them, ﴿and the religion of truth﴾, which is Islam. ﴿That He may make it prevail over all religion﴾, meaning: that He may elevate Islam above all the (other) creeds, ﴿even though the polytheists dislike it﴾, [dislike] its prevalence over them, by Allah's (will).

* *

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have differed concerning the meaning of His words: ﴿That He may make it prevail over all religion﴾.

Some of them said: That refers to the time of the descent of Jesus, when all creeds will become one.

Those who said this:

16645. Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, who said: Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan narrated to us, who said: Shaqiq narrated to us, who said: Thabit al-Haddad, Abu al-Miqdam, narrated to me, from a shaykh, from Abu Hurairah, regarding His words: ﴿That He may make it prevail over all religion﴾, he said: At the time of the coming of Jesus son of Mary.

16646. Ibn Wakee' narrated to us, who said: Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Fudayl ibn Marzuq, who said: Someone who heard Abu Ja'far narrated to me: ﴿That He may make it prevail over all religion﴾, he said: When Jesus, peace be upon him, comes forth, every religion will follow him.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: that He may teach him all the laws of the religion and make him aware of them.

Those who said this:

Al-Muthanna narrated to me, who said: Abu Salih narrated to us, who said: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿That He may make it prevail over all religion﴾, he said: That Allah may make His Prophet prevail over all matters of religion, so that He gives him all of it, and nothing of it remains hidden from him. And the polytheists and the Jews disliked that.

**The interpretation of His saying:** ﴿O you who have believed, indeed, many of the rabbis and the monks consume the wealth of people unjustly and avert [people] from the way of God﴾ [9:34].

Abu Ja'far [al-Tabari] said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: O you who have believed in God and His Messenger, and acknowledged the oneness of your Lord, indeed many of the scholars and reciters among the Children of Israel, from the Jews and the Christians [[See the explanation of "al-ahbar" and "al-ruhban" above, p. 209, note 2, and p. 208, note 2, and the references there.]] ﴿consume the wealth of people unjustly﴾: that is, they take bribes in their judgements, distort the Book of God, write books with their own hands and then say, "This is from God," and take a small price for them from their lowly [possessions]. [[See the explanation of "consuming wealth unjustly" above, vol. 9, p. 392, note 1, and the references there.]] ﴿And avert [people] from the way of God﴾: that is, they prevent those who want to enter Islam from entering it, by forbidding them from it. [[See the explanation of "al-sadd" above, p. 151, note 1, and the references there. And the explanation of "the way of God" in the lexical indices (s-b-l).]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the opinions on this is the view reported from Ibn Umar: that any wealth whose zakat has been paid is not a hoard, and its hoarding is prohibited for its owner even if it is large; and that any wealth whose zakat has not been paid, its owner is liable and deserves God's threat, unless God graciously pardons him, even if it is little, provided it is of the kind on which zakat is obligatory.

And that is because God obligated, through the tongue of His Messenger, a fortieth of one-fourth... [translation below]

Let me give the translation accurately:

That is because God obligated, through the tongue of His Messenger, on five awqiyah of silver (al-warq, meaning silver) a quarter of its tenth, and on twenty mithqals of gold the same, a quarter of its tenth. Since God made this obligatory on gold and silver through the tongue of His Messenger, it is known that much wealth, even if it reaches thousands upon thousands in quantity, if it were treasure (kunuz) for which God threatened its owners with punishment, then even if its zakat were paid, it would not carry the zakat we mentioned, a quarter of the tenth. For what is obligatory is to remove all of it from one's wealth, and its holding is forbidden; so its zakat is to come out of all of it to its people, not a quarter of its tenth. This is like usurped property, which is forbidden for the usurper to keep, and obligatory for him to remove from his hand to another's hand, its purification being its return to its owner. So if what exceeds four thousand dirhams, or what is beyond the owner's necessary need, which its possessor deserves for holding it, if he pays to the people of the shares (ahl al-suhman) their rights from it as charity, [still] incurs God's threat, then the one bound (lazim) to its owner would not owe a quarter of its tenth; rather, what is required of him is to remove all of it to its people and spend it on what he must spend it on, just as we mentioned about the one obligated to return a man's wealth to its owner when he has usurped it.

* *

Now then, among what is:

16667 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar said: Suhayl ibn Abi Salih informed me, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "There is no man who does not pay the zakat of his wealth except that it will be made on the Day of Resurrection into plates of fire, with which his forehead, his brow and his back will be branded, on a day whose measure is fifty thousand years, until judgment is passed between the people, then he will see his path. And if it is camels, [they will] be made to lie flat on a level plain (qa'r qarqar), trampling him with their hooves" — I think he said: "and biting him with their mouths" — "one after the other returning to the first, until judgment is passed between the people, then he will see his path. And if it is sheep, it is similar, except that they will gore him with their horns and trample him with their hooves."

* *

And in the like of these reports, which we disliked to lengthen by mentioning, is clear evidence that the threat is from God only upon wealth on which the obligatory dues were not paid to their people from charity, not upon possessing and hoarding it. And in what we have shown there is clear explanation that the verse is particular, as Ibn 'Abbas said, and that is what:

16668 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: "And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of God, give them tidings of a painful punishment" [9:34] — he says: they are the People of the Book. And he said: it is both particular and general.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: By his saying "it is both particular and general," he means: it is particular to Muslims regarding whoever among them did not pay the zakat of his wealth, and general regarding the People of the Book, because they are disbelievers and their expenditures are not accepted if they spend. Evidence for the correctness of what we have said in the interpretation of this saying of Ibn 'Abbas is what:

16669 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words: "And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it" up to His words: "This is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard" [9:35] — he said: they are those who do not pay the zakat of their wealth. He said: every wealth whose zakat is not paid is a hoard, whether it is on the surface of the earth or in its belly; and every wealth whose zakat is paid is not a hoard, whether it is on the surface of the earth or in its belly.

16670 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "And those who hoard gold and silver": "The hoard" is what is hoarded apart from obedience to God and His obligation, and that is "the hoard." He said: zakat and prayer were both made obligatory, not distinguished between.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: We only said "it is particular" because "kanz" (hoard) in the speech of the Arabs is: everything gathered, some of it upon the other, whether in the belly of the earth or on its surface. The poet's verse indicates this:

[Poetry: al-Mutanakhkhil al-Hudhali's verse, and the commentary on the lines as given in the source — "Lā darra darrī..." etc.]

He means by it: "and with me the wheat is gathered, some of it upon the other." Likewise the Arabs say of a body gathered together: "mukhtaniz" (compact), because some of it is joined to another.

And when this is the meaning of "kanz" among them, and His words "And those who hoard gold and silver" mean: those who gather gold and silver, some of it onto others, and do not spend it in the way of God, and it is general in recitation, and there was no clarification in the verse of how much of gold and silver, when gathered some onto others, deserves the threat — it was known that the particularity of this was only realized by the Messenger's explanation of it, as we showed: that it is the wealth whose God-right of zakat was not paid, to the exclusion of other things, due to the evidence we have clarified for its soundness.

Some of the Companions used to say: it is general in every hoard, except that it is particular to the People of the Book, and it is them God meant by it.

Mention of those who said that:

16671 - Abu Husayn 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Husayn narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Wahb, who said: I passed by al-Rabadha and met Abu Dharr, and I said: "O Abu Dharr, what brought you to these lands?" He said: "I was in Syria, and I recited this verse: 'And those who hoard gold and silver,' etc. Mu'awiyah said: 'This verse is not about us; it is about the People of the Book!' I said: 'It is about us and about them!'" He said: the speech between me and him escalated, so he wrote to 'Uthman complaining of me, and 'Uthman wrote to me to come to him. So I came, and when I arrived in Medina the people rode me as though they had not seen me before that day. I complained of that to 'Uthman, and he said to me: "Withdraw nearby." I said: "By God, I will not abandon what I used to say!"

16672 - Abu Kurayb, Abu al-Sa'ib and Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: Husayn narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Wahb, who said: "We passed by al-Rabadha," then he mentioned similar from Abu Dharr.

16673 - Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Ash'ath and Hisham, from Abu Bishr, who said: Abu Dharr said: "I went out to Syria and recited this verse: 'And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of God.' Mu'awiyah said: 'It is only about the People of the Book!' I said: 'It is about us and about them.'"

16674 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Husayn informed us, from Zayd ibn Wahb, who said: I passed by al-Rabadha, and there I found Abu Dharr. I said to him: "What brought you to this place?" He said: "I was in Syria, and I disputed with Mu'awiyah about this verse..." — he said: he said: "It was revealed about the People of the Book." I said: "It was revealed about us and about them" — then he mentioned something like the hadith of Hushaym from Husayn.

* *

If someone says: Why was it said "and do not spend it in the way of God," bringing the "ha'" and the "alif" in the form of a pronoun referring to one of the two types?

It is said: this may have two aspects:

One: that "gold and silver" is meant as the hoards, as if it were said: "those who hoard the hoards and do not spend them in the way of God," because gold and silver are "the hoards" in this place.

The other: that he dispensed with the report about one of them in the pronoun referring to them, from the report about the other, because the speech indicates the report about the other is like the report about it. This is common in the speech and poetry of the Arabs, and among it is the poet's saying: [poem by 'Amr ibn Imru' al-Qays...]

"We are content with what we have, and you with what you have, though opinions differ," so he said "radin" and did not say "ridwan". Another said [Hassan ibn Thabit]: "The youth's prime and black hair, as long as it is not disobeyed, is madness," so he said "yu'as" and did not say "yu'asiyā", in many things. Among it is God's saying: "And when they see a trade or amusement, they scatter to it" [62:11], and He did not say "ilayhimā" (to both of them).

**The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 9, Verse 35**

Concerning the interpretation of His saying: ﴿On the Day when it will be heated in the fire of Hell, and their foreheads, their sides and their backs will be branded with it: "This is what you hoarded for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard."﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: So give them tidings, O Muhammad, of a painful punishment, [namely] those who hoard gold and silver and do not pay the rights of Allah from them. ﴿On the Day when it will be heated in the fire of Hell﴾. Thus "the Day" is connected to "a painful punishment," as if it were said: He gives them tidings of a painful punishment, with which Allah will punish them on a day when it is heated.

By His saying ﴿it will be heated﴾ is meant that it will be put into the Fire and kindled upon, i.e., the gold and silver they hoarded. ﴿in the fire of Hell, and their foreheads, their sides and their backs will be branded with it﴾.

* *

Everything that is put into the fire is said to have been "heated" (uhmiya ihmaan). It is said from this: "I heated the iron bar in the fire, I heat it, heating (ihmaan)."

* *

As for His saying ﴿their foreheads will be branded with it﴾, it means: with the hoarded gold and silver, which will be heated in the fire of Hell, with which Allah will brand [them]. He says: Allah will burn the foreheads of those who hoard them, and their sides and their backs. ﴿This is what you hoarded﴾, and its meaning is: and it will be said to them: "This is what you hoarded in the world, O disbelievers, who withheld your treasures from the obligatory duties of Allah concerning them, for yourselves." ﴿So taste what you used to hoard﴾. He says: It will be said to them: "Taste the punishment of Allah for what you used to withhold from your wealth, the rights of Allah, and hoard it out of rivalry and boasting." [[See the explanation of "taste" (dhaqa) earlier, p. 15, note 4, and the references there.]]

From His saying ﴿This is what you hoarded﴾ the words "it will be said to them" have been omitted, because the context indicates them.

* *

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said so:

[[The report 16675: Humayd ibn Hilal al-'Adawi is trustworthy but has been spoken of, because he entered the service of the rulers. al-Bazzar said in his Musnad: he did not hear from Abu Dharr. Humayd died during the governorship of Khalid ibn 'Abd Allah al-Qasri over Iraq. It has passed as no. 13768.]]

I have kept what is in the manuscript, which agrees with the narration of Muslim. "Al-khashin" and "al-akhshan," and the feminine "khashinah" and "khashna'," derive from roughness; it means the most rugged of anything. It is said: "a rough man (rajul akhshan, khashin)."]] and he stood over them and said: "Give the hoarders tidings of a heated stone (radf) that will be heated in the fire of Hell, which will be placed on the nipple of one of them until it comes out through the shoulder-blade, and placed on the shoulder-blade until it comes out through the nipple of his breast, shaking." [[Radf (with a fatha and then a sukun): hot stones heated in the fire, with which the Arabs curdle milk and roast meat.]] [[Nughd al-katf (with a damma and sukun, or fatha and sukun) and nagid al-katf: this is at the top of the shoulder, a thin bone at its edge, which moves when the walker walks, i.e., it shakes.]] [[Yatazalzal: i.e., it moves and trembles, as if it slips again and again. Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 36 (part 1 of 2):

The explanation of His saying: ﴿Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve months in the register of Allah from the day He created the heavens and the earth; of them, four are sacred. That is the correct religion. So do not wrong yourselves therein. And fight against the polytheists all together as they fight against you all together. And know that Allah is with the righteous.﴾ (9:36)

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted. He says: Indeed, the number of the months of the year is twelve months in the Book of Allah, in which He has written everything that is to occur in His decree, ﴿from the day He created the heavens and the earth; of them, four are sacred.﴾ He says: Of these twelve months, four are sacred months which the Jahiliyyah used to venerate and hold sacred, and in which they held fighting to be forbidden, to the extent that if a man met the killer of his father during them, he would not touch him. They are: Rajab (Mudar), and three consecutive months: Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, and al-Muharram. Thus the reports from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ are consistent on this.

16684 - Musa b. Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi narrated to us, saying: Zayd b. Hubab narrated to us, saying: Musa b. Ubayda al-Rabadhi narrated to us, saying: Sadaqah b. Yasar narrated to me, from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ delivered a sermon during the Farewell Pilgrimage at Mina, in the middle of the days of Tashriq, and said: "O people, indeed time has returned to its original form as on the day Allah created the heavens and the earth, and indeed the number of months with Allah is twelve months, of which four are sacred: first, Rajab of Mudar, between Jumada and Sha'ban; and Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, and al-Muharram."

[[Narration: 16684 - Musa b. Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi, a teacher of al-Tabari, who has passed many times, the last being no. 8906.
And Zayd b. Hubab al-Ukli, who has passed many times, including no. 11134.
And Musa b. Ubayda b. Nashit al-Rabadhi, very weak, munkar al-hadith, who has passed many times, including no. 11134.
And Sadaqah b. Yasar al-Jazari, a Makkan, trustworthy, who narrated from Ibn Umar. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and al-Kabir 2/2/294, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/428.
And this chain is weak, due to the weakness of Musa b. Ubayda al-Rabadhi.]]

Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed time has returned to its original form as on the day Allah created the heavens and the earth, and indeed the number of months with Allah is twelve months in the Book of Allah, the day He created the heavens and the earth; of them four are sacred: three consecutive, and Rajab of Mudar between Jumada and Sha'ban."

[[Narration: 16685 - Muhammad b. Mu'ammar b. Rib'i al-Bahrani, a teacher of al-Tabari, trustworthy, one of the teachers of al-Bukhari and Muslim, passed as nos. 241, 3056, 5393.

And "Ash'ath" is Ash'ath b. Abd al-Malik al-Humrani, trustworthy and reliable, biographed in al-Tahdhib and al-Kabir 1/1/431, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/275.

[[Narration: 16686 - This report has a broken chain (munqati'), because Muhammad b. Sirin did not hear from Abu Bakrah. Musa narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sulayman al-Taymi narrated to us, saying: A man in Bahrain narrated to me: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said in his sermon during the Farewell Pilgrimage: "Indeed time has returned to its original form as on the day Allah created the heavens and the earth, and indeed the number of months with Allah is twelve months, three consecutive: Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, and al-Muharram, and Rajab which is between Jumada and Sha'ban."

16688 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Ibn Abi Najih, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve months in the Book of Allah from the day He created the heavens and the earth; of them four are sacred﴾, that the Prophet ﷺ said: three consecutive: Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, and al-Muharram, and Rajab which is between Jumada and Sha'ban.

16689 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said in his sermon on the day of Mina: "Indeed time has returned to its original form as on the day Allah created the heavens and the earth, and indeed the number of months with Allah is twelve months, of which four are sacred: three consecutive: Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, and al-Muharram, and Rajab of Mudar which is between Jumada and Sha'ban."

* *
This is the view of the majority of the exegetes.
Those who said so:

16690 - Muhammad b. al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad b. al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve months in the Book of Allah from the day He created the heavens and the earth; of them four are sacred﴾: As for "four sacred", they are Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, al-Muharram, and Rajab. As for "the Book of Allah", it is that which is with Him.

16691 - Muhammad b. Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of Allah: "Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve months": he said: by it is known the matter of the nasi' (intercalation), what is reduced from the year.

16692 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve months in the Book of Allah﴾: he said: by it is mentioned the matter of the nasi'.

* *
