As for His saying: ﴿That is the correct religion﴾, its meaning is: this which I have informed you of, that the number of months with Allah is twelve months in the Book of Allah, and that of them four are sacred, is the upright religion, as:

16693 - Muhammad b. al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad b. al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿That is the correct religion﴾, he says: the upright.

16694 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd, regarding His saying: ﴿That is the correct religion﴾, said: the upright matter. He says: Allah the Exalted said: "Know, O people, that the number of months with Allah is twelve months in the Book of Allah, in which He has written everything that is to occur, and that of these twelve months four are sacred months, that is the upright religion of Allah, not what the nasi' does by making lawful what he makes lawful of the months of the year and making unlawful what he makes unlawful of them." [["al-Nasi'", thus it came in the manuscript also, meaning "al-Nasi'" (the one who intercalates), who used to make a month lawful for them and forbid it. I fear it may be a scribal error, for "al-Nasi'" is on the pattern "fa'il" and means "maf'ul", or is the verbal noun of "nasa'a al-shahr"; and I have not seen them call the man anything but "nasi'", its plural "nasa'ah", like "fasiq" and "fasaqah".
See what will come later in the explanation of "al-Nasi'", p. 343, and reports nos. 16708, 16709, and the note there.]]

As for His saying: ﴿So do not wrong yourselves therein﴾, its meaning is: do not disobey Allah therein, and do not make lawful therein what Allah has forbidden to you, so that you earn for yourselves what they cannot bear of Allah's wrath and punishment. As:

16695 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿So do not wrong yourselves therein﴾: wronging is acting in disobedience to Allah and abandoning His obedience.

* *
Then the exegetes differed regarding what the "ha'" and "nun" in His saying ﴿therein﴾ refer back to.

Some of them said: It refers back to "the twelve months", and said: its meaning is: do not wrong yourselves in all the months. [[In the printed edition: "upon the twelve months", and I have confirmed what is in the manuscript.]]

Those who said so:

16696 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve months in the Book of Allah from the day He created the heavens and the earth; of them four are sacred. That is the correct religion. So do not wrong yourselves therein﴾: in all of them. Then He singled out four months from that and made them sacred, and magnified their sacredness, and made the sin therein greater, and the righteous deed and its reward greater.

16697 - Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Suwayd b. Amr narrated to us, from Hammad b. Salamah, from Ali b. Zayd, from Yusuf b. Mihran, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿So do not wrong yourselves therein﴾, he said: in all the months.

* *
Others said: Rather, the meaning is: do not wrong yourselves in the four sacred months = and the "ha'" and "nun" refer to "the four months".

Those who said so:

16698 - Bishr b. Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: As for His saying: ﴿So do not wrong yourselves therein﴾, wronging in the sacred months is a greater sin and burden than wronging in other than them, though wronging is great in every case; but Allah magnifies what He wills of His command. He said: Indeed Allah has chosen select creatures from His creation: from the angels He chose messengers, from mankind He chose messengers, from speech He chose His remembrance, from the earth He chose the mosques, from the months He chose Ramadan and the sacred months, from the days He chose Friday, from the nights He chose the Night of Power. So magnify what Allah has magnified, for affairs are magnified only by what Allah has magnified in the eyes of people of understanding and intellect.

* *
Others said: Rather, the meaning is: do not wrong yourselves by your making the sacredness of the four sacred months lawful and their lawful things unlawful.

Those who said so:

16699 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve months﴾, up to His saying: ﴿So do not wrong yourselves therein﴾: i.e., do not make their sacred things lawful nor their lawful things unlawful, as the polytheists did. For the nasi' that they practised is "an increase in disbelief by which those who disbelieve are led astray", and so on. [[Narration: 16699 - Sirah of Ibn Hisham 4:193, and it follows the earlier narration no. 16615.]]

16700 - Muhammad b. Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Qays b. Muslim, from al-Hasan: ﴿So do not wrong yourselves therein﴾, he said: "wronging yourselves" is that you do not treat them as sacred as their sanctity requires.

16701 - al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Qays b. Muslim, from al-Hasan b. Muhammad b. Ali: ﴿So do not wrong yourselves therein﴾, he said: "wronging yourselves" is that you do not treat them as sacred as their sanctity requires.

16702 - Ahmad b. Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Qays b. Muslim, from al-Hasan b. Muhammad, with similar.

* *
Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these sayings in my view, as to its interpretation, is the saying of whoever said: "So do not wrong yourselves in the four sacred months by making lawful their sacredness", for Allah has magnified them and magnified their sanctity.

We only said that this is more correct in its interpretation because of His saying: ﴿So do not wrong yourselves therein﴾, where He brought the pronoun referring to them in the form used for referring to a number between three and ten. For the Arabs, when referring to what is between three and ten, say: "We did that three nights past, and four days remaining", and when they speak of what is above ten up to twenty they say: "We did that thirteen past, and fourteen gone." So in His saying, ﴿So do not wrong yourselves therein﴾, and His bringing the reference to the number of months in which He forbade the believers to wrong themselves, in the form of reference to a small plural number from three to ten, there is clear evidence that the "ha'" and "nun" refer to the mention of the four months, not the twelve. For if it were a reference to "the twelve months", it would have been: "So do not wrong yourselves in them." [[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:435.]]

* *
If someone says: What prevents this from being a reference to "the twelve", even though what you mentioned is the familiar usage of the Arabs? For you know that [from] the familiar usage of the Arabs, [[In the printed edition and manuscript: "that the familiar usage of them", and the context requires the insertion of what is between the brackets, because this objector first acknowledged that what al-Tabari said is "the familiar usage of them", i.e., the well-known and agreed upon. The better course is to object with something else, namely "what is permissible in their usage", and for this reason I added "from" between the brackets, so the statement is consistent.]] the use of a reference to what is between three and ten with the "ha'" without the "nun" occurs; and the poet has said: [[He is Umar b. Lajaʾ al-Taymi.]]

Asbahna fi qurhin wa fi daratiha ... sab'a layalin ghayra ma'lufatiha
[[Hamasah of Abu Tammam 4:157, and Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:435, and al-Lisan (qarh). Not attributed, but it indicates that they are by Umar b. Lajaʾ; verses narrated by al-Asma'i in al-Asma'iyyat pp. 25, 26. "Qurh" (with a damma on the qaf and sukun on the ra') is the market of Wadi al-Qura, where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed and built a mosque; the version in al-Hamasah and al-Lisan is "habasna fi qurh".]]

He did not say "ma'lufatihin", which would refer to the seven?
It is said: That, although permissible, is not the most eloquent and most familiar in their usage. And directing the speech of Allah to what is most eloquent and most familiar is more fitting than directing it to what is most unusual.

* *
If someone says: If the matter is as you describe, then it would have to be permissible for us to wrong ourselves in other months of the year besides them?
It is said: That is not so; rather, that is forbidden to us at every time and in every era. But Allah magnified the sanctity of these months and honoured them above the other months of the year, so He singled out sin in them for magnification, just as He singled them out for honour. This is similar to His saying: ﴿Guard over the prayers and the middle prayer﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 238]. There is no doubt that Allah has commanded us to guard all the obligatory prayers by His saying: ﴿Guard over the prayers﴾, and He did not permit abandoning the guarding of them by commanding the guarding of the middle prayer; rather, He, the Exalted, increased it in magnification, and in guarding it as emphasis, and in neglecting it as intensified severity. Likewise is this in His saying: ﴿of them four are sacred. That is the correct religion. So do not wrong yourselves therein﴾.

* *
As for His saying: ﴿And fight against the polytheists all together as they fight against you all together﴾, He, the Exalted, says: Fight the polytheists who associate others with Allah, O believers, all together, not disagreeing, united, not divided, as the polytheists fight you all together, gathered, not scattered. As:

16703 - Muhammad b. al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad b. al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And fight against the polytheists all together as they fight against you all together﴾: as for "kaffah", it is "all", and your affair is gathered.

16704 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And fight against the polytheists all together﴾, he says: "jami'an" (all).

* *
16705 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And fight against the polytheists all together﴾: i.e., all.

* *
"Kaffah" is in every case in one form; it is not made masculine or plural, for although it is in the form of "fa'ilah", it has the meaning of a verbal noun, like "al-'afiyah" and "al-'aqibah". The Arabs do not attach "al" to it, since it is the last word of the sentence, together with what it carries of the meaning of a verbal noun, just as they did not attach it when they say "qamu ma'an" and "qamu jami'an". [[See the explanation of "kaffah" in what preceded, 4:257, 258, and see Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:436.]]

* *

Now as for His saying, ﴿And know that Allah is with the God-fearing﴾, its meaning is: Know, O believers in Allah, that if you fight the polytheists all together, and you are mindful of Allah (ittaqaytum Allah) by obeying Him in what He has commanded you and forbidden you, and do not oppose His command so as to disobey Him, then Allah will be with you against your enemy and His enemy among the polytheists. And whoever has Allah with him, nothing will overcome him, [[See the explanation of "ma'a" (with) above, 13:576, footnote 2, and the references there.]] because Allah is with those who are mindful of Him, fear Him, and obey Him in what He has imposed upon them of His commands and prohibitions.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 9, verse 37 (part 1 of 2)

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿Indeed, the postponing (al-nasi') is an increase in disbelief by which those who disbelieve are led astray. They make it lawful one year and make it unlawful another year, to conform with the number of what Allah has made unlawful, and so make lawful what Allah has made unlawful. The evil of their deeds is made attractive to them. And Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.﴾ (9:37)

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, means: The postponing is nothing but an increase in disbelief.
* *
And "al-nasi'" (postponing) is a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker, "nasa'tu fi ayyamika" and "nasa'a Allahu fi ajalika," meaning: Allah increased the days of your life and the duration of your lifetime, so that you remain alive in them. And every increase that occurs in a thing, the thing in which that increase occurs because of what happened in it is called "nasi'." For this reason milk that has been diluted with water is called "nasi'," a pregnant woman is called "nasu'," and "nusi'at al-mar'ah" (the woman was made to have an increase), because of the increase of the child in her. It is also said: "nasa'tu al-naqah wa-ansa'tuha" when I drove the she-camel so that her pace would increase.
It is possible that "al-nasi'" is an "fa'il" form turned from "maf'ul," as it is said "la'in" and "qatil," meaning cursed and killed. Its meaning would then be: indeed the postponed month is an increase in disbelief.
The first opinion, however, seems closer to the meaning of the speech, namely that it means: indeed the postponement which the people of polytheism postpone of the four sacred months, and their making the forbidden among them lawful and the lawful among them forbidden, is an increase in their disbelief and their denial of the rulings and signs of Allah.
* *
Some reciters used to read it: ﴿innama al-nasy﴾ without the hamza and without its lengthening, and: ﴿yudall bihi alladhina kafaru﴾.
* *
The reciters differed concerning the recitation of this.
The common reading of the people of Kufa was: ﴿yaḍallu bihi alladhina kafaru﴾, meaning: Allah leads astray by the postponing which they devised and originated, those who disbelieve.
* *
The common reading of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the Kufans, was: ﴿yuḍillu bihi alladhina kafaru﴾, meaning: it departs from the path of Allah which He made a way for His servants to follow toward His pleasure, those who disbelieve.
* *
It has been related from al-Hasan al-Basri: ﴿yuḍillu bihi alladhina kafaru﴾, meaning: by the postponing which those who disbelieve instituted, they lead astray the people.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The correct position on this is to say that these are two well-known readings, each recited by the reciters of knowledge of the Qur'an and those knowledgeable in it, and their meanings are close. For whoever Allah misguides is "dall" (astray), and whoever goes astray does so by Allah's misguiding him and forsaking him. So whichever of the two a reciter reads, he is correct in that.
* *
As for the correct reading of "al-nasi'," it is with the hamza, and it is recited in the form "fa'il," because it is the widely transmitted reading among the reciters of the cities, which it is not permissible to oppose in what they have agreed upon.
* *
As for His words: ﴿yuḥillūnahu 'aman﴾, its meaning is: those who disbelieve make the postponing lawful, and the pronoun in His words ﴿yuḥillūnahu﴾ refers back to it.
The meaning of the speech: they make lawful the thing whose prohibition they postponed, of the four sacred months, one year, ﴿and make it unlawful another year, to conform with the number of what Allah has made unlawful﴾, meaning: by their making lawful what they made lawful of the months and their making unlawful what they made unlawful of them, to match the number of what Allah has made unlawful. ﴿So they make lawful what Allah has made unlawful﴾, meaning: the evil of their deeds is made attractive and beloved to them, and what opposes the command and obedience of Allah. ﴿And Allah does not guide the disbelieving people﴾, meaning: Allah does not grant success to the good and beautiful acts, and what is pleasing to Him, to the people who deny His Oneness and reject the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ). Rather He forsakes them from guidance, just as they forsook these people from the sacred months.
* *
Those among the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) who said the like of what we have said in this:
Mention of those who said that:
16706. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words: ﴿Indeed, the postponing is an increase in disbelief﴾. He said: "Al-nasi'" is that Junadah ibn 'Awf ibn Umayyah al-Kinani used to attend the pilgrimage season every year, and he was called Abu Thumamah, and he would proclaim: "Verily Abu Thumamah is not rebuked and not blamed, and verily Safar of the first year is lawful for the year," so the people would make it lawful, and Safar would be made unlawful one year and al-Muharram made unlawful one year. That is His words: ﴿Indeed, the postponing is an increase in disbelief﴾ up to His words: ﴿the disbelieving﴾. And His words: ﴿Indeed, the postponing is an increase in disbelief﴾: they leave the forbidden month one year, and make it forbidden another year.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: This interpretation from Ibn 'Abbas indicates the correctness of the reading of the one who read ﴿al-nasy﴾ without the hamza and without the lengthening, and directing the meaning to it being a "fa'l," from the saying of the speaker, "nasitu al-shay' ansa'uhu" (I forgot the thing), and from the words of Allah: ﴿They forgot Allah, so He forgot them﴾ (9:67), meaning: they abandoned Allah, so He abandoned them.
16707. Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Indeed, the postponing is an increase in disbelief﴾. He said: it is the making forbidden; it used to make one year forbidden, and Safar one year, and another Safar was added among the sacred months, and they used to make Safar forbidden once and lawful once, so Allah rebuked that. Hawazin, Ghatafan and Banu Sulaym used to do it.
16708. Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Abu Wa'il: ﴿Indeed, the postponing is an increase in disbelief﴾. He said: "al-Nasi'" was a man from Banu Kinanah, who had an opinion among them, and he would make the forbidden month Safar as a custom, so they would raid in it, take booty in it, and gain, and he would make it forbidden for a year.
16709. ...... He said: my father related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Abu Wa'il: ﴿Indeed, the postponing is an increase in disbelief﴾, the verse. There was a man from Banu Kinanah called "al-Nasi'," who would make the forbidden month Safar and would treat as lawful the spoils in it, so this verse was revealed.
16710. Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Idris related to us, saying: I heard Layth, from Mujahid, who said: A man from Banu Kinanah used to come every year to the pilgrimage season on his donkey, and say: "O people, verily I am not blamed and not rebuked, and there is no refusal to what I say. Verily we have made the forbidden forbidden and postponed Safar." Then the following year he would come and say the same statement, and say: "Verily we have made Safar forbidden and postponed the forbidden," and that is His words: ﴿to conform with the number of what Allah has made unlawful﴾. He said: meaning the four; ﴿so they make lawful what Allah has made unlawful﴾, because of the postponing of this sacred month.
16711. It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His words: ﴿Indeed, the postponing is an increase in disbelief﴾: "al-Nasi'" is the forbidden (month); he used to make al-Muharram forbidden one year and Safar forbidden one year, so the increase is Safar. They used to postpone the months until they made Safar al-Muharram, and so they made lawful what Allah had made unlawful. Hawazin, Ghatafan and Banu Sulaym used to glorify it, and they were the ones who did that in the pre-Islamic era.
16712. Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿Indeed, the postponing is an increase in disbelief﴾, up to His words: ﴿the disbelieving﴾. Some people of misguidance deliberately added Safar to the sacred months. Their leader would stand in the pilgrimage season and say: "Verily your gods have made al-Muharram forbidden this year," so they would make it forbidden that year. Then the following year he would say: "Verily your gods have made Safar forbidden," so they would make it forbidden that year. And these two were called "al-Safarain." He said: The first to postpone the postponing were Banu Malik ibn Kinanah, and they were three: Abu Thumamah Safwan ibn Umayyah, one of Banu Fuqaym ibn al-Harith, then one of Banu Kinanah. [Note in the printed edition: The manuscript has "and they were three," and then only one is mentioned. Regarding "Abu Thumamah, Safwan ibn Umayyah": an earlier report (no. 16706) said that Abu Thumamah is Junadah ibn 'Awf ibn Umayyah; as for this Safwan, Abu 'Ubayd al-Bakri mentioned him in Sharh al-Amali, saying: al-Laythi said: the one who took up the nasi' was al-Qalmas, who is Safwan ibn Mahrath of Banu Malik ibn Kinanah... Ibn Habib in al-Muhabbar and Ibn Hisham in his Sirah related from Ibn Ishaq the list: al-Qalmas, Hudhayfah ibn 'Abd ibn Fuqaym..., then 'Awf ibn Umayyah, then Abu Thumamah Junadah ibn 'Awf, the last of them, and upon him Islam came. ... Safwan ibn Mahrath mentioned by al-Bakri is Safwan ibn Umayyah mentioned in this report, of the lineage of Banu Makhdaj ibn 'Amir ibn Tha'labah, not Banu Fuqaym ibn al-Harith... See also the note on al-Qalmas in the verse of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hakam.]
I did not find this report elsewhere, so I cannot verify the statement of Qatadah concerning the matter of the nasi' and the nasa'ah.
* *
Concerning His words: ﴿zīyādatun fi al-kufr﴾, its meaning is: an increase of disbelief in the postponing, in addition to their disbelief in Allah before their devising the postponing, as:-
16717. al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿Indeed, the postponing is an increase in disbelief﴾, meaning: they increased in disbelief through it, in addition to their disbelief.
* *
As for His words: ﴿liyuwāṭi'ū﴾, it comes from the saying of the speaker, "wāṭa'tu fulānan 'alā kadhā uwāti'uhu mu-wāṭa'atan," meaning: when I agree with him upon it, assisting him, not opposing him in it.
* *
It has been related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning this:-
16718. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words: ﴿to conform with the number of what Allah has made unlawful﴾, he said: they resemble it.
* *

Abu Ja'far said: This is close in meaning to what we have explained, because whatever resembles a thing agrees with it in the respect in which it resembles it.

The meaning of the statement is that they agree, in the number of months they make sacred, with the number of the four months which Allah made sacred, neither adding to them nor subtracting from them, even though they shift them around. So that is their matching the number to the number of what Allah has made sacred.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 38:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿O you who believe, what is [the matter] with you that when it is said to you, "Go forth in the cause of Allah," you adhere heavily to the earth? Are you satisfied with the life of this world rather than the Hereafter? But the enjoyment of the worldly life, compared to the Hereafter, is but little.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: This verse is an exhortation from Allah, glorified is His praise, to the believers among the Companions of His Messenger to fight the Romans. This refers to the expedition of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to Tabuk.

He, glorified is His praise, says: O you who have affirmed Allah and His Messenger. ﴿What is [the matter] with you?﴾ That is, what is your situation? ﴿When it is said to you, "Go forth in the cause of Allah,"﴾ that is, when Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, says to you, ﴿"Go forth,"﴾ that is, leave your dwellings for your campaign.

* *

The root of *al-nafr* (to go forth) is departing from one place to another because of a matter that stirs one to do so. From it comes the expression *nafarat al-dabbah* (the animal bolted). However, it is said of going forth to a military expedition: *nafara fulan ila thaghr kadha yanfiru naft̤ran wa nafīran* (so-and-so set out for such-and-such a frontier). I think this is one of the distinctions by which they differentiate the various ways in which the subject is described, [[Abu Ja'far means that they did not say *nufūran* as the verbal noun for going forth to military expedition, although lexicographical books have confirmed that it is said in its verbal noun *nafara ila al-ghazw nufūran*.]] even though the meanings of the statement are the same. [[See *al-nafr* above, 8:536, where he did not explain it there.]]

* *

So the meaning of the speech is: What is [the matter] with you, O believers, that when it is said to you, "Go forth as raiders"? ﴿"In the cause of Allah,"﴾ that is, in the struggle against the enemies of Allah. [[See the interpretation of *sabīl Allah* above in the lexical indexes (s-b-l).]] ﴿You adhere heavily to the earth﴾ means you cling heavily to remaining in your land and dwellings and sitting in them.

* *

It has been said: *ithāqaltum* (you adhere heavily) has the *tā'* assimilated into the *thā'*, and an *alif* was introduced for it [[In the printed edition: "because he assimilated the *tā'* into the *thā'* and introduced an *alif* for it." In the manuscript it read "because he *ghām*," which the copyist did not read well, so he altered the sentence. I have restored it correctly from the manuscript. See what has passed on assimilation, 2:224.]] so that speech could be reached through it, because the *tā'* is assimilated into the *thā'*. Had the *alif* been dropped and the word begun with it, it would only have been vowelled, so the *alif* was introduced so that the vowel would fall upon it, as He, glorified is His praise, said: ﴿Until, when they had all overtaken one another therein﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 38], and as the poet said: [[I did not know who said it.]]

*She turns away from her bedfellow when he inhales her slender waist,*
*sweet of taste, when kisses follow one another.*

[[Its explanation and interpretation have passed just above, 2:223, and in the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:438.]]

[So it is from *al-thiql* (heaviness), and its figurative sense is that of *if'altum* (the form *if'altum*)] from *al-tathāqul* (to be heavy). [[The position of this sentence in the printed edition reads: "so he built the verb *if'altum* from *al-tathaqul*," which is very poor speech. In the manuscript it reads: "so it is between the verb *if'altum* from *al-tathaqul*," unpointed, and I corrected this phrase by judgement, relying on what Abu 'Ubaydah said in Majaz al-Qur'an 1:260, where he says: "*Majaz* of *ithāqaltum* is the *majaz* of *if'altum*, from *al-tathāqul*, so the *tā'* was assimilated into the *thā'*, and it became heavy and doubled." Abu 'Ubaydah means that if you formed *if'al* from *al-thiql*, assimilating the *tā'* into the *thā'* would have been necessary. See also the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:437, 438.]]

As for His words: ﴿Are you satisfied with the life of this world rather than the Hereafter?﴾ He, glorified is His praise, says: Are you content with the share of this world, its ease and comfort, in exchange for the bliss of the Hereafter and what Allah has prepared for the God-fearing in His gardens? ﴿But the enjoyment of the worldly life, compared to the Hereafter﴾ means: what is it that those who enjoy the worldly life gain from its living and its pleasures, compared with the bliss of the Hereafter and the honour that Allah has prepared for His friends and the people of His obedience? [[See the interpretation of *matā'* (enjoyment) above in the lexical indexes (m-t-').]] ﴿Is but little﴾, meaning insignificant. He is saying to them: So seek, O believers, the bliss of the Hereafter and the nobility of the honour that is with Allah for His friends, [[In the printed edition: "and the luxury of honour," but the correct reading is in the manuscript.]] through obedience to Him and hastening to answer His command to go forth to struggle against His enemy.

* *

And in accordance with what we have said about this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have spoken.

Those who said that:

16719. Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿What is [the matter] with you when it is said to you, "Go forth in the cause of Allah," you adhere heavily to the earth?﴾ They were commanded to the expedition of Tabuk after the conquest, after al-Ta'if, and after Hunayn. They were commanded to go forth in the summer, when the dates were being harvested [[*Kharafa al-nakhl yakhrifuhu kharfan, wa-ikhtarafahu ikhtirafan*: he cut its fruit and gathered it after it had ripened.]] and the fruits were ripe, and they craved shade, and the journey was hard upon them.

16720. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿O you who believe, what is [the matter] with you when it is said to you, "Go forth in the cause of Allah," you adhere heavily to the earth?﴾ The verse. He said: This was when they were commanded to the expedition of Tabuk after the conquest, after Hunayn, and after al-Ta'if. He commanded them to go forth in the summer, when the dates had been harvested, the fruits were ripe, they craved shade, and the journey was hard upon them. He said: They said, "The heavy one," meaning the one with needs, the one with a dependent family, the one with work, [[In the printed edition: "They said: among us are the heavy one, the one with needs, the one with a dependent family..." which differs from the manuscript; what I have written is the manuscript reading. It is acceptable, though I suspect something may have dropped from the speech. His statement "the heavy one: the one with needs and dependents" is the explanation of His words (Go forth, light and heavy), the plural of *thaqīl*, as you will see in the explanation of the verse, p. 262 and following.]] and the one whose affair was spread about in all of that. Then Allah revealed: ﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 41].

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Unless you go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment and will replace you with another people, and you will not harm Him at all. And Allah is over all things competent.﴾ (9:39)

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, mentioning those believers among the Companions of His Messenger, threatening them for abandoning going forth (al-nafr) against their enemy, the Romans: If you do not go forth, O believers, to those whom the Messenger of Allah has called you to go forth against, Allah will punish you swiftly in this world for your abandoning going forth to them, with a painful punishment [[See the explanation of "al-nafr" above, p. 249.]] = ﴿and will replace you with another people﴾, meaning: Allah will replace you, along with His Prophet, with a people other than you who will go forth when called upon to go forth, who will answer him when he summons them, and who will obey Allah and His Messenger [[See the explanation of "al-istibdal" above, vol. 8, p. 123, note 2, and the references there.]] = ﴿and you will not harm Him at all﴾, meaning: you will not harm Allah at all by your abandoning the march and your disobedience to Him, because He has no need of you; rather, you are the ones in need of Him, He is Self-Sufficient above you, and you are the poor = ﴿And Allah is over all things competent﴾, meaning, may His praise be exalted: Allah is competent to destroy you, to replace you with another people, and over everything He wills among things. [[See the explanation of "qadir" above in the lexical indices, under (q-d-r).]]

* *

It has been mentioned that "the painful punishment" in this place was the withholding of rain from them.

Those who said this:

16721. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Zayd ibn al-Habbab narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Mu'min ibn Khalid al-Hanafi narrated to me, saying: Najdah al-Khurasani narrated to me, saying: I heard Ibn Abbas being asked about His saying: ﴿Unless you go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment﴾. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called upon a tribe of the Arabs to go forth, and they were sluggish in responding to him, so the rain was withheld from them, and that was their punishment. That is His saying: ﴿Unless you go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment.﴾ [[The report 16721: "Zayd ibn al-Habbab al-Ukli," mentioned many times, the last being no. 16684.

"Abd al-Mu'min ibn Khalid al-Hanafi" is trustworthy, passed at no. 11914.

"Najdah al-Khurasani" is: "Najdah ibn Nafi' al-Hanafi," trustworthy, also passed at no. 11914.

This report al-Tabari narrates below as no. 16722, by way of Yahya ibn Wadih, from Abd al-Mu'min.

Abu Dawud narrated it in his Sunan 3:16, no. 2506, by way of Zayd ibn al-Habbab, in abridged form. al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan 9:48, in similar wording. al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur 3:239, and attributed it further to Ibn al-Mundhir, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Hakim, who authenticated it.]]

16722. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Mu'min narrated to us, from Najdah, who said: I asked Ibn Abbas, and he mentioned something similar, except that he said: "Their punishment was that the rain was withheld from them." [[Report 16722 is a repetition of the preceding report. This wording, "the rain," is also the wording of Abu Dawud and al-Bayhaqi, by way of Zayd ibn al-Habbab mentioned above.]]

16723. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿Unless you go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment﴾. Allah called upon the believers to go forth in the intense heat during the expedition of Tabuk toward Syria, [["Lahaban al-harr" (with a fatha on the lam and the ha) means its intensity on sand heated by the sun. It is said "a day of lahaban," as an adjective, meaning intensely hot. "Al-lahaban" is a verbal noun like "al-lahab," "al-lahib," and "al-lihab" (with a damma on the lam), and it is the blazing of fire once it has cleared of smoke.]] in accordance with what Allah knew of their hardship.

* *

Some have claimed that this verse is abrogated (mansukh).

Those who said this:

16724. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, from al-Husayn, from Yazid, from Ikrimah and al-Hasan al-Basri, who both said, regarding: ﴿Unless you go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment﴾, and he recited: "It was not for the people of Medina and those around them of the Bedouins to remain behind from the Messenger of Allah, nor to prefer themselves over his self..." up to His saying: ﴿that Allah may reward them with the best of what they used to do﴾; and then the verse that follows abrogated it: ﴿And it is not for the believers to go forth all together﴾, up to His saying: ﴿that they may beware﴾. [Surat al-Tawbah: 120–122.]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: There is no report supporting what Ikrimah and al-Hasan said about the abrogation of the ruling of this verse which they cited, such that it must be accepted, nor is there any evidence negating the soundness of that. A number of the Companions and Successors, whom we will mention below, held that the ruling was established by it. It is permissible that His saying: ﴿Unless you go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment﴾ refers to a specific group of people, and that what is meant is those whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called to go forth but who did not go, in accordance with the report we cited from Ibn Abbas.

Since this is the case, His saying: ﴿It was not for the believers to go forth all together﴾ is a prohibition from Allah to the believers against leaving the lands of Islam without a believer remaining in them, and it is a notice from Allah to them that the obligation is to go forth on some of them and not others, namely on those among them who are called to go forth, not on those who are not called. Since this is the case, there is no abrogation of one of the two verses by the other, and the ruling of each of them stands in what it refers to.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 40:

The explanation of His words: ﴿Unless you support him, Allah has already supported him when those who disbelieved expelled him, the second of two. When they were both in the cave, when he said to his companion, "Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This is an announcement from Allah to the Companions of His Messenger ﷺ that He is the One who undertakes to give victory to His Messenger over the enemies of his religion and to make him prevail over them without them, whether they help him or do not help him, and a reminder from Him to them of what He did for him, when he was few in number and the enemy was many. How then would it be with them, when they are many and the enemy is few?

He, may His praise be exalted, says to them: "If you do not go forth, O believers, with My Messenger when he calls you forth to fight, and so support him, then Allah is his Supporter and Helper against his enemy, and He suffices him without you and without your aid and support, just as He supported him ﴿when those who disbelieved expelled him﴾, by Allah, from the Quraysh, from his homeland and his dwelling. ﴿The second of two﴾: he means they expelled him while he was one of the two, that is, one of the two."

* *

Thus the Arabs say, "He is the second of two" meaning one of the two, and "the third of three, the fourth of four", meaning one of the three and one of the four. This differs from their saying, "He is the brother of six, and the boy of seven," because "the brother" and "the boy" are not themselves the six or the seven, whereas "the third of the three" is one of the three.

* *

By His words ﴿the second of two﴾, He, may His praise be exalted, meant the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him), because they were the two who went out fleeing from the Quraysh when they plotted to kill the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they hid in the cave.

* *

His words ﴿when they were both in the cave﴾ mean: when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Abu Bakr (may Allah have mercy on him) were in the cave.

* *

"Al-ghar" (the cave) is a large opening in a mountain.

* *

= ﴿when he said to his companion﴾: that is, when the Messenger of Allah said to his companion Abu Bakr, ﴿Do not grieve﴾. This was because he feared that the pursuers would learn of their location, and he was distressed by that, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, "Do not grieve, for Allah is with us and Allah is our Helper." [[See the explanation of "ma'a" (with) above, p. 240, note 2, and the references there.]]

"The polytheists will not know of us, nor will they reach us."

He, may His praise be exalted, says: Allah has already given him victory over his enemy while he was in this state of fear and few in number. So how would He forsake him and make him need you, when Allah has multiplied his helpers and numbered his armies?

* *

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said what we have said on this matter.

Those who said so:

16725. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Unless you support him﴾: he mentioned what happened at the beginning of his affair when He sent him. Allah says: "I will do that for him and be his Helper, just as I helped him at that time, when he was the second of two."

16726. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿Unless you support him, Allah has already supported him﴾, he said: "He mentioned what happened at the beginning of his affair when he was sent. So Allah will do the same for him, being his Helper as He helped him at that time, ﴿the second of two when they were both in the cave﴾."

16727. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His words ﴿Unless you support him, Allah has already supported him﴾, the verse, he said: "His companion was Abu Bakr. As for 'al-ghar', it is a mountain in Makkah called Thawr."

16728. Abd al-Warith ibn Abd al-Samad narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: Aban al-Attar narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn Urwah narrated to us, from Urwah, who said: When the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) went out, Abu Bakr had a mănīhah (a loan) of sheep which went out to graze for his family. [["Al-manihah" is a sheep or a camel that a man lends to his brother, to milk and benefit from its milk for a year, then return it to him.]] Abu Bakr sent Amir ibn Fuhayrah with the sheep to Thawr. Amir ibn Fuhayrah used to bring those sheep to the Prophet ﷺ in the cave of Thawr, and this is the "cave" which Allah named in the Qur'an. [[The report 16728: this is a part of the book of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr to Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan, which I took out earlier under number 16083 and in many other places. This part of the book is in Tarikh al-Tabari 2: 246.]]

16729. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Jubayr al-Wasiti narrated to me, saying: Affan and Hibban narrated to us, both saying: Hammam narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, that Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) told them, saying: "While I was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the cave, and the feet of the polytheists were above our heads, I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, if one of them were to lift his foot, he would see us!' He said: 'O Abu Bakr, what do you think of two whose third is Allah?'" [[The report 16729: "Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Jubayr al-Wasiti", a teacher of al-Tabari, for whom I have found no biography other than in al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil of Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/302.

"Affan" is "Affan ibn Muslim ibn Abd Allah al-Saffar", trustworthy, one of the teachers of Ahmad and al-Bukhari, passed under number 5392.

"Hibban" is "Hibban ibn Hilal al-Bahili", trustworthy, whom the group (of compilers) narrated from. Passed under number 5472. "Hibban" is with a fatha on the ha, not a kasra.

"Hammam" is "Hammam ibn Yahya ibn Dinar al-Azdi", trustworthy, whom the group narrated from, passed several times, the last being 16306.

"Thabit" is "Thabit ibn Aslam al-Bunani", trustworthy, whom the group narrated from, passed under numbers 2942, 7030.

This report was narrated through the chain of Affan ibn Muslim by Ibn Sa'd in al-Tabaqat 3/1/123, Ahmad in his Musnad number 11, and al-Tirmidhi in his commentary on the verse.

It was narrated through the chain of Hibban ibn Hilal by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (al-Fath 8: 245), and Muslim in his Sahih 15: 149.

Al-Bukhari narrated it through the chain of Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hilal, in his Sahih (al-Fath 7: 9).

Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a sound, strange hadith; it is only transmitted through Hammam. And Hibban ibn Hilal and more than one narrated this hadith from Hammam, similar to this."

Al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr 3: 242, adding its attribution to Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Awanah, Ibn Hibban, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh.]]

16730. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sharik, from Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, from Mujahid, who said: Abu Bakr remained with the Prophet ﷺ in the cave for three nights.

16731. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, regarding ﴿when they were both in the cave﴾, he said: "In the mountain called Thawr, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Abu Bakr remained in it for three nights."

16732. Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from his father, that Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah have mercy on him) when he delivered a sermon said: "Which of you recites 'Surat al-Tawbah'?" [[In the manuscript: "Surat al-Baqarah", which is an error too clear to indicate a correction.]] A man said: "I do." He said: "Recite." When he reached ﴿When he said to his companion, "Do not grieve"﴾, Abu Bakr wept and said: "By Allah, I am his companion." [[The report 16732: "Amr ibn al-Harith ibn Ya'qub al-Ansari al-Misri", trustworthy, whom the group narrated from, passed under number 5973.

His father is "al-Harith ibn Ya'qub ibn Tha'labah, or: ibn Abd Allah, al-Ansari al-Misri". Trustworthy. Biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 1/2/282, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/93.]]

* *

The explanation of His words, may He be exalted: ﴿So Allah sent down His tranquility upon him and supported him with armies you did not see, and made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest, while the word of Allah is the highest. And Allah is Mighty and Wise.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: His praise be exalted says: Allah sent down His calm and tranquility upon His Messenger [[See the explanation of "al-sakinah" (tranquility) above, p. 189, note 1, and the references there.]] = and it has been said: upon Abu Bakr = ﴿and supported him with armies you did not see﴾: that is, He strengthened him with armies from Him of the angels, which you did not see [[See the explanation of "al-ta'yid" (support) above, p. 44, note 3, and the references there.]] = ﴿and made the word of those who disbelieved﴾: which is the word of polytheism = ﴿the lowest﴾: because it was subdued and humiliated, and Allah the Exalted nullified it and wiped out its people. Every subdued and defeated thing is lower than the victor, and the victor is the highest = ﴿and the word of Allah is the highest﴾: that is, the religion of Allah, His monotheism, and the saying "There is no god but Allah", which is His word = ﴿the highest﴾ over polytheism and its people, the prevailing one, [[See the explanation of "al-a'la" (the highest) above, vol. 7, p. 234.]] as in:

16733. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words ﴿and made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest﴾, which is polytheism, ﴿and the word of Allah is the highest﴾, which is "There is no god but Allah."

* *

His words ﴿and the word of Allah is the highest﴾ are a predicate of a subject, not returned upon His words ﴿and made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest﴾, because if that were conjoined to the first "word", it would be in the accusative case. [[The detailed explanation of this is in al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 438, and it is a good and clear discussion.]]

* *

As for His words ﴿and Allah is Mighty (ʿazīz)﴾, He means: ﴿and Allah is Mighty﴾ in His retribution upon those who disbelieve in Him; no one overpowers Him, no victor defeats Him, and no one who punishes is helped by a helper = ﴿Wise (ḥakīm)﴾ in His management of His creation and His disposition of them according to His will. [[See the explanation of "ʿazīz" and "ḥakīm" above, in the language indexes under (ʿ-z-z) and (ḥ-k-m).]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 41 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Go forth, light and heavy, and strive with your wealth and your persons in the way of Allah. That is better for you, if you only knew.﴾ (41)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the meaning of "lightness" (al-khiffah) and "heaviness" (al-thiql), by which Allah commanded whoever had one of them to go forth with Him.

Some of them said: The "lightness" that Allah intended in this place is youth, and the "heaviness" is old age.

Mention of those who said this:

16734 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from ʿAnbasah, from a man, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying: ﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾, he said: the aged and the young.

16735 - Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: Hafs narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from al-Hasan, who said: the elders and the young.

16736 - ...... He said: Ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us, from ʿAli ibn Zayd, from Anas, from Abu Talhah, regarding ﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾, he said: the middle-aged and the young. "I do not hear that Allah has excused anyone!" So he went out to Syria and fought until he died. [[In the printed edition: "ʿudhr aḥadan" ("excused anyone"), and I have established what is in the manuscript.
The narration 16736: "ʿAli ibn Zayd ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Mulaykah", has passed several times and is trustworthy. My brother al-Sayyid Ahmad, in what preceded, no. 4897: Ahmad and others spoke of him, saying: "weak in narration." "Anas" is "Anas ibn Malik", servant of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).
"Abu Talhah" is "Zayd ibn Sahl al-Ansari", companion of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who witnessed al-ʿAqabah, Badr, and all the battles.
This report was narrated by Ibn Saʿd in al-Tabaqat 3/2/66 through the route of ʿAffan ibn Muslim, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Thabit and ʿAli ibn Yazid, from Anas, at length, with wording other than this. al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak 3:353 by this same route and said: "This is a sound hadith according to the condition of Muslim, though they did not record it."
al-Suyuti takes it up in al-Durr al-Manthur 3:246, and attributes it additionally to Ibn Abi ʿUmar al-ʿAdani in his Musnad, ʿAbd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal in the Zawaid of al-Zuhd, Abu Yaʿla, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh.
al-Haythami takes it up in Majmaʿ al-Zawaid 9:312, with wording other than this, and said: "Abu Yaʿla narrated it, and its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]]

16737 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from ʿAnbasah, from al-Mughirah ibn al-Nuʿman, who said: A man from al-Nakhaʿ, who was an elderly heavy-set man, wished to go on a raid, but Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas prevented him. He said: Indeed Allah says: ﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾. So Saʿd permitted him, and the old man was killed. Later ʿUmar asked about him, saying: What became of the old man who was as if he were of the Banu Hashim? [[In the printed edition: "kāna min Banī Hāshim" ("he was of the Banu Hashim"), which is an undoubted error, for the man is "from al-Nakhaʿ," as mentioned before; the correct reading is what is in the manuscript.]] They said: He was killed, O Commander of the Faithful! [[The narration 16737: "al-Mughirah ibn al-Nuʿman al-Nakhaʿi", trustworthy, passed under no. 13622.]]

16738 - Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, from Ismaʿil, from Abu Salih, who said: The young man and the old man.

16739 - ...... He said: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Malik ibn Mighwal, from Ismaʿil, from ʿIkrimah, who said: The young man and the old man.

16740 - ...... He said: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: the middle-aged and the young.

16741 - ...... He said: Hubawayh Abu Yazid narrated to us, from Yaʿqub al-Qummi, from Jaʿfar ibn Humayd, from Bishr ibn ʿAtiyyah: the middle-aged and the young. [[The narration 16741: "Hubawayh, Abu Yazid" is "Ishaq ibn Ismaʿil al-Razi", has passed several times, including no. 15993; the printed edition wrote "Hayawah", which differs from the manuscript and is a plain error.
As for "Jaʿfar ibn Humayd", I have found no mention of him in any of my references; the one who narrates from him, Yaʿqub ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Qummi, is "Jaʿfar ibn Abi al-Mughirah al-Khuzaʿi al-Qummi", and what Ibn Hajar reported in al-Tahdhib in his biography from Abu Nuʿaym is that the name of "Abu al-Mughirah" is "Dinar", not "Humayd".
As for "Bishr ibn ʿAtiyyah", I have found no one by this name except "Bishr ibn ʿAtiyyah", a man from whom Makhul narrated, said to be a Companion, and said to be "Bishr ibn ʿIsmah al-Muzani"; see Lisan al-Mizan 2:26, 27, in both biographies, and al-Isabah in the biography of both names. All of this is confused.]]

16742 - al-Walid narrated to us, saying: ʿAli ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, from Bukayr ibn Maʿruf, from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, regarding His saying: ﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾, he said: the young and the middle-aged.

16743 - Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾, he said: the young and the elderly, and the rich and the poor.

16744 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: al-Hasan said: the elders and the young.

16745 - Saʿid ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Baqiyyah narrated to us, saying: Hariz narrated to us, saying: Habban ibn Zayd al-Shardabi narrated to me, who said: We went forth with Safwan ibn ʿAmr, who was governor of Homs facing al-Afsus, toward al-Jarajimah, [["al-Afsus" is a town in the frontier-posts of Tarsus, and "Tarsus" is a city in the frontier-posts of Syria between Antioch, Aleppo, and the lands of Rum.
"al-Jarajimah" are the Nabateans of Syria; it is also said they are a people of non-Arabs in al-Jazirah.
In the manuscript it was: "qibal al-Afsun ila al-Hirasah," and the correct reading is in the printed edition, which agrees with Ibn Kathir 4:176, quoting this passage of al-Tabari.]] and I met an old man, very decrepit, whose eyebrows had fallen over his eyes, from the people of Damascus, on his mount, among those who raided. I approached him and said: O uncle, Allah has indeed excused you! He raised his eyebrows and said: O nephew, Allah has summoned us light and heavy; whoever Allah loves, He tests; then He returns him and tests him again; Allah only tests among His servants those who give thanks, are patient, remember, and worship none but Allah. [[In the printed edition: "min yuḥibbuhu Allah yabtalīhi, thumma yuʿīduhu fa-yabtalīhi" versus the manuscript; I have established what is in the manuscript, which alone is correct.
The narration 16745: "Baqiyyah" is "Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid", has passed many times.
"Hariz" is "Hariz ibn ʿUthman ibn Jabr al-Rahbi", trustworthy and reliable in hadith; what was ascribed to him by those who fabricated was due to his speaking ill of ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him), then he gave that up. "Hariz" is pronounced with fatha on the ḥāʾ and kasra on the rāʾ. Abu Dawud said: "The teachers of Hariz are all trustworthy." He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 2/1/96, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/289.
In the printed edition it was "Jarir", and in the manuscript it is undotted.
"Habban ibn Zayd al-Shardabi" (with kasra on the ḥāʾ of Habban), Abu Khidash al-Himsi; Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat, and it has passed that Abu Dawud declared all the teachers of Hariz ibn ʿUthman trustworthy. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 2/1/78, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/269.
"Safwan ibn ʿAmr", apparently he is "Safwan ibn ʿAmr ibn Harim al-Sakasiki", trustworthy. What led me to this supposition is that I saw in his biography in al-Tahdhib, from Abu al-Yaman, from Safwan: "I reached some of the caliphate of ʿAbd al-Malik, and we went out on an expedition in the year 94," but I did not find mention of his governorship of Homs.
"Safwan ibn ʿAmr al-Sakasiki" has passed many times, including nos. 7009, 12807, 13108.]]
16746 - Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Ismaʿil narrated to us, from Abu Salih: ﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾, he said: every old man and young man.

* *

Others said: the meaning is: the busy and the not busy.

Mention of those who said this:

16747 - Ibn Bashshar and Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, both saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from al-Hakam regarding His saying: ﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾, he said: the busy and the not busy.

* *

Others said: its meaning is: go forth, rich and poor.

Mention of those who said this:

16748 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from ʿAnbasah, from one he mentioned, from Abu Salih: ﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾, he said: rich and poor.

* *

Others said: its meaning is: energetic and not energetic.

Mention of those who said this:

16749 - Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: ﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾, he said: Go forth, energetic and not energetic.

* *

16750 - Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah: ﴿light and heavy﴾, he said: energetic and not energetic.

* *

Others said: its meaning is: riders and walkers.

Mention of those who said this:

16751 - ʿAli ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: al-Walid narrated to us, saying: Abu ʿAmr said: When the going forth is toward the frontier routes of Syria, the people go forth to them "light," as riders. And when the going forth is to these coasts, they go forth to them "light and heavy," as riders and walkers.

* *

Others said: the meaning of that is: one who has property, and one who does not.

Mention of those who said this:

16752 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾: "The heavy" is the one who has property, so he is heavy, disliking to let his property be lost and to go out. And "the light" is the one who has no property, so Allah said: ﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾.

16753 - Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: al-Muʿtamir narrated to us, from his father, who said: A man of Hadramawt claimed that it was mentioned to him that some people, one of whom might be sick or old, would say: If I refrain from it out of reluctance, then I am sinful! [[In the printed edition, in place of "in ajtanibhu ibaʾan, fa-innī āthim," there is the text: "fa-yaqūlu: innī aḥsabuhu qāla: anā lā āthim," which is very confused; in Ibn Kathir 4:174, 175, the speech was abridged and written: "fa-yaqūlu: innī lā āthim"; and in al-Durr al-Manthur 3:246, the same abridged.
As for the manuscript, its writing was thus: "fa-yaqūlu: in aḥsabuhu abban qāla āthim," and I preferred reading it as I have established it; its meaning: if I refrain from going forth out of reluctance to the raid, then I am sinful, but my sickness or old age is an excuse that removes from me the sin of staying behind. This is what I preferred, and Allah knows best.]] So Allah revealed: ﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾.

16754 - Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, saying: Ayyub narrated to us, from Muhammad, who said: Abu Ayyub witnessed Badr with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then he did not stay behind from any raid of the Muslims except that he was in another, [[In the printed edition: "illa wa-huwa fī ukhrā" ("except that he was in another"), while in the manuscript: "fī ākharīn" ("among others"); Ibn Kathir omitted this phrase in his tafsir, and so did al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur. It is sound in meaning; Ibn Saʿd narrated it as "fī ukhrā" as in the printed edition; al-Hakim narrated it as "illa huwa fīhā".]] except one year. And Ayyub used to say: ﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾, so I find myself only light or heavy. [[The narration 16754: narrated by Ibn Saʿd in al-Tabaqat 3/2/49 through the route of Ismaʿil ibn Ibrahim al-Asadi, who is "Ibn ʿAtiyyah", at length and in detail.
Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak 3:458, by this same route, at length.]]

16755 - ʿAli ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, saying: Hariz ibn ʿUthman narrated to us, from Rashid ibn Saʿd, from one who saw al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, the horseman of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), on a chest of the money-changers in Homs, and it overhung him because of his largeness. I said to him: Allah has indeed excused you! He said: The "chapter of the expeditions" refused us: ﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾. [[Thus it came here in the manuscript: "al-buʿūth" ("the expeditions"), and I am very doubtful of it, for I have not found anyone who named "Surat al-Tawbah" "Surat al-Buʿūth"; rather they agreed to name it "Surat al-Buḥūth" ("the chapter of investigations"), as I will explain after p. 265, note 6. Then see the end of the note on the report no. 16756.]] [[The narration 16755: "Hariz ibn ʿUthman ibn Jabr al-Rahbi", passed just above under no. 16745. In the printed edition it was "Jarir", which is an error; in the manuscript it is undotted.
"Rashid ibn Saʿd al-Muqra'i al-Hibrani al-Himsi", trustworthy, there is no harm in him if no one abandoned in narration narrates from him; the teachers of "Hariz ibn ʿUthman" are all trustworthy, as I stated in no. 16745, and "Hariz" is trustworthy in himself. This report will come after this; it contains no unknown person.]]

16756 - Saʿid ibn ʿAmr al-Sakuni narrated to us, saying: Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid narrated to us, saying: Hariz narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Maysarah narrated to me, saying: Abu Rashid al-Hibrani narrated to me, saying: I came upon al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, the horseman of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), sitting on a chest of the money-changers in Homs, which overhung him because of his largeness, [[In the printed edition: "faḍala ʿanhu," and I have established what is in the manuscript, for it is pure correctness, since "the chest" may be referred to with masculine or feminine gender.]] wishing to go on a raid. I said to him: Allah has indeed excused you! He said: The "chapter of the investigations" refused us: [[In the printed edition: "al-Buʿūth," and I have established what is in the manuscript, which agrees with the narration of this report in the sources I will mention. "al-Buḥūth": some pronounce it with a damma on the bāʾ, the plural of "baḥth"; it was so named because it investigated the hypocrites and their secrets, that is, it stirred them up and searched them out.
Ibn al-Athir said he saw in al-Fa'iq of al-Zamakhshari "al-Buḥūth" with a fatha on the bāʾ, but the printed al-Fa'iq has no vowelling. Then Ibn al-Athir said: "If it is sound, it is a form of intensification (fa'ul). As for al-Zamakhshari, he said: 'The chapter of the investigations: it is the chapter of Repentance, because of its investigation of the hypocrites and uncovering of their secrets, and it is called al-Mubaʿthirah.'"
All of this supports what I pursued in p. 265, note 3.]] ﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾. [[The narration 16756: see the note on the preceding report no. 16755.
"Saʿid ibn ʿAmr al-Sakuni", shaykh of al-Tabari, trustworthy, has passed under nos. 5563, 6521, and elsewhere.
"Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid", his trustworthiness has passed, and whoever spoke of him recently, no. 16745.
"Hariz" is "Hariz ibn ʿUthman", passed in the preceding report, with its references there; in the printed edition here also it was "Jarir", and the manuscript is undotted.
"ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Maysarah al-Hadrami", Abu Salamah al-Himsi, trustworthy, since Abu Dawud said so. "Abu Rashid al-Hibrani al-Himyari al-Himsi", a trustworthy Successor. None narrated from him except "Hariz". Biographed in al-Tahdhib and al-Kuna of al-Bukhari: 30.
This report was narrated by Ibn Saʿd in al-Tabaqat 3/1/115, through the route of Yazid ibn Harun, from Hariz ibn ʿUthman (in al-Tabaqat: "Jarir," which is an error as I have shown).
al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak through the route of Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid, from Hariz ibn ʿUthman (in which: "Jarir," an error).
al-Haythami mentioned it in Majmaʿ al-Zawaid 7:30, and said: "al-Tabarani narrated it, and in it is Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid, in whom there is weakness, though he was declared trustworthy. Baqiyyah's narrators are trustworthy."
I say: It has become clear from the takhrij that he narrated it from "Hariz": "Yazid ibn Harun", who is trustworthy, whom the group narrated from, as has passed many times.
Here, Majmaʿ al-Zawaid has "Surat al-Buʿūth," and see what I wrote above at p. 265, note 3, and p. 265, note 6.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these sayings in our view is that it should be said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, commanded the believers to go forth to strive against His enemies in His way, light and heavy. The "light" may include everyone for whom going forth is easy because of the strength of his body, the soundness of his frame, and his youth, and whoever is possessed of wealth and free from preoccupation, and able to provide mounts and riding animals. And the "heavy" includes everyone in the opposite condition: the weak of body, the sick, the infirm, the poor in wealth, the one occupied with property and livelihood, the one who has no mount or riding animal, the old man, and the one with years and dependents.

Since the "light" and the "heavy" may include those of the described conditions we have mentioned, and Allah, may His praise be exalted, did not single out one category over another in the Book, nor upon the tongue of the Messenger (ﷺ), nor did He establish a proof for its particular application, it is necessary to say: Allah, may His praise be exalted, commanded the believers among the companions of His Messenger to go forth to strive in His way, light and heavy, with His Messenger (ﷺ), in every state of lightness and heaviness.

* *

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 41 (part 2 of 2):**

16757. Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Masruq, from Muslim ibn Subaih, who said: The first of "Bara'ah" (Repentance) to be revealed was: "Go forth, light and heavy."

16758. Ibn Wakee' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Abu al-Duha, the like of it.

16759. Al-Harith narrated to us, saying: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: The first of "Bara'ah" to be revealed was: "Allah had already given you victory on many occasions." He said: He makes them aware of His help and prepares them for the expedition to Tabuk.

* *

**On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: "And strive with your wealth and your lives in the way of Allah. That is better for you, if you only knew."**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The Exalted says to those who believe in Him and in His Messenger, from among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Strive" (jahadu), O believers, against the disbelievers, "with your wealth" (bi-amwalikum), so spend it in your striving for the religion of Allah that He has prescribed for you, until they submit to you and enter it willingly or unwillingly, or they give you the jizya (poll tax) with humiliation, if they are People of the Book, or you kill them [[See the explanation of "jihad" (striving in the way of Allah) above, p. 173, note 5, and the references there.
= And the explanation of "sabil Allah" (the way of Allah) above, in the lexical indexes (under s-b-l).]] "and your lives" (wa-anfusikum), meaning: and with your lives, so fight them with your hands; Allah will disgrace them and give you victory over them. "That is better for you" means: this which I command you to do, namely going forth in the way of Allah Almighty, light and heavy, and striving against His enemies with your wealth and your lives, is better for you than being sluggish toward the earth when you are called to go forth, and than settling into it and being content with the little of the enjoyment of the worldly life in place of the Hereafter. "If you only knew" means: if you are among the people of knowledge of the reality of what has been made clear to you concerning the excellence of striving in the way of Allah over remaining behind from it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 42:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Had it been a near gain and a moderate journey, they would have followed you. But the distance seemed long to them. And they will swear by Allah, "Had we been able, we would have gone out with you," destroying themselves; and Allah knows that they are liars.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, glorified is His praise, says to the Prophet ﷺ, and a group of his companions had asked his permission to stay behind when he set out for Tabuk, so he gave them permission. He says: Had what you invite them to, those who stay behind from you and who ask your permission not to go out with you on your campaign to which you called them to march, been ﴿a near gain﴾, meaning a ready booty [see the explanation of "al-'Arad" (gain) above, p. 59, note 1, and the references there], and ﴿a moderate journey﴾, meaning a near and easy destination, ﴿they would have followed you﴾, and marched with you toward them. But you called them to a distant place and imposed on them a journey that was hard for them, because you summoned them in the time of heat, in the season of summer and at a time when they needed shelter. ﴿And they will swear by Allah, "Had we been able, we would have gone out with you"﴾: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Those who asked you, O Muhammad, for permission not to go out with you will swear to you, as an excuse they offer you falsely, so that you accept their excuse and permit them to stay behind from you, swearing by Allah falsely. ("Had we been able, we would have gone out with you"), meaning: had we been capable of going out with you, through having ample means, mounts, provisions, and what the traveler and the warrior must have, and bodily health and strength, we would have gone out with you against your enemy. ﴿Destroying themselves﴾:

He says: they bring upon themselves, by their false oaths by Allah, destruction and ruin, because they earn for themselves the wrath of Allah and acquire for themselves the painful punishment of Him. ﴿And Allah knows that they are liars﴾ in their oath by Allah, "Had we been able, we would have gone out with you," because they were able to go out, given the means available to them through the wealth they had, of what the warrior needs in his campaign and the traveler on his journey, and bodily health and physical strength.

* *

And in accordance with what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Those who said that:

16760. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Had it been a near gain﴾, up to His saying ﴿they are liars﴾: They were able to go out, but it was a slackening from their own selves and from Satan, and a disinclination toward good.

16761. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿Had it been a near gain﴾, he said: It is the expedition of Tabuk.

16762. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿And Allah knows that they are liars﴾, meaning: that they were able. [The report: 16762 – Sirat Ibn Hisham 4: 194, which follows the earlier report no. 16699.]

The explanation of His saying: ﴿May Allah pardon you! Why did you grant them permission until those who told the truth became clear to you and you knew the liars?﴾ (9:43)

Abu Ja'far said: This is a reproach from Allah, exalted is His remembrance, addressed to His Prophet ﷺ regarding his granting permission to those hypocrites who asked him for leave to stay behind from him, when he set out for Tabuk to fight the Romans.

His saying, exalted is His praise: ﴿May Allah pardon you﴾, O Muhammad, for what you did in granting permission to these hypocrites who asked you to be excused from going out with you and from staying behind you, before you knew who among them was truthful and who was lying. [[See the explanation of "al-'afw" in the earlier lexical indices (ʿafā).]]

= ﴿Why did you grant them permission?﴾ = For what reason did you grant them permission?
= ﴿until those who told the truth became clear to you and you knew the liars﴾: He says, it was not fitting for you to grant them permission to stay behind you when they said to you: ﴿If we had been able, we would have gone out with you﴾, until you knew which of them had a valid excuse for staying behind and which of them had no excuse, so that your granting permission to those whom you permitted would be with knowledge of their excuse, and you would know which of them was the liar, the one who stayed behind out of hypocrisy and doubt concerning the religion of Allah.

* *

The commentators have said what is similar to what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said that:

16763. Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿May Allah pardon you! Why did you grant them permission?﴾: He said: Some people said: "Ask the permission of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. If he gives you permission, sit; and if he does not give you permission, sit."

16764. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding his saying: ﴿May Allah pardon you! Why did you grant them permission until those who told the truth became clear to you﴾, the verse. He reproached him, as you hear, then Allah revealed the verse in "Surat al-Nur", granting him leave to permit them if he wished, saying: ﴿So when they ask your permission for some of their affairs, grant permission to whom you will among them﴾ [Surat al-Nur: 62]. So Allah made it a concession for him in that matter.

16765. al-Harith narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Amr ibn Maymun al-Awdi, who said: There were two things the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did for which he was not commanded: his granting permission to the hypocrites, and his taking ransom from the captives. Then Allah revealed: ﴿May Allah pardon you! Why did you grant them permission?﴾, the verse.

16766. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I read to Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, who said: That is how I heard it from Qatadah, his saying: "May Allah pardon you! Why did you grant them permission?", the verse. Then after that Allah revealed in "Surat al-Nur": ﴿So when they ask your permission for some of their affairs, grant permission to whom you will among them﴾, the verse.

16767. Salih ibn Masmar narrated to us, saying: al-Nadr ibn Shumayl narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Sarwan informed us, who said: I asked Muwarriq about his saying: ﴿May Allah pardon you﴾, and he said: His Lord reproached him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 44:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Those who believe in Allah and the Last Day do not ask your permission to be exempted from striving with their wealth and their lives, and Allah is Knowing of the God-fearing (muttaqun)﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: This is an informing from Allah to His Prophet ﷺ about the distinguishing marks (sima) of the hypocrites (munafiqun): that among their signs by which they are recognized is their lagging behind from striving (jihad) in the way of Allah, by asking the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for permission to leave off going out with him when they are called to march, using false excuses.

His Exalted Praise says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: O Muhammad, do not grant permission to stay behind from you when you go out to fight your enemy, to whoever asks you for permission to stay behind without an excuse, for only a hypocrite who does not believe in Allah and the Last Day asks you for that. As for the one who affirms Allah, acknowledges His oneness, and believes in the Resurrection, the Abode of the Hereafter, reward and punishment, he does not ask you to abandon the campaign and the striving against the enemies of Allah with his wealth and his person [[See the explanation of "jahada" above, p. 270, footnote 1, and the references there.]] = ﴿And Allah is Knowing of the God-fearing﴾. He says: Allah has knowledge of those who fear Him and guard themselves against Him by performing His obligations, avoiding His prohibitions, and hastening to obey Him by fighting His enemy and striving against them with their wealth and their persons, and in other matters of His commands and prohibitions. [[See the explanation of "taqwa" above in the lexical indices (w-q-y).]]

* *

Those who gave this interpretation said the same as what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

16768. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Those who believe in Allah do not ask your permission﴾. This is a reproach to the hypocrites, who asked permission to sit back from jihad without an excuse, while Allah excused the believers, saying: ﴿They do not depart until they have asked his permission﴾ [Surah al-Nur: 62].

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 45:

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿Only those who do not believe in Allah and the Last Day ask your permission, and their hearts are in doubt, so in their doubt they hesitate﴾ (9:45).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Allah, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet (ﷺ): "Only those ask your permission, O Muhammad, to stay behind from you and to abandon striving with you, without a clear excuse, who do not affirm Allah and do not acknowledge His oneness." ﴿And their hearts are in doubt﴾ means: their hearts have doubts about the reality of Allah's oneness, about the reward of those who obey Him, and about His punishment of those who disobey Him [[See the explanation of "al-irtiyab" (doubt) and "al-rayb" (uncertainty) in what has preceded, 11:172, note 3, and the references there; then 11:280, note 1, and the references there.]]. ﴿So in their doubt they hesitate﴾ means: in their uncertainty they are bewildered, and in the darkness of confusion they waver, not knowing truth from falsehood, so they act without insight. This is the attribute of the hypocrites.

A group of scholars held that these two verses were abrogated by the verse mentioned in Surat al-Nur.

Mention of those who said so:

16769. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, from al-Husayn, from Yazid, from Ikrimah and al-Hasan al-Basri, who both said regarding His saying: ﴿Only those who believe in Allah ask your permission﴾ up to His saying ﴿so in their doubt they hesitate﴾: they were abrogated by the verse in al-Nur: ﴿The believers are only those who have believed in Allah﴾ up to ﴿indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (24:62).

* *

We have already explained "abrogating and abrogated (naskh)" (al-nasikh wa'l-mansukh, the doctrine of verses superseding others) sufficiently to make repetition unnecessary here. [[See his discussion in "al-Nasikh wa'l-Mansukh" above, p. 42, note 2, and the references there. See also the general indices and the indices of grammar and Arabic language, and others.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 46:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And had they intended to go out, they would have made preparation for it, but Allah disliked their being dispatched, so He held them back, and it was said, "Sit with those who sit [at home]."﴾
