Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Almighty Allah says: Had these men who ask your permission, O Muhammad, to remain behind rather than go out with you to fight your enemy, intended to go out with you, ﴿they would have made preparation for it﴾, meaning: they would have made preparation for the going out, and they would have readied themselves for the journey and for the enemy, taking up its equipment [[See the explanation of "a'adda" (to prepare) above, p. 31.]]. ﴿But Allah disliked their being dispatched﴾, meaning: their going out for that purpose [[See the explanation of "al-kurh" (dislike) above, 8:104, note 1, and the references there. Also the explanation of "al-ba'th" (dispatch) above, 11:407, note 2, and the references there.]]. ﴿So He held them back﴾, meaning: He made going out burdensome for them, until they found sitting in their homes in opposition to you light, and found the journey and going out with you heavy, so they left off going out for that reason. ﴿And it was said, "Sit with those who sit [at home]"﴾, meaning: sit with the sick and the weak who cannot find anything to spend, and with the women and the children, and leave off going out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the fighters in the way of Allah. [[See the explanation of "al-qu'ud" (sitting) above, 9:85.]]

* *

Allah's holding them back from going out with His Messenger (ﷺ) and the believers was because of His knowledge of their hypocrisy and their deceit toward Islam and its people, and that if they had gone out with them they would have harmed them and not benefited them. It is mentioned that those who asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for permission to stay behind were: "Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul" and "al-Jadd ibn Qays," and those who were of the same mind as these two. Thus:

16770 - Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Those who asked him for permission, as has reached me, were of the people of standing, among them: Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul and al-Jadd ibn Qays, and they were nobles among their people. So Allah held them back, knowing about them that if they went out with them they would corrupt his army. [[The report: 16770 - Ibn Hisham's Sirah 4:194, a continuation of the earlier report no. 16762. In the manuscript it reads "fa-yufsidu 'alayhi hissahu" (unpointed, corrupt script). What is printed matches Ibn Hisham's Sirah, which is correct.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 47:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Had they gone forth among you, they would not have increased you except in corruption, and they would have hastened between you, seeking to cause you fitnah (trial, discord), and among you are listeners to them. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers﴾ (9:47).

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His mention, says: Had these hypocrites gone forth among you, O believers, ﴿they would not have increased you except in corruption﴾, meaning: their going forth among you would have increased you only in corruption and harm, and for this reason I held them back from going out with you.

* *

The meaning of "khabal" (corruption, ruin) has already been explained, with its evidence, earlier. [See the explanation of "khabal" above, 7:139, 140.]

* *

﴿And they would have hastened between you﴾, meaning: they would have quickened their mounts in their journey among you.

* *

Its origin is from "iyda' of horses and mounts", which is hastening them in travel. It is said of a she-camel when she quickens her pace: "the she-camel wada'at, taḍa' wad'an and mawḍū'an", and "her owner awda'ahā", when he urged her on and hastened her, "yūḍi'uhā īḍā'an". From this is the saying of the rajiz (rajaz poet):

[The verse is by Durayd ibn al-Simmah.]

Ya laytanī fīhā jadha' ... akhubbu fīhā wa-aḍa'
(Would that I were in it, a young man ... I would gallop in it and hasten)

[Sirah of Ibn Hisham 4:82, Lisan (wḍ‘), and others. This rajaz was composed by Durayd on the day of the Battle of Hunayn, when he went out with Hawazin, commanded by Malik ibn Awf al-Nasri. Durayd ibn al-Simmah was then an elderly shaykh, having nothing but the benefit of his opinion and his knowledge of war, and he was an experienced elder. Malik ibn Awf disliked that Durayd should have any opinion or mention in this war, so Durayd said: "This is a day I did not witness, and it did not escape me." Ya laytanī fīhā jadha' ... akhubbu fīhā wa-aḍa'
Uqūdu waṭfā' al-zama‘ ... ka-annahā shāt ṣada‘
"Jadha'", the small young one. "Khabab", a kind of gait like the wad'. Then he described his horse in what he wished for. "Waṭfā'", long-maned. "Zama'a" is the protruding extra growth above the hoof of a sheep. "Shāh" here: the wa‘l, the mountain goat. "Ṣada‘" is the strong young male of the wa‘ul.]

* *

As for the origin of "khilal" (between/among), it is from "khalal", which are the gaps that occur among people, in rows and elsewhere. From this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Stand shoulder to shoulder in the rows, lest the devils slip between you (lā yatakhallalakum [al-shayāṭīn, ka-annahā]) like the young of the ḥadhf." [He did not mention its chain, and it is a well-known hadith, narrated by Abu Dawud in his Sunan 1:252, no. 667, without this wording, and by al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan 2:92. What I placed between the brackets is from what the author of al-Lisan narrated, since in the Sunan it reads: "ka-annahā al-ḥadhf", and in al-Lisan also "ka-annahā banāt ḥadhf". As for the printed edition, it joined parts of the text together, although in the manuscript there was a blank between "lā yatakhallalakum" and "awlād al-ḥadhf", and in the margin the letter (ṭ) indicating an error.

"Al-ḥadhf" are black, hairless, small sheep with no ears and no tails, brought to the Hijaz from Jarash of Yemen; its singular is "ḥadhfah" (with two fathas), and he likened the devils to them.]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿seeking to cause you fitnah﴾, the meaning of "yabghūnakum al-fitnah" is that they seek for you what you would be tested by, regarding your departure on your campaign, by their holding you back from it. [See the explanation of "fitnah" above, p. 86, note 1, and the references there.]

* *

It is said from it: "baghaytuhu al-sharr" and "baghaytuhu al-khayr", "abghīhi bughā'an", when you sought it for him, meaning "baghaytu lahu" (I sought for him). Likewise "a'kamtuka" and "ḥalabtuka", meaning "ḥalabtu laka" and "a'kamtu laka" [["a'kamahu" and "a'kama lahu" is to arrange the saddle-packs for the animal and tie them on]]. When they intend "I helped you to seek and search for it", they say "abghaytuka kadhā", "aḥlabtuka", "a'kamtuka", meaning: I helped you in it. [See the explanation of "baghā" above, 13:84, note 1, and the references there. Then see a similar detailed discussion above, 7:53.]

* *

Those who interpreted the verse said things similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

16771 — Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿and they would have hastened between you﴾, among you = ﴿seeking to cause you fitnah﴾, by that.

16772 — Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿and they would have hastened between you﴾, meaning: [they would have hastened among you] between you, with fitnah. [In the printed and manuscript texts: "they would have placed their weapons between you with fitnah", which conveys no meaning. My view is that "their weapons" is "among you", which is the explanation of "between you" as in the earlier report of Qatadah, but he placed later the word he explained, which is "between you".]

16773 — Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿and they would have hastened between you, seeking to cause you fitnah﴾, they would slow you down. He said: Rifa'ah ibn al-Tabut, 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, and Aws ibn Qayzi.

16774 — al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿and they would have hastened between you﴾, he said: they would have hastened the alleys [printed and manuscript: "al-azqah", the plural of "zuqaq" (with a damma on the zay), a narrow path, short of a street; making "al-azqah" the object of "hastened" is strange, and I fear there is a flaw or misreading in the text] = ﴿between you, seeking to cause you fitnah﴾, they would slow you down: 'Abd Allah ibn Nabtal, Rifa'ah ibn al-Tabut, and 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul.

16775 — ...... He said: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to me, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿and they would have hastened between you﴾, he said: they would have hastened between you, seeking to cause you fitnah by that.

16776 — Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿Had they gone forth among you, they would not have increased you except in corruption﴾, he said: These are the hypocrites at the expedition of Tabuk. Allah consoled His Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers, saying: And what grieves you? ﴿Had they gone forth among you, they would not have increased you except in corruption﴾! They would say: "An army has been gathered against you, and such-and-such has been done," discouraging you = ﴿and they would have hastened between you, seeking to cause you fitnah﴾, disbelief.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and among you are listeners to them﴾, the scholars of interpretation differed in its explanation.

Some said: The meaning is: among you are listeners to your talk who carry it to them, spies for them against you.

Those who said so:

16777 — Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿and among you are listeners to them﴾, who relate your conversations, spies, not hypocrites.

16778 — al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿and among you are listeners to them﴾, he said: narrators, spies, not hypocrites. [In the printed edition: "not hypocrites", and I have adopted what is in the manuscript.]

16779 — Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿and among you are listeners to them﴾, they listen to what they convey to your enemy.

* *

Others said: Rather, the meaning is: among you are those who hear their speech and obey them.

Those who said so:

16780 — Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿and among you are listeners to them﴾, among you are those who listen to their speech.

16781 — Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Those who asked permission, as has reached me, were of the noble ones, among them 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul and al-Jadd ibn Qays, who were nobles among their people. So Allah held them back, knowing about them, from going out with them, lest they corrupt His army against Him. There were among His army people who loved them and obeyed them in what they called them to, because of their nobility among them, so He said: ﴿and among you are listeners to them﴾. [The report 16781: the beginning of this account has passed as number 16770, and he repeats it here later; it is in Ibn Hisham's Sirah 4:194, and it follows the earlier report number 16762.]

Abu Ja'far said: According to this interpretation: among you are people of hearing and obedience from among you, who, if they accompanied you, would corrupt them against you by holding them back from marching with you.

As for the first interpretation, its meaning is: among you there are some of them who listen to your talk to them, and convey it to them, and report it to them, spies for them against you.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two interpretations in my view is the interpretation of those who said: its meaning is "among you are listeners to your talk for them, who convey it from you, spies for them", because the more common usage of the Arabs in saying "sammā'" (one who listens often) describes one who is described as being a listener to speech, as Allah, exalted is His praise, said in more than one place of His Book: ﴿Listeners to falsehood﴾ (5:41), describing by that people who listen to falsehood in talk. As for when they describe a man as listening to the speech, command, and prohibition of a man, accepting it from him and submitting to him, they describe him as: "he is a listener and obedient to him", and they hardly say: "he is a listening obedient one to him". [See the explanation of "sammā'" above, 10:309.]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers﴾, its meaning is: Allah is the One who has knowledge of those who direct their actions to other than their proper aims and place them in other than their proper places, and of those who ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) permission for an excuse, and of those who ask his permission out of doubt about Islam and hypocrisy, and of those who listen to the hadith of the believers in order to inform the hypocrites of it, and of those who listen to it in order to rejoice in what the believers rejoice in, and are grieved by what grieves them. Nothing of the secrets of His creatures or their openness is hidden from Him. [In the printed edition: "bimā sarra al-mu'minīn"; in the manuscript: "bimā sarra al-mu'minūn", and the correct form is what I adopted.] [See the explanation of "'alīm" above in the language indexes (‘-l-m).]

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "ẓulm" (wrongdoing) in more than one place in this book, in a way that suffices without repeating it in this place. [See the explanation of "ẓulm" above in the language indexes (ẓ-l-m).]

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 9, Verse 48:**

*On the interpretation of His words: ﴿Indeed, they sought discord before, and they turned matters over in their minds against you until the truth came and the command of God prevailed, while they were averse.﴾*

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Exalted is He, the One who is mentioned, says: These hypocrites sought discord for your Companions, O Muhammad. They sought to divert them from their religion [[See the explanation of "ibtagha" (sought) earlier, p. 279, note 4, and the references there.]] and they were eager to turn them back to disbelief by discouraging them from it [[See the explanation of "fitnah" (discord, trial) earlier, p. 279, note 2, and the references there.]], as the deed of Abdullah ibn Ubayy did to you and your Companions on the Day of Uhud, when he withdrew from you with those of his people who followed him. And this was their seeking of what they had sought for the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) of discord before. By His words ﴿before﴾, He means: before this. ﴿And they turned matters over in their minds against you﴾ means: they deliberated about you and about nullifying the religion with which God sent you, scheming to discourage people from you, denying what you brought them, and rejecting it from you [[See the explanation of "taqlib" (turning over) earlier, 12:44, 45, and the root (q-l-b) in the indexes of language.]]. ﴿Until the truth came﴾ means: until the victory of God came. ﴿And the command of God prevailed﴾ means: the religion of God prevailed, the one He commanded and made obligatory upon His creation, which is Islam [[See the explanation of "zuhur" (prevalence) earlier, pp. 214, 215.]]. ﴿While they were averse﴾ means: while the hypocrites were averse to the prevalence of God's command and His support of you [[See the explanation of "karh" (aversion) earlier, p. 276, note 3, and the references there.]]. And likewise now: God will make you prevail, and He will make His religion prevail over those who disbelieve, from among the Romans and others of the people of disbelief in Him, while they are averse.

* *

And the people of interpretation have said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

*Mention of those who said this:*

16782. Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, regarding ﴿and they turned matters over in their minds against you﴾: that is, to discourage your Companions from you and to turn your affair back upon you, ﴿until the truth came and the command of God prevailed.﴾ [[The report: 16782 — Sirat Ibn Hisham 4:194, and it follows the preceding report no. 16781.]]

* *

It is mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning a group of men named specifically.

16783. Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Amr, from al-Hasan regarding His words: ﴿and they turned matters over in their minds against you﴾, he said: Among them were Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, Abdullah ibn Nabtal, brother of the Banu Amr ibn Awf, Rifa'ah ibn Rafi', and Zayd ibn al-Tabut al-Qaynuqa'i. [[The report: 16783 — I did not find it in Sirat Ibn Hisham. However, it is in Tarikh al-Tabari 3:143, with the same wording.]]

* *

The discouragement of his Companions from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) by Abdullah ibn Ubayy in this expedition was as follows:

16784. Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from al-Zuhri, Yazid ibn Ruman, Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah, and others, each of whom related what reached him about the expedition of Tabuk, some of the people relating what others did not, and all of their accounts agreed upon this narration: that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) commanded his Companions to prepare for fighting the Romans, at a time of hardship for the people [[In the Sirah: "at a time of hardship among the people."]], intense heat, drought in the land, and when the fruits had ripened and the shade was desirable [["And the shade was desirable" is not in Sirat Ibn Hisham, but it is established in Abu Ja'far's narration in the History 3:142. Likewise in the printed edition: "and the people love," but I have kept what is in the manuscript, as it is what the context requires.]], so the people loved to remain in their fruit and shade and disliked departing from them, given the circumstances of the time they were in. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) rarely went out on an expedition without concealing it and indicating that he intended other than the target he was aiming for [["Samada lil-amr yasmudu" means he aimed at the matter directly.]], except for the expedition of Tabuk, which he made clear to the people, because of the great distance, the severity of the time, and the great number of the enemy he was targeting, so that the people could prepare for it with the proper preparation. So he commanded the people to strive, and informed them that he intended the Romans. The people then equipped themselves, despite what was in their hearts of aversion to that direction because of what it entailed, along with what they magnified of the mention of the Romans and fighting them. [[This last sentence, from the beginning of His words "the people equipped themselves," I did not find in this place of Sirat Ibn Hisham 4:159. I will mention the place of what follows in the referencing, as it has omitted what comes after that until it reaches what follows.]]

= Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) pressed on with his journey, and commanded the people to make ready and to hasten [["Al-inkimash" means speed and diligence in work and pursuit.]], and urged the wealthy to spend and to provide mounts for the cause of God [["Al-humlan" (with a vowel on the h and then a sukun) is a verbal noun like "al-haml," meaning: carrying the one who has no mount on a riding animal for this journey.

This sentence, from the beginning of His words "then the Messenger of God," to this point, is in Sirat Ibn Hisham 4:161, and what follows it is from another place I will clarify.]]

= When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) set out, he pitched his camp at Thaniyat al-Wada' [[This sentence stands alone in Sirat Ibn Hisham 4:162, after which is a passage that Abu Ja'far omitted, and he connected it to what follows.]], and Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul pitched his camp separately, below him, opposite "Dhubab" [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "on Dhu Hidda." In the manuscript the word "Dayn" had been written before "Dhu" and then struck out. I have not found them saying "on Dhu Hidda," and what confirms the correctness of this is that Ibn Hisham said "on Hidda," and Abu Ja'far mentioned this report in his History 3:143, where it also says "on Hidda." For this reason I have disregarded what is in the printed edition and the manuscript. In the printed edition and in Sirat Ibn Hisham it says "near Dhubab," while in the manuscript it says "nahwa," and the alif is faint and short, but what is in the History is what I have adopted: "bi-hadha'," which is the correct reading beyond doubt. The location of the mountain is not mentioned in the Sirah but is mentioned in the History.]] = a mountain in al-Jaban-ah below Thaniyat al-Wada' = and it was, as they claim, not the smaller of the two armies. When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) set out, Abdullah ibn Ubayy lagged behind him, along with those hypocrites and people of doubt who lagged behind. Abdullah ibn Ubayy was the brother of the Banu Awf ibn al-Khazraj, Abdullah ibn Nabtal was the brother of the Banu Amr ibn Awf, and Rifa'ah ibn Zayd ibn al-Tabut [[In the printed edition: "Rifa'ah ibn Yazid," which is an error; the correct form is from the manuscript and the History.]] was the brother of the Banu Qaynuqa', and they were among the great hypocrites, and they were among those who schemed against Islam and its people.

= He said: Among them, as Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Amr ibn Ubayd, from al-Hasan al-Basri, that God revealed: ﴿Indeed, they sought discord before﴾, the verse. [[The report: 16784 — This is a report in scattered parts, whose places I have mentioned earlier. It is in Sirat Ibn Hisham 4:159, then 4:161, then 4:162, and in its entirety in Tarikh al-Tabari 3:142, 143. The last part of this report has passed as no. 16873.]]

The commentary on the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And among them is he who says, "Grant me leave and do not tempt me. Have they not already fallen into temptation?"﴾ and Hell is surely encompassing of the disbelievers (49)

Abu Ja'far said: It is reported that this verse was revealed concerning al-Jadd ibn Qays.

* *

By His words, may His praise be exalted, ﴿And among them﴾, meaning among the hypocrites, ﴿is he who says, "Grant me leave"﴾, meaning, let me stay behind and I will not go out with you, ﴿and do not tempt me﴾, meaning: do not test me by seeing the women of the Banu al-Asfar and their daughters, for I am infatuated with women, so I would go out and sin thereby. [[See the explanation of "fitnah" (temptation, trial) above, p. 283, footnote 2, and the references there.]]

* *

Reports from the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have come in agreement with this interpretation.

Mention of the narration with this meaning from those who said it:

16785- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the words of Allah: ﴿Grant me leave and do not tempt me﴾, he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Go out to Tabuk, you will plunder the daughters of al-Asfar and the women of the Romans!" Then al-Jadd said: "Grant us leave, and do not tempt us with women."

16786- al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, they said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Go out, you will plunder the daughters of al-Asfar," meaning the women of the Romans, then he mentioned the like of it.

16787-...... He said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said concerning His words: ﴿Grant me leave and do not tempt me﴾, he said: It is al-Jadd ibn Qays, who said: "The Ansar know that when I see women I cannot restrain myself until I am tempted. But I will help you with my wealth."

16788- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from al-Zuhri, and Yazid ibn Ruman, and Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, and Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah and others, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said one day while he was preparing (for the expedition), to al-Jadd ibn Qays, brother of the Banu Salamah: "Will you, O Jadd, join this year's campaign against the Banu al-Asfar?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, will you grant me leave and not tempt me? By Allah, my people know that no man is more prone to being infatuated with women than I am, and I fear that if I see the women of the Banu al-Asfar I will not be able to restrain myself from them!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) turned away from him and said: "I have granted you leave." Concerning al-Jadd ibn Qays this verse was revealed: ﴿And among them is he who says, "Grant me leave and do not tempt me"﴾, the verse; meaning: even if he fears temptation from the women of the Banu al-Asfar, that is not the case, for the temptation into which he fell by staying behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and by preferring his own self over himself is greater. [[The report 16788 is in Ibn Hisham's Sirah 4: 159, 160; it continues the opening of the earlier report no. 16784, after his words there: "and informed them that he intends the Romans"; between what Abu Ja'far narrated and what is in the Sirah there is a slight difference at the end of the report.]]

16789- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His words: ﴿And among them is he who says, "Grant me leave and do not tempt me"﴾, he said: He is a man from among the hypocrites called Jadd ibn Qays. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "This year we will raid the Banu al-Asfar and take from them concubines and servants" — so he said: "O Messenger of Allah, grant me leave and do not tempt me; if you do not grant me leave, I will be tempted and will sit back!" [[In the printed edition: "and I stayed," in place of "and sit back"; I have kept what is in the manuscript; he meant staying behind from going out to the expedition, contrary to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).]] And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) became angry, so Allah said: ﴿Have they not already fallen into temptation? And Hell is surely encompassing of the disbelievers﴾. He was from the Banu Salamah, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to them: "Who is your chief, O Banu Salamah?" They said: "Jadd ibn Qays, except that he is stingy and cowardly!" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "And what disease is worse than stinginess? Rather, your chief is the fair, curly-haired youth: Bishr ibn al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur." [[In the printed edition: "al-Ja'd al-sha'r al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur," differing from the manuscript; the manuscript reading is the correct one, since the report is about Bishr ibn al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur being made chief over the Banu Salamah. As for his father al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur, he was among the first to pledge at the First Pledge of al-Aqabah, the first to face the qiblah, the first to bequeath a third of his wealth, one of the nuqaba', and he died before the Hijrah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), a month before the Messenger's arrival in Madinah; when they buried him, they turned his grave toward the qiblah.

It is said: "a man ja'd," meaning one whose build is compact, whose limbs are firm, strong in his joints, not slack or unsteady, and this is an adornment of the noble. It also means: curliness of hair, which is praised among the Arabs, since straight hair is found among the Romans and the Persians. In the report he intends the first meaning.]]

16790- al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas concerning His words: ﴿And among them is he who says, "Grant me leave and do not tempt me"﴾, he says: "Grant me leave and do not put me in difficulty" ﴿Have they not already fallen into temptation?﴾, meaning: they have fallen into difficulty.

16791- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And among them is he who says, "Grant me leave and do not tempt me"﴾, and do not make me sinful; have they not already fallen into sin?

* *

As for His words: ﴿And Hell is surely encompassing of the disbelievers﴾, He says: Indeed the Fire surrounds those who disbelieve in Allah, deny His signs and reject His messengers, encircling them, gathering them all together on the Day of Resurrection. [[See the explanation of "ihatah" (encompassing) above, vol. 13, p. 581, footnote 3, and the references there.]]

He says: Thus the burning of Hell is sufficient disgrace for al-Jadd ibn Qays and his likes among the hypocrites.

**The explanation of His saying:** ﴿If good befalls you, it grieves them; and if a misfortune strikes you, they say, "We had already taken our precaution beforehand," and they turn away rejoicing.﴾ (9:50)

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): O Muhammad, if happiness reaches you, through Allah granting you the conquest of the land of the Romans in this expedition of yours, [[See the explanation of "al-Isabah" (striking/reaching) in what preceded: 13:473, note 2, and the references there. And see the explanation of "al-Hasanah" (good) in the preceding linguistic indexes, under (h-s-n).]] it grieves al-Jadd ibn Qays, his counterparts and their followers among the hypocrites. And if a misfortune strikes you, through the rout (fulul) of your army in it, [["al-Fulul," the verbal noun of "fall" (falla), used intransitively, meaning: was defeated. It has been mentioned earlier in al-Tabari's words as well, but I did not find it mentioned in the lexicon books. See what preceded, 7:313, note 3, and what I said in correcting that, inferring from their saying "min fall dhall," meaning: whoever was defeated and fled from his enemy was humiliated.]] Al-Jadd and his counterparts say: ﴿We had already taken our precaution beforehand,﴾ meaning: we had already taken our caution by staying behind from Muhammad and abandoning his followers to his enemy. ﴿Beforehand﴾ means: before this misfortune befell him. ﴿And they turn away rejoicing﴾ means: and they turn back from Muhammad rejoicing at the misfortune that befell Muhammad and his companions, at the rout of his companions and their fleeing from him, [["al-Tawalli" (turning away): see its explanation in the preceding linguistic indexes, under (w-l-y).]] and at the killing of those among them who were killed.

* *

Ahl al-ta'wil (the people of interpretation) said what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

16792. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Ibn Abbas said regarding ﴿If good befalls you, it grieves them,﴾ "it means: if good befalls you in this expedition of yours, the expedition of Tabuk, ﴿good, it grieves them.﴾" He said: "al-Jadd and his companions."

16793. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿We had already taken our precaution beforehand,﴾ "our caution."

16794. Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Waraqa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "our caution."

16795. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿If good befalls you, it grieves them,﴾ "if there was a conquest for the Muslims, that was great and grievous to them."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 51:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿Say: Nothing will ever befall us except what Allah has decreed for us; He is our Protector, and upon Allah let the believers rely.﴾ (9:51)

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, Who mentions Himself, disciplining His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, to these hypocrites who stayed behind from you: ﴿Nothing will ever befall us﴾, you doubters in your religion, ﴿except what Allah has decreed for us﴾, in the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz), and has determined upon us [[See the explanation of "kataba" in the previous indexes of linguistic terms (k-t-b).]] ﴿He is our Protector﴾, meaning: He is our helper against His enemies [[See the explanation of "al-mawla" in the previous indexes of linguistic terms (w-l-y).]] ﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely﴾, meaning: upon Allah let the believers rely, for if they rely upon Him, and do not hope for victory from other than Him, and do not fear anything other than Him, He will suffice them in their affairs and grant them victory over those who seek to harm them and plot against them. [[See the explanation of "al-tawakkul" previously, p. 43, footnote 1, and the references there.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 52:

The interpretation (ta'wil) of His words: ﴿Say: Do you await for us anything but one of the two best things? And we await for you that Allah will afflict you with a punishment from Him or at our hands. So wait; indeed, we are waiting with you.﴾ (9:52)

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, to these hypocrites whose characteristics I have described to you and whose affair I have made clear to you: Do you await for us anything but one of the two states that are better than the others [[See the explanation of "tarabbus" (waiting) above, p. 177, footnote 3, and the references there.

And the explanation of "al-husna" (the best) above, 9:96-97.]] — either victory over the enemy and a conquest for us by our overcoming them, in which there is reward, booty and safety; or the killing of some of our enemy for us, in which there is martyrdom, success with Paradise, and deliverance from the Fire. Both are things we love and do not dislike. ﴿And we await for you that Allah will afflict you with a punishment from Him﴾, meaning: we await for you that Allah will afflict you with a punishment from Him, a swift retribution that destroys you. ﴿Or at our hands﴾, so that we kill you. ﴿So wait; indeed, we are waiting with you﴾, meaning: so wait; indeed, we are waiting with you to see what Allah will do with us and what the outcome of each of us and of you will be.

* *

And the people of ta'wil have said what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

16796. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿Do you await for us anything but one of the two best things?﴾ He says: victory or martyrdom. He said on another occasion: He means killing, in which there is martyrdom, life and provision. ﴿Or [Allah will afflict you] at our hands﴾ ... (meaning) He will humiliate you by our hands.

16797. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, he said: My paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿Do you await for us anything but one of the two best things?﴾ He says: killing, in which there is life and provision; or that he (the fighter) overcomes, and Allah will grant him a great reward. This is like His words: ﴿And whoever fights in the way of Allah﴾, up to ﴿then he is killed or overcomes, We shall grant him a great reward﴾ (Surah al-Nisa, 74).

16798. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, he said: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Waraqa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words: ﴿other than one of the two best things﴾. He said: killing in the way of Allah, and dominance over His enemies.

16799. ...... He said: Muhammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, he said: It reached me from Mujahid, he said: killing in the way of Allah, and dominance.

16800. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿one of the two best things﴾: killing in the way of Allah, and dominance over the enemies of Allah.

16801. Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: ﴿a punishment from Him﴾ means death. ﴿Or at our hands﴾: he said: killing.

16802. Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada regarding His words: ﴿Do you await for us anything but one of the two best things?﴾ Except victory or killing in the way of Allah. ﴿And we await for you that Allah will afflict you with a punishment from Him or at our hands﴾: that is, killing.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 53:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Say: Spend willingly or unwillingly; it will never be accepted from you. Indeed, you have been a defiantly disobedient people.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah the Exalted says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Say⁠

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 54:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿And nothing prevented their expenditures from being accepted from them except that they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger, and they do not come to the prayer except while they are lazy, and they do not spend except while they are unwilling﴾.

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Nothing prevented these hypocrites, O Muhammad, from having their expenditures, which they spent on their journeys with you and in other ways, accepted from them, except that they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger. The first "an" (that) is in the accusative position, and the second is in the nominative position, [[By the second "an" he means the emphatic "anna" in "annahum"; as for the first, it is the light "an".]] because the meaning of the statement is: what prevented the acceptance of their expenditures was only their disbelief in Allah. ﴿And they do not come to the prayer except while they are lazy﴾, meaning: they do not come to it except reluctantly, burdened by it. [[See the explanation of "kusala" (lazy) earlier, vol. 9, pp. 330-331.]] This is because they do not hope for reward by performing it, nor do they fear punishment by abandoning it; rather, they perform it only out of fear for themselves of the believers should they abandon it, and when the believers grant them security, they do not perform it. ﴿And they do not spend﴾, meaning: they do not spend anything of their wealth ﴿except while they are unwilling﴾, [to spend it] in the way they spend it, of what strengthens Islam and its people. [[See the explanation of "al-kurh" (unwillingness) earlier, p. 293, note 1, and the references there.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 55:

The discussion of His saying: ﴿So let not their wealth nor their children impress you. Allah only intends to punish them thereby in the worldly life, and that their souls should depart while they are disbelievers﴾ (9:55).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the interpretation of this.

Some of them said: its meaning is: "Let not their wealth nor their children impress you, O Muhammad, in the worldly life. Allah only intends to punish them with them in the Hereafter." And they said: the meaning of this is taqdim (anticipation, i.e. inversion of word order), and it is postponed (mu'akhkhar).

Mention of those who said this:

16804 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿So let not their wealth nor their children impress you﴾, he said: "This is of the taqadim (inversions) of speech. [[This is the first time I find the use of "taqadim" as a plural in this tafsir. It is the plural of "taqdim," like its counterparts in their saying "al-takadhib," "al-takalif," "al-tahasin," "al-taqasib," and what resembles them.

In the manuscript it read: "This is of the taqadim of Allah, to punish them with them in the Hereafter," but the editor of the printed edition took this text established in the print from al-Durr al-Manthur 3:249, and it seems to be correct, God willing, and therefore I left it as it is.

See also Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1:442.]] It means: Let not their wealth nor their children in the worldly life impress you. Allah only intends to punish them with them in the Hereafter."

16805 - al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: "Allah only intends to punish them with them in the Hereafter."

* * *

Others said: rather, the meaning of this is: "Allah only intends to punish them with them in the worldly life, through the obligations He imposed upon them in it."

Mention of those who said this:

16806 - It was related to me from al-Musayyib ibn Shurayk, from Salman al-Ansari, from al-Hasan: ﴿Allah only intends to punish them thereby in the worldly life﴾, he said: "By taking the zakat and expenditure in the way of Allah. [[Report 16806: "al-Musayyib ibn Shurayk al-Tamimi, Abu Sa'id," whose narrations people abandoned, and al-Bukhari said: "They remained silent about him." Listed in al-Kabir 4/1/408, Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/294, Mizan al-I'tidal 3:171, and Lisan al-Mizan 6:38.

"Salman al-Ansari" is thus in the manuscript, while in the printed edition it reads "al-Aqsari," and I was unable to learn anything about this name.]]

16807 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿Allah only intends to punish them thereby in the worldly life﴾, "by the calamities in it. They are a punishment for them, and for the believers they are a reward."

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: The interpretation most correct in our view is the interpretation we mentioned from al-Hasan, because it is the apparent meaning of the revelation, and turning its interpretation to what its outward sense indicates is better than turning it to a hidden meaning for which there is no evidence of soundness.

Those who directed it to taqdim (postponed inversion) did so only because they did not know a direction in which Allah's punishing the hypocrites with their wealth and children in the worldly life could be understood. They said: "How would He punish them with that in the world, when they have joy in it?" They overlooked the understanding that among the greatest punishments for them is the imposition upon them of what Allah made obligatory in it of His rights and obligations, since it is taken from them while they are not content, nor do they hope for any reward from Allah, nor do they give thanks or praise to the one who takes it, out of distress and aversion.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿and that their souls should depart while they are disbelievers﴾, it means: their souls depart, so they die upon their disbelief in Allah and their denial of the prophethood of the Prophet of Allah Muhammad (ﷺ).

* * *

It is said from it: "zahaqat nafs fulan" and "zahiqat" (both forms); whoever says "zahaqat" says "tazhaq," and whoever says "zahiqat" says "tazhaq," "zuhuqan." From it is said: "zahaqa fulan bayna aydi al-qawm yazhaqu zuhuqan" when he outpaces them and goes ahead of them. And it is said: "zahaqa al-batil," when it departs and vanishes. [[I do not know what this is, for the lexicographers mention in the present tense of both dialects only "tazhaq" with a fatha on the ha'; as for the other, I do not know what it would be, and I find no justification for it, so I left it as it is without vowelling it.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 56:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿And they swear by Allah that they are surely of you, but they are not of you; rather, they are a people who are fearful﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: "And these hypocrites swear by Allah to you, O believers, falsely and baselessly, out of fear of you: ﴿that they are surely of you﴾ in religion and faith." Allah, may He be exalted, says, refuting them: ﴿but they are not of you﴾, that is, they are not of the people of your religion and faith, but rather they are people of doubt and hypocrisy. ﴿Rather, they are a people who are fearful﴾, He says: rather, they are a people who fear you. So, out of fear of you, they say with their tongues: "We are of you," so that they may be safe among you and not be killed.

**The commentary on His words: ﴿Had they found a refuge, or caves, or a place to enter﴾ [9:57]**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: If these hypocrites found a *malja'* (refuge), meaning a fortress from which they could seek protection and a stronghold in which they could take shelter from you, ﴿or caves﴾,

* *

that is, the hollows in the mountains. Its singular is *mughara*, which is a *maf'ala* form, from "the man entered (*ghara*) into the thing, *yaghuru* into it," meaning he went in. From this comes the expression "the eye sank (*gharat*)," meaning it went into the socket.

* *

﴿Or a place to enter﴾ means a *sarab* (a tunnel or passage) in the earth into which they could enter.

* *

He said "or a place to enter," the verse [continues], because it derives from "*iddakhala yaddakhilu*" (to enter). [[In the printed edition: "or a place to enter, the verse, because it," which is a printing error in my opinion. It appears that "the verse" was added because of its resemblance to the "because it" that follows it. The corrector of the edition disagreed and restored what he had corrected!!]]

* *

As for His words ﴿they would turn away to it﴾, meaning they would flee to it from you, ﴿while they rush headlong﴾, meaning they would hasten in their walking. [[See the explanation of "*al-tawalli*" in the earlier language indexes under (w-l-y).]]

* *

It has been said that *al-jimah* is a gait between two gaits. [[This is a rare text which you will not find in the books of lexicography, so it should be noted, along with its evidence.]] From it comes the verse of Muhalhil:

*Indeed I rushed headlong into their blood, until I saw their noblest men become still.* [[I have not found this verse in what I have examined of Muhalhil's poetry. His phrase "*khamadu*" means they became quiet and died, as an ember goes out.]]

* *

God described them with this attribute only because they remained among the companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) while concealing their disbelief, hypocrisy, and enmity toward them, and toward what they held of belief in God and His Messenger. They lived among their people and clan, in their homes and with their wealth, and so they could not give up that life or leave it. So they flattered the people with hypocrisy, and defended themselves, their wealth, and their children with disbelief and claims of faith, while in their hearts lay the hatred of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and the people of faith, and enmity toward them. Therefore God, describing them by what was in their inner selves, said: ﴿If they found a refuge or caves﴾, and so on.

* *

Ahl al-ta'wil (the people of interpretation) said things in agreement with what we have said.

**Those who said this:**

16808. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿If they found a refuge﴾: "*al-malja'*" is a stronghold in the mountains. "*Al-maghabat*" (caves) are the hollows in the mountains. As for His words ﴿or a place to enter﴾, "*al-mudakhal*" is a *sarab* (passage).

16809. Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿If they found a refuge or caves or a place to enter, they would turn away to it while rushing headlong﴾: "*malja'*" means a stronghold; ﴿or caves﴾ means the hollows; ﴿or a place to enter﴾ means a going-away into the earth, which is a tunnel in the earth, which is a *sarab*.

16810. And Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿If they found a refuge or caves or a place to enter﴾, he said: a stronghold for them to flee to from you.

16811. Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid regarding His words: ﴿If they found a refuge or caves or a place to enter﴾, he said: a stronghold for them, they would flee to it from you. And Ibn Abbas said regarding His words: ﴿If they found a refuge﴾, a stronghold; ﴿or caves﴾, he said: the hollows; ﴿or a place to enter﴾, he said: a tunnel in the earth.

16812. Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, from Sa'id, from Qatada: ﴿If they found a refuge or caves or a place to enter﴾, he said: "If they found a refuge": fortresses; ﴿or caves﴾: hollows; ﴿or a place to enter﴾: passages; ﴿they would turn away to it while rushing headlong﴾.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 58:**

*On the interpretation of His words:* ﴿And among them are those who criticise you concerning the charities. If they are given from them, they are pleased; and if they are not given from them, at once they are angry﴾ (9:58).

Abu Ja'far said: Almighty God says: "And among the hypocrites whom I have described to you, O Muhammad, in these verses, their description [is]: ﴿who criticise you concerning the charities﴾," meaning: they find fault with you regarding their distribution, and they slander you concerning them.

* *

It is said of this: "Fulan *lamaza* Fulan *yalmizuhu* and *yalmuzuhu*" when he found fault with him and taunted him. Likewise *hamazahu*. From this it is said, "Fulan is a *humazah lumazah*" (a backbiter and a slanderer). From this is the verse of Ru'bah:

*I have brought close together my ʿanaq (gait) and my jamz (gallop)*
*in the shade of my two ages of falsehood and slander.*

[[His Diwan: 64. It is from his rajaz (poem) concerning Aban ibn al-Walid al-Bajali, in which he then mentioned himself, saying: "If you see me today as Umm Hamz, / I have brought close together my ʿanaq and my jamz, / after the leaping of youth, the swift one, / in the shade of my two ages of falsehood and slander. / So every good beginning or ignoble one / meets the death-blow of the cut-off term."

"Umm Hamz" means "Umm Hamzah." The *ʿanaq* is a kind of running, and the *jamz* is above the ʿanaq and below the full gallop, and it is an intense running. He means that his running has come close to a walk because he has grown old. "Taqammus al-shabab" (the leaping of youth) is from *qamas*: "the horse *qamas*," when it shied and kicked up, which is to raise both its forelegs together and throw them down, and to bounce with its hind legs. *Taqammus* is a verbal noun which the lexicons do not mention. *Al-abaz* is one who leaps much and rushes in his running; it is said "a *abuz* and *abaz* gazelle." The lexicographers did not mention *al-abaz* among the adjectives, and it is here used as an adjective in the form of a verbal noun. *Al-badʾ* is a young noble chief, put forward and of praised opinion. *Al-naqz* (with a kasra on the nun) is a base and vile person among people.]]

And from it is the saying of another:

[[He is Ziyad al-Aʿjam.]]

*When I meet you, you show me flattery,*
*but if I am absent, you are the backbiter and the slanderer.*

[[Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu ʿUbaydah 1: 263; Islah al-Mantiq: 475; al-Jamhara of Ibn Duraid 3: 18; al-Maqayis 6: 66; al-Lisan (h-m-z). It will come in the tafsir 30: 188 (Bulaq) with a version other than this, which is: "You show affection when you meet me, falsely, / but if I am absent, you are the one who defames and slanders."

This is the version of Ibn al-Sikkit, Ibn Faris, and al-Tabari afterward, and the version of Ibn Duraid and the author of al-Lisan. "When I meet you from a distance, you flatter me."

And his saying "wa in ughayyab" (but if I am absent) is in the passive voice, not as it is vocalised in Majaz al-Qur'an.]]

*= ﴿If they are given from them, they are pleased﴾*: he says, "It is not religion that moves them in their criticism of you and their slander of you concerning them, but anger for their own selves. If you give them from it what satisfies them, they are pleased with you; and if you do not give them from it, they are angry with you and find fault with you."

* *

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said in accordance with what we have said regarding this.

*Mention of those who said that:*

16813- Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Waraqa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid concerning His words: ﴿And among them are those who criticise you concerning the charities﴾, he said: "yarūzuk" (he tests you).

[["Razahu yarūzuhu rawzan": he tested him and examined him. This report has been mentioned in the lexicons from the words of Mujahid, and they explained it, saying: "It is said: I tested what Fulan has, when I tested him and examined him. The meaning is: he examines you and tastes your affair, whether you fear his censure or not."]]

16814- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid concerning His words: ﴿And among them are those who criticise you concerning the charities﴾, "yarūzuk and yasʾaluk" (he tests you and asks you). [["Razahu yarūzuhu rawzan," he tested him and examined him... (as above).]] Ibn Juraij said: Dawud ibn Abi ʿAsim informed me, saying: "A charity was brought to the Prophet ﷺ, and he distributed it here and here until it was gone." He said: "A man from the Ansar saw him and said: 'This is not justice!' So this verse was revealed."

16815- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah concerning His words: ﴿And among them are those who criticise you concerning the charities﴾, he says: "And among them are those who taunt you concerning the charities." And it has been related to us that a man from the people of the desert, recently acquainted with the Bedouin life, came to the Prophet of God ﷺ while he was distributing gold and silver, and said: "O Muhammad, by God, if God has commanded you to be just, you have not been just!" The Prophet of God ﷺ said: "Woe to you! Who then will be just to you after me?" Then the Prophet of God ﷺ said: "Beware of this one and his likes, for among my community there are those like this, who recite the Qur'an but it does not pass their collarbones. When they go out, kill them; then when they go out, kill them; then when they go out, kill them." And it has been related to us that the Prophet of God ﷺ used to say: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, I do not give you anything, nor withhold it from you; I am only a treasurer."

16816- Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah: ﴿And among them are those who criticise you concerning the charities﴾, he said: "yatʿanu" (he defames).

16817- ...... narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, from Abu Saʿid, who said: While the Messenger of God ﷺ was distributing a share, there came to him Ibn Dhi al-Khuwaysirah al-Tamimi, [[In Muslim and al-Bukhari it is "Dhu al-Khuwaysirah," without "Ibn." This is the known and well-established form.]] and he said: "Be just, O Messenger of God!" He said: "Woe to you! Who will be just if I am not just?" ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab said: "O Messenger of God, permit me to strike his neck!" He said: "Leave him, for he has companions, whose prayer one of you will consider small compared to their prayer, and whose fasting [one of you considers small] compared to their fasting. They pass through the religion as an arrow passes through the game; [[*Maraqa al-sahm min al-ramiyyah*: it came out of the other side with rapid exit. *Al-ramiyyah* is the thing shot at, meaning the game shot with an arrow or the like.]] then one looks at its feathers and sees nothing, then looks at its point and sees nothing, then looks at its shaft and sees nothing; it has outrun the dung and the blood. [[*Al-farth*: the dung of an animal, as long as it is in its stomach.]] Their sign is a man, black, [[*Al-aya*: the sign.]] with one of his hands — or he said: his hands — like the breast of a woman, or like a lump of flesh that trembles; [[*Al-bidʿah*: a piece of meat. *Tadardar*: it jerks, i.e., it moves about.]] they will come out at a time of interval among the people." He said: Then it was revealed: ﴿And among them are those who criticise you concerning the charities﴾. Abu Saʿid said: "I bear witness that I heard this from the Messenger of God ﷺ, and I bear witness that ʿAli, may God have mercy on him, when he killed them, the man was brought in according to the description that the Messenger of God ﷺ had described."

[[The report 16817: This is a hadith of sound chain. al-Bukhari related it in his Sahih (al-Fath 6: 455) and Muslim in his Sahih 7: 165, by way of al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman.

The report has come through many sound channels; see the commentary on al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim.]]

16817m- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His words: ﴿And among them are those who criticise you concerning the charities. If they are given from them, they are pleased; and if they are not given from them, at once they are angry﴾, he said: "These are the hypocrites. They said: 'By God, Muhammad gives it only to whom he loves, and he prefers with it only his own desire!' So God informed His Prophet, and informed them that it had come only from God, and that this was a command from God, not from Muhammad: ﴿The charities are only for the poor﴾," and so on (the verse).

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 59:

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿And if only they had been content with what Allah and His Messenger gave them, and had said, "Allah is sufficient for us; Allah will give us of His bounty, and so will His Messenger; to Allah we are turning in hope"﴾.

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is His mention, says: And if only these people who find fault with you, O Muhammad, concerning the alms (sadaqat), had been content with what Allah and His Messenger gave them of bestowal, and with the portion He allotted to them from the division, ﴿and had said, "Allah is sufficient for us"﴾, meaning: and had said, "Allah is our sufficiency" [[See the explanation of "hasb" (sufficiency) above, p. 49, footnote 1, and the references there.]] ﴿"Allah will give us of His bounty, and so will His Messenger"﴾, meaning: Allah will give us of the abundance of His treasures, and His Messenger will give us of the alms and other things [[See the explanation of "atā" (to give) and "fadl" (bounty) in the language indexes (ātā), (faḍl).]] ﴿"To Allah we are turning in hope"﴾, meaning: and had said, "To Allah we turn in desire that He expand His bounty for us, so that He makes us independent of the alms and of other gifts from people and of our need for them."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 60 (part 1 of 3):

The explanation of His words: ﴿Indeed, the alms are only for the poor and the needy, and those employed to collect them, and those whose hearts are to be reconciled, and for the freeing of captives, and for those in debt, and for the cause of Allah, and for the wayfarer—an obligation from Allah. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.﴾ [9:60]

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of His words, exalted is His remembrance, is: The alms are only for the poor and the needy, [In the printed edition: "la yanal al-sadaqat" ("does not attain the alms"), which is not a sound reading; the correct reading is what is in the manuscript, but its reading was not well done.] and those whom Allah, exalted is His praise, named.

* *

Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the description of the "faqir" (poor) and the "miskin" (needy).

Some of them said: the "faqir" is the person in need who abstains from asking, and the "miskin" is the person in need who asks. [See the explanation of "miskin" above, 13:560, note 2, and the references there.]

Those who said this:

16818- Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿Indeed, the alms are only for the poor and the needy﴾, he said: "The faqir" is the one who sits in his house, and "the miskin" is the one who goes about (seeking).

16819- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to us, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding his words: ﴿Indeed, the alms are only for the poor and the needy﴾, he said: "The miskin" are the wanderers, and "the fuqara'" are the poor among the Muslims.

16820- Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Abu Usama narrated to us, from Jarir ibn Hazim, who said: a man narrated to me, from Jabir ibn Zayd, that he was asked about "the fuqara'", and he said: "The fuqara'" are those who abstain (from asking), and "the masakin" are those who ask.

16821- Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Ma'qil ibn 'Ubayd Allah al-Jazari narrated to us, saying: I asked al-Zuhri about His words: ﴿Indeed, the alms are only for the poor﴾, and he said: Those who are in their houses and do not ask, and "the masakin" are those who go out and ask. [The report 16821: "Ma'qil ibn 'Ubayd Allah al-Jazari al-'Absi, al-Harrani", trustworthy, with nothing wrong with him. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/1/393, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/286. In the printed edition it was "al-Harrani" instead of "al-Jazari", which is correct, but I retain what is in the manuscript.]

16822- Al-Harith narrated to us, saying: al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Warith ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "The faqir" is the one who does not ask, and "the miskin" is the one who asks.

16823- Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, the alms are only for the poor and the needy﴾: "The fuqara'" are those who do not ask people, the people of need, [In the printed edition: "wa-huwa ahl hajah" ("and he is one of the people of need"), which adds what is not in the manuscript.] and "the masakin" are those who ask people.

16824- Al-Harith narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-Warith narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "The fuqara'" are those who do not ask, and "the masakin" are those who ask.

* *

Others said: "The faqir" is the one who is afflicted by a disability among the people in need, and "the miskin" is the one among them who is physically sound. [In the printed edition, "minhum" ("among them") is omitted.]

Those who said this:

16825- Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding ﴿Indeed, the alms are only for the poor and the needy﴾, he said: "The faqir" is the one who has a disability, and "the miskin" is the sound one who is in need.

16826- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding his words: ﴿Indeed, the alms are only for the poor and the needy﴾: As for "the faqir", he is the disabled person who has a disability, and as for "the miskin", he is the one who has no disability.

* *

Others said: "The fuqara'" are the poor among the Emigrants (muhajirun), and "the masakin" are those among the Muslims who did not emigrate and are in need.

Those who said this:

16827- Al-Harith narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, regarding ﴿Indeed, the alms are only for the poor﴾, he said: The poor among the Emigrants, and "the masakin" are those who did not emigrate. [The report 16827: "'Ali ibn al-Hakam al-Bunani", trustworthy, with some traditions. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/181.]

16828- ...... narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, regarding ﴿Indeed, the alms are only for the poor﴾, the Emigrants. He said: Sufyan: meaning, and nothing from it is given to the Bedouins.

16829- Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, who said: It used to be said: the alms are only for the poor Emigrants.

16830- ...... narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, who said: The alms used to be placed among the poor Emigrants, and in the cause of Allah.

16831- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza, who both said: [In the printed edition: "qal" ("he said"), and the correct reading is from the manuscript.] Some of the Emigrants had a house, a wife, a slave, and a camel on which they performed Hajj and went to war, so Allah attributed to them the description of being poor, and assigned them a share in the zakat.

16832- Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, who said: It used to be said: the alms are for the poor Emigrants and in the cause of Allah.

* *

Others said: "The miskin" is the one weak in earning. [In the printed edition: "al-da'if al-bu'is" ("the weak and wretched"), which mis-reads the manuscript; the manuscript had "al-nasab", which is a distortion, as the following reports show.]

Those who said this:

16833- Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Awn informed us, from Muhammad, who said: 'Umar said: The poor man is not the one who has no wealth, but the poor man is the one whose earning is worn out (akhlaq al-kasb). Ya'qub said: Ibn 'Ulayyah said: "Al-akhlaq", according to us, means the one whose fortune is diminished. [ʿUmar meant: the poor man is the one who has sent forward nothing for his Hereafter for which he would be rewarded, and that the greatest poverty is the poverty of the Hereafter, and that the poverty of this world is the lesser of the two poverties. "Al-akhlaq" derives from the expression "hadbah khalqa'", a smooth hill with no vegetation on it; and a solid mountain on which nothing has an effect is called "akhlaq". In the hadith of Fatima bint Qays: "As for Mu'awiya, he is a man akhlaq min al-mal," meaning: empty and bare of it. As for "al-mahraf", as Ibn 'Ulayyah explained it, it is one whose share is diminished, so he is deprived and cut off: when he seeks provision he is not provided for; the opposite of "al-mubarak" (blessed).]

16834- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Ayyub, from Ibn Sirin, that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The miskin is not the one who has no wealth, but the miskin is the one whose earning is worn out.

* *

Some said: "The faqir" is from among the Muslims, and "the miskin" is from among the People of the Book.

Those who said this:

16835- Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: 'Umar ibn Nafi' narrated to us, saying: I heard 'Ikrimah regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, the alms are only for the poor and the needy﴾, he said: Do not call the poor Muslims "masakin"; rather, "the masakin" are the needy among the People of the Book.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these opinions in my view is the view of the one who said: "The faqir" is the one who has poverty or need, and who, despite his need, abstains from asking people and from humbling himself before them, in this context; and "the miskin" is the one in need who humbles himself before people by asking them.

We said that this is so, even though both groups are given only on account of poverty and need, not on account of humiliation and asking, [In the printed edition: "al-dhull wal-maskanah" ("humiliation and destitution"), and the correct reading is what is in the manuscript, which they did not read well.] because all the scholars agree that "the miskin" is given from the obligatory alms on account of poverty, and that the meaning of "maskanah" among the Arabs is humiliation, as Allah, exalted is His praise, said: ﴿And humiliation and wretchedness were struck upon them﴾ [2:61], meaning by that: disgrace and humiliation, not poverty. Since Allah, exalted is His praise, has classified those to whom He assigns a share of the obligatory alms by poverty, making them two categories, it is known that each category is other than the other. Since that is so, there is no doubt that the one assigned by the name "faqir" is other than the one assigned by the name of poverty and "maskanah"; the faqir who is given that by the name of the absolute poor is the one who has no maskanah in him, and the one given by the name of maskanah and poverty is the one who combines with his poverty maskanah, which is humiliation through seeking and asking.

= So the meaning of the statement, given that this is its sense, is: the alms are for the poor: the abstaining among them who does not ask, and the humbled among them who asks.

* *

It has also been related from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a report similar to what we have said on this matter.

16836- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from Shurayk ibn Abi Namir, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The miskin is not the one who is turned away by one morsel or two, or one date or two. Rather, the miskin is the one who abstains! Recite if you wish: ﴿They do not ask people persistently﴾" [2:273]. [The report 16836: "Isma'il ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Kathir al-Ansari", narrated by the group; it passed as no. 6884, 8398. "Shurayk ibn Abi Namir" is "Shurayk ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Namir al-Qurashi", trustworthy, narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim, biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 2/2/237, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/363. This report was narrated by al-Bukhari through the route of Muhammad ibn Ja'far from Shurayk ibn Abi Namir (al-Fath 8:152), and Muslim narrated it in his Sahih through the route of Isma'il ibn Ja'far, from Shurayk, and through the route of Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Shurayk, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Amrah, from Abu Hurayrah (7:129).]

The meaning of his saying (ﷺ): "Rather, the miskin is the one who abstains" is in accordance with the common usage of people in calling the poor "masakin", not as a distinction between the miskin and the faqir.

Among what indicates that this is so is that he (ﷺ) cited the words of Allah [In the printed edition: "intizaʿan li-qawl Allah" ("as a citation of the words of Allah"), which is an error; the correct reading is in the manuscript. It is said "intaza'a bil-ayah" or "bil-shi'r" when one recites the verse or the poetry as a proof.] Recite if you wish: ﴿They do not ask people persistently﴾, and that was in the description of those whom Allah, exalted is His remembrance, began by mentioning and described as poor, saying: ﴿For the poor who are confined in the cause of Allah, unable to move about in the land. The ignorant man thinks them wealthy because of their abstinence. You recognize them by their mark; they do not ask people persistently﴾ [2:273].

* *

As for His words: ﴿and those employed to collect them﴾, they are the collectors in taking them from their owners and placing them with those entitled to them; they are given that for their work, whether they are rich or poor.

* *

The people of interpretation said things in agreement with what we have said on this.

Those who said this:

16837- Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Ma'qil ibn 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, saying: I asked al-Zuhri about "those employed to collect them", and he said: the collectors.

16838- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿and those employed to collect them﴾, he said: its collectors who gather it and work at it.

16839- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: ﴿and those employed to collect them﴾: the one who works on it.

* *

Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the amount that the worker is given from that.

Some of them said: he is given one-eighth of it.

Those who said this:

16840- Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Hasan ibn Salih, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, who said: For those employed to collect them there is one-eighth of the alms.

16841- It was related to me from Muslim ibn Khalid, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words: ﴿and those employed to collect them﴾, he said: the workers eat from the eighth share.

* *

Others said: rather, he is given according to the amount of his labor.

Those who said this:

16842- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn 'Ata' narrated to us, from al-Akhdar ibn 'Ajlan, who said: 'Ata' ibn Zuhayr al-'Amiri narrated to us, from his father, that he met 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As and asked him about the alms: what kind of wealth is it? He said: It is the wealth of the lame, the blind, the one-eyed, and everyone who is cut off. ["Munqati' bih" (passive), is the man who, when he is unable to travel for lack of expenses that have been lost, or when his mount has come to a stop, or when something comes upon him that prevents him from moving with it. One says "qati'a bihi" and "inqata'a bihi".] He said to him: Indeed, the workers have a right, and so do the fighters! He said: Indeed, the fighters are a people for whom it is permitted, and those employed to collect them are given according to the amount of their labor. [In the printed edition: "wa-lil-'amilin" ("and for the workers"); I have retained what is in the manuscript.] Then he said: The alms are not lawful for the rich, nor for one who has able strength. [The report 16842: "'Abd al-Wahhab ibn 'Ata' al-Khaffaf", trustworthy, passed as nos. 5429, 5432, 10522. "Al-Akhdar ibn 'Ajlan al-Shaybani", trustworthy, biographed in al-Tahdhib and al-Kabir 1/2/67. "'Ata' ibn Zuhayr ibn al-Asbagh al-'Amiri", narrated from his father, narrated from him Shumayt and al-Akhdar ibn 'Ajlan; thus mentioned by Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/332, and I have found no biography of him elsewhere. His father: "Zuhayr ibn al-Asbagh al-'Amiri", narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, narrated from him his son 'Ata'; biographed in al-Kabir 2/1/392 and Ibn Hatim 1/2/587, and neither mentions any criticism of him. This report was cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 3:252, attributing it only to Abu al-Shaykh, and in it is "'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar", which is an error.]

16843- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: It is for the worker on it if he works in truth; and 'Umar, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, and those others did not give the worker an eighth; rather, they assigned him according to the amount of his labor.

16844- Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿and those employed to collect them﴾, he said: the workers used to be given.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the views on this matter is the statement of the one who said: the worker on it is given according to the amount of his labor and the wage of his like.

We say that this is more correct because Allah, exalted is His praise, did not divide the alms of wealth among the eight categories into eight shares; rather, He made His creation know that the alms will not go beyond these eight categories to others. Since that is so, as we will clarify later, and as we have clarified elsewhere, it is known that whoever is given a portion of it is given according to the effort of the one who gives it. Since that is so, and since the worker on it is given for his work, not for the need which is removed by the gift, it is known that what he is given from it is a return for his effort and work, and that this is an amount he deserves as a return for his work, which is not removed by the gift, but is removed only by dismissal.

* *

As for "those whose hearts are to be reconciled" (al-mu'allafah qulubuhum), they are people who were won over to Islam, among those whose support was not sound, in order to reform through them themselves and their clans, such as Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, 'Uyaynah ibn Badr, al-Aqra' ibn Habis, and their counterparts among the chiefs of the tribes.

* *

The people of interpretation said things in agreement with what we have said on this.

Those who said this:

16845- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding his words: ﴿and those whose hearts are to be reconciled﴾, and they are people who used to come to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) having embraced Islam, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would give them a small share from the alms. ["Radkha lahu min maalihi radikhatan" means he gave him a modest gift, not a large one; its origin is from "al-radkh", which is breaking the date-stone and the like, as if he broke off for him a piece of his wealth.] So when he gave them from the alms and they benefited from it, they said: This is a good religion! And if it was otherwise, they found fault with it and abandoned it.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 60 (part 2 of 3)**

16846. Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: [[In the printed edition: "Abd al-A'la narrated to us," which is an error; the correct reading, from the manuscript, is as given here. This chain recurs in the tafsir, and Tabari's teacher is "Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la."]] Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, that those whose hearts were to be reconciled (al-mu'allafa qulubuhum) from the Banu Umayya were: Abu Sufyan ibn Harb; from the Banu Makhzum: al-Harith ibn Hisham and Abd al-Rahman ibn Yarbu'; from the Banu Jumah: Safwan ibn Umayya; from the Banu Amir ibn Lu'ayy: Suhayl ibn Amr and Huwaytib ibn Abd al-Uzza; from the Banu Asad ibn Abd al-Uzza: Hakim ibn Hizam; from the Banu Hashim: Sufyan ibn al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib; from the Banu Fazara: Uyayna ibn Hisn ibn Badr; from the Banu Tamim: al-Aqra' ibn Habis; from the Banu Nasr: Malik ibn Awf; from the Banu Sulaym: al-Abbas ibn Mirdas; and from Thaqif: al-Ala' ibn Harithah. The Prophet (ﷺ) gave each one of them a hundred camels, except Abd al-Rahman ibn Yarbu' and Huwaytib ibn Abd al-Uzza, to whom he gave fifty each.

16847. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, who said: Safwan ibn Umayya said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave me, and he was the most hateful of people to me, yet he kept on giving until he became the most beloved of people to me." [[The report: 16847. Muslim narrated it in his Sahih (15:72-73), in a lengthier form, by way of Abd Allah ibn Wahb, from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Safwan ibn Umayya. Ahmad also narrated it in his Musnad (3:401) by way of Zakariyya ibn Adi, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Safwan (as it appears here in the Musnad).
