The correct version is what will come in the Musnad (6:465), by way of Zakariyya ibn Adi, from Ibn al-Mubarak, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab.]]

16848. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "Some people whom he (the Prophet) used to win over with gifts: Uyayna ibn Badr and those who were with him."

16849. Ibn Wakf narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, concerning ﴿those whose hearts are to be reconciled﴾: they are those who are won over to Islam.

16850. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: As for "those whose hearts are to be reconciled," they are some people from the Bedouin and others, whom the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) used to win over with gifts so that they would believe.

16851. Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Ma'qil ibn Ubayd Allah narrated to us, saying: I asked al-Zuhri about the words of Allah ﴿and those whose hearts are to be reconciled﴾, and he said: "Whoever of a Jew or a Christian embraces Islam." I said: "Even if he is wealthy?" He said: "Even if he is wealthy."

16852. al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, saying: Ma'qil ibn Ubayd Allah al-Jazari narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, concerning ﴿and those whose hearts are to be reconciled﴾: he said: "He is a Jew or a Christian." [[The report: 16852. "Ma'qil ibn Ubayd Allah al-Jazari" passed shortly before, under no. 16821. In the printed edition here "al-Jazari" was also given as "al-Harrani," in place of "al-Jazari," which is correct; but I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

Then the scholars differed over whether the "reconciled hearts" exist today, and whether anyone today may be given from the alms (sadaqah) to win them over to Islam.

Some of them said: The category of "those whose hearts are to be reconciled" has ceased today, and no one has a share in the obligatory alms except one in need of them, and in the way of Allah, or an official who collects them.

Mention of those who said this:

16853. Ibn Wakf narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from al-Hasan, concerning ﴿and those whose hearts are to be reconciled﴾, he said: As for "those whose hearts are to be reconciled," it does not apply today.

16854. Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Jabir, from Amir, who said: "No one among the people today is of those whose hearts are to be reconciled; they existed only in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

16855. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Yahya narrated to us, from Hibban ibn Abi Jabalah, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said, when Uyayna ibn Hisn came to him: ﴿The truth is from your Lord; so whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve﴾ [Surah al-Kahf: 29], meaning: there are no "reconciled hearts" today.

16856. al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, saying: Mubarak narrated to us, from al-Hasan, who said: "There are no 'reconciled hearts' today."

16857. Ibn Wakf narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Jabir, from Amir, who said: "Those whose hearts were to be reconciled existed only in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ). When Abu Bakr (may Allah have mercy on him) assumed authority, the bribes ceased."

* * *

Others said: "Those whose hearts are to be reconciled" exist in every age, and they have a right to the alms.

Mention of those who said this:

16858. Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far, who said: "Among the people today there are those whose hearts are to be reconciled."

16859. Ibn Wakf narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far, the same.

* * *

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The correct view on this matter, in my opinion, is that Allah made the alms serve two purposes: one, to fill the need of the Muslims; the other, to support and strengthen Islam. Whatever is given for the support of Islam and the strengthening of its causes, it is given to both the rich and the poor, because whoever is given it is not given it out of need for it, but is given it as support for the religion. This is like the one who is given for striving in the way of Allah: he is given this, whether rich or poor, for the military campaign, not to fill his need. Likewise, those whose hearts are to be reconciled are given this even if they are rich, in order to win them over by giving them the matter of Islam and seeking to strengthen and support it. The Prophet (ﷺ) gave to some of those whose hearts were to be reconciled after Allah had granted him conquests, and Islam had spread and its people had grown mighty. So there is no argument for anyone who says: "No one is won over to Islam today, since its people have become numerous enough to repel whoever they wish," for the Prophet (ﷺ) gave to some of them in the circumstances I have described.

* * *

As for His words ﴿and for the captives (fi al-riqab)﴾, the interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) differed about its meaning.

Some of them said, and they are the vast majority: They are the mukatabun (slaves who have contracted to buy their freedom), who are given from it to free their necks. [[See the explanation of "al-riqab" previously: 3:347; 9:35-36; 10:552-557.]]

Mention of those who said this:

16860. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from al-Hasan ibn Dinar, from al-Husayn: that a mukatab stood before Abu Musa al-Ash'ari (may Allah have mercy on him) while he was delivering a sermon to the people on Friday, and said to him: "O Commander, urge the people on my behalf!" So Abu Musa urged them on his behalf, and the people threw on him turbans, cloaks and rings, until they threw down a great quantity. When Abu Musa saw what had been thrown on him, he said: "Gather it!" It was gathered, and then he ordered that it be sold. He gave the mukatab his contract (mukatabah) money, then gave the surplus for the captives, and did not return it to the people, saying: "The people have given it only for the captives."

16861. Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Ma'qil ibn Ubayd Allah narrated to us, saying: I asked al-Zuhri about His words ﴿and for the captives﴾, and he said: "The mukatabun."

16862. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His words ﴿and for the captives﴾: "The mukatab."

16863. Ibn Wakf narrated to us, saying: Sahl ibn Yusuf narrated to us, from Amr, from al-Hasan, concerning ﴿and for the captives﴾: "They are the mukatabun."

* * *

It is reported from Ibn Abbas that he said: "There is no harm in freeing a slave with zakat."

* * *

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The correct view on this matter, in my opinion, is the view of the one who said: "By 'the captives' in this verse are meant the mukatabun," because of the consensus of the authoritative scholars (ijma' al-hujjah) on this. For Allah made zakat an obligatory right upon the one on whom He imposed it in his wealth, which he gives out of it; no benefit or return of worldly goods comes back to him from it. Whoever frees a slave with it, however, has the wala' (patronage) of the one he freed returning to him, and that is a benefit that comes back to him from it.

* * *

As for "the debtors (al-gharimun)," they are those who incurred debts in other than disobedience to Allah, and then could not find payment for them in goods or in cash.

* * *

The interpreters said what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said this:

16864. Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Uthman ibn al-Aswad, from Mujahid, who said: "The debtors (al-gharimun)" are those whose house burned down, or whom a flood struck so that their goods were lost, and who borrowed for the sake of their dependents; these are of the debtors.

16865. al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Uthman ibn al-Aswad, from Mujahid, concerning His words ﴿and the debtors﴾, he said: "Whose house burned down, or whose wealth the flood carried off, and who borrowed for his dependents."

16866. Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far, who said: "The debtors (al-gharimin)" are those who borrow without extravagance; the imam should pay their debts from the public treasury.

16867. ...... He said: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Ma'qil ibn Ubayd Allah narrated to us, saying: We asked al-Zuhri about "the debtors," and he said: "The creditors' companions (ashab al-din)."

16868. ...... He said: Ma'qil narrated to us, from Abd al-Karim, who said: A servant of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz who served him for twenty years told me: "Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz wrote that the debtors should be given" (Ahmad said: "My strongest impression is: from the alms").

16869. ...... He said: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far, who said: "The debtors (al-gharimun)" are those who borrow without extravagance.

16870. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: As for "the debtors," they are a people whom debts overwhelmed without poverty-inducing waste (al-imlaq) [[Al-imlaq here means: spending wealth and squandering it until it results in need; al-imlaq also means: corruption. See what has passed in the report no. 6233, vol. 5:602, footnote 2.]] and without extravagance or corruption.

16871. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "The gharim is the one upon whom the debt (ghurm) falls."

16872. Ibn Wakf narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Uthman ibn al-Aswad, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿and the debtors﴾, he said: "He is the one whose wealth is carried off by flood and fire, and who borrows for his dependents."

16873. ...... He said: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far, who said: "The one who borrows without corruption."

16874. ...... He said: My father narrated to me, from Isra'il, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far, who said: "The debtors are those who borrow without corruption; the imam should pay their debts."

16875. Ibn Wakf narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Uthman ibn al-Aswad, from Mujahid: "They are a people whom debts overwhelmed without corruption or squandering, so Allah has assigned them a share in this verse."

* * *

As for His words ﴿and in the way of Allah﴾, it means: and in spending for the support of the religion of Allah, His path, and His law which He prescribed for His servants, by fighting His enemies; and that is the raid against the disbelievers. [[See the explanation of "the way of Allah" previously in the lexical indexes (sabl).]]

* * *

The interpreters said what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said this:

16876. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His words ﴿and in the way of Allah﴾: "The one who goes out to fight (al-ghazi) in the way of Allah."

16877. Ibn Wakf narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ata' ibn Yasar, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Charity is not lawful for the rich except for five: a man who works on it (as a collector), or a man who buys it with his own wealth, or one in the way of Allah, or the wayfarer (ibn al-sabil), or a man who had a neighbor who gave him charity and he gave it to him as a gift." [[The report: 16877. Abu Dawud narrated it in his Sunan (2:158, no. 1635) by way of Malik, from Zayd ibn Aslam, as a mawquf report (ending with a Companion). Then he narrated it under no. 1636, by way of Ma'mar, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet (ﷺ), as a marfu' report. Ibn Majah also narrated it in his Sunan (589, no. 1841), as a marfu' report, in similar wording.]]

16878. ...... He said: My father narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Charity is not lawful for the rich except for three: one in the way of Allah, or the wayfarer, or a man who had a neighbor who gave him charity and he gave it to him as a gift." [[The report: 16878. "Atiyyah" is Atiyyah ibn Sa'd ibn Janadah al-Awfi, weak; he has passed several times. This report was narrated by Abu Dawud in his Sunan (2:160, no. 1637), by way of Sufyan, from Imran al-Barqi, from Atiyyah, in similar wording. Abu Dawud then said: "Firas and Ibn Abi Layla also narrated it, from Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet (ﷺ), the same." It is a weak hadith because of the weakness of Atiyyah al-Awfi.]]

* * *

As for His words ﴿and the wayfarer (ibn al-sabil)﴾, it is the traveler who passes from one land to another.

* * *

"Al-sabil" means the road [[See the explanation of "al-sabil" previously in the lexical indexes (sbl), and the explanation of "ibn al-sabil" previously: 3:345; 4:295; 8:346-347.]], and the one who travels on it is called "ibn al-sabil" because of his constant attachment to it, as the poet said: [[I do not know who said it.]]

"I am the son of war, which raised me as a youth, until I grayed and my peers became old."

And so the Arabs do: they call whoever is constantly attached to a thing by its name, "its son." [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "yu'raf bi-abnihi" (is known by his son), which does not make sense; the correct reading is what I have written.]]

* * *

The interpreters said what is similar to what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said this:

16879. al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far, who said: "Ibn al-sabil is the one who passes from land to land."

16880. Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Mandal narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿and ibn al-sabil﴾: "The wayfarer has a right to zakat even if he is rich, if he has been cut off from his means."

16881. Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Ma'qil ibn Ubayd Allah narrated to us, saying: I asked al-Zuhri about "ibn al-sabil," and he said: "A wayfarer comes to me in need." I said: "What if he is rich?" He said: "Even if he is rich."

16882. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿and ibn al-sabil﴾: "The guest; a right in it has been assigned to him."

16883. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd [said]: "Ibn al-sabil is the traveler, whether rich or poor, when his provisions are lost, or taken, or something happens to them, or he has nothing with him; his right is binding."

16884. Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, that he said: "Concerning a rich man who travels and becomes needy during his journey, he said: He takes from the zakat."

16885. Ibn Wakf narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far, who said: "Ibn al-sabil is the one who passes from land to land."

* * *

As for His words ﴿an obligation from Allah﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 60], He, may His praise be exalted, says: It is a portion that Allah has apportioned for them, making it obligatory in the wealth of the wealthy for them [[See the explanation of "the obligation" previously: 9:212, footnote, and the reference there.]]; ﴿and Allah is Knowing﴾ of the welfare of His creatures in what He has ordained for them, and in other things, nothing is hidden from Him. So with knowledge from Him He ordained what He ordained of the alms and the welfare in them; ﴿Wise﴾ in His management of His creation, into whose management no defect enters. [[See the explanation of "Knowing" and "Wise" previously in the lexical indexes (ʿlm), (ḥkm).]]

The scholars differed over the manner of dividing the alms mentioned by Allah in this verse: whether a share is obligatory for each of the eight categories in it, or whether that is left to the owner of the wealth; and who undertakes its distribution, whether he has the right to give all of it to whichever of the eight categories he wishes.

The majority of the scholars said: The one who undertakes its distribution has the right to distribute it and place it in whichever of the eight categories he chooses. Allah mentioned the eight categories in the verse only to inform His creatures that the alms do not go out of these eight categories to anything else, not as an obligation to divide them among all eight categories He named.

Mention of those who said this:

16886. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Harun narrated to us, from al-Hajjaj ibn Artah, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Hudhayfah, concerning His words ﴿The alms are only for the poor and the needy and the workers thereon﴾: he said: "If you wish, place it in one category, or two, or three."

16887. Ibn Wakf narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-Hajjaj, from al-Minhal, from Zirr, from Hudhayfah, who said: "If you place it in one category, it suffices for you."

١٦٨٨٨-...... He said: Jarir narrated to us, from Layth, from ʿAṭāʾ, from ʿUmar: "Verily, the alms are only for the poor..." He said: Whichever category you give it to from among these, it suffices you.

١٦٨٨٩-...... He said: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, from ʿAṭāʾ: "Verily, the alms are only for the poor..." — the verse — He said: If you place it in one category from these categories, it suffices you. And if you look at a household of Muslims who are poor and modest, and you relieve them with it, that is more beloved to me.

١٦٨٩٠-...... He said: Jarir informed us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr: "Verily, the alms are only for the poor and the needy... and the wayfarer." Whichever category you give it to from these categories, it suffices you.

١٦٨٩١-...... He said: ʿImran ibn ʿUyayna narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, the like of it.

١٦٨٩٢-...... He said: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughira, from Ibrahim: "Verily, the alms are only for the poor and the needy and those who work for them..." He said: This is something I know: whichever category of these categories you give it to, it suffices for you.

١٦٨٩٣-...... He said: My father narrated to us, from Shuʿba, from al-Hakam, from Ibrahim: "Verily, the alms are only for the poor..." He said: In whichever of these categories you place it, it suffices you.

١٦٨٩٤-...... He said: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sa'ib, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, who said: If you place it in one category of those that God named, it suffices you.

١٦٨٩٥-...... He said: My father narrated to us, from Abu Jaʿfar al-Razi, from al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas, from Abu al-ʿAliya, who said: If you place it in one category of those that God named, it suffices you.

١٦٨٩٦-...... He said: Khalid ibn Hayyan Abu Yazid narrated to us, from Jaʿfar ibn Yurqan, from Maymun ibn Mihran: "Verily, the alms are only for the poor..." He said: If you make it for one category of these, it suffices for you. [[The report: 1689６ - "Khalid ibn Hayyan al-Raqqi", Abu Yazid al-Kindi al-Kharraz, trustworthy, with some discussion about him, listed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 2/1/133, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/326.]]

١٦٨٩٧-...... He said: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, from Masʿud, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr: "Verily, the alms are only for the poor and the needy..." — the verse — He said: He informs its recipients who they are.

١٦٨٩٨-...... He said: Hafs narrated to us, from Layth, from ʿAṭāʾ, from ʿUmar: that he used to take the obligatory portion of the alms and place it in one category.

* *

Some of the later scholars used to say: If the owner of the wealth undertakes its distribution himself, he must place it in six categories, because the mu'allafa qulubuhum (those whose hearts are to be reconciled), in his view, have ceased to exist, and the share of the workers (al-ʿamilin ʿalayha) is nullified by his distributing it himself. He claims that it does not suffice for him to give to fewer than three persons from each category. He used to say: If the imam undertakes its distribution, he must distribute it among seven categories; nothing other than that suffices in his view.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 61:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And among them are those who harm the Prophet and say, "He is an ear." Say, "An ear of good for you; he believes in Allah and has faith in the believers, and is a mercy to those of you who believe."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says: Among these hypocrites are a group who harm the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and disparage him [[See the explanation of "harm" (adha) above, 8:84–86, and p. 85, note 2, and the references there.]] = ﴿and say, "He is an ear"﴾, meaning one who listens, who hears whatever anyone says and accepts it and believes it.

* *

This comes from their saying "a man who is adhanah" (an ear), on the pattern of "fa'alah" [[Thus it appears in the printed edition and the manuscript: "a man who is adhanah, on the pattern of fa'alah." I have not been able to determine the vocalisation of this, and I have found nothing in the lexicons supporting it. What the lexicons say is that one says "rajul adhan" (with a dammah and a sukun) and "adhan" (with two dammahs). I do not know whether this is on the pattern "fa'alah" (with a dammah then a fathah): "hamazah" and "lumazah," or on some other pattern. I am very doubtful about the correctness of what is mentioned here, and I fear that something has dropped out from the copyist's text, or that the wording has been corrupted.]], when he is quick to listen and to accept, just as one says "huwa yaqan" and "yaqin" when he is certain of everything he is told. Its root is from "adhina lahu yadhan," meaning he listened to him. From this is the report from the Prophet ﷺ: "Allah has not listened to anything as He listens to a Prophet who chants the Qur'an beautifully" [[This hadith was cited without its chain. It is a sound hadith, narrated by Muslim in his Sahih (6:78, 79) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah.]], and from it is the verse of 'Adi ibn Zayd:

"O heart, be distracted with amusement ... indeed my concern is in listening and in song" [[Amali al-Sharif al-Murtada 1:33, and Lisan (adhana) and (dadan). "Al-dad" (with a fathah on the dal) and "al-dadan" mean amusement. "Al-sama'," means singing, and a female singer is called "al-musmi'ah."]]

It is mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning Nabtal ibn al-Harith. [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "concerning Rabi' ibn al-Harith," which is an utter error, beyond any doubt.]]

16899 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Allah mentioned their deceit [[In the printed edition: "Allah mentioned their faults," which is an error; the correct reading is that of the manuscript and Ibn Hisham's Sirah.]] = meaning the hypocrites = and their harm to the Prophet ﷺ, and said: ﴿And among them are those who harm the Prophet and say, "He is an ear,"﴾ the verse. The one who said that statement, as it has reached me, was Nabtal ibn al-Harith, a brother of the Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf, and this verse was revealed concerning him, for he said: "Muhammad is only an ear! Whoever tells him something, he believes it!" Allah says: ﴿Say, "An ear of good for you,"﴾ meaning: he hears good and believes it. [[The report 16899: Sirah of Ibn Hisham 4:195, and it follows the earlier report no. 16783. See also the report of Nabtal ibn al-Harith in Sirah of Ibn Hisham 2:168.]]

* *

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His saying: ﴿Say, "An ear of good for you."﴾

The majority of the readers of the major cities recited it: ﴿Qul udhunu khayrin lakum﴾, with "udhun" construed with "khayr," meaning: Say to them, O Muhammad: he is an ear of good, not an ear of evil.

* *

It is reported from al-Hasan al-Basri that he recited it: ﴿Qul udhunun khayrun lakum﴾, with tanwin on "udhun," and "khayr" as its predicate, meaning: Say: whoever among you, O hypocrites, hears what you say and believes you, if Muhammad is as you have described him, that when you come to him and deny what has been reported to him of your harm to him and your disparagement of him, he listens to you and believes you, is better for you than that he should call you liars and not accept what you say. Then Allah rejects them, saying: rather, he accepts only from the believers = ﴿He believes in Allah and has faith in the believers.﴾

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct recitation in my view is the reading of the one who recites: ﴿Qul udhunu khayrin lakum﴾, with "udhun" construed with "khayr" and "khayr" in the genitive, meaning: Say, he is an ear of good for you, not an ear of evil. [[See the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:444.]]

* *

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

16900 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to me, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿And among them are those who harm the Prophet and say, "He is an ear,"﴾ meaning he listens to everyone.

16901 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah concerning His saying: ﴿And among them are those who harm the Prophet and say, "He is an ear,"﴾ He said: They used to say: "Muhammad is only an ear; he does not relate anything about us except that he is an ear that hears what is said to him."

16902 - Ibn Wakī' related to us, saying: Ibn Numayr related to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿They say, "He is an ear,"﴾ we say whatever we wish, and swear, and he believes us.

16903 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to us, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid concerning His saying: ﴿"He is an ear,"﴾ He said: They would say: "We say whatever we wish, then we swear to him and he believes us."

16904 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿He believes in Allah﴾, He means: he affirms belief in Allah alone, with no partner.

And His saying: ﴿and has faith in the believers﴾, He means: and he believes the believers, not the disbelievers nor the hypocrites.

This is a rebuke from Allah to the hypocrites who said, "Muhammad is an ear!" Exalted is His praise, says: Muhammad ﷺ is only a listener to good, who believes in Allah and in what came to him from Him, and believes the believers, not the people of hypocrisy and disbelief in Allah.

* *

It has been said: ﴿and has faith in the believers﴾ means: and believes the believers, because the Arabs say, as has been related to us from them: "I believed him" and "I believed in him," meaning: I affirmed him, just as it is said: ﴿Some of what you are hastening for may have drawn near to you﴾ [Surah al-Naml: 72], meaning: it has drawn near to you; and as He says: ﴿For those who fear their Lord﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 154], meaning: for those who fear their Lord.

* *

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

16905 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah related to me, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿He believes in Allah and has faith in the believers﴾, meaning: he believes in Allah, and affirms the believers.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and a mercy for those of you who believe﴾, the readers differed in its recitation. The majority of the readers of the major cities recited it: ﴿wa rahmatun lilladhina amanu﴾, meaning: Say, he is an ear of good for you, and he is a mercy for those of you who believe, so "mercy" is in the nominative, conjoined with "ear."

* *

Some of the Kufans recited it: ﴿wa rahmatin﴾, conjoined with "good," with the interpretation: Say, an ear of good for you, and an ear of mercy. [[See the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:444.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two readings in my view is the reading of the one who recites ﴿wa rahmatun﴾ with the nominative, conjoined with "ear," meaning: and he is a mercy for those of you who believe. Allah made him a mercy for whoever follows him, is guided by his guidance, and affirms what came to him from his Lord, because Allah rescued them through him from misguidance, and bequeathed to them, by following him, His gardens.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And those who harm the Messenger of Allah, for them is a painful punishment﴾ (61)

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says: For these hypocrites who disparage the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and say, "He is an ear," and for their likes among his deniers, and those who say against him obscenity and falsehood, [[See the explanation of "harm" above, p. 324, note 1, and the references there.]] is a punishment from Allah, painful to them, in the Fire of Hell. [[See the explanation of "painful" (alim) above in the indexes of language, root (a-l-m).]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 62:

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿They swear to you by God, to please you, but God and His Messenger have more right that they should please Him, if they are believers﴾ (9:62)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The Exalted One says to the believers in Him and in His Messenger (ﷺ): "They swear to you by God, O believers, these hypocrites (munafiqun), to please you, regarding what has reached you concerning their harming the Messenger of God (ﷺ), their mentioning him with criticism and disparagement, and their secret collusion with the people of disbelief against you, with God and with false oaths, that they did not do that, that they are indeed upon your religion and with you against those who oppose you, seeking by that your pleasure." God, Exalted is His remembrance, says: ﴿But God and His Messenger have more right that they should please Him﴾, through repentance and turning back from what they said and uttered, ﴿if they are believers﴾, meaning: if they are truly convinced of the Oneness of God and affirm His promise and His threat.

* *

Ahl al-ta'wil (the exegetes) said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

16906. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿They swear to you by God, to please you﴾, the verse. It was mentioned to us that a man among the hypocrites said: "By God, these are our best and our nobles, and if what Muhammad says is true, they are worse than donkeys!" He said: A man among the Muslims heard it and said: "By God, what Muhammad says is true, and you are worse than the donkey!" The man reported it to the Prophet of God (ﷺ), so he sent for the man and summoned him, and said to him: "What moved you to what you said?" So he began to swear (yaltani') and swear by God that he had not said that. [["Al-ta'ana al-rajul" means: when a man is fair in supplicating against himself, or curses himself.]] He said: The Muslim man began to say: "O God, confirm the truthful and refute the liar!" So God revealed concerning that: ﴿They swear to you by God, to please you, but God and His Messenger have more right that they should please Him, if they are believers﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 63:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿Do they not know that whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger, for him is the Fire of Hell, abiding therein eternally? That is the great disgrace.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, says: Do these hypocrites, who swear by Allah falsely to the believers in order to please them while they remain upon hypocrisy, not know that whoever wages war against Allah and His Messenger, and opposes them, acting as an enemy to them through opposition to them, ﴿for him is the Fire of Hell﴾, in the Hereafter, ﴿abiding therein﴾, meaning: remaining therein, staying forever without end? [[See the explanation of "khulud" (abiding eternally) in the earlier lexical indices under (kh-l-d).]] ﴿That is the great disgrace﴾, meaning: his remaining in the Fire of Hell and his abiding therein is the great humiliation and degradation. [[See the explanation of "khizy" (disgrace) earlier, p. 160, note 1, and the references there.]]

* *

The reciters read ﴿fa-anna﴾ with the alif of "anna" pointed open (fath), meaning: Do they not know that for those who oppose Allah and His Messenger is the Fire of Hell? The verb "ya'lamu" governs it, as though they made the second "anna" a repetition of the first and relied upon it, since the predicate is with it and not with the first.

* *

Some of the grammarians of Basra preferred the kasra in this, as an inceptive (ibtida'), because of the entry of the "fa" (fa') into it, and because its entry with the fa', in his view, is evidence that it is the response of a conditional (jaza'), and when it is a response of a conditional, the preference with it is the inceptive.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The reading which I do not permit other than is the fath of the alif in both particles, I mean the first and the second "anna," because it is the reading of the metropolitan cities (amsar), and for the grammatical reason that I mentioned.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 64:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿The hypocrites are wary lest a surah should be sent down concerning them, informing them of what is in their hearts. Say, "Mock on! Indeed, Allah will bring forth what you fear."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: The hypocrites fear that something will be revealed concerning them [[See the explanation of "al-hadhar" (wariness, caution) above, 10:575.]] ﴿a surah informing them of what is in their hearts﴾, meaning, it will expose the believers to what is in their hearts. [[See the explanation of "al-naba'" (information, report) above, 13:252, footnote 2, and the references there.]]

* *

It has been said: Allah sent down this verse to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) because the hypocrites, whenever they disparaged the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and spoke of some of his affairs and the affairs of the Muslims, would say: "Perhaps Allah will not disclose our secret!" So Allah said to His Prophet (ﷺ): Say to them, ﴿Mock on!﴾, threatening them and warning them: ﴿Indeed, Allah will bring forth what you fear.﴾

* *

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said something similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said so:

16907. Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿The hypocrites are wary lest a surah should be sent down concerning them﴾, he said: They would speak their words among themselves, then say: "Perhaps Allah will not disclose our secret against us!"

16908. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it, except that he said: "This secret of ours."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah will bring forth what you fear﴾, He means: Indeed, Allah will make manifest against you, O hypocrites, what you were wary of revealing, so Allah made that manifest against them and exposed them. [[See the explanation of "al-ikhraj" (bringing forth) above, 2:228 and 12:211.]] Thus this surah was called ﴿al-Fadihah﴾ (the Exposer).

16909. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: This surah used to be called ﴿al-Fadihah﴾, the exposer of the hypocrites.

**The interpretation of His words: ﴿And if you were to ask them, they would surely say, "We were only chatting and playing." Say, "Was it Allah, His signs, and His Messenger that you were mocking?"﴾ (9:65)**

Abu Ja'far [al-Tabari] said: The Exalted, may His majesty be praised, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: "And if you were to ask these hypocrites, O Muhammad, about what they said of falsehood and lies, they would surely say to you: 'We only said that in play, and we were only engaged in idle talk and mockery!'" [[See the explanation of "al-khawd" (plunging into talk) above, 11: 529, note 3, and the references there.

= And the explanation of "al-la'ib" (play), above, 11: 529, note 4, and the references there.

= And the explanation of "al-istihza'" (mockery), above, 11: 262, note 3, and the references there.]] Allah says to Muhammad ﷺ: "Say, O Muhammad: 'Was it Allah, His signs, and His Book and His Messenger that you were mocking?'"

Ibn Ishaq used to say: The one who uttered this statement was, as has reached me: Wadi'ah ibn Thabit, brother of the Banu Umayya ibn Zayd, of the Banu Amr ibn Awf. [[The report 16910: Sirat Ibn Hisham 4: 195, and it is a continuation of the earlier report no. 16899.]]

* *

16911- Ali ibn Dawud narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: al-Layth narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn Sa'd narrated to me, from Zayd ibn Aslam, that a man from among the hypocrites said to Awf ibn Malik during the expedition of Tabuk: "What about these reciters of ours? They are the greediest of stomachs, the most lying of tongues, and the most cowardly when meeting the enemy!" Awf said to him: "You lie, but you are a hypocrite! I will certainly inform the Messenger of Allah ﷺ!" So Awf went to the Messenger of Allah to inform him, but he found that the Qur'an had preceded him. [Zayd said] Abdullah ibn Umar said: "I saw him clinging to the saddle-strap of the camel of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, as the stones were striking him, saying: 'We were only chatting and playing!'" And the Prophet ﷺ was saying to him: ﴿Was it Allah, His signs, and His Messenger that you were mocking?﴾ He added nothing to that. [[[Zayd] The text in the printed edition and the manuscript reads: "fa-qala Zayd" with the fa', and the context requires dropping it.

[[Report 16911: Hisham ibn Sa'd al-Madani, trustworthy but with something said about him, mentioned earlier under nos. 5490, 11704, 12821. Zayd ibn Aslam al-Adawi, the jurist, who narrated from Abdullah ibn Umar; many transmitters narrated from him. He has been mentioned many times, and the report that follows it comes via Ibn Wahb from him. This chain is sound.]]]]

16912- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Hisham ibn Sa'd narrated to me, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: A man said during the expedition of Tabuk, in an assembly: "We have never seen anything like these reciters of ours: the greediest of stomachs, the most lying of tongues, and the most cowardly when meeting the enemy!" A man in the assembly said: "You lie, but you are a hypocrite! I will certainly inform the Messenger of Allah ﷺ!" The news reached the Prophet ﷺ and the Qur'an was revealed. Abdullah ibn Umar said: "I saw him clinging to the saddle-strap of the camel of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, as the stones struck him, saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, we were only chatting and playing!'" And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was saying: ﴿Was it Allah, His signs, and His Messenger that you were mocking? Make no excuse; you have disbelieved after your belief.﴾ [[Report 16912: a repetition of the earlier report, and its chain is sound.]]

16913- Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Ayyub informed us, from Ikrimah, regarding His words: ﴿And if you were to ask them, they would surely say, "We were only chatting and playing,"﴾ up to His words: ﴿because they were criminals﴾, he said: "There was a man, among those whom Allah, if He wills, pardons, who used to say: 'O Allah, I hear a verse that concerns me; the skins shiver because of it, and the hearts pound because of it. O Allah, make my death a killing in Your way, so that no one will say: "I washed him, I shrouded him, I buried him."'" He said: So he was martyred on the day of Yamama, and no one among the Muslims was found except that he was found [unwashed, with] him.

16914- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿And if you were to ask them, they would surely say, "We were only chatting and playing,"﴾ the verse, he said: While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was marching on his expedition to Tabuk, some hypocrites were walking in front of him and said: "This man hopes to conquer the palaces of Syria and its fortresses! Far-fetched, far-fetched!" Allah informed His Prophet ﷺ of that, and the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: "Hold the riders back for me!" So he came to them and said: "You said such and such, you said such and such." They said: "O Prophet of Allah, we were only chatting and playing." So Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed concerning them what you hear.

16915- Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿And if you were to ask them, they would surely say, "We were only chatting and playing,"﴾ he said: While the Prophet ﷺ was on the expedition to Tabuk, a group of hypocrites were walking ahead of him, and they said: "This one thinks he will conquer the palaces and fortresses of Rome!" Allah informed His Prophet ﷺ of what they said, and he said: "Bring these people to me!" He called them and said: "You said such and such!" They swore: "We were only chatting and playing!"

16916- al-Harith narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, saying: Abu Ma'shar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b and others, who said: A man from among the hypocrites said: "I do not see these reciters of ours except as the greediest of stomachs, the most lying of tongues, and the most cowardly when meeting the enemy!" This was reported to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ after he had set off and mounted his camel. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, we were only chatting and playing!" He said: ﴿Was it Allah, His signs, and His Messenger that you were mocking?﴾ up to His words: ﴿criminals﴾. Indeed his legs were throwing up stones, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not turn toward him, while he was clinging to the strap of the Messenger of Allah's camel. [[The printed edition reads "layasfa'an bil-hijara" (they strike with stones), which is wrong in its verb; the manuscript's reading is correct, and the correct form is "nasafat" as above. "Nasafat al-naqah al-hijara wal-turab" means she flung up stones and dust in her running; the same is said of a person when his running is intense.]] [["Al-nis'ah" (with a kasra and a sukun): a braided leather strap used as a rein for a camel; it may also be a wide woven band placed on the camel's chest. The bit and the saddle-girth are also called "al-nis'atan."]]

16918- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similar to it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 66:

The exposition (qawl fi ta'wil) of His words: ﴿Make no excuses; you have disbelieved after your belief. If We pardon a group among you, We will punish another group because they were criminals.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: May His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say to those whose description I have given you: ﴿Make no excuses﴾, falsely, by saying: ﴿We were only conversing and playing﴾. ﴿You have disbelieved﴾, meaning: you have denied the truth by your statements about the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and the believers in him [[In the manuscript: "yaqulu: lahamma al-haqq" ("he says: the flesh of the truth"), which cannot be read. What is in the printed edition is close to the correct reading, so I have left it as it is.]] ﴿after your belief﴾, meaning: after your affirmation of him and your acknowledgment of him. ﴿If We pardon a group among you, We will punish a group﴾. [[See the explanation of "al-'afw" (pardon) in the earlier lexical indexes under (ʿafā).]]

* *

It is reported that by "a group" (ta'ifa), in this place, is meant one man.

Ibn Ishaq used to say concerning this:

16919 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salama related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: The one who was pardoned, as it has reached me, was Makhshi ibn Humayyir al-Ashja'i, an ally of Banu Salama, and that is because he denied some of what he heard from them. [[Report 16919: Sirat Ibn Hisham 4:195, which continues the earlier report numbered 16910.]]

16920 - Ibn Wakī' related to us, saying: Zayd ibn Habban related to us, from Musa ibn 'Ubayda, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b: ﴿If We pardon a group among you﴾, he said: "a group" is one man.

* *

The people of ta'wil (interpretation) differed regarding the interpretation of this.

Some of them said: its meaning is: ﴿If We pardon a group among you﴾, because of his denial of what was denied to you before, that is, of disbelief, ﴿We will punish a group﴾, because of their disbelief and their mockery of the signs of God and His Messenger.

Those who said this:

16922 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, who said: Some of them said: There was a man among them who did not join them in their talk, but would walk apart from them. So this was revealed: ﴿If We pardon a group among you, We will punish a group﴾, and he was called "a group" although he was one person.

* *

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: If a group among you repents, God will pardon it, and God will punish a group among you for abandoning repentance.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Indeed they were criminals﴾, its meaning is: We will punish a group of them for their earning of guilt (jurm), which is disbelief in God and their defaming of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). [[See the explanation of "al-ijram" (committing crime) in the earlier section, 13:408, note 2, and the references there.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 67:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿The hypocrite men and hypocrite women are of one another. They enjoin what is unjust and forbid what is just, and they withhold their hands. They have forgotten Allah, so He has forgotten them. Indeed, the hypocrites are the defiantly disobedient.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: ﴿The hypocrite men and the hypocrite women﴾, who show belief to the believers with their tongues while concealing disbelief in Allah and His Messenger [[See the explanation of "hypocrisy" (nifaq) earlier: 1:234, 270, 273, 324–327, 346–363, 408, 409, 414; 4:232, 233; 8:513; 9:7.]] = ﴿they are of one another﴾, meaning: they are one category, and their affair is one, in their declaring belief and their inwardly harboring disbelief = ﴿they enjoin what is unjust﴾, meaning whoever accepts from them, = ﴿what is unjust﴾, which is disbelief in Allah and in Muhammad ﷺ, and in what he brought, and denying him [[See the explanation of "what is unjust" (al-munkar) earlier: 13:165, note 2, and the references there.]] = ﴿and they forbid what is just﴾, meaning: they forbid them from believing in Allah and His Messenger, and in what has come to them from Allah [[See the explanation of "what is just" (al-ma'ruf) earlier: 13:165, note 1, and the references there.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and they withhold their hands﴾, meaning: they hold back their hands from spending in the way of Allah, and restrain them from giving charity, so they withhold from those to whom Allah has made obligatory rights in their wealth, as prescribed in zakat, their due rights, as related:

16923 – Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿and they withhold their hands﴾, he said: They do not extend them with spending in what is right.

16924 – Al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, he said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

16925 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Ishaq narrated to us, he said: Abd Allah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

16926 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similar to it.

16927 – Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿and they withhold their hands﴾, they do not extend them with good.

16928 – Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿and they withhold their hands﴾, he said: They withhold their hands from every good.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿They have forgotten Allah, so He has forgotten them﴾, its meaning is: they abandoned Allah, not obeying Him or following His command, so He abandoned them from His success, guidance and mercy.

* *

We have already shown earlier, with its evidences, that the meaning of "forgetting" (nisyan) is abandonment, and that suffices so it need not be repeated here. [[See the explanation of "forgetting" (nisyan) earlier: 12:475, note 2, and the references there.]]

* *

Qatada used to say about this:

16929 – Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿They have forgotten Allah, so He has forgotten them﴾, they were forgotten from good, and they did not forget from evil.

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites are the defiantly disobedient﴾, means: indeed, those who deceive the believers by showing them with their tongues belief in Allah, while inwardly harboring disbelief, are those who depart from obedience to Allah, leaving the faith in Him and His Messenger. [[See the explanation of "defiant disobedience" (fisq) earlier: p. 293, note 2, and the references there.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 68:

The discussion on the interpretation of His words: ﴿Allah has promised the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women and the disbelievers the fire of Hell, abiding therein. It is sufficient for them. Allah has cursed them, and theirs is a lasting punishment.﴾ (9:68)

Abu Ja'far said: He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: ﴿Allah has promised the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women and the disbelievers﴾ with Allah, ﴿the fire of Hell﴾, that He will make them burn in it all together. ﴿Abiding therein﴾ means remaining in it forever, neither living nor dying therein. [[See the explanation of "al-khulud" (abiding) in the earlier linguistic indexes under the root (kh-l-d).]] ﴿It is sufficient for them﴾ means it is enough for them as punishment and recompense for their disbelief in Allah. [[See the explanation of "hasb" (sufficiency) earlier, p. 403, footnote 1, and the references there.]] ﴿Allah has cursed them﴾ means Allah has removed them far away and banished them from His mercy. ﴿And theirs is a lasting punishment﴾ means: and for both groups together, that is, the people of hypocrisy and disbelief, with Allah, ﴿a lasting punishment﴾, constant, which will not cease or perish. [[See the explanation of "muqim" (lasting) earlier, vol. 10: pp. 293–294, and vol. 14: p. 172.]]

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 69:

The explanation of His words: ﴿Like those before you, who were stronger than you in might and greater in wealth and children, and they enjoyed their portion, so you enjoy your portion as those before you enjoyed their portion, and you indulged in vain talk as they indulged. Those are the ones whose deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter, and those are the losers.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Say, O Muhammad, to these hypocrites who said: ﴿We were only conversing and playing﴾: Was it at Allah and His verses and His Messenger that you were mocking? ﴿Like those before you﴾, from the nations who did what you did, so Allah destroyed them, and hastened for them disgrace in this world, along with what He prepared for them of punishment and torment in the Hereafter. He, may His praise be exalted, says to them: Beware lest there descend upon you a punishment from Allah like what descended upon them, for they were stronger than you in might and force, and greater than you in wealth and children. ﴿And they enjoyed their portion﴾, he says: they took their enjoyment of their share and portion of their worldly life and their religion, [[See the explanation of "al-istimta'" (enjoyment) earlier, 12:116, note 1, and the references there.]] and they were content with that share of the world in exchange for their share of the Hereafter, [[See the explanation of "al-khalaq" (portion) earlier, 2:452-454 \ 4:201-203 \ 6:527, 528.]] and you, O hypocrites, have followed their path in enjoying your portion. He says: you acted with your religion and your world, as those nations before you enjoyed, whom I destroyed for their opposition to My command. ﴿As those before you enjoyed their portion﴾, he says: as those before you did with their share of their worldly life and their religion. ﴿And you indulged﴾, in falsehood and vanity against Allah. ﴿As they indulged﴾, he says: and you too, O hypocrites, indulged as those nations before you indulged. [[See the explanation of "al-khawd" (indulging) earlier, p. 332, note 2, and the references there.]]

* *

And in accordance with what we have said on this, the people of interpretation have said.

Those who said that:

16930 - My father al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Abu Ma'shar narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: You will surely follow the ways of those nations before you, span by span, and cubit by cubit, and fathom by fathom, until if one of them had entered a lizard's burrow you would enter it too! Abu Hurayrah said: Recite if you wish the Qur'an: ﴿Like those before you, who were stronger than you in might and greater in wealth and children, and they enjoyed their portion, so you enjoy your portion as those before you enjoyed their portion, and you indulged as they indulged﴾. They said: O Messenger of Allah, as Persia and Byzantium did? He said: And who are the people other than they? [[Report 16930: its isnad is weak.

"Abu Ma'shar" is Najih ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Sindi, munkar al-hadith, previously mentioned under number 1275.

However, this report has a basis in the Sahih, for al-Bukhari related it in his Sahih by way of Ahmad ibn Yunus, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah (al-Fath 13:254), with other than this wording.

It is said: "akhadha akhdha fulan," meaning he followed his conduct.]]

16931 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Amr ibn Ata, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿Like those before you﴾, the verse. He said: Ibn Abbas said: How similar tonight is to yesterday! ﴿Like those before you﴾: these are the Children of Israel; we are likened to them. I do not know except that he said: By Him in whose hand is my soul, you will surely follow them, until if one of them entered a lizard's burrow you would enter it. [[Report 16931: "Amr ibn Ata," the narrator from Ikrimah here, is "Amr ibn Ata ibn Waraz," who is weak, not worth anything. Ahmad said: "Ibn Jurayj narrated from Amr ibn Ata, from Ikrimah, he is Ibn Waraz; and everything Ibn Jurayj narrated from Amr ibn Ata from Ibn Abbas is from Ibn Abi al-Khuwar," and they are two men. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, Ibn Abi Hatim 13\126, and Mizan al-I'tidal 2:265.

So this isnad is also weak, but it has a basis in the Sahih, as mentioned before.]]

16932 - Ibn Jurayj said: And Ziyad ibn Sa'd informed us, from Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn Muhajir, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: By Him in whose hand is my soul, you will surely follow the ways of those before you, a span by span, and cubit by cubit, and fathom by fathom, until if they entered a lizard's burrow you would enter it! They said: And who are they, O Messenger of Allah? The People of the Book! He said: Then who? [[Report 16932: this isnad follows the previous isnad, but I have separated it from it, because the first isnad was completed with Ibn Jurayj's narration of the hadith of Ibn Abbas, then it moved to another isnad to Abu Hurayrah.

"Ziyad ibn Sa'd ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Khurasani," who was Ibn Jurayj's partner, and he is trustworthy; the group related from him. Biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 2\1\327, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1\2\533.

"Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn Muhajir ibn Qunfudh al-Taymi al-Qurashi," trustworthy, previously mentioned under number 10521.

So this report has a sound isnad.

As for his words "famah," it is written in the printed edition as "faman," but in the manuscript it is clearly with a ha' with a sukun on it. What confirms this correctness is Ibn Jurayj's limiting himself in the following report to mentioning "faman" without the report, which indicates that the first differs from the second, not that it matches it.

The use of "mah" in the sense of interrogation: the author of Lisan al-Arab mentioned as evidence for it, under the entry "ma," a verse,

but he erred in his transmission from Ibn Jinni afterward, so what he meant before was not made clear. He said: "ma: a particle of negation, and it can mean 'alladhi'... and it is used in place of 'min,' and it can mean interrogation, and the alif is replaced by a ha', so one says 'mah'. The rajiz said: 'Qad waradat min amkinah, wa min hahuna wa-min huneh, in lam urawwiha famah.' Ibn Jinni said: 'mah' here may have two meanings: one is that it is 'famah' as a rebuke from him, meaning: restrain yourself from me, for I am not fit for reproach; or: 'famah, O man,' addressing himself and rebuking it."

I say: this is an arbitrary judgment by Abu al-Fath ibn Jinni, for the context of the verse requires that its meaning be: if I do not water these camels, then who will water them? This is the plain meaning of the inference which the author of Lisan al-Arab cited, but he was poor in exposition and brief, and he was faulty in appending to the speech what he appended from Abu al-Fath's words.

This report narrated by Ibn Jurayj from Abu Hurayrah is another proof and strong evidence for their use of "mah" in the sense of interrogation.]]

16933 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj who said: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said that he said: "faman." [[Report 16933: the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri with the meaning of the previous reports was related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (al-Fath 13:255), and Muslim in his Sahih 16:219, by way of Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ata ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.

This report was narrated by Ibn Jurayj abbreviated to a single word, "faman," to clarify that the meaning of Abu Hurayrah's earlier narration "famah" is "faman," as an interrogation, as mentioned in the note before it.]]

16934 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan regarding: ﴿So they enjoyed their portion﴾, he said: their religion.

16935 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "He warned you against introducing innovations in Islam, and He knew that groups from this community would do that." [[This appears thus in the manuscript: "hadathakum an tahthu fi al-Islam hadathan, wa qad 'alimtum annahu ..." which is illegible and not sound, and what is in the printed edition seems to be quoted from al-Durr al-Manthur 3:255, where it is attributed to Abu al-Shaykh and not to Ibn Jarir, and it is moreover abridged in al-Durr al-Manthur.]] Then Allah said concerning that: ﴿So they enjoyed their portion, so you enjoy your portion as those before you enjoyed their portion, and you indulged as they indulged﴾, and they only supposed that there would not befall them the trial that befell the Children of Israel before them, and that the trial returns just as it began.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Those are the ones whose deeds have become worthless﴾, its meaning is: these are the ones who said: ﴿We were only conversing and playing﴾, and they did in that matter the deed of those destroyed nations before them, (whose deeds have become worthless), he says: their deeds went to waste in vanity. So there is no reward for them except the Fire, because they were in what displeases and angers Allah. [[See the explanation of "habt" earlier, p. 166, note 1, and the references there.]] ﴿And those are the losers﴾, he says: and those are the ones who were cheated in their bargain, by exchanging the bliss of the Hereafter for their portion of the lowly, scant worldly life. [[See the explanation of "al-khusran" (loss) earlier, 13:535, note 1, and the references there.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 70:

Concerning the interpretation of His words: ﴿Has there not come to them the news of those before them: the people of Noah, ʿAd, Thamud, the people of Abraham, the companions of Madyan, and the overturned cities? Their messengers came to them with clear proofs. It was not Allah who wronged them, but they used to wrong themselves.﴾ (9:70)

Abu Jaʿfar said: The Exalted says: Has there not come to these hypocrites, who conceal disbelief in Allah and forbid faith in Him and His Messenger, ﴿the news of those before them﴾, meaning the report of the nations that were before them [[See the explanation of "al-naba'" (news) above, p. 331, note 2, and the references there.]], when they disobeyed Our messengers and opposed Our command, and what punishment from Us befell them?

Then the Exalted explained which nations He meant when He said "Has there not come to them their news," so He said: ﴿the people of Noah﴾. The word "qawm" is in the genitive because it is a substitute (badal) for "alladhina," and "alladhina" is in the genitive position.

* *

The meaning of the speech is: Has there not come to these hypocrites the news of the people of Noah and what We did to them, when they denied Our messenger Noah and opposed My command? Did I not drown them by the flood?

= ﴿And ʿAd﴾, meaning: and the news of ʿAd, when they disobeyed My messenger Hud. Did I not destroy them with a furious screaming wind? = And the news of Thamud, when they disobeyed My messenger Salih. Did I not destroy them with the quake, so that they lay in their homes, prostrate? = And the news of the people of Abraham, when they disobeyed him and rejected what he brought them of the truth from Allah. Did I not strip them of blessing and destroy their king Nimrod? = And the news of the companions of Madyan, the son of Abraham. Did I not destroy them with the punishment of the Day of the Canopy, when they denied My messenger Shuʿayb? = And the news of those whose land was overturned upon them, so that its upper part became its lower part, when they disobeyed My messenger Lot [[See the explanation of "al- infikak" (overturning) above, p. 208, note 1, and the references there.]] and denied what he brought them of the truth from Me? The Exalted says: Do these hypocrites, who mock Allah, His signs and His Messenger, feel secure that they will be treated in the same way in retribution against them and the swift humiliation and punishment for them in this world, the path of their predecessors among the nations, and that there will befall them, for their denial of My messenger Muhammad ﷺ, what befell those who denied Our messengers when clear proofs came to them?

* *

Ahl al-ta'wil have said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said so:

16936. Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and the overturned cities﴾, he said: the people of Lot, whose land was overturned upon them, so that its upper part became its lower part.

16937. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His words ﴿and the overturned cities﴾, he said: they are the people of Lot.

* *

If someone says: If by "the overturned cities" the people of Lot are meant, then how is it said "al-mu'tafikat" in the plural, rather than singular?

It is said: They were three towns, so it was made plural for that reason, and it was given the feminine plural ending, as in Allah's words: ﴿And the overturned cities He hurled down﴾ [Surah al-Najm 53:53]. [[See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an, 1:446.]]

If someone says: How is it said "their messengers came to them with clear proofs," when the one sent to them was singular?

It is said: The meaning is that to each town of the overturned cities came a messenger calling them to Allah, so the messengers of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ whom he sent to them to call them to Allah concerning his message are messengers to them, just as the Arabs said of a people who were attributed to Abu Fudayk the Kharijite: "al-Fudaykat," while "Abu Fudayk" is one person. But his companions, when they were attributed to him as their leader, were called by that name and attributed to their leader. Likewise His words: ﴿their messengers came to them with clear proofs﴾.

* *

It may also be said that the meaning is: the messengers from Allah came with clear proofs to the people of Noah, ʿAd, Thamud, and the other nations mentioned by Allah in this verse.

* *

As for His words ﴿It was not Allah who wronged them﴾, the Exalted says: Allah did not destroy these nations He mentioned except for their crimes and their wronging of themselves, and their deserving of great punishment from Allah, not as an injustice from Allah toward them, nor as Him placing punishment on one who is not deserving of it, for Allah is Wise, with no flaw in His management and no error in His decree. Rather, the people He destroyed wronged themselves by disobeying Allah and denying His messengers, until they incurred the wrath of their Lord, so the word of punishment was justified against them and they were punished.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 71:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And the believing men and believing women are allies of one another. They enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and they establish prayer and give zakah and obey Allah and His Messenger. Those - Allah will have mercy on them. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His mention, says: As for "the believing men and believing women," meaning those who affirm Allah and His Messenger and the signs of His Book, their description is that some of them are helpers and supporters of others [[See the explanation of "al-awliya'" (allies) in the linguistic indices of what has preceded, under (wly).]] = ﴿They enjoin what is right﴾, meaning: they command people to have faith in Allah and His Messenger, and in what has come to them from Allah, [[See the explanation of "al-ma'ruf" (what is right) above, p. 338, footnote 2, and the references there.]] = [﴿and forbid what is wrong﴾ ... ] [[What is between the brackets I added as a supplement, and it is the completion of the verse; the copyist omitted it and dropped its explanation, as is clear from Abu Ja'far's context in his commentary.

See the explanation of "al-munkar" (what is wrong) above, p. 338, footnote 1, and the references there.]] = ﴿and establish prayer﴾, meaning: they perform the obligatory prayer [[See the explanation of "iqamat al-salah" (establishing prayer) in the linguistic indices of what has preceded, under (qwm).]] = ﴿and give zakah﴾, meaning: they give the obligatory zakah to its people [[See the explanation of "iita' al-zakah" (giving zakah) in the linguistic indices of what has preceded, under (ata).]] = ﴿and obey Allah and His Messenger﴾, so they comply with the command of Allah and His Messenger and refrain from what they have forbidden them = ﴿Those - Allah will have mercy on them﴾, meaning: these, whose description is this, are those whom Allah will have mercy on, rescuing them from His punishment and admitting them to His Garden, not the people of hypocrisy and of denying Allah and His Messenger, who forbid what is right, command what is wrong, and withhold their hands from paying the right of Allah from their wealth = ﴿Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might﴾, meaning: Allah is mighty in His retribution against those whom He punishes among His creation for disobeying Him and disbelieving in Him, and nothing prevents Him from punishing them, and no helper can save them from Him = ﴿and Wise﴾, in His retribution against them and in all His actions. [[See the explanation of "'Aziz" and "Hakim" in the linguistic indices of what has preceded, under (‘zz) and (hkm).]]

* *

And according to what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation have said.

Mention of those who said so:

16938. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, who said: Everything that Allah mentioned in the Qur'an of "enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong," then "enjoining what is right" is calling from polytheism to Islam, and "forbidding what is wrong" is forbidding the worship of idols and devils.

16939. ...... He said: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿establish prayer﴾, he said: The five prayers.

The commentary of Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) on the verse: "God has promised the believing men and believing women gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein, and goodly dwellings in Gardens of Eden. And God's good pleasure is greater. That is the supreme triumph" (9:72).

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: God has promised those who affirmed God and His Messenger, and acknowledged Him and what came to them from God, among men and women, [gardens beneath which rivers flow], meaning: gardens whose trees have rivers flowing beneath them [[See the explanation of "jannah" (garden) in the earlier linguistic indexes, root (j-n-n).]] [abiding therein], meaning: remaining in them forever, dwelling, whose bliss does not leave them nor perish [[See the explanation of "khulud" (eternal abiding) in the earlier linguistic indexes, root (kh-l-d).]] [and goodly dwellings], meaning: dwellings they inhabit that are good. [[See the explanation of "tayyibah" (good) in the earlier linguistic indexes, root (t-y-b).]]

As for its goodness, it is reported to us, as follows:

16940. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Jisr, from al-Hasan, who said: I asked Imran ibn Husayn and Abu Hurayrah about a verse in the Book of God, blessed and exalted: "and goodly dwellings in Gardens of Eden." They said: "You have fallen upon one who knows!" We asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and he said: "It is a palace in Paradise, of pearl, in which are seventy houses of red ruby, in each house seventy chambers of green emerald, and in each chamber seventy couches."

[[Report 16940: Ishaq ibn Sulayman al-Razi, the teacher of Abu Kurayb, is trustworthy; the group (of compilers) narrated from him; he has passed several times, the last of which is number 13224.
"Jisr" is Jisr ibn Farqad, Abu Ja'far al-Qassab. Ishaq ibn Sulayman narrated from him, and he narrated from al-Hasan and others. He was a righteous man, but in hadith he is "not anything." He is biographed in al-Kabir (1/2/245), where he says: "not that one," and in Ibn Abi Hatim (1/1/538), Mizan al-I'tidal (1:184), and Lisan al-Mizan (2:104).
In the printed edition it read: "Ishaq ibn Sulayman, from al-Hasan who said: I asked," and the name "Jisr" was dropped, because in the manuscript it had been written: "from al-Hasan, from al-Hasan," and then the copyist struck through the "alif lam" of the first "al-Hasan," thinking he had struck out the whole word. The correct reading is what I have recorded, and it will appear in the following chain.
This report was mentioned by al-Haythami in Majma' al-Zawa'id (7:30–31), where he said: "It was narrated by al-Bazzar and al-Tabarani in al-Awsat. In it is Jisr ibn Farqad, who is weak, though Sa'id ibn 'Amir declared him trustworthy, and the rest of al-Tabarani's narrators are trustworthy."
He then cited it again in Majma' al-Zawa'id (10:420), saying: "It was narrated by al-Tabarani, and in it is Jisr ibn Farqad, who is weak," abridging what preceded.
This chain is weak, as he said, for al-Bukhari and other imams declared Jisr ibn Farqad weak.]]

16941. Ibrahim ibn Sa'id al-Jawhari narrated to us, saying: Qurrah ibn Habib narrated to us, from Jisr ibn Farqad, from al-Hasan, from Imran ibn Husayn and Abu Hurayrah, who both said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was asked about this verse: "and goodly dwellings in Gardens of Eden." He said: "A palace of a single pearl; in that palace are seventy houses of red ruby, in each house seventy chambers of green chrysolite, in each chamber seventy couches, on each couch a bed of every colour, on each bed a wife of the wide-eyed houris, in each chamber seventy tables, on each table seventy kinds of food, in each chamber seventy maidservants, and the believer is given such strength in a single morning that he can accomplish all of that entirely."

[[Report 16941: Qurrah ibn Habib ibn Yazid ibn Shahrazad al-Qanawi al-Rammah is trustworthy. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir (41/183), and Ibn Abi Hatim (3/2/132).
"Jisr ibn Farqad" has passed in the chain above and before it. In the printed edition and the manuscript it read "Hasan ibn Farqad," and the correct form is what I have recorded.
This chain is also weak.]]

* *

As for His saying: "in Gardens of Eden," it means: these goodly dwellings which He has described, [are] "in Gardens of Eden."

* *

The "fi" (in) is connected to "masakin" (dwellings).

* *

It has been said: they are called "Gardens of Eden" because they are gardens of eternity and permanence, from which no one departs.

* *

It has also been said: they are called "Gardens of Eden" because they are the abode of God which He has chosen for Himself and for whomever of His creation He wills. This derives from the Arabs' saying: "So-and-so took up residence (ʿadana) in such-and-such a land," when he stayed there and remained there permanently; and from it comes "al-ma'din" (the mine/source, a place of origin), and it is said: "He is in a true source (ma'din sidq)," meaning he is in a firm origin. Some transmitters recited the verse of al-A'sha:

"And if they seek hospitality from his forbearance, they are received by a man of weight who has taken up residence (qad 'adan)."

[[Its source: his Diwan, p. 17; the manuscript of his Diwan, poem no. 15; Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah (1:264); and Lisan (root "wazn"). It is from his first poem, with which he came to Qays ibn Ma'd Yakrib al-Kindi. The Diwan's version reads "ila hukmihi" (to his judgment), but it is in the manuscript and Majaz al-Qur'an as I have recorded it; the printed edition wrote "hukmihi."
He says before it: "But my Lord has sufficed for my exile, with the praise of God, and it has delivered me to a brother of trust, of high stature, of abundant gifts and generous favours, generous in his character, of the Banu Mu'awiyah, the most noble in custom. If they follow his command they will be guided, and if they ask for his wealth he will not withhold."
And "istada'a ilayhi" means: he sought refuge with him in time of need.]] And it is recited: "qad wazan" (weighed). [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "qad wazan," with a waw. The version in the Diwan is "qad razan" with a ra', and both are correct in meaning. The version al-Tabari cited is the one Lisan explained under "wazn."
It is said: "wazana al-shay'" (the thing weighed), meaning it was heavy; "wazana al-rajul wazanah," when a man was steadfast; and "rajul wazin al-ra'y," meaning of sound judgment. "Razin" with a ra' has the same meaning, as in "rajul razin," meaning dignified.]]

* *

Ibn 'Abbas and a group with him, as reported, interpreted it according to what we have said on this matter.

16942. Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Habib ibn al-Shahid narrated to me, saying: 'Attab ibn Bashir narrated to us, from Khusayf, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: "Gardens of Eden," he said: "the mine (ma'din) of a man," in which he is.

16943. Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn 'Askar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, saying: al-Layth ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Ziyadah ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from Fudalah ibn 'Ubayd, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "God opens the Reminder (al-Dhikr) in three hours that remain of the night. In the first of those hours He looks into the Book, which no one else looks into, and He erases what He wills and affirms. Then in the second hour He descends to the Garden of Eden, which is in His house that no eye has seen and no thought of a human heart has conceived. It is His dwelling, and no one of the sons of Adam dwells with Him except three: the prophets, the truthful ones, and the martyrs. Then He says: 'Blessed is the one who enters you.' And He mentioned the third hour."

[[Reports 16943 and 16944: Ziyadah ibn Muhammad al-Ansari is "munkar al-hadith" (one whose narrations are rejected). He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir (2/1/407), where he mentions the chain of this report; Ibn Abi Hatim (1/2/619); and Mizan al-I'tidal (1:361), where he narrates this hadith in full, including mention of the third hour, and then says: "These are rejected words, which none brought except Ziyadah."
Al-Haythami cited it in Majma' al-Zawa'id (10:412), saying: "It was narrated by al-Bazzar, and in it is Ziyadah ibn Muhammad, who is weak."
In the printed edition, in the first report, it read: "al-Kindi Sa'd, from Ziyadah ibn Muhammad," and the correct reading is "al-Layth ibn Sa'd." The editor failed to read the manuscript well, because its letters were joined together.]]

16944. Musa ibn Sahl narrated to me, saying: Adam narrated to us, saying: al-Layth ibn Sa'd narrated to us, saying: Ziyadah ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from Fudalah ibn 'Ubayd, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "'Adn is his dwelling" — meaning the dwelling of God — "which no eye has seen and no thought of a human heart has conceived, and no one of the sons of Adam dwells in it with Him except three: the prophets, the truthful ones, and the martyrs. God, blessed and exalted, says: 'Blessed is the one who enters you.'"

[[Report 16944: See the preceding note. "Adam" is Adam ibn Abi Iyas.]]

* *

Others said: the meaning of "Gardens of Eden" is gardens of grapevines and vines.

Those who said this:

16945.
