Ahmad ibn Abi Suraj al-Razi narrated to me, saying: Zakariyya ibn 'Adi narrated to us, saying: 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Amr narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Harith: that Ibn 'Abbas asked Ka'b about "Gardens of Eden," and he said: "They are the vines and grapevines, in Syriac."

[[Report 16945: Ahmad ibn Abi Suraj al-Razi is Ahmad ibn al-Sabbah al-Nahshali al-Razi, a teacher of Abu Ja'far. al-Bukhari, Abu Dawud, and al-Nasa'i narrated from him. He is trustworthy. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim (1/1/56).
Zakariyya ibn 'Adi ibn Zurayq al-Taymi is trustworthy; he has passed as number 15446.
'Ubaydullah ibn 'Amr al-Raqqi is trustworthy; the group narrated from him; he has passed several times, including number 7187.
Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah al-Jazari is trustworthy; he has passed several times, the last as number 13855.
Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad al-Qurashi, client of 'Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal, is trustworthy, but his hadith is considered weak. He has passed several times, the last as number 13308.
'Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal al-Hashimi, the group narrated from him; he has also passed, as number 13308.]]

* *

Others said: it is the name of the lowest part (buṭnan) of Paradise and its center.

Those who said this:

16946. Humayd ibn Mas'adah narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Sulayman al-A'mash, from 'Abdullah ibn Murrah, from Masruq, from 'Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud), who said: "'Adn" is the buṭnan of Paradise.

16947. Muhammad ibn Bashshar and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, both saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Sufyan and Shu'bah, from al-A'mash, from 'Abdullah ibn Murrah, from Masruq, from 'Abdullah, concerning His saying: "Gardens of Eden." He said: "the buṭnan of Paradise." Ibn Bashshar said in his report: "I said: what is its buṭnan?" And Ibn al-Muthanna said in his report: "I said to al-A'mash: what is the buṭnan of Paradise?" He said: "Its center."

16948. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from 'Abdullah ibn Murrah and Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from 'Abdullah: "Gardens of Eden," he said: "the buṭnan of Paradise."

16949. ...... narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from 'Abdullah, similarly.

16950. Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Sulayman, from 'Abdullah ibn Murrah, from Masruq, from 'Abdullah, similarly.

16951. Ahmad ibn Abi Suraj narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha and 'Abdullah ibn Murrah, from both of them together or from one of them, from Masruq, from 'Abdullah: "Gardens of Eden," he said: "the buṭnan of Paradise."

16952. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, concerning God's saying: "Gardens of Eden," he said: "the buṭnan of Paradise."

* *

Others said: "'Adn" is the name of a palace.

Those who said this:

16953. 'Ali ibn Sa'id al-Kindi narrated to me, saying: 'Abdah Abu Ghassan narrated to us, from 'Awn ibn Musa al-Kinani, from al-Hasan, who said: "Gardens of Eden," and what will make you know what the Gardens of Eden are? A palace of gold, which none enters except a prophet, or a truthful one, or a martyr, or a just judge. And al-Hasan raised his voice with it.

[[Report 16953: "'Abdah, Abu Ghassan": I do not know who he is.
"'Awn ibn Musa al-Kinafi al-Laythi, Abu Rawh, is trustworthy and heard from al-Hasan. He is biographed in al-Kabir (4/1/17) and Ibn Abi Hatim (3/1/386).]]

16954. Ahmad ibn Abi Suraj narrated to us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Awn ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan say: "Gardens of Eden, and what will make you know what the Gardens of Eden are? A palace of gold, which none enters except a prophet, or a truthful one, or a martyr, or a just judge." Al-Hasan raised his voice with it.

[[Report 16954: Ahmad ibn Abi Suraj has passed as number 16945.
"'Abdullah ibn 'Asim al-Hammani" is truthful; Abu Hatim and Abu Zur'ah narrated from him. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim (2/2/134).
"'Awn ibn Musa al-Kinani" has passed before.]]

16955. Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah informed us, from Ya'la ibn 'Ata', from Nafi' ibn 'Asim, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who said: "In Paradise there is a palace called 'Adn,' around which are the towers and the rooftops. It has fifty thousand gates, and at each gate is a hibarah [["al-hibarah" (with a kasra on the ha' and a fatha on the ba'): a kind of striped Yemeni cloth. They said: "'hibarah' is not a fixed place or a known thing; it is only a kind of cloth." It seems this is what is meant in such a report, that is, embroidered curtains.]]. None enters it except a prophet or a truthful one."

16956. al-Hasan ibn Nasih narrated to us, saying: Abu Dawud narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Ya'la ibn 'Ata', who said: I heard Ya'qub ibn 'Asim narrate, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr: "In Paradise there is a palace called 'Adn,' which has five thousand gates, and at each gate five thousand hibarahs. None enters it except a prophet, or a truthful one, or a martyr."

[[Report 16956: "al-Hasan ibn Nasih" is "al-Hasan ibn Nasih al-Basri al-Sarraj." Ibn Abi Hatim said: "He narrated from 'Uthman ibn 'Uthman al-Ghatafani, Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman, Mu'adh ibn Mu'adh, and Yahya ibn Rashid; my father heard from him in the second stage." (al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil 1/2/39; Tarikh Baghdad 7:435).
There is also "al-Hasan ibn Nasih al-Khallal al-Makhrami," who narrated from Ishaq ibn Mansur and others. Ibn Abi Hatim said: "I met him, but I did not write from him, and he was truthful." It seems this is the teacher of al-Tabari. He is biographed in Ibn Abi Hatim (1/2/39) and Tarikh Baghdad (7:435).
In the printed edition it read "al-Hasan ibn Najih," which differs from the manuscript.
"Ya'qub ibn 'Asim ibn 'Urwah ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi": Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy; he is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir (4/2/388), and Ibn Abi Hatim (4/2/211).]]

* *

Others said: it is the city of Paradise.

Those who said this:

16957. It was reported to me from 'Abd al-Rahman al-Muharibi, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, concerning "Gardens of Eden," he said: "It is the city of Paradise, in which are the messengers, the prophets, the martyrs, and the leaders of guidance, and the people are around them, and the gardens are around it."

* *

Others said: it is the name of a river.

Those who said this:

16958. It was reported to me from al-Muharibi, from Wasil ibn al-Sa'ib al-Raqqashi, from 'Ata', who said: "'Adn" is a river in Paradise, its gardens are on its two banks.

* *

As for His saying: "and God's good pleasure is greater," its meaning is: God's pleasure with them is greater than all of that, [[See the explanation of "ridwan" (good pleasure) in the earlier pages, p. 174, note 2, and the references there.]] and the report from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) came accordingly.

16959. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Malik ibn Anas, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "God says to the people of Paradise: 'O people of Paradise!' They say: 'Here we are, our Lord, and at Your service!' He says: 'Are you pleased?' They say: 'Why should we not be pleased, when You have given us what You have not given anyone of Your creation?' He says: 'I will give you something better than that.' They say: 'O Lord, what is better than that?' He says: 'I will cause My good pleasure to descend upon you, so I shall never be displeased with you after it, forever.'"

[[Report 16959: This is a sound hadith, which al-Bukhari narrated with this same chain and in this wording in his Sahih (al-Fath 11:363–364). Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar fully discussed it in his commentary. Muslim narrated it in his Sahih (17:168). See what has preceded as number 6751 and 16567, from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, not raised to the Prophet, and what I added there. Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his tafsir at this place (4:202), saying: "al-Bazzar narrated it in his Musnad, from the hadith of al-Thawri." And al-Hafiz Diya' al-Din al-Maqdisi said in his book Sifat al-Jannah: "This, in my view, meets the conditions of the sound (hadith)."]]

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 72 (part 2 of 2):**

10. 169960: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub told me, from Hafs, from Shamir, who said: The Qur'an will come on the Day of Resurrection in the form of a pale man, to a man when he rises from his grave. It will say: "Rejoice in the honor of Allah! Rejoice in the pleasure of Allah!" He will say: "Who are you, who brings good news like this?" It will say: "I am the Qur'an, which kept you awake at night and made you thirsty by day." It will carry him on its neck until it brings him before his Lord. He will stand before Him and say: "O Lord, this is your servant. Reward him on my behalf with good, for he kept me awake at night and made him thirsty by day. I commanded him and he obeyed me, and I forbade him and he obeyed me." The Lord, blessed and exalted, will say: "For him is a robe of honor." It will say: "O Lord, increase it for him, for he deserves that." He will say: "For him is My pleasure." [Shamir] said: "And approval from Allah is greater" [Qur'an 9:72].

[Editor's note: For 169960, Ya'qub is "Ya'qub ibn Abd Allah al-Qummi," trustworthy, mentioned several times earlier, including at no. 13045.
Hafs is "Hafs ibn Humayd al-Qummi," trustworthy, mentioned earlier at no. 8518.
Shamir is "Shamir ibn Atiyya al-Asadi al-Kahili," trustworthy, mentioned earlier at no. 11545.
See also supporting reports for some wording of this narration in al-Haythami's Majma' al-Zawa'id 7: 159–165.
I did not find this report with a complete isnad in this exact wording.]

The statement that "the pleasure of Allah for the believing men and women is greater than everything mentioned" begins with the word "ridwan" (pleasure) in the nominative case, even though it is among what He has promised them. It is not grammatically conjoined (i'rab, grammatical analysis) with "the gardens" and "the pleasant dwellings," so as to show that Allah's pleasure with the believers is superior to all the other portions of His bounty and honor He has bestowed on them. This is like a speaker telling another: "I have given you and rewarded you with such-and-such, and honored you, but My approval of you afterward is better for you."

[Editor's note: In the printed edition, the sentence is arranged as: "better than that, these things which Allah promised the believing men and women…", which is not sound. What I have adopted is what appears in the manuscript. However, it is evident that some of Abu Ja'far's words have been lost by the copyist. I therefore judged that the context is the quotation of the verse, followed by an explanation of "that" as "these things…", so I have recorded it in that way and separated the two statements completely.
See also al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 446.]

* *

"That is the great triumph" [Qur'an 9:72]: these are the things promised to the believing men and women. "It is the great triumph": he says, it is the great victory and the great deliverance, because they gained the honor of eternity and were saved from humiliation in Saqar (Hell). [Editor's note: In the printed edition and the manuscript it reads "humiliation in the journey," which has no meaning; the correct reading is what I have adopted.] Therefore it is the great triumph, greater than which there is nothing.

[Editor's note: See the explanation of "al-fawz" (triumph) earlier, 11: 286, note 1, and the references there.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 73:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be harsh with them. Their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination.﴾ (9:73)

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, He says: ﴿O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers﴾ with the sword and weapons, ﴿and the hypocrites﴾.

* *

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the nature of the "jihad" (striving) which God commanded His Prophet to wage against the hypocrites. [[See the explanation of "jihad" above, p. 257, note 1, and the references there.

And the explanation of "munafiq" (hypocrite) above, p. 339, note 3, and the references there.]] Some of them said: He commanded him to strive against them with the hand and the tongue, and with everything he was able to strive against them with.

Those who said this:

16961. Ibn Wakī' related to us, saying: Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman and Yahya ibn Adam related to us, from Hasan ibn Salih, from 'Ali ibn al-Aqmar, from 'Amr ibn Jundub, from Ibn Mas'ud, regarding His saying: ﴿Strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾, he said: With his hand; if he is not able, then with his tongue; if he is not able, then with his heart; if he is not able, then let him scowl in their faces. [[The report 16961: Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Ru'asi is trustworthy (thiqah), related from by the group of compilers, and has passed several times.

And Yahya ibn Adam is trustworthy, related from by the group of compilers, and has passed several times.

And Hasan ibn Salih ibn Salih ibn Hayy al-Thawri is trustworthy, and has passed several times.

And 'Ali ibn al-Aqmar al-Wada'i al-Hamdani is trustworthy, related from by the group of compilers, and has passed several times.

And "'Amr ibn Abi Jundub" or "'Amr ibn Jundub" is Abu 'Atiyah al-Wada'i, whose name is disputed. He is recorded in al-Tahdhib, under the names and under the kunyas, and it says: "al-Bukhari said in his History: Abu Ishaq and 'Ali ibn al-Aqmar related from him," then it says: "The correct view is that although he is known as Abu 'Atiyah, he is other than al-Wada'i." He is trustworthy, one of the companions of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud. Ibn Abi Hatim recorded him in 3/1/224 under the name "'Amr ibn Jundub," and in the printed edition it was "'Amr ibn Jundub," but I have affirmed what is in the manuscript, and both are correct as you see.

This report was cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 3:248, and he attributed it to Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Abi al-Dunya in Kitab al-Amr bi'l-Ma'ruf, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman.

His saying "fa-liyakfahir fi wajhihi" means: let him meet them with a constricted, scowling face, without cheerfulness or openness.]]

* *

Others said: Rather, He commanded him to strive against them with the tongue.

Those who said this:

16962. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be harsh with them﴾: God commanded him to strive against the disbelievers with the sword, and against the hypocrites with the tongue, and He removed gentleness from them.

16963. Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to me, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿Strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾: "the disbelievers" with fighting, and "the hypocrites" by being harsh toward them in speech.

16964. It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His saying: ﴿Strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites and be harsh with them﴾: he says: Strive against the disbelievers with the sword, and be harsh toward the hypocrites with words, and that is striving against them.

* *

Others said: Rather, He commanded him to establish the prescribed punishments (hudud) upon them.

Those who said this:

16965. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan: ﴿Strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾, he said: Strive against the disbelievers with the sword, and against the hypocrites with the hudud; establish upon them the hudud of God.

16966. Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites and be harsh with them﴾, he said: God commanded His Prophet ﷺ to strive against the disbelievers with the sword, and to be harsh toward the hypocrites in the hudud.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the sayings concerning the interpretation of this, in my view, is what Ibn Mas'ud said: that God commanded His Prophet ﷺ to strive against the hypocrites in a manner similar to that in which He commanded him to strive against the polytheists.

If someone says: How then did he ﷺ leave them remaining among the midst of his companions, while knowing them? It is said: God, exalted is His remembrance, only commanded fighting against those among them who openly expressed a word of disbelief and then persisted in displaying what they had displayed. As for one who, when it was discovered that he had spoken a word of disbelief and was seized for it, denied it, retracted it, and said, "I am a Muslim," then God's ruling concerning everyone who displays Islam with his tongue is that thereby his blood and property are protected, even if he inwardly believes otherwise; and He, exalted is His praise, has taken charge of their inner secrets, and has not made it for the creation to investigate the secrets. Therefore the Prophet ﷺ, despite knowing them and God's informing him of their inner hearts and the convictions of their breasts, would leave them among the companions, and he did not pursue striving against them in the manner of striving against one who has openly declared war upon him for associating partners with God, because whoever of them was discovered to have said a word of disbelief in God and was seized for it would deny it and openly profess Islam with his tongue. So he ﷺ would not seize him except for what was openly displayed to him from his speech, at the moment of his presence before him and his resolve to carry out the judgment upon him, not for a word he had uttered previously, nor for the belief of his inner heart, which God did not permit anyone to act upon in judgment, and which He reserved to Himself alone to act upon, not His creation.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and be harsh with them﴾, [[See the explanation of "ghilzah" (harshness) above, 7:341.]] He, exalted is His remembrance, says: be severe toward them through striving, fighting, and intimidation. [[In the printed edition: "wal-i'ra'" with an ayn, which contradicts correct Arabic; in the manuscript it is said: "ra'abahu yar'abuhu ra'aban, fahuwa mar'ub wa ra'eeb, and 'ra'abahu' tarhibaan," and they stated: "Do not say: arba'ahu."]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and their refuge is Hell﴾, He says: their dwelling place is Hell, and it is their abode and refuge [[See the explanation of "ma'wa" (refuge) above, p. 77, note, and the references there.]] ﴿and wretched is the destination﴾, He says: and wretched is the place to which one returns, which is Hell. [[See the explanation of "masir" (destination) above, 13:441, note 4, and the references there.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 74:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿They swear by Allah that they said nothing, but they did indeed utter the word of disbelief, and they disbelieved after their submission (Islam), and they planned what they could not attain, and they sought revenge only because Allah and His Messenger had enriched them out of His bounty. So if they repent, it will be better for them; but if they turn away, Allah will punish them with a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have no protector or helper on earth﴾ (9:74).

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the person about whom this verse was revealed, and concerning the statement he had made, which Allah reported that he swore by Allah he had not said.

Some of them said: the one about whom this verse was revealed was al-Jullas ibn Suwayd ibn al-Samit.

* *

As for the statement he made, it was:

16967 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father: ﴿They swear by Allah that they said nothing, but they did indeed utter the word of disbelief﴾, he said: It was revealed concerning al-Jullas ibn Suwayd ibn al-Samit, who said: "If what Muhammad has brought is true, then we are worse than donkeys!" [[See the use of "asharr" in the two reports above, nos. 5080 and 11723. In the printed edition it reads "al-Himar", and I have kept what is in the manuscript.]] Then his stepson said to him: "By Allah, O enemy of Allah, I will inform the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of what you said, for if I do not do so, I fear a calamity will befall me and I will be held accountable for your sin!" So the Prophet ﷺ summoned al-Jullas and said: "O Jullas, did you say such and such?" He swore that he had not said it. So Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed: ﴿They swear by Allah that they said nothing, but they did indeed utter the word of disbelief, and they disbelieved after their submission, and they planned what they could not attain, and they sought revenge only because Allah and His Messenger had enriched them out of His bounty﴾.

16968 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah al-Darir narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, who said: This verse was revealed: ﴿They swear by Allah that they said nothing, but they did indeed utter the word of disbelief, and they disbelieved after their submission﴾, concerning al-Jullas ibn Suwayd ibn al-Samit. He and his stepson Mus'ab came from Quba'. Al-Jullas said: "If what Muhammad has brought is true, then we are worse than these donkeys of ours upon which we ride!" [[In the printed edition: "hamirina" in the singular; I have kept the manuscript.]] Mus'ab said: "By Allah, O enemy of Allah, I will certainly inform the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of what you have said!" I came to the Prophet ﷺ, and I feared that the Qur'an would be revealed concerning me, or that a calamity would befall me, or that I would be mixed up with his sin. I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I and al-Jullas came from Quba', and he said such and such. Had I not feared being mixed up with his sin, or that a calamity would befall me, I would not have informed you." He said: So he summoned al-Jullas and said to him: "O Jullas, did you say what Mus'ab said?" He swore, and Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed: ﴿They swear by Allah that they said nothing...﴾, the verse.

16969 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: The one who made that statement, as it has reached me, was al-Jullas ibn Suwayd ibn al-Samit, but it was reported against him by a man who was under his care, called "'Umayr ibn Sa'id" [[In the manuscript and printed edition: "Sa'id"; in the Sirah of Ibn Hisham it is "Sa'd". I have left what is in the manuscript, because I found al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar in al-Isabah mention this difference, so I fear this is the version of Abu Ja'far in Ibn Ishaq's Sirah.]], and he denied it and swore by Allah that he had not said it. When the Qur'an was revealed concerning him, he repented, desisted, and his repentance was good, as has reached me. [[Report 16969: Sirah of Ibn Hisham 4:196; it follows the earlier report no. 16919.]]

16970 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿the word of disbelief﴾: one of them said: "If what Muhammad says is true, then we are worse than donkeys!" A believing man said to him: "What he said is true, and you are worse than a donkey!" He said: The hypocrites then planned to kill him, and that is His saying: ﴿and they planned what they could not attain﴾.

16971 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

16972 - ...... narrated to us, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

16973 - Ayyub ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Raja' narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Simak, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting in the shade of a tree, and he said: "A man will come to you who looks at you with the eye of a devil; when he comes, do not speak to him." He had not stayed long when a blue-eyed man appeared [[When it is said "a blue-eyed man," they mean blueness of the eye. Al-Jahiz in al-Hayawan (5:330) counted "the blue-eyed among the Arabs," and the Arabs considered blue-eyed people ill-omened and base. See also Tabaqat Fuhul al-Shu'ara' (111), in the words of Mirdas concerning the killer of 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him.]], and the Prophet ﷺ summoned him and said: "Why do you and your companions revile me?" The man went and brought his companions, and they swore by Allah that they had not said or done it, until he pardoned them. So Allah revealed: ﴿They swear by Allah that they said nothing﴾, then described them all, to the end of the verse. [[Report 16973: Ayyub ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, Abu Ayyub al-Baghdadi, a teacher of al-Tabari. This isnad is sahih. al-Suyuti recorded it in al-Durr al-Manthur (3:258) and attributed it also to al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh.]]

Others said: Rather, it was revealed concerning 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. They said: the word he uttered was:

16974 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿They swear by Allah that they said nothing﴾, to His saying: ﴿nor any protector or helper﴾, he said: It was mentioned to us that two men fought, one from Juhaynah and the other from Ghifar, and Juhaynah were allies of the Ansar, and the Ghifari prevailed over the Juhani. 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy said to the Aws: "Help your brother! By Allah, our likeness and that of Muhammad is only as the saying goes: 'Fatten your dog and it will devour you.'" And he said: ﴿If we return to Madinah, the mightier will surely expel the meaner from it﴾ [Surah al-Munafiqun: 8]. A man from the Muslims reported it to the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, who sent for him and questioned him, and he began to swear by Allah that he had not said it. So Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed: ﴿They swear by Allah that they said nothing, but they did indeed utter the word of disbelief﴾.

16975 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿They swear by Allah that they said nothing, but they did indeed utter the word of disbelief﴾, he said: It was revealed concerning 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view in this matter, in our opinion, is that it should be said: Allah, exalted is He, informed about the hypocrites that they swear falsely by Allah that they did not utter the words of disbelief that they spoke. It is permissible that the statement was what was transmitted from 'Urwah, that al-Jullas said it; and it is permissible that its speaker was 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, and the statement was what Qatadah mentioned from him.

We have no knowledge of which of these is the case, since there is no report about either of them that establishes proof or leads to certain knowledge, and it is not something whose knowledge is grasped by the intellect's natural disposition. So the correct course is to say of it what Allah, majestic is His praise, said: ﴿They swear by Allah that they said nothing, but they did indeed utter the word of disbelief, and they disbelieved after their submission﴾.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and they planned what they could not attain﴾, the people of interpretation differed concerning the one who planned it, and what the thing was that he planned.

[Some of them said: it was a man among the hypocrites, and what he planned was] to kill the stepson who heard what he said, and he feared that it would be disclosed against him. [[In the manuscript the text reads: "...and what was the thing he planned: the stepson of his wife," while the printed edition reads: "...planned it, to kill his stepson," with a note that there seems to be a lacuna. The correct reading, God willing, is what I have placed between the brackets, since the following report is from Mujahid and does not name the hypocrite, as in no. 16970 and what follows; the best course is that the hypocrite's name remain unspecified in the translation of the reports, as is Abu Ja'far's practice in the sections of his tafsir.]]

Those who said this:

16976 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: The hypocrite planned to kill him, meaning to kill the believer who had said to him: "You are worse than a donkey!" That is His saying: ﴿and they planned what they could not attain﴾.

16977 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly. [[In the printed edition: "from Mujahid, bihi"; in the manuscript the chain is broken and mentions nothing, so I kept the form Abu Ja'far customarily used.]]

* *

Others said: the one who planned was a man from Quraysh, and what he planned was to kill the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

Those who said this:

16978 - Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Jabir, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿and they planned what they could not attain﴾, he said: A man from Quraysh planned to kill the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, called "al-Aswad."

* *

Others said: The one who planned was 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, and his planned aim which he did not attain was His saying: ﴿If we return to Madinah, the mightier will surely expel the meaner from it﴾ [Surah al-Munafiqun: 8], from the statement of Qatadah, which we have already mentioned. [[See above, no. 16974.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and they sought revenge only because Allah and His Messenger had enriched them out of His bounty﴾, it has been mentioned to us that the hypocrite about whom Allah reported that he uttered the word of disbelief had been poor, and Allah enriched him by the fact that a client of his was killed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave him his blood-money. When he said what he said, Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿and they sought revenge﴾, meaning: they found fault with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for nothing [[See the explanation of "naqama" in 10:433 and 13:35.]], = ﴿only because Allah and His Messenger had enriched them out of His bounty﴾.

Those who said this:

16979 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father: ﴿and they sought revenge only because Allah and His Messenger had enriched them out of His bounty﴾. Al-Jullas had had a client killed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered that his blood-money be given to him, and he became rich; that is His saying: ﴿and they sought revenge only because Allah and His Messenger had enriched them out of His bounty﴾.

16980 - ...... narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from 'Amr, from 'Ikrimah, who said: The Prophet ﷺ ruled the blood-money at twelve thousand, concerning a client of the clan of 'Adi ibn Ka'b, and concerning him this verse was revealed: ﴿and they sought revenge only because Allah and His Messenger had enriched them out of His bounty﴾.

16981 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿and they sought revenge only because Allah and His Messenger had enriched them out of His bounty﴾, he said: 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy had a blood-money, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ paid it for him.

16982 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to us, from Sufyan, who said: 'Amr narrated to us, who said: I heard 'Ikrimah: that a client of the clan of 'Adi ibn Ka'b killed a man of the Ansar, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled the blood-money at twelve thousand, and concerning this it was revealed: ﴿and they sought revenge only because Allah and His Messenger had enriched them out of His bounty﴾. 'Amr said: I did not hear this from the Prophet ﷺ except through 'Ikrimah, meaning: the blood-money of twelve thousand.

16983 - Salih ibn Misman narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sinan al-'Awaqi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Ta'ifi narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Ikrimah, client of Ibn 'Abbas, from Ibn 'Abbas: that the Prophet ﷺ fixed the blood-money at twelve thousand. That is the meaning of His saying: ﴿and they sought revenge only because Allah and His Messenger had enriched them out of His bounty﴾, he said: by taking the blood-money. [[Report 16983: Salih ibn Misman al-Sulami al-Marwazi, a teacher of al-Tabari, mentioned at no. 224. Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Bahili al-'Awaqi, Abu Bakr al-Basri, is trustworthy. Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Ta'ifi is trustworthy but has some weakness in his memory, mentioned at nos. 447, 3473, 4491. Abu Ja'far did not mention this report in the chapter on blood-money in his tafsir; see above no. 10143, vol. 9, p. 50.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So if they repent, it will be better for them﴾, the Exalted One means: If these utterers of the word of disbelief repent of their statement and turn back from it, their return and repentance will be better for them than hypocrisy [[See the explanation of "tawbah" in the vocabulary indexes above (root t-w-b).]] = ﴿but if they turn away﴾, meaning: if they turn their backs on repentance, refusing to take it up and persisting in their disbelief [[See the explanation of "tawalli" above (root w-l-y).]] = ﴿Allah will punish them with a painful punishment﴾, meaning: He will punish them with a painful torment in this world, either by killing or by a swift disgrace for them therein, and He will punish them in the Hereafter with the Fire. [[See the explanation of "alim" above (root '-l-m).]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and they will have no protector or helper on earth﴾, meaning: if Allah punishes these hypocrites in the immediate world, they will have no protector = ﴿from a protector﴾ who would protect them from the punishment of Allah [[See the explanation of "wali" above (root w-l-y).]] = ﴿nor any helper﴾ who would help them against Allah and rescue them from His punishment [[See the explanation of "nasir" above (root n-s-r).]]. They had been people of might and protection through their clans and folk, by whom they defended themselves against anyone who wished them harm. So Allah, blessed and exalted, informed that those who used to protect them from those who wished them harm among their clans and allies would not protect them from Allah nor help them against Him, should they need their help.

* *

It is mentioned that the one about whom this verse was revealed repented of the hypocrisy he had been upon.

Those who said this:

16984 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father: ﴿So if they repent, it will be better for them﴾, he said: al-Jullas said: "Allah has made an exception for me regarding repentance, so I repent." And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ accepted it from him.

16985 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father: ﴿So if they repent, it will be better for them﴾, the verse. Al-Jullas said: "O Messenger of Allah, I see that Allah has made an exception for me regarding repentance, so I repent!" He repented, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ accepted it from him.

The commentary of Abu Ja'far, that is al-Tabari, on the verses (75–77) of Surah al-Tawbah (Part 1 of 2)

**On the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying:** ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty, we will surely give charity and we will surely be among the righteous." (75) But when He gave them of His bounty, they became stingy with it and turned away while refusing.(76) So He caused hypocrisy to follow in their hearts until the Day they meet Him, because they failed Allah in what they promised Him and because they used to lie.﴾ (77)

Abu Ja'far says: May His remembrance be exalted, He says: And among these hypocrites whose description I have told you, O Muhammad, ﴿those who made a covenant with Allah﴾, meaning: they gave a pledge to Allah [[See the explanation of "ʿāhada" earlier: p. 141, note 1, and the references there.]] ﴿"If He gives us of His bounty"﴾, meaning: If Allah gives us of His bounty, provides us with wealth and widens His provision for us [[See the explanation of "ātā" and "al-faḍl" in the earlier lexical indexes (ʾtā) and (faḍl).]] ﴿"we will surely give charity"﴾, meaning: we will surely bring out charity from that wealth which our Lord has provided us [[See the explanation of "al-taṣaddu"" earlier: 9:31, 37, 38.]] ﴿"and we will surely be among the righteous"﴾, meaning: and we will surely act within it, with their wealth, in the manner of the people of righteousness, by maintaining ties of kinship through it and spending it in the way of Allah. [[See the explanation of "al-ṣāliḥ" in the earlier lexical indexes (ṣalaḥa).]]

Allah, blessed and exalted, says: So Allah provided for them and gave them of His bounty. ﴿So when He gave them of His bounty, they became stingy with it﴾, meaning: by the bounty of Allah which He gave them, they did not give charity from it, they did not maintain ties of kinship with it, and they did not spend from it in the right of Allah. ﴿And turned away﴾, meaning: they turned their backs on the covenant they had made with Allah. [[See the explanation of "al-tawallī" earlier in the lexical indexes (wallā).]] ﴿While refusing﴾, meaning: from it. [[See the explanation of "al-iʿrāḍ" earlier: 13:463, note 6, and the references there, vol. 14 (24).]] ﴿So He caused﴾ Allah ﴿hypocrisy to follow in their hearts﴾, meaning: because of their stinginess with the right of Allah which He had made obligatory upon them in what He had given them of His bounty, and their failure to keep the promise they had made to Allah, and their breaking of His covenant in their hearts. [[See the explanation of "al-nifāq" earlier: p. 358, note 1, and the references there.]] ﴿Until the Day they meet Him, because they failed Allah in what they promised Him﴾, meaning: of charity and spending in His way. ﴿And because they used to lie﴾, meaning: in their statements, and He deprived them of repentance from it. For He, may His praise be exalted, made the condition of their hypocrisy that He would cause it to follow them until the Day they meet Him, and that is the day of their death and their departure from this world.

* *

The people of interpretation (ahl al-taʾwīl) differed concerning the intended meaning of this verse.

Some of them said: It refers to a man called "Thaʿlabah ibn Ḥāṭib", from the Anṣār. [[In the manuscript, the text stops at his saying "called", and does not mention the man's name. The first editor inferred it from the reports, and he was correct in what he did.]]

Those who said this:

16986. Muḥammad ibn Saʿd said: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His saying: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty"﴾, to the end of the verse. The reason was that a man called "Thaʿlabah ibn Ḥāṭib", from the Anṣār, came to a gathering and called them to witness, saying: "If Allah gives me of His bounty, I will give every person with a right his right, and I will give charity from it, and I will maintain ties of kinship with it!" Then Allah tested him and gave him of His bounty, so he broke the promise Allah had made him, and angered Allah by breaking what He had promised. So Allah related his story in the Qur'an: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah﴾, the verse, to His saying: ﴿lie﴾.

16987. Al-Muthannā related to me, saying: Hishām ibn ʿAmmār related to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Shuʿayb related to us, saying: Maʿān ibn Rifāʿah al-Sulamī related to us, from Abū ʿAbd al-Malik ʿAlī ibn Yazīd al-Ilhānī: that he informed him from al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān: that he informed him from Abū Umāmah al-Bāhilī, from Thaʿlabah ibn Ḥāṭib al-Anṣārī, that he said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Ask Allah to provide me with wealth!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Woe to you, O Thaʿlabah! A little that you can thank for is better than a lot that you cannot bear!" He said: Then he asked again, and he said: "Are you not content to be like the Prophet of Allah? By Him in whose hand is my soul, if I wished, mountains would move with me as gold and silver!" He said: "By He who sent you with truth, if you invoke Allah and He provides me with wealth, I will surely give every person with a right his right!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, provide Thaʿlabah with wealth!" He said: So he acquired sheep, and they multiplied as worms multiply, and the city became too tight for him, so he withdrew from it and settled in one of its valleys, until he began praying Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr in congregation and abandoned everything else. Then they multiplied and increased, and he withdrew until he gave up prayers except Friday, and they kept multiplying as worms multiply, until he gave up Friday too. He began meeting caravans on Friday, asking them for news. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "What has Thaʿlabah done?" They said: "O Messenger of Allah, he acquired sheep and the city became too tight for him!" They informed him of his affair. He said: "Woe to Thaʿlabah! Woe to Thaʿlabah! Woe to Thaʿlabah!" He said: And Allah revealed: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity﴾ [Sūrat al-Tawbah: 103], the verse, and the obligatory charity rules were revealed to him. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent two men to collect the charity, a man from Juhaynah and a man from Sulaym, and he wrote for them how they should take charity from the Muslims. He said to them: "Pass by Thaʿlabah, and so-and-so, a man from Banū Sulaym, and take their charities!" So they set out until they came to Thaʿlabah, and asked him for the charity, and they read to him the letter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: "This is nothing but jizyah! This is nothing but the sister of jizyah! I do not know what this is! Go until you are free, then come back to me." So they left, and the Sulamī heard of them, so he looked at the best of his camels' ages, separated them for charity, and then met them with them. When they saw them they said: "This is not obligatory upon you, and we do not want to take this from you." He said: "Yes, take it, for my soul is content with that, and it is mine!" So they took it from him. When they finished their collection they returned, until they passed by Thaʿlabah, and he said: "Show me your letter!" He looked into it and said: "This is nothing but the sister of jizyah! Go until I see my opinion." So they left until they came to the Prophet (ﷺ). When he saw them, he said, before speaking to them: "Woe to Thaʿlabah!" He invoked blessing for the Sulamī, and they informed him of what Thaʿlabah had done and what the Sulamī had done. Then Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed concerning him: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty, we will surely give charity and we will surely be among the righteous"﴾, to His saying: ﴿And because they used to lie﴾. A man from Thaʿlabah's relatives was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he heard that, so he went out until he came to him and said: "Woe to you, O Thaʿlabah! Allah has revealed such-and-such concerning you!" So Thaʿlabah went out until he came to the Prophet (ﷺ), and asked him to accept his charity. He said: "Allah has forbidden me to accept your charity from you!" So he began throwing dust on his head. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "This is your deed! I commanded you and you did not obey me!" When he refused, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was taken [in death], and he returned to his home. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) died and did not accept anything from him. Then he came to Abū Bakr when he was appointed caliph, and said: "You know my standing with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and my position among the Anṣār, so accept my charity!" Abū Bakr said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not accept it, and I will accept it?" Then Abū Bakr died without having accepted it. When ʿUmar became caliph, he came to him and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, accept my charity!" He said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not accept it, nor did Abū Bakr, and I will accept it from you?" Then he died without accepting it. Then ʿUthmān, may Allah have mercy on him, became caliph, and he came to him and asked him to accept his charity. He said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not accept it, nor did Abū Bakr, nor ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, and I will accept it from you!" [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "and I do not accept it," and the correct reading is to omit "not" as stated in the statements of Abū Bakr and ʿUmar. This matches what is in Usd al-Ghābah.]] So he did not accept it from him. Thaʿlabah died during the caliphate of ʿUthmān, may Allah have mercy on him. [[The report 16987: "Hishām ibn ʿAmmār ibn Nuṣayr al-Sulamī," reliable; al-Bukhārī, Abū Dāwūd, al-Nasāʾī and Ibn Mājah related from him. They criticised him, saying: when he grew old, he changed. It passed as number 11108. And "Muḥammad ibn Shuʿayb ibn Shābūr al-Umawī" is reliable, it passed as number 16987.
And "Maʿān ibn Rifāʿah al-Sulamī," or "al-Salāmī," which is the more well known, is weak in narration; his narrations are written down but not used as evidence. He is mentioned in al-Tahdhīb and al-Kabīr 4/2/70, and in one of its copies it reads "al-Sulamī" as in al-Ṭabarī, so I left it as it is; and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
And "ʿAlī ibn Yazīd al-Alhānī," "Abū ʿAbd al-Malik," is extremely weak; he related from al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, the companion of Abū Umāmah, a large collection, and these narrations of his are all weak. It passed as number 11525.
And "al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Shāmī," his reliability has been explained earlier, and what is rejected from him came only from the weak narrators who related from him. It passed as numbers 1939, 11525.
As for Thaʿlabah ibn Ḥāṭib al-Anṣārī, there is much confusion in his biography. Is he one man or two? The first of them is the one whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made a brother-bond between him and Muʿattib ibn al-Ḥamrāʾ, and who witnessed Badr and Uḥud. The other is the subject of this story. It is said that the first was killed at Uḥud. Some considered them one man and denied that he was killed at Uḥud. See his biography in al-Iṣābah, al-Istīʿāb: 78, Usd al-Ghābah 1: 237, and Ibn Saʿd: 3/2/32.
This report was related with this chain by Ibn al-Athīr in Usd al-Ghābah 1: 237, 238, and al-Haythamī cited it in Majmaʿ al-Zawāʾid 7: 21, 32, and said: "al-Ṭabarānī related it, and in it is ʿAlī ibn Yazīd al-Alhānī, who is abandoned."
It is extremely weak, has no supporting report from another source, and some of its narrators are severely weak.
This report was also cited by al-Suyūṭī in al-Durr al-Manthūr 3: 260, attributing it to al-Ḥasan ibn Sufyān, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, Abū al-Shaykh, al-ʿAskarī in al-Amthāl, al-Ṭabarānī, Ibn Mandah, al-Bārūdī, Abū Nuʿaym in Maʿrifat al-Ṣaḥābah, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqī in al-Dalāʾil, and Ibn ʿAsākir.]]

16988. Bishr related to us, saying: Yazīd related to us, saying: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah regarding His saying: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty"﴾, the verse: It was mentioned to us that a man from the Anṣār came to a gathering of the Anṣār and said: "If Allah gives me wealth, I will surely pay every person with a right his right!" Then Allah gave him wealth, and he did with it what you have heard. He said: ﴿So when He gave them of His bounty, they became stingy with it﴾, to His saying: ﴿And because they used to lie﴾. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) related that when Mūsā (peace be upon him) brought the Torah to the Children of Israel, the Children of Israel said: "The Torah is large, and we do not have free time for it, so ask your Lord for us a set of matters we can keep and by which we can be free for our livelihood!" He said: "O people, wait, wait! This is the Book of Allah, the light of Allah, and the safeguard of Allah!" He said: They repeated it to him, and he repeated to them, saying it three times. He said: Then Allah revealed to Mūsā: "What are My servants saying?" He said: "O Lord, they say: such-and-such." He said: "I command them with three things: if they keep them, they will enter Paradise by them: that they come to the division of inheritance and not wrong in it, that they not let their eyes enter houses until permission is given to them, and that they not eat food until they perform ablution like the ablution for prayer." He said: The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) returned with them to his people, and they rejoiced and thought they would uphold them. He said: By Allah, the people did not remain long before they veered away and were cut off from them. When the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) related this story of the Children of Israel, he said: "Take on for me six, and I will take on for you Paradise!" They said: "What are they, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "When you speak, do not lie; when you promise, do not break it; when you are entrusted, do not betray; and restrain your eyes, your hands and your private parts: your eyes from betrayal, your hands from theft, and your private parts from fornication."

16989. Bishr related to us, saying: Yazīd related to us, saying: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah, from al-Ḥasan: that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say: "Three things, whoever has them is a hypocrite, even if he fasts and prays and claims he is a Muslim: when he speaks he lies, when he is entrusted he betrays, and when he promises he breaks it."

* *

Others said: Rather, the one intended by it is two men: one of them is Thaʿlabah, and the other is Muʿattib ibn Qushayr.

Those who said this:

16990. Ibn Ḥumayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, from ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd, from al-Ḥasan: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty"﴾, the verse, [[In the printed edition it read: "of His bounty, to the other," which is very strange; in the manuscript: "of His bounty the other," and the correct reading of it is what I have recorded; the copyist erred as is his habit.]] and those among them who made a covenant with Allah were Thaʿlabah ibn Ḥāṭib and Muʿattib ibn Qushayr, and both were from Banū ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf. [[The report 16990: Sīrat Ibn Hishām 4: 196, and it is a continuation of the earlier report number 16969.]]

16991. Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us, saying: ʿĪsā related to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty"﴾, he said: Two men went out before a seated assembly and said: "By Allah, if Allah provides us, we will surely give charity!" When He provided them, they became stingy with it.

16992. Al-Muthannā related to me, saying: Abū Ḥudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty"﴾: two men went out before a seated assembly and said: "By Allah, if Allah provides us, we will surely give charity!" When He provided them, they became stingy with it, = ﴿So He caused hypocrisy to follow in their hearts because they failed Allah in what they promised Him﴾, when they said: "We will surely give charity," and they did not do it.

16993. Al-Muthannā related to me, saying: Isḥāq related to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh related to us, from Warqāʾ, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, similarly.

16994. Yūnus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty"﴾, the verse: These are a category of hypocrites. When He gave them that, they became stingy with it, and when they became stingy with it, He caused hypocrisy to follow them because of it until the Day they meet Him, and they have no repentance, no forgiveness, and no pardon from it, just as Iblīs was struck when He denied him repentance.

* *

Abū Ja'far says: In this verse there is a clarification from Allah, blessed and exalted, about a sign of the people of hypocrisy, meaning in His saying: ﴿So He caused hypocrisy to follow in their hearts until the Day they meet Him, because they failed Allah in what they promised Him and because they used to lie﴾.

* *

The saying of a group of the Companions and the Successors (tābiʿūn) was similar to this view, and reports were transmitted with it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). [[In the printed edition: "and it came with it," and I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

Those who said this:

16995. Abū al-Sāʾib related to us, saying: Abū Muʿāwiyah related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿUmārah, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, who said: ʿAbd Allāh (Ibn Masʿūd) said: "Judge the hypocrite by three: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he makes a covenant he betrays," and Allah revealed the confirmation of this in His Book: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty"﴾, to His saying: ﴿lie﴾. [[The report 16995: "ʿUmārah" is "ʿUmārah ibn ʿUmayr al-Taymī," reliable, related from by the group, passed as numbers 3294, 5789, 15359.
And "ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd al-Nakhaʿī," a reliable Successor, related from by the group. Passed as numbers 3294, 3295, 3299.
And "ʿAbd Allāh" means "ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd."
This report has a sound chain, halted at Ibn Masʿūd, and I did not find it raised to the Prophet from him. Al-Haythamī mentioned it in Majmaʿ al-Zawāʾid 1: 108, with this same wording, and said: "al-Ṭabarānī related it in al-Kabīr, and its narrators are the narrators of the Ṣaḥīḥ." He mentioned before it a similar hadith: "from ʿAbd Allāh, meaning Ibn Masʿūd, from the Prophet (ﷺ)," without the verse, then said: "al-Bazzār related it, and its narrators are the narrators of the Ṣaḥīḥ."]]

16996. Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā related to me, saying: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar related to us, saying: Shuʿbah related to us, from Simāk, from Ṣabīḥ ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmayrah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, who said: "Three things, whoever has them is a hypocrite: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he is entrusted he betrays." He said: And he recited this verse: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty, we will surely give charity and we will surely be among the righteous"﴾, to the end of the verse. [[The report 16996: This report comes with another chain after it.

"Sabih ibn Abdullah ibn Umayrah" and "Sabih ibn Abdullah al-Absi" are the same person as the one that follows. Both appeared earlier under nos. 12741 and 12742. It was noted earlier that al-Bukhari included him in al-Kabir (2/2/319) under the name "Sabih ibn Abdullah," and in the isnad he is given the nisba "al-Absi." The annotator there noted that Ibn Makula has "Sabih ibn Abdullah ibn Umayr al-Taghlibi," whereas al-Tabari here has "Umayrah." I found nothing to favour either reading. Ibn Abi Hatim included him (2/1/449), and they did not mention any narration from "Abdullah ibn Amr." In the printed edition here it was "Abdullah ibn Umar," which I believe is an error, as the report that follows shows (see below).

My brother al-Sayyid Ahmad cited this report with this isnad in his commentary on the Musnad, under the Musnad of "Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As," no. 6879. He then said: "Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Firyabi narrated it in his Kitab Sifat al-Nifaq (pp. 50-51), from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, from Ghundar, from Shu'bah, from Simak ibn Harb, from Sabih ibn Abdullah, from Abdullah ibn Amr," and then he quoted the report in similar wording. Then he said: "This is a mawquf (companion-level) report, and its isnad is sound. It is a good corroboration for this hadith, since it is, in ruling, equivalent to a marfu' (prophetic) report. Sabih ibn Abdullah, with a damma on the sad, is a senior Tabi'i who met Uthman and Ali. al-Bukhari included him in al-Kabir (2/2/319) and mentioned no criticism of him."

The hadith in the Musnad is a marfu' hadith.

The hadith of the sign of the hypocrite was narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (al-Fath 1:83-84) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah and of Abdullah ibn Amr. Muslim narrated it in his Sahih (2:46-48) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr and of Abu Hurayrah.

16997. Ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: Abu Dawud told us, saying: Shu'bah told us, from Simak, who said: I heard Sabih ibn Abdullah al-Absi say: "I asked Abdullah ibn Amr about the hypocrite," and he related something similar.

[Report 16997: "Sabih ibn Abdullah al-Absi": see the preceding no. 16996. In the printed and manuscript editions it was "al-Qaysi," with a qaf and a ya; I corrected it from the sources and from the earlier nos. 12741 and 12742.]

16998. Muhammad ibn Ma'mar told me, saying: Abu Hisham al-Makhzumi told us, saying: Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad told us, saying: Uthman ibn Hakim told us, saying: I heard Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi say: "I used to hear that the hypocrite is recognised by three things: lying, breaking promises, and betrayal. I searched for them in the Book of Allah for a time and could not find them, then I found them in two places in the Book of Allah," [In the printed edition it reads "in two verses." I have kept what is in the manuscript, which in my view is correct, since the verses he mentions after this are three verses from Surat al-Tawbah and one from Surat al-Ahzab, making four. He must have meant "in two surahs of the Qur'an," or something close to that.] namely: His saying: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah﴾ up to ﴿and because they used to lie﴾, and His saying: ﴿Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth﴾ [Surat al-Ahzab: 72], this verse.

16999. Ibn Hamid... [no]

Correction: 16999. Al-Qasim ibn Bishr ibn Ma'ruf told me, saying: Shababah told us, saying: Muhammad al-Muhrim told us, saying: I heard al-Hasan say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever has three things in him is a hypocrite, even if he prays, fasts, and claims to be a Muslim: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he is entrusted he betrays." I said to al-Hasan: "O Abu Sa'id, if a man is owed a debt by me, and he meets me and demands it from me, and I do not have it, and I fear that he will imprison me and ruin me, so I promise him that I will pay it at the new moon, and I do not do so. Am I a hypocrite?" He said: "That is how the hadith came!" Then he related from Abdullah ibn Amr that his father, when death approached him, said: "Marry So-and-so, for I promised him that I would marry him. I will not meet Allah with a third of hypocrisy!" I said: "O Abu Sa'id, can a man be a third hypocrite and two-thirds believer?" He said: "That is how the hadith came." He said: "I went on pilgrimage and met Ata ibn Abi Rabah, and I told him the hadith I had heard from al-Hasan, and what I had said to him and what he had said to me. He said to me: 'Were you unable to say to him: Tell me about the brothers of Yusuf, peace be upon him. Did they not promise their father and break it, did they not speak to him and lie to him, did they not get entrusted and betray him? Were they hypocrites? Were they not prophets? Their father was a prophet, and their grandfather was a prophet?'" He said: "I said to Ata: 'O Abu Muhammad, tell me the origin of hypocrisy, and the origin of this hadith.' He said: 'Jabir ibn Abdullah told me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) only said this hadith about the hypocrites specifically, who spoke to the Prophet and lied to him, who were entrusted with his secret and betrayed it, and who promised him that they would go out with him on the campaign and then broke it.'" He said: "Abu Sufyan went out from Makkah, and Jibril came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'Abu Sufyan is at such-and-such a place.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said to his companions: 'Abu Sufyan is at such-and-such a place, so go out to him, and keep it secret.' He said: 'A man among the hypocrites wrote to him: "Muhammad intends to attack you, so take your precautions." So Allah revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not betray Allah and the Messenger or betray your trusts while you know﴾ [Surat al-Anfal: 27], and He revealed concerning the hypocrites: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty..."﴾ up to ﴿so He penalised them with hypocrisy in their hearts until the Day they meet Him, because they broke to Allah what they promised Him and because they used to lie﴾. When you meet al-Hasan, give him my greetings, and tell him the origin of this hadith and what I said to you.'" He said: "I came to al-Hasan and said: 'O Abu Sa'id, your brother Ata sends you greetings,' and I told him the hadith he had related and what he had said to me. Al-Hasan took my hand and raised it [In the printed edition it reads "fa-amalaha" (inclined it), which has no meaning at all. The manuscript has "fa-asalaha" without dots, and this is the correct reading. It is said: "the she-camel raised her tail" (shalat al-naqatu bi-dhanabiha wa-ashalathu), meaning lifted it; and "ashal al-hajar" or "shal bihi" or "shawalahu" means to lift it; and "shal al-sa'il bi-yadayhi" means when he raised his hands in asking with them.] and said: 'O people of Iraq, were you unable to be like this? He heard a hadith from me and did not accept it until he had derived its origin. Ata is right. That is how the hadith came, and this is about the hypocrites specifically.'"

[Report 16999: "al-Qasim ibn Bishr ibn Ahmad ibn Ma'ruf," the teacher of al-Tabari, who appeared earlier under nos. 10509 and 10531. "Shababah" is Shababah ibn Sawwar al-Fazari, from whom the whole group narrated; he appeared earlier under no. 12851 and before it. In the printed edition it read "Usamah," which reflects a failure to read the manuscript, and so it is a grave distortion. "Muhammad al-Muhrim" is Muhammad ibn Umar al-Muhrim, also called Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr al-Laythi, and he is munkar al-hadith (weak in narration). His condition was explained in detail earlier under no. 15922, along with the places where he is biographed. In the printed edition it read "Muhammad al-Makhrami," which differs from the manuscript without any basis or explanation, and it is an error. This report is extremely munkar. al-Bukhari pointed to it in al-Tarikh al-Kabir (1/1/248) in his biography of "Muhammad al-Muhrim," saying: "From Ata and al-Hasan. Munkar al-hadith: when he promises he breaks it. Shababah narrated from him," meaning this report.]

17000. Ya'qub told me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah told us, saying: Ya'qub informed us, from al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever has three things in him, even if he prays, fasts, and claims to be a Muslim, is a hypocrite." It was asked of him: "What are they, O Messenger of Allah?" The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "When he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he is entrusted he betrays."

17001. Al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Mubashshir told us, from al-Awza'i, from Harun ibn Riyab, from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Wa'il, that when death approached him he said: "So-and-so proposed to my daughter, and I had said to him something like a promise. By Allah, I will not meet Allah with a third of hypocrisy! I call you to witness that I have married her to him."

[Report 17001: "Mubashshir" is Mubashshir ibn Isma'il al-Halabi, trustworthy (thiqah), one of Ahmad's teachers, from whom the whole group narrated. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir (4/2/11), and Ibn Abi Hatim (4/1/343). In the printed edition it read "Maysarah," which is a faulty alteration, and in the manuscript it reads "Musir" without dots.
"Harun ibn Riyab al-Tamimi al-Usayyidi" was among the worshippers who concealed their asceticism. He was trustworthy. Ibn Hazm said: "al-Yaman, Harun, and Ali, the sons of Riyab: Harun was among the People of the Sunnah, al-Yaman was among the imams of the Khawarij, and Ali was among the imams of the Rafidah, and they were all hostile to one another!!" He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir (4/2/219), and Ibn Abi Hatim (4/2/89).
As for "Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Wa'il," this is unusual but sound, for it is "Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As ibn Wa'il." I do not know why it was done this way in the form of his name, unless something dropped out from the copyist's text.
Furthermore, the isnad in the printed edition was as follows: "al-Qasim told us, al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Maysarah told us." I have corrected "Maysarah" before it. As for "saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Juraij," the copyist of the manuscript wrote it, but he struck it through with pen strokes, meaning to delete it. The editor, however, did not know their convention for striking through text, so I have kept what he deleted.]

* *

Others said: The covenant which those hypocrites made with Allah was something they resolved in their hearts without speaking it.

Those who said this:

17002. Al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: I heard Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman al-Taymi say: "I boarded the sea, and a violent wind struck us, so some people among us vowed vows, and I made an intention but did not speak it. When I arrived at Basra, I asked my father Sulayman, and he said to me: 'O my son, fulfil it.'" [In the printed edition it read "fah bihi," which is used only at pause, and the correct form is "fi" as a single letter, the imperative of "wafa yafi" (to fulfil). I have kept what is in the manuscript.]

= Mu'tamir said: And Kahmas told us, from Sa'id ibn Thabit, concerning His saying: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah﴾, the verse, he said: "It is only something they resolved in their hearts without speaking it. Did you not hear His saying: ﴿Do they not know that Allah knows their secret and their private talk, and that Allah is the Knower of the unseen?﴾"

[Report 17002: "Kahmas ibn al-Hasan al-Tamimi," trustworthy, from whom the whole group narrated. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir (4/1/239), and Ibn Abi Hatim (3/2/170).
As for "Sa'id ibn Thabit," this is how it stands in the manuscript. I have not found any mention of him in the books of biography available to me, and I fear that a distortion may have entered the name.]

The commentary of Abu Ja'far, that is al-Tabari, on the verses (75–77) of Surah al-Tawbah (Part 1 of 2)

**On the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying:** ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty, we will surely give charity and we will surely be among the righteous." (75) But when He gave them of His bounty, they became stingy with it and turned away while refusing.(76) So He caused hypocrisy to follow in their hearts until the Day they meet Him, because they failed Allah in what they promised Him and because they used to lie.﴾ (77)

Abu Ja'far says: May His remembrance be exalted, He says: And among these hypocrites whose description I have told you, O Muhammad, ﴿those who made a covenant with Allah﴾, meaning: they gave a pledge to Allah [[See the explanation of "ʿāhada" earlier: p. 141, note 1, and the references there.]] ﴿"If He gives us of His bounty"﴾, meaning: If Allah gives us of His bounty, provides us with wealth and widens His provision for us [[See the explanation of "ātā" and "al-faḍl" in the earlier lexical indexes (ʾtā) and (faḍl).]] ﴿"we will surely give charity"﴾, meaning: we will surely bring out charity from that wealth which our Lord has provided us [[See the explanation of "al-taṣaddu"" earlier: 9:31, 37, 38.]] ﴿"and we will surely be among the righteous"﴾, meaning: and we will surely act within it, with their wealth, in the manner of the people of righteousness, by maintaining ties of kinship through it and spending it in the way of Allah. [[See the explanation of "al-ṣāliḥ" in the earlier lexical indexes (ṣalaḥa).]]

Allah, blessed and exalted, says: So Allah provided for them and gave them of His bounty. ﴿So when He gave them of His bounty, they became stingy with it﴾, meaning: by the bounty of Allah which He gave them, they did not give charity from it, they did not maintain ties of kinship with it, and they did not spend from it in the right of Allah. ﴿And turned away﴾, meaning: they turned their backs on the covenant they had made with Allah. [[See the explanation of "al-tawallī" earlier in the lexical indexes (wallā).]] ﴿While refusing﴾, meaning: from it. [[See the explanation of "al-iʿrāḍ" earlier: 13:463, note 6, and the references there, vol. 14 (24).]] ﴿So He caused﴾ Allah ﴿hypocrisy to follow in their hearts﴾, meaning: because of their stinginess with the right of Allah which He had made obligatory upon them in what He had given them of His bounty, and their failure to keep the promise they had made to Allah, and their breaking of His covenant in their hearts. [[See the explanation of "al-nifāq" earlier: p. 358, note 1, and the references there.]] ﴿Until the Day they meet Him, because they failed Allah in what they promised Him﴾, meaning: of charity and spending in His way. ﴿And because they used to lie﴾, meaning: in their statements, and He deprived them of repentance from it. For He, may His praise be exalted, made the condition of their hypocrisy that He would cause it to follow them until the Day they meet Him, and that is the day of their death and their departure from this world.

* *

The people of interpretation (ahl al-taʾwīl) differed concerning the intended meaning of this verse.

Some of them said: It refers to a man called "Thaʿlabah ibn Ḥāṭib", from the Anṣār. [[In the manuscript, the text stops at his saying "called", and does not mention the man's name. The first editor inferred it from the reports, and he was correct in what he did.]]

Those who said this:

16986. Muḥammad ibn Saʿd said: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His saying: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty"﴾, to the end of the verse. The reason was that a man called "Thaʿlabah ibn Ḥāṭib", from the Anṣār, came to a gathering and called them to witness, saying: "If Allah gives me of His bounty, I will give every person with a right his right, and I will give charity from it, and I will maintain ties of kinship with it!" Then Allah tested him and gave him of His bounty, so he broke the promise Allah had made him, and angered Allah by breaking what He had promised. So Allah related his story in the Qur'an: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah﴾, the verse, to His saying: ﴿lie﴾.

16987. Al-Muthannā related to me, saying: Hishām ibn ʿAmmār related to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Shuʿayb related to us, saying: Maʿān ibn Rifāʿah al-Sulamī related to us, from Abū ʿAbd al-Malik ʿAlī ibn Yazīd al-Ilhānī: that he informed him from al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān: that he informed him from Abū Umāmah al-Bāhilī, from Thaʿlabah ibn Ḥāṭib al-Anṣārī, that he said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Ask Allah to provide me with wealth!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Woe to you, O Thaʿlabah! A little that you can thank for is better than a lot that you cannot bear!" He said: Then he asked again, and he said: "Are you not content to be like the Prophet of Allah? By Him in whose hand is my soul, if I wished, mountains would move with me as gold and silver!" He said: "By He who sent you with truth, if you invoke Allah and He provides me with wealth, I will surely give every person with a right his right!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, provide Thaʿlabah with wealth!" He said: So he acquired sheep, and they multiplied as worms multiply, and the city became too tight for him, so he withdrew from it and settled in one of its valleys, until he began praying Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr in congregation and abandoned everything else. Then they multiplied and increased, and he withdrew until he gave up prayers except Friday, and they kept multiplying as worms multiply, until he gave up Friday too. He began meeting caravans on Friday, asking them for news. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "What has Thaʿlabah done?" They said: "O Messenger of Allah, he acquired sheep and the city became too tight for him!" They informed him of his affair. He said: "Woe to Thaʿlabah! Woe to Thaʿlabah! Woe to Thaʿlabah!" He said: And Allah revealed: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity﴾ [Sūrat al-Tawbah: 103], the verse, and the obligatory charity rules were revealed to him. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent two men to collect the charity, a man from Juhaynah and a man from Sulaym, and he wrote for them how they should take charity from the Muslims. He said to them: "Pass by Thaʿlabah, and so-and-so, a man from Banū Sulaym, and take their charities!" So they set out until they came to Thaʿlabah, and asked him for the charity, and they read to him the letter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: "This is nothing but jizyah! This is nothing but the sister of jizyah! I do not know what this is! Go until you are free, then come back to me." So they left, and the Sulamī heard of them, so he looked at the best of his camels' ages, separated them for charity, and then met them with them. When they saw them they said: "This is not obligatory upon you, and we do not want to take this from you." He said: "Yes, take it, for my soul is content with that, and it is mine!" So they took it from him. When they finished their collection they returned, until they passed by Thaʿlabah, and he said: "Show me your letter!" He looked into it and said: "This is nothing but the sister of jizyah! Go until I see my opinion." So they left until they came to the Prophet (ﷺ). When he saw them, he said, before speaking to them: "Woe to Thaʿlabah!" He invoked blessing for the Sulamī, and they informed him of what Thaʿlabah had done and what the Sulamī had done. Then Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed concerning him: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty, we will surely give charity and we will surely be among the righteous"﴾, to His saying: ﴿And because they used to lie﴾. A man from Thaʿlabah's relatives was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he heard that, so he went out until he came to him and said: "Woe to you, O Thaʿlabah! Allah has revealed such-and-such concerning you!" So Thaʿlabah went out until he came to the Prophet (ﷺ), and asked him to accept his charity. He said: "Allah has forbidden me to accept your charity from you!" So he began throwing dust on his head. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "This is your deed! I commanded you and you did not obey me!" When he refused, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was taken [in death], and he returned to his home. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) died and did not accept anything from him. Then he came to Abū Bakr when he was appointed caliph, and said: "You know my standing with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and my position among the Anṣār, so accept my charity!" Abū Bakr said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not accept it, and I will accept it?" Then Abū Bakr died without having accepted it. When ʿUmar became caliph, he came to him and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, accept my charity!" He said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not accept it, nor did Abū Bakr, and I will accept it from you?" Then he died without accepting it. Then ʿUthmān, may Allah have mercy on him, became caliph, and he came to him and asked him to accept his charity. He said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not accept it, nor did Abū Bakr, nor ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, and I will accept it from you!" [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "and I do not accept it," and the correct reading is to omit "not" as stated in the statements of Abū Bakr and ʿUmar. This matches what is in Usd al-Ghābah.]] So he did not accept it from him. Thaʿlabah died during the caliphate of ʿUthmān, may Allah have mercy on him. [[The report 16987: "Hishām ibn ʿAmmār ibn Nuṣayr al-Sulamī," reliable; al-Bukhārī, Abū Dāwūd, al-Nasāʾī and Ibn Mājah related from him. They criticised him, saying: when he grew old, he changed. It passed as number 11108. And "Muḥammad ibn Shuʿayb ibn Shābūr al-Umawī" is reliable, it passed as number 16987.
And "Maʿān ibn Rifāʿah al-Sulamī," or "al-Salāmī," which is the more well known, is weak in narration; his narrations are written down but not used as evidence. He is mentioned in al-Tahdhīb and al-Kabīr 4/2/70, and in one of its copies it reads "al-Sulamī" as in al-Ṭabarī, so I left it as it is; and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
And "ʿAlī ibn Yazīd al-Alhānī," "Abū ʿAbd al-Malik," is extremely weak; he related from al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, the companion of Abū Umāmah, a large collection, and these narrations of his are all weak. It passed as number 11525.
And "al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Shāmī," his reliability has been explained earlier, and what is rejected from him came only from the weak narrators who related from him. It passed as numbers 1939, 11525.
As for Thaʿlabah ibn Ḥāṭib al-Anṣārī, there is much confusion in his biography. Is he one man or two? The first of them is the one whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made a brother-bond between him and Muʿattib ibn al-Ḥamrāʾ, and who witnessed Badr and Uḥud. The other is the subject of this story. It is said that the first was killed at Uḥud. Some considered them one man and denied that he was killed at Uḥud. See his biography in al-Iṣābah, al-Istīʿāb: 78, Usd al-Ghābah 1: 237, and Ibn Saʿd: 3/2/32.
This report was related with this chain by Ibn al-Athīr in Usd al-Ghābah 1: 237, 238, and al-Haythamī cited it in Majmaʿ al-Zawāʾid 7: 21, 32, and said: "al-Ṭabarānī related it, and in it is ʿAlī ibn Yazīd al-Alhānī, who is abandoned."
It is extremely weak, has no supporting report from another source, and some of its narrators are severely weak.
This report was also cited by al-Suyūṭī in al-Durr al-Manthūr 3: 260, attributing it to al-Ḥasan ibn Sufyān, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, Abū al-Shaykh, al-ʿAskarī in al-Amthāl, al-Ṭabarānī, Ibn Mandah, al-Bārūdī, Abū Nuʿaym in Maʿrifat al-Ṣaḥābah, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqī in al-Dalāʾil, and Ibn ʿAsākir.]]

16988.
