Bishr related to us, saying: Yazīd related to us, saying: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah regarding His saying: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty"﴾, the verse: It was mentioned to us that a man from the Anṣār came to a gathering of the Anṣār and said: "If Allah gives me wealth, I will surely pay every person with a right his right!" Then Allah gave him wealth, and he did with it what you have heard. He said: ﴿So when He gave them of His bounty, they became stingy with it﴾, to His saying: ﴿And because they used to lie﴾. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) related that when Mūsā (peace be upon him) brought the Torah to the Children of Israel, the Children of Israel said: "The Torah is large, and we do not have free time for it, so ask your Lord for us a set of matters we can keep and by which we can be free for our livelihood!" He said: "O people, wait, wait! This is the Book of Allah, the light of Allah, and the safeguard of Allah!" He said: They repeated it to him, and he repeated to them, saying it three times. He said: Then Allah revealed to Mūsā: "What are My servants saying?" He said: "O Lord, they say: such-and-such." He said: "I command them with three things: if they keep them, they will enter Paradise by them: that they come to the division of inheritance and not wrong in it, that they not let their eyes enter houses until permission is given to them, and that they not eat food until they perform ablution like the ablution for prayer." He said: The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) returned with them to his people, and they rejoiced and thought they would uphold them. He said: By Allah, the people did not remain long before they veered away and were cut off from them. When the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) related this story of the Children of Israel, he said: "Take on for me six, and I will take on for you Paradise!" They said: "What are they, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "When you speak, do not lie; when you promise, do not break it; when you are entrusted, do not betray; and restrain your eyes, your hands and your private parts: your eyes from betrayal, your hands from theft, and your private parts from fornication."

16989. Bishr related to us, saying: Yazīd related to us, saying: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah, from al-Ḥasan: that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say: "Three things, whoever has them is a hypocrite, even if he fasts and prays and claims he is a Muslim: when he speaks he lies, when he is entrusted he betrays, and when he promises he breaks it."

* *

Others said: Rather, the one intended by it is two men: one of them is Thaʿlabah, and the other is Muʿattib ibn Qushayr.

Those who said this:

16990. Ibn Ḥumayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, from ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd, from al-Ḥasan: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty"﴾, the verse, [[In the printed edition it read: "of His bounty, to the other," which is very strange; in the manuscript: "of His bounty the other," and the correct reading of it is what I have recorded; the copyist erred as is his habit.]] and those among them who made a covenant with Allah were Thaʿlabah ibn Ḥāṭib and Muʿattib ibn Qushayr, and both were from Banū ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf. [[The report 16990: Sīrat Ibn Hishām 4: 196, and it is a continuation of the earlier report number 16969.]]

16991. Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us, saying: ʿĪsā related to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty"﴾, he said: Two men went out before a seated assembly and said: "By Allah, if Allah provides us, we will surely give charity!" When He provided them, they became stingy with it.

16992. Al-Muthannā related to me, saying: Abū Ḥudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty"﴾: two men went out before a seated assembly and said: "By Allah, if Allah provides us, we will surely give charity!" When He provided them, they became stingy with it, = ﴿So He caused hypocrisy to follow in their hearts because they failed Allah in what they promised Him﴾, when they said: "We will surely give charity," and they did not do it.

16993. Al-Muthannā related to me, saying: Isḥāq related to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh related to us, from Warqāʾ, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, similarly.

16994. Yūnus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty"﴾, the verse: These are a category of hypocrites. When He gave them that, they became stingy with it, and when they became stingy with it, He caused hypocrisy to follow them because of it until the Day they meet Him, and they have no repentance, no forgiveness, and no pardon from it, just as Iblīs was struck when He denied him repentance.

* *

Abū Ja'far says: In this verse there is a clarification from Allah, blessed and exalted, about a sign of the people of hypocrisy, meaning in His saying: ﴿So He caused hypocrisy to follow in their hearts until the Day they meet Him, because they failed Allah in what they promised Him and because they used to lie﴾.

* *

The saying of a group of the Companions and the Successors (tābiʿūn) was similar to this view, and reports were transmitted with it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). [[In the printed edition: "and it came with it," and I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

Those who said this:

16995. Abū al-Sāʾib related to us, saying: Abū Muʿāwiyah related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿUmārah, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, who said: ʿAbd Allāh (Ibn Masʿūd) said: "Judge the hypocrite by three: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he makes a covenant he betrays," and Allah revealed the confirmation of this in His Book: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty"﴾, to His saying: ﴿lie﴾. [[The report 16995: "ʿUmārah" is "ʿUmārah ibn ʿUmayr al-Taymī," reliable, related from by the group, passed as numbers 3294, 5789, 15359.
And "ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd al-Nakhaʿī," a reliable Successor, related from by the group. Passed as numbers 3294, 3295, 3299.
And "ʿAbd Allāh" means "ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd."
This report has a sound chain, halted at Ibn Masʿūd, and I did not find it raised to the Prophet from him. Al-Haythamī mentioned it in Majmaʿ al-Zawāʾid 1: 108, with this same wording, and said: "al-Ṭabarānī related it in al-Kabīr, and its narrators are the narrators of the Ṣaḥīḥ." He mentioned before it a similar hadith: "from ʿAbd Allāh, meaning Ibn Masʿūd, from the Prophet (ﷺ)," without the verse, then said: "al-Bazzār related it, and its narrators are the narrators of the Ṣaḥīḥ."]]

16996. Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā related to me, saying: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar related to us, saying: Shuʿbah related to us, from Simāk, from Ṣabīḥ ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmayrah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, who said: "Three things, whoever has them is a hypocrite: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he is entrusted he betrays." He said: And he recited this verse: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty, we will surely give charity and we will surely be among the righteous"﴾, to the end of the verse. [[The report 16996: This report comes with another chain after it.

"Sabih ibn Abdullah ibn Umayrah" and "Sabih ibn Abdullah al-Absi" are the same person as the one that follows. Both appeared earlier under nos. 12741 and 12742. It was noted earlier that al-Bukhari included him in al-Kabir (2/2/319) under the name "Sabih ibn Abdullah," and in the isnad he is given the nisba "al-Absi." The annotator there noted that Ibn Makula has "Sabih ibn Abdullah ibn Umayr al-Taghlibi," whereas al-Tabari here has "Umayrah." I found nothing to favour either reading. Ibn Abi Hatim included him (2/1/449), and they did not mention any narration from "Abdullah ibn Amr." In the printed edition here it was "Abdullah ibn Umar," which I believe is an error, as the report that follows shows (see below).

My brother al-Sayyid Ahmad cited this report with this isnad in his commentary on the Musnad, under the Musnad of "Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As," no. 6879. He then said: "Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Firyabi narrated it in his Kitab Sifat al-Nifaq (pp. 50-51), from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, from Ghundar, from Shu'bah, from Simak ibn Harb, from Sabih ibn Abdullah, from Abdullah ibn Amr," and then he quoted the report in similar wording. Then he said: "This is a mawquf (companion-level) report, and its isnad is sound. It is a good corroboration for this hadith, since it is, in ruling, equivalent to a marfu' (prophetic) report. Sabih ibn Abdullah, with a damma on the sad, is a senior Tabi'i who met Uthman and Ali. al-Bukhari included him in al-Kabir (2/2/319) and mentioned no criticism of him."

The hadith in the Musnad is a marfu' hadith.

The hadith of the sign of the hypocrite was narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (al-Fath 1:83-84) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah and of Abdullah ibn Amr. Muslim narrated it in his Sahih (2:46-48) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr and of Abu Hurayrah.

16997. Ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: Abu Dawud told us, saying: Shu'bah told us, from Simak, who said: I heard Sabih ibn Abdullah al-Absi say: "I asked Abdullah ibn Amr about the hypocrite," and he related something similar.

[Report 16997: "Sabih ibn Abdullah al-Absi": see the preceding no. 16996. In the printed and manuscript editions it was "al-Qaysi," with a qaf and a ya; I corrected it from the sources and from the earlier nos. 12741 and 12742.]

16998. Muhammad ibn Ma'mar told me, saying: Abu Hisham al-Makhzumi told us, saying: Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad told us, saying: Uthman ibn Hakim told us, saying: I heard Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi say: "I used to hear that the hypocrite is recognised by three things: lying, breaking promises, and betrayal. I searched for them in the Book of Allah for a time and could not find them, then I found them in two places in the Book of Allah," [In the printed edition it reads "in two verses." I have kept what is in the manuscript, which in my view is correct, since the verses he mentions after this are three verses from Surat al-Tawbah and one from Surat al-Ahzab, making four. He must have meant "in two surahs of the Qur'an," or something close to that.] namely: His saying: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah﴾ up to ﴿and because they used to lie﴾, and His saying: ﴿Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth﴾ [Surat al-Ahzab: 72], this verse.

16999. Ibn Hamid... [no]

Correction: 16999. Al-Qasim ibn Bishr ibn Ma'ruf told me, saying: Shababah told us, saying: Muhammad al-Muhrim told us, saying: I heard al-Hasan say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever has three things in him is a hypocrite, even if he prays, fasts, and claims to be a Muslim: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he is entrusted he betrays." I said to al-Hasan: "O Abu Sa'id, if a man is owed a debt by me, and he meets me and demands it from me, and I do not have it, and I fear that he will imprison me and ruin me, so I promise him that I will pay it at the new moon, and I do not do so. Am I a hypocrite?" He said: "That is how the hadith came!" Then he related from Abdullah ibn Amr that his father, when death approached him, said: "Marry So-and-so, for I promised him that I would marry him. I will not meet Allah with a third of hypocrisy!" I said: "O Abu Sa'id, can a man be a third hypocrite and two-thirds believer?" He said: "That is how the hadith came." He said: "I went on pilgrimage and met Ata ibn Abi Rabah, and I told him the hadith I had heard from al-Hasan, and what I had said to him and what he had said to me. He said to me: 'Were you unable to say to him: Tell me about the brothers of Yusuf, peace be upon him. Did they not promise their father and break it, did they not speak to him and lie to him, did they not get entrusted and betray him? Were they hypocrites? Were they not prophets? Their father was a prophet, and their grandfather was a prophet?'" He said: "I said to Ata: 'O Abu Muhammad, tell me the origin of hypocrisy, and the origin of this hadith.' He said: 'Jabir ibn Abdullah told me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) only said this hadith about the hypocrites specifically, who spoke to the Prophet and lied to him, who were entrusted with his secret and betrayed it, and who promised him that they would go out with him on the campaign and then broke it.'" He said: "Abu Sufyan went out from Makkah, and Jibril came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'Abu Sufyan is at such-and-such a place.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said to his companions: 'Abu Sufyan is at such-and-such a place, so go out to him, and keep it secret.' He said: 'A man among the hypocrites wrote to him: "Muhammad intends to attack you, so take your precautions." So Allah revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not betray Allah and the Messenger or betray your trusts while you know﴾ [Surat al-Anfal: 27], and He revealed concerning the hypocrites: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty..."﴾ up to ﴿so He penalised them with hypocrisy in their hearts until the Day they meet Him, because they broke to Allah what they promised Him and because they used to lie﴾. When you meet al-Hasan, give him my greetings, and tell him the origin of this hadith and what I said to you.'" He said: "I came to al-Hasan and said: 'O Abu Sa'id, your brother Ata sends you greetings,' and I told him the hadith he had related and what he had said to me. Al-Hasan took my hand and raised it [In the printed edition it reads "fa-amalaha" (inclined it), which has no meaning at all. The manuscript has "fa-asalaha" without dots, and this is the correct reading. It is said: "the she-camel raised her tail" (shalat al-naqatu bi-dhanabiha wa-ashalathu), meaning lifted it; and "ashal al-hajar" or "shal bihi" or "shawalahu" means to lift it; and "shal al-sa'il bi-yadayhi" means when he raised his hands in asking with them.] and said: 'O people of Iraq, were you unable to be like this? He heard a hadith from me and did not accept it until he had derived its origin. Ata is right. That is how the hadith came, and this is about the hypocrites specifically.'"

[Report 16999: "al-Qasim ibn Bishr ibn Ahmad ibn Ma'ruf," the teacher of al-Tabari, who appeared earlier under nos. 10509 and 10531. "Shababah" is Shababah ibn Sawwar al-Fazari, from whom the whole group narrated; he appeared earlier under no. 12851 and before it. In the printed edition it read "Usamah," which reflects a failure to read the manuscript, and so it is a grave distortion. "Muhammad al-Muhrim" is Muhammad ibn Umar al-Muhrim, also called Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr al-Laythi, and he is munkar al-hadith (weak in narration). His condition was explained in detail earlier under no. 15922, along with the places where he is biographed. In the printed edition it read "Muhammad al-Makhrami," which differs from the manuscript without any basis or explanation, and it is an error. This report is extremely munkar. al-Bukhari pointed to it in al-Tarikh al-Kabir (1/1/248) in his biography of "Muhammad al-Muhrim," saying: "From Ata and al-Hasan. Munkar al-hadith: when he promises he breaks it. Shababah narrated from him," meaning this report.]

17000. Ya'qub told me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah told us, saying: Ya'qub informed us, from al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever has three things in him, even if he prays, fasts, and claims to be a Muslim, is a hypocrite." It was asked of him: "What are they, O Messenger of Allah?" The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "When he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he is entrusted he betrays."

17001. Al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Mubashshir told us, from al-Awza'i, from Harun ibn Riyab, from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Wa'il, that when death approached him he said: "So-and-so proposed to my daughter, and I had said to him something like a promise. By Allah, I will not meet Allah with a third of hypocrisy! I call you to witness that I have married her to him."

[Report 17001: "Mubashshir" is Mubashshir ibn Isma'il al-Halabi, trustworthy (thiqah), one of Ahmad's teachers, from whom the whole group narrated. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir (4/2/11), and Ibn Abi Hatim (4/1/343). In the printed edition it read "Maysarah," which is a faulty alteration, and in the manuscript it reads "Musir" without dots.
"Harun ibn Riyab al-Tamimi al-Usayyidi" was among the worshippers who concealed their asceticism. He was trustworthy. Ibn Hazm said: "al-Yaman, Harun, and Ali, the sons of Riyab: Harun was among the People of the Sunnah, al-Yaman was among the imams of the Khawarij, and Ali was among the imams of the Rafidah, and they were all hostile to one another!!" He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir (4/2/219), and Ibn Abi Hatim (4/2/89).
As for "Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Wa'il," this is unusual but sound, for it is "Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As ibn Wa'il." I do not know why it was done this way in the form of his name, unless something dropped out from the copyist's text.
Furthermore, the isnad in the printed edition was as follows: "al-Qasim told us, al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Maysarah told us." I have corrected "Maysarah" before it. As for "saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Juraij," the copyist of the manuscript wrote it, but he struck it through with pen strokes, meaning to delete it. The editor, however, did not know their convention for striking through text, so I have kept what he deleted.]

* *

Others said: The covenant which those hypocrites made with Allah was something they resolved in their hearts without speaking it.

Those who said this:

17002. Al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: I heard Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman al-Taymi say: "I boarded the sea, and a violent wind struck us, so some people among us vowed vows, and I made an intention but did not speak it. When I arrived at Basra, I asked my father Sulayman, and he said to me: 'O my son, fulfil it.'" [In the printed edition it read "fah bihi," which is used only at pause, and the correct form is "fi" as a single letter, the imperative of "wafa yafi" (to fulfil). I have kept what is in the manuscript.]

= Mu'tamir said: And Kahmas told us, from Sa'id ibn Thabit, concerning His saying: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah﴾, the verse, he said: "It is only something they resolved in their hearts without speaking it. Did you not hear His saying: ﴿Do they not know that Allah knows their secret and their private talk, and that Allah is the Knower of the unseen?﴾"

[Report 17002: "Kahmas ibn al-Hasan al-Tamimi," trustworthy, from whom the whole group narrated. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir (4/1/239), and Ibn Abi Hatim (3/2/170).
As for "Sa'id ibn Thabit," this is how it stands in the manuscript. I have not found any mention of him in the books of biography available to me, and I fear that a distortion may have entered the name.]

The commentary of Abu Ja'far, that is al-Tabari, on the verses (75–77) of Surah al-Tawbah (Part 1 of 2)

**On the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying:** ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty, we will surely give charity and we will surely be among the righteous." (75) But when He gave them of His bounty, they became stingy with it and turned away while refusing.(76) So He caused hypocrisy to follow in their hearts until the Day they meet Him, because they failed Allah in what they promised Him and because they used to lie.﴾ (77)

Abu Ja'far says: May His remembrance be exalted, He says: And among these hypocrites whose description I have told you, O Muhammad, ﴿those who made a covenant with Allah﴾, meaning: they gave a pledge to Allah [[See the explanation of "ʿāhada" earlier: p. 141, note 1, and the references there.]] ﴿"If He gives us of His bounty"﴾, meaning: If Allah gives us of His bounty, provides us with wealth and widens His provision for us [[See the explanation of "ātā" and "al-faḍl" in the earlier lexical indexes (ʾtā) and (faḍl).]] ﴿"we will surely give charity"﴾, meaning: we will surely bring out charity from that wealth which our Lord has provided us [[See the explanation of "al-taṣaddu"" earlier: 9:31, 37, 38.]] ﴿"and we will surely be among the righteous"﴾, meaning: and we will surely act within it, with their wealth, in the manner of the people of righteousness, by maintaining ties of kinship through it and spending it in the way of Allah. [[See the explanation of "al-ṣāliḥ" in the earlier lexical indexes (ṣalaḥa).]]

Allah, blessed and exalted, says: So Allah provided for them and gave them of His bounty. ﴿So when He gave them of His bounty, they became stingy with it﴾, meaning: by the bounty of Allah which He gave them, they did not give charity from it, they did not maintain ties of kinship with it, and they did not spend from it in the right of Allah. ﴿And turned away﴾, meaning: they turned their backs on the covenant they had made with Allah. [[See the explanation of "al-tawallī" earlier in the lexical indexes (wallā).]] ﴿While refusing﴾, meaning: from it. [[See the explanation of "al-iʿrāḍ" earlier: 13:463, note 6, and the references there, vol. 14 (24).]] ﴿So He caused﴾ Allah ﴿hypocrisy to follow in their hearts﴾, meaning: because of their stinginess with the right of Allah which He had made obligatory upon them in what He had given them of His bounty, and their failure to keep the promise they had made to Allah, and their breaking of His covenant in their hearts. [[See the explanation of "al-nifāq" earlier: p. 358, note 1, and the references there.]] ﴿Until the Day they meet Him, because they failed Allah in what they promised Him﴾, meaning: of charity and spending in His way. ﴿And because they used to lie﴾, meaning: in their statements, and He deprived them of repentance from it. For He, may His praise be exalted, made the condition of their hypocrisy that He would cause it to follow them until the Day they meet Him, and that is the day of their death and their departure from this world.

* *

The people of interpretation (ahl al-taʾwīl) differed concerning the intended meaning of this verse.

Some of them said: It refers to a man called "Thaʿlabah ibn Ḥāṭib", from the Anṣār. [[In the manuscript, the text stops at his saying "called", and does not mention the man's name. The first editor inferred it from the reports, and he was correct in what he did.]]

Those who said this:

16986. Muḥammad ibn Saʿd said: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His saying: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty"﴾, to the end of the verse. The reason was that a man called "Thaʿlabah ibn Ḥāṭib", from the Anṣār, came to a gathering and called them to witness, saying: "If Allah gives me of His bounty, I will give every person with a right his right, and I will give charity from it, and I will maintain ties of kinship with it!" Then Allah tested him and gave him of His bounty, so he broke the promise Allah had made him, and angered Allah by breaking what He had promised. So Allah related his story in the Qur'an: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah﴾, the verse, to His saying: ﴿lie﴾.

16987. Al-Muthannā related to me, saying: Hishām ibn ʿAmmār related to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Shuʿayb related to us, saying: Maʿān ibn Rifāʿah al-Sulamī related to us, from Abū ʿAbd al-Malik ʿAlī ibn Yazīd al-Ilhānī: that he informed him from al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān: that he informed him from Abū Umāmah al-Bāhilī, from Thaʿlabah ibn Ḥāṭib al-Anṣārī, that he said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Ask Allah to provide me with wealth!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Woe to you, O Thaʿlabah! A little that you can thank for is better than a lot that you cannot bear!" He said: Then he asked again, and he said: "Are you not content to be like the Prophet of Allah? By Him in whose hand is my soul, if I wished, mountains would move with me as gold and silver!" He said: "By He who sent you with truth, if you invoke Allah and He provides me with wealth, I will surely give every person with a right his right!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, provide Thaʿlabah with wealth!" He said: So he acquired sheep, and they multiplied as worms multiply, and the city became too tight for him, so he withdrew from it and settled in one of its valleys, until he began praying Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr in congregation and abandoned everything else. Then they multiplied and increased, and he withdrew until he gave up prayers except Friday, and they kept multiplying as worms multiply, until he gave up Friday too. He began meeting caravans on Friday, asking them for news. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "What has Thaʿlabah done?" They said: "O Messenger of Allah, he acquired sheep and the city became too tight for him!" They informed him of his affair. He said: "Woe to Thaʿlabah! Woe to Thaʿlabah! Woe to Thaʿlabah!" He said: And Allah revealed: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity﴾ [Sūrat al-Tawbah: 103], the verse, and the obligatory charity rules were revealed to him. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent two men to collect the charity, a man from Juhaynah and a man from Sulaym, and he wrote for them how they should take charity from the Muslims. He said to them: "Pass by Thaʿlabah, and so-and-so, a man from Banū Sulaym, and take their charities!" So they set out until they came to Thaʿlabah, and asked him for the charity, and they read to him the letter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: "This is nothing but jizyah! This is nothing but the sister of jizyah! I do not know what this is! Go until you are free, then come back to me." So they left, and the Sulamī heard of them, so he looked at the best of his camels' ages, separated them for charity, and then met them with them. When they saw them they said: "This is not obligatory upon you, and we do not want to take this from you." He said: "Yes, take it, for my soul is content with that, and it is mine!" So they took it from him. When they finished their collection they returned, until they passed by Thaʿlabah, and he said: "Show me your letter!" He looked into it and said: "This is nothing but the sister of jizyah! Go until I see my opinion." So they left until they came to the Prophet (ﷺ). When he saw them, he said, before speaking to them: "Woe to Thaʿlabah!" He invoked blessing for the Sulamī, and they informed him of what Thaʿlabah had done and what the Sulamī had done. Then Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed concerning him: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty, we will surely give charity and we will surely be among the righteous"﴾, to His saying: ﴿And because they used to lie﴾. A man from Thaʿlabah's relatives was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he heard that, so he went out until he came to him and said: "Woe to you, O Thaʿlabah! Allah has revealed such-and-such concerning you!" So Thaʿlabah went out until he came to the Prophet (ﷺ), and asked him to accept his charity. He said: "Allah has forbidden me to accept your charity from you!" So he began throwing dust on his head. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "This is your deed! I commanded you and you did not obey me!" When he refused, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was taken [in death], and he returned to his home. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) died and did not accept anything from him. Then he came to Abū Bakr when he was appointed caliph, and said: "You know my standing with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and my position among the Anṣār, so accept my charity!" Abū Bakr said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not accept it, and I will accept it?" Then Abū Bakr died without having accepted it. When ʿUmar became caliph, he came to him and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, accept my charity!" He said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not accept it, nor did Abū Bakr, and I will accept it from you?" Then he died without accepting it. Then ʿUthmān, may Allah have mercy on him, became caliph, and he came to him and asked him to accept his charity. He said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not accept it, nor did Abū Bakr, nor ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, and I will accept it from you!" [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "and I do not accept it," and the correct reading is to omit "not" as stated in the statements of Abū Bakr and ʿUmar. This matches what is in Usd al-Ghābah.]] So he did not accept it from him. Thaʿlabah died during the caliphate of ʿUthmān, may Allah have mercy on him. [[The report 16987: "Hishām ibn ʿAmmār ibn Nuṣayr al-Sulamī," reliable; al-Bukhārī, Abū Dāwūd, al-Nasāʾī and Ibn Mājah related from him. They criticised him, saying: when he grew old, he changed. It passed as number 11108. And "Muḥammad ibn Shuʿayb ibn Shābūr al-Umawī" is reliable, it passed as number 16987.
And "Maʿān ibn Rifāʿah al-Sulamī," or "al-Salāmī," which is the more well known, is weak in narration; his narrations are written down but not used as evidence. He is mentioned in al-Tahdhīb and al-Kabīr 4/2/70, and in one of its copies it reads "al-Sulamī" as in al-Ṭabarī, so I left it as it is; and Ibn Abī Ḥātim.
And "ʿAlī ibn Yazīd al-Alhānī," "Abū ʿAbd al-Malik," is extremely weak; he related from al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, the companion of Abū Umāmah, a large collection, and these narrations of his are all weak. It passed as number 11525.
And "al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Shāmī," his reliability has been explained earlier, and what is rejected from him came only from the weak narrators who related from him. It passed as numbers 1939, 11525.
As for Thaʿlabah ibn Ḥāṭib al-Anṣārī, there is much confusion in his biography. Is he one man or two? The first of them is the one whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made a brother-bond between him and Muʿattib ibn al-Ḥamrāʾ, and who witnessed Badr and Uḥud. The other is the subject of this story. It is said that the first was killed at Uḥud. Some considered them one man and denied that he was killed at Uḥud. See his biography in al-Iṣābah, al-Istīʿāb: 78, Usd al-Ghābah 1: 237, and Ibn Saʿd: 3/2/32.
This report was related with this chain by Ibn al-Athīr in Usd al-Ghābah 1: 237, 238, and al-Haythamī cited it in Majmaʿ al-Zawāʾid 7: 21, 32, and said: "al-Ṭabarānī related it, and in it is ʿAlī ibn Yazīd al-Alhānī, who is abandoned."
It is extremely weak, has no supporting report from another source, and some of its narrators are severely weak.
This report was also cited by al-Suyūṭī in al-Durr al-Manthūr 3: 260, attributing it to al-Ḥasan ibn Sufyān, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, Abū al-Shaykh, al-ʿAskarī in al-Amthāl, al-Ṭabarānī, Ibn Mandah, al-Bārūdī, Abū Nuʿaym in Maʿrifat al-Ṣaḥābah, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Bayhaqī in al-Dalāʾil, and Ibn ʿAsākir.]]

16988. Bishr related to us, saying: Yazīd related to us, saying: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah regarding His saying: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty"﴾, the verse: It was mentioned to us that a man from the Anṣār came to a gathering of the Anṣār and said: "If Allah gives me wealth, I will surely pay every person with a right his right!" Then Allah gave him wealth, and he did with it what you have heard. He said: ﴿So when He gave them of His bounty, they became stingy with it﴾, to His saying: ﴿And because they used to lie﴾. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) related that when Mūsā (peace be upon him) brought the Torah to the Children of Israel, the Children of Israel said: "The Torah is large, and we do not have free time for it, so ask your Lord for us a set of matters we can keep and by which we can be free for our livelihood!" He said: "O people, wait, wait! This is the Book of Allah, the light of Allah, and the safeguard of Allah!" He said: They repeated it to him, and he repeated to them, saying it three times. He said: Then Allah revealed to Mūsā: "What are My servants saying?" He said: "O Lord, they say: such-and-such." He said: "I command them with three things: if they keep them, they will enter Paradise by them: that they come to the division of inheritance and not wrong in it, that they not let their eyes enter houses until permission is given to them, and that they not eat food until they perform ablution like the ablution for prayer." He said: The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) returned with them to his people, and they rejoiced and thought they would uphold them. He said: By Allah, the people did not remain long before they veered away and were cut off from them. When the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) related this story of the Children of Israel, he said: "Take on for me six, and I will take on for you Paradise!" They said: "What are they, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "When you speak, do not lie; when you promise, do not break it; when you are entrusted, do not betray; and restrain your eyes, your hands and your private parts: your eyes from betrayal, your hands from theft, and your private parts from fornication."

16989. Bishr related to us, saying: Yazīd related to us, saying: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah, from al-Ḥasan: that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say: "Three things, whoever has them is a hypocrite, even if he fasts and prays and claims he is a Muslim: when he speaks he lies, when he is entrusted he betrays, and when he promises he breaks it."

* *

Others said: Rather, the one intended by it is two men: one of them is Thaʿlabah, and the other is Muʿattib ibn Qushayr.

Those who said this:

16990. Ibn Ḥumayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Isḥāq, from ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd, from al-Ḥasan: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty"﴾, the verse, [[In the printed edition it read: "of His bounty, to the other," which is very strange; in the manuscript: "of His bounty the other," and the correct reading of it is what I have recorded; the copyist erred as is his habit.]] and those among them who made a covenant with Allah were Thaʿlabah ibn Ḥāṭib and Muʿattib ibn Qushayr, and both were from Banū ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf. [[The report 16990: Sīrat Ibn Hishām 4: 196, and it is a continuation of the earlier report number 16969.]]

Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim related to us, saying: ʿĪsā related to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty"﴾, he said: Two men went out before a seated assembly and said: "By Allah, if Allah provides us, we will surely give charity!" When He provided them, they became stingy with it.

16992. Al-Muthannā related to me, saying: Abū Ḥudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty"﴾: two men went out before a seated assembly and said: "By Allah, if Allah provides us, we will surely give charity!" When He provided them, they became stingy with it, = ﴿So He caused hypocrisy to follow in their hearts because they failed Allah in what they promised Him﴾, when they said: "We will surely give charity," and they did not do it.

16993. Al-Muthannā related to me, saying: Isḥāq related to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh related to us, from Warqāʾ, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, similarly.

16994. Yūnus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty"﴾, the verse: These are a category of hypocrites. When He gave them that, they became stingy with it, and when they became stingy with it, He caused hypocrisy to follow them because of it until the Day they meet Him, and they have no repentance, no forgiveness, and no pardon from it, just as Iblīs was struck when He denied him repentance.

Abū Ja'far says: In this verse there is a clarification from Allah, blessed and exalted, about a sign of the people of hypocrisy, meaning in His saying: ﴿So He caused hypocrisy to follow in their hearts until the Day they meet Him, because they failed Allah in what they promised Him and because they used to lie﴾.

* *

The saying of a group of the Companions and the Successors (tābiʿūn) was similar to this view, and reports were transmitted with it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). [[In the printed edition: "and it came with it," and I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

Those who said this:

16995. Abū al-Sāʾib related to us, saying: Abū Muʿāwiyah related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿUmārah, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, who said: ʿAbd Allāh (Ibn Masʿūd) said: "Judge the hypocrite by three: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he makes a covenant he betrays," and Allah revealed the confirmation of this in His Book: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty"﴾, to His saying: ﴿lie﴾. [[The report 16995: "ʿUmārah" is "ʿUmārah ibn ʿUmayr al-Taymī," reliable, related from by the group, passed as numbers 3294, 5789, 15359.
And "ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd al-Nakhaʿī," a reliable Successor, related from by the group. Passed as numbers 3294, 3295, 3299.
And "ʿAbd Allāh" means "ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd."
This report has a sound chain, halted at Ibn Masʿūd, and I did not find it raised to the Prophet from him. Al-Haythamī mentioned it in Majmaʿ al-Zawāʾid 1: 108, with this same wording, and said: "al-Ṭabarānī related it in al-Kabīr, and its narrators are the narrators of the Ṣaḥīḥ." He mentioned before it a similar hadith: "from ʿAbd Allāh, meaning Ibn Masʿūd, from the Prophet (ﷺ)," without the verse, then said: "al-Bazzār related it, and its narrators are the narrators of the Ṣaḥīḥ."]]

16996. Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā related to me, saying: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar related to us, saying: Shuʿbah related to us, from Simāk, from Ṣabīḥ ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmayrah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, who said: "Three things, whoever has them is a hypocrite: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he is entrusted he betrays." He said: And he recited this verse: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty, we will surely give charity and we will surely be among the righteous"﴾, to the end of the verse. [[The report 16996: This report comes with another chain after it.

"Sabih ibn Abdullah ibn Umayrah" and "Sabih ibn Abdullah al-Absi" are the same person as the one that follows. Both appeared earlier under nos. 12741 and 12742. It was noted earlier that al-Bukhari included him in al-Kabir (2/2/319) under the name "Sabih ibn Abdullah," and in the isnad he is given the nisba "al-Absi." The annotator there noted that Ibn Makula has "Sabih ibn Abdullah ibn Umayr al-Taghlibi," whereas al-Tabari here has "Umayrah." I found nothing to favour either reading. Ibn Abi Hatim included him (2/1/449), and they did not mention any narration from "Abdullah ibn Amr." In the printed edition here it was "Abdullah ibn Umar," which I believe is an error, as the report that follows shows (see below).

My brother al-Sayyid Ahmad cited this report with this isnad in his commentary on the Musnad, under the Musnad of "Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As," no. 6879. He then said: "Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Firyabi narrated it in his Kitab Sifat al-Nifaq (pp. 50-51), from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, from Ghundar, from Shu'bah, from Simak ibn Harb, from Sabih ibn Abdullah, from Abdullah ibn Amr," and then he quoted the report in similar wording. Then he said: "This is a mawquf (companion-level) report, and its isnad is sound. It is a good corroboration for this hadith, since it is, in ruling, equivalent to a marfu' (prophetic) report. Sabih ibn Abdullah, with a damma on the sad, is a senior Tabi'i who met Uthman and Ali. al-Bukhari included him in al-Kabir (2/2/319) and mentioned no criticism of him."

The hadith in the Musnad is a marfu' hadith.

The hadith of the sign of the hypocrite was narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (al-Fath 1:83-84) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah and of Abdullah ibn Amr. Muslim narrated it in his Sahih (2:46-48) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr and of Abu Hurayrah.

16997. Ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: Abu Dawud told us, saying: Shu'bah told us, from Simak, who said: I heard Sabih ibn Abdullah al-Absi say: "I asked Abdullah ibn Amr about the hypocrite," and he related something similar.

[Report 16997: "Sabih ibn Abdullah al-Absi": see the preceding no. 16996. In the printed and manuscript editions it was "al-Qaysi," with a qaf and a ya; I corrected it from the sources and from the earlier nos. 12741 and 12742.]

16998. Muhammad ibn Ma'mar told me, saying: Abu Hisham al-Makhzumi told us, saying: Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad told us, saying: Uthman ibn Hakim told us, saying: I heard Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi say: "I used to hear that the hypocrite is recognised by three things: lying, breaking promises, and betrayal. I searched for them in the Book of Allah for a time and could not find them, then I found them in two places in the Book of Allah," [In the printed edition it reads "in two verses." I have kept what is in the manuscript, which in my view is correct, since the verses he mentions after this are three verses from Surat al-Tawbah and one from Surat al-Ahzab, making four. He must have meant "in two surahs of the Qur'an," or something close to that.] namely: His saying: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah﴾ up to ﴿and because they used to lie﴾, and His saying: ﴿Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth﴾ [Surat al-Ahzab: 72], this verse.

16999. Ibn Hamid... [no]

Correction: 16999. Al-Qasim ibn Bishr ibn Ma'ruf told me, saying: Shababah told us, saying: Muhammad al-Muhrim told us, saying: I heard al-Hasan say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever has three things in him is a hypocrite, even if he prays, fasts, and claims to be a Muslim: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he is entrusted he betrays." I said to al-Hasan: "O Abu Sa'id, if a man is owed a debt by me, and he meets me and demands it from me, and I do not have it, and I fear that he will imprison me and ruin me, so I promise him that I will pay it at the new moon, and I do not do so. Am I a hypocrite?" He said: "That is how the hadith came!" Then he related from Abdullah ibn Amr that his father, when death approached him, said: "Marry So-and-so, for I promised him that I would marry him. I will not meet Allah with a third of hypocrisy!" I said: "O Abu Sa'id, can a man be a third hypocrite and two-thirds believer?" He said: "That is how the hadith came." He said: "I went on pilgrimage and met Ata ibn Abi Rabah, and I told him the hadith I had heard from al-Hasan, and what I had said to him and what he had said to me. He said to me: 'Were you unable to say to him: Tell me about the brothers of Yusuf, peace be upon him. Did they not promise their father and break it, did they not speak to him and lie to him, did they not get entrusted and betray him? Were they hypocrites? Were they not prophets? Their father was a prophet, and their grandfather was a prophet?'" He said: "I said to Ata: 'O Abu Muhammad, tell me the origin of hypocrisy, and the origin of this hadith.' He said: 'Jabir ibn Abdullah told me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) only said this hadith about the hypocrites specifically, who spoke to the Prophet and lied to him, who were entrusted with his secret and betrayed it, and who promised him that they would go out with him on the campaign and then broke it.'" He said: "Abu Sufyan went out from Makkah, and Jibril came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'Abu Sufyan is at such-and-such a place.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said to his companions: 'Abu Sufyan is at such-and-such a place, so go out to him, and keep it secret.' He said: 'A man among the hypocrites wrote to him: "Muhammad intends to attack you, so take your precautions." So Allah revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not betray Allah and the Messenger or betray your trusts while you know﴾ [Surat al-Anfal: 27], and He revealed concerning the hypocrites: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty..."﴾ up to ﴿so He penalised them with hypocrisy in their hearts until the Day they meet Him, because they broke to Allah what they promised Him and because they used to lie﴾. When you meet al-Hasan, give him my greetings, and tell him the origin of this hadith and what I said to you.'" He said: "I came to al-Hasan and said: 'O Abu Sa'id, your brother Ata sends you greetings,' and I told him the hadith he had related and what he had said to me. Al-Hasan took my hand and raised it [In the printed edition it reads "fa-amalaha" (inclined it), which has no meaning at all. The manuscript has "fa-asalaha" without dots, and this is the correct reading. It is said: "the she-camel raised her tail" (shalat al-naqatu bi-dhanabiha wa-ashalathu), meaning lifted it; and "ashal al-hajar" or "shal bihi" or "shawalahu" means to lift it; and "shal al-sa'il bi-yadayhi" means when he raised his hands in asking with them.] and said: 'O people of Iraq, were you unable to be like this? He heard a hadith from me and did not accept it until he had derived its origin. Ata is right. That is how the hadith came, and this is about the hypocrites specifically.'"

[Report 16999: "al-Qasim ibn Bishr ibn Ahmad ibn Ma'ruf," the teacher of al-Tabari, who appeared earlier under nos. 10509 and 10531. "Shababah" is Shababah ibn Sawwar al-Fazari, from whom the whole group narrated; he appeared earlier under no. 12851 and before it. In the printed edition it read "Usamah," which reflects a failure to read the manuscript, and so it is a grave distortion. "Muhammad al-Muhrim" is Muhammad ibn Umar al-Muhrim, also called Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr al-Laythi, and he is munkar al-hadith (weak in narration). His condition was explained in detail earlier under no. 15922, along with the places where he is biographed. In the printed edition it read "Muhammad al-Makhrami," which differs from the manuscript without any basis or explanation, and it is an error. This report is extremely munkar. al-Bukhari pointed to it in al-Tarikh al-Kabir (1/1/248) in his biography of "Muhammad al-Muhrim," saying: "From Ata and al-Hasan. Munkar al-hadith: when he promises he breaks it. Shababah narrated from him," meaning this report.]

17000. Ya'qub told me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah told us, saying: Ya'qub informed us, from al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever has three things in him, even if he prays, fasts, and claims to be a Muslim, is a hypocrite." It was asked of him: "What are they, O Messenger of Allah?" The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "When he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he is entrusted he betrays."

17001. Al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Mubashshir told us, from al-Awza'i, from Harun ibn Riyab, from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Wa'il, that when death approached him he said: "So-and-so proposed to my daughter, and I had said to him something like a promise. By Allah, I will not meet Allah with a third of hypocrisy! I call you to witness that I have married her to him."

[Report 17001: "Mubashshir" is Mubashshir ibn Isma'il al-Halabi, trustworthy (thiqah), one of Ahmad's teachers, from whom the whole group narrated. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir (4/2/11), and Ibn Abi Hatim (4/1/343). In the printed edition it read "Maysarah," which is a faulty alteration, and in the manuscript it reads "Musir" without dots.
"Harun ibn Riyab al-Tamimi al-Usayyidi" was among the worshippers who concealed their asceticism. He was trustworthy. Ibn Hazm said: "al-Yaman, Harun, and Ali, the sons of Riyab: Harun was among the People of the Sunnah, al-Yaman was among the imams of the Khawarij, and Ali was among the imams of the Rafidah, and they were all hostile to one another!!" He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir (4/2/219), and Ibn Abi Hatim (4/2/89).
As for "Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Wa'il," this is unusual but sound, for it is "Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As ibn Wa'il." I do not know why it was done this way in the form of his name, unless something dropped out from the copyist's text.
Furthermore, the isnad in the printed edition was as follows: "al-Qasim told us, al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Maysarah told us." I have corrected "Maysarah" before it. As for "saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Juraij," the copyist of the manuscript wrote it, but he struck it through with pen strokes, meaning to delete it. The editor, however, did not know their convention for striking through text, so I have kept what he deleted.]

Others said: The covenant which those hypocrites made with Allah was something they resolved in their hearts without speaking it.

Those who said this:

17002. Al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: I heard Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman al-Taymi say: "I boarded the sea, and a violent wind struck us, so some people among us vowed vows, and I made an intention but did not speak it. When I arrived at Basra, I asked my father Sulayman, and he said to me: 'O my son, fulfil it.'" [In the printed edition it read "fah bihi," which is used only at pause, and the correct form is "fi" as a single letter, the imperative of "wafa yafi" (to fulfil). I have kept what is in the manuscript.]

= Mu'tamir said: And Kahmas told us, from Sa'id ibn Thabit, concerning His saying: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah﴾, the verse, he said: "It is only something they resolved in their hearts without speaking it. Did you not hear His saying: ﴿Do they not know that Allah knows their secret and their private talk, and that Allah is the Knower of the unseen?﴾"

[Report 17002: "Kahmas ibn al-Hasan al-Tamimi," trustworthy, from whom the whole group narrated. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir (4/1/239), and Ibn Abi Hatim (3/2/170).
As for "Sa'id ibn Thabit," this is how it stands in the manuscript. I have not found any mention of him in the books of biography available to me, and I fear that a distortion may have entered the name.]

**The Interpretation of His Words: ﴿Do they not know that Allah knows their secret and their private talk, and that Allah is the Knower of the unseen?﴾ (9:78)**

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Do these hypocrites, who disbelieve in Allah and His Messenger in secret while displaying faith in them openly to the people of faith, not know ﴿that Allah knows their secret﴾, which they conceal within themselves, of disbelief in Him and in His Messenger? ﴿And their private talk﴾, meaning: their private talk when they confer with one another, slandering Islam and its people and mentioning them in ways they should not be mentioned, so that they would fear Allah's punishment, that He might inflict it upon them, and His might, that He might strike them with it, for their disbelief in Allah and His Messenger and their disparagement of Islam and its people, so that they would desist from that and repent of it. ﴿And that Allah is the Knower of the unseen﴾: Do they not know that Allah knows what is hidden from the hearing, sight and senses of His creatures, of what their souls conceal, which does not appear on their outward limbs, and that this should restrain them from deceiving His friends with hypocrisy and lying, and deter them from concealing other than what they display and showing what is contrary to what they believe?[[See the explanation of "ʿAllām al-ghuyūb" (Knower of the unseen) in what has preceded, vol. 11, p. 238, note 1, and the references there.]]

* *

**The Interpretation of His Words: ﴿Those who find fault with those among the believers who give voluntarily to charity, and with those who find nothing to give except their effort, so they ridicule them—Allah will ridicule them, and for them is a painful punishment.﴾ (9:79)**

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Those who find fault with the volunteers among the believers in charity to the needy and the poor, with what Allah has not made obligatory upon them in their wealth, and who revile them for it, saying: "They only gave it out of showing off and seeking reputation, and they did not seek the face of Allah."[[See the explanation of "al-lamz" (fault-finding) in what has preceded, pp. 300–301.
And see the explanation of "al-taṭawwuʿ" (voluntary giving) in what has preceded, vol. 3, pp. 247 and 441, and its explanation will come shortly, pp. 392–393.]] And they find fault with those who have nothing to give in charity except their effort, which is their capacity, so they belittle them and say: "Allah has surely no need of this people's charity!"—mocking them. ﴿So they ridicule them—Allah will ridicule them.﴾

* *

We have already explained the nature of "Allah's mockery" toward whomever He mocks among His creatures, in another place, in a way that makes repeating it here unnecessary.[[The explanation of "sakhar" has not passed. Abu Ja'far meant the verse in Surat al-Baqara: "Allah mocks them" (2:15). See what has preceded, vol. 1, pp. 301–306.]]

* *

﴿And for them is a painful punishment﴾: meaning, for them from Allah on the Day of Resurrection is a punishment that is severe and painful.[[See the explanation of "alīm" (painful) in what has preceded in the indices of language, under the root (ʾ-l-m).]]

* *

It has been mentioned that those meant by His words ﴿the volunteers among the believers﴾ were ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf and ʿĀṣim ibn ʿAdī al-Anṣārī. And that those meant by His words ﴿those who find nothing except their effort﴾ was Abū ʿAqīl al-Arāshī, brother of Banū Unayf.

Those who said this:

17003. al-Muthanna told me, he said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ told us, he said: Muʿāwiya told me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His words: ﴿Those who find fault with the volunteers among the believers in charity﴾: He said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf came to the Prophet (ﷺ) with forty ounces of gold, and a man of the Anṣār came with a ṣāʿ of food. Some of the hypocrites said: "By Allah, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān has not brought what he brought except for show!" And they said: "If Allah and His Messenger were in need of this ṣāʿ!"

17004. Muḥammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said: my father told me, he said: my paternal uncle told me, he said: my father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His words: ﴿Those who find fault with the volunteers among the believers in charity, and those who find nothing except their effort﴾: That the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out to the people one day and called out among them: "Gather your charities!" So the people gathered their charities. Then a man came from among the last of them with a man[[In the printed edition: "min aḥwajihim bi-man min tamr," which differs from the manuscript to no purpose; "al-man" is a measure.]] of dates, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is a ṣāʿ of dates. I spent my night drawing water with a rope[[al-Jarīr is the rope; he meant that he was watering by means of a rope.]] until I earned two ṣāʿs of dates. I kept one and brought you the other." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded him to scatter it among the charities. Some men mocked him and said: "By Allah, Allah and His Messenger are surely in no need of this! What would they do with your ṣāʿ?" Then ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, a man of Quraysh from Banū Zuhra, said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Is there anyone left from among the people of these charities?" He said: "No!" ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf said: "I have a hundred ounces of gold for charity." ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said to him: "Are you mad?" He said: "There is no madness in me!" He said: "Then teach us what you said?"[[In the printed edition: "Do you know what you said?" In the manuscript: "Afaʿlamna mā qulta," which is the correct reading.]] He said: "Yes! My wealth is eight thousand: as for four thousand, I lend it to my Lord, and as for four thousand, it is mine!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "May Allah bless you in what you kept and in what you gave!" The hypocrites disliked this and said: "By Allah, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān has given his gift only for show!" And they were liars; he gave it only voluntarily. So Allah revealed His excuse for him and the excuse of his companion, the poor man who brought the ṣāʿ of dates, and Allah said in His Book: ﴿Those who find fault with the volunteers among the believers in charity﴾, the verse.

17005. Ibn Wakīʿ told us, he said: Abū Usāma told us, from Shibl, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid: ﴿Those who find fault with the volunteers among the believers﴾: He said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf came with the charity of his wealth, four thousand, and the hypocrites found fault with him and said: "He is showing off!" ﴿And those who find nothing except their effort﴾: He said: a man of the Anṣār who hired himself out for a ṣāʿ of dates, having nothing else, brought it, and they found fault with him and said: "Allah had no need of the ṣāʿ of this one!"

17006. Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, similarly.

17007. al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abū Ḥudhayfa told us, he said: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, similarly.

17008. Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda, regarding His words: ﴿Those who find fault with the volunteers among the believers﴾, the verse. He said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf came with half of his wealth, drawing near to Allah with it, and the hypocrites found fault with him and said: "He gave that only for show and reputation!" Then a poor man of the Muslims, called "Ḥabḥāb, Abū ʿAqīl,"[["Ḥabḥāb": Ibn Ḥajar mentioned it in al-Iṣāba under "Ḥabḥāb." Then he said: "It is rare with two b's, and the more well-known is with two th's (mithallatayn), and it will come." He did not mention it under "Ḥathḥāth," as his following comment indicates, but mentioned it under "Jathjāth" with j and th, earlier before it, and said there: "It is said he is the name of Abū ʿAqīl, the owner of the ṣāʿ; al-Suhaylī vouched for it following Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr, and others vouched with an unpointed ḥāʾ. Other things have been said about his name. His biography will come in the kunya section." However, al-Ḥāfiẓ Ibn Ḥajar said in Fatḥ al-Bārī 8:249: "al-Suhaylī mentioned that he saw it in the handwriting of some memorizers vowelled with two j's."
I did not find a vowelling of him in al-Istīʿāb of Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr, where he is biographed under "Abū ʿAqīl ṣāḥib al-ṣāʿ," p. 673, and in the printed edition of al-Istīʿāb it is with ḥāʾ and th, from the vowelling of its editor. In al-Suhaylī (al-Rawḍ al-Unuf 2:331): "Jathjāth," with j and th.
As for the author of Usd al-Ghāba, he biographed him under "Abū ʿAqīl, owner of the ṣāʿ" (5:257), without vowelling him, and it is distorted in the printed edition. But he included him under "Ḥabḥāb" (with ḥāʾ and bāʾ), and said: he is Abū ʿAqīl al-Anṣārī. Usd al-Ghāba 1:366.
Ibn Saʿd also biographed him in al-Ṭabaqāt 3/2/41 under "Banū Unayf ibn Jushm ibn ʿĀʾidh Allāh, of Balī, allies of Banū Jaḥjabā ibn Kalfa," and said: "Abū ʿAqīl, whose name is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Arāshī al-Unayfī," and did not mention the story of the ṣāʿ.
Moreover, al-Ḥāfiẓ Ibn Ḥajar, in Fatḥ al-Bārī 8:249, comprehensively covered the mention of "Abū ʿAqīl," and mentioned the disagreement about the owner of the ṣāʿ. This is its summary:
First: that he is "al-Ḥabjāb, Abū ʿAqīl," and he mentioned what al-Ṭabarī narrated here and in what will come, and what others narrated.
Second: that he is "Suhayl ibn Rāfiʿ," and his evidence for it is a report narrated by al-Ṭabarānī in al-Awsaṭ, through Saʿīd ibn ʿUthmān al-Balawī, "from his grandmother, the daughter of ʿAdī, that their mother ʿUmayra bint Suhayl ibn Rāfiʿ was the owner of the ṣāʿ whom the hypocrites found fault with," and Ibn al-Kalbī said likewise.
Third: through ʿIkrima: that he is "Rifāʿa ibn Suhayl ibn Rāfiʿ," and he said: "And in Abū Ḥātim's (narration) it is Rifāʿa ibn Saʿd," and it may be a scribal error, and it may be that the name of "Abū ʿAqīl" is "Suhayl" and his nickname "Ḥabḥāb"; or they are two Companions.
Fourth: among the Companions is "Abū ʿAqīl ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Thaʿlaba al-Balawī," a man of Badr, whom Mūsā ibn ʿUqba did not name, nor Ibn Isḥāq, and al-Wāqidī named him "ʿAbd al-Raḥmān." He said: he was martyred at Yamāma. He said: al-Ṭabarī's words indicate that he is the owner of the ṣāʿ in his view. Some later scholars followed him, but the first view is better.
Fifth: that he is "ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Samḥān"?? (thus it came).
Sixth: that the owner of the ṣāʿ is "Abū Khaythama": "ʿAbd Allāh ibn Khushayma, of Banū Sālim, from the Anṣār," and his evidence is what came in the hadith of the repentance of Kaʿb ibn Mālik. See the report no. 17016.
Seventh: from al-Wāqidī that the owner of the ṣāʿ is "ʿUlayya ibn Zayd al-Muḥāribī."
Al-Ḥāfiẓ said: "This indicates a multiplicity of those who brought the ṣāʿ."
This is a severe disagreement, requiring considerable verification and review; I have noted it here so that it may serve as a reminder to whoever wishes to follow it up and verify it.]] said: "O Prophet of Allah, I spent the night drawing the rope for two ṣāʿs of dates. As for one ṣāʿ, I have kept it for my family, and as for one ṣāʿ, here it is!" The hypocrites said: "By Allah, Allah and His Messenger are surely in no need of this!" So Allah revealed the Qur'an concerning that: ﴿Those who find fault﴾, the verse.

17009. Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Muḥammad ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda: ﴿Those who find fault with the volunteers among the believers in charity﴾: He said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf gave in charity half of his wealth, and his wealth was eight thousand dinars, so he gave four thousand dinars in charity. Some people among the hypocrites said: "ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf is greatly showing off!" Then Allah said: ﴿Those who find fault with the volunteers among the believers in charity﴾. And a man had two ṣāʿs of dates; he brought one of them, and some of the hypocrites said: "If Allah is in need of this ṣāʿ!" The hypocrites used to belittle them and mock them, so Allah said: ﴿And those who find nothing except their effort, so they ridicule them—Allah will ridicule them, and for them is a painful punishment.﴾

17010. al-Muthanna told me, he said: al-Ḥajjāj ibn al-Minhāl al-Anmāṭī told us, he said: Abū ʿAwāna told us, from [ʿUmar ibn] Abī Salama, from his father: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Give in charity, for I intend to send out an expedition." He said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have four thousand: two thousand I lend to Allah, and two thousand for my dependents." He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "May Allah bless you in what you gave, and bless you in what you kept!" Then a man of the Anṣār said: "And I have two ṣāʿs of dates: one ṣāʿ for my Lord, and one ṣāʿ for my dependents!" He said: The hypocrites found fault and said: "Ibn ʿAwf gave this only for show!" And they said: "Did Allah not have need of this ṣāʿ?" So Allah revealed: ﴿Those who find fault with the volunteers among the believers﴾, to the end of the verse.[[The report 17010: "Abū ʿAwāna" is "al-Waḍḍāḥ ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Yashkurī," trustworthy, from whom the group narrated, passed as no. 4498, 10336, 10337.
And "ʿUmar ibn Abī Salama ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf" is considered weak, passed several times, the last being no. 12755. In the printed edition and the manuscript it was: "Abū ʿAwāna, from Abū Salama," which is an error beyond doubt; the correct form is from its chain in the Tafsīr of Ibn Kathīr, and from Majmaʿ al-Zawāʾid.
And his father "Abū Salama ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf" is trustworthy, from whom the group narrated, passed several times, the last being no. 12822.
al-Haythamī cited it in Majmaʿ al-Zawāʾid 7:32, from Abū Salama and from Abū Hurayra, then said: "al-Bazzār narrated it through two routes: one connected from Abū Hurayra, and the other from Abū Salama as a mursal (disconnected). He said: We have not heard anyone trace it to the hadith of ʿUmar ibn Abī Salama except Ṭālūt ibn ʿAbbād. In it is ʿUmar ibn Abī Salama, whom al-ʿIjlī and Abū Khaythama and Ibn Ḥibbān declared trustworthy, and Shuʿba and others declared weak. The rest of their narrators are trustworthy."
And the hadith of al-Bazzār was narrated by Ibn Kathīr in his Tafsīr 4:212–213, and its chain is: "al-Ḥāfiẓ Abū Bakr al-Bazzār said: Ṭālūt ibn ʿAbbād told us, Abū ʿAwāna told us, from ʿUmar ibn Abī Salama, from his father, from Abū Hurayra," and he related the report. Then Ibn Kathīr said: "Then he narrated it from Abū Kāmil, from Abū ʿAwāna, from ʿUmar ibn Abī Salama, from his father, as a mursal. He said: No one traced it except Ṭālūt."]]

17011. al-Muthanna told me, he said: Isḥāq told us, he said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Saʿd told us, he said: Abū Jaʿfar informed us, from al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas, regarding His words: ﴿Those who find fault with the volunteers among the believers in charity﴾: He said: Severe hardship befell the people, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded them to give in charity. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān came with four hundred ounces, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, bless him in what he kept back." The hypocrites said: "ʿAbd al-Raḥmān has done this only for show and reputation!" He said: And a man came with a ṣāʿ of dates and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I hired myself out for two ṣāʿs; I took one ṣāʿ of them to my family, and came with a ṣāʿ of dates." The hypocrites said: "Allah is surely in no need of this ṣāʿ!" So Allah revealed this verse: ﴿And those who find nothing except their effort, so they ridicule them—Allah will ridicule them, and for them is a painful punishment.﴾[[The report 17011: "ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Saʿd" is "ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿd al-Dashtakī al-Rāzī," passed as no. 10666, 10855.]]

17012. Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Salama told us, from Ibn Isḥāq: ﴿Those who find fault with the volunteers among the believers in charity﴾, the verse. And the volunteers among the believers in charity were ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, who gave in charity four thousand dinars, and ʿĀṣim ibn ʿAdī, brother of Banū al-ʿAjlān,[[In the printed edition: "akhū Banī ʿAjlān," which is a faulty alteration.]] and that was because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) encouraged charity and urged it, so ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf stood up and gave four thousand dirhams in charity, and ʿĀṣim ibn ʿAdī stood up and gave a hundred wasqs of dates in charity. They found fault with both of them and said: "This is only for show!" And the one who gave with his effort was Abū ʿAqīl, brother of Banū Unayf, al-Arāshī, an ally of Banū ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf,[[His saying: "al-Arāshī, ally of Banī ʿUmar ibn ʿAwf" is not in the printed edition of Ibn Hishām's Sīra; see the note preceding, p. 384, no. 1.]] who came with a ṣāʿ of dates and poured it into the charity, so they laughed at him and said: "Allah is surely in no need of Abū ʿAqīl's ṣāʿ!!" [[The report 17012: Sīrat Ibn Hishām 4:196, and it follows the earlier report no. 16990.]]

17013. Muḥammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abū al-Nuʿmān al-Ḥakam ibn ʿAbd Allāh told us, he said: Shuʿba told us, from Sulaymān, from Abū Wāʾil, from Abū Masʿūd, who said: When the verse of charity was revealed, we used to carry loads (nuḥāmil)[[His saying "nuḥāmil" is from "al-muḥāmala," and Ibn Ḥajar explained it in al-Fatḥ, saying: "That is, we carry loads on our backs for wages. It is said: ḥāmaltu, meaning ḥamaltu, like sāfartu. Al-Khaṭṭābī said: he means: we would exert ourselves to carry for wages, so as to earn what we give in charity. And the second narration after it supports this—meaning in al-Bukhārī—where he said: one of us went to the market and sought loads for hire (yuḥāmil)."]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 78–79 (part 2 of 2):

This is also clarified by the tafsir of Abu al-Nu'man with his words: "We used to work" — and this is, in my judgment, a tafsir rather than a different narration in the report.]] = Abu al-Nu'man said: "We used to work" = He said: A man came and gave a great deal in charity. And a man came and gave a sa' of dates in charity, and they said: "Surely Allah is not in need of this sa'!" So there was revealed: ﴿Those who find fault with those among the believers who give voluntarily in charity, and with those who find nothing to give except their effort﴾. [[The report: 17013 — "Abu al-Nu'man", "al-Hakam ibn Abd Allah al-Ansari", trustworthy (thiqah). al-Bukhari said: "His narration is well known; he had a good memory." He has no narration in Sahih al-Bukhari other than this hadith. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.
And "Abu Mas'ud" is "Abu Mas'ud al-Ansari al-Badri", whose name is "Uqbah ibn Amr ibn Tha'labah", a companion of the Messenger of Allah, who witnessed al-'Aqabah. In the manuscript it read: "from Ibn Mas'ud", which is a plain error.
This report was narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (al-Fath 3: 224) through the chain of Ubayd Allah ibn Sa'id, from Abu al-Nu'man al-Hakam ibn Abd Allah al-Basri, with the like of it, and in it there is an addition after his words "a great deal", namely: "So they said: 'He is showing off.'"
Then al-Bukhari also narrated it in his Sahih (al-Fath 8: 249) through the chain of Bishr ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Shu'bah, from Sulayman, from Abu Wa'il, from Abu Mas'ud, with a wording other than this, and in it there is explicit mention of the name "Abu 'Aqil" who brought half a sa'. Muslim also narrated it in his Sahih 7: 105 by this route. See further p. 389, note 1.]]
17014 — Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Zayd ibn Hubab narrated to us, from Musa ibn Ubaydah, who said: Khalid ibn Yasar narrated to me, from Ibn Abi 'Aqil, from his father, who said: I spent the night hauling a rope ("al-jarir": the rope, its explanation was given earlier, p. 383, note 2) on my back for two sa's of dates. I returned with one of them to my family, that they might subsist on it [("tabalagha bi-ba'd al-ta'am": he was satisfied with it from its abundance, until it sufficed him)], and I brought the other, seeking nearness to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ [("qawluhu 'ila rasul Allah' is connected to his words 'ji'tu' not to 'ataqarrabu bihi'": i.e., I brought it to the Messenger of Allah, seeking nearness to Allah through it)]. I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and informed him, and he said: "Scatter it in the charity." The hypocrites mocked him and said: "Surely Allah was not in need of the charity of this poor man!" So Allah revealed: ﴿Those who find fault with those among the believers who give voluntarily in charity﴾, the two verses. [[The report: 17014 — "Musa ibn Ubaydah ibn Nashit al-Rabadhi", extremely weak; narrating from him is not permissible, as Ahmad said. It has passed many times, the last being no. 11811.
As for "Khalid ibn Yasar", who narrated from Ibn Abi 'Aqil and from whom Musa ibn Ubaydah narrated, I have found no biography or mention of him. There is another "Khalid ibn Yasar" who narrated from Abu Hurayrah, from whom Shu'ayb ibn al-Hubhab narrated, but I do not think he is the same; and this one too they called unknown (majhul).
As for "Ibn Abi 'Aqil", his name is "Ridha ibn Abi 'Aqil", biographed in al-Kabir 2/1/313 and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/523, who said: "He narrated from his father, and narrated from Muhammad ibn Fudayl," and no criticism is mentioned of him.
As for "Abu 'Aqil", whose mention has passed, he is biographed in al-Kuna of al-Bukhari: 62, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/416, who said: his son Ridha ibn Abi 'Aqil narrated from him.
This report is extremely weak in its chain, due to the weakness of Musa ibn Ubaydah and the unknown narrator in it, Khalid ibn Yasar.
However, al-Haythami in Majma' al-Zawa'id 7: 32, 33, narrated this report with nearly its wording, then said: "al-Tabarani narrated it, and its narrators are trustworthy, except Khalid ibn Yasar, for I have found no one who authenticated him or criticized him." I do not know whether al-Tabarani's chain had anyone other than Musa ibn Ubaydah narrating from Khalid ibn Yasar, or whether Musa ibn Ubaydah himself is the transmitter. If Musa is the transmitter, then it has been said many times that al-Haythami deemed him weak. And it appears to be from Musa's narration, for I saw Ibn Kathir in his tafsir 4: 213 quote this report from al-Tabari, then say: "Likewise al-Tabarani narrated it from the hadith of Zayd ibn al-Hubab, with it. And he said: the name of Abu 'Aqil is Hubab (Hubhab), and it is said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Tha'labah" (see p. 383, note 2). This indicates that in al-Tabarani's chain is "Musa ibn Ubaydah", who is extremely weak.]]
17015 — Yaqub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: al-Jurayri informed us, from Abu al-Sulayl, who said: A man stood over the people [in the Musnad: "a man stood over us in our gathering at al-Baqi'", and the wording of the report differs afterwards], and said: My father or my uncle narrated to me, saying: I witnessed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saying: "Who will give charity today, that I may testify for him before Allah on the Day of Resurrection?" He said: And I had a turban on me. He said: So I removed one or two lengths of it, to give them in charity. [("laatha al-'imamah 'ala ra'sihi, yulawwiduha": he wrapped, rolled and turned it, i.e., bound it. "al-lawth" is a fold of the folds of the turban.)] He said: Then there came upon me what comes upon the son of Adam, so I bound my head with it. He said: Then came a man, and I did not see at al-Baqi' a man shorter in stature ["al-qimmah" with a kasra is the stature of a person when standing; this is the meaning here. "al-qimmah" also means the top of a person's head, which is not meant here.], nor blacker, nor uglier in his eye than him [In the printed edition: "wa la adhamm li'aynih minhu", which is corrupt, differing from the manuscript. This sentence in the Musnad of Ahmad is distorted: "wa la adam yu'ayyir bi-naqah", and in Ibn Kathir's tafsir quoting the Musnad: "wa la adhamm bi-ba'ir sa'ahu", which adds further distortion. The correct reading is that of Tabari's tafsir. "wa la adam" from "al-damamah": "damma al-rajul yadumm damamah", meaning shortness and ugliness. In the hadith of Ibn Umar: "Let none of you marry his daughter to one who is ugly (damim)."], leading a camel, and I did not see at al-Baqi' a camel better or more beautiful than it. He said: "Is it charity, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes!" He said: "Then take it!" ["dunakaha": i.e., take it.] So he let go its halter — or its lead rope [In the manuscript: "fa-alqa Allah bi-khatamiha aw bi-zimamiha", which is a clear error; the correct reading is what is recorded. But the editor of the printed edition omitted it and wrote: "fa-alqa bi-khatamiha."] = He said: A man sitting there mocked him, and said: "By Allah, he is giving it in charity, and it is better than him!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked at him and said: "Rather, he is better than you and it!" [In the printed and manuscript editions: "yaqulu dhalika nabiyyuna ﷺ", which is a scribal distortion; the correct reading is what is recorded, for he saw in the copy from which we transcribed: "yaqulu dhalika thalathan" and read it as "nabiyyuna"; the correct reading is "thalathan", as they used to write it with the alif omitted. I deduce this from the hadith in the Musnad of Ahmad, which says: "three times."] He said that three times. (ﷺ). [The report: 17015 — "Abu al-Sulayl" is "Dariyb ibn Nufayr ibn Samir al-Qaysi al-Jurayri", trustworthy. He narrated from Sa'id al-Jurayri and others. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 2/2/343, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/470.
This report was narrated by Ahmad in the Musnad 5: 34, and quoted by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir 4: 211, 212, with additions and variation in some of its wording, as I indicated above in the notes.]]
17016 — Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik informed me, saying: The one who gave a sa' of dates in charity, whom the hypocrites found fault with, was "Abu Khaythamah al-Ansari". [The report: 17016 — "Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik al-Ansari", trustworthy. It has passed under no. 16147. See what preceded at vol. 13: 567, note 1.]
17017 — al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Raja' Abu Sahl al-Abbadani narrated to us, saying: Amir ibn Yasaf al-Yamami narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir al-Yamami, who said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf came with four thousand dirhams to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, my wealth is eight thousand; I have brought you four thousand, so place it in the way of Allah, and I have kept four thousand for my dependants." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "May Allah bless what you gave and what you kept!" Some of the hypocrites said: "By Allah, Abd al-Rahman gave only for show and reputation, and surely Allah and His Messenger were in no need of the sa' of so-and-so!" So Allah revealed: ﴿Those who find fault with those among the believers who give voluntarily in charity﴾, meaning Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf: ﴿and with those who find nothing to give except their effort﴾, meaning the owner of the sa': ﴿they mock them; Allah will mock them, and for them is a painful punishment﴾. [The report: 17017 — "Muhammad ibn Raja' Abu Sahl al-Abbadani": I have found no biography of him among the references available to me.
As for "Amir ibn Yasaf al-Yamami", namely "Amir ibn Abd Allah ibn Yasaf", Ibn Ma'in and others authenticated him, and Ibn 'Adi said: "He is reprehensible in narrating from the trustworthy.
