Ibn Kathir: al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: Ibn Abbas said: The Prophet ﷺ commanded the Muslims to gather their charities, and behold, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf came with four thousand, and said: "This is my wealth, which I lend to Allah, and there remains for me the like of it." He said to him: "May it be blessed for you in what you gave and what you kept!" The hypocrites said: "He gave only for show; and the owner of the sa' gave only for show. Surely Allah and His Messenger were in need of nothing from this! And what can Allah do with a sa' of something?"
17019 — Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: ﴿Those who find fault with those among the believers who give voluntarily in charity﴾, up to His words: ﴿and for them is a painful punishment﴾: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, commanded the Muslims to give charity, and Umar ibn al-Khattab stood up: he found that matter by chance, my wealth abundant, so I will take half of it. [In the printed edition: "Umar ibn al-Khattab stood, and found wealth abundant, and took half of it", which misreads the manuscript, distorting, altering and omitting, and doing great harm by what it did. Rather, this is Umar's own statement, saying: he found this matter by chance, my wealth abundant, so I will take half of it.]
He said: So I came bearing a great deal of wealth. A man among the hypocrites said to him: "Showing off, O Umar!" He said: "Yes, I show off to Allah and His Messenger; as for others, no!" And a man from the Ansar, who had nothing, hired himself out to haul a rope over his neck for two sa's for the night, so he left one sa' for his dependants and came with one sa' carrying it. A man among the hypocrites said to him: "Surely Allah and His Messenger are in need of your sa'!" So that is the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿Those who find fault with those among the believers who give voluntarily in charity, and with those who find nothing to give except their effort﴾ — this is the Ansari — ﴿they mock them; Allah will mock them, and for them is a painful punishment﴾.
* *
We have already explained the meaning of "al-lamz" (finding fault) in the speech of the Arabs, with its evidence, and what it involves of language and recitation, previously. [See the explanation of "al-lamz" above, pp. 300, 301, 382.]
* *
As for His words ﴿al-mutawwi'in﴾, its meaning is "al-mutatawwi'in", the ta' was assimilated into the ta', becoming a doubled ta', as it is said: ﴿wa man yattawwa' khayran﴾ [Surat al-Baqarah: 158], [This reading was mentioned by Abu Ja'far earlier, 3: 247, and it is the reading of the common readers of Kufa.
As for our reading in our Mushaf today: (wa man tatawwa'a khayran).] meaning: "yatatawwa'" (volunteers). [See the explanation of "al-tatawwu'" earlier, 3: 247, 441; 14: 382, and see al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 447.]
* *
As for "al-juhd", the Arabs have two dialects regarding it. It is said: "a'taani min juhdih" with a dammah on the jim, and this, as reported, is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz; and "min jahdih" with a fathah on the jim, which is the dialect of Najd. [See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 447, Abu Ubaydah's Majaz al-Qur'an 1: 264, and what preceded at p. 382.]
The reading with the dammah is that of the common readers (al-amsar), and that is the preferred choice in our view, because of the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it.
As for the scholars of Arabic speech, the transmitters of poetry and the grammarians, they claim that the fathah and dammah have one meaning, and the difference is only due to differing dialect in it, just as their dialects differed regarding "al-wajd" and "al-wujd" with dammah and fathah, from "wajadtu". [See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 447, Abu Ubaydah's Majaz al-Qur'an 1: 264, and what preceded at p. 382.]

And it has been related from al-Sha'bi regarding this that:

[In the printed edition, the phrase "al-juhd, al-juhd" was omitted and replaced with "fa-al-jahd", "al-jahd", beginning the speech with it. I have restored what is in the manuscript.]

[In the printed edition: "wa al-juhd fi al-ma'ishah" ("in livelihood"), which misread the manuscript and altered it. "al-qut", "al-qaytah" (with a kasra on the qaf), and "al-qaytah" (with a kasra on the qaf) are all one, and mean the sustenance of provision, and what sustains the human body of food.]

**The Interpretation of His Words: ﴿Do they not know that Allah knows their secret and their private talk, and that Allah is the Knower of the unseen?﴾ (9:78)**

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Do these hypocrites, who disbelieve in Allah and His Messenger in secret while displaying faith in them openly to the people of faith, not know ﴿that Allah knows their secret﴾, which they conceal within themselves, of disbelief in Him and in His Messenger? ﴿And their private talk﴾, meaning: their private talk when they confer with one another, slandering Islam and its people and mentioning them in ways they should not be mentioned, so that they would fear Allah's punishment, that He might inflict it upon them, and His might, that He might strike them with it, for their disbelief in Allah and His Messenger and their disparagement of Islam and its people, so that they would desist from that and repent of it. ﴿And that Allah is the Knower of the unseen﴾: Do they not know that Allah knows what is hidden from the hearing, sight and senses of His creatures, of what their souls conceal, which does not appear on their outward limbs, and that this should restrain them from deceiving His friends with hypocrisy and lying, and deter them from concealing other than what they display and showing what is contrary to what they believe?[[See the explanation of "ʿAllām al-ghuyūb" (Knower of the unseen) in what has preceded, vol. 11, p. 238, note 1, and the references there.]]

* *

**The Interpretation of His Words: ﴿Those who find fault with those among the believers who give voluntarily to charity, and with those who find nothing to give except their effort, so they ridicule them—Allah will ridicule them, and for them is a painful punishment.﴾ (9:79)**

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Those who find fault with the volunteers among the believers in charity to the needy and the poor, with what Allah has not made obligatory upon them in their wealth, and who revile them for it, saying: "They only gave it out of showing off and seeking reputation, and they did not seek the face of Allah."[[See the explanation of "al-lamz" (fault-finding) in what has preceded, pp. 300–301.
And see the explanation of "al-taṭawwuʿ" (voluntary giving) in what has preceded, vol. 3, pp. 247 and 441, and its explanation will come shortly, pp. 392–393.]] And they find fault with those who have nothing to give in charity except their effort, which is their capacity, so they belittle them and say: "Allah has surely no need of this people's charity!"—mocking them. ﴿So they ridicule them—Allah will ridicule them.﴾

* *

We have already explained the nature of "Allah's mockery" toward whomever He mocks among His creatures, in another place, in a way that makes repeating it here unnecessary.[[The explanation of "sakhar" has not passed. Abu Ja'far meant the verse in Surat al-Baqara: "Allah mocks them" (2:15). See what has preceded, vol. 1, pp. 301–306.]]

* *

﴿And for them is a painful punishment﴾: meaning, for them from Allah on the Day of Resurrection is a punishment that is severe and painful.[[See the explanation of "alīm" (painful) in what has preceded in the indices of language, under the root (ʾ-l-m).]]

* *

It has been mentioned that those meant by His words ﴿the volunteers among the believers﴾ were ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf and ʿĀṣim ibn ʿAdī al-Anṣārī. And that those meant by His words ﴿those who find nothing except their effort﴾ was Abū ʿAqīl al-Arāshī, brother of Banū Unayf.

He has no narration in Sahih al-Bukhari other than this hadith. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.
And "Abu Mas'ud" is "Abu Mas'ud al-Ansari al-Badri", whose name is "Uqbah ibn Amr ibn Tha'labah", a companion of the Messenger of Allah, who witnessed al-'Aqabah. In the manuscript it read: "from Ibn Mas'ud", which is a plain error.
This report was narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (al-Fath 3: 224) through the chain of Ubayd Allah ibn Sa'id, from Abu al-Nu'man al-Hakam ibn Abd Allah al-Basri, with the like of it, and in it there is an addition after his words "a great deal", namely: "So they said: 'He is showing off.'"
Then al-Bukhari also narrated it in his Sahih (al-Fath 8: 249) through the chain of Bishr ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Shu'bah, from Sulayman, from Abu Wa'il, from Abu Mas'ud, with a wording other than this, and in it there is explicit mention of the name "Abu 'Aqil" who brought half a sa'. Muslim also narrated it in his Sahih 7: 105 by this route. See further p. 389, note 1.]]
17014 — Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Zayd ibn Hubab narrated to us, from Musa ibn Ubaydah, who said: Khalid ibn Yasar narrated to me, from Ibn Abi 'Aqil, from his father, who said: I spent the night hauling a rope ("al-jarir": the rope, its explanation was given earlier, p. 383, note 2) on my back for two sa's of dates. I returned with one of them to my family, that they might subsist on it [("tabalagha bi-ba'd al-ta'am": he was satisfied with it from its abundance, until it sufficed him)], and I brought the other, seeking nearness to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ [("qawluhu 'ila rasul Allah' is connected to his words 'ji'tu' not to 'ataqarrabu bihi'": i.e., I brought it to the Messenger of Allah, seeking nearness to Allah through it)]. I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and informed him, and he said: "Scatter it in the charity." The hypocrites mocked him and said: "Surely Allah was not in need of the charity of this poor man!" So Allah revealed: ﴿Those who find fault with those among the believers who give voluntarily in charity﴾, the two verses. [[The report: 17014 — "Musa ibn Ubaydah ibn Nashit al-Rabadhi", extremely weak; narrating from him is not permissible, as Ahmad said. It has passed many times, the last being no. 11811.
As for "Khalid ibn Yasar", who narrated from Ibn Abi 'Aqil and from whom Musa ibn Ubaydah narrated, I have found no biography or mention of him. There is another "Khalid ibn Yasar" who narrated from Abu Hurayrah, from whom Shu'ayb ibn al-Hubhab narrated, but I do not think he is the same; and this one too they called unknown (majhul).
As for "Ibn Abi 'Aqil", his name is "Ridha ibn Abi 'Aqil", biographed in al-Kabir 2/1/313 and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/523, who said: "He narrated from his father, and narrated from Muhammad ibn Fudayl," and no criticism is mentioned of him.
As for "Abu 'Aqil", whose mention has passed, he is biographed in al-Kuna of al-Bukhari: 62, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/416, who said: his son Ridha ibn Abi 'Aqil narrated from him.
This report is extremely weak in its chain, due to the weakness of Musa ibn Ubaydah and the unknown narrator in it, Khalid ibn Yasar.
However, al-Haythami in Majma' al-Zawa'id 7: 32, 33, narrated this report with nearly its wording, then said: "al-Tabarani narrated it, and its narrators are trustworthy, except Khalid ibn Yasar, for I have found no one who authenticated him or criticized him." I do not know whether al-Tabarani's chain had anyone other than Musa ibn Ubaydah narrating from Khalid ibn Yasar, or whether Musa ibn Ubaydah himself is the transmitter. If Musa is the transmitter, then it has been said many times that al-Haythami deemed him weak. And it appears to be from Musa's narration, for I saw Ibn Kathir in his tafsir 4: 213 quote this report from al-Tabari, then say: "Likewise al-Tabarani narrated it from the hadith of Zayd ibn al-Hubab, with it. And he said: the name of Abu 'Aqil is Hubab (Hubhab), and it is said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Tha'labah" (see p. 383, note 2). This indicates that in al-Tabarani's chain is "Musa ibn Ubaydah", who is extremely weak.]]
17015 — Yaqub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: al-Jurayri informed us, from Abu al-Sulayl, who said: A man stood over the people [in the Musnad: "a man stood over us in our gathering at al-Baqi'", and the wording of the report differs afterwards], and said: My father or my uncle narrated to me, saying: I witnessed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saying: "Who will give charity today, that I may testify for him before Allah on the Day of Resurrection?" He said: And I had a turban on me. He said: So I removed one or two lengths of it, to give them in charity. [("laatha al-'imamah 'ala ra'sihi, yulawwiduha": he wrapped, rolled and turned it, i.e., bound it. "al-lawth" is a fold of the folds of the turban.)] He said: Then there came upon me what comes upon the son of Adam, so I bound my head with it. He said: Then came a man, and I did not see at al-Baqi' a man shorter in stature ["al-qimmah" with a kasra is the stature of a person when standing; this is the meaning here. "al-qimmah" also means the top of a person's head, which is not meant here.], nor blacker, nor uglier in his eye than him [In the printed edition: "wa la adhamm li'aynih minhu", which is corrupt, differing from the manuscript. This sentence in the Musnad of Ahmad is distorted: "wa la adam yu'ayyir bi-naqah", and in Ibn Kathir's tafsir quoting the Musnad: "wa la adhamm bi-ba'ir sa'ahu", which adds further distortion. The correct reading is that of Tabari's tafsir. "wa la adam" from "al-damamah": "damma al-rajul yadumm damamah", meaning shortness and ugliness. In the hadith of Ibn Umar: "Let none of you marry his daughter to one who is ugly (damim)."], leading a camel, and I did not see at al-Baqi' a camel better or more beautiful than it. He said: "Is it charity, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes!" He said: "Then take it!" ["dunakaha": i.e., take it.] So he let go its halter — or its lead rope [In the manuscript: "fa-alqa Allah bi-khatamiha aw bi-zimamiha", which is a clear error; the correct reading is what is recorded. But the editor of the printed edition omitted it and wrote: "fa-alqa bi-khatamiha."] = He said: A man sitting there mocked him, and said: "By Allah, he is giving it in charity, and it is better than him!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked at him and said: "Rather, he is better than you and it!" [In the printed and manuscript editions: "yaqulu dhalika nabiyyuna ﷺ", which is a scribal distortion; the correct reading is what is recorded, for he saw in the copy from which we transcribed: "yaqulu dhalika thalathan" and read it as "nabiyyuna"; the correct reading is "thalathan", as they used to write it with the alif omitted. I deduce this from the hadith in the Musnad of Ahmad, which says: "three times."] He said that three times. (ﷺ). [The report: 17015 — "Abu al-Sulayl" is "Dariyb ibn Nufayr ibn Samir al-Qaysi al-Jurayri", trustworthy. He narrated from Sa'id al-Jurayri and others. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 2/2/343, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/470.
This report was narrated by Ahmad in the Musnad 5: 34, and quoted by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir 4: 211, 212, with additions and variation in some of its wording, as I indicated above in the notes.]]
17016 — Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik informed me, saying: The one who gave a sa' of dates in charity, whom the hypocrites found fault with, was "Abu Khaythamah al-Ansari". [The report: 17016 — "Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik al-Ansari", trustworthy. It has passed under no. 16147. See what preceded at vol. 13: 567, note 1.]
17017 — al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Raja' Abu Sahl al-Abbadani narrated to us, saying: Amir ibn Yasaf al-Yamami narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir al-Yamami, who said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf came with four thousand dirhams to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, my wealth is eight thousand; I have brought you four thousand, so place it in the way of Allah, and I have kept four thousand for my dependants." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "May Allah bless what you gave and what you kept!" Another man came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I spent the night hauling water on two sa's; as for one of them, I left it for my dependants, and as for the other, I have brought it to you; let me place it in the way of Allah." He said: "May Allah bless what you gave and what you kept!" Some of the hypocrites said: "By Allah, Abd al-Rahman gave only for show and reputation, and surely Allah and His Messenger were in no need of the sa' of so-and-so!" So Allah revealed: ﴿Those who find fault with those among the believers who give voluntarily in charity﴾, meaning Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf: ﴿and with those who find nothing to give except their effort﴾, meaning the owner of the sa': ﴿they mock them; Allah will mock them, and for them is a painful punishment﴾. [The report: 17017 — "Muhammad ibn Raja' Abu Sahl al-Abbadani": I have found no biography of him among the references available to me.
As for "Amir ibn Yasaf al-Yamami", namely "Amir ibn Abd Allah ibn Yasaf", Ibn Ma'in and others authenticated him, and Ibn 'Adi said: "He is reprehensible in narrating from the trustworthy. Despite his weakness, his hadith is written." He is biographed in Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/329, Mizan al-I'tidal 2: 7, Ta'jil al-Manfa'ah: 206, and Lisan al-Mizan 3: 224.
As for "Yahya ibn Abi Kathir al-Yamami", he is trustworthy; the collectors all narrated from him. He has passed many times, the last being no. 12760.]]
17018 — Abu Kurayb, ... Ibn Kathir: al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: Ibn Abbas said: The Prophet ﷺ commanded the Muslims to gather their charities, and behold, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf came with four thousand, and said: "This is my wealth, which I lend to Allah, and there remains for me the like of it." He said to him: "May it be blessed for you in what you gave and what you kept!" The hypocrites said: "He gave only for show; and the owner of the sa' gave only for show. Surely Allah and His Messenger were in need of nothing from this! And what can Allah do with a sa' of something?"
17019 — Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: ﴿Those who find fault with those among the believers who give voluntarily in charity﴾, up to His words: ﴿and for them is a painful punishment﴾: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, commanded the Muslims to give charity, and Umar ibn al-Khattab stood up: he found that matter by chance, my wealth abundant, so I will take half of it. [In the printed edition: "Umar ibn al-Khattab stood, and found wealth abundant, and took half of it", which misreads the manuscript, distorting, altering and omitting, and doing great harm by what it did. Rather, this is Umar's own statement, saying: he found this matter by chance, my wealth abundant, so I will take half of it.]
He said: So I came bearing a great deal of wealth. A man among the hypocrites said to him: "Showing off, O Umar!" He said: "Yes, I show off to Allah and His Messenger; as for others, no!" And a man from the Ansar, who had nothing, hired himself out to haul a rope over his neck for two sa's for the night, so he left one sa' for his dependants and came with one sa' carrying it. A man among the hypocrites said to him: "Surely Allah and His Messenger are in need of your sa'!" So that is the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿Those who find fault with those among the believers who give voluntarily in charity, and with those who find nothing to give except their effort﴾ — this is the Ansari — ﴿they mock them; Allah will mock them, and for them is a painful punishment﴾.
* *
We have already explained the meaning of "al-lamz" (finding fault) in the speech of the Arabs, with its evidence, and what it involves of language and recitation, previously. [See the explanation of "al-lamz" above, pp. 300, 301, 382.]
* *
As for His words ﴿al-mutawwi'in﴾, its meaning is "al-mutatawwi'in", the ta' was assimilated into the ta', becoming a doubled ta', as it is said: ﴿wa man yattawwa' khayran﴾ [Surat al-Baqarah: 158], [This reading was mentioned by Abu Ja'far earlier, 3: 247, and it is the reading of the common readers of Kufa.
As for our reading in our Mushaf today: (wa man tatawwa'a khayran).] meaning: "yatatawwa'" (volunteers). [See the explanation of "al-tatawwu'" earlier, 3: 247, 441; 14: 382, and see al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 447.]
* *
As for "al-juhd", the Arabs have two dialects regarding it. It is said: "a'taani min juhdih" with a dammah on the jim, and this, as reported, is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz; and "min jahdih" with a fathah on the jim, which is the dialect of Najd. [See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 447, Abu Ubaydah's Majaz al-Qur'an 1: 264, and what preceded at p. 382.]
The reading with the dammah is that of the common readers (al-amsar), and that is the preferred choice in our view, because of the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it.
As for the scholars of Arabic speech, the transmitters of poetry and the grammarians, they claim that the fathah and dammah have one meaning, and the difference is only due to differing dialect in it, just as their dialects differed regarding "al-wajd" and "al-wujd" with dammah and fathah, from "wajadtu". [See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 447, Abu Ubaydah's Majaz al-Qur'an 1: 264, and what preceded at p. 382.]
* *
And it has been related from al-Sha'bi regarding this that:
17020 — Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh narrated to us, from Isa ibn al-Mughirah, from al-Sha'bi, who said: "al-Jahd" and "al-Juhd": al-Jahd is in labour, and al-Juhd is in sustenance. [In the printed edition, the phrase "al-juhd, al-juhd" was omitted and replaced with "fa-al-jahd", "al-jahd", beginning the speech with it. I have restored what is in the manuscript.]
17021 — Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Hafs narrated to us, from Isa ibn al-Mughirah, from al-Sha'bi, the like of it.
17022 — ..., narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Isa ibn al-Mughirah, from al-Sha'bi, who said: al-Jahd is in labour, and al-Juhd is in al-qaytah. [In the printed edition: "wa al-juhd fi al-ma'ishah" ("in livelihood"), which misread the manuscript and altered it. "al-qut", "al-qaytah" (with a kasra on the qaf), and "al-qaytah" (with a kasra on the qaf) are all one, and mean the sustenance of provision, and what sustains the human body of food.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 80:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Ask forgiveness for them, or do not ask forgiveness for them; even if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will never forgive them. That is because they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger, and Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.﴾ (80)

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Pray to Allah for forgiveness for these hypocrites, whose attributes have been described in these verses [[In the printed and manuscript copies: "وصف صفاتهم" (wasf sifatihim), but what I have recorded is clearer.]], or do not pray for them.

This is a statement that takes the form of a command, but its meaning is a report, and its sense is: whether you ask forgiveness for them, O Muhammad, or do not ask forgiveness for them, Allah will never forgive them.

As for His saying: ﴿Even if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will never forgive them﴾, it means: even if you ask that their sins be covered over, by His pardoning them for them and leaving them unexposed because of them, Allah will not cover them over, nor will He pardon them for them; rather, He will expose them because of them before all witnesses on the Day of Resurrection [[See the explanation of "istighfar" (seeking forgiveness) and "maghfirah" (forgiveness) in the earlier linguistic indices under (gh-f-r).]]. ﴿That is because they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger﴾: He, may His praise be exalted, says: this act of Allah toward them, namely His not pardoning them for their sins, is because they denied the Oneness of Allah and the mission of His Messenger. ﴿And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people﴾: He says, Allah does not grant success in believing in Him and His Messenger to those who prefer disbelief in Him and departure from His obedience over belief in Him and His Messenger [[See the explanation of "al-hudan" (guidance) in the earlier linguistic indices under (h-d-y). See the explanation of "al-fisq" (defiant disobedience) earlier: 339, note 2, and the references there.]].

* *

It is narrated from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that when this verse was revealed he said: "I will certainly increase the number of my requests for their forgiveness beyond seventy times," hoping that Allah would forgive them. Then the verse was revealed: ﴿It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; Allah will never forgive them﴾ [Surah al-Munafiqun: 6].

17023 - Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: 'Abdah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father: that 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul said to his companions: "Were it not that you spend on Muhammad and his companions, they would disperse from around him!" He was also the one who said: ﴿If we return to Madinah, the mightier will surely expel the meaner from it﴾ [Surah al-Munafiqun: 8]. So Allah revealed: ﴿Ask forgiveness for them, or do not ask forgiveness for them; even if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will never forgive them.﴾ The Prophet ﷺ said: "I will surely go beyond the seventy!" So Allah revealed: ﴿It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them﴾, and Allah, blessed and exalted, refused to forgive them.

17024 - Ibn Humayd and Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Shabak, from al-Sha'bi, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul invited the Prophet ﷺ to his father's funeral. The Prophet ﷺ said to him: "What is your name?" He said: "Hubab ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy." The Prophet ﷺ said to him: "Rather, you are 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul; indeed, 'al-Hubab' is the Devil." [["al-Hubab" (with a vowelled ḥ), the snake; Ibn Kathir said: "It also applies to the snake, just as it is called the Devil, so the two are shared in it."]]

Then the Prophet ﷺ, peace be upon him, said: "It has been said to me: ﴿Ask forgiveness for them, or do not ask forgiveness for them; even if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will never forgive them﴾, so I will ask forgiveness for them seventy, seventy, and seventy times." And the Prophet ﷺ clothed him in his shirt while it was damp with sweat.

17025 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Even if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times﴾; the Prophet ﷺ said: "I will add to the seventy requests for forgiveness!" So Allah revealed in the surah in which the hypocrites are mentioned: ﴿Allah will never forgive them﴾, decisively ["'azman", meaning emphatically and as a binding truth].

17026 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

17027 - ...... narrated to us, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, in a similar manner.

17028 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly.

17029 - ...... narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Mughirah informed us, from al-Sha'bi, who said: When 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy became gravely ill, his son went to the Prophet ﷺ and said to him: "My father is at the point of death, and I would love for you to attend him and pray over him." The Prophet ﷺ said: "What is your name?" He said: "Hubab ibn 'Abd Allah." He said: "Rather, you are 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy; indeed, 'al-Hubab' is the name of a devil." He said: So he went with him until he attended him, clothed him in his shirt while it was damp with sweat, and prayed over him. He was asked: "Do you pray over him when he is a hypocrite?" He said: "Indeed Allah said: ﴿If you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will never forgive them﴾, and I will ask forgiveness for him seventy, seventy times!" — Hushaym said: "And I am doubtful about the third."

17030 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Ask forgiveness for them, or do not ask forgiveness for them﴾ up to His saying: ﴿the defiantly disobedient people﴾. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, when this verse was revealed: "I hear that my Lord has granted me leave regarding them; by Allah, I will ask forgiveness for them more than seventy times, perhaps Allah will forgive them!" Then Allah, out of the intensity of His anger toward them, said: ﴿It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; Allah will never forgive them. Indeed Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people﴾ [Surah al-Munafiqun: 6].

17031 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: ﴿Ask forgiveness for them, or do not ask forgiveness for them; even if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will never forgive them﴾: the Prophet of Allah said: "My Lord has given me a choice, so I will surely add to the seventy for them!" So Allah revealed: ﴿It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them﴾, the verse.

17032 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: When the verse was revealed: ﴿Even if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will never forgive them﴾, the Prophet ﷺ said: "I will surely add to the seventy!" Then Allah said: ﴿It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; Allah will never forgive them.﴾

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 81:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Those who were left behind rejoiced in their sitting [at home] in opposition to the Messenger of Allah, and they disliked to strive with their wealth and their lives in the way of Allah, and they said, "Do not go forth in the heat." Say, "The Fire of Hell is more intense in heat," if only they understood.﴾ (9:81)

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says: Those whom Allah left behind from going out to raid with His Messenger and the believers in him, and from striving against His enemies, rejoiced = ﴿in their sitting [at home] in opposition to the Messenger of Allah﴾, meaning: by their sitting in their dwellings [see the explanation of "al-qu'ud" (sitting) above: 9:85 \ 14:277]. = ﴿in opposition to the Messenger of Allah﴾, meaning: acting in opposition to the Messenger of Allah in his sitting and his staying put. That is because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had commanded them to go forth to fight the enemies of Allah, but they disobeyed his command and sat in their dwellings.

* *

As for His words, ﴿khilaf﴾ (opposition), it is a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker, "Fulan opposed Fulan, so he opposes him, opposition (khilaf)." Therefore its verbal noun comes in the pattern of "fi'al," just as one says, "He fought him, so he fights him, fighting (qital)." Had it been a verbal noun from "khalafahu" (to stay behind him), the reading would have been "bi-maq'adihim khalfa Rasul Allah" (behind the Messenger of Allah), because the verbal noun of "khalafahu" is "khalf," not "khilaf." But it is, as I have shown, a verbal noun of "khalafa" (to oppose), so it is recited ﴿khilaf rasul Allah﴾, and this is the reading upon which the reciters of the great cities agree, and it is the correct one in our view.

* *

Some have interpreted it to mean "after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ" [this is Abu 'Ubaydah in Majaz al-Qur'an 1: 264], citing the verse of the poet [this is al-Harith ibn Khalid al-Makhzumi]:

"The spring rain followed their absence (khilafahum), as though the palm-leaf strippers had spread mats between them."

[Al-Aghani 3: 336 (Dar al-Kutub) 15: 128 (Sasi), and Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1: 264, and al-Lisan ('-q-b), (kh-l-f), from a qasida some of which Abu al-Faraj related in his Aghani, which he composed about 'A'isha bint Talha, alluding to her and explicitly to her slave-girl Busra. He says before it: "O traces of Busra, if decay has harmed you, I have known you as inhabited and well-populated."

Abu al-Faraj's version is "'aqib al-radhadh," and "al-radhadh" means small rain. "Al-rabi'" is the rain that falls in spring. Abu al-Faraj al-Isfahani said: "His words, 'aqib al-radhadh, mean: the drizzle came after it. From this one says, 'aqiba li-fulan ghina ba'da faqr (he gained wealth after poverty)'; and 'aqiba al-rajul abahu' means he stood in his father's place after him. The 'awaqib al-umur (outcomes of affairs) are derived from this; its singular is 'aqiba... And al-shawatib are the women who strip the bark of palm fronds, making mats from it. From this comes the notched sword (al-saif al-mushattab), and al-shatbiyya: a portion of a thing. One says, 'We sent to so-and-so a shatbiyya of our horses,' meaning a piece." I say: He only described the traces of rain in the dwellings, likening its land to ornamented mats, because of the lines that remain in the sand after rain.]

This is close to the meaning we have stated, because they sat behind him in opposition to him.

* *

As for His words, ﴿and they disliked to strive with their wealth and their lives in the way of Allah﴾, Exalted is He, says: These people left behind disliked to fight the disbelievers with their wealth and their lives [see the explanation of "jihad" above: p. 358, note 1, and the references there] = ﴿in the way of Allah﴾, meaning: in the religion of Allah which He legislated for His servants so that they would support it, [see the explanation of "the way of Allah" in the indexes of language above (s-b-l)], out of inclination to ease and comfort, and preference for rest over fatigue and hardship, and stinginess with wealth that they would spend in obedience to Allah.

* *

= ﴿And they said, "Do not go forth in the heat,"﴾. That is because the Prophet ﷺ called them to go forth on this expedition, which was the expedition of Tabuk, in severe heat [see the explanation of "al-nafr" (going forth) above: 58: 536 \ 14: 251, 254]. The hypocrites said to one another, "Do not go forth in the heat." So Allah said to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿Say﴾ to them, O Muhammad, = ﴿the Fire of Hell﴾, which Allah prepared for whoever opposes His command and disobeys His Messenger, = ﴿is more intense in heat﴾ than this heat about which you urge one another not to go forth in it. He means: That which is more intense in heat is more worthy of being feared and guarded against than that which is least harmful of the two. = ﴿if only they understood﴾, meaning: if these hypocrites understood from Allah His admonition and reflected upon the verses of His Book [see the explanation of "fiqh" (understanding) above: p. 51, note 1, and the references there], but they do not understand from Allah. So they fear the heat that is least disagreeable and lightest in harm, and they expose themselves to its most disagreeable and most grievous form, which is the affliction of those who burn in it.

* *

Those who interpreted it said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

17033 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words: ﴿Those who were left behind rejoiced in their sitting [at home] in opposition to the Messenger of Allah﴾, to His words: ﴿if only they understood﴾. That was because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded the people to set out with him, and that was in the summer. Some men said, "O Messenger of Allah, the heat is severe, and we cannot go forth. Do not march in the heat!" So Allah said: ﴿Say, "The Fire of Hell is more intense in heat, if only they understood."﴾ Then Allah commanded him to go out.

17034 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada regarding His words: ﴿in their sitting [at home] in opposition to the Messenger of Allah﴾, he said: It is the expedition of Tabuk.

17035 - al-Harith related to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz related to us, saying: Abu Ma'shar related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi and others, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out in severe heat toward Tabuk, and a man from the Banu Salima said: "Do not go forth in the heat!" So Allah revealed: ﴿Say, "The Fire of Hell"﴾, the verse.

17036 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salama related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: [Then] he mentioned the saying of some of them to others, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded jihad and resolved to march to Tabuk, in the severity of the heat and the barrenness of the lands. Allah, exalted is His praise, says: ﴿And they said, "Do not go forth in the heat." Say, "The Fire of Hell is more intense in heat."﴾

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on Surah 9, verse 82:

**On the interpretation (ta'wil, the explanation of the meaning) of His words: ﴿So let them laugh a little, and let them weep much, as a recompense for what they used to earn﴾ (9:82)**

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, says: The joy of these who stayed behind, in remaining at home contrary to the Messenger of Allah, is such that let them laugh, rejoicing a little in this perishing world, because of their staying behind contrary to the Messenger of Allah and their heedlessness of the obedience of their Lord. For they will weep much in Hell in place of their little laughter in this world. ﴿As a recompense﴾ means: a reward from Us for them for their disobedience, in their refusal to march forth when they were called to march against their enemy, and their sitting in their dwellings contrary to the Messenger of Allah. [[See the explanation of "al-jaza'" (recompense) in the earlier lexical indexes (under j-z-y).]] ﴿For what they used to earn﴾ means: for the sins which they committed. [[See the explanation of "al-kasb" (earning) in the earlier lexical indexes (under k-s-b).]]

* *

Ahl al-ta'wil (the people of interpretation) said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Those who said that:

17037. Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from Isma'il, from Abu Razin, regarding ﴿So let them laugh a little and let them weep much﴾: He said: Allah, blessed and exalted, says: The world is little; so let them laugh in it as much as they wish. But when they arrive at the Hereafter, they will weep a weeping that does not end. That is the "much."

17038. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Mansur, from Abu Razin, from al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym: ﴿So let them laugh a little﴾, he said: in this world; ﴿and let them weep much﴾, he said: in the Hereafter.

17039. Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman and Yahya narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Sami', from Abu Razin, regarding His words: ﴿So let them laugh a little and let them weep much﴾, he said: in the Hereafter.

17040. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Mansur, from Abu Razin, that he said regarding this verse: ﴿So let them laugh a little and let them weep much﴾: "Let them laugh in this world a little, and let them weep in the Fire much." And he said regarding this verse: ﴿And then you would not be given enjoyment except a little﴾ (33:16): "Until their terms." One of these two reports he traced back to al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym. [[The report 17040 will appear again with its chain in the commentary on the verse of Surah al-Ahzab. In the printed edition here it read "qala: ajaluhum," and in the manuscript "qala: ajaluhum" with "ila" omitted; I have restored "ila" from the text of the report in the tafsir of Surah al-Ahzab.

In the printed edition, in this report, the preceding one, and what follows, it read "al-Rabi' ibn Khaythum," whereas the correct form is "Khuthaym," as occurred many times before; I have changed it and did not note it.]]

17041. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan: ﴿So let them laugh a little﴾, he said: they laugh a little in this world; ﴿and let them weep much﴾, in the Hereafter, in the Fire of Hell; ﴿as a recompense for what they used to earn﴾.

It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, if you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep much." 17044. ...... narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Sami', from Abu Razin: ﴿So let them laugh a little﴾, he said: in this world; when they arrive at the Hereafter, they will weep a weeping that does not end. That is the "much."

And he said: ﴿Indeed, those who committed crime used to laugh at those who believed﴾ (83:29), until He reached: ﴿Have the disbelievers been rewarded for what they used to do?﴾ (83:36).

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 83:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿And if Allah returns you to a group of them and they ask your permission to go out, then say: "You will never go out with me, and you will never fight an enemy with me. Indeed, you were content with sitting [at home] the first time, so sit [now] with those who remain behind."﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: His Majesty says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: If Allah returns you, O Muhammad, to a group of these hypocrites from this expedition of yours [[See the explanation of "ṭāʾifah" above, p. 336, footnote 3, and the references there.]] = ﴿and they ask your permission to go out﴾ with you on another campaign besides it = ﴿then say﴾ to them = ﴿"You will never go out with me, and you will never fight an enemy with me. Indeed, you were content with sitting [at home] the first time"﴾, and that was at the departure of the Prophet ﷺ to Tabuk [[See the explanation of "al-qaʿūd" above, p. 397, footnote 1, and the references there.]] = ﴿so sit [now] with those who remain behind﴾. He says: So sit with those among the hypocrites who stayed behind, in opposition to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, because you are among them; so follow their guidance and do the same as they did of disobedience to Allah, for Allah has indeed become wrathful toward you.

* *

What we have said concerning this is also what the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of those who said that:

17047- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, the heat is intense, and we cannot go out, so do not march in the heat!" = and that was during the expedition of Tabuk = so Allah said: ﴿Say: "The fire of Hell is more intense in heat, if only they understood."﴾ Then Allah commanded him to go out. Some men stayed behind, and their own souls reproached them, and they said: "By Allah, we have done nothing!" Then three of them set off and caught up with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When they came to him, they repented; then they returned to Madinah. So Allah revealed: ﴿And if Allah returns you to a group of them﴾, up to His saying: ﴿nor stand at his grave﴾. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Those who stayed behind have perished." So Allah revealed their excuse once they repented, saying: ﴿Certainly Allah has turned in forgiveness to the Prophet and the Emigrants and the Helpers﴾, up to His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 117, 118].

17048- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And if Allah returns you to a group of them﴾, up to His saying: ﴿so sit [now] with those who remain behind﴾, that is: with the women. It was mentioned to us that they were twelve men from among the hypocrites, about whom what was said was said. [[In the printed edition: "fa-qīla fīhim…", and in the manuscript: "qutila minhum mā qutila", the correct reading being that of the printed edition.]]

17049- al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿so sit [now] with those who remain behind﴾, and "al-khālifūn" are the men.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct interpretation of His saying ﴿al-khālifīn﴾ is what Ibn 'Abbas said.

* *

As for what Qatadah said, that it refers to the women, this is a view without meaning. For the Arabs do not form the masculine plural with the ya' and nun (or the waw and nun) for women when there are no men with them. And if the meaning had been the women, it would have been said: "fa-q'udū ma'a al-khawālif" or "ma'a al-khālifāt". Rather, its meaning is what we have stated: that what is intended is: sit with the sick men and the disabled among them, the weak, and the women. When men and women are included together in a statement, the Arabs give precedence to the masculine over the feminine, and therefore it was said: ﴿so sit [now] with those who remain behind﴾, and the meaning is what we have mentioned.

* *

Had the meaning been directed to: "sit with the people of corruption", from their saying "khalafa al-rajul 'an ahlihi yakhlufu khulūfan" when he became corrupt, and from their saying "huwa khalf saw'" (he is a bad successor) — that would be a valid view. Its root, if this meaning is intended, comes from their saying "khalafa al-laban yakhlufu khulūfan", when milk turned sour from being kept long in the waterskin until it spoiled, and from their saying "khalafa fam al-ṣā'im" when the breath of the fasting person changed in smell. [[See the explanation of "khalafa" above: 13:209, 210.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 84:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And never pray over any of them who dies, nor stand at his grave. Indeed, they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger, and died while they were defiantly disobedient.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His praise be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Do not pray, O Muhammad, over anyone among these hypocrites who died after staying behind from going out with you, ever. ﴿Nor stand at his grave﴾ means: do not take charge of his burial and interment. [[In the printed edition: "wa tuqabbirahu" (and entomb him), which differs from the manuscript. "Taqbir" means burial and is one of the terms used by early jurists. Abu Ja'far's use of this term has already occurred before, and my comment on it appears earlier, vol. 9, p. 387, note 1.]]

This is from the saying of the speaker: "So-and-so stood with the matter of so-and-so," when he took care of his affair for him.

* *

﴿Indeed, they disbelieved in Allah﴾ means: they denied the oneness of Allah (tawhid) and the messengership of His Messenger. ﴿And died while they were departing from Islam, deviating from the command and prohibition of Allah.﴾ [[See the explanation of "fisq" (defiant disobedience) earlier, p. 385, note 1, and the references there.]]

* *

It has been mentioned that this verse was revealed when the Prophet (ﷺ) prayed over Abdullah ibn Ubayy.

Those who said this:

17050. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, Sufyan ibn Waki', and Sawwar ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Ubaydullah, who said: Nafi' informed me, from Ibn Umar, who said: The son of Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when his father had died, and said: "Give me your shirt so that I may shroud him in it, and pray over him, and ask forgiveness for him." So he gave him his shirt. And [he said]: "When you have finished, inform me." Then when he wanted to pray over him, Umar pulled him [[the word "jadhabahu" (pulled him) between the brackets is missing from the manuscript; the first editor added it, and he was right]] and said: "Has Allah not forbidden you to pray over the hypocrites?" He said: "Rather, my Lord gave me a choice, and He said: ﴿Ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; even if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will not forgive them.﴾" He said: So he prayed over him. He said: Then Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed: ﴿And never pray over any of them who dies, nor stand at his grave.﴾ He said: So he abandoned praying over them. [[Report 17050: The report of Ubaydullah ibn Umar, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, is narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (al-Fath 3:110 and 8:251, 255). He narrated it through Yahya ibn Sa'id from Ubaydullah ibn Umar, then through Abu Usama from Ubaydullah, then through Anas ibn Iyad from Ubaydullah.
Muslim also narrated it in his Sahih (17:121), through Abu Usama from Ubaydullah ibn Umar.
It will come from Abu Ja'far's narration through Usama in the next report, number 17051.
Ibn Kathir also cited it in his tafsir (4:217-219), so refer to it there.]]

17051. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Abu Usama narrated to us, from Ubaydullah, from Ibn Umar, who said: When Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul died, his son Abdullah came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and asked him to give him his shirt to shroud his father in, and he gave it to him. Then he asked him to pray over him, and Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) stood up, took hold of the garment of the Prophet (ﷺ), and said: "Son of Salul! Will you pray over him when Allah has forbidden you to pray over him?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "My Lord only gave me a choice, for He said: ﴿Ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; even if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will not forgive them.﴾ I will add more than seventy." [Umar] said: "He is a hypocrite!" So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed over him, and Allah revealed: ﴿And never pray over any of them who dies, nor stand at his grave.﴾ [[Report 17051: See the earlier takhrij (source citation).]]

17052. Sawwar ibn Abdullah al-Anbari narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Mujahid, who said: Amir related to me, from Jabir ibn Abdullah: that the head of the hypocrites died in Medina, and he bequeathed that the Prophet (ﷺ) should pray over him and that he be shrouded in his shirt. So he was shrouded in his shirt, the Prophet (ﷺ) prayed over him and stood at his grave, and Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed: ﴿And never pray over any of them who dies, nor stand at his grave.﴾ [[Report 17052: The hadith of Jabir ibn Abdullah through this chain is mentioned by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (4:219), from the Musnad of al-Bazzar, through Amr ibn Ali, from Yahya, from Mujalid, from al-Sha'bi, from Jabir. He said: "Its chain is not objectionable, and what precedes it is corroborating evidence for it." The hadith of Jabir through another route will come, number 17054.]]

17053. Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Yazid al-Raqqashi, from Anas: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wanted to pray over Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, so Jibril (peace be upon him) took hold of his garment and said: ﴿And never pray over any of them who dies, nor stand at his grave.﴾ [[Report 17053: "Yazid al-Raqqashi" is Yazid ibn Aban al-Raqqashi, who is weak, indeed abandoned (matruk). He has occurred before under numbers 6654, 6728, 7577, and elsewhere.]]

17054. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Uyayna narrated to us, from Amr, from Jabir, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) came to Abdullah ibn Ubayy when he had been placed in his grave pit. He brought him out, laid him on his knees, dressed him in his shirt, and spat on him from his saliva. And Allah knows best. [[Report 17054: The hadith of Jabir occurred earlier through the route of al-Sha'bi, number 10752.
As for this route, al-Bukhari narrated it in his Sahih (al-Fath 3:111), and Muslim in his Sahih (17:175 [sic], 121), and they also narrated it through Ibn Jurayj, from Amr ibn Dinar.
As for his saying "And Allah knows best," it means: Allah knows best about His decree, since the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did what he did, along with Allah's decree concerning the hypocrites in accordance with what He decreed about them.]]

17055. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from al-Zuhri, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn Utba ibn Mas'ud, from Abdullah ibn Abbas, who said: I heard Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) say: When Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul died, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was called to pray over him, so he stood up to him. When he stood over him intending to pray, I moved until I stood in front of his chest, and I said: "O Messenger of Allah, will you pray over the enemy of Allah, Abdullah ibn Ubayy, who said on such-and-such a day such-and-such!" I enumerated his days, while the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was smiling. When I persisted against him, he said: "Step back from me, O Umar. I was given a choice and I chose. It has been said to me: ﴿Ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; even if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will not forgive them.﴾ If I knew that if I added to the seventy he would be forgiven, I would add to it!" He said: Then he prayed over him, walked with him, and stood at his grave until he finished. He said: I was amazed at myself and at my boldness toward the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Allah and His Messenger know best. By Allah, it was not long before these two verses were revealed: ﴿And never pray over any of them who dies﴾, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) never prayed after that over any hypocrite, nor stood at his grave, until Allah took him. [[Report 17055: Ibn Hisham's Sirah (4:196, 197), and it follows the earlier report, number 17036.
The hadith of al-Zuhri from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn Utba ibn Mas'ud was narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (al-Fath 8:254), through Yahya ibn Bukayr, from al-Layth, from Aqil, from Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri. It will come through this route under number 17057.
Ibn Kathir also cited it in his tafsir (4:218).
As for his saying "Step back from me, O Umar," meaning: step back from me your opinion. He abbreviated it with conciseness and eloquence, as they said. I have mentioned earlier (vol. 10, p. 339, note 6) that they curtailed its explanation, and that its meaning is "turn your opinion away from me and remove it," and that it is among what could be expanded beyond the explanation in lexicographical books.]]

17056. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada, who said: When Abdullah ibn Ubayy died, his son Abdullah ibn Abdullah came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and asked him for his shirt, so he gave it to him, and he shrouded his father in it. [[Report 17056: I did not find this report in Ibn Hisham's Sirah.]]

17057. Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: al-Layth narrated to me, saying: Aqil narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn Utba informed me, from Abdullah ibn Abbas, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, who said: When Abdullah ibn Ubayy died... [and he mentioned a report similar to the hadith of Ibn Humayd from Salama.] [[Report 17057: Its takhrij was given under number 17055.]]

17058. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding his saying: ﴿And never pray over any of them who dies, nor stand at his grave﴾, the verse, he said: Abdullah ibn Ubayy sent to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), while he was ill, asking him to come to him, but Umar forbade him from doing so. Then the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) came to him, and when he entered upon him, the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The love of the Jews has destroyed you!" He said: "O Prophet of Allah, I did not send for you so that you would reproach me, but I sent for you so that you would ask forgiveness for me!" He asked him for his shirt to be shrouded in, so he gave it to him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked forgiveness for him. He died and was shrouded in the shirt of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and [the Prophet] breathed on his skin and lowered him into his grave. Then Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed: ﴿And never pray over any of them who dies﴾, the verse. He said: It was related to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) was addressed about this and said: "What will my shirt avail him against Allah?" — or: "my Lord" — "And I pray over him" — "and I truly hope that a thousand of his people will become Muslim because of it." [[The phrase "and he prayed over him" is as it appears in the manuscript. The printed edition reads "wa salati 'alayhi" (and my prayer over him), apparently taking it as coordinated with his saying "what will my shirt avail him," but it is possible that what I have recorded from the manuscript is correct. It is a report from Qatada or someone else, which separates it from the words of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). That is why I placed it between two lines.]]

17059. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, who said: Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul sent to the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was ill; when he entered upon him, the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "The love of the Jews has destroyed you!" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I only sent for you so that you would ask forgiveness for me, and I did not send for you so that you would reproach me!" Then Abdullah asked him to give him his shirt to shroud himself in it, so he gave it to him, and prayed over him and stood at his grave, and Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, revealed: ﴿And never pray over any of them who dies, nor stand at his grave.﴾

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 85:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And let not their wealth or their children impress you. Allah only intends to punish them thereby in this world, and that their souls should depart while they are disbelievers.﴾ (9:85)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "Let not the wealth and children of these hypocrites impress you, O Muhammad, so that you pray over one of them when he dies and stand at his grave, because of the abundance of his wealth and children. Indeed, I have only given him what I have given him of that so that I may punish him with it in this world, through griefs and worries, by what I impose on him therein of burdens, expenses and zakat, and by what befalls him therein of calamities and misfortunes." = ﴿And that their souls should depart﴾ means: and that he dies, so his soul leaves his body [[See the explanation of "zahaqa" above, p. 297.]], and so he parts from the wealth and children I have given him. That will be a regret for him at his death and a burden upon him at that time, and a burden upon him in the Hereafter, by dying as one who denies the Oneness of Allah and the prophethood of His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ).

17060 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi: ﴿And that their souls should depart﴾ — in the life of this world.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 86:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿And when a surah is sent down [commanding]: "Believe in Allah and strive with His Messenger," the men of wealth among them ask your permission and say, "Leave us so that we may be with those who sit [at home]."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, He says: "And when a surah is sent down to you, O Muhammad, from the Qur'an, [commanding] that these hypocrites be told: ﴿Believe in Allah﴾, that is, affirm Allah [as true] = ﴿and strive with His Messenger﴾, that is, fight the polytheists alongside the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) [[See the explanation of "jihad" (struggle in the way of Allah) above, p. 399, note 1, and the references there.]] = ﴿the men of wealth among them ask your permission﴾, that is, the people of wealth and property among them ask your permission to remain behind from you and sit at home [[See the explanation of "tawl" (means, abundance) above, 8:182–185.]] = ﴿and say, "Leave us"﴾, that is, they say to you: "Leave us [alone]," [[See the explanation of "dhar" (leave) above, 13:291, note 2, and the references there.]] "so that we may be among those who sit in their houses with the weak among the people and their sick, and those who are unable to go out with you on the campaign." [[See the explanation of "qu'ud" (sitting/remaining behind) above, p. 404, note 1, and the references there.]]

* *

The commentators have said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mentioning those who said that:

17061. Ali ibn Dawud related to us, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿the men of wealth among them ask your permission﴾, he said: It means the people of wealth.

17062. Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿the men of wealth among them﴾, meaning: the rich.

17063. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿And when a surah is sent down [commanding]: "Believe in Allah and strive with His Messenger," the men of wealth among them ask your permission﴾. Among them were Abdullah ibn Ubayy and al-Jadd ibn Qays, and Allah censured them for that. [[The report 17063: Sirat Ibn Hisham 4:197, which continues the earlier report No. 17055, except that Ibn Hisham said: "Ibn Ubayy was among those, and Allah censured him for that, and mentioned it of him." Here "al-Jadd ibn Qays" is not mentioned.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 87:

The explanation of His words: ﴿They are content to be with those who stay behind (al-khawalif)﴾ and ﴿a seal has been set upon their hearts, so they do not understand﴾ (87).

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, He says: These hypocrites were content, those who, when it was said to them, "Believe in God and strive with His Messenger," asked your permission, the wealthy among them, to stay behind from the raid and to not go out with you to fight the enemies of God among the polytheists, to remain in their dwellings, like the women, upon whom the obligation of jihad does not fall, so they sit in their homes and houses [see the explanation of "al-khawalif" above, p. 405, note 1, and the references there]. ﴿And a seal was set upon their hearts﴾, meaning: God sealed the hearts of these hypocrites, ﴿so they do not understand﴾, meaning, they do not grasp God's admonitions, so that they would heed them [see the explanation of "fiqh" above, p. 399, note 4, and the references there].

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "ṭab'" (sealing) and how the sealing of hearts occurs, earlier, in a way that makes repeating it in this place unnecessary [see the explanation of "ṭab'" above, 13:10, note 1, and the references there].

* *

Those of the interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) said in accordance with what we have said regarding the meaning of "al-khawalif".

Those who said this:

17064 - Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Abdullah ibn Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿They are content to be with those who stay behind﴾, he said: "al-khawalif" are the women.

17065 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: My father related to me, he said: My paternal uncle related to me, he said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿They are content to be with those who stay behind﴾, meaning: the women.

17066 - Ibn WakI' related to us, he said: Hubaywa Abu Yazid related to us, from Ya'qub al-Qummi, from Hafs ibn Humayd, from Shamir ibn Atiyya: ﴿They are content to be with those who stay behind﴾, he said: the women.

17067 - ...... He said: al-Maharibi related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: ﴿with those who stay behind﴾, he said: with the women.

17068 - Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada regarding His words: ﴿They are content to be with those who stay behind﴾, meaning: with the women.

17069 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada and al-Hasan: ﴿They are content to be with those who stay behind﴾, both said: the women.

17070 - Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, he said: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

17071 - Al-Qasim related to us, he said: Al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

17072 - Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: ﴿They are content to be with those who stay behind﴾, he said: with the women.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 88:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿But the Messenger and those who believed with him strove with their wealth and their lives. And those—for them are the good things, and those are the successful.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His mention, says: These hypocrites whose stories I have related did not strive against the polytheists. Rather, the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) and those who affirmed Allah and His Messenger along with him are the ones who strove against the polytheists with their wealth and their lives. They spent their wealth in their striving and exhausted their lives in fighting, and gave them up [[See the explanation of "jihad" above, p. 411, footnote 2, and the references there.]]. ﴿And those﴾, meaning: and for the Messenger and for those who believed with him who strove with their wealth and their lives, ﴿the good things﴾, which are the good things of the Hereafter, namely: its women, its gardens, and its bliss.

* *

[It is said that] its singular is "khayrah" (good, excellent), as the poet said: [[By a man of the Banu 'Adi, 'Adi Taym Tamim, and he is from the pre-Islamic era.]]

"And indeed I have stabbed the gatherings of the thighs... the thighs of Hind, the best of queens"

[[Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu 'Ubayda 1:267, and Lisan (kh-y-r). "Al-Rabalat" is the plural of "rabala" (with a fatha on the ra and sukun on the ba, or with a fatha on it), which is the fleshy inner part of the thigh. He meant a shameful matter. His saying "khayrah" is the feminine of "khayr", as an adjective, not in the sense of comparison; it is said: "a man khayr, and a woman khayrah." If you want the comparative, you say: "So-and-so is the best of people."]]

And "khayrah," of every thing, is its excellent part. [[See Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu 'Ubayda 1:267.]]

* *

﴿And those are the successful﴾, meaning: and those are the ones who will abide forever in the gardens, remaining therein, triumphant with them. [[See the explanation of "al-falah" above 13:574, footnote 2, and the references there.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 89:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿Allah has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the great triumph.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Allah has prepared for His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) and for those who believed with him [[See the explanation of "a'adda" (prepared) above, pp. 31, 267.]] ﴿gardens﴾, which are orchards, [[See the explanation of "Jannah" (paradise/garden) above in the language indices (j-n-n).]] beneath whose trees rivers flow ﴿abiding therein forever﴾, meaning: remaining therein, not dying therein, nor departing from it [[See the explanation of "khulud" (eternal abiding) above in the language indices (kh-l-d).]] ﴿That is the great triumph﴾, meaning: that is the great deliverance and the abundant portion. [[See the explanation of "fawz" (triumph) above, p. 357, footnote 3, and the references there.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 90:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿And those who made excuses among the Bedouins came [to Allah's Messenger] seeking permission, and those who lied to Allah and His Messenger sat back [and did not come]. Those of them who disbelieved will be touched by a painful punishment.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His mention, says: ﴿And came﴾ (to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ) ﴿the excusers among the Bedouins, seeking permission﴾ (to stay behind) ﴿and sat back﴾ (from coming to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and from fighting with him) [[See the explanation of "sitting back" above, p. 412, note 1, and the references there.]] ﴿those who lied to Allah and His Messenger﴾, and who spoke falsehood and made excuses with baseless claims. He, exalted is His mention, says: Those among them who denied the Oneness of Allah and the prophethood of His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ will be touched by a painful punishment. [[See the explanation of "painful" above in the lexical indexes (under ʿ-l-m).]]

* *

If someone says: "And the excusers came" — but you know that "al-muʿadhdhir" in the speech of the Arabs is the one who makes an excuse in a matter but does not exert himself in it nor perfect it? These are not the attributes of these people. Rather, their attribute is that they had striven to seek what they could undertake with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ against their enemy, and were eager for that, but did not find a way to it. So they are more fitting and more deserving of being described as "those who have an excuse" than of being described as "those who make excuses." And when they are described by that, [[In the printed edition: "that they made excuses, when they are described by that," as if it is linked to what precedes. The correct reading is that it begins a new sentence, and the waw in "wa-idha" is present in the manuscript.]] then the correct reading in this regard is the one recited by Ibn ʿAbbas. That is what:

17073 – Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Hammad narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn ʿUmara narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, who said: Ibn ʿAbbas used to recite: ﴿Wa-jaʾa al-muʿdhirun﴾ with a light (unshaddated) dhal, and he would say: They are the people of excuse.

= along with the agreement of Mujahid with him and others on it? It is said: The meaning of that is other than what you have taken it to be, and its meaning is: "And the excuse-makers (al-muʿtadhirun) among the Bedouins came," but the "taʾ" was assimilated into the "dhal" when it was adjacent to it, so both were made a doubled dhal, because the articulation points of the two are close to each other, as it is said "yadhdhakkarun" for "yatadhakkarun," and "yudhakkir" for "yatadhakkar." The ʿayn in "al-muʿadhdhirin" took a fatha, because the vowel of the taʾ in "al-muʿtadhirin," which is a fatha, was transferred to it, so it was moved with what it was moved with. The Arabs also use the meaning of "iʿtidhar" to refer to "iʿdhar," so one says: "So-and-so has made an excuse (iʿtadhara) in such-and-such," meaning: he gave an excuse (aʿdhara). [[See al-Farra's Maʿani al-Quran 1: 447, 448.]] And from that is the verse of Labid:

Until the year turns, then peace be upon you both... and whoever weeps a full year has indeed made an excuse (iʿtadhar)

[[The verse was cited earlier, 1: 119, note 1.]]

He said: "faqad iʿtadhar," meaning: "faqad aʿdhar."

* *

However, the people of interpretation have differed regarding the description of these people whom Allah described as having come to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as "excusers."

Some of them said: They were lying in their excuses, so Allah did not excuse them.

Those who said that:

17074 – Abu ʿUbayda ʿAbd al-Warith ibn ʿAbd al-Samad narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from al-Husayn, who said: Qatada used to recite: ﴿Wa-jaʾa al-muʿadhdhirun min al-aʿrab﴾ and said: They made excuses with lies.

17075 – Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd al-ʿAziz narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Zakariyya narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid: ﴿Wa-jaʾa al-muʿadhdhirun min al-aʿrab﴾, he said: A group from Banu Ghifar came and made excuses, so Allah did not excuse them.

* *

= Those we have mentioned from these narrators have reported that these people were only people of excuse with falsehood, not with truth. It is therefore impermissible that they be described as "excusers" except in the sense that they excused in making excuses with falsehood. As for with truth, according to what the one whose saying we have cited from them said, it is impermissible that they be described by it.

* *

Some of them used to say: They came as "excusers" who were not serious, presenting what they did not intend to do. For whoever directs it to this interpretation, there is no difficulty in that, but I do not know of any scholar of the interpretation of the Quran who directed its interpretation to that, so I prefer the saying of it.

Moreover, the reading upon which the recitation of the regions is established is the doubling of the dhal in "al-muʿadhdhirun," by which I mean in His saying: ﴿al-muʿadhdhirun﴾. In that is evidence for the soundness of the interpretation of the one who interpreted it in the sense of making excuses, because the people who were described by that were not charged with a matter about which they made excuses; rather they were two groups: either a striving obedient one, or a hypocritical, defiant one opposing the command of Allah. So there is no one among the two groups described as making excuses in refraining from setting out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; rather he is either an excessive excuser or an excuse-maker.

If that is so, and the proof of the reciters is agreed upon the doubling of the dhal in "al-muʿadhdhirin," it is known that its meaning is what we have described as the interpretation.

* *

It has been mentioned from Mujahid in that an agreement with Ibn ʿAbbas.

17076 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq informed us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to us, from Ibn ʿUyayna, from Humayd, who said: Mujahid recited: ﴿Wa-jaʾa al-muʿdharun﴾ with a light dhal, and said: They are the people of excuse.

17077 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: "The excusers," [as it reached me, a group from Banu Ghifar, among them: Khafaf ibn Ayma ibn Rahada; then the account was about the people of excuse, until it reached His saying: ﴿nor [is there blame] upon those who, when they come to you to be provided with mounts, you say, "I cannot find anything to mount you on"﴾, the verse] . [[Report 17077: Sirat Ibn Hisham 4: 197, which continues the earlier report no. 17063. This report was truncated in the manuscript and the printed edition; I completed it from Sirat Ibn Hisham and placed its completion between the brackets.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 91:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿There is no blame upon the weak, nor upon the sick, nor upon those who find nothing to spend, when they are sincere toward Allah and His Messenger. There is no cause [for blame] against the good-doers. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (9:91).

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: There is no blame upon the disabled and those incapable of traveling and going out to fight [[See the explanation of "al-du'afa'" (the weak) above, 5:551 and 8:19.]], nor upon the sick, nor upon those who do not have the provision to carry them to their campaign = "ḥaraj" (blame), which is sin [[See the explanation of "ḥaraj" above, 12:295, footnote 2, and the references there.]]. He says: there is no sin upon them, when they are sincere to Allah and His Messenger in their absence from jihad with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ = ﴿nor upon the good-doers is there any way﴾, meaning: there is no way (path) by which one who does good and is sincere to Allah and His Messenger in staying behind from fighting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, for a valid excuse for which he is excused, may be taken to be punished by Him [[See the explanation of "al-muḥsin" (the good-doer) and "al-sabil" (the way) above in the lexical indexes, under (ḥ-s-n) and (s-b-l).]] = ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, meaning: Allah conceals the sins of the good-doers, covering them with His pardon for them = ﴿Merciful﴾, toward them, by not punishing them for them. [[See the explanation of "Forgiving" and "Merciful" above in the lexical indexes, under (gh-f-r) and (r-ḥ-m).]]

* *

It is mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning "A'idh ibn 'Amr al-Muzani".

* *

And some of them said it was revealed concerning "Abdullah ibn Mughaffal".

* *

Mention of those who said: it was revealed concerning "A'idh ibn 'Amr".

17078- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding: ﴿There is no blame upon the weak, nor upon the sick, nor upon those who find nothing to spend, when they are sincere toward Allah and His Messenger﴾, that it was revealed concerning A'idh ibn 'Amr.

* *

Mention of those who said: it was revealed concerning "Ibn Mughaffal".

17079- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿There is no blame upon the weak, nor upon the sick﴾, up to His saying: ﴿grieving that they could not find what to spend﴾. That was because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded the people to set out fighting with him. A group of his companions came to him, among them "Abdullah ibn Mughaffal al-Muzani," and they said: O Messenger of Allah, carry us. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: By Allah, I do not find anything to carry you upon! So they turned away weeping, and it was difficult for them to sit out from jihad [[In the printed edition: "wa 'azza 'alayhim", and I have adopted what is in the manuscript, which is entirely correct.]], and they did not find provision or a mount. When Allah saw their eagerness for His love and the love of His Messenger, He revealed their excuse in His Book, saying: ﴿There is no blame upon the weak, nor upon the sick, nor upon those who find nothing to spend, [when they are sincere]﴾, up to His saying: ﴿but they do not know﴾.

**The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 9, Verse 92**

On the discussion of His saying (ta'wil, interpretation): ﴿Nor [is there any blame] upon those who, when they come to you that you might provide them with mounts, you say, "I cannot find anything to mount you on," and they turn away while their eyes overflow with tears of grief that they cannot find anything to spend.﴾
