Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Nor is there any way (of blame) either against the group of men who, when they come to you, [O Muhammad], asking you to provide them with mounts so that they may reach their destination for striving against the enemies of God with you, you say to them, "I cannot find a mount to carry you on." ﴿They turned away﴾ means they withdrew from you. [[See the explanation of "tawalli" (turning away) in the earlier lexical indexes under (w-l-y).]] ﴿And their eyes overflowed with tears of grief﴾ means they wept out of sorrow that they could not find anything to spend, which they would use to equip themselves for jihad in the way of God. [[See the explanation of "tafid min al-dam'" (overflowing with tears) in the earlier volume, 10: 507.]]

* *

Some have said: This verse was revealed concerning a group from the tribe of Muzaynah.

Those who said this:

17080. He related to me Muhammad ibn 'Amr, who said: Abu 'Asim related to us, who said: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Nor [is there any blame] upon those who, when they come to you that you might provide them with mounts, you say, "I cannot find anything to mount you on"﴾. He said: They were from Muzaynah.

17081. He related to me al-Muthanna, who said: Ishaq informed us, who said: 'Abd Allah related to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿Nor [is there any blame] upon those who, when they come to you that you might provide them with mounts﴾. He said: They were the sons of Muqarrin, from Muzaynah.

17082. He related to me al-Muthanna, who said: Suwayd related to us, who said: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, by recitation, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿Nor [is there any blame] upon those who, when they come to you that you might provide them with mounts﴾, up to His saying: ﴿grief that they cannot find anything to spend﴾. He said: They were the sons of Muqarrin, from Muzaynah.

17083. Ibn WakI' related to us, who said: Ibn Numayr related to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Nor [is there any blame] upon those who, when they come to you that you might provide them with mounts﴾. He said: They were the sons of Muqarrin from Muzaynah.

17084. ...... He said: My father related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, from 'Urwah, from Ibn Mughaffal al-Muzani, who was one of the group concerning whom it was revealed: ﴿Nor [is there any blame] upon those who, when they come to you that you might provide them with mounts﴾, the verse.

17085. He related to me al-Muthanna, who said: Ishaq informed us, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr related to us, from Ibn 'Uyaynah, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿They turned away while their eyes overflowed with tears of grief﴾. He said: Among them was Ibn Muqarrin. And Sufyan said: People say: Among them was 'Irbad ibn Sariyah.

* *

Others have said: Rather, it was revealed concerning 'Irbad ibn Sariyah.

Those who said this:

17086. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, who said: Abu 'Asim related to us, from Thawr ibn Yazid, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Amr al-Sulami and Hujr ibn Hujr al-Kala'i, who both said: We entered upon 'Irbad ibn Sariyah, and he is the one concerning whom it was revealed: ﴿Nor [is there any blame] upon those who, when they come to you that you might provide them with mounts﴾, the verse. [[The report 17086: "'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Amr ibn 'Abasah al-Sulami" is reliable (thiqah), and is biographed in al-Tahdhib. And "Hujr ibn Hujr al-Kala'i" is reliable and is biographed in al-Tahdhib.]]

17087. He related to me al-Muthanna, who said: Sulayman ibn 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, who said: al-Walid related to us, who said: Thawr related to us, from Khalid, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Amr and Hujr ibn Hujr, with similar wording.

* *

Others have said: Rather, it was revealed concerning a group of seven men from various tribes.

Those who said this:

17088. al-Harith related to me, who said: 'Abd al-'Aziz related to us, who said: Abu Ma'shar related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b and others, who said: Some men from the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ came to him asking him for mounts, and he said: ﴿I cannot find anything to mount you on﴾! So God revealed: ﴿Nor [is there any blame] upon those who, when they come to you that you might provide them with mounts﴾, the verse. He said: They were seven men: from the Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf: Salim ibn 'Umayr; from the Banu Waqif: Harmi ibn 'Amr [[In the printed and manuscript editions: "Hurmi ibn 'Amr," but the correct form is "Harmi" with a ha', see his biography in al-Isabah.]]; from the Banu Mazin ibn al-Najjar: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka'b, known as Abu Layla; from the Banu al-Mu'alla: Salman ibn Sakhr; from the Banu Harithah: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, Abu 'Ublah, and he is the one who gave his property in charity and God accepted it from him; from the Banu Salimah: 'Amr ibn Ghanmah and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr al-Muzani.

17089. Ibn Humayd related to us, who said: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, regarding His saying: ﴿Nor [is there any blame] upon those who, when they come to you that you might provide them with mounts﴾, up to His saying: ﴿grief﴾, and they were the weepers, and they were seven. [[Report 17089: This is the continuation of the earlier report no. 17077 in Ibn Hisham's Sirah, 4: 197, and in this place it does not contain the phrase "and they were seven." As for their number according to Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Hisham mentioned it in his Sirah, 4: 161, and said: "They were seven men from the Ansar and others," and then enumerated them.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 93:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿Surely the blame is only against those who ask you for leave while they are rich. They are content to be with the women who stay behind, and Allah has sealed their hearts, so they do not know.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, He says: There is no blame by way of punishment upon those with a valid excuse, O Muhammad. Rather, it is upon those who ask you for leave to stay behind, away from you, and to abandon jihad with you, while they are people of wealth, strength and capacity for jihad and military campaign, out of hypocrisy and doubt concerning Allah's promise and His threat [[See the explanation of "al-sabil" (the way, the blame) in the preceding lexical indexes (s-b-l).]] = ﴿They are content to be with the women who stay behind﴾. He says: they are content to sit behind after you with the women, who are the "khawalif" (those who stay behind), left behind by the men in the houses, and to leave off the campaign with you. [[See the explanation of "al-khawalif" (those left behind) in the preceding pages, p. 413, note 1, and the references there.]] = ﴿And Allah has sealed their hearts﴾. He says: Allah has stamped upon their hearts because of the sins they earned. [[See the explanation of "al-taba'" (sealing, stamping) in the preceding pages, p. 413, note 3, and the references there.]] = ﴿So they do not know﴾, the evil end awaiting them, by their staying behind from you and abandoning jihad with you, and the ugly reputation they incur in this world and the great affliction in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 94:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿They will make excuses to you when you return to them. Say: "Do not make excuses; we will not believe you. Allah has already informed us of your news. And Allah will see your deeds, and [so will] His Messenger; then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: These who stayed behind, opposing the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), leaving off striving against the polytheists alongside you from among the hypocrites, will make excuses to you, O believers in Allah, with falsehoods and lies, when you return to them from your journey and your struggle. ﴿Say﴾ to them, O Muhammad: ﴿Do not make excuses; we will not believe you﴾, meaning: we will not accept as true what you say. ﴿Allah has already informed us of your news﴾, meaning: Allah has already informed us of your news and made known to us of your affairs what has made us aware of your lies. ﴿And Allah will see your deeds, and [so will] His Messenger﴾, meaning: Allah and His Messenger will see your deeds in the future: will you repent of your hypocrisy, or will you persist in it? ﴿Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾, meaning: then you will return after your death ﴿to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾, meaning: the One who knows the secret and the open, to whom the inner and outer aspects of your affairs are not hidden. ﴿And He will inform you of what you used to do﴾, meaning: He will tell you of all your deeds, the evil and the good, and will recompense you for them: the good with good, and the evil with evil.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 95:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿They will swear to you by Allah, when you return to them, that you may leave them alone. So leave them alone. Indeed, they are impure, and their refuge is Hell — a recompense for what they used to earn.﴾ (9:95)

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, says: The hypocrites, who rejoiced in their sitting behind the Messenger of Allah, will swear to you, O believers, by Allah, ﴿when you return to them﴾, meaning: when you return to them from your military campaign [[See the explanation of "al-inqilab" (turning back) earlier, 13:35, note 1, and the references there.]] ﴿that you may leave them alone﴾, that is, that you may not reproach them. ﴿So leave them alone﴾ — His saying, may His praise be exalted, to the believers: So abandon their reproach, and leave them with what they have chosen for themselves of disbelief and hypocrisy. [[See the explanation of "al-i'rad" (turning away) earlier, p. 369, note 6, and the references there.]] ﴿Indeed, they are impure (rijs), and their refuge is Hell﴾, He says: Indeed, they are unclean [[See the explanation of "al-rijs" earlier, 12:194, note 3, and the references there.]] ﴿and their refuge is Hell﴾, He says: their destination is Hell, and it is their dwelling place which they will take as refuge in the Hereafter. [[See the explanation of "al-ma'wa" (refuge) earlier, p. 360, note 3, and the references there.]] ﴿a recompense for what they used to earn﴾ [[In the printed edition and the manuscript it reads "jaza'an bima kanu ya'malun" (what they used to do), which is, I believe, a copyist's error.]] He says: a reward for their deeds which they used to do in the world, of disobedience to Allah. [[See the explanation of "al-jaza'" (recompense) in the earlier vocabulary indexes under (j-z-y), and the explanation of "al-kasb" (earning) under (k-s-b).]]

* *

It is mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning two men among the hypocrites, who said:

17090 — Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to us, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿They will swear to you by Allah, when you return to them, that you may leave them alone﴾, up to: ﴿a recompense for what they used to earn.﴾ That was because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was told: "Will you not go out to fight the Banu al-Asfar? [["Banu al-Asfar" means the Romans.]] Perhaps you may take a daughter of the great man of the Romans, for their women are beautiful!" Two men said: "O Messenger of Allah, you know that women are a trial, so do not tempt us with them! Give us permission!" So he gave them permission. When the two of them set off, one of them said: "This is nothing but a morsel for the first eater!" [["The shahma" refers to a piece of the fat of a camel's hump, which is one of the choicest parts of the camel, and which the eater hastens to. Zufar ibn al-Harith al-Kilabi said: "We used to think every fair woman was a morsel, during the nights we clashed with Judham and Himyar. But when we clashed spear with spear, its shafts refused to break." And in the proverb: "Not every white thing is fat, nor every black thing a date."]] The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out, and nothing had been revealed to him concerning that. When he was in some part of the road, while he was at some water, this was revealed to him: ﴿Had it been a near gain and an easy journey, they would have followed you, but the distance seemed long to them﴾ (9:42), and this was revealed to him: ﴿Allah pardon you! Why did you give them permission?﴾ (9:43), and this was revealed to him: ﴿Those who believe in Allah and the Last Day do not ask your permission﴾ (9:44), and this was revealed to him: ﴿Indeed, they are impure, and their refuge is Hell, a recompense for what they used to earn.﴾ A man from among those who had gone out with the Prophet (ﷺ) heard that, so he came to them while they were behind, and said: "Do you know that some Qur'an has been revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) after you?" They said: "What did you hear?" He said: "I do not know, except that I heard him say: 'They are impure!'" Then a man called "Makhshiyy," [[In the manuscript: "Makhshi," and the correct form is that of the printed edition, "Makhshiyy ibn Humayr al-Ashja'i"; see his biography in al-Isabah.]] said: "By Allah, I would love to be flogged a hundred lashes, and that I were not with you!" So he came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "What brought you?" He said: "The face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is being scorched by the wind, while I am in shelter!" [["Safa'ahu al-nar, al-shams, al-sumum, tasfa'uhu safa'an" means it singed him slightly, changing the colour of his skin and darkening it. "Al-kinn" (with a kasra on the kaf) is what wards off heat and cold from buildings and dwellings, and anything that screens from the sun and the hot wind is a kinn.]] So Allah revealed to him: ﴿And among them is one who says: "Give me permission and do not tempt me"﴾ (9:49), and ﴿They said: "Do not go forth in the heat"﴾ (9:81). And concerning the man who said: "I would love to be flogged a hundred lashes," there was revealed the saying of Allah: ﴿The hypocrites fear that a surah will be sent down about them, informing them of what is in their hearts﴾ (9:64). Then a man who was with the Messenger of Allah said: "If these are as they say, there is no good among us!" This reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said to him: "Are you the one who spoke the word I heard?" He said: "No, by Him who revealed the Book to you!" So Allah revealed concerning him: ﴿They did say a word of disbelief, and they disbelieved after their Islam﴾ (9:74), and revealed concerning him: ﴿And among you are listeners to them, and Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers﴾ (9:47).

17091 — Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik informed me, that Abd Allah ibn Ka'b said: I heard Ka'b ibn Malik say: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned from Tabuk, he sat down for the people. When he did so, those who had stayed behind came, and began to make excuses to him and swear to him, and they were some eighty men. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) accepted their outward declarations, pledged allegiance to them, asked forgiveness for them, and left their inner states to Allah. Ka'b said: By Allah, Allah has never bestowed upon me any blessing after guiding me to Islam greater in my estimation than the truthfulness of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) toward him, that I did not lie to him and so perish as those who lied perished. Indeed, Allah said of those who lied, when the revelation was sent down, a worse thing than He said to anyone: ﴿They will swear to you by Allah, when you return to them, that you may leave them alone. So leave them alone. Indeed, they are impure, and their refuge is Hell, a recompense for what they used to earn,﴾ up to His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is not pleased with the defiant people.﴾ [[The report 17091 is an abridgement of the long report on the repentance of Ka'b ibn Malik, which Muslim narrated in his Sahih (17:87–100) by this chain, and a further part of it has passed under No. 16147.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 96:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿They swear to you that you may be pleased with them. But if you are pleased with them, indeed Allah is not pleased with a defiant people.﴾ (9:96)

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His mention, says: These hypocrites swear to you, O believers in Allah, offering excuses based on falsehood and lies, ﴿that you may be pleased with them. But if you are pleased with them, indeed Allah is not pleased with a defiant people.﴾ He means: if you, O believers, are pleased with them and accept their excuse, while you do not know their truthfulness from their lying, then your pleasure with them will not benefit them with Allah, because Allah knows the hidden matters of their affairs that you do not know, and the concealed beliefs that you are ignorant of, and that they are upon disbelief in Allah.......... [[I have no doubt that the place of these dots is a lacuna in the words of Abu Ja'far, from the copyist of his book, and the correct wording was probably: "and that they remain upon disbelief in Allah, and that they are the defiant ones, meaning: they are the ones who have gone out..." or words similar to this.]] He means that they have gone out from faith into disbelief in Allah, and from obedience into disobedience. [[See the explanation of "fisq" (defiance) earlier, p. 406, footnote 1, and the references there.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 97:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿The Bedouins are the most severe in disbelief and hypocrisy, and most likely not to know the limits of what Allah has revealed to His Messenger. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾ (9:97).

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: The Bedouins are more emphatic in denying the oneness of Allah, and more hypocritical, than the people of the settled towns and cities. He, may His praise be exalted, described them thus because of their harshness, the hardness of their hearts, and their infrequent association with the people of goodness. Because of that, they are harder of heart and less knowledgeable of the rights of Allah.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and most likely not to know the limits of what Allah has revealed to His Messenger﴾, it means: and most fitting that they not know the limits of what Allah has revealed to His Messenger [see the explanation of "the limits of Allah" above, 8:68, note 3, and the references there]. This, according to Qatadah, refers to the Sunan (the prophetic traditions and practices).

17092- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿and most likely not to know the limits of what Allah has revealed to His Messenger﴾, he said: They are less knowledgeable of the Sunan.

17093- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mughra' narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, who said: A Bedouin sat with Zayd ibn Sawhan while he was narrating to his companions, and his hand had been injured on the day of Nahawand. The Bedouin said: "By Allah, your speech pleases me, but your hand troubles me!" Zayd said: "What about my hand troubles you? It is the left hand!" The Bedouin said: "By Allah, I do not know, do they cut off the right hands or the left hands?" Zayd ibn Sawhan then said: "Allah has spoken truly: ﴿The Bedouins are the most severe in disbelief and hypocrisy, and most likely not to know the limits of what Allah has revealed to His Messenger﴾."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾, it means: ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing﴾ of who knows the limits of what was revealed to His Messenger, and of the hypocrite among His creatures and the disbeliever among them; none of them is hidden from Him. ﴿All-Wise﴾ in His management of them, and in His forbearance regarding their punishment, despite His knowledge of their inner secrets and their deception of His allies.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 98:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And among the desert Arabs are those who consider what they spend as a loss, and they await misfortunes to befall you. Upon them is the misfortune of evil, and Allah is Hearing and Knowing﴾ (9:98).

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says: Among the desert Arabs are those who count the spending they give in the struggle against a polytheist, or in aiding a Muslim, or in some of what Allah has urged His servants to do, as ﴿a loss﴾, meaning a burden imposed on them, for which they hope for no reward and by which they ward off no punishment from themselves. ﴿And they await misfortunes to befall you﴾, meaning: they wait for the turns of fortune against you [[See the explanation of "tarabbus" above, p. 291, note 2, and the references there.]], that the days and nights turn against you with what is disliked and the arrival of what is not loved, and the victory of an enemy over you. [[See the explanation of "dawa'ir" above, 10: 404.]] Allah, Exalted is He, says: ﴿Upon them is the misfortune of evil﴾, meaning: Allah has made the misfortune of evil fall upon them, and the descent of what is disliked upon them, not upon you, O believers, nor upon you = ﴿and Allah is Hearing﴾, of the supplications of those who supplicate = ﴿Knowing﴾ of their schemes, and of what descends upon them of the punishment of Allah, and of the painful punishment to which they are headed. [[See the explanation of "Hearing" and "Knowing" above in the lexical indices (sami'a), ('alima).]]

* *

And in accordance with what we have said on this, the people of interpretation have said.

Mention of those who said that:

17094 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning the words of Allah: ﴿And among the desert Arabs are those who consider what they spend as a loss, and they await misfortunes to befall you﴾, he said: These are the hypocrites among the desert Arabs, who spend only out of ostentation, for fear of being raided, fought, or made to fight, and they regard their spending as a loss. Do you not see that He says: ﴿They await misfortunes to befall you. Upon them is the misfortune of evil﴾?

* *

The readers differed in the recitation of this.

The majority of the readers of Medina and Kufa recited: ﴿عَلَيهِم دَائِرَةُ السَّوْءِ﴾ with a fatha on the sin, in the sense of an adjective to "the misfortune" (al-dA'ira), even though "the misfortune" is in construct with it, as in their saying: "he is a man of evil" (rajul al-sawʾ) and "a man of truth" (imru' al-sidq), since when the verbal noun from their saying "sa'ahu, as'uhu, sawan, wa-masa'atan, wa-masa'iyatan" is vocalized with a fatha, [it is used as an adjective]. [[See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 449, 450.]]

* *

Some people of the Hijaz and some Basrans recited it: ﴿عَلَيهِم دَائِرَةُ السُّوْءِ﴾ with a damma on the sin, as if they made it a noun, as one says: "upon him is the misfortune of calamity and punishment." Whoever says "upon them is the misfortune of evil" with a damma does not say "this is a man of evil" with a damma; rather "al-rajul al-sūʾ" [is used]. [[See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 450.]] The poet said: [[He is al-Farazdaq.]]

"And I was like the wolf of evil when it saw blood
in its companion one day, it turned upon the blood."

[[From his Diwan: 749; Tabaqat Fuhul al-Shu'ara': 306; al-Hayawan 5: 319, 6: 298; Lisan (h-w-l), and many others, from verses with a long story. His words "turned upon the blood" mean he came toward it. Two wolves may approach a man together in one approach, equal in their enmity and their resolve to eat him; but when one of them draws blood, it leaps upon its companion, tears it apart and eats it, leaving the man. (From the words of al-Jahiz.) Al-Farazdaq repeated this meaning in his saying: "A youth who is not to his paternal cousin like a wolf, if it sees in its companion blood one day, it is the one that eats it."]]

Abu Ja'far said: The correct recitation in this, in our view, is with a fatha on the sin, meaning: upon them is the misfortune that makes them suffer evil, as one says: "he is a man of truth," in the manner of an adjective.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 99:

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿And among the Bedouins are those who believe in God and the Last Day, and take what they spend as means of nearness to God and the prayers of the Messenger. Indeed, it is a means of nearness for them. God will admit them into His mercy. Indeed God is Forgiving, Merciful.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says: Among the Bedouins are those who affirm God and acknowledge His oneness, and (affirm) the resurrection after death, and the reward and punishment, and who intend, by what they spend of expenditure in the struggle against the polytheists, [[In the printed edition: "yanwi bima yunfiq" (intend by what they spend). I have adopted what is in the manuscript, which is correct.]] and in their journey with the Messenger of God (ﷺ), ﴿means of nearness to God﴾. "Qurbat" is the plural of "qurba," which is that which brings one near to God's pleasure and love. ﴿And the prayers of the Messenger﴾ means: they seek, by the expenditure of what they spend, together with seeking nearness to God, the Messenger's supplication and his asking forgiveness for them.

We have already shown, earlier in our book, that among the meanings of "salah" (prayer) is supplication, which makes repeating it unnecessary at this point. [[See the explanation of "salah" in the earlier linguistic indexes (s-l-w).]]

* *

The commentators (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

17095. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Salih told us, he said: Mu'awiya told us, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words ﴿and the prayers of the Messenger﴾: meaning the Prophet's asking forgiveness (upon him be prayers and peace).

17096. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatada regarding His words: ﴿And among the Bedouins are those who take what they spend as means of nearness to God and the prayers of the Messenger﴾, he said: "the prayers of the Messenger": He said: "This is God's exception (thaniyya) from among the Bedouins." [[Thaniyya: that which is excepted from something. In the saying of Ka'b al-Ahbar: "The martyrs are God's thaniyya on earth," meaning they are among those whom God excepted from the first blast, interpreting by His words, exalted is He: "And the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on earth will swoon, except whom God wills." So he made the martyrs among them, because they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision.]]

17097. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid regarding His words: ﴿And among the Bedouins are those who believe in God and the Last Day﴾, he said: "They are the Banu Muqarrin of Muzayna, and they are those about whom God said: ﴿Nor (is there blame) on those who came to you that you might provide them mounts, and you said, 'I cannot find anything to mount you on,' and they turned back while their eyes overflowed with tears out of grief﴾ [Surah al-Tawba: 92]." He said: "They are the Banu Muqarrin of Muzayna." He said: Hajjaj told me, he said: Ibn Jurayj said regarding His words: ﴿The Bedouins are more severe in disbelief and hypocrisy﴾, then He made an exception, saying: ﴿And among the Bedouins are those who believe in God and the Last Day﴾, to the end of the verse.

17098. Ahmad told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Ja'far told us, from al-Bakhtari ibn al-Mukhtar al-Abdi, who said: I heard Abd al-Rahman ibn Ma'qil say: "We were ten sons of Muqarrin, and this verse was revealed about us: ﴿And among the Bedouins are those who believe in God and the Last Day﴾," to the end of the verse. [[The report 17098: al-Bakhtari ibn al-Mukhtar al-Abdi is trustworthy (thiqa). He is biographically recorded in al-Kabir 1/2/136 and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/427.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Ma'qil al-Muzani is a trustworthy Successor (tabi'i), and some counted him among the Companions because of this report.

The Hafiz Ibn Hajar said: "He only meant by his saying 'we': his father and his paternal uncles, while he himself was too young for that. Among his uncles was Abd al-Rahman ibn Muqarrin, whom Ibn Sa'd mentioned among the Companions." He is biographically recorded in al-Tahdhib, Ibn Sa'd 6:122, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/284.

In the printed edition it read "Abd Allah ibn Mughaffal," which differs from the manuscript; it substituted, distorted, and erred in a way that admits no excuse.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: God said: ﴿Indeed, it is a means of nearness for them﴾, meaning, exalted is He: Indeed the prayers of the Messenger are a means of nearness for them to God.

It may also be that its meaning is: indeed, the expenditure they spend in this manner is a means of nearness for them with God. ﴿God will admit them into His mercy﴾, meaning: God will admit them among those whom He has shown mercy, and He will cause them to enter Paradise by His mercy. ﴿Indeed God is Forgiving﴾ toward what they have committed, ﴿Merciful﴾ toward them, so that, given their repentance and reform, He does not punish them. [[See the explanation of "Ghafur" (Forgiving) and "Rahim" (Merciful) in the earlier linguistic indexes (gh-f-r) and (r-h-m).]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 100:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And the foremost, the first of the Emigrants and the Helpers, and those who followed them in goodness—Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. And He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the great achievement.﴾ (9:100)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: those who preceded the people first to faith in Allah and His Messenger, ﴿of the Emigrants﴾, who emigrated from their people and kin, and departed from their dwellings and homelands [[See the explanation of "hijrah" (emigration) above, p. 173, note 4, and the references there.]], ﴿and the Helpers﴾, who supported the Messenger of Allah ﷺ against his enemies from among the people of disbelief in Allah and His Messenger [[See the explanation of "Ansar" (Helpers) above, 10:481, note 5, and the references there.]], ﴿and those who followed them in goodness﴾, meaning: those who trod their path in faith in Allah and His Messenger, and in emigrating from the abode of war to the abode of Islam, seeking the pleasure of Allah [[See the explanation of "ihsan" (goodness) in the lexical indices above under (ḥ-s-n).]], ﴿Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him.﴾

The people of interpretation differed concerning the referent of His saying: ﴿And the foremost, the first﴾.

Some of them said: They are those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the Pledge of al-Ridwan (Pledge of Good Pleasure), or who attained it.

Those who said this:

17099. Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Bishr related to us, from Isma'il, from 'Amir: ﴿And the foremost, the first﴾, he said: Those who attained the Pledge of al-Ridwan.

17100. ...... He said: Ibn Fudayl related to us, from Mutarrif, from 'Amir, who said: ﴿The first Emigrants﴾: those who attained the pledge under the tree.

17101. Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Yahya related to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid related to us, from al-Sha'bi, who said: ﴿The first Emigrants﴾: those who witnessed the Pledge of al-Ridwan.

17102. al-Harith related to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Mutarrif, from al-Sha'bi, who said: "The first Emigrants": whoever was before the pledge up to the pledge, these are the first Emigrants, and whoever came after the pledge is not among the first Emigrants.

17103. al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Isma'il and Mutarrif informed us, from al-Sha'bi, who said: ﴿And the foremost, the first of the Emigrants and the Helpers﴾: they are those who pledged the Pledge of al-Ridwan.

17104. al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Awn related to us, saying: Hushaym related to us, from Dawud, from 'Amir, who said: The distinction between the two emigrations is the Pledge of al-Ridwan, which is the Pledge of al-Hudaybiyah.

17105. al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Awn informed us, saying: Hushaym informed us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid and Mutarrif informed us, from al-Sha'bi, who said: They are those who pledged the Pledge of al-Ridwan.

17106. Ahmad ibn Ishaq related to us, saying: Abu Ahmad related to us, saying: 'Abthar Abu Zubayd related to us, from Mutarrif, from al-Sha'bi, who said: The first Emigrants are those who attained the Pledge of al-Ridwan. [[The report 17106: "'Abthar, Abu Zubayd" is 'Abthar ibn al-Qasim al-Zubaydi, Abu Zubayd, who has passed as no. 12402 and elsewhere.]]

* *

Others said: Rather, they are those who prayed towards both qiblahs with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

Those who said this:

17107. Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Adam related to us, from Qays, from 'Uthman al-Thaqafi, from a freedman of Abu Musa, from Abu Musa, who said: The first Emigrants are those who prayed towards both qiblahs with the Prophet ﷺ.

17108. al-Harith related to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz related to us, saying: Qays ibn al-Rabi' related to us, from 'Uthman ibn al-Mughirah, from Abu Zur'ah ibn 'Amr ibn Jarir, from a freedman of Abu Musa, who said: I asked Abu Musa al-Ash'ari about His saying: ﴿And the foremost, the first of the Emigrants and the Helpers﴾, and he said: They are those who prayed towards both qiblahs together.

17109. Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: my father related to us, from Abu Hilal, from Qatadah, who said: I said to Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: Why were they called "the first Emigrants"? He said: Whoever prayed with the Prophet ﷺ towards both qiblahs together, he is among the first Emigrants.

17110. Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id related to us, from Ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: The first Emigrants are those who prayed towards both qiblahs.

17111. Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, regarding his saying: ﴿And the foremost, the first of the Emigrants and the Helpers﴾, he said: They are those who prayed towards both qiblahs together.

17112. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: 'Abbas ibn al-Walid related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, the like of it.

17113. al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Awn related to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from some of his companions, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab = and from Ash'ath, from Ibn Sirin = regarding His saying: ﴿And the foremost, the first﴾, he said: They are those who prayed towards both qiblahs.

17114. Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Mu'adh ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Ibn 'Awn related to us, from Muhammad, who said: The first Emigrants: those who prayed towards both qiblahs.

17115. al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And the foremost, the first of the Emigrants and the Helpers﴾, he said: They are those who prayed towards both qiblahs together.

* *

As for those who followed the first Emigrants and the Helpers in goodness, they are those who submitted to Allah with the submission of those (before them), and followed their method in emigration, support, and righteous deeds. As related:

17116. Ahmad ibn Ishaq related to us, saying: Abu Ahmad related to us, saying: Abu Ma'shar related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, who said: 'Umar passed by a man who was reciting this verse: ﴿And the foremost, the first of the Emigrants and the Helpers and those who followed them in goodness﴾, and he said: Who taught you this verse? [[This is 'Umar's question, as will appear in no. 17118, concerning the recitation of the verse with the genitive "al-Ansar" joined by "wa" to "alladhina", whereas his own recitation was the nominative "al-Ansar" and without "wa" before "alladhina ittaba'uhum".]] He said: Ubayy ibn Ka'b taught it to me. He said: Do not leave me until I take you to him! So he came to him and said: Did you recite this verse this way? He said: Yes! He said: And did you hear it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?! He said: [Yes!]. [[The bracketed addition is necessary and is not in the manuscript or the printed edition; I have taken it from Ibn Kathir's tafsir, 4:229.]] Indeed, I used to think we had been raised to a rank that no one after us would reach! Ubayy said: Its confirmation is in the beginning of the verse in the beginning of al-Jumu'ah, the middle of al-Hashr, and the end of al-Anfal. As for the beginning of al-Jumu'ah: ﴿And others among them who have not yet joined them﴾, [Surah al-Jumu'ah: 3], and the middle of al-Hashr: ﴿And those who came after them say: Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith﴾, [Surah al-Hashr: 10], and the end of al-Anfal: ﴿And those who believed after and emigrated and strove with you—those are of you﴾, [Surah al-Anfal: 75].

17117. Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn 'Atiyah related to us, saying: Abu Ma'shar related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab passed by a man reciting: ﴿And the foremost, the first of the Emigrants and the Helpers﴾, until he reached: ﴿and they are pleased with Him﴾. He said: 'Umar took his hand and said: Who taught you this? He said: Ubayy ibn Ka'b! He said: Do not leave me until I take you to him! When he came to him, 'Umar said: Did you recite this verse like this? He said: Yes! He said: Did you hear it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? He said: Yes! He said: I had thought we had been raised to a rank no one after us would reach! Ubayy said: Indeed, the confirmation of this verse is in the beginning of Surah al-Jumu'ah: ﴿And others among them who have not yet joined them﴾, up to: ﴿and He is the Mighty, the Wise﴾, and in Surah al-Hashr: ﴿And those who came after them say: Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith﴾, and in al-Anfal: ﴿And those who believed after and emigrated and strove with you—those are of you﴾, to the end of the verse.

* *

It has been related from 'Umar concerning this what follows:

17118. Ahmad ibn Yusuf related to me, saying: al-Qasim related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to us, from Harun, from Habib ibn al-Shahid, and from Ibn 'Amir al-Ansari: that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab recited: ﴿And the foremost, the first of the Emigrants and the Helpers and those who followed them in goodness﴾, raising "al-Ansar" and not adding the waw to "alladhina". Zayd ibn Thabit said to him: "wa-alladhina ittaba'uhum bi-ihsan" (with waw). 'Umar said: "alladhina ittaba'uhum bi-ihsan." Zayd said: The Commander of the Faithful knows best! 'Umar said: Bring me Ubayy ibn Ka'b. He came, and he asked him about it, and Ubayy said: ﴿wal-ladhina ittaba'uhum bi-ihsan﴾. 'Umar said: Then we will follow Ubayy.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The recitation with the genitive "al-Ansar", coordinated with "al-Muhajirin", is the reading.

* *

It has been mentioned from al-Hasan al-Basri that he used to recite ﴿al-Ansaru﴾ with the nominative, coordinating them with "al-sabiqun".

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The recitation I do not permit other than is the genitive in ﴿al-Ansari﴾, because the Muslim scholars of recitation (qurra') agree upon it, and because the foremost were from both groups together, the Emigrants and the Helpers; the statement intends to report about the foremost from both groups, not a report about all of them. And the adding of the "waw" in "alladhina ittaba'uhum bi-ihsan" [[His saying: "and the adding of the waw" is coordinated with his saying: "The recitation I do not permit other than, the genitive..."]] because that is so in the codices of all Muslims, and because "those who follow in goodness" are other than "the Emigrants and the Helpers". As for "the foremost", they are in the nominative by the pronoun referring back to them in His saying: ﴿Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him.﴾

* *

The meaning of the statement: Allah is pleased with all of them, because they obeyed Him and answered His Prophet in what he called them to of His commands and prohibitions; and the foremost first of the Emigrants and the Helpers, and those who followed them in goodness, are pleased with Him, because of the abundant reward He bestowed upon them for their obedience to Him and their faith in Him and His Prophet, peace be upon him. ﴿And He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾, they will enter them; ﴿abiding therein﴾, remaining therein; ﴿forever﴾, they will not die therein nor leave from it; ﴿That is the great achievement.﴾

**The Commentary of Abu Ja'far al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 9, Verse 101**

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿Among those around you of the Bedouins are hypocrites, and among the people of Madinah are those who have persisted in hypocrisy. You do not know them; We know them. We will punish them twice; then they will be returned to a great punishment.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Among the people around your city of the Bedouins are hypocrites, and among the people of your city too there are similar groups who are hypocrites.

* *

As for His words ﴿persisted in hypocrisy﴾, it means: they became accustomed to it and trained themselves in it.

From the same root comes the expression "a rebellious devil (shaytan mārid) and a defiant one (marīd)," meaning the wicked and obstinate one. From it is said: "So-and-so rebelled against his Lord (tamarrada 'alā rabbihi)," meaning he became arrogant, and became accustomed to disobedience to Him and habituated to it. [[See the explanation of "marīd" above, vol. 9, pp. 211–212. In the printed edition: "meaning he was arrogant and persisted in his disobedience…", and the correct reading is what appears in the manuscript.]]

* *

Ibn Zayd said concerning this:

17119 – Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words ﴿And among the people of Madinah are those who have persisted in hypocrisy﴾: they remained upon it and did not repent as the others repented.

17120 – Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿And among the people of Madinah are those who have persisted in hypocrisy﴾, meaning: they insisted upon it and refused anything else. [[The report 17120 is in Ibn Hisham's Sirah 4:198, and it follows the earlier report no. 17089.]]

* *

As for His words ﴿You do not know them﴾, it means that He says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): You do not know, O Muhammad, these hypocrites whose description I have given you, from among those around you of the Bedouins and the people of Madinah; but We know them. As follows:

17121 – Al-Hasan related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah regarding His words ﴿And among those around you of the Bedouins are hypocrites﴾ up to His words ﴿We know them﴾, he said: What is the matter with people who take upon themselves to know the affairs of others? "So-and-so is in Paradise, and so-and-so is in Hell!" When you ask one of them about himself, he says, "I do not know!" By my life, you know yourself better than you know the deeds of people, and you have undertaken something that the prophets before you did not undertake! The Prophet of God, Noah (peace be upon him), said: ﴿And I have no knowledge of what they used to do﴾ [Surah al-Shu'ara': 112], and the Prophet of God, Shu'ayb (peace be upon him), said: ﴿The remainder of God is better for you, if you are believers. And I am not a watcher over you﴾ [Surah Hud: 86], and God said to His Prophet (peace be upon him): ﴿You do not know them; We know them.﴾

* *

As for His words ﴿We will punish them twice﴾, it means: We will punish these hypocrites twice, one of them in this world and the other in the grave.

* *

Then the people of interpretation differed concerning the punishment in this world, what it is.

Some of them said: It is their disgrace; God disgraced them by exposing their affairs and clarifying their inner secrets to the people through the tongue of the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

* *

Those who said this:

17122 – Al-Husayn ibn Amr al-Anqazi related to us, saying: My father related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik, from Ibn Abbas regarding God's words ﴿And among those around you of the Bedouins are hypocrites, and among the people of Madinah are those who have persisted in hypocrisy﴾ up to His words ﴿a great punishment﴾, he said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) stood delivering a sermon on Friday and said: "Go out, so-and-so, for you are a hypocrite! Go out, so-and-so, for you are a hypocrite!" He expelled some of them from the mosque, disgracing them. Then Umar came upon them as they were leaving the mosque, and he hid from them out of shame that he had not attended the Friday prayer, and he thought that the people had dispersed; and they too hid from Umar, thinking that he had learned of their affair. Then Umar came and entered the mosque, and found that the people had not yet prayed. A man from among the Muslims said to him: Rejoice, O Umar, for God has disgraced the hypocrites today! So this is the first punishment, when He expelled them from the mosque; and the second punishment is the punishment of the grave. [[The report 17122 was narrated by al-Haythami in Majma' al-Zawa'id 7:33, where he said: "It was related by al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, and in its chain is al-Husayn ibn Amr ibn Muhammad al-Anqazi, who is weak."]]

17123 – Al-Harith related to me, saying: Abd al-Aziz related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik: ﴿We will punish them twice﴾, he said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to deliver a sermon in which he mentioned the hypocrites, and he would punish them with his tongue; and the punishment of the grave.

* *

[Others said: What befalls them of captivity, killing, hunger and fear in this world.] [[This heading in brackets is not in the manuscript or the printed edition; I have inferred it from the context of the following reports.]]

* *

Those who said this:

17124 – Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿We will punish them twice﴾, he said: killing and captivity.

17125 – Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿We will punish them twice﴾, with hunger, and the punishment of the grave. He said: ﴿Then they will be returned to a great punishment﴾, on the Day of Resurrection. [[In the printed edition: "with hunger…", with the letter bā' at its beginning; I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

17126 – Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Awn, al-Qasim, and Yahya ibn Adam related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words ﴿We will punish them twice﴾, he said: with hunger and killing. Yahya said: fear and killing. [[In the printed edition: "with hunger…", with the letter bā' at its beginning; I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

17127 – Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Yaman related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: with hunger and killing.

17128 – Ibn Wakf'i related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Yaman related to us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik: ﴿We will punish them twice﴾, he said: with hunger, and the punishment of the grave.

17129 – Ahmad ibn Ishaq related to us, saying: Abu Ahmad related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿We will punish them twice﴾, he said: hunger and killing. [[In the printed edition: "with hunger", and I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: We will punish them with a punishment in this world and a punishment in the Hereafter.

Those who said this:

17130 – Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿We will punish them twice﴾, the punishment of this world and the punishment of the grave; ﴿then they will be returned to a great punishment﴾. It has been related to us that the Prophet of God (ﷺ) confided to Hudhayfah the names of twelve men among the hypocrites, and said: "Six of them, the ad-Dubaylah will suffice for them [[The word "ad-Dubaylah" in lexicography means a large abscess and boil that appears in the abdomen, which usually kills its sufferer; it is a diminutive of "dublah" (with a dammah on the dal and a sukun on the bā'), having a similar meaning.]], a lamp of the fire of Hell, which seizes one of them in the shoulder until it reaches his chest; and six will die a natural death." It has been related to us that Umar ibn al-Khattab (may God have mercy on him), whenever a man died whom he thought to be one of them, looked at Hudhayfah: if he prayed over him, he (Umar) would do so; otherwise he left him. It has been related to us that Umar said to Hudhayfah: I adjure you by God, am I among them? He said: No, by God, and I will not absolve anyone after you!

17131 – Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan: ﴿We will punish them twice﴾, he said: the punishment of this world and the punishment of the grave.

17132 – Muhammad ibn Bashshar and Muhammad ibn al-Ala' related to us, both saying: Badal ibn al-Muhabbar related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿We will punish them twice﴾, he said: a punishment in this world and a punishment in the grave.

17133 – Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraj, who said: the punishment of this world and the punishment of the grave; then they will be returned to the punishment of the Fire.

* *

Others said: Their punishment was one of the two times: their calamities in their wealth and children; and the other time is in Hell.

Those who said this:

17134 – Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: ﴿We will punish them twice﴾, he said: As for the punishment in this world, it is wealth and children. He recited the saying of God: ﴿So let not their wealth nor their children impress you; God only intends to punish them thereby in the life of this world﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 55], with calamities upon them; these are a punishment for them, and for the believers they are a reward. He said: And a punishment in the Hereafter, in the Fire; ﴿then they will be returned to a great punishment﴾, he said: the Fire.

* *

Others said: Rather, one of the two times is the prescribed punishments (hudud), and the other is the punishment of the grave.

This was related from Ibn Abbas through a chain that is not accepted. [[In the printed edition: "not approved". I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

* *

Others said: Rather, one of the two times is the taking of zakat from their wealth, and the other is the punishment of the grave. This was related from Sulayman ibn Arqam, from al-Hasan.

* *

Others said: Rather, one of the two times is their punishment by what enters upon them of rage at the affairs of Islam.

Those who said this:

17135 – Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿We will punish them twice﴾, he said: The punishment that He promised them twice, as it has reached me, is their grief at what they are in regarding the affairs of Islam, and what enters upon them of rage at that without reckoning; then their punishment in the grave when they go to it; then the great punishment to which they will be returned, the punishment of the Hereafter, and abiding forever in it. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "as it has reached me from them what they are in regarding the affairs of Islam"; the correct reading is from Ibn Hisham's Sirah. In the printed edition: "and they will abide in it", while the manuscript reads "and abides in it"; the correct reading is from Ibn Hisham's Sirah.]] [[The report 17135 is in Ibn Hisham's Sirah 4:198, and it follows the earlier report no. 17120.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these opinions in my view is to say that God informed that He will punish those who have persisted in hypocrisy twice, and He did not provide us with any evidence by which we could arrive at knowledge of the nature of those two punishments, [[In the printed edition: "by which we could arrive", and I have kept what is in the manuscript.]] though it is possible that some of what we have mentioned from those who spoke is what has been reported to us about them; and we have no knowledge of which of these is which. [[In the printed edition: "which of that is from which," and the phrase "in His words" was altered and corrupted, distorting the meaning entirely. See the discussion of "which of that was from which" above, p. 365, note 1, and the references there, for its like has passed many times and the copyist garbled it.]] However, in His words, may His praise be exalted: ﴿then they will be returned to a great punishment﴾, there is an indication that the punishment in both times occurs before they enter the Fire. And the more likely interpretation regarding one of the two times is that it is in the grave.

* *

As for His words ﴿then they will be returned to a great punishment﴾, it means: then these hypocrites, after God has punished them twice, will be returned to a great punishment, and that is the punishment of Hell.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 102:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And others have acknowledged their sins; they had mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil. Perhaps Allah will turn to them in forgiveness. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (9:102)

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, says: "And among the people of Madinah are hypocrites who persisted in hypocrisy. And among them are 'others who acknowledged their sins'," meaning: they confessed their sins. ﴿They had mixed a righteous deed﴾ — by the righteous deed that He, mighty is His praise, means here, which they mixed with the evil deed: their acknowledgment of their sins and their repentance from them. And "another that was evil" is their staying behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he went out to fight, and their abandoning jihad with the Muslims.

* *

If someone says: How is it said, ﴿they had mixed a righteous deed and another that was evil,﴾ when the phrase should be: they had mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil?

It is said: The grammarians have differed on this.

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: It is said thus, and it is permissible in Arabic that it be "bi-akhara" (with another), as you say "istawa al-ma'u wa-l-khashaba" (the water and the wood became level), meaning: with the wood, and "khalatu al-ma'a wa-l-laban" (I mixed the water and the milk).

And [Akhar] denied that this is like their saying "istawa al-ma'u wa-l-khashaba." He argued for this on the basis that the verb "mixing" governs both the first and the second, and it is permissible to place each of them before the other, whereas placing "the wood" before "the water" is not permissible in their saying "istawa al-ma'u wa-l-khashaba," and this was for them a proof of the difference of that "mixing." Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this, in my opinion, is that it has the meaning of their saying "khalatu al-ma'a wa-l-laban," meaning: I mixed it with the milk.

* *

﻿"Perhaps Allah will turn to them in forgiveness" means: perhaps Allah will turn to them. "Perhaps" (ʿasā) from Allah is binding, and its meaning is: Allah will surely turn to them, but it is in the speech of the Arabs as I have described. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ means: Indeed Allah is possessed of pardon and forgiveness toward whoever repents from his sins, and covers them over for him; "Merciful" means: toward him, that He should punish him for them.

* *

The people of interpretation have differed concerning who is meant by this verse, and the reason for which it was revealed.

Some of them said: It was revealed concerning ten men who had stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the Battle of Tabuk, among them Abu Lubabah. Seven of them tied themselves to the pillars when the Prophet (ﷺ) arrived, as repentance for their sin.

Those who said this:

17136- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: ﴿And others have acknowledged their sins; they had mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil﴾, he said: They were ten men who stayed behind from the Prophet (ﷺ) in the Battle of Tabuk. When the Prophet's (ﷺ) return drew near, seven of them tied themselves to the pillars of the mosque, and the Prophet (ﷺ) passed by them in the mosque when he returned.

When he saw them, he said: "Who are these who have tied themselves to the pillars?" They said: "This is Abu Lubabah and companions of his who stayed behind from you, O Messenger of Allah, [and swore that no one would release them] until you release them and excuse them." The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "And I swear by Allah that I will not release them nor excuse them until Allah is the one who releases them. They turned away from me and stayed behind from the campaign with the Muslims!" When this reached them, they said: "And we will not release ourselves until Allah is the one who releases us!" So Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed: ﴿And others have acknowledged their sins; they had mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil. Perhaps Allah will turn to them in forgiveness﴾ — and "perhaps" from Allah is binding. When it was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) sent for them, released them, and excused them.

* *

Others said: Rather, they were six, one of them Abu Lubabah.

Those who said this:

17137- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, he said: My paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: ﴿And others have acknowledged their sins; they had mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil. Perhaps Allah…﴾, to His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. The reason was that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out on the Battle of Tabuk, and Abu Lubabah and five with him stayed behind from the Prophet (ﷺ). Then Abu Lubabah and two men with him reflected and regretted, and were certain of destruction, and said: "We remain in shelter and tranquility with the women, while the Messenger of Allah and the believers with him are in jihad! By Allah, we will tie ourselves to the pillars, and not release ourselves until the Messenger of Allah himself releases us and excuses us." So Abu Lubabah went and tied himself, and two men with him, to the pillars of the mosque, and three men remained who did not tie themselves. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned from his campaign, and his path was through the mosque, so he passed by them and said: "Who are these who have tied themselves to the pillars?" They said: "This is Abu Lubabah and companions of his, who stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). They pledged to Allah that they would not release themselves until you are the one who releases them and is pleased with them, and they have acknowledged their sins." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By Allah, I will not release them until I am commanded to release them, nor excuse them until Allah is the one who excuses them, for they stayed behind from me and turned themselves away from the campaign and jihad of the Muslims!" So Allah revealed in His mercy: ﴿And others have acknowledged their sins; they had mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil. Perhaps Allah will turn to them in forgiveness. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ — and "perhaps" from Allah is binding. When the verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) released them, excused them, and overlooked them.

* *

Others said: Those who tied themselves to the pillars were eight.

Those who said this:

17138- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Ya'qub narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam: ﴿And others have acknowledged their sins…﴾, he said: They are the eight who tied themselves to the pillars, among them Kurdam, Mirdas, and Abu Lubabah.

17139- Ibn Waki' narrated to us, he said: Jarir narrated to us, from Ya'qub, from Ja'far, from Sa'id who said: Those who tied themselves to the pillars: Hilal, Abu Lubabah, Kurdam, Mirdas, and Abu Qays. [These are five; he did not mention the full eight, as the context of the speech indicates.]

* *

Others said: They were seven.

Those who said this:

17140- Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: ﴿And others have acknowledged their sins; they had mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil. Perhaps Allah will turn to them in forgiveness﴾, he said: It was mentioned to us that they were seven men who stayed behind from the Battle of Tabuk. As for four of them, they had mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil: Jadd ibn Qays, Abu Lubabah, Haram, and Aws, all of them from the Ansar, and they are the ones concerning whom it was said: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity that purifies them﴾, the verse.

17141- Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿they had mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil﴾, he said: They were a group of those who stayed behind from Tabuk, among them Abu Lubabah, and among them Jadd ibn Qays, and they were forgiven. Qatadah said: And they were not three.

17142- Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿And others have acknowledged their sins﴾, he said: They were seven, among them Abu Lubabah, who stayed behind from the Battle of Tabuk, and they were not the three.

17143- It was narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: ʿUbayd ibn Sulayman informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿And others have acknowledged their sins; they had mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil﴾: It was revealed concerning Abu Lubabah and his companions, who stayed behind from the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) in the Battle of Tabuk. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned from his campaign, and he was near Madinah, they regretted their staying behind from the Messenger of Allah and said: "We remain in the shade, the food, and the women, while the Prophet of Allah is in jihad and hardship! By Allah, we will surely tie ourselves to the pillars, then not release ourselves until the Prophet of Allah releases us and excuses us!" They tied themselves, and three remained who did not tie themselves to the pillars. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came from his campaign, passed through the mosque, which was on his route, saw them, and asked about them. He was told: "Abu Lubabah and his companions, who stayed behind from you, O Prophet of Allah, have done to themselves what you see, and pledged to Allah that they would not release themselves until you are the one who releases them!" The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I will not release them until I am commanded to release them, nor excuse them until Allah excuses them; they have turned themselves away from the campaign of the Muslims!" So Allah revealed: ﴿And others have acknowledged their sins﴾, up to: ﴿Perhaps Allah will turn to them in forgiveness﴾ — and "perhaps" from Allah is binding — so the Prophet of Allah released them and excused them.

* *

Others said: Rather, this verse refers specifically to Abu Lubabah, and the sin for which he acknowledged and was forgiven was what occurred concerning him regarding the Banu Qurayzah.

Those who said this:

17144- Ibn Waki' narrated to us, he said: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And others have acknowledged their sins﴾, he said: It was revealed concerning Abu Lubabah, when he said to the Banu Qurayzah what he said.

17145- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, he said: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, he said: ʿIsa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And others have acknowledged their sins﴾, he said: It was Abu Lubabah, when he said to Qurayzah what he said, gesturing to his throat: "Muhammad will slaughter you if you come down under the judgment of Allah."

17146- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, he said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who mentioned something similar, except that he said: "If you come down under his judgment."

17147- Ibn Waki' narrated to us, he said: Jarir narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid: Abu Lubabah tied himself to a pillar and said: "I will not loosen myself until Allah and His Messenger loosen me!" He said: The Prophet (ﷺ) untied him, and this verse was revealed concerning it: (And others have acknowledged their sins; they had mixed a righteous deed…), the verse.

17148- Ibn Waki' narrated to us, he said: Al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid: ﴿And others have acknowledged their sins﴾, he said: It was revealed concerning Abu Lubabah.

* *

Others said: Rather, it was revealed concerning Abu Lubabah, because of his staying behind from Tabuk.

Those who said this:

17149- Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, who said: Al-Zuhri said: Abu Lubabah was among those who stayed behind from the Prophet (ﷺ) in the Battle of Tabuk, and he tied himself to a pillar and said: "By Allah, I will not loosen myself from it, nor taste food or drink, until I die or Allah turns to me in forgiveness!" He remained for seven days without tasting food or drink, until he fell down unconscious. He said: Then Allah turned to him in forgiveness, and it was said to him: "You have been forgiven, O Abu Lubabah!" He said: "By Allah, I will not loosen myself until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) himself loosens me!" He said: So the Prophet (ﷺ) came and loosened him with his own hand. Then Abu Lubabah said: "O Messenger of Allah, among my repentance is that I abandon the house of my people in which I committed the sin, and that I strip myself of all my wealth as charity to Allah and to His Messenger!" He said: "A third will suffice you, O Abu Lubabah."

* *

Some of them said: By this verse is meant the Bedouins.

Those who said this:

17150- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, he said: My paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿And others have acknowledged their sins; they had mixed a righteous deed with another that was evil﴾, he said: He said they are from the Bedouins.

17151- Ibn Waki' narrated to us, he said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, from Hajjaj ibn Abi Zaynab, who said: I heard Abu ʿUthman say: There is no verse in the Qur'an more hopeful to me for this Ummah than His saying: ﴿And others have acknowledged their sins﴾, up to: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these opinions regarding this matter is the view of the one who said: This verse was revealed concerning those who acknowledged the error of their deed in staying behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and abandoning jihad with him, and going out to fight the Romans, when he set out for Tabuk. And that those concerning whom it was revealed were a group, among whom was Abu Lubabah.

We say that this is more correct because Allah, mighty is His praise, said: ﴿And others have acknowledged their sins﴾, and He informed of the acknowledgment of a group of their sins. And the one who acknowledged his sin and tied himself to a pillar during the siege of Qurayzah was none other than Abu Lubabah alone. Since that is so, and since Allah, blessed and exalted, described in His saying: ﴿And others have acknowledged their sins﴾ a group as acknowledging their sins, it is known that the group He described thus is not a single individual. Thus it has become clear that since this attribute belongs only to a group, and no group did that, as reported by the historians and narrators and agreed upon by the people of interpretation, except a group of those who stayed behind from the Battle of Tabuk, what we have said is correct. And we said, "Abu Lubabah was among them," on the consensus of the authoritative scholars of interpretation on this.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 9, Verse 103:

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cleanse them, and pray for them. Indeed, your prayer is a comfort for them. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing﴾ (9:103)

Abu Ja'far said: The Exalted says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): O Muhammad, take from the wealth of those who have acknowledged their sins and repented of them = ﴿a charity that purifies them﴾, from the defilement of their sins [[See the explanation of "purification" (al-tathir) above, 12:549, note 2, and the references there.]] = ﴿and cleanses them thereby﴾, meaning: and raises them up and elevates them by it from the base ranks of the hypocrites to the ranks of the sincere [[See the explanation of "purification" (al-tazkiyah) in the lexical indices above under (z-k-a).]] = ﴿and pray for them﴾, meaning: invoke forgiveness for their sins and ask forgiveness for them from them = ﴿Indeed, your prayer is a comfort for them﴾, meaning: indeed, your supplication and your seeking of forgiveness is a reassurance for them, that Allah has pardoned them and accepted their repentance [[See the explanation of "prayer" (al-salah) above in the lexical indices under (s-l-a), and the explanation of "comfort" (sakan) above, 11:557.]] = ﴿And Allah is Hearing and Knowing﴾, meaning: Allah hears your supplication when you pray for them, and whatever else His creatures say = ﴿Knowing﴾, of what you seek for them by your supplication to your Lord for them, and of other matters concerning His servants. [[See the explanation of "Hearing" and "Knowing" above in the lexical indices under (s-m-' ) and ('-l-m).]]

* *

Likewise, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said what we have said.

Those who said so:

17152. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: They brought their wealth — meaning Abu Lubabah and his companions — when they were released, and they said: O Messenger of Allah, these are our possessions, so give charity from them on our behalf, and seek forgiveness for us! He said: I was not commanded to take anything from your wealth! So Allah revealed: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity﴾, meaning by the zakat: obedience to Allah and sincerity = ﴿and pray for them﴾, meaning: seek forgiveness for them.

17153. Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) released Abu Lubabah and his two companions, Abu Lubabah and his two companions set out with their wealth and brought it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they said: Take from our wealth and give charity from it on our behalf, and pray for us = they mean: seek forgiveness for us = and purify us. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: I will not take anything from it until I am commanded. So Allah revealed: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cleanse them, and pray for them, indeed your prayer is a comfort for them﴾, meaning: seek forgiveness for them from their sins which they had committed. When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took a portion of their wealth and gave it in charity on their behalf.

17154. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Ya'qub related to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: When the Prophet (ﷺ) released Abu Lubabah and those who had tied themselves to the pillars, they said: O Messenger of Allah, take from our wealth a charity that purifies us by it! So Allah revealed: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity that purifies them﴾, the verse.

17155. Ibn WakI' related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Ya'qub, from Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Those who had tied themselves to the pillars said, when he pardoned them: O Prophet of Allah, purify our wealth! So Allah revealed: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cleanse them﴾. Whenever one of the three fell ill, the other two would fall ill like him, and two of them went blind, and the third kept supplicating until he too went blind.

17156. Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, who said: The four: Jadd ibn Qays, Abu Lubabah, Haram, and Aws, are the ones about whom it was said: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cleanse them, and pray for them; indeed your prayer is a comfort for them﴾, meaning: a tranquility for them. And they had pledged from themselves that they would spend, strive, and give charity.

17157. It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say: When the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) released Abu Lubabah and his companions, they brought their wealth to the Prophet of Allah and said: O Prophet of Allah, take from our wealth and give charity from it on our behalf, and purify us, and pray for us! They mean: seek forgiveness for us. The Prophet of Allah said: I will not take anything from your wealth until I am commanded concerning it. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity that purifies them﴾, from their sins which they had committed = ﴿and pray for them﴾, meaning: seek forgiveness for them. The Prophet of Allah, peace be upon him, did what Allah had commanded him.

17158. Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said concerning His saying: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity﴾: Abu Lubabah and his companions. = ﴿and pray for them﴾, meaning: seek forgiveness for them, for their sins which they had committed.

17159. Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cleanse them, and pray for them; indeed your prayer is a comfort for them﴾: These are people from among the hypocrites who had stayed behind from the Prophet (ﷺ) in the expedition of Tabuk. They acknowledged hypocrisy and said: O Messenger of Allah, we have doubted, been hypocritical and wavered, but here is a fresh repentance, and a charity we will bring out from our wealth! So Allah said to His Prophet, peace be upon him: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cleanse them﴾, after He had said: ﴿And do not pray over any of them who has died, ever, nor stand at his grave﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 84].

* *

The grammarians (ahl al-'Arabiyyah) differed concerning the grammatical basis for the nominative case of "tuzakkihim" (they cleanse them).

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: "tuzakkihim bihā" is nominative as a new (inceptive) clause, and if you wish you may make it a qualifier of "ṣadaqah" (charity), then you bring it as an emphasis, and likewise "tuṭahhiruhum" (they purify them).

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: If His saying ﴿tuṭahhirahum﴾ refers to the Prophet, peace be upon him, then the preferred reading is the jussive, because no pronoun returns to "ṣadaqah" (charity), and ﴿tuzakkihim﴾ is a resumed (independent) clause. But if the charity purifies them and you cleanse them by it, it is permissible to put both verbs in the jussive or in the nominative.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view in this matter is that His saying ﴿tuṭahhirahum﴾ is a relative (descriptive) clause of "ṣadaqah," because the readers (al-qurra') are agreed on its nominative case, and this is evidence that it is a relative clause of "ṣadaqah." As for His saying ﴿wa-tuzakkihim bihā﴾, it is a new predicate, meaning: "and you cleanse them by it," and therefore it is nominative.

* *

The people of interpretation differed concerning the interpretation of His saying: ﴿Indeed, your prayer is a comfort for them﴾.

Some of them said: It means mercy for them.

Those who said so:

17160. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Indeed, your prayer is a comfort for them﴾, meaning: a mercy for them.

* *

Others said: Rather, its meaning is: indeed your prayer is a tranquility (waqar) for them.

Those who said so:

17161. Bishr related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿Indeed, your prayer is a comfort for them﴾, meaning: a tranquility for them.

* *

The readers differed in their recitation of this.

The reciters of Medina recited: ﴿inna ṣalawātaka sakanun lahum﴾ (in plural "ṣalawat"), meaning: your supplications.

* *

The reciters of Iraq and some of the Meccans recited: ﴿inna ṣalātaka sakanun lahum﴾ (in singular "ṣalat"), meaning: indeed your supplication.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: It seems that those who recited it in the singular regarded the singular recitation as more correct, because in the singular there is a sense of collectivity and multiplicity that is not in His saying ﴿inna ṣalawātaka sakanun lahum﴾, since "ṣalawāt" (plural) is the plural of a number ranging from three to ten, and not more than that. What they said is, in our view, as they said; and the recitation in the singular is, in our view, correct, not because of the reason that the plural denotes a greater number, but because the intended meaning is the report of the Prophet's (ﷺ) supplication and prayers, that they are a comfort for these people, and not a report about number. Since this is so, the singular for "ṣalāh" is preferable.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Do they not know that Allah—He it is who accepts repentance from His servants and takes charities, and that Allah is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful?﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: This is a report from Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, which He gave to the believers: that accepting the repentance of those hypocrites who repent, and taking charity from their wealth when they give it, are not in the hands of the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ).
