And that the Prophet of Allah, when he refused to release those who had tied themselves to the pillars, among those who stayed behind from the campaign with him, and when he left off accepting their charity after Allah had released them and permitted him to do so, only did that because it was not his to decide (ﷺ), and that it belongs to Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, and not to Muhammad. And that Muhammad only does what he does, whether leaving or releasing, or taking charity, or other of his actions, by the command of Allah. So He, may His praise be exalted, said: Did those who stayed behind from jihad with the believers, who tied themselves to the pillars, who said, "We will not release ourselves until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is the one who releases us," and who asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to take the charity of their wealth, not know that this is not up to Muhammad, and that it is up to Allah, and that Allah is the One who accepts the repentance of whoever of His servants repents, or rejects it, and takes the charity of whoever gives charity from among them, or returns it to them, not Muhammad? So let them direct their repentance and their charity to Allah, and aim thereby at His face alone, not Muhammad or anyone else, and make their repentance sincerely for Him, and desire Him with their charity, and know that Allah is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful? He says: the One who returns to His servants with pardon for them when they return to His obedience, the Merciful toward them when they turn in repentance to His pleasure, sparing them from His punishment. [See the explanation of "repentance" (tawbah), "the Accepting of repentance" (al-tawwab), and "the Merciful" (al-rahim), in the earlier indexes of language, under (ت و ب) and (ر ح م).]

* *

Ibn Zayd used to say about this:

17162: Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "The others said," meaning those among the stayers-behind who had not repented: "These, meaning those who repented, were with us yesterday, not spoken to and not sat with. So what is their state?" Then Allah said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is He who accepts repentance from His servants and takes charities, and indeed Allah is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.﴾ [See the explanation of "repentance," "the Accepting of repentance," and "the Merciful," in the earlier indexes of language, under (ت و ب) and (ر ح م).]

17163: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: A man who used to visit Hammad but did not sit with him informed me. Shu'bah said: al-Awwam ibn Hawshab said: "He is Qatadah, or the son of Qatadah, a man of Muharib." He said: I heard Abd Allah ibn al-Sa'ib, who was his neighbor, say: I heard Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud say: "No servant gives a charity but it falls into the hand of Allah, and He is the One who places it into the hand of the beggar." And he recited this verse: ﴿He it is who accepts repentance from His servants and takes charities.﴾ [The report 17163: "Qatadah," or "Ibn Qatadah," a man of Muharib. I have not found it in this form.

I have found no one who spoke about his case or mentioned him. The plain sense of this chain shows that this "Qatadah" or "Ibn Qatadah" the Muharibi is the one who informed Shu'bah, and he is the one who used to visit Hammad without sitting with him, and that he is the one who heard from Abd Allah ibn al-Sa'ib, who was his neighbor, and that "Abd Allah ibn al-Sa'ib" is the one who heard from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud. This is a difficulty:

"Abd Allah ibn al-Sa'ib" is "Abd Allah ibn al-Sa'ib al-Kindi," who related from his father, and from Zadan al-Kindi, and Abd Allah ibn Ma'qil ibn Muqarrin, and Abd Allah ibn Qatadah al-Muharibi (as will come in the following reports). Al-A'mash, Abu Ishaq al-Shaybani, al-Awwam ibn Hawshab, and Sufyan al-Thawri related from him. He is trustworthy, biographed in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/75, and they did not mention a narration of his from Ibn Mas'ud, as you see, but rather they mentioned his narration from "Abd Allah ibn Qatadah al-Muharibi," as will come in the following reports.

So I fear there is something in the chain of this report, as shown by the reports that follow it, which are sound according to what is mentioned in the books of biographies. I fear that Shu'bah heard it from a man who used to visit Hammad without sitting with him, from Abd Allah ibn al-Sa'ib, from Qatadah, or the son of Qatadah, a man of Muharib; then he heard it from al-Awwam ibn Hawshab, from Abd Allah ibn al-Sa'ib, from Qatadah, or Qatadah, a man of Muharib; and that the copyist has corrupted the chain. See the discussion on "Abd Allah ibn Abi Qatadah al-Muharibi," or "Abd Allah ibn Qatadah," in the commentary on the following reports.]

17164: al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Abd Allah ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Qatadah al-Muharibi, from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "No man gives a charity but it falls into the hand of Allah before it falls into the hand of the beggar, and He places it into the hand of the beggar." Then he recited: ﴿Did they not know that Allah is He who accepts repentance from His servants and takes charities?﴾ [The reports 17164–17166: "Abd Allah ibn al-Sa'ib al-Kindi," already mentioned in the earlier commentary.

As for "Abd Allah ibn Abi Qatadah al-Muharibi," it is thus in all of them, except in number 17165, where in the manuscript it reads "Abd Allah ibn Qatadah," but the publisher of the printed edition added "Abi" from his own opinion.

As for the books of biographies, they mention only "Abd Allah ibn Qatadah al-Muharibi." Ibn Abi Hatim biographed him at 2/2/141 and said: "He related from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud; Abd Allah ibn al-Sa'ib related from him; I heard my father say that." Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar also biographed him in Ta'jil al-Manfa'ah: 233, and said: "From Ibn Mas'ud, and from him Abd Allah ibn al-Sa'ib; Ibn Hibban deemed him trustworthy," then he said: "The words of al-Bukhari indicate that he did not narrate anything with a connected chain, for he said: 'It is related from Ibn Mas'ud his saying about charity,' said by al-Thawri, from Abd Allah ibn al-Sa'ib, from him."

As for "Abd Allah ibn Abi Qatadah," I have not found his mention in this form except in the tafsir of Abu Ja'far.

17166: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abd Allah ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Qatadah, who said: "Abd Allah (Ibn Mas'ud) said: Indeed the charity falls into the hand of Allah before it falls into the hand of the beggar." Then he recited this verse: ﴿He it is who accepts repentance from His servants and takes charities.﴾ [The reports 17164–17166: "Abd Allah ibn al-Sa'ib al-Kindi," already mentioned in the earlier commentary.

As for the books of biographies, they mention only "Abd Allah ibn Qatadah al-Muharibi." Ibn Abi Hatim biographed him at 2/2/141 and said: "He related from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud; Abd Allah ibn al-Sa'ib related from him; I heard my father say that." Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar also biographed him in Ta'jil al-Manfa'ah: 233, and said: "From Ibn Mas'ud, and from him Abd Allah ibn al-Sa'ib; Ibn Hibban deemed him trustworthy," then he said: "The words of al-Bukhari indicate that he did not narrate anything with a connected chain, for he said: 'It is related from Ibn Mas'ud his saying about charity,' said by al-Thawri, from Abd Allah ibn al-Sa'ib, from him."

As for "Abd Allah ibn Abi Qatadah," I have not found his mention in this form except in the tafsir of Abu Ja'far.

This report was mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 275, and he attributed it to Abd al-Razzaq, al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi in Nawadir al-Usul, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Tabarani.

al-Haythami mentioned it in Majma' al-Zawa'id 3: 111, and said: "al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Kabir, and in it is Abd Allah ibn Qatadah al-Muharibi, whom no one has declared weak, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy."]

17168: Abu Kurayb [said, Waki' narrated to us] narrated to us, saying: Abbad ibn Mansur narrated to us, from al-Qasim, that he heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah accepts charity and takes it with His right hand, and He nurtures it for one of you as one of you nurtures his foal, until a morsel becomes like Uhud." And the confirmation of this in the Book of Allah is: ﴿He it is who accepts repentance from His servants and takes charities﴾, [The verse appears in the manuscript as "He it is who accepts repentance," as Ahmad also narrated in al-Musnad, number 10090, with this chain, with the same error. The recitation is: "Did they not know that Allah is He who accepts repentance..." My brother Sayyid Ahmad has deduced that this is an ancient error, as he said in the commentary on report number 6253 above. In the printed edition, the publisher corrected it to "Indeed Allah is He who accepts repentance..." I have kept what is in the manuscript so this error may be known.] and ﴿Allah destroys usury and makes charities grow﴾. [Surah al-Baqarah: 276. The report 17168: this report was mentioned above with this chain at number 6253, and my brother Sayyid Ahmad annotated it there.]

17169: Sulayman ibn Umar ibn al-Aqta' al-Raqqi narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abbad ibn Mansur, from al-Qasim, from Abu Hurayrah, and I do not think he raised it: "Indeed Allah accepts charity," then he mentioned something similar. [The report 17169: "Sulayman ibn Umar ibn Khalid al-Aqta' al-Raqqi," mentioned at number 6254. In the printed edition it read "al-Rabi," the editor not having read the manuscript well; the correct reading is "al-Raqqi."

It was mentioned at number 6254, and my brother Sayyid Ahmad annotated it earlier.]

[The report 17170: mentioned at number 6256, through Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, in similar terms. My brother Sayyid Ahmad annotated it there, and pointed to al-Tabari's narration in this place, and confirmed its chain.]

17172: al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And that Allah is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful﴾, meaning: if they remain upright.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 9, Verse 105**

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿And say, "Work, for Allah will see your deeds, and so will His Messenger and the believers. And you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do."﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: May His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿And say﴾, O Muhammad, to those who acknowledged their sins to you from among those who stayed behind from jihad with you: ﴿Work﴾, for Allah, by that which pleases Him, of obedience to Him and performance of His obligations. ﴿For Allah will see your deeds and His Messenger﴾, meaning: Allah will see, if you do your deeds, and His Messenger and the believers will see them in this world. ﴿And you will be returned﴾, on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿to the One who knows your secrets and your public conduct, so nothing is hidden from Him of the inner or outer aspects of your affairs﴾ [[See the explanation of "the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed" in what has preceded in the indexes of language (ghayb), (shahida).]]. ﴿And He will inform you of what you used to do﴾, meaning: He will inform you of what you used to do, and of what among it was sincere, what among it was for show, what among it was obedience, and what among it was disobedience to Allah, and He will recompense you for all of that with your due recompense: the doer of good with his goodness, and the doer of evil with his evil. [[See the explanation of "news" (naba') in what has preceded in the indexes of language (naba').]]

* *

17173 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from a man, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And say, "Work, for Allah will see your deeds, and so will His Messenger and the believers"﴾, he said: This is a warning (wa'īd).

[[At this point the eleventh part of our manuscript ends. At its end is the following text:

"The eleventh volume of the book al-Bayan is complete, by the praise of Allah, His help, and His good success. It is followed in the twelfth part, God willing, by: The discussion on the interpretation of His saying: (And others are deferred to the command of Allah, either He will punish them or He will accept their repentance, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise).

The copying was finished in the blessed month of Sha'ban in the year 715 (AH). May Allah forgive its author, its owner, its scribe, and all Muslims.

Amen, amen, amen, amen."

Then follows the twelfth part, beginning with: "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful. My Lord, make it easy."]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 106:

The explanation of His words: ﴿And others are deferred to the command of Allah, either He will punish them or He will turn to them in forgiveness. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And among those who stayed behind from you when you set out against your enemy, O believers, are others.

* *

The word "others" (ākharūn) is in the nominative case, being joined (ʿaṭfan) to His words: ﴿And others have acknowledged their sins; they had mixed a righteous deed with another that was bad﴾.

* *

= ﴿And others are deferred﴾, meaning: held in suspense (murjawna) regarding the command of Allah and His decree.

* *

It is said of it: "I deferred him (arjaʾtuhu) — I defer him (urjiʾuhu) — deferment (irjāʾ) — and he is deferred (murjaʾ)," with the hamza and without the hamza; they are two dialects with one meaning. The reciters have recited with both. [[See the explanation of "irjāʾ" above, 13:20, 21.]]

* *

It has also been said: By these "others" is meant a group of those who had stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during the expedition of Tabuk. They regretted what they had done, and they did not make an excuse to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ upon his arrival, and they did not tie themselves to the pillars. So Allah deferred their affair until their repentance was sound, then He turned to them and pardoned them.

* *

Ahl al-ta'wil (the scholars of interpretation) have said in accordance with what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said so:

17174- Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: And three of them — meaning: of those who stayed behind from the expedition of Tabuk — had not tied themselves to the pillars; they were deferred for a period (sabtah) — [[His words "sabtah" mean a span of time.]] — not knowing whether they would be punished or whether they would be turned to in forgiveness. So Allah revealed: ﴿Certainly Allah has turned in forgiveness to the Prophet and the Emigrants﴾ until His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 117, 118].

17175- Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: When this verse was revealed — meaning His words: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them increase﴾ — the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took from their wealth — meaning from the wealth of Abu Lubabah and his two companions — and gave it in charity on their behalf. The three who had opposed Abu Lubabah remained, and they had not tied themselves up, and they were not mentioned for anything, and no excuse for them was revealed, and the earth became constricted for them despite its vastness. They are the ones of whom Allah said: ﴿And others are deferred to the command of Allah, either He will punish them or He will turn to them in forgiveness. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.﴾ So people began to say: "They are destroyed!", since no excuse was revealed for them, and others began to say: "Perhaps Allah will forgive them!" Thus they became deferred to the command of Allah, until there was revealed: ﴿Certainly Allah has turned in forgiveness to the Prophet and the Emigrants and the Helpers who followed him in the hour of hardship﴾ — those who went out with him toward Syria — ﴿after the hearts of a group of them had nearly inclined away. Then He turned to them in forgiveness. Indeed, He is to them Kind and Merciful﴾. Then He said: ﴿And [He turned in forgiveness] to the three who were left behind﴾, meaning the deferred ones regarding the command of Allah, upon whom repentance was revealed, and it encompassed them, so He said: ﴿until, when the earth was constricted for them in spite of its vastness and their souls confined them﴾, until His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful﴾.

17176- Ibn Wakiʿ related to us, saying: Suwayd ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Zayd, from Ayyub, from ʿIkrimah: ﴿And others are deferred to the command of Allah﴾, he said: They are the three who were left behind.

17177- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And others are deferred to the command of Allah﴾, he said: Hilal ibn Umayyah, Murarah ibn Rabiʿi, and Kaʿb ibn Malik, from the Aws and the Khazraj.

17178- Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Huthayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And others are deferred to the command of Allah﴾: Hilal ibn Umayyah, Murarah ibn Rabiʿi, and Kaʿb ibn Malik, from the Aws and the Khazraj. [[Report 17177: "Murarah ibn Rabiʿi" is thus written in the manuscript in this report and in the following one. The printed edition corrected it to "Murarah ibn al-Rabiʿ." Then in no. 17183 the manuscript has "Murarah ibn Rabiʿah," and both are other than the well-known form found in the books of the biographies of the Companions and the sound collections, where he is "Murarah ibn al-Rabiʿ al-Ansari," of the Banu ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf.

As for "Murarah ibn Rabiʿi ibn ʿAdi ibn Yazid ibn Jushm," none mentions him except Ibn al-Kalbi, who said: "He was one of the weepers."

I have retained what is in Tabari's manuscript, since the name agrees in this form in several places, and I fear there may be a disagreement regarding his name of which I have not come to know. See what will come below under no. 17436.

Then see no. 17433 and what follows it, where there are "Ibn Rabiʿah" and "Ibn al-Rabiʿ."]]

17179- ...... He said: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

17180- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly.

17181- ...... He said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak, similarly.

17182- I was related from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His words: ﴿And others are deferred to the command of Allah﴾: They are the three who were left behind from the repentance — he means: other than Abu Lubabah and his companions — and Allah did not reveal their excuse, so the earth became constricted for them despite its vastness. The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were of two factions regarding them: a faction saying, "They are destroyed," since Allah did not reveal regarding them what He revealed regarding Abu Lubabah and his companions.

And another faction said: "Perhaps Allah will pardon them!" And they were deferred to the command of Allah. Then Allah sent down His mercy and forgiveness, saying: ﴿Certainly Allah has turned in forgiveness to the Prophet and the Emigrants﴾, the verse, and He revealed: ﴿And [He turned in forgiveness] to the three who were left behind﴾, the verse.

17183- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿And others are deferred to the command of Allah﴾, he said: We were told that they are the three who were left behind: Kaʿb ibn Malik, Hilal ibn Umayyah, and Murarah ibn Rabiʿah, a group from the Helpers. [[Report 17183: "Murarah ibn Rabiʿah," known as "Murarah ibn al-Rabiʿ," but thus it is in the manuscript, and the editor corrected it in the printed edition. See no. 17177.]]

17184- Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah: ﴿And others are deferred to the command of Allah﴾, he said: They are the three who were left behind.

17185- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿And others are deferred to the command of Allah, either He will punish them or He will turn to them in forgiveness﴾: they are the three who were left behind, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ deferred their affair until their repentance came to them from Allah. [[Report 17185: Ibn Hisham's Sirah 4:198, 199, which continues the earlier report no. 17135.]]

* *

As for His words: ﴿either He will punish them﴾, it means: either Allah will withhold them from repentance by forsaking them, and He will punish them for their sins with which they die, in the Hereafter. ﴿Or He will turn to them in forgiveness﴾: that is, or He will grant them success in repentance so that they repent of their sins, and He will forgive them. ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾: that is, Allah has knowledge of their affair and what they will come to, whether repentance or persistence in sin. ﴿All-Wise﴾: in His management of them and of others among His creation, there is no flaw in His judgment. [[See the explanation of "ʿAlim" and "Hakim" in the earlier lexical indices under (ʿ-l-m) and (ḥ-k-m).]]

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And those who took a mosque for harm, and for disbelief, and for dividing the believers, and as an outpost for those who had warred against Allah and His Messenger before, and they will surely swear, "We intended nothing but good," but Allah bears witness that they are indeed liars﴾ (9:107).

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "And those who built a mosque for harm." They, as it is reported, were twelve men from the Ansar.

Those who said this:

17186. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from al-Zuhri, Yazid ibn Ruman, Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, and Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah, and others, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came back (from Tabuk), that is, from Tabuk, until he halted at Dhu Awan, a place an hour's journey from Medina. The people of the mosque of harm had come to him while he was preparing for Tabuk, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, we have built a mosque for the sick, the needy, and for the rainy and the wintry nights, and we would love for you to come to us and lead prayer in it for us!" He said: "I am on a journey and occupied with affairs," or as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "but if we return, we will come to you, God willing, and pray for you in it." When he halted at Dhu Awan, news of the mosque reached him. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned Malik ibn al-Dukhshum, brother of Banu Salim ibn Awf, and Ma'n ibn Adi, or his brother Asim ibn Adi, of Banu al-Ajlan, and said: "Go to this mosque whose people are wrongdoers, and demolish it and burn it!" The two went out quickly until they reached Banu Salim ibn Awf, who were the kin of Malik ibn al-Dukhshum. Malik said to Ma'n: "Wait for me until I bring you fire from my family." He entered his family's house, took a palm frond, lit fire in it, then the two went running until they entered the mosque, where its people were, and they burned it and demolished it, and the people dispersed from it. And what was revealed about them of the Qur'an was revealed: ﴿And those who took a mosque for harm and disbelief﴾, to the end of the story. Those who built it were twelve men: Khidham ibn Khalid, of Banu Ubayd ibn Zayd, of [the editor's note: in the printed and manuscript texts "Khidham ibn Khalid ibn Ubayd," and I have kept what is in Ibn Hisham's Sirah], a man of Banu Amr ibn Awf, and from his house the mosque of discord was brought out; and Tha'labah ibn Hatib, of Banu Ubayd, and he belongs to Banu Umayyah ibn Zayd; and Mu'attib ibn Qushayr, of Banu Dubay'ah ibn Zayd; and Abu Habibah ibn al-Azar, of Banu Dubay'ah ibn Zayd; and Abbad ibn Hanif, brother of Sahl ibn Hanif, of Banu Amr ibn Awf; and Jariyah ibn Amir, and his two sons, Majma' ibn Jariyah and Zayd ibn Jariyah; and Nabtal ibn al-Harith, and they are of Banu Dubay'ah; and Bahzaj, [the editor's note: in the printed text "Bakhdaj," and the correct form is what is in the manuscript and Ibn Hisham's Sirah], and he belongs to Banu Dubay'ah; and Bujad ibn Uthman, and he is of Banu Dubay'ah; and Wadi'ah ibn Thabit, and he belongs to Banu Umayyah, the kin of Abu Lubabah ibn Abd al-Mundhir. [Note: the report 17186, Sirah of Ibn Hisham 4: 173, 174.]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the speech is: "And those who built a mosque for harm" against the mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, "and for disbelief" in Allah, by opposing the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in that, "and to divide the believers by it," so that some of them would pray in it instead of the mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and some would pray in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so they would differ because of that and split apart. ﴿And as an outpost for those who had warred against Allah and His Messenger before﴾: that is, an preparation for him, for Abu Amir the disbeliever who opposed Allah and His Messenger, disbelieved in them both, and fought the Messenger of Allah. ﴿Before﴾: that is, before their building of that mosque. For Abu Amir was the one who had gathered the confederates (ahzab), that is, gathered the confederates to fight the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When Allah frustrated him, he joined the Byzantines seeking help from their king against the Prophet of Allah, and he wrote to the people of the mosque of harm [see the explanation of "harm" previously: 5: 7, 8, 46, 53 / 6: 85-91] ordering them to build the mosque they had built, as is reported from him, so that he might pray in it, as he claimed, when he returned to them. They did so. This is the meaning of the saying of Allah, exalted be His praise: ﴿and as an outpost for those who had warred against Allah and His Messenger before﴾.

= ﴿And they will surely swear, "We intended nothing but good"﴾: Allah, exalted be His praise, says: its builders will surely swear, "We intended nothing but good" by building it, except kindness to the Muslims, benefit, and ease for the weak and the sick and those unable to go to the mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to pray in it, and that is the good deed. ﴿But Allah bears witness that they are indeed liars﴾ in their oath and their saying: "We did not build it except that we wanted good," but they built it intending by its building evil, harm to the mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, disbelief in Allah, dividing the believers, and an outpost for the wicked Abu Amir.

* *

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said this:

17187. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And those who took a mosque for harm﴾: they were people of the Ansar who built a mosque. Abu Amir said to them: "Build your mosque, and prepare for it what you can of strength and weapons, for I am going to Caesar, king of the Romans, and will bring an army of Romans, and expel Muhammad and his companions!" When they finished their mosque, they came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and said: "We have finished building our mosque, and we would love for you to pray in it and invoke blessing upon us!" So Allah revealed concerning it: ﴿Do not stand in it ever. A mosque founded on piety from the first day is more worthy that you stand in it﴾, to His saying: ﴿and Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾.

17188. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ("And those who took a mosque for harm and disbelief and division among the believers"), he said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ built the mosque of Quba, men of the Ansar went out, among them: Bahzaj, [the editor's note: in the printed text "Bakhdaj," and what is in Ibn Hisham's Sirah 4: 174 is kept, as previously in no. 17186. I later saw in al-Muhabbar: 47: "Bakhdaj," but I could not verify it. See also Jamharat al-Ansab by Ibn Hazm: 316 in the genealogy of "Sahl ibn Hanif," "Uthman ibn Hanif," and "Abbad ibn Hanif". See the following note.

I do not know the saying "grandfather of Abdullah ibn Hanif," and I do not know whether it is from the words of Ibn Abbas or from the words of someone else, though I lean toward its being from someone else's words, because I have not found among the Companions or the Successors an "Abdullah ibn Hanif," and his grandfather is "Bahzaj." The one mentioned among the hypocrites who built the mosque of harm is "Abbad ibn Hanif," brother of "Sahl ibn Hanif." I fear something has dropped from the report, so the speech became confused. In the genealogy of "Sahl ibn Hanif" there is "Amr, who is Bahzaj, son of Hanash ibn Awf ibn Amr" (see Ibn Sa'd 3/2/39, and then 5: 59), and Jamharat al-Ansab by Ibn Hazm: 316, but this is very ancient in the pre-Islamic period, and it is without doubt not "Bahzaj" who had the affair in the mosque of harm.

What is here requires further verification, which I have not been able to reach.] and Wadi'ah ibn Hizam, and Majma' ibn Jariyah al-Ansari, and they built the mosque of hypocrisy. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Bahzaj [the editor's note: in the printed text "Bakhdaj," see the previous notes]: "Woe to you! What did you intend by what I see?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I intended nothing but good!" He was lying, and the Messenger of Allah accepted it from him and wished to excuse him, but Allah revealed: ﴿And those who took a mosque for harm and disbelief and division among the believers and an outpost for those who had warred against Allah and His Messenger﴾, meaning a man among them called "Abu Amir" who had been at war with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and who had gone to Heraclius. They were watching for Abu Amir to come [when he returned], so he would pray in it [the printed text runs these words together; the manuscript has a gap, and in the margin there is the letter (ṭ) indicating error; I have placed in brackets what is between the parentheses from al-Durr al-Manthur 1: 276, which narrates the report through Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Abi Hatim. What I have adopted matches in meaning what will come in the following reports], and he had gone out of Medina at war with Allah and His Messenger. ﴿And they will surely swear, "We intended nothing but good," but Allah bears witness that they are indeed liars﴾.

17189. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Ibn Abbas said: ﴿And as an outpost for those who had warred against Allah and His Messenger before﴾: he said: Abu Amir the monk, who went to Caesar, and they said: "When he comes, he will pray in it," for they thought he would prevail over Muhammad ﷺ.

17190. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And those who took a mosque for harm and disbelief﴾: the hypocrites said. ﴿For the one who warred against Allah and His Messenger﴾: for Abu Amir the monk.

17191. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

17192. ... narrated to us, saying: Abu Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And those who took a mosque for harm and disbelief and division among the believers﴾: he said: It was revealed concerning the hypocrites. And His saying: ﴿and as an outpost for those who had warred against Allah and His Messenger before﴾: he said: He is Abu Amir the monk.

17193. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the same.

17194. Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Suwayd ibn Amr narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Zayd, from Ayyub, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿And those who took a mosque for harm and disbelief﴾: he said: They are the Banu Ghanm ibn Awf.

17195. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Ayyub, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿And those who took a mosque for harm and disbelief﴾: he said: They are a tribe called "Banu Ghanm."

So it may also be said that the Byzantines killed him for his Islam, as this report states. As for his later saying, "He said: When he comes, he prays in it," it is from Qatadah's words. See the following reports, for it is said that he became Christian.] He said: When he comes, he prays in it, so Allah revealed: ﴿Do not stand in it ever, for a mosque founded on piety﴾, the verse.

And they used to say: "When he arrives, he will prevail over the Prophet of Allah ﷺ."

17199. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿And those who took a mosque for harm and disbelief and division among the believers and an outpost for those who had warred against Allah and His Messenger before﴾: he said: It is the mosque of Quba. They all used to pray in it. There was a man from the leaders of the hypocrites called "Abu Amir," the father of "Hanzalah Ghasil al-Mala'ikah," and "Sayfi," and [the editor's note: in the printed text "and his brother," and what is in the manuscript, as I have recorded, is not legible enough to be trusted. It could be "and his brother," but then it would be an error; the correct form would be "and his brother" as the editor of the printed text recorded.

However, the context indicates that what is in brackets is a third name, the name of Hanzalah's brother, and Sayfi, and I have not been able to find a report of that.

As for "Sayfi," Ibn Hajar mentioned him in al-Isabah in the biography of "Sayfi," and that he was among those who witnessed Uhud, attributing that to Ibn Sa'd and al-Tabarani, but I did not find it in the printed Tabaqat of Ibn Sa'd.] and these three were from the best of the Muslims. Abu Amir fled, he and Ibn Abd Yalil, of Thaqif, [the editor's note: the manuscript and the printed text have "Ibn Balin," though in the manuscript it is unpointed. This is without doubt an error in my view, and its correct form is "Ibn Abd Yalil," as I have recorded. For Ibn Abd al-Barr in al-Isti'ab: 105, in the biography of "Hanzalah al-Ghasil," mentioned that when Mecca was conquered, Abu Amir the wicked fled to Heraclius to the Byzantines, and died a disbeliever at Heraclius's court, and there with him was "Kinanah ibn Abd Yalil" and "Alqamah ibn Alathah," and they disputed his inheritance before Heraclius, and he gave it to Kinanah ibn Abd Yalil, and said to Alqamah: "They are people of the settlements, and you are people of the tents."

"Kinanah ibn Abd Yalil al-Thaqafi" was included by Ibn Hajar in the fourth section, and Ibn Sallam al-Jumahi mentioned him in Tabaqat Fuhul al-Shu'ara, p. 217, among the poets of Ta'if, and he did not give any report after mentioning him.] and Alqamah ibn Alathah, of Qays, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until they joined the king of the Romans. As for Alqamah and Ibn Abd Yalil, [the editor's note: in the printed text and manuscript "Ibn Balin," and in the manuscript unpointed. See the previous note,] they returned, pledged allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ, and embraced Islam. As for Abu Amir, he became Christian and remained there. He said: Some of the hypocrites built the mosque of harm for Abu Amir. They said: "So that Abu Amir may come and pray in it," and "dividing the believers," so that they would split their congregation, [the editor's note: in the printed text "between their congregation," and I have recorded what is in the manuscript,] because they used to all pray together in the mosque of Quba. They came deceiving the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, perhaps the flood will come and cut between us and the valley, and separate us from the people, and we pray in our mosque," [the editor's note: in the printed text "and we pray," and I have recorded what is in the manuscript,] "and when the flood recedes, we pray with them!" He said: They built it upon hypocrisy. He said: Their mosque collapsed in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: People threw on it straw and refuse, [the editor's note: in the printed text "the stench and the ..." and the correct form is what is in the manuscript. "Tibn" is the stalk of grain, which is what is thrown. As for "nataan," it is the foul smell, so it seems he thought "nataan" is a metaphor for "filth," because of the stench of its smell! And that is false.] so Allah revealed: ﴿And those who took a mosque for harm and disbelief and division among the believers﴾, so that all the believers would not pray in the mosque of Quba = ﴿and as an outpost for those who had warred against Allah and His Messenger before﴾: that is Abu Amir = ﴿And they will surely swear, "We intended nothing but good," but Allah bears witness that they are indeed liars﴾.

17200. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Harun narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from Layth: that a certain man did not reach the prayer in the mosque of the Banu Amir. It was said to him: "The mosque of the Banu so-and-so, they have not prayed in it yet!" He said: "I do not like to pray in it, for it was built upon harm, and every mosque built for harm or for show or for reputation, its origin leads back to the mosque that was built upon harm."

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 9, verse 108 (part 1 of 3)**

**On the interpretation of His words: ﴿Do not stand in it ever. A mosque founded upon piety from the first day is more worthy that you stand in it﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: Almighty God says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "Do not stand, O Muhammad, in the mosque that these hypocrites built, for harm and for division among the believers, and as an ambush for those who have waged war against God and His Messenger." Then His majesty swore, saying: ﴿A mosque founded upon piety from the first day is more worthy that you stand in it﴾, meaning you ﴿in it﴾.

* *

By His words ﴿founded upon piety﴾, He means: its foundation and origin were laid upon the piety and obedience of God. ﴿From the first day﴾ means: from the beginning of its construction. ﴿More worthy that you stand in it﴾ means: more deserving that you stand in it in prayer.

* *

It has also been said that the meaning of His words ﴿from the first day﴾ is the starting point of the first day, as the Arabs say, "I have not seen him since such a day," meaning: since its beginning. And "from the first day" may be intended to mean "from the first of the days," like the saying of one who says, "I met every man," meaning every (one of the) men.

* *

The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil, those who interpret the Qur'an) differed concerning the mosque that He meant by His words ﴿a mosque founded upon piety from the first day﴾.

Some of them said: It is the Mosque of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in which are his pulpit and his grave today.

* *

Mention of those who said this:

The Mosque of Madinah, or the Mosque of Quba? He said: No, the Mosque of Madinah.

The interpretation of His words: ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves, and God loves those who purify themselves﴾ (108)

Abu Ja'far said: Almighty God says: In the present company of the mosque founded upon piety from the first day, there are men who love to cleanse their seats with water when they come from relieving themselves, and God loves those who purify themselves with water.

* *

The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said concerning this.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 108 (part 2 of 3):**

Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Salam ibn al-Harith al-Khazraji al-Isra'ili (the Israelite), who had a recognised vision and a preserved narration. He is biographed in Ta'jil al-Manfa'a (Ibn Hajar's work on those omitted from the earlier biographical dictionaries): 366, 367; in al-Kabir (al-Bukhari's Tarikh al-Kabir) 1/1/18; in Ibn Abi Hatim 3/2/297; in al-Istiab: 234, 235; in Usd al-Ghaba 4: 324; and in al-Isaba, in his entry.

This report was narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad 6: 6, through the chain: "Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us: Malik (meaning Ibn Mughawwal) said: I heard Sayyar Abu al-Hakam, more than once, narrating from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Salam, who said: When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) arrived. . . ."

Al-Bukhari also narrated it in al-Tarikh al-Kabir 1/1/18, through Muhammad ibn Yusuf, from Malik ibn Mughawwal, in similar wording, and then said: "Ishaq narrated from Jarir, from Layth, from a man of the Ansar from the people of Quba': When it was revealed, [it was] like this." He thereby showed the disagreement regarding it on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, and that he left the man from the Ansar unnamed.

The hafiz Ibn Abd al-Barr also referred to it in his biography and said: "His narration is transmitted in the tafsir, and its chain differs; some of them treat it as mursal (a report in which the companion is omitted from the chain)." The mursal version is the report of al-Tabari mentioned earlier, number 17225. Ibn Hajar said in al-Isaba: "Ibn Mandah said: Dawud ibn Abi Hind narrated it from Shahr as mursal, not mentioning Muhammad or his father."

Ibn al-Athir also narrated it in Usd al-Ghaba in his biography.

Yahya ibn Adam's statement, "I do not know it except from his father," will come at number 17230. See the commentary on the report there.

**17229.** Sufyan ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Yahya [ibn Rafi'] narrated to us, from Malik ibn Mughawwal, who said: I heard Sayyar Abu al-Hakam, more than once, narrating from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Salam, who said: When the Prophet (ﷺ) came to the people of Quba', he said: "God has praised you well for purification," meaning His saying: ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves﴾. They said: "We find it written among us in the Torah: the cleansing (istinja', washing oneself with water after relieving oneself) with water."

[[Report 17229: "Yahya ibn Rafi'," as it appears in both places in the printed edition of al-Tabari and its manuscript. I do not know how this came about, for there is no one in this generation of narrators whom I know to be called "Yahya ibn Rafi'." As for "Yahya ibn Rafi' al-Thaqafi," he is very early, having heard Uthman and Abu Hurayrah, and he passed earlier under number 5777. But since it stands like this in both places, I have left it as it is.

What I scarcely doubt is that the correct name is "Yahya ibn Adam," as in the Musnad of Ahmad, and as Ibn Hajar mentioned in Ta'jil al-Manfa'a and al-Isaba. He also mentioned the narration of Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i from Yahya ibn Adam, as you will see later, through al-Baghawi.

This report was narrated by Ibn Hajar in al-Isaba, who said: "Ahmad, al-Bukhari in his Tarikh, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Qani' and al-Baghawi recorded it." See the commentary on numbers 17228 and 17230.]]

**17230.** Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i narrated to us, saying: Yahya [ibn Rafi'] narrated to us, saying: Malik ibn Mughawwal narrated to us, from Sayyar, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Salam = Yahya said: "And I do not know it except from his father" = He said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said to the people of Quba': "God has praised you well for purification!" They said: "We find it written against us in the Torah: the cleansing with water." And concerning it was revealed: ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves﴾.

[[Report 17230: "Yahya ibn Rafi'" like this; the preferred correct form is "Yahya ibn Adam," as stated in the previous commentary.

Ibn Hajar mentioned it from this route in al-Isaba and Ta'jil al-Manfa'a, and in it is the addition "And I do not know it except from his father." He attributed it to al-Baghawi in (the book on) the Companions, then followed it with his words: "Abu Hisham (meaning al-Rifa'i) said: and I copied it from the original of Yahya ibn Adam's book, in which there is no 'from his father.'" Then he said: "Al-Baghawi said: al-Firyabi narrated it to us, from Malik ibn Mughawwal, from Sayyar, from Shahr, from the Prophet (ﷺ), not mentioning his father."

Then he said: "Salamah ibn Rajاء narrated from Malik ibn Mughawwal, adding in it: from his father." Abu Zur'ah al-Razi said: "The correct version with us is from Muhammad; it does not have 'from his father.'"

Al-Haythami takht rajah this in Majma' al-Zawa'id 1: 212, 213, from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Salam, from his father, then said: "Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Kabir, and in its chain is Shahr ibn Hawshab, about whom they differ. But Ahmad, Ibn Ma'in, Abu Zur'ah and Ya'qub ibn Abi Shaybah declared him trustworthy." Then he recorded it from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Salam, then said: "Ahmad narrated it from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Salam, and did not say 'from his father,' as al-Tabarani said. In it is also Shahr."

What I have mentioned here indicates, first, that the correct name is "Yahya ibn Adam," not "Yahya ibn Rafi'" as it appears in the manuscript and the printed edition. It also indicates the disagreement over this report, a disagreement that calls for examination.

There remains another matter, which I did not find anyone mentioning in the discussion of this report, and I hope I have been right in mentioning and explaining it.

It is that the praise from God upon the men who love to purify themselves, who kept to the mosque founded on piety from the first day, which is undoubtedly the mosque of Quba'. And that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) only asked these men about God's praise of them. These men were from the Banu Amr ibn Awf ibn Malik ibn al-Aws, and their dwelling was in Quba'. They were Arab people upon their religion in the Jahiliyyah, and no one has mentioned that they were Jews.

And this report of Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Salam, mentioned God's praise of these men, and that their answer was: "We find it written among us in the Torah: the cleansing with water." The apparent meaning of this report indicates that their religion was Judaism. This is what I have not found anyone saying.

As for "Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Salam," and his father "Abd Allah ibn Salam ibn al-Harith," they were from the Banu Qaynuqa', of the Jews, from the descendants of the Prophet Joseph (peace be upon him). Abd Allah ibn Salam was an ally (halif) of the Qawaqil of the Khazraj, who are the Banu Amr ibn Awf ibn al-Khazraj, and they are not in any way the "Banu Amr ibn Awf ibn Malik ibn al-Aws," and the dwellings of these are other than the dwellings of those. In the account of Abd Allah ibn Salam's conversion (Sirat Ibn Hisham 2: 163), he said, mentioning the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his migration: "When he alighted at Quba', among the Banu Amr ibn Awf, a man came until he informed (people) of his arrival, while I was at the top of a palm tree of mine, working on it." Abd Allah ibn Salam and his sons, then, had none of them been at Quba'.

So his words in report number 17228, "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) stood over us and said: Will you not inform me. . . ," through to the end of the report, are very problematic, because the report is the report of Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Salam, and the pronoun in it refers to him and to his people or his allies, the Banu Amr ibn Awf ibn al-Khazraj, and this cannot be correct at all, by the evidence of his statement in the one that follows: that this was "when the Prophet (ﷺ) came to the people of Quba'."

What I have mentioned is a severe disturbance (idtirab) in the core of the report, which nothing supports. Whatever the case with its chain, and the disagreement of those who differed about it on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, its defect in its wording is, in my view, greater than its defect in its chain. God knows best where this disturbance came from. And what is beyond doubt is that it is very unlikely that this answer was the speech of the Banu Amr ibn Awf ibn Malik ibn al-Aws, and that it more resembles being the speech of one of their Jewish allies.

Clearer than this is what came in the report of Uways ibn Sa'idah (number 17231), which is: "We know nothing, except that neighbours of ours from among the Jews, whom we saw washing their backsides from excrement, so we washed as they washed." This is clearer and closer to the context of what they were asked about, and nearer to removing the disturbance. And God the Exalted knows best.]]

**17231.** Abd al-A'la ibn Wasil narrated to me, saying: Isma'il ibn Subayh al-Yashkuri narrated to us, saying: Abu Uways al-Madani narrated to us, from Sharahbil ibn Sa'd, from Uwaym ibn Sa'idah, who was among the people of Badr, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to the people of Quba': "I hear that God has praised you well for purification, [[In the Musnad: "has praised you well (qad ahsana 'alaykum al-thana')." If what is in the manuscript, "qad asna" (meaning: he raised), were read, it would be fine.]] so what is this purification?" They said: "O Messenger of God, we know nothing, except that neighbours of ours from among the Jews, whom we saw washing their backsides from excrement, so we washed as they washed."

[[Report 17231: "Abd al-A'la ibn Wasil ibn Abd al-A'la ibn Hilal al-Asadi," the shaykh of al-Tabari, passed earlier under number 11125.

"Isma'il ibn Subayh al-Yashkuri," a trustworthy narrator, passed under numbers 2996, 8640, 11158.

"Abu Uways al-Madani," he is "Abd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Uways ibn Malik al-Asbahi," truthful but not an authority, passed under number 8640.

Ibn Hajar mentioned in al-Tahdhib his narration from Uwaym ibn Sa'idah, saying: "As for his hearing from Uwaym ibn Sa'idah, there is doubt, because Uwaym died during the life of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and it is said: in the caliphate of Umar (may God be pleased with him)."

This report was narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad 3: 422, through the route of Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abu Uways, in similar wording.

Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his tafsir 4: 41, then said: "Ibn Khuzaymah narrated it in his Sahih." Al-Haythami recorded it in Majma' al-Zawa'id 1: 212, and said: "Ahmad and al-Tabarani narrated it in the three (works). **17232.** Muhammad ibn Umarah narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Sharahbil ibn Sa'd, who said: I heard Khuzaymah ibn Thabit say: This verse was revealed: ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves, and God loves those who purify themselves﴾. **17233.** Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Abu Layla, from Amir, who said: Some people of Quba' used to cleanse with water, so there was revealed: ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves, and God loves those who purify themselves﴾.

**17240.** Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, who said: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Malik ibn Mughawwal, who said: I heard Sayyar Abu al-Hakam narrating, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Salam, who said: When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) came to Madinah = or he said: the Messenger of God came to us = he said: "God has praised you well for purification; will you not tell me?" They said: "O Messenger of God, we find it written against us in the Torah: the cleansing with water." = Malik said: meaning His saying: ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves﴾.

[[Report 17240: This repeats the earlier reports from number 17225, then numbers 17228–17230; see the commentary on them there.]]

17241. Ahmad ibn Ishaq related to me, saying: Abu Ahmad related to us, saying: Fudayl ibn Marzuq related to us, from ʿAtiyyah, who said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves﴾, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) asked them: "What is this purification that God has mentioned?" They said: "O Messenger of God, in the Jahiliyyah we used to cleanse ourselves with water (istinja', cleansing after relieving oneself), and when Islam came we did not abandon it." He said: "Then do not abandon it."

17242. Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "In the mosque of Quba' there were men from the Ansar who washed their *sufalah* with water. They would enter the palm groves while the water flowed, and perform ablution. So God praised them for this, saying: ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves﴾, to the end of the verse."

[[Regarding his words "yuwaddi'una sufalatahum" (they wash their *sufalah*): it means they wash their posteriors. *Al-sufalah* in the sense of the anus and the rear is not mentioned in the lexicographical works, and the attested form with this meaning is *al-safilah*. I have vocalized it with a fatha on the *sin* and a kasra on the *fa'*, by analogy with their saying *sufalat al-baʿir*, meaning the legs of a camel, because they are the lowest part.]]

17243. Ahmad related to us, saying: Abu Ahmad related to us, saying: Talhah ibn ʿAmr related to us, from ʿAta', who said: "A group of people from the people of Quba' introduced washing with water for ablution, and so this was revealed concerning them: ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves, and God loves those who purify themselves﴾."

* *

It has been said that the phrase ﴿and God loves the purifiers﴾ is actually *al-mutatahhirin* (those who purify themselves), but the *ta'* was assimilated into the *ta'* of *al-tatahhur*... more precisely, the *ta'* was assimilated into the *ta'* (ṭāʾ) and was made a doubled *ṭāʾ*, because the points of articulation of the two letters are close to each other. [[See the explanation of *al-mutahhir* above, vol. 4, p. 384.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 109:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words: ﴿Is one who founded his building upon piety from Allah and His good pleasure better, or one who founded his building upon the brink of a crumbling precipice, so that it collapsed with him into the Fire of Hell? And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾ (9:109).

Abu Ja'far [al-Tabari] said: The reciters differed over the recitation of His words: ﴿Afaman assasa bunyanahu﴾.

Some of the reciters of Madina recited it as: (Afaman ussisa bunyanuhu ʿala taqwa min Allahi wa ridwanin khayrun am man ussisa bunyanuhu), in the passive form (mā lam yusammi fāʿiluhu, "whose agent is not named") in both instances.

* *

The common reciters of the Hijaz and Iraq recited it as: "Afaman assasa bunyanahu ʿala taqwa min Allahi wa ridwanin khayrun am man assasa bunyanahu," treating "man" as the agent who founded his building. [[In the printed edition: "ʿala wasf min bina' al-fa'il" ("on the description of the building of the agent"), which is a confusion in the wording. The correct reading is what is in the manuscript, which is what I have adopted.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: These are two readings with the same meaning, so whichever of them the reciter uses is correct. However, his reciting the verb as applying to "man," since he is the one who founded it, is more preferable to me. [[In the printed edition: "idha kana min al-muassis," but I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is entirely correct.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the speech is therefore: Which of these people who built mosques, O people, is better in your view: those who began building their mosque upon piety towards Allah, by their obedience in its construction and the performance of His obligations, with Allah's approval of their building what they built of it and their doing what they did, is better; or those who began building their mosque upon the brink of a crumbling precipice?

By His words "upon the brink of a crumbling precipice," He means: upon the edge of a crumbling precipice. [[See the explanation of "shafa" above, 7:85-86.]]

* *

"Al-jurf" refers to the wells that have no curb built for them. [[In the printed edition: "min al-rakiy," but I have kept what is in the manuscript, which matches what Abu ʿUbayda said in Majaz al-Qur'an 1:269, and this is his exact text.

"Al-rakaya" is the plural of "rakiyya," which is also pluralized as "rakiy" by dropping the taʾ, and it means a well. "Al-jawl" (with a damma on the jim) is the side of a well, and the grave, from its bottom up to its top.

This explanation that Abu ʿUbayda gave, I have not found in the explanation of the word in the lexicographical books, but it is permissible and correct in meaning, if its transmission is sound.]]

* *

"Hari" means "about to tumble." It is originally "hā'ir," but it was transposed, so the yaʾ was delayed and it became "hārin," as they say "huwa shākī al-silāh" [he is armed], with "shā'ik" [from the same root], and its origin is from "hāra yahūru, fa-huwa hā'ir." It was also said: "he is from hāra yahār," meaning it collapsed. Whoever takes it from this dialect says "hirtu yā jurf" [I fell, O precipice], and whoever takes it as "from hāra yahūru" says "hurtu yā jurf" [I fell, O precipice]. [[In the printed edition: "shāk al-silāh," but the correct reading is what is in the manuscript with the yaʾ at its end.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: This is only an allegory. He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Which of these two groups is better? And which of these two buildings is more durable? Is it the one who began the foundation of his building upon obedience to Allah, and with knowledge from Him that his building is obedience to Him, and Allah is pleased with it? Or the one who began it with hypocrisy and error, and without insight from himself into the correctness of his action from its error, so he does not know when the error of his action and the enormity of his sin will become clear to him, and so he demolishes it? [This is] like a building set upon the edge of a well, with no barrier against the flood waters or other waters, with soil that is moist and scattered, which the floods will not delay in demolishing and scattering.

= Allah, exalted is His praise, says: ﴿So it collapsed with him into the fire of Hell﴾, meaning the crumbling precipice collapsed with its building into the fire of Hell, as:

17244 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿So it collapsed with him﴾, meaning its foundations = ﴿into the fire of Hell﴾. [[In the printed edition, "meaning" ("yaʿni") is omitted.]]

* *

As for His words: ﴿And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾, He says: Allah does not grant success in right guidance in his actions to one who builds his building in other than its right place and proper position, and to one who is a hypocrite, opposing by his action the command of Allah and the command of His Messenger.

**The Commentary on His Words:** ﴿Their building which they built will never cease to be a doubt in their hearts, unless their hearts are cut to pieces. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾ (9:110)

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, He says: The building of these people who took a mosque for harm and disbelief will never cease to be ﴿a doubt﴾, meaning their mosque which they built will never cease to be ﴿a doubt in their hearts﴾, meaning doubt and hypocrisy in their hearts. They suppose that they were doing good by building it. [[See the explanation of "al-rayba" (doubt) above, p. 275, note 3, and the references there.]] ﴿Unless their hearts are cut to pieces﴾, meaning unless their hearts are split apart so that they die. ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing﴾ of what these hypocrites who built the mosque of harm are upon, of their doubt concerning their religion, of what they intended and wanted in building it, of what their affair will come to in the Hereafter and during their life for as long as they live, and of other matters concerning them and others. ﴿All-Wise﴾ in His management of them and His management of all His creation. [[See the explanations of "'Alim" (All-Knowing) and "Hakim" (All-Wise) above in the lexical indices under (ʿ-l-m) and (ḥ-k-m).]]

* *

* *

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of His words: ﴿Unless their hearts are cut to pieces﴾.

Some of the reciters of the Hijaz, Madina, Basra and Kufa recited it: ﴿إِلا أَنْ تُقَطَّعَ قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾ with a damma on the "ta'" of "tuqatta'a" (تُقَطَّعَ), taking the verb in the passive form (no subject named), and meaning: unless Allah cuts their hearts to pieces.

* *

Some of the reciters of Madina and Kufa recited it: ﴿إِلا أَنْ تَقَطَّعَ قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾ with a fatha on the "ta'" of "taqatta'a" (تَقَطَّعَ), taking the verb as belonging to the hearts, meaning: unless their hearts be cut to pieces, with one of the two "ta'"s elided.

* *

It is reported that al-Hasan used to recite: "إِلَى أَنْ تَقَطَّعَ قُلُوبُهُمْ" (with "ila" instead of "illa"), meaning: until their hearts are cut to pieces. [[See the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1: 452.]]

* *

It is reported that in the recitation of Abd Allah it is: ﴿وَلَوْ قُطِّعَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾ ("even if their hearts were cut to pieces"), and on the basis of this, whoever recited it: ﴿إلا أَنْ تُقَطَّع﴾ with a damma on the "ta'" did so.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The view I hold on this is that the fatha on the "ta'" and the damma are close in meaning, because the hearts are not cut to pieces, once they are cut, except by Allah cutting them, and Allah does not cut them except when they are already cut. Both are well-known recitations, and a group of reciters has recited each of them. So whichever of the two a reader recites, he is correct in his recitation.

As for the recitation: ﴿إلَى أَنْ تَقَطَّعَ﴾ ("until ... is cut"), it contradicts the copies of the Qur'an of the Muslims (mashahif al-muslimin), and I do not consider a recitation that differs from what is in their copies to be permissible.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 111:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties; for them is Paradise. They fight in the cause of Allah, so they kill and are killed. It is a promise binding upon Him in the Torah and the Gospel and the Qur'an. And who is truer to his covenant than Allah? So rejoice in your transaction which you have contracted. And that is the great attainment.﴾ (111)

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His mention, says: Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties, in exchange for Paradise. ﴿A promise binding upon Him﴾ means: He, whose praise is great, promised them Paradise, a promise binding upon Him that He would fulfil it for them, in His revealed books: the Torah, the Gospel and the Qur'an, if they fulfil what they covenanted with Allah, by fighting in His way and supporting His religion against His enemies, so they kill and are killed. ﴿And who is truer to his covenant than Allah?﴾ He, whose praise is great, says: And who fulfils his guarantee and condition from Allah more excellently? ﴿So rejoice﴾ – He says this to the believers: Rejoice, O believers, who were truthful to Allah in what they covenanted, in your selling of your lives and properties for that which you have sold them to your Lord, for that is the great attainment. [[See the explanation of the words of this verse in the earlier lexical indices.]] As follows:

17266. Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Ya'qub related to us, from Hafs ibn Humayd, from Shamir ibn 'Atiyyah, who said: There is no Muslim except that Allah has a pledge of allegiance upon his neck; he fulfils it or dies upon it, regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers﴾ up to His saying: ﴿And that is the great attainment﴾, then He described them, saying: ﴿The repentant, the worshippers﴾ up to: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾.

17267. Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties﴾, meaning: in exchange for Paradise.

17268. ...... He said: Suwayd related to us, he said: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Muhammad ibn Yasar, from Qatadah: that he recited this verse: ﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties, for them is Paradise﴾, and he said: Allah bargained with them, and raised the price for them. [[It is said "thamantu al-rajul fi al-mabi'", when you negotiate with him over its price, discuss with him, and haggle with him over its sale and purchase.]]

The commentary of Abu Ja'far al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on Surah 9, verse 112

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿The repentant, the worshippers, the praisers, the wanderers, the bowers, the prostrators, those who enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and those who keep the limits of God. And give good tidings to the believers.﴾ (112)

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed God has purchased from the believers, the repentant, the worshippers, their souls and their wealth. But He has put it in the nominative, since it was begun anew after the completion of another similar phrase. The Arabs do this, and we have already explained it in His words ﴿Deaf, dumb, blind﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 18], in a way that makes repeating it here unnecessary. [See what has passed: 1:330, 331.]

* *

The meaning of "al-taibun" (the repentant) is those who return from what God dislikes and abhors to what He loves and approves. [See the explanation of "ta'ib" in the earlier lexical indexes (tawba).] As follows:
