[In the printed edition, "dhakara" is omitted from the phrase "dhakara al-siyaha". The wording is somewhat disturbed. See a better version in no. 17306.]

17302. ...... related to us, saying: My father related to us, from al-Mas'udi, from Abu Sinan, from Ibn Abi al-Hudhayl, from Abu Amr al-Abdi, who said: ﴿al-sa'ihun﴾, those who perpetually fast among the believers.

17303. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, from Tha'labah ibn Suhayl, who said: al-Hasan said: ﴿al-sa'ihun﴾, the fasting ones.

17304. al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Mansur ibn Harun related to me, from Abu Ishaq al-Fazari, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, who said: ﴿al-sa'ihun﴾, those who fast the month of Ramadan.

17305. Ibn Wakī' related to us, saying: Abu Khalid related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, who said: ﴿al-sa'ihun﴾, the fasting ones.

17306. ...... related to us, saying: Abu Usama related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, who said: Everything in the Qur'an that says ﴿al-sa'ihun﴾, it means the fasting ones.

17307. al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Amr ibn Awn related to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: ﴿al-sa'ihun﴾, the fasting ones.

17308. It was related to me on the authority of al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His words ﴿al-sa'ihun﴾: meaning the fasting ones.

17309. Ibn Wakī' related to us, saying: Ibn Numayr, Ya'la, and Abu Usama related to us, from Abd al-Malik, from Ata', who said: ﴿al-sa'ihun﴾, the fasting ones.

17310. al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Amr ibn Awn related to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Abd al-Malik, from Ata', the like of it.

17311. ...... related to us, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr related to us, from Ibn Uyaynah, who said: Amr related to us, that he heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say: Wandering (siyaha) existed among the Children of Israel, and a man who wandered for forty years would see what the wanderers before him had seen. A son of an adulteress wandered for forty years and saw nothing, so he said: O my Lord, what if my parents did evil and I did good? He said: So he was shown what the wanderers before him had seen. Ibn Uyaynah said: Whoever gives up food, drink and women is a wanderer.

17312. Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿al-sa'ihun﴾, a people who took from their bodies by fasting for God.

17313. Ahmad ibn Ishaq related to us, saying: Abu Ahmad related to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Yazid related to us, from al-Walid ibn Abd Allah, from Aisha, who said: The wandering of this community is fasting. [The report 17313: Ibrahim ibn Yazid al-Khuzi is abandoned in hadith (matruk al-hadith), see nos. 7484 and 16259. Al-Walid ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Mughith is trustworthy (thiqah), see no. 16259, but he did not meet Aisha, so the report is mursal from Aisha. Thus this report is extremely weak in its chain.]

* *

As for His words ﴿al-raki'un al-sajidun﴾ (the bowers, the prostrators), this means those who pray, bowing in their prayer and prostrating in it. [See the explanation of "ruku'" and "sujud" in the earlier lexical indexes (rka', sjd).] As follows:

17314. al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Mansur ibn Harun related to me, from Abu Ishaq al-Fazari, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan: ﴿al-raki'un al-sajidun﴾, he said: The obligatory prayer.

* *

As for His words ﴿al-amirun bil-ma'ruf wal-nahun 'an al-munkar﴾ (those who enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong), this means that they command people to the truth in their religion, to following right guidance and the good, and [the commanding of the right] ... and forbid them from the wrong, which is their forbidding people from every deed and word that God has forbidden His servants from. [See the explanation of "al-ma'ruf" in the earlier pages: p. 347, note 2, and the references there. See the explanation of "al-munkar" in the earlier pages: p. 347, note 3, and the references there.]

* *

It has been related from al-Hasan on this matter what follows:

17315. al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Mansur ibn Harun related to me, from Abu Ishaq al-Fazari, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan: ﴿al-amirun bil-ma'ruf﴾, "there is no god but God" = ﴿wal-nahun 'an al-munkar﴾, from polytheism.

17316. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, from Tha'labah ibn Suhayl, who said: al-Hasan said concerning His words ﴿al-amirun bil-ma'ruf﴾, he said: Indeed they did not command people until they were among its people = ﴿wal-nahun 'an al-munkar﴾, he said: Indeed they did not forbid the wrong until they had refrained from it themselves.

17317. al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-Aliyah, who said: Everything mentioned in the Qur'an as "commanding right" and "forbidding wrong": commanding right is calling from polytheism to Islam = and forbidding wrong is forbidding the worship of idols and devils.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: We have already shown earlier the correctness of what we have said: that "commanding right" is everything God or His Messenger ﷺ commanded His servants, and "forbidding wrong" is everything God or His Messenger forbade His servants. Since this is so, and there is no indication in the verse that it refers to a specific matter rather than a general one, nor any report from the Messenger, nor any evidence of sound reason, then the general sense is preferable, as we have shown in other places in our books.

* *

As for His words ﴿wal-hafizun li-hudud Allah﴾ (and those who keep the limits of God), this means: those who perform God's obligations, who stop at His command and prohibition, who do not neglect anything He has obliged them to do, nor commit anything He has forbidden them to commit. [See the explanation of "hifz" in the earlier pages: 5:167 / 8:295 / 10:562 / 11:532. And the explanation of "hudud" in the earlier pages: p. 429, note 1, and the references there.] Like what follows:

17318. al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿wal-hafizun li-hudud Allah﴾, meaning: those who uphold obedience to God. It is a condition which He stipulated for the people of jihad: if they fulfil to God His condition, He fulfils to them their condition. [In the printed edition: "if they fulfil to God His condition, He fulfils to them their condition," and I have restored what is in the manuscript.]

17319. Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿wal-hafizun li-hudud Allah﴾, he said: those who uphold obedience to God.

17320. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, from Tha'labah ibn Suhayl, who said: al-Hasan said concerning His words ﴿wal-hafizun li-hudud Allah﴾, he said: those who uphold the command of God.

17321. al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Mansur ibn Harun related to me, from Abu Ishaq al-Fazari, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan: ﴿wal-hafizun li-hudud Allah﴾, he said: for the obligations of God.

* *

As for His words ﴿wa-bashshir al-mu'minin﴾ (and give good tidings to the believers), this means: give good tidings to those who affirm what God has promised them, if they fulfil to God His covenant, that He will fulfil to them what He promised them of admitting them into Paradise. [See the explanation of "tabshir" in the earlier pages: p. 174, note 1, and the references there.] As follows:

17322. Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Hawdhah ibn Khalifah related to us, saying: Awf related to us, from al-Hasan: ﴿Indeed God has purchased from the believers their souls﴾, until the end of the verse, he said: those who fulfilled their pledge = ﴿the repentant, the worshippers, the praisers﴾, until the end of the verse, then he said: this is their deed and conduct in ease, then they met the enemy and were truthful in what they had covenanted with God.

* *

Some of them said: The meaning of this is: give good tidings to those who do these actions = meaning His words ﴿the repentant, the worshippers﴾, to the end of the verse = even if they did not fight.

Mention of those who said this:

17323. al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Mansur ibn Harun related to me, from Abu Ishaq al-Fazari, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan: ﴿wa-bashshir al-mu'minin﴾, he said: Those who did not fight.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 113 (part 1 of 2):

On the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were of kin, after it has become clear to them that they are companions of the Blazing Fire﴾ (9:113), and ﴿The asking of forgiveness by Abraham for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, he disassociated himself from him﴾ (9:114).

Abu Ja'far said: The Exalted says: It was not fitting for the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) and those who believe in him ﴿to ask forgiveness﴾, that is, to pray for forgiveness for the polytheists, even if the polytheists for whom they ask forgiveness were ﴿of kin﴾, relatives to them, ﴿after it has become clear to them that they are companions of the Blazing Fire﴾. That is: after they have died in their polytheism, worshipping Allah's partners and idols, and it has become clear to them that they are among the people of the Fire. For Allah has decreed that He will not forgive a polytheist, so it is not fitting for them to ask their Lord to do what they know He will not do.

If they say: But Abraham asked forgiveness for his father while he was a polytheist? The answer: Abraham's asking forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. So when it became clear to him, and he knew that he was an enemy of Allah, he left him and abandoned him, and stopped asking forgiveness for him, and preferred Allah and His command over him. Thus he disassociated himself from him when his condition became clear to him. [[See the explanation of the words of this verse in the indexes of language in what has preceded.]]

* *

The commentators (ahl al-ta'wil) differed about the occasion on which this verse was revealed.

Some of them said: It was revealed concerning Abu Talib, the uncle of the Prophet (ﷺ), because the Prophet (ﷺ) wished to ask forgiveness for him after his death, and Allah forbade him from doing so.

Those who said this:

17324. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, who said: When death approached Abu Talib, the Prophet (ﷺ) entered upon him, and with him were Abu Jahl and 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Umayya. He said: "O uncle, say: There is no god but Allah, a word by which I may plead for you before Allah!" Abu Jahl and 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Umayya said to him: "O Abu Talib, will you turn away from the religion of 'Abd al-Muttalib?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I will certainly ask forgiveness for you as long as I am not forbidden from you!" So this was revealed: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists﴾, and this was revealed: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love﴾ (28:56).

17325. Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Wahb related to me, saying: My paternal uncle 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb related to us, saying: Yunus related to me, from al-Zuhri, who said: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab informed me, from his father, who said: When death approached Abu Talib, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came and found with him Abu Jahl ibn Hisham and 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Umayya ibn al-Mughira. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O uncle, say: There is no god but Allah, a word by which I may testify for you before Allah!" Abu Jahl and 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Umayya said: "O Abu Talib, will you turn away from the religion of 'Abd al-Muttalib?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) kept presenting it to him and repeating that statement to him, until Abu Talib said, as the last thing he spoke to them: "He is upon the religion of 'Abd al-Muttalib," and he refused to say: "There is no god but Allah." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By Allah, I will certainly ask forgiveness for you as long as I am not forbidden from you!" So Allah revealed: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists﴾, and Allah revealed concerning Abu Talib, so He said to the Messenger of Allah: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love﴾, the verse. [[The report 17325: This is a sound hadith. Al-Bukhari narrated it and authenticated it (al-Fath 3:176, 177), by way of Ishaq, from Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri. He also narrated it (al-Fath 8:258) by way of Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, from 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri. Then he narrated it again (al-Fath 8:389) by way of Abu al-Yaman, from Shu'ayb, from al-Zuhri.
Muslim narrated it in his Sahih 1:213-216, by various routes, the first of which is this route from which Abu Ja'far narrated.
Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad 5:433, by way of 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri.
All of these chains are sound.
It will come under number 17328, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, not raised to the Prophet, from his father, with a wording other than this one.]]

17326. Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists﴾. He said: The believers said: Should we not ask forgiveness for our fathers, when Abraham asked forgiveness for his father who was a disbeliever? So Allah revealed: ﴿The asking of forgiveness by Abraham for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him﴾, the verse.

17327. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar: that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Abraham asked forgiveness for his father while he was a polytheist, so I will not stop asking forgiveness for Abu Talib until my Lord forbids me from it!" His companions said: "We will certainly ask forgiveness for our fathers just as the Prophet (ﷺ) asked forgiveness for his uncle!" So Allah revealed: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists﴾, up to His saying: ﴿disassociated himself from him﴾.

17328. Ibn WakI' related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun related to us, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: When death approached Abu Talib, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to him, and with him were 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Umayya and Abu Jahl ibn Hisham. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "O uncle, you are the person of greatest right over me, and the one whose favour upon me is the finest, and truly you have a greater right over me than my father. So say a word by which the intercession will be due to me on the Day of Resurrection. Say: There is no god but Allah." = Then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Ibn 'Abd al-A'la, from Muhammad ibn Thawr.

* *

Others said: Rather, it was revealed concerning the mother of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), for he wished to ask forgiveness for her, but he was prevented from doing so.

Those who said this:

17329. Ahmad ibn Ishaq related to us, saying: Abu Ahmad related to us, saying: Fudayl related to us, from 'Ata': When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to Mecca, he stood at the grave of his mother until the sun heated it upon him, hoping that he would be permitted to ask forgiveness for her, until this was revealed: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were of kin﴾, up to His saying: ﴿disassociated himself from him﴾.

17330. ..... related to us, saying: Abu Ahmad related to us, saying: Qays related to us, from 'Alqama ibn Martad, from Sulayman ibn Buraydah, from his father: that the Prophet (ﷺ) came to the traces (rasm) = he said: and my strong opinion is that he said: a grave [[In the printed edition: "came to traces - and my greater opinion is that he said: a grave", differing from what is in the manuscript; the correct reading is what is in the manuscript, because he mentioned the construct "traces" and then specified and said "grave", as the more likely of his suppositions, meaning: "traces of a grave", in apposition.]] = and he sat beside it and began to speak, then he rose weeping. I said: "O Messenger of Allah, we saw what you did!" He said: "I asked my Lord for permission to visit the grave of my mother, and He permitted me. I asked Him for permission to ask forgiveness for her, but He did not permit me." Never was he seen weeping more than on that day. [[The report 17330: 'Alqama ibn Martad al-Hadrami is trustworthy, and the group (of compilers) narrated from him. He has passed under number 11330.
Sulayman ibn Buraydah ibn al-Husayb al-Aslami is trustworthy; he narrated from his father, and he is trustworthy. He has passed under number 11330.
And his father, Buraydah ibn al-Husayb al-Aslami, is a Companion. He embraced Islam before Badr but did not take part in it. This report is of sound chain, and Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his tafsir (4:35) with this wording.
Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad 5:359, by way of Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Khalaf, from Khalifa, from Sulayman ibn Buraydah, from his father, with a different wording, in a longer form.
He narrated it from the route of Muharib ibn Dithar, from Ibn Buraydah, from his father (5:355), then from the route of al-Qasim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Buraydah, from his father (5:356).]]

17331. Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe﴾, up to: ﴿that they are companions of the Blazing Fire﴾: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wished to ask forgiveness for his mother, but Allah forbade him from doing so. He said: "Indeed Abraham, the friend of Allah, asked forgiveness for his father!" So Allah revealed: ﴿The asking of forgiveness by Abraham for his father﴾, up to: ﴿forbearing and tender-hearted﴾.

Others said: Rather, it was revealed because some people among the believers were asking forgiveness for their dead polytheist relatives, so they were forbidden from doing so.

Those who said this:

17332. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to me, saying: Mu'awiya related to us, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists﴾, the verse. They used to ask forgiveness for them, until this verse was revealed. When it was revealed, they refrained from asking forgiveness for their dead, but He did not forbid them from asking forgiveness for the living until they die. Then Allah revealed: ﴿The asking of forgiveness by Abraham for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him﴾, the verse.

17333. Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada regarding His saying: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists﴾, the verse. It was mentioned to us that some men among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O Prophet of Allah, among our fathers were those who were good neighbours, who maintained ties of kinship, who freed captives, and who fulfilled their covenants. Should we not ask forgiveness for them?" He said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Yes! By Allah, I will certainly ask forgiveness for my father, just as Abraham asked forgiveness for his father!" He said: So Allah revealed: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists﴾, until: ﴿the Blazing Fire﴾. Then Allah excused Abraham, saying: ﴿The asking of forgiveness by Abraham for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, he disassociated himself from him﴾. He said: It was also mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah said: "Words were revealed to me which entered my ear and settled in my heart: I have been commanded not to ask forgiveness for one who dies a polytheist; whoever gives the surplus of his wealth, it is good for him; whoever withholds it, it is evil for him; and Allah does not blame anyone for what is sufficient (kafaf)." [[Kafaf (with a fatha on the kaf) means the provision that is sufficient for a person's need, with nothing left over.
If a person has no surplus beyond his sustenance, the Exalted does not blame him, provided he does not give to anyone. Compare this meaning in what has preceded, number 4173.]]

The grammarians (ahl al-'arabiyya) differed about the meaning of His saying: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists﴾.

Some grammarians of Basra said: The meaning is: it was not for them to ask forgiveness. Likewise the meaning of His saying: ﴿It is not for any soul to believe﴾ means: it is not for a soul to believe ﴿except by the permission of Allah﴾ (10:100).

* *

Some grammarians of Kufa said: Its meaning is: it was not fitting for them to ask forgiveness for them. He said: Likewise, when "an" (that) comes with "kana" (was), all of it is interpreted as "yanbaghi" (it is fitting): ﴿It is not for a Prophet to deceive﴾ (3:161), meaning: it was not fitting for him; this is not among his characteristics. He said: Therefore, when "an" enters to indicate the future, [[In the printed and manuscript editions: "tadullu" without the lam; the context requires it.]] because "yanbaghi" demands the future.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿The asking of forgiveness by Abraham for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him﴾, the scholars differed about the occasion on which it was revealed.

Some of them said: It was revealed because the Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions used to ask forgiveness for their dead polytheist relatives, thinking that Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful, had done so, when Allah revealed His words reporting about Abraham: ﴿He said: Peace be upon you. I will ask forgiveness for you of my Lord; indeed, He has been gracious to me﴾ (19:47).

We have mentioned the reports from some of those whose names we have mentioned, and we will mention those whose names we have not mentioned.

17334. Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Khalil, from 'Ali, who said: I heard a man asking forgiveness for his parents while they were both polytheists. I said: Does a man ask forgiveness for his parents while they are both polytheists? He said: Did Abraham not ask forgiveness for his father? He said: So I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and mentioned that to him, and Allah revealed: ﴿The asking of forgiveness by Abraham﴾, up to: ﴿he disassociated himself from him﴾. [[The report 17334: Abu al-Khalil is 'Abd Allah ibn Abi al-Khalil al-Hamdani, trustworthy, whose biography is in al-Tahdhib, and in Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/45, and Ibn Sa'd in al-Tabaqat 6:169, and he said: "He narrated from 'Ali three hadiths, from the hadith of Ibn Abi Ishaq." He distinguished him from "'Abd Allah ibn al-Khalil al-Hadrami" (al-Tabaqat 6:170), and Ibn Abi Hatim and others did likewise.
This report was narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad, number 1085, by way of Wakí', from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, and by way of 'Abd al-Rahman, from Sufyan, from him. He narrated it earlier, number 771, by way of Yahya ibn Adam, from Sufyan. See the following report.]]

17335. Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Yahya related to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Khalil, from 'Ali: that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to ask forgiveness for his two parents while they were polytheists, until this was revealed: ﴿The asking of forgiveness by Abraham for his father﴾, up to His saying: ﴿he disassociated himself from him﴾. [[The report 17335: Ahmad narrated it in the Musnad, number 771, also by way of Yahya ibn Adam, but with a wording other than this one, and that the one asking forgiveness was a man among the Muslims, like the one that has passed. See its explanation in the commentary of my brother al-Sayyid Ahmad.]]

It was said: ﴿The asking of forgiveness by Abraham for his father was only because of a promise﴾, and its meaning is: only after a promise, as one says: "This matter was not except because of such-and-such a cause," meaning: after that cause, or on account of it. Likewise His saying: "only because of a promise" means: on account of a promise and after it. [[See the explanation of "'an" in the sense of "ba'd" (after) in what has preceded, 10:313.]]

* *

Some people interpreted the words of Allah: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were of kin﴾, the verse, to mean that the prohibition from Allah concerns asking forgiveness for polytheists after their death, based on His saying: ﴿after it has become clear to them that they are companions of the Blazing Fire﴾. They said: That is not made clear to anyone except by dying in their disbelief; but while a person is alive there is no way to know that, so it is permissible for the believers to ask forgiveness for them.

Those who said this:

17336. Sulayman ibn 'Umar al-Raqqi related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak related to us, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from al-Shaybani, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: A Jewish man died, and he had a Muslim son who did not go out with his funeral. This was mentioned to Ibn 'Abbas, who said: It was fitting for him to walk with him and bury him, and to pray for him for goodness while he is alive; but when he dies, leave him to his affair! Then he recited: ﴿The asking of forgiveness by Abraham for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, he disassociated himself from him﴾, and he did not pray for him. [[The report 17336: "al-Shaybani" is Dirar ibn Murra, Abu Sinan al-Shaybani the elder, trustworthy, whose biography is in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 2/2/340, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/465. He was mentioned previously under number 10238, to distinguish him from Abu Sinan al-Shaybani the younger, who is Sa'id ibn Sinan al-Barjami.
The following report will state his name explicitly.]]

17337. Ibn Wakí' related to us, saying: Fudayl related to us, from Dirar ibn Murra, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: A Christian man died, and his son left him to the people of his religion. I came to Ibn 'Abbas and mentioned that to him, and he said: What would it have cost him if he had walked with him, shrouded him (ajannahu), and asked forgiveness for him? [[ "Ajannahu": he covered him, meaning buried him in his grave.]] Then he recited: ﴿The asking of forgiveness by Abraham for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him﴾, the verse. [[The report 17337: Dirar ibn Murra is al-Shaybani, who was mentioned in the commentary before it. The wording of this report shows clear confusion, for the first report before it, from al-Shaybani, indicates a prohibition on asking forgiveness for him after his death, whereas in this report there is permission to ask forgiveness for him after his death. I do not know where this disagreement in al-Shaybani's wording came from.]]

* *

Others interpreted "al-istighfar" (asking forgiveness) in this place to mean prayer (al-salat).

Those who said this:

17338. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to me, saying: Kathir ibn Hisham related to us, from Ja'far ibn Burqan, who said: Habib ibn Abi Marzuq related to us, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, who said: I never refrained from praying over anyone of the people of this qibla, even if she were an Abyssinian woman pregnant from fornication, because I have not heard that Allah withholds prayer except from the polytheists. Allah says: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to ask forgiveness for the polytheists﴾.

* *

Others interpreted it to mean the asking of forgiveness which is supplication (du'a').

Those who said this:

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 113 (part 2 of 2):

17339. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from ʿIṣmah ibn Zāmil, from his father, who said: I heard Abū Hurayrah say: "May Allah have mercy on a man who asks forgiveness for Abū Hurayrah and his mother." I said: "And for his father?" He said: "No. My father died as a polytheist."

[[Report 17339: ʿIṣmah ibn Zāmil al-Ṭāʾī is biographed in al-Kabīr 4/1/63, Ibn Abī Ḥātim 3/2/20, and Lisān al-Mīzān 4:168-169, where it is said: "He related from his father, from Abū Hurayrah. Related from him: Wakīʿ and Jamīl ibn Ḥammād al-Ṭāʾī." Al-Barqānī said: "I said to al-Dāraqutnī: Jamīl ibn Ḥammād related from ʿIṣmah ibn Zāmil, and he mentioned this chain. He said: 'A Bedouin chain, which is used for corroboration (iʿtibār).'"
In the printed edition it was "ʿIṣmah ibn Rāshid," which differs from the manuscript; it seems the editor searched, did not find it, and assumed a distortion.
His father, Zāmil ibn Awus al-Ṭāʾī, is biographed in al-Kabīr 2/1/405 and Ibn Ḥātim 1/2/617, and Lisān al-Mīzān 2:469. Al-Dāraqutnī said: "A chain that is narrated, used for corroboration." Ibn Ḥibbān mentioned him among the reliable (al-Thiqāt).]]
* *
Abū Jaʿfar (al-Ṭabarī) said: We have shown that the meaning of "istighfār" (seeking forgiveness) is a servant's asking his Lord to forgive sins. Since that is so, and a servant's asking his Lord for this may occur during prayer and outside prayer, [[See the explanation of istighfār in the earlier linguistic indexes, under (ghafara).]] neither of the two opinions we mentioned is invalid. This is because Allah, by prohibiting the seeking of forgiveness for a polytheist, gave a general ruling after it became clear that he is among the companions of the Blazing Fire, and He did not single out any circumstance in which seeking forgiveness for him was permitted.
* *
As for His saying ﴿after it has become clear to them that they are the companions of the Blazing Fire﴾, its meaning is what I have already explained: after they know that he died as a disbeliever, that he is among the people of the Fire.
* *
It has been said that "companions of the Blazing Fire" means that they are its inhabitants and its residents who dwell in it, just as one says of the residents of a house, "These are the companions of this house," meaning its inhabitants. [[See the explanation of "companions of the Fire" and similar expressions in the earlier linguistic indexes, under (ṣaḥiba).]]
* *
Those of the exegetes (ahl al-taʾwīl) said things similar to what we have said.
Those who said that:
17340. Al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: Isḥāq narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatādah, regarding His saying ﴿after it has become clear to them that they are the companions of the Blazing Fire﴾, he said: It became clear to the Prophet ﷺ when Abū Ṭālib died that repentance had been cut off from him.
17341. Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah, who said: "It became clear to him" when he died, and he knew that repentance had been cut off from him. He meant by this His saying ﴿after it has become clear to them that they are the companions of the Blazing Fire﴾.
17342. It was related from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd ibn Sulaymān narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk regarding His saying ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to seek forgiveness for the polytheists﴾, the verse, he said: [This refers to] when they die as polytheists. Allah says: ﴿Indeed, whoever associates others with Allah, Allah has forbidden him Paradise﴾, [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "wa-man yushrik", which is an error; the recitation is what has been established.]] the verse [al-Māʾidah: 72].
* *
The exegetes differed regarding the interpretation of His saying ﴿So when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, he disowned him﴾.
Some of them said: Its meaning is: when it became clear to him by his death as a polytheist associating others with Allah, he disowned him and abandoned seeking forgiveness for him.
Those who said that:
17343. Muḥammad ibn Bashshār narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, saying: Sufyān narrated to us, from Ḥabīb, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Ibrāhīm continued to seek forgiveness for his father until he died. ﴿So when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, he disowned him.﴾
17344. Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Ḥabīb, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Ibrāhīm continued to seek forgiveness for his father until he died. When he died, it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah.
17345. Al-Ḥārith narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz narrated to us, saying: Sufyān narrated to us, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Ibrāhīm did not cease seeking forgiveness for his father until he died; when he died, he no longer sought forgiveness for him.
17346. Al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, saying: Muʿāwiyah narrated to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿The seeking of forgiveness by Ibrāhīm for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, he disowned him﴾, meaning: he sought forgiveness for him while he was alive; when he died, he refrained from seeking forgiveness for him.
17347. Muṭar ibn Muḥammad al-Ḍabbī narrated to me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim and Abū Qutaybah Muslim ibn Qutaybah narrated to us, both saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Mujāhid, regarding His saying ﴿When it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, he disowned him﴾, he said: When he died.
17348. Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from al-Ḥakam, from Mujāhid, the like of it.
17349. Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: ʿĪsā narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid: ﴿When it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah﴾, he said: His death while he was a disbeliever.
17350. Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from Shuʿbah, from al-Ḥakam, from Mujāhid, the like of it.
17351. ...... narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abī Ghaniyyah narrated to us, from his father, from al-Ḥakam: ﴿When it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, he disowned him﴾, he said: When he died without having believed. [[Report 17351: Ibn Abī Ghaniyyah is Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Ḥumayd ibn Abī Ghaniyyah al-Khuzāʿī, who has passed several times, the last being no. 11085.
His father is ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Ḥumayd ibn Abī Ghaniyyah, who related from al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtaybah; he has also passed, nos. 10597 and 11085.
In the printed edition it was "narrated to us: al-Barrāʾ ibn ʿUtbah," which differs from the manuscript, because the copyist made an error in the dots; the correct reading is what has been established.]]
17352. Al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: Abū Ḥudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār: ﴿When it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, he disowned him﴾: his death while he was a disbeliever.
17353. ...... narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr ibn ʿAwn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, regarding His saying ﴿When it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, he disowned him﴾, he said: When he died.
17354. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah: ﴿When it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, he disowned him﴾: when he died upon his polytheism, [then] "he disowned him."
17355. It was related from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd ibn Sulaymān narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say regarding His saying ﴿And the seeking of forgiveness by Ibrāhīm for his father﴾: Ibrāhīm, may Allah's blessings be upon him, was hoping that his father would believe as long as he was alive; when he died upon his polytheism, he disowned him.
17356. Al-Qāsim narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjāj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujāhid: ﴿When it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, he disowned him﴾, he said: His death while he was a disbeliever.
17357. Aḥmad ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, saying: Abū Aḥmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyān narrated to us, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Ibrāhīm continued to seek forgiveness for his father until he died; when he died, it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, so he no longer sought forgiveness for him. [[Report 17357: Aḥmad ibn Isḥāq al-Ahwāzī, the teacher of Abū Jaʿfar, has passed many times, and this chain recurs in the tafsīr. In the manuscript and the printed edition here it reads "Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq," which is a plain error.]]
17358. ...... narrated to us, saying: Abū Aḥmad narrated to us, saying: Abū Isrāʾīl narrated to us, from ʿAlī ibn Badhīmah, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿When it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah﴾, he said: When he died.
* *
Others said: Its meaning is: when it became clear to him in the Hereafter. This is because his father will cling to him when he wants to cross the Ṣirāṭ (bridge), so he passes him by it; when he almost gets past him, Ibrāhīm glances back, and there is his father in the form of an ape or a hyena. Then he releases him and disowns him at that moment. [[In the printed edition: "fa-kha-allā ʿanhu wa-tabarra'a minhu" ("then he released him and disowned him"); the correct reading is what is in the manuscript.]]
Those who said that:
17359. ʿAmr ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, saying: Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sulaymān narrated to us, saying: I heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr say: Ibrāhīm will say on the Day of Resurrection: "My Lord, my father! My Lord, my father!" When it is the third time, he will take his hand, and he will turn toward him, and he is a hyena [ḍiʿbān], and he will disown him. [["Ḍiʿbān" (with a kasra and sukūn), the male hyena; the word ḍubaʿ, hyenas, takes the alif and nūn only for the masculine. The feminine is "ḍabuʿ" (with fatḥa and ḍamma), and "ḍabuʿ" is also said of the male. The masculine form appears in Ṭabarī's speech just above and will appear in the report that follows this one.]]
17360. Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Jarīr narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr, who said: You will all be gathered on the Day of Resurrection in one plain; the caller will make you hear, and the sight will reach you. He said: Then Hell will exhale a breath such that no angel brought near and no sent prophet remains but falls upon his knees, his muscles trembling! He said: I think he said: "Myself, myself!" And the Ṣirāṭ will be set over Hell like the edge of a sword, a slippery, treacherous path [dahḍ maziyyah], and on its two sides will be angels with hooks like the thorns of saʿdān. He said: They will pass like lightning, like the wind, like birds, like the swift mounts, like the swift men. [[The phrase "like the swift mounts, like the swift men": "ajāwīd" is the plural of "ajwad," which is the plural of "jawād," the excellent, swift horse; one says "faras jawād al-shadd" when it gallops with continuous, untiring speed. "Rikāb" are camels ridden upon, singular "rāḥilah," which has no singular from its own root. As for "rijāl," I think it is the plural of "rajīl," a horse trodden for riding that does not sweat, or it is the plural of "rajul," meaning fast runners, because the Majmaʿ al-Zawāʾid has: "like the running of a horse, then like the running of a man."
However, the version in Lisān al-Arab under (jawd) says: "In the hadith of the Ṣirāṭ: some of them pass like the swift horses," and al-Ḥākim's version in al-Mustadrak: "like the swift horses and the mounts."]] And the angels will say: "My Lord, keep us safe, keep us safe!" So there is the one who escapes safe, and the one who escapes torn, and the one thrown into the Fire [makdūs]. [[Makdūs: pushed into it, from "al-kads," which is throwing down and felling; "kadasa bihi al-arḍ" means he threw him down to the ground and pressed him against it; "kadasahu" means he drove him from behind and herded him. This is one of two versions; the other is "mukardas," and "mukardas" is one whose hands and feet are gathered and bound, then thrown to the ground as is done to a captive. This is al-Ḥākim's version in al-Mustadrak.]] Ibrāhīm will say to his father: "I used to command you in this world, but you disobeyed me, and I will not leave you today. So take hold of my waist-cloth!" [ḥaqw: the place where the waist-wrap is tied at the side]. Then he will take hold of his two forelegs [ḍabʿayh], and he will be transformed into a hyena. When he sees that he has been transformed, he will disown him. [[Report 17360: The hadith of the Ṣirāṭ was related by al-Ḥākim in al-Mustadrak 4:582-584 by way of Hishām ibn Saʿd, from Zayd ibn al-Muslim, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, at length. He said: "A hadith with a sound chain, though they did not record it in this form," and it contains no mention of our father Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him.
Among the hadiths about the Ṣirāṭ is that which al-Haythamī recorded in Majmaʿ al-Zawāʾid 10:358-359, from the hadith of ʿĀʾishah. "Aḥmad related it, and in its chain is Ibn Lahīʿah, who is weak, though he has been declared trustworthy. The rest of its narrators are narrators of the Ṣaḥīḥ." This report contains the mention I pointed to in the note on p. 522, from his saying "like the swift horses and the mounts." Al-Haythamī also recorded it (10:359-360) from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, a report containing "like the running of a horse, then like the running of a man," as I pointed out in note 2 on p. 522.]]
* *
Abū Jaʿfar said: The most correct of these opinions is the statement of Allah, which is His report about Ibrāhīm: that when it became clear to him that his father was an enemy of Allah, he disowned him. That was at the time of his knowledge and certainty that he was an enemy of Allah, and that he was a polytheist, which was the state at his death upon his polytheism.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 114 (part 1 of 2):

The discussion of the interpretation of His words: ﴿Indeed, Abraham was ʾawwāh, forbearing﴾ (9:114).

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation differed concerning "al-awwāh."

Some of them said: It is the one who supplicates much (al-daʿʿāʾ). [["al-daʿʿāʾ" (with the ʿayn shaddah): one who supplicates much.]]

Those who said this:

17361 – Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from ʿAsim, from Zirr, from ʿAbd Allah, who said: "Al-awwāh" is al-daʿʿāʾ.

17362 – Abu Kurayb and Ibn Wakiʿ related to us, both saying: Abu Bakr related to us, from ʿAsim, from Zirr, from ʿAbd Allah, who said: "Al-awwāh" is al-daʿʿāʾ.

17363 – Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Jarir ibn Hazim related to me, from ʿAsim ibn Bahdalah, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, who said: I asked ʿAbd Allah about "al-awwāh," and he said: It is al-daʿʿāʾ.

17364 – Ibn Wakiʿ related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Bishr related to us, from Ibn Abi ʿArubah, from ʿAsim, from Zirr, from ʿAbd Allah, the like of it.

17365 – … related to us, saying: Qabisah related to us, from Sufyan, from ʿAbd al-Karim, from Abu ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbd Allah, who said: "Al-awwāh": al-daʿʿāʾ.

17366 – … related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Sufyan, from ʿAsim, from Zirr, from ʿAbd Allah, the like of it.

17367 – Ahmad related to us, saying: Abu Ahmad related to us, saying: Sufyan and Israʾil related to us, from ʿAsim, from Zirr, from ʿAbd Allah, the like of it. [[The reports 17363–17367: the hadith of Zirr from ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, cited by al-Haythami in Majmaʿ al-Zawaʾid 7:35, who said: "Al-Tabarani narrated it, and in its chain is ʿAsim – meaning ʿAsim ibn Abi al-Najud – who is trustworthy but has some weakness."]]

17368 – Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim and Ibn Wakiʿ related to me, both saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah related to us, saying: Dawud ibn Abi Hind related to us, who said: I was informed from ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr, who said: "Al-awwāh": al-daʿʿāʾ.

17369 – Ishaq ibn Shahin related to me, saying: Dawud related to us, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr al-Laythi, from his father, who said: "Al-awwāh": al-daʿʿāʾ.

* *

Others said: Rather, it is the merciful (al-raḥīm).

Those who said this:

17370 – Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Salamah, from Muslim al-Batin, from Abu al-ʿUbaydayn, who said: ʿAbd Allah was asked about "al-awwāh," and he said: Al-raḥīm. [[The report 17370: the report of Abu al-ʿUbaydayn from ʿAbd Allah, which al-Tabari transmits under numbers 17370, 17378, 17386.
"Salamah" is Salamah ibn Kuhayl al-Hadrami, trustworthy, who has appeared many times, the last at no. 14503.
"Muslim al-Batin" is Muslim ibn ʿImran, trustworthy, appearing at no. 14503 – 14056.
"Abu al-ʿUbaydayn" is Muʿawiyah ibn Sabrah ibn Husayn al-Sawaʾi al-ʿAmiri al-Aʿma, trustworthy; Ibn Masʿud used to draw him near and favor him. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/1/329, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/387.
This report was cited by al-Haythami in Majmaʿ al-Zawaʾid 7:35 in full, and he said: "All of it was narrated by al-Tabarani through several chains, and the men of the first two narrations are trustworthy."]]

17371 – Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar related to me, saying: Shuʿbah related to us, from al-Hakam, who said: I heard Yahya ibn al-Jazzar narrate, from Abu al-ʿUbaydayn, a man blind in sight, that he asked ʿAbd Allah about "al-awwāh," and he said: Al-raḥīm. [[The report 17371: Yahya ibn al-Jazzar al-ʿUrani is trustworthy; he has appeared at nos. 5425, 16405, 16406, 16408.]]

17374 – Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us – and Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: My father related to us – from Sufyan, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Muslim al-Batin, from Abu al-ʿUbaydayn, who said: I asked ʿAbd Allah about "al-awwāh," and he said: It is al-raḥīm.

17375 – Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from al-Hakam, from Yahya ibn al-Jazzar, who said: Abu al-ʿUbaydayn came to ʿAbd Allah and said to him: What is your need? He said: What is "al-awwāh"? He said: Al-raḥīm.

17379 – Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: Abu Usamah related to us, from Zakariyya, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Maysarah, who said: "Al-awwāh": al-raḥīm.

17380 – … related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Maysarah, the like of it.

17381 – Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Maysarah, the like of it.

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these sayings in my view is the saying of ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, which Zirr narrated from him: that it is al-daʿʿāʾ (the one who supplicates much). [[See the preceding reports 17361–17368.]]

We said that this is more correct because God mentioned this and described Abraham, His intimate friend (peace be upon him), with it, after describing him with supplication and seeking forgiveness for his father. He said: ﴿And the plea of forgiveness of Abraham for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy to God, he disassociated himself from him﴾ (9:114), and he abandoned supplication and seeking forgiveness for him. Then He said: Indeed Abraham was one who supplicates much to his Lord, who complains to Him, forbearing toward whoever reviles him and harms him with what is disliked. That is because he (peace be upon him) promised his father to seek forgiveness for him and to ask God to forgive him, at the time of his father's threat and his warning to him with insult, after he had rejected his counsel regarding God and his saying: ﴿Do you reject my gods, O Abraham? If you do not desist, I will surely stone you, so leave me for a long time﴾ (19:46). So he (peace be upon him) said to him: ﴿Peace be upon you. I will ask my Lord to forgive you; indeed He is ever gracious to me. And I will leave you and what you invoke other than God, and I will invoke my Lord; perhaps I will not be in invoking my Lord unhappy﴾ (19:47–48). So he fulfilled his promise to his father by seeking forgiveness for him, until it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God. Then God described him as one who supplicates much to his Lord, forbearing toward the one who acted foolishly toward him.

**Tabari's commentary (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 9, verse 114 (part 2 of 2)**

17418: Yahya ibn Uthman ibn Salih al-Sahmi narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, saying: Ibn Lahi'a narrated to us, saying: al-Harith ibn Yazid narrated to me, from Ali ibn Rabah, from Uqba ibn Amir, that he said to a man called "Dhu al-Bajadayn": "Indeed he is awwah!" This was because he was a man who frequently remembered God with the Qur'an and supplication, and raised his voice.

[[The narrator: Yahya ibn Uthman ibn Salih al-Qurashi al-Sahmi al-Misri, the shaykh of al-Tabari, was criticized because he used to narrate from books other than his own. He is listed in al-Tahdhib and in Ibn Abi Hatim, 4/2/175.
His father: Uthman ibn Salih ibn Safwan al-Sahmi al-Misri, trustworthy but subject to some criticism. He is listed in al-Tahdhib and in Ibn Abi Hatim, 3/1/154. Abu Hatim said: "He was a righteous shaykh, sound in his reports. It was said that he used to be taught (his narrations), and he said: No."
Ibn Lahi'a has been mentioned many times, and the discussion about him has been recorded.
al-Harith ibn Zubayd al-Hadrami al-Misri, trustworthy. He is listed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 1/2/283, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/93.
Ali ibn Rabah ibn Qusayr al-Lakhmi al-Misri, trustworthy. He has passed under numbers 4747 and 10341.
Uqba ibn Amir al-Juhani, a Companion who held the governorship of Egypt.
Dhu al-Bajadayn is Abdullah ibn Abd Nahm al-Muzani. He is listed in al-Isabah under this name, and in al-Isti'ab, p. 349, under "Abdullah Dhu al-Bajadayn al-Muzani," and similarly in Usd al-Ghaba 3:123.
This report was narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad 4:159 through this same chain. al-Haythami cited it in Majma' al-Zawa'id 9:369 and said: "Ahmad and al-Tabarani narrated it, and their chains are good." Ibn Hajar cited it in al-Isabah, saying: "Ahmad and Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ghariyabi narrated it in the Book of Remembrance (Kitab al-Dhikr), through Ibn Lahi'a..." and he mentioned the chain and the report.
Regarding the matter of Abdullah Dhu al-Bajadayn there is a difficulty. This is the place to present it briefly. The author of al-Isabah mentioned in his biography that he was the guide of the Prophet ﷺ on his migration, and he cited a report which al-Hajari transmitted in his Nawadir (manuscript), where he said:
"Abdullah ibn Dhi al-Bajadayn al-Muzani said, while driving the Prophet ﷺ on a swift mount, in the hollow of the dry ground from the white hill of al-Arj during his migration:
Make your paths and your pace open wide
Like the Gemini crossing the stars
This is Abu al-Qasim, so be straight, O she-camel."
al-Hafiz (Ibn Hajar) mentioned this verse in his report. The author of Lisan al-Arab cited the report of his guiding our Prophet ﷺ under the root (b-j-d), cited the verse under (d-r-j), (ʿ-r-d), and (s-w-m), and it includes al-Hajari's report.
The rajaz (verse) he says to his she-camel, saying to her: "Ta'arradi" (move aside), meaning: take to the right and left, and avoid the rough passes between the mountains, which are the "madarij" (paths). "Sumi" is from al-sawm, which is swiftness of passage together with aiming for the direction in travel. "Ta'arrud al-Jawza'" (the way the Gemini crosses) because the Gemini passes obliquely at its side, not straight across the sky.
It is said regarding the reason he was called "Dhu al-Bajadayn": when he wished to go to the Prophet ﷺ, his mother cut a bajad (cloak) in two; he wrapped himself in one and covered himself with the other. It is also said that when the Messenger of God ﷺ migrated, Abdullah said to his father: "Let me guide them to the way!" But his father refused, took his clothes from him, and left him naked. So he made a bajad of hair and threw it over his private parts, then caught up with them, took hold of the bridle of the Prophet's ﷺ she-camel, and began to recite the rajaz that we have mentioned.
What we have seen in the biographies is that the guide of the Messenger of God ﷺ on his migration was Abdullah ibn Urayqit al-Laythi. This Abdullah was not a Muslim, and there is no sound report that he became Muslim afterward, and he was hired (as a guide).
(Ibn Hisham 2:136; al-Rawd al-Unuf 2:28; then his biography in al-Isabah and elsewhere.) He is without doubt not Dhu al-Bajadayn, because Dhu al-Bajadayn was from Muzayna; also because he died at Tabuk; and also because they mention that the Prophet ﷺ did not enter the grave of anyone except five people, among them Abdullah al-Muzani, Dhu al-Bajadayn.
Once this is understood, the confusion that suggests they were one man is dispelled, and the matter of Dhu al-Bajadayn's guiding requires clarification which the books of biography do not mention.]] For this reason it is said to one who groans from pain or sickness: "la tata'awwah" (do not groan). [[In the printed edition it reads "lam tata'awwah." This was done because the scribe of the manuscript confused the "la" in his writing, so the editor made an effort, and the correct reading is what has been established here.]] As al-Mutaqqib al-Abdi said:

When I rise at night to saddle her,
she groans the groan of a grieving man.

[[His Diwan: 29; al-Mufaddaliyyat: 586; Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu Ubayda 1:270; Tabaqat Fuhul al-Shu'ara': 231; Lisan al-Arab (awh). This verse was mentioned earlier in the commentary on a verse of the same qasida, 2:548, note 1. He means by this his she-camel, which longs for her homes and homelands.]]

And from it is the saying of al-Ja'di:

Swift, lively, following the doves after they
halt for a complaint, a groan, and a bristling.

[[His Diwan: 33, 52; Jamharat Ash'ar al-Arab: 146; al-Ma'ani al-Kabir: 315. From the qasida of al-Nabigha, which the Messenger of God ﷺ heard, may my father and mother be sacrificed for him. When he reached his saying:
"Our glory and our ancestors have reached the sky,
and we seek after that a further height."
He said to him: "Where is the height, O Abu Layla?" He said: "Paradise!" He said: "Indeed, if God wills." Then he recited to him what was in it of wisdom. He said: "May God not break your teeth." So he remained the most beautiful of people in his teeth; whenever a tooth fell out, another grew in its place, and al-Nabigha lived to a great age.
His saying "darub" (ḍurūḥ): meaning she kicks with her legs, strikes with them, meaning her vigor and her extending of her stride on the journey. It is also narrated as "khanuf" and "turuh." "Marwah" means very vigorous, from al-maraḥ (exuberance). His saying "tatba' al-warq" is thus in the manuscript; the narration in his Diwan is "tab'ath al-warq" and "tu'ajjil al-warq," meaning that she frightens them and makes them leave their halting place; both narrations are clear in meaning. As for the narration of the commentary, if it is sound, then he meant that she follows the complaint and the groaning, so she is startled and takes fright. "Al-warq" here means the sand grouse (al-qata). "Al-qata" is of mixed colors. In the printed edition it read "al-wadq," which is an error. His saying "wa-tanammara" was in the printed edition "wa-tashammara," which is an undoubted error; the manuscript is undotted, and this is the correct reading. "Al-tanammur" means anger. The narration in the Diwan and elsewhere is "wa-tadhammara," which is clearer and more evident. His saying "ahah" means groaning.
The verse's second half in the Diwan reads: "yu'arrisna tashku ahatan wa-tadhamara," and what is in the manuscript agrees with what is in al-Ma'ani al-Kabir of Ibn Qutayba, "shakwa."]] The Arabs hardly ever say it in the form "fa'ala yaf'ulu," but rather they say "tafa''ala yatafa''alu," like "ta'awwaha yata'awwahu" and "awwaha yu'awwihu."
As the rajiz said:

So the herdsman groaned, and his dogs yelped.
[[I do not know who said it. "Dawda" means they cried out and shouted. In the hadith, when he mentioned the Prophet's ﷺ seeing the Fire, may God protect us from its punishment: "He saw in it people who, when its flame reached them, yelped (dawdawa)," meaning they made a clamor from their shouting and noise.]]

They also say: "Awh minka!" (Oh, from you!). al-Farra' mentioned that Abu al-Jarrah recited to him:

Ah! from the remembrance, whenever I recall her,
and from the distance of land and sky between us.

[[Lisan al-Arab (awh). I do not know who said it; its variant readings are mentioned there.]]

He said: "Sometimes they recited to us: *fa-awwin min al-dhikra* (with a different vowelling)." Had the form "fa'ala" come from it in its original root, it would have been: "ah, ya'uhu awhan."

* * *

Since the meaning of that is "to lament, to grieve, and to humble oneself," the interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) differed about it in the way I have mentioned. Some said its meaning is "compassion": that this came from Abraham out of tenderness toward his father, and mercy toward him and toward other people.

Others said: it was only from him because of the soundness of his certainty, his good knowledge of God's greatness, and his humility before Him.

Others said: it was because of the soundness of his faith in his Lord.

Others said: it was from him when reciting the revelation of God, the One who sent it down to him.

Others said: it was from him when mentioning his Lord.

All of this returns to what I have said, and the meanings of some of it are close to one another, because the grieving one who humbles himself to his Lord, whose heart is submissive to Him, is overcome by this when he asks his Lord and calls upon Him for his needs, and these qualities which the commentators pointed to as the interpretation of God's words come upon him: ﴿Indeed, Abraham was tender-hearted and forbearing﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 115:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And Allah would not let a people go astray after He had guided them until He makes clear to them what they should beware of. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, He says: "And Allah would not decree against you misguidance, in your seeking forgiveness for your dead polytheist relatives, after He had granted you guidance and enabled you to believe in Him and His Messenger, until He sends forward to you a prohibition against it, so that you would then abandon refraining from it. As for before He makes clear to you the dislike of that through a prohibition, and then you transgress His prohibition regarding what He has forbidden you, He will not judge you to be astray, because obedience and disobedience only occur with respect to one who is commanded and prohibited. As for one who has not been commanded and has not been prohibited, he is not obedient or disobedient in what he was not commanded and was not forbidden." "Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things" means: May His remembrance be exalted, Allah has knowledge of what occurred within your souls when Allah forbade you to seek forgiveness for your dead polytheist relatives, of the anguish over what had passed from you of seeking forgiveness for them before He sent forward to you the prohibition against it, and of other hidden aspects of your affairs and the affairs of His servants, both inward and outward. Thus He made clear to you His forbearance in that regard, so as to lift from you the burden of grief over it. [[See the explanation of the words of this verse in the linguistic indexes of what preceded.]]

* *

And in accordance with what we have said on this matter, the people of interpretation said:

Those who said so:

17419- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "[And Allah would not] lead a people astray after He had guided them until He makes clear to them what they should beware of," he said: It is Allah's making clear to the believers concerning seeking forgiveness for the polytheists specifically, and in His making clear His obedience and His disobedience, so do or leave.

17420- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And Allah would not lead a people astray after He had guided them until He makes clear to them what they should beware of," he said: It is Allah's making clear to the believers that they should not seek forgiveness for the polytheists specifically, and in His making clear His obedience and His disobedience generally, so do or leave.

17421- ..... He said: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

17422- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, his statement: "And Allah would not lead a people astray after He had guided them until He makes clear to them what they should beware of," he said: Allah makes clear to the believers that they should not seek forgiveness for the polytheists, in His making clear His obedience and His disobedience, so do or leave.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words: ﴿Indeed, to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He gives life and causes death. And you have, besides Allah, no protector and no helper.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed Allah, O people, holds sovereignty over the heavens and the earth and their dominion, and every other ruler besides Him is His servant and slave. Their life and their death are in His hand; He gives life to whom He wills among them and causes death to whom He wills among them. So do not despair, O believers, of fighting those among the rulers who disbelieve in Me, whether they are the kings of Byzantium (al-Rum), the kings of Persia, Abyssinia, or others. Fight them and strive against them in My obedience, for I am the One who grants might to whom I will among them and among you, and who humbles whom I will.

This is an exhortation from Allah, exalted is His praise, to the believers to fight every one of the slave-rulers who disbelieve in Him, and an incitement from Him to them to wage war against them.

As for His words: ﴿And you have, besides Allah, no protector and no helper﴾, He means: You have no one, besides Allah, who is an ally to you and supports you against Him, should you oppose the command of Allah and He punish you for your opposition to His command, nor anyone who can rescue you from His punishment; ﴿and no helper﴾, who can help you against Him if He intends harm to you. That is to say: So put your trust in Allah, fear Him alone, and strive in His way against those who disbelieve in Him, for He has purchased from you your selves and your wealth in exchange for the Garden, [so that] you fight in His way, and so you kill and are killed. [[See the explanation of the words of this verse in the earlier indexes of language.]]

**The commentary on His words: ﴿Certainly Allah turned in mercy toward the Prophet, and the Emigrants and the Helpers who followed him in the hour of hardship, after the hearts of a group of them had nearly swerved. Then He turned to them in mercy. Indeed, He is Kind and Merciful to them.﴾ (9:117)**

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, He means: Allah granted the turning back (to Him) in obedience to His command to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and to the Emigrants who left their homes and their kinsfolk for the Abode of Islam, and to the Helpers of His Messenger for the sake of Allah [[See the explanation of "muhajir" (emigrant) above, p. 434, footnote 2, and the references there.]] = those who followed the Messenger of Allah in the hour of hardship, which involved hardship in provisions, mounts, food and water [[See the explanation of "'usrah" (hardship) above, vol. 6, pp. 28–29.]] = ﴿after the hearts of a group of them had nearly swerved﴾. He means: after the hearts of some of them had nearly inclined away from the truth, doubted their religion and wavered, because of the hardship and distress they suffered on the journey and the campaign [[See the explanation of "zaygh" (swerving) above, vol. 6, pp. 183–184, and the explanation of "fariq" (group) above, vol. 12, p. 388, footnote 1, and the references there.]] = ﴿Then He turned to them﴾. He means: then His majesty and praise granted them the turning back and return to steadfastness in His religion, and the seeing of the truth which had nearly become confused for them = ﴿Indeed, He is Kind and Merciful to them﴾. He means: indeed your Lord is Kind (raʾūf) and Merciful toward those whose hearts were touched by that, because of the hardship and distress they endured on their journey = ﴿Merciful﴾, that He would not destroy them and strip faith from them after they had shown in Allah's cause what they showed alongside His Messenger, and had endured patiently the adversity and the hardship. [[See the explanation of "ra'uf" (kind) and "rahim" (merciful) in the lexical indexes above under the roots (r-'-f) and (r-h-m).]]

* *

Those of the people of ta'wil (interpretation) said what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

17423. Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, saying: 'Asim told us, saying: 'Isa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿in the hour of hardship﴾: during the expedition of Tabuk.

17424. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Aqil, regarding ﴿in the hour of hardship﴾, he said: They set out on a campaign, [[In the printed edition: "during the expedition of Tabuk", which he added on his own; it is not in the manuscript, and it is without doubt the expedition of Tabuk.]] two men and three on one camel. They set out in intense heat, and on that day they suffered intense thirst, so they began slaughtering their camels and squeezing out their stomach contents and drinking its water, [[In the printed edition: "its water", but what is in the manuscript is also correct.]] and that was hardship of water, hardship of mounts, and hardship of provisions. [[The report 17424: "'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Aqil ibn Abi Talib al-Hashimi": weak in narration, not reliable, and his narrations are not used as evidence for his memorization. It passed as no. 487. See the report no. 17427.]]

17425. Al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿the hour of hardship﴾, he said: the expedition of Tabuk. He said: "the hardship": they suffered severe exhaustion, so much that two men would split a date between them, and they would suck on a single date and drink water over it.

17426. Ibn Wakic told us, saying: Ibn Numayr told us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿who followed him in the hour of hardship﴾, he said: the expedition of Tabuk.

17427. ...... told us, saying: Zakariyya ibn 'Adi told us, from Ibn al-Mubarak, from Ma'mar, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Aqil, from Jabir, regarding ﴿who followed him in the hour of hardship﴾, he said: the hardship of mounts, the hardship of provisions, and the hardship of water. [[The report 17427: "Zakariyya ibn 'Adi ibn Zurayq al-Tamimi", trustworthy, passed as nos. 1566, 15446, 16945. In the printed edition it was "Zakariyya ibn 'Ali", and the correct reading is what is in the manuscript, but its reading was not well done.

"'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Aqil": passed as no. 17424.]]

17428. Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, regarding his words: ﴿Certainly Allah turned in mercy toward the Prophet, and the Emigrants and the Helpers who followed him in the hour of hardship﴾, to the end of the verse: those who followed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the expedition of Tabuk toward Syria, in the scorching heat, as Allah knows, the exertion; they suffered severe exhaustion in it, so much so that we were told that two men would split a date between them, and a group would take a date among themselves, one sucking it and then drinking over it, then another sucking it and drinking over it. So Allah turned to them in mercy and brought them back from their campaign.

17429. Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, from 'Utba ibn Abi 'Utba, from Nafi' ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas: that it was said to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah have mercy on him, concerning the matter of the hardship. 'Umar said: We set out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ toward Tabuk in intense summer heat. We stopped at a place where we suffered thirst, so much that we thought our necks would be severed. A man would go to seek water and not return until he thought his neck would be severed, and a man would slaughter his camel, squeeze out its contents [[Al-farth: the dung of the stomach, as long as it is in the stomach.]] and drink it, and place what remained on his liver. Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of Allah, Allah has accustomed you to good in supplication, so pray for us! He said: Do you want that? He said: Yes! So he raised his hands, and did not lower them until the sky spoke, and it overshadowed, then poured down, [["Qalat al-sama'": that is, it came with clouds. In the printed edition it was "malat" (inclined), and I have restored what is in the manuscript, which agrees with what is in Majma' al-Zawa'id. In Ibn Kathir and others it is "sala" (flowed), which is not right. This is a fine and excellent expression.

His words "fa-azallat": that is, the cloud came with shade. In Ibn Kathir and others it is "fa-ahtalat" (poured), which is not right. In Majma' al-Zawa'id it is "fa-atallat", which seems to be a scribal error.]] so they filled what they had with them, then we went to look and did not find it: it had passed beyond the army. [[In the printed edition: "then we returned to look and did not find it, it had passed beyond the army", which differs from what is in the manuscript, and it is correct, agreeing with the references. His words "dhahabna nanzur" (we went to look): the Arabs use "dhahaba" in speech as an auxiliary of the verb; see above vol. 11, p. 128, footnote 1; then p. 250 in the words of Abu Ja'far, and footnote 1; then no. 16206.]] [[The report 17429: "'Amr ibn al-Harith ibn Ya'qub al-Ansari al-Misri": trustworthy and precise, passed many times, the last being nos. 13570, 16732.

"Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal al-Laythi al-Misri": trustworthy, passed many times, the last being no. 13570.

"'Utba ibn Abi 'Utba": he is "'Utba ibn Muslim al-Taymi", trustworthy, biographed in al-Tahdhib, and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/374.

"Nafi' ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im": a trustworthy Successor, one of the leading imams, biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/2/82, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/451.

The narrators of the chain of this report are trustworthy.

This report was cited by al-Haythami in Majma' al-Zawa'id 6: 194, 195, and he said: "It was narrated by al-Bazzar and al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, and the narrators of al-Bazzar are trustworthy." It was cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 3: 286, and he attributed it to Ibn Jarir, Ibn Khuzayma, Ibn Hibban, al-Hakim, who authenticated it, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu'aym, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il.

It is in Abu Nu'aym's Dala'il al-Nubuwwa, p. 190, in the chapter "Mention of what occurred in the expedition of Tabuk", with this chain.

Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir 4: 257, 258, and al-Baghawi in its margin.]]

17430. Ishaq ibn Ziyada al-'Attar told me, saying: Ya'qub ibn Muhammad told us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb told us, saying: 'Amr ibn al-Harith told us, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, from Nafi' ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: It was said to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah have mercy on him: Tell us about the matter of the army of hardship! 'Umar said: We set out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then he mentioned something similar. [[The report 17430: "Ishaq ibn Ziyad al-'Attar", the shaykh of al-Tabari, passed as no. 14146, and we have found no mention of him. It has passed there: "Ishaq ibn Ziyad al-'Attar al-Nasri", without the "ta'" in "Ziyad", in both the printed and manuscript editions. It is not possible to settle this matter until we find a biography that guides us to the correct form.]]

**The interpretation of His words (Exalted is He):** ﴿And [He turned in mercy] to the three who were left behind, until when the earth, for all its vastness, closed in on them, and their own souls closed in on them, and they perceived that there was no refuge from God except in Him. Then He turned to them in mercy so that they might repent. Indeed God is the Ever-Relenting, the Most Merciful﴾ (9:118).

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is His remembrance, He says: ﴿Certainly God turned in mercy to the Prophet and the Emigrants and the Helpers﴾, and ﴿to the three who were left behind﴾. These three, whom God described in this verse with what He described them with, are, as has been said, the others of whom the One whose praise is majestic said: ﴿And there are others held in suspense for God's command, whether He will punish them or turn to them in mercy. God is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾ (9:106). So He turned to them in mercy, Mighty is His remembrance, and graciously favoured them.

The statements of those among the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) who said this have already been mentioned, in a way that makes repeating them here unnecessary. [[See what preceded, pp. 464–467.]]

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the speech, then, is: Certainly God turned in mercy to the three whom God left behind from repentance, deferring them relative to those whom He turned to in mercy among those who stayed behind from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), as:

17431. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from one who heard ʿIkrima regarding His words: ﴿And to the three who were left behind﴾, he said: "They were left behind from repentance."

17432. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada: As for His words ﴿were left behind﴾, they were left behind from repentance.

* *

﴿Until when the earth, for all its vastness, closed in on them﴾: he says, with its spaciousness [[See the explanation of "raḥuba" above, p. 179.]], out of grief and remorse over their staying behind from jihad with the Messenger of God (ﷺ). ﴿And their own souls closed in on them﴾: because of the anguish and distress that befell them on account of that. ﴿And they perceived that there was no refuge﴾: he says, they became certain in their hearts that there was nothing for them to take refuge in from what had descended upon them of God's trial, by their staying behind in opposition to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), which could rescue them from his distress, nor from what they feared of God's punishment, except God. Then He granted them the turning back (inābah) to His obedience and the return to what pleases Him concerning them, so that they would turn to Him, return to His obedience, and cease at His command and prohibition. ﴿Indeed God is the Ever-Relenting, the Most Merciful﴾: he says, indeed God is the Bestower on His servants of the turning back to His obedience, the Granter of success to whomever among them He loves to be granted success in what pleases Him. ﴿The Most Merciful﴾: toward them, [in not] punishing them after repentance, or forsaking whoever among them desires repentance and return, so that He does not turn to him in mercy. [[See the explanation of "al-tawwāb" and "al-raḥīm" in the language indices above, under (thawb) and (raḥim).]]

The people of interpretation said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said that:

17433. Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: Abu Muʿawiya narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, regarding ﴿and to the three who were left behind﴾, he said: Kaʿb ibn Malik, Hilal ibn Umayya, and Murara ibn al-Rabiʿ, all of them from the Helpers. [[Narration 17433: The famous form is "Murara ibn al-Rabiʿ", but it came in this way in the manuscript and the printed edition here. Then in the following reports it is "al-Rabiʿ". A similar difference, and greater, has passed before in the note on nos. 17177, 17178, 17183. Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir (4:264) mentioned this report and said: "Likewise in Muslim: Rabiʿa, in some of his copies, and in some: Murara ibn al-Rabiʿ".]]

17434. Ḥaddathanī ʿUbayd ibn Muḥammad al-Warrāq, saying: Abu Usama narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir with something similar, except that he said: "Murara ibn al-Rabiʿ, or: ibn Rabiʿa" — Abu Usama doubted. [[Narration 17434: ʿUbayd ibn Muḥammad al-Warrāq is ʿUbayd ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Qasim ibn Sulayman ibn Abi Maryam, Abu Muḥammad al-Warrāq al-Nisaburi, who settled in Baghdad and narrated there from Musa ibn Hilal al-ʿAbdi, Abu al-Nadr Hashim ibn al-Qasim, al-Ḥasan ibn Musa al-Ashyab, Yaʿqub ibn Muḥammad al-Zuhri, and Bishr ibn al-Ḥarith. He was trustworthy (thiqa); he died in 255 AH. I have found no biography of him except in Tarikh Baghdad 11:97. Al-Tabari narrated from him in two places in his history (2:202, 250); he narrated from Rawḥ ibn ʿUbada. In the printed edition it read "ʿUbayd ibn al-Warrāq", the editor not reading the manuscript well, since the copyist wrote "ʿUbayd ibn Muḥammad" as one word with interlocked letters. As for "Murara ibn al-Rabiʿ" or "ibn Rabiʿa", see the earlier note.]]

17435. Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Israʾil, from Jabir, from ʿIkrima and ʿAmir: ﴿and to the three who were left behind﴾, he said: They were deferred, in the middle of "Barāʾa" (Surat al-Tawba).

17436. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿the three who were left behind﴾, he said: those who were deferred in the middle of "Barāʾa", His words ﴿and others held in suspense for God's command﴾ (9:106): Hilal ibn Umayya, Murara ibn Rabʿi, and Kaʿb ibn Malik. [[Narration 17436: "Murara ibn Rabʿi" is as it stands in the manuscript, which I have recorded; in the printed edition it is "ibn Rabiʿa", but it came here like what passed in nos. 17177 and 17178, so see the note there.]]

17437. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Ḥudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿and to the three who were left behind﴾, those who were deferred in the middle of "Barāʾa".
