17438. Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from his father, from Layth, from Mujahid: ﴿and to the three who were left behind﴾, he said: All of them were from the Helpers: Hilal ibn Umayya, Murara ibn Rabiʿa, and Kaʿb ibn Malik.

17439. ...... narrated to us, saying: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Warqaʾ, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿and to the three who were left behind﴾, he said: those who were deferred.

17440. ...... narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Yaʿqub, from Jaʿfar, from Saʿid, who said: ﴿the three who were left behind﴾: Kaʿb ibn Malik, who was a poet, Murara ibn al-Rabiʿ, and Hilal ibn Umayya, and all of them were Ansari. [[In the printed edition: "Anṣār" (plural); I have recorded what is in the manuscript, which is sound.]]

17441. ...... narrated to us, saying: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar and al-Maharibi narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Ḍaḥḥak, who said: All of them were from the Helpers: Hilal ibn Umayya, Murara ibn al-Rabiʿ, and Kaʿb ibn Malik.

17442. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: ʿAmr ibn ʿAwn narrated to us, saying: Hashim informed us, from Juwaybir, from al-Ḍaḥḥak regarding His words: ﴿and to the three who were left behind﴾, he said: Hilal ibn Umayya, Kaʿb ibn Malik, and Murara ibn al-Rabiʿ, all of them from the Helpers.

17443. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada regarding His words: ﴿and to the three who were left behind﴾, to His words ﴿then He turned to them in mercy so that they might repent. Indeed God is the Ever-Relenting, the Most Merciful﴾: Kaʿb ibn Malik, Hilal ibn Umayya, and Murara ibn Rabiʿa, who stayed behind in the expedition of Tabuk. It was mentioned to us that Kaʿb ibn Malik tied himself to a pillar and said: "I will not untie it" — or "I will not untie myself" [[In the printed edition: "I will not untie it, or I will not untie myself"; I have recorded what is in the manuscript.]] — "until the Messenger of God (ﷺ) unties me!" The Messenger of God said: "By God, I will not untie him until his Lord unties him, if He wills!" As for the other, he stayed behind by a garden of his which had ripened fruit, [[The "ḥā'iṭ" is a garden of palm trees when it has a wall around it; it is the enclosing wall. It is also called "ḥadīqa", because its wall surrounds it. If it has no wall, it is "ḍāḥiya", because it is exposed to the eye. "Adraka al-thamar" means it reached ripeness.] and he made it a charity in the way of God, and said: "By God, I will not eat it!" As for the other, he went through the deserts following the Messenger of God; the ground lifted him and set him down, and his feet were dripping blood. [["Tashalshalān" or "tatashalshalān", with one of the two tāʾs elided. "Tashalshala al-māʾ wa al-dam" means when drops of water or blood follow one another in scattered flow.]]

17444. Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: ʿUbayd Allah narrated to us, from Israʾil, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik, who said: ﴿the three who were left behind﴾: Hilal ibn Umayya, Kaʿb ibn Malik, and Murara ibn Rabiʿa.

17445. ...... narrated to us, saying: Abu Dawud al-Ḥafari narrated to us, from Salam Abu al-Aḥwas, from Saʿid ibn Masruq, from ʿIkrima: ﴿and to the three who were left behind﴾, he said: Hilal ibn Umayya, Murara, and Kaʿb ibn Malik.

17446. Yaʿqub narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayya narrated to us, saying: Ibn ʿAwn informed us, from ʿUmar ibn Kathir ibn Aflaḥ, who said: Kaʿb ibn Malik said: "I was never in a campaign easier for the mount and the provisions than I was in that campaign!" Kaʿb ibn Malik said: "When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) set out, I said: 'I will equip myself tomorrow and then catch up with him,' so I set about my equipment, but I evening came and I had not finished. When the third day came, I set about my equipment, but I evening came and I had not finished. I said: 'Far-fetched! The people have travelled for three days!' So I stayed behind. When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) came back, the people began to offer excuses to him, so I came and stood before him and said: 'I was never in a campaign easier for the mount and the provisions than I was in this campaign!' The Messenger of God (ﷺ) turned away from me, and he ordered the people not to speak to us, and our women were ordered to move away from us." He said: "One day I scaled a wall, and there was Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah, so I said: 'O Jabir! I adjure you by God, do you know that I ever cheated God and His Messenger at any time?' He was silent with me and kept not speaking to me. [[See "jaʿala", and that it is among the particles of seeking help, as passed above, 11:250, in al-Tabari's speech, with the note there, no. 1, and the note on the report no. 13862.]] Then one day, while I was there, I heard a man on the hill calling: 'Kaʿb! Kaʿb!' until he came near me and said: 'Give Kaʿb good news!'" [[Narration 17446: ʿUmar ibn Kathir ibn Aflaḥ al-Madani, client of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, is trustworthy. Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the followers of the followers, and apparently his meeting with the Companions was not established according to him. Others mentioned that he narrated from Kaʿb ibn Malik, Ibn ʿUmar, and Safina. It appeared before as no. 12223. This report was also narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (4:454, 455), by this same chain, with something similar.]]

17447. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed me, from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) campaigned in the expedition of Tabuk, intending the Romans and the Christian Arabs in Syria. When he reached Tabuk, he stayed there some ten-odd nights, and there came to him the delegation of Adhruh and the delegation of Aylah, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) made peace with them on the jizya. Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) returned from Tabuk without passing beyond it. God sent down: ﴿Certainly God turned in mercy to the Prophet and the Emigrants and the Helpers who followed him in the hour of hardship﴾ (9:117), the verse, and the three who were left behind: a group of them: Kaʿb ibn Malik, who is one of Banu Salima, Murara ibn Rabiʿa, who is one of Banu ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf, and Hilal ibn Umayya, who is from Banu Waqif. They had stayed behind from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in that campaign, about eighty-some men. When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) returned to Medina, those men told him their account and confessed their sins, while the rest lied and swore to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that only excuse had kept them back. The Messenger of God accepted from them and gave them his allegiance, and he entrusted their inner states to God. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) forbade speech with those who had been left behind, and said to them when they recounted their story and confessed their sins: "You have spoken truly; so stand until God decides about you." When God sent down the Qur'an, He turned in mercy to the three, and said of the others: ﴿They will swear by God to you when you return to them, that you may turn away from them﴾ until ﴿God is not pleased with the people who are defiant﴾ (9:95–96).

= Ibn Shihab said: ʿAbd al-Raḥman ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Kaʿb ibn Malik informed me, that ʿAbd Allah ibn Kaʿb ibn Malik — and he was the guide of Kaʿb from among his sons when he went blind — said: I heard Kaʿb ibn Malik narrate his account when he stayed behind from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in the expedition of Tabuk. Kaʿb said: "I never stayed behind from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in any expedition he undertook, except the expedition of Tabuk, though I did stay behind from the battle of Badr, and he did not reproach anyone who stayed behind from it. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) only went out, and the Muslims intended the caravan of Quraysh, until God brought them together with their enemy without prior arrangement. I witnessed with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) the night of ʿAqaba, when we pledged ourselves to Islam, and I would not like to have the battle of Badr in exchange for it, though Badr was more famous among the people than it." [[His words "adhkar" mean more famous in mention.]]

= "My account of when I stayed behind from the Prophet (ﷺ) in the expedition of Tabuk is that I was never stronger nor more well-off than I was when I stayed behind from him in that expedition. By God, I had never before gathered two mounts, but I gathered them in that expedition. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) campaigned in intense heat, faced a long journey and deserts, and faced a numerous enemy. So he made clear to the Muslims their situation, so that they would prepare for the readiness of their campaign, and he informed them of the direction he intended. The Muslims with the Prophet (ﷺ) were numerous, and no register (kitāb ḥāfiẓ) gathered them" — by which he means the register (dīwān) — "Kaʿb said: So no man wanted to absent himself but thought that it would remain hidden, as long as no revelation from God had come down about it. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) campaigned in that expedition when the fruits and the shade were pleasant, and I was inclining toward them. [[" Aṣʿar" means inclining, on the form of the comparative "afʿal", and its root is "al-ṣaʿr" (with two fatḥas), which is a tilt of the face, as if one turns toward something out of longing.]] So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and the Muslims with him prepared, and I began to go out in the mornings so that I might prepare with them, but I would return having accomplished nothing, saying to myself: 'I am able to do that whenever I want.' That kept dragging on with me until the people became earnest, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) set out in the morning, and the Muslims with him" — [[What is between the brackets is missing from the manuscript; I have recorded it from the narration of Muslim in his Sahih. In the printed edition it read: "... so that I might prepare with them, but I did not finish any of my equipment," whereas the manuscript contained something showing the copyist had dropped words from the text: "... so that I might prepare with them and the Muslims with him, and I did not finish any of my equipment."]] and I had finished nothing of my equipment. Then I went out and returned without finishing anything. That kept dragging on [with me], [[The addition between the brackets is from Sahih Muslim.]] until they hurried, and the raid slipped away [[ "Tafāraṭa al-ghazw" means its time passed; similar is "tafarrata", and in the hadith: "He slept through the ʿisha prayer until it had passed", meaning its time had gone.]] and I resolved to set out and catch up with them — would that I had done it! But that was not decreed for me. So whenever I went out among the people after the Prophet (ﷺ) had left, it grieved me that I saw no model for myself except a man defamed for hypocrisy [[ "Uswa" means model and example. "Al-maghmūṣ ʿalayhi" is from their saying "ghamaṣa ʿalayhi qawlan qālahu", meaning he found fault with him for it and slandered him with it. It means: one slandered in his religion, accused of hypocrisy.]] or a man among the weak whom God excused. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) did not mention me until he reached Tabuk, and then he said while he was sitting among the people at Tabuk: 'What has Kaʿb ibn Malik done?' A man from Banu Salima said: 'O Messenger of God, his two garments held him back, and the admiring glance at his own sides!' [[ "The admiring glance at his sides" is a metaphor for self-admiration and vain pride in his fine clothing. "al-ʿAṭfān" are the two sides, so he looks about from the intensity of his conceit.]] [Muʿadh ibn Jabal said: 'What an evil thing you said! By God, O Messenger of God, we know nothing of him except good!'] [[What is between the brackets is from Sahih Muslim. It is evident that the copyist dropped it in his copy.]] The Messenger of God (ﷺ) fell silent. While he was in that state, he saw a man in white clothing, whom the mirage carried up and down, [[ "Al-mubayyaḍ" (with the bāʾ doubled and with kasra) is one who wears white. "Yazūl bihi al-sarāb" means it lifts him and lowers him; it merely stirs his image.]] and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'Be Abu Khaythama!' And behold, it was Abu Khaythama al-Ansari, the one who had given a ṣāʿ of dates in charity, and the hypocrites found fault with him. [[ "Lamazahu" means he reproached him and belittled him.]]"

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 118 (part 2 of 3):

= Ka'b said: When I heard that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had set out on his return from Tabuk, my distress (bathth) weighed heavily on me. [[In the printed edition it reads "hammi" (my concern), which is a misreading of the manuscript. The manuscript reading agrees with Muslim's narration in his Sahih. "Bath" means intense grief. When a person's sorrow becomes severe, he needs to pour out his anguish and sadness to a friend who consoles him, comforts him, or sympathises with him.]] I began to think of lying, and I would say: "By what means can I escape his displeasure tomorrow?" I sought help in this from every man of judgement among my family. When it was said, "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has drawn near, arriving," falsehood departed from me. [[" Azalla qadiman" means he drew near and his arrival was imminent, as if he had cast his shadow over Madinah. His words "zaha 'anni al-batil" mean that it departed, went away, and receded.]] Until I knew that I would never be saved from him by anything at all, so I resolved to tell the truth. [["Ajma'a sidqahu" means I firmly determined upon it with complete resolve. "Ajma'a sidqahu" and "ajma'a 'ala sidqihi" have the same meaning.]] The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrived in the morning. [[In the printed edition it reads "wa-asbaha", and I have restored what is in the manuscript, which agrees with Sahih Muslim.]] Whenever he returned from a journey, he would begin at the mosque and pray two rak'ahs in it, then sit down to meet the people. When he did that, those who had stayed behind came to him, began to make excuses and swear oaths to him. They numbered about eighty men. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) accepted their outward profession, pledged allegiance to them, asked forgiveness for them, and left their inner states to Allah. Then I came. When I greeted him, he smiled the smile of one who is angry, and said: "Come here!" So I walked until I sat before him. He said to me: "What kept you back? Had you not bought your mount?" I said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, if I were sitting before anyone other than you among the people of this world, I would think that I could escape his displeasure with an excuse. I have indeed been given skill in argument. [[" Al-jadal" means fierce contentiousness in dispute, and the ability to meet argument with argument.]] But by Allah, I know that if I tell you a false story today that pleases you, Allah will soon make you angry with me. And if I tell you a true account, which will make you angry with me, I hope in it for the pardon of Allah. [[Here the manuscript reads "afw Allah" (the pardon of Allah), and so does Musnad Ahmad (3: 460). In Sahih Muslim it reads "uqba Allah", meaning that He may give me something good in return and keep me steadfast in it.]] By Allah, I had no excuse! By Allah, I was never stronger or more well-off than when I stayed behind from you!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "As for this, he has spoken the truth. Stand up until Allah decides concerning you!" So I stood up. Men of Banu Salamah rose and followed me, and said: "By Allah, we did not know you to have committed a sin before this! You were incapable of not making an excuse to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as the others who stayed behind did, for the Messenger of Allah's seeking forgiveness for you was sufficient for you!" He said: "By Allah, they did not cease rebuking me until I wanted to return to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and call myself a liar!" He said: "Then I said to them: Has anyone else met with what I have met?" They said: "Yes, two men met with it with you. They said what you said, and they were told what you were told." He said: "I asked: Who are they?" They said: "Murarah ibn al-Rabi' al-'Amiri, [[In the printed edition it reads "Ibn al-Rabi'". I have restored the manuscript reading. See Muslim's narration, which has "Murarah ibn Rabi'ah". Consider also what they said about the variant that Muslim narrated, and that the correct form of "al-'Amiri" is "al-'Umari", referring to Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf.]] and Hilal ibn Umayyah al-Waqifi." He said: "They mentioned to me two righteous men who had fought at Badr, in whom there is an example." [[In the printed edition it reads "li fihima uswah" (there is an example for me in them). That addition is not in the manuscript or in Sahih Muslim. It comes from al-Bukhari's narration, by a different chain.]] He said: "I went on as soon as they mentioned them to me." [[" Mada" means I carried out what I had decided. From their saying "mada fi al-amr mada'" meaning he went through with the matter, and "amdahu" meaning he carried it out.]]

= The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade the Muslims from speaking to us, O you three, [[His words "ayyuha al-thalathah" mean that we were singled out from the rest of those who had stayed behind. This expression is used for specification, and it is used with the one speaking about himself and the one addressed. You say: "As for me, I will do this, O man," meaning himself. See what has preceded, 3: 147, note 1, report no. 2182.]] from among those who had stayed behind. He said: "People avoided us and changed towards us, until the earth seemed strange to me in my own soul; it was no longer the earth I knew. We remained in that state for fifty nights. As for my two companions, they grew humble and sat in their houses weeping. As for me, I was the youngest and strongest of the people, so I would go out, attend the prayer, and walk through the markets, but no one would speak to me. I would come to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), greet him while he was in his gathering after the prayer, and say to myself: 'Did he move his lips to return the greeting or not?' Then I would pray with him and steal glances at him. When I turned to my prayer he would look at me, and when I turned towards him he would turn away from me. When this had lasted long for me, because of the coldness of the Muslims, I walked until I climbed over the wall of the garden of Abu Qatadah, who was my cousin and the dearest of people to me. I greeted him, but by Allah, he did not return my greeting! I said: 'O Abu Qatadah, I adjure you by Allah, do you know that I love Allah and His Messenger?' He was silent. I went back and adjured him again, and he was silent. I went back and adjured him again, and he said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best!' My eyes overflowed, and I turned away until I climbed back over the wall."

= While I was walking in the market of Madinah, there was a Nabataean (nabati) from the Nabataeans of Syria, who had come bringing food to sell in Madinah, saying: "Who will guide me to Ka'b ibn Malik?" So the people began to point to me, until he came to me and handed me a letter from the king of Ghassan. I could write, so I read it, and in it was: "To proceed: we have heard that your companion has treated you harshly, but Allah has not made you a dwelling of humiliation or of loss. So join us, and we will console you."

= He said: When I read it, I said: "This too is one of the trials!" So I threw it into the oven and set it alight with it. [[" Fa-ta'ammamtu", in the manuscript as well, and in al-Bukhari's narration it is "fa-tayammamtu". In Sahih Muslim it is "fa-ta'ayyamtu". Al-Nawawi said: "This is how it is in all the copies in our lands, and it is a dialect form of tayammamtu, meaning: I aimed at." As for al-Qadi 'Iyad, he said in Mashariq al-Anwar (under amm): "Similarly: fa-tayammamtu bi-ha al-tanur, as al-Bukhari narrated it. In Muslim: fa-ta'ammamtu. Both have the same meaning. The hamzah is softened in one narration and made firm in another," meaning: I aimed at it. See also the explanation of "al-umm" and "al-ta'ammum" in Abu Ja'far's commentary above, 5: 558 / 8: 407 / 9: 471. In the printed edition it reads "fa-ta'ammamtu bihi", and I have restored the manuscript reading, which agrees with Muslim and al-Bukhari, except that Muslim has "fa-sajjartuha bi-ha" and al-Bukhari has "fa-sajjartuhu bi-ha". "Bi-ha" is feminine, referring to the meaning of the sahifah (the letter), which is the writing, and then the pronoun returns to "al-kitab" (the writing). "Al-tannur" is the oven in which bread is baked. "Sajjara al-tannur" means he lit it, heated it, and fully fed it with fuel. He meant that he made the oven blaze further by throwing the letter into its fire. This is a striking remark, by which he intended to mock the message of the king of Ghassan sent to him.]] Until forty of the fifty days had passed, and the revelation was delayed. [[" Istalbatha" means he was slow and delayed.]] Then the messenger of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to me and said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commands you to withdraw from your wife." I said: "Shall I divorce her, or what shall I do?" He said: "No, rather withdraw from her and do not approach her." He said: "He also sent to my companion with the same instruction." He said: "I said to my wife: Go back to your family and remain with them until Allah decides this matter." [[In the printed edition it reads "takuni", and I have restored the manuscript reading, which agrees with Sahih Muslim. In al-Bukhari, by a different chain, it reads "fa-takuni".]]

= He said: The wife of Hilal came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, Hilal ibn Umayyah is an old man who has been neglected and has no servant. Would you dislike it if I served him?" He said: "No, but let him not come near you!" She said: "I said: By Allah, he has no inclination towards anything at all! By Allah, he has not ceased weeping since what happened to him until this day!" He said: "Then some of my family said to me: 'If only you had asked permission from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about your wife, since he permitted the wife of Hilal to serve him?' I said: 'I will not ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about her, for I do not know what he would say to me if I asked him about her, and I am a young man!'"

= I remained after that for ten nights, so that the fifty nights were completed for us from the time the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade us from speaking. [[In Sahih Muslim it reads "hina nuhiya 'an kalamina" (when we were forbidden from speaking), with "nuhiya" vocalised in the passive. Abu Ja'far's narration confirms the active vocalisation as well.]] He said: "Then I prayed the dawn prayer on the fiftieth morning on the roof of one of our houses. While I was sitting in the state that Allah has mentioned about us, [[In the printed edition it reads "allati dhakara Allah 'anna", which differs from the manuscript. The manuscript version agrees with Sahih Muslim, and it is the authentic Arabic usage.]] my soul had become constricted and the earth had become narrow for me despite its vastness, I heard the voice of a crier who had climbed onto the mountain of Sal', [[" Awfa 'alayhi" means he climbed it, rose above it, and looked out over the valley from it.]] calling with his loudest voice: 'O Ka'b ibn Malik, rejoice!' He said: 'I fell down in prostration, and I knew that relief had come.' He said: 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) announced Allah's acceptance of our repentance when he prayed the dawn prayer, [[" Adhdhana" means he made it known to the people. In Muslim's narration it reads "fa-adhdhana Rasul Allah (ﷺ) al-nas", and what is here agrees with al-Bukhari's narration by a different chain.]] and the people went to give us good news. Some announcers went toward my two companions, a man rushed to me on a horse, and a man of Aslam ran towards me and climbed the mountain, and the voice was faster than the horse. When the one whose voice I had heard came to give me the good news, I took off my two garments and gave them to him in return for his good news. By Allah, I owned no other garments that day, so I borrowed two garments and put them on, and set off to meet the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).' [[See p. 553, note 1.]]

People met me in groups, group after group, congratulating me on my repentance and saying: "May the acceptance of Allah's repentance of you bring you joy!" [[In the manuscript and the printed edition it reads "li-tahnika", which is also the reading in al-Bukhari's narration by a different chain. In the printed Sahih Muslim it reads "li-tahniu'ka". Al-Qadi 'Iyad mentioned it in Mashariq al-Anwar (under hana') and said: "wa-li-tahnuka tawbatu Allah", which is pronounced with hamzah and with its softening. Sahib Lisan al-'Arab (under hana') mentioned that the Arabs say "li-yahni'uka al-fari s" with the hamzah jussive, and "li-yahniyuka al-fari s" with a quiescent ya', and that "li-yahnuka" is not permissible as the common people say. What he said and attributed to the common people is, in my view, undoubtedly correct.]] Until I entered the mosque, and there was the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sitting in the mosque with people around him. Talhah ibn 'Ubayd Allah rose to me, hurrying until he shook my hand and congratulated me. By Allah, no man among the Muhajirun stood up for me except him.' He said: 'Ka'b never forgot this for Talhah.' [[Al-Hafiz (Ibn Hajar) said in Fath al-Bari: "They said the reason for this is that the Prophet (ﷺ) had established brotherhood between him and Talhah when he established brotherhood between the Muhajirun and the Ansar. What the people of the maghazi (military expeditions) mention is that he was the brother of al-Zubayr, but al-Zubayr was Talhah's brother in the brotherhood of the Muhajirun, so he was his brother's brother."]]

= Ka'b said: When I greeted the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said, while his face shone with joy: "Rejoice in the best day that has passed over you since your mother bore you!" I said: "Is this from you, O Messenger of Allah, or from Allah?" He said: "No, rather from Allah!" Whenever the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was pleased, his face would light up until it looked like a piece of the moon, and we knew that about him.

= He said: When I sat before him, I said: "O Messenger of Allah, part of my repentance is that I should strip myself of all my wealth as charity for Allah and His Messenger." [[" Yankhali'a min malihi" means he goes out from all his wealth and is left bare of it, as a person is stripped when he removes his garment. He meant giving it away in charity.]] The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Keep some of your wealth; it is better for you!" I said: "Then I will keep my share at Khaybar." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, Allah saved me only through truthfulness, and part of my repentance is that I should speak nothing but the truth as long as I live!" He said: "By Allah, I know of no one among the Muslims whom Allah has tested in truthfulness of speech, since I mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), more excellently than He has tested me. By Allah, I have not deliberately told a single lie from the time I said that to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) until this day, and I hope that Allah will preserve me in what remains." He said: "Then Allah revealed: ﴿Allah has certainly turned in forgiveness to the Prophet﴾, until His words: ﴿and to the three who were left behind﴾, to His words: ﴿Fear Allah and be with the truthful﴾ [9:117–119]." [[" Abla" here means he bestowed favour upon him.]]

= Ka'b said: By Allah, Allah has never bestowed on me any blessing after guiding me to Islam greater in my soul than my truthfulness to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that I did not lie to him, for then I would have perished as those who lied to him perished. For Allah said of those who lied, when the revelation was sent down, the worst thing He said to anyone: ﴿They will swear to you by Allah when you return to them, that you may turn away from them. So turn away from them. Indeed, they are impure, and their refuge is Hell, as recompense for what they used to earn.﴾ up to His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not approve of the defiantly disobedient people﴾ [9:95–96]. [[" Ann la" here, the "la" is redundant, as in His saying: (What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you?) [Surah al-A'raf 7:12]. See what has preceded in the tafsir of verse 12: 323–325.]]

= Ka'b said: We, the three of us, were left behind from the matter of those whose repentance the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) accepted when they swore to him; he pledged allegiance to them and asked forgiveness for them, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) deferred our matter until Allah decided concerning it. Therefore Allah said: ﴿and to the three who were left behind﴾, and what Allah mentioned is not that we were left behind from the expedition. [[In Sahih Muslim it reads "mimma khullifna, takhallafna 'an al-ghazw" (of what we were left behind from, we stayed behind from the expedition), and what is here and in the manuscript agrees with al-Bukhari's narration by a different chain.]] It is rather His leaving us behind, and His deferring our matter in regard to those who swore to him and made excuses to him, and he accepted from them. [[In the printed edition the sentence ends with "fa-qabila minhum" in the plural, which differs from the manuscript. What I have indicated agrees with Sahih Muslim and al-Bukhari.]]

[[The report: 17447. The hadith of Ka'b ibn Malik, which Abu Ja'far will narrate from several chains that I will show later. As for this narration, by way of Ibn Wahb, from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab, it is the chain of Muslim in his Sahih (17: 87, 98). See the commentary on the following reports. See also the two earlier reports, nos. 16147 and 17091, and the commentary on them.]]

17448 – Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: al-Layth narrated to me, from 'Aqil, from Ibn Shihab, who said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik informed me that 'Abd Allah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik, who was Ka'b's guide from among his sons when he became blind, said: I heard Ka'b ibn Malik narrate his account of when he stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the expedition of Tabuk, and he mentioned something similar. [[The report: 17448. Al-Bukhari narrated it in his Sahih by this chain (Fath 8: 86–93), and Ahmad in his Musnad (3: 459, 460), the hadith in full.]]

17449 – Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka'b, from his father, who said: "I never stayed behind from the Prophet (ﷺ) in any campaign he undertook except Badr, and the Prophet (ﷺ) did not rebuke anyone who stayed behind from Badr," then he mentioned something similar. [[The report: 17449. From this chain, the chain of Ma'mar, Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad (6: 387–390). See also what Ahmad narrated in his Musnad (3: 456), by way of Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim, from the son of al-Zuhri's brother, Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah, from his paternal uncle Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Zuhri, the hadith in full; and Sahih Muslim (17: 98–100).]]

17450. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik al-Ansari, then al-Salami, from his father, that his father, Abd Allah ibn Ka'b, who was the guide of his father Ka'b when Ka'b's sight was afflicted, said: I heard my father, Ka'b ibn Malik, relate his account of how he stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the expedition to Tabuk, and the account of his two companions. He said: I did not stay behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on any expedition he undertook, except that I had stayed behind from him on the expedition of Badr. Then he mentioned something similar.

[[Athar (report): 17450. Sirah Ibn Hisham 4: 175–181, the hadith in its full length.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 119:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and be with the truthful.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to the believers, informing them of the way to salvation from His punishment and deliverance from His painful torment: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, in Allah and His Messenger, ﴿fear Allah﴾, be mindful of Him by performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions, ﴿and be with the truthful﴾, in the Hereafter, [that is,] in Paradise. The meaning is: be with those who were truthful to Allah in faith in Him, whose deeds confirmed their words, and who were not among the hypocrites in it, whose deeds contradict their speech.

The true meaning of the statement is: be with the truthful in the Hereafter by fearing Allah in this world, as He, may His majesty be praised, said: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger – those are with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor of the prophets, the steadfast in truth, the martyrs, and the righteous﴾ [Surah an-Nisa: 69].

* *

We said that this is the meaning of the statement because the presence of a hypocrite with the believers does not benefit him, in whatever manner he is with them, unless he acts as they act. And if he acts as they act, he is one of them. And if he is one of them, the sense of the statement would be: ﴿Fear Allah and be with the truthful﴾, [Note: in the printed edition: "there is no sense in the statement that it be said", differing from the manuscript; what is in the manuscript is what I have recorded, and it is sound and correct. What he brought from his own opinion corrupts the statement.] And to direct the statement toward the meaning we have indicated, those among the exegetes who interpreted it said: its meaning is: be with Abu Bakr and Umar, or: with the Prophet ﷺ and the Emigrants, may Allah have mercy on them.

* *

Mention of those who said this or other than it in its interpretation:

17451. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Nafi', regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿Fear Allah and be with the truthful﴾, he said: with the Prophet ﷺ and his companions.

17452. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Hubayyah Abu Yazid narrated to us, from Ya'qub al-Qummi, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Nafi', who said: It was said to the three who were left behind: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and be with the truthful﴾, [meaning] Muhammad and his companions.

17453. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq ibn Isma'il narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman al-Muharibi, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding His saying: ﴿and be with the truthful﴾, he said: with Abu Bakr and Umar and their companions, may Allah have mercy on them.

17454. ...... He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Bishr al-Kahili narrated to us, saying: Khalaf ibn Khalifah narrated to us, from Abu Hashim al-Rummani, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿Fear Allah and be with the truthful﴾, he said: with Abu Bakr and Umar, may Allah have mercy on both of them. [Note on the report 17454: Abu Hashim al-Rummani is trustworthy, and the group (of compilers) narrated from him. His name is disputed; it passed under no. 10818.]

17455. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His saying: ﴿Fear Allah and be with the truthful﴾, he said: with the truthful Emigrants.

* *

It is mentioned that Ibn Mas'ud used to recite it: ﴿وَكُونُوا مِن الصَّادِقينَ﴾ [and be of the truthful], and interpreted it as a prohibition from Allah against lying.

Mention of the narration from him to that effect:

17456. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Adam al-Asqalani narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Amr ibn Murrah, who said: I heard Abu Ubaydah ibn Abdullah ibn Mas'ud say: Ibn Mas'ud said: Lying is not permissible in either earnest or jest. Recite, if you wish: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and be of the truthful﴾. He said: And thus is the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: ﴿min al-Sadiqin﴾. So do you see any concession regarding lying?

17457. ...... He said: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Shu'bah, from Amr ibn Murrah, who said: I heard Abu Ubaydah, from Abdullah, similarly.

17458. ...... He said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Amr ibn Murrah, who said: I heard Abu Ubaydah narrate from Abdullah, who said: Lying is not fitting in either earnest or jest. Recite, if you wish: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and be of the truthful﴾ = and it is thus in the recitation of Abdullah = So do you see any concession regarding lying?

17459. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Abdullah, who said: Lying is not fitting in jest or earnest. Then Abdullah recited: ﴿Fear Allah and be with﴾ – I do not know whether he said ﴿min al-Sadiqin﴾ or ﴿ma'a al-Sadiqin﴾ – and it is in my copy: ﴿with the truthful﴾.

17460. ...... He said: My father narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, from Abu Ma'mar, from Abdullah, the like of it.

17461. ...... He said: My father narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu Ubaydah, from Abdullah, the like of it.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The sound interpretation in this matter is the interpretation we mentioned from Nafi' and al-Dahhak. This is because the orthography of all the codices agrees on: ﴿and be with the truthful﴾, and it is the recitation which I do not permit anyone to recite contrary to.

* *

The interpretation of Abdullah, may Allah have mercy on him, according to his recitation, is a sound interpretation, except that the recitation is contrary to it.

Commentary on the words of God: ﴿It was not [proper] for the people of Medina and those of the Bedouins around them to remain behind from the Messenger of God, nor to prefer their own selves over his self. That is because they will not be afflicted by thirst, nor fatigue, nor hunger in the way of God, nor will they tread on a place that enrages the disbelievers, nor will they gain anything from an enemy but that a righteous deed is written for them thereby. Indeed God does not waste the reward of the good-doers.﴾ (9:120)

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: It was not [proper] for the people of Medina, the city of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), = ﴿and those of the Bedouins around them﴾, the dwellers of the desert, who remained behind from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) during the expedition of Tabuk, and who were among the people of faith in him, to remain behind with their families and without a home of their own, [[In the printed edition: "wa la darihim" (and not their home); I have adopted what is in the manuscript.]] nor to prefer their own selves over his self, in accompanying him on his journey, in fighting alongside him, and in aiding him in what he undergoes in that expedition. [[See the explanation of "raghiba" (prefer/desire) above, 3:89.]] He says: it was not permissible for them to do this = ﴿because﴾, due to the fact that, and by reason that, = ﴿they will not be afflicted﴾, on their journey when they are with him, = ﴿by thirst﴾, which is the thirst of [being without water], = ﴿nor fatigue﴾, meaning: nor exhaustion, = ﴿nor hunger in the way of God﴾, meaning: nor hunger in establishing the religion of God and supporting it, and in demolishing the signposts of disbelief. [[See the explanation of "makhmasa" (hunger) below, p. 564, note 1, and the explanation of "sabil Allah" (the way of God) in the vocabulary index under (s-b-l).]] = ﴿nor will they tread on a place﴾, meaning: a land; he says: they will not tread upon land = ﴿that enrages the disbelievers﴾, by their treading upon it. [[See the explanation of "al-ghayz" (rage) above, 7:215 and 11:114, 16:..]] = ﴿nor will they gain anything from an enemy﴾, he says: nor will they obtain anything from the enemy of God and their enemy, in their wealth, their persons, or their children, = ﴿but that a righteous deed is written for them thereby﴾, God records for them, for all of that, the reward of a righteous deed with which He is pleased. [[See the explanation of "kataba" (wrote/prescribed) in the vocabulary index under (k-t-b).]] = ﴿Indeed God does not waste the reward of the good-doers﴾, he says: God does not leave any good-doer among His creation who has done good in his deed, obeyed Him in what He commanded, and refrained from what He forbade, without rewarding him for his good and recompensing him for his righteous deed. [[See the explanation of "al-muhsin" (the good-doer) in the vocabulary index under (h-s-n).]] Thus He wrote for those who did this from among the people of Medina and the Bedouins around them what is mentioned in this verse, the reward for everything they did, and He did not waste the reward of that deed.

* *

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have differed concerning the ruling (hukm) of this verse.

* *

Some of them said: it is muhkam (definitive, not abrogated), and that this applied only to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) specifically: it was not permissible for anyone to remain behind when he went out to fight, staying back from him, except one who had an excuse. As for other than him from among the imams and rulers, it is permissible for whichever believers wish to remain behind them, when the Muslims have no dire need for them.

Those who said this:

17462- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿It was not [proper] for the people of Medina and those of the Bedouins around them to remain behind from the Messenger of God, nor to prefer their own selves over his self﴾: this is when the Prophet of God goes out to fight in person; then it is not permissible for anyone to remain behind. It has been mentioned to us that the Prophet of God (ﷺ) said: Were it not that I would burden my community, I would not remain behind a expedition (sariyya) that fights in the way of God; but I do not find room (to carry them), so I set out with them, and it burdens me, or: I dislike, to leave them behind after me.

17463- Ali ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Awza'i, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, al-Fazari, al-Sab'i, Ibn Jabir, and Sa'id ibn Abd al-Aziz say concerning this verse: ﴿It was not [proper] for the people of Medina and those of the Bedouins around them to remain behind from the Messenger of God﴾, to the end of the verse: it applies to the first and last of this community of those who strive in the way of God.

* *

Others said: this verse was revealed when the Muslims were few; when they increased, God abrogated it and permitted remaining behind for whoever wished, saying: ﴿It is not for the believers to go forth all together﴾ (9:122).

Those who said this:

17464- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His words: ﴿It was not [proper] for the people of Medina and those of the Bedouins around them to remain behind from the Messenger of God﴾, and he recited until reaching: ﴿that God may reward them with the best of what they used to do﴾, and said: this was when Islam was small; then when Islam grew numerous, He said: ﴿It is not for the believers to go forth all together; so why should not a party from every division of them go forth﴾, to the end of the verse.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view in this matter, in my opinion, is that God meant by it those whom He described with His words: ﴿And those who made excuses among the Bedouins came seeking permission﴾ (9:90). Then He, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿It was not [proper] for the people of Medina﴾, who remained behind from the Messenger of God, nor for those of the Bedouins around them who sat back from striving with him, to remain behind from him or to prefer their own selves over his self. That is because the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had called upon, in that expedition, everyone able to rise and set out with him, except those he permitted or commanded to stay behind after him. So it was not permissible for one who was able to set out to remain behind. Then He, may His praise be exalted, enumerated those among them who remained behind, showing the hypocrisy of those whose remaining behind was hypocrisy, excusing those whose remaining behind was for an excuse, and forgiving those whose remaining behind was negligence without doubt or uncertainty about the command of God, since he repented from the error of what he had done. As for remaining behind from him in a time of his independence (from need), it was not forbidden, provided it was not out of his (ﷺ) displeasure with it. Likewise is the ruling for Muslims today regarding their imam: it is not obligatory upon all of them to rise with him, except in a time of his need for them, since it is necessary for Islam and its people to have their presence, gathering, and his calling them forth; then obedience to him becomes binding upon them at that time.

And if this is the meaning of the verse, then neither of the two verses we have mentioned abrogates the other, since neither of them negates the ruling of the other in all its aspects, and no report has come establishing that one of them abrogates the other.

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "al-makhmasa" (hunger), that it is famine, with its evidences, and we have mentioned the narration from those who said so in another place, so that suffices from repeating it here. [[See the explanation of "makhmasa" above, 9:532–534.]]

* *

As for "al-nayl" (gaining), it is a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker: "nalani yanilani" (he obtained for me), and "niltu al-shay'a fa-huwa manil" (I obtained the thing, so it is obtainable). This is when you attain it with your hand, and it is not from "al-tanawul" (taking hold of). That is because "al-tanawul" derives from "al-nawal" (gift), from which one says: "nultu lahu, anwal lahu" (I gave him a gift), meaning a grant.

Some of the scholars of the Arabic language said: "al-nayl" is a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker: "nalani bi-khayr yanulni nawalan" (he gave me good), and "analani khayran, inalatan" (he granted me good). He said: it is as if "al-nayl" comes from the waw, and the waw was changed into a ya' for its lightness and the heaviness of the waw. This is not well known in the speech of the Arabs; rather it is the habit of the Arabs to keep the waw in words of waw-origin when it is quiescent and what precedes it is fatha, such as their saying "al-qawl," "al-awl," and "al-hawl." And if what he said were permissible, then "al-qayl" would be permissible. [[See the explanation of "al-nayl" above, 3:20 / 6:587 / 12:408, 469 / 13:133. "Al-nayl" was not explained above with this kind of exposition in this place. This is a useful remark for extracting the method by which Abu Ja'far composed this tafsir.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verses 121–122 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And they spend no expenditure, small or great, nor do they cross a valley, but it is recorded for them, that Allah may reward them with the best of what they used to do﴾ (9:121).

Abu Ja'far said: May He be exalted in remembrance, says: "That is because they will not be afflicted with thirst," and all that is mentioned: ﴿nor do they suffer any harm from an enemy⁠—﴾ ﴿and they spend no expenditure, small or great,﴾ in the way of Allah [[Neither "nor great" was in the manuscript nor the printed edition; I added it because the sense of the speech requires it.]] ﴿nor do they cross a valley,﴾ with the Messenger of Allah on his campaign, ﴿but it is recorded for them,⁠﴾ meaning: the reward of their deed is recorded for them, as a recompense for them for it, as the best recompense for their best deeds which they used to do while they were staying at their homes, as:

17465. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And they spend no expenditure, small or great﴾, the verse, he said: No people's distance from their families in the way of Allah increases except that their nearness to Allah increases.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿It was not for the believers to go forth all together. So why should not a company from every division of them go forth, that they may gain understanding in the religion and warn their people when they return to them, that they may beware?⁠﴾ (9:122).

Abu Ja'far said: May He be exalted in remembrance, says: The believers were not to go forth all together. [[See the explanation of "nafr" (going forth) previously: 8:536 / 14:254, 399.]]

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "kaffah" (all together) with its evidence and the sayings of the people of interpretation concerning it, which suffices so that it need not be repeated in this place. [[See the explanation of "kaffah" previously: 4:257, 258 / 14:242.]]

* *

Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning Allah intended by this verse, and what is the "nafr" (going forth) which He disliked for all the believers?

Some of them said: It was a group of people who were in the desert, whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had sent to teach the people Islam. When His saying was revealed: ﴿It was not for the people of Medina and those around them of the Bedouins to remain behind from the Messenger of Allah⁠﴾, they withdrew from the desert to the Prophet ﷺ, fearing that they would be among those who remained behind and among those intended by the verse. So Allah revealed their excuse in that with His saying: ﴿And it was not for the believers to go forth all together﴾, and He disliked the departure of all of them from the desert to Medina.

Mention of those who said that:

17466. Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And it was not for the believers to go forth all together. So why should not a company from every division of them go forth⁠﴾: He said: People from the companions of Muhammad ﷺ went out into the deserts, and they obtained from the people kindness and fertility from which they benefited, and they called those whom they found among the people to guidance. Then the people said to them: "We see you have only abandoned your companions and come to us!" So they felt distress in themselves because of that, and they all came back from the desert until they entered upon the Prophet ﷺ. Then Allah said: ﴿So why should not a company from every division of them go forth⁠﴾, seeking good ⁠= ﴿that they may gain understanding⁠﴾, and that they may hear what is among the people and what Allah has revealed after them ⁠= ﴿and warn their people⁠﴾, all the people ⁠= ﴿when they return to them, that they may beware.﴾

17467. Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it, except that he said in his narration: Then Allah said: ﴿So why should not a company from every division of them go forth⁠﴾, some went forth and some sat, seeking good.

17468. ...... He said: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abdullah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similar to his narration from Abu Hudhayfah.

17469. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similar to the narration of al-Muthanna from Abu Hudhayfah, except that he said in his narration: "We see you have only abandoned your companion!" and he said: ﴿that they may gain understanding⁠﴾, that they may hear what is among the people.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: It was not for the believers to go forth all together against their enemy and leave their Prophet ﷺ alone, as:

17470. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿And it was not for the believers to go forth all together⁠﴾: He said: that they all go away ⁠= ﴿So why should not a company from every clan and tribe go forth, and a company remain behind⁠﴾ ⁠= ﴿that they may gain understanding in the religion⁠﴾, that those who remained behind with the Prophet ﷺ may gain understanding in the religion ⁠= and that those who remained behind may warn those who went forth when they return to them, that they may beware.

* *

Mention of those who said that:

17471. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And it was not for the believers to go forth all together⁠﴾, he says: It was not for the believers to go forth all together and leave the Prophet ﷺ alone ⁠= ﴿So why should not a company from every division of them go forth⁠﴾, meaning a band, meaning the detachments (sariyyah), and they should not go out on detachments except with his permission. So when the detachments returned, and Qur'an had been revealed after them, which those who stayed with the Prophet ﷺ had learned, they said: "Indeed Allah has revealed to your Prophet after you a Qur'an, and we have learned it." So the detachments remained, learning what Allah had revealed to their Prophet after them, [and He sent other detachments, and that is His saying: ﴿that they may gain understanding in the religion⁠﴾, He says they learn what Allah revealed to His Prophet] [[What is between the brackets is not in the manuscript; the printer of the printed edition added it from al-Durr al-Manthur 3:292, as I think likely.]] and they teach the detachments when they return to them, that they may beware. [[In the printed edition it was: "and they teach it," in al-Durr: "and they teach him," and in the manuscript: "and they teach," coordinated with His saying: "that they may gain understanding."]]

17472. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And it was not for the believers to go forth all together⁠﴾ to His saying: ﴿that they may beware⁠﴾, he said: This is when the Prophet of Allah sends the armies, he commands them not to harm his Prophet, and a group remains with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gaining understanding in the religion, and a group sets out to call their people and warn them of the events of Allah concerning those who passed before them.

17473. Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿And it was not for the believers to go forth all together⁠﴾, the verse: When the Prophet of Allah went on a campaign himself, it was not lawful for any of the Muslims to remain behind him, except those with an excuse. And when he stayed behind, the detachments set out, and it was not lawful for them to depart except with his permission. So a man, when he set out on a detachment and a Qur'an was revealed after him, the Prophet of Allah recited it to his companions who remained with him. When the detachment returned, those who stayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: "Indeed Allah has revealed to His Prophet a Qur'an after you," and they recited it to them and gave them understanding in the religion. This is His saying: ﴿And it was not for the believers to go forth all together⁠﴾, meaning: when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ remains. ⁠= ﴿So why should not a company from every division of them go forth⁠﴾, meaning by that: it is not fitting for the Muslims to go forth all together while the Prophet of Allah remains seated; rather, when the Prophet of Allah remains seated, the detachments set out, and the majority of the people remain seated with him.

* *

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: those who went forth are not believers; had they been believers, not all of them would have gone forth, but they are hypocrites. And had they been truthful that they were believers, a part would have gone forth to gain understanding in the religion and warn their people when they returned to them.

Mention of those who said that:

17474. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And it was not for the believers to go forth all together⁠﴾: it is not in reference to jihad. Rather, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ invoked against Mudar with years of drought, their lands became barren, and a tribe from them would come with all of its members until they alighted in Medina out of hardship, and they would claim Islam while they were liars. They distressed the companions of the Prophet ﷺ and burdened them, and Allah revealed informing the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that they were not believers. So the Messenger of Allah returned them to their tribes and warned their people not to do what they did. That is His saying: ﴿and that they may warn their people when they return to them, that they may beware.⁠﴾

* *

A third opinion has also been related from Ibn 'Abbas on this matter, which is that:

17475. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And it was not for the believers to go forth all together⁠﴾, to His saying: ﴿that they may beware⁠﴾: He said: A band would set out from every tribe of the Arabs, and they would come to the Prophet ﷺ and ask him about what they wanted of their religion, and they would gain understanding in their religion, and they would say to the Prophet of Allah: "What do you command us to do, and tell us what we should say to our tribes when we set out to them?" He said: The Prophet of Allah would command them to obey Allah and obey His Messenger, and send them to their people with prayer and zakat. When they came to their people, they would call out: "Whoever has embraced Islam is one of us," and they would warn them, to the point that a man would acquaint his father and mother [with Islam]. [[This sentence is as it appears in both the manuscript and the printed edition; it is of strange construction, and I fear something may have dropped from it.]] And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would inform them, and they would warn their people. When they returned to them, they would invite them to Islam, warn them of the Fire, and give them the good news of Paradise.

* *

Others said: This is only a rebuke from Allah to hypocrites who disparaged the Bedouin Muslims and others regarding their staying behind contrary to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while they were among those whom Allah had excused for remaining behind. [[In the printed edition: "among the Bedouin Muslims and they blamed them," and the correct reading is what is in the manuscript.]]

Mention of those who said that:

17476. Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Sulayman al-Ahwal, from 'Ikrimah, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿It was not for the people of Medina and those around them of the Bedouins to remain behind from the Messenger of Allah⁠﴾, to: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not allow the reward of the doers of good to be lost⁠﴾, some hypocrites said: "Those who stayed behind are destroyed!" So ﴿And it was not for the believers to go forth all together⁠﴾ was revealed, to: ﴿that they may beware⁠﴾, and ﴿Those who argue about Allah after He has been responded to, their argument is void⁠﴾ was revealed, the verse [Surah al-Shura: 16].

17477. Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to us, from Ibn 'Uyaynah, who said: Sulayman al-Ahwal narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, who said: I heard him say: When ﴿If you do not go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment⁠﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 39] was revealed, and ﴿It was not for the people of Medina and those around them of the Bedouins⁠﴾, to His saying: ﴿that Allah may reward them with the best of what they used to do⁠﴾, the hypocrites said: "The companions of the desert who stayed behind from Muhammad and did not go forth with him are destroyed!" Some of the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had gone out to the desert, to their people, to give them understanding, so Allah revealed: ﴿And it was not for the believers to go forth all together. So why should not a company from every division of them go forth⁠﴾, to His saying: ﴿that they may beware⁠﴾, and ﴿Those who argue about Allah after He has been responded to⁠﴾, the verse.

* *

Those who said that "it refers to the prohibition of all going forth together in a detachment, leaving the Prophet ﷺ alone" differed regarding the persons referred to in His saying: ﴿that they may gain understanding in the religion and warn their people when they return to them⁠﴾.

Some of them said: It refers to the group that remained behind with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. They said: The meaning of the speech is: Why should not a company from every division go forth for jihad, so that those who remained behind may gain understanding in the religion, and warn their people who went forth in the detachment when they return to them from their campaign? That is the saying of Qatadah, and we have already mentioned the report from him through the narration of Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah. [[See what preceded, number 17472.]] And:

17478. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿So why should not a company from every division of them go forth, that they may gain understanding in the religion⁠﴾, the verse, he said: That those who sat with the Prophet of Allah may gain understanding ⁠= ﴿and warn their people when they return to them⁠﴾, meaning: that they may warn those who went forth when they return to them.

17479. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan and Qatadah: ﴿It was not for the believers to go forth all together⁠﴾, both said: "all together," and leave the Prophet ﷺ.

* *

Others among them said: Rather, the meaning of that is: that the group that went forth should gain understanding, not the group that remained behind, and that the one who went forth should warn the one who remained behind.

Mention of those who said that:

17480. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan: ﴿So why should not a company from every division of them go forth, that they may gain understanding in the religion⁠﴾, he said: That those who went out may gain understanding through what Allah shows them of victory and support over the polytheists, and that they may warn their people when they return to them.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the sayings regarding the interpretation of this, in terms of truth, is that it be said: Its interpretation is: It was not for the believers to go forth all together and leave the Messenger of Allah ﷺ alone. Allah, by this verse, forbade the believers in Him from going out on a raid, jihad, or other matters, leaving the Messenger of Allah ﷺ alone. Rather, it is incumbent upon them, when the Messenger of Allah dispatches a detachment, that a group from every tribe of the Arab tribes go forth with it, and this is the "firqah" (division) [[See the explanation of "al-fariq" and "al-firqah" previously: p. 539, note 1, and the references there.]] = ﴿ṭā'ifah⁠﴾ (a company), and that is from one person up to whatever number is reached, [[See the explanation of "ṭā'ifah" previously: p. 403, note 1, and the references there.]] as Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, said: ﴿So why should not a company from every division of them go forth⁠﴾, meaning: Why not a company from every division of them go forth? [[See the explanation of "law-la" previously: 11:356, note 2, and the references there.]] This is as far as this goes, according to one of the sayings related from Ibn 'Abbas, which is the saying of al-Dahhak and Qatadah.

We only said that this saying is the most correct of the sayings on this matter, because Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, forbade the believers, the people of Medina the city of the Messenger ﷺ and the Bedouins, from remaining behind contrary to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ without an excuse for which they would be excused, when the Messenger of Allah went out on a campaign and jihad against an enemy, in the verse before this, with His saying: ﴿It was not for the people of Medina and those around them of the Bedouins to remain behind from the Messenger of Allah⁠﴾. Then He, may His praise be exalted, followed that with His saying: ﴿And it was not for the believers to go forth all together⁠﴾. So it was known by that, since He had informed them in the preceding verse of what was obligatory upon them regarding the duty of going forth, and what was permitted to them to leave it while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was campaigning and departing from his city for jihad against an enemy, and informed them that it was not fitting for them to remain behind contrary to him except for an excuse, after he had urged some of them to go forth and left some of them behind, that it should follow their being informed of that, that He inform them of what is obligatory upon them when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ remains in his city and sends others away from it, just as the beginning of informing them about what is obligatory when he departs and leaves some behind.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿that they may gain understanding in the religion and warn their people when they return to them⁠﴾, [[See the explanation of "tafaqquh" previously: p. 413, note 2, and the references there.]] the most correct of the sayings regarding it is the saying of him who said: The group that goes forth should gain understanding through what they witness of Allah's victory for the people of His religion and the companions of His Messenger, over the people of His enmity and disbelief in Him, so that whoever has not understood the reality of the knowledge of the matter of Islam and its dominance over the religions may gain understanding through witnessing it; and that they may warn their people, so that they caution them that there may descend upon them from the might of Allah the like of what descended upon those whom they witnessed and saw of the polytheists whom the Muslims overcame ⁠= when they return to them from their campaign ⁠= ﴿that they may beware⁠﴾, [[See the explanation of "al-hadhar" previously: 10:575 / 14:331.]] meaning: perhaps their people, when they warn them of what they witnessed of that, will beware, and believe in Allah and His Messenger, out of fear that there may descend upon them what descended upon those who were informed of their account.

We only said that this is the most correct of the sayings, and it is the saying of al-Hasan al-Basri which we related from him, [[See what preceded, number 17480.]] because "nafr" has been explained earlier: that when it is unrestricted and not joined to anything, the more common usage of the Arabs of it is in jihad and campaigning. [[See what preceded: pp. 251–256.]] Since that is the more prevalent of its meanings, and He, may His majesty be exalted, said: ﴿So why should not a company from every division of them go forth, that they may gain understanding in the religion⁠﴾, it is known that His saying ﴿that they may gain understanding⁠﴾ is only a condition for the going forth and not for anything else, since it follows it and not other speech.

* *

If a speaker says: And what would prevent you from saying that its meaning is: that those who remained behind may gain understanding in the religion?

It was said: "We deny that, because it is impossible. For if the departure of the group that goes forth were the cause of the remaining group gaining understanding, then their remaining behind would have to be the cause of their ignorance and their abandoning of understanding. Yet we know that if they had stayed and not gone forth, their staying would not have been a cause of preventing them from gaining understanding."

* *

Furthermore, He, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿And that they may warn their people when they return to them﴾, joining it by conjunction to His saying: ﴿that they may gain understanding in the religion﴾. There is no doubt that the group that went forth did not go forth except after the warning had already come to them from Allah, and it was out of that warning and fear of the threat that they went forth. So what is the sense of the remaining group warning the group that went forth, when both are equal in knowledge of the warning of Allah to them both? And if it were permissible for one of them to be described as warning the other, the group that went forth would be more deserving of being described by it, because they had witnessed, of the power of Allah and the victory of the believers over the people of disbelief in Him, what the remaining group had not witnessed. But that, if Allah wills, is as we have said: that they warn their own clan and tribe, those who have not believed in Allah, when they return to them, that there may befall them what befell those whom they witnessed, from among their counterparts among the people of polytheism, whom Allah gave the believers victory over.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verses 121–122 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And they spend no expenditure, small or great, nor do they cross a valley, but it is recorded for them, that Allah may reward them with the best of what they used to do﴾ (9:121).

Abu Ja'far said: May He be exalted in remembrance, says: "That is because they will not be afflicted with thirst," and all that is mentioned: ﴿nor do they suffer any harm from an enemy⁠—﴾ ﴿and they spend no expenditure, small or great,﴾ in the way of Allah [[Neither "nor great" was in the manuscript nor the printed edition; I added it because the sense of the speech requires it.]] ﴿nor do they cross a valley,﴾ with the Messenger of Allah on his campaign, ﴿but it is recorded for them,⁠﴾ meaning: the reward of their deed is recorded for them, as a recompense for them for it, as the best recompense for their best deeds which they used to do while they were staying at their homes, as:

17465. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And they spend no expenditure, small or great﴾, the verse, he said: No people's distance from their families in the way of Allah increases except that their nearness to Allah increases.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿It was not for the believers to go forth all together. So why should not a company from every division of them go forth, that they may gain understanding in the religion and warn their people when they return to them, that they may beware?⁠﴾ (9:122).

Abu Ja'far said: May He be exalted in remembrance, says: The believers were not to go forth all together. [[See the explanation of "nafr" (going forth) previously: 8:536 / 14:254, 399.]]

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "kaffah" (all together) with its evidence and the sayings of the people of interpretation concerning it, which suffices so that it need not be repeated in this place. [[See the explanation of "kaffah" previously: 4:257, 258 / 14:242.]]

* *

Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning Allah intended by this verse, and what is the "nafr" (going forth) which He disliked for all the believers?

Some of them said: It was a group of people who were in the desert, whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had sent to teach the people Islam. When His saying was revealed: ﴿It was not for the people of Medina and those around them of the Bedouins to remain behind from the Messenger of Allah⁠﴾, they withdrew from the desert to the Prophet ﷺ, fearing that they would be among those who remained behind and among those intended by the verse. So Allah revealed their excuse in that with His saying: ﴿And it was not for the believers to go forth all together﴾, and He disliked the departure of all of them from the desert to Medina.

Mention of those who said that:

17466. Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And it was not for the believers to go forth all together. So why should not a company from every division of them go forth⁠﴾: He said: People from the companions of Muhammad ﷺ went out into the deserts, and they obtained from the people kindness and fertility from which they benefited, and they called those whom they found among the people to guidance. Then the people said to them: "We see you have only abandoned your companions and come to us!" So they felt distress in themselves because of that, and they all came back from the desert until they entered upon the Prophet ﷺ. Then Allah said: ﴿So why should not a company from every division of them go forth⁠﴾, seeking good ⁠= ﴿that they may gain understanding⁠﴾, and that they may hear what is among the people and what Allah has revealed after them ⁠= ﴿and warn their people⁠﴾, all the people ⁠= ﴿when they return to them, that they may beware.﴾

17467. Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it, except that he said in his narration: Then Allah said: ﴿So why should not a company from every division of them go forth⁠﴾, some went forth and some sat, seeking good.

17468. ...... He said: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abdullah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similar to his narration from Abu Hudhayfah.

17469. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similar to the narration of al-Muthanna from Abu Hudhayfah, except that he said in his narration: "We see you have only abandoned your companion!" and he said: ﴿that they may gain understanding⁠﴾, that they may hear what is among the people.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: It was not for the believers to go forth all together against their enemy and leave their Prophet ﷺ alone, as:

17470. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿And it was not for the believers to go forth all together⁠﴾: He said: that they all go away ⁠= ﴿So why should not a company from every clan and tribe go forth, and a company remain behind⁠﴾ ⁠= ﴿that they may gain understanding in the religion⁠﴾, that those who remained behind with the Prophet ﷺ may gain understanding in the religion ⁠= and that those who remained behind may warn those who went forth when they return to them, that they may beware.

* *

Mention of those who said that:

17471. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And it was not for the believers to go forth all together⁠﴾, he says: It was not for the believers to go forth all together and leave the Prophet ﷺ alone ⁠= ﴿So why should not a company from every division of them go forth⁠﴾, meaning a band, meaning the detachments (sariyyah), and they should not go out on detachments except with his permission. So when the detachments returned, and Qur'an had been revealed after them, which those who stayed with the Prophet ﷺ had learned, they said: "Indeed Allah has revealed to your Prophet after you a Qur'an, and we have learned it." So the detachments remained, learning what Allah had revealed to their Prophet after them, [and He sent other detachments, and that is His saying: ﴿that they may gain understanding in the religion⁠﴾, He says they learn what Allah revealed to His Prophet] [[What is between the brackets is not in the manuscript; the printer of the printed edition added it from al-Durr al-Manthur 3:292, as I think likely.]] and they teach the detachments when they return to them, that they may beware. [[In the printed edition it was: "and they teach it," in al-Durr: "and they teach him," and in the manuscript: "and they teach," coordinated with His saying: "that they may gain understanding."]]

17472. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And it was not for the believers to go forth all together⁠﴾ to His saying: ﴿that they may beware⁠﴾, he said: This is when the Prophet of Allah sends the armies, he commands them not to harm his Prophet, and a group remains with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gaining understanding in the religion, and a group sets out to call their people and warn them of the events of Allah concerning those who passed before them.

17473. Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿And it was not for the believers to go forth all together⁠﴾, the verse: When the Prophet of Allah went on a campaign himself, it was not lawful for any of the Muslims to remain behind him, except those with an excuse.
