So a man, when he set out on a detachment and a Qur'an was revealed after him, the Prophet of Allah recited it to his companions who remained with him. When the detachment returned, those who stayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: "Indeed Allah has revealed to His Prophet a Qur'an after you," and they recited it to them and gave them understanding in the religion. This is His saying: ﴿And it was not for the believers to go forth all together⁠﴾, meaning: when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ remains. ⁠= ﴿So why should not a company from every division of them go forth⁠﴾, meaning by that: it is not fitting for the Muslims to go forth all together while the Prophet of Allah remains seated; rather, when the Prophet of Allah remains seated, the detachments set out, and the majority of the people remain seated with him.

* *

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: those who went forth are not believers; had they been believers, not all of them would have gone forth, but they are hypocrites. And had they been truthful that they were believers, a part would have gone forth to gain understanding in the religion and warn their people when they returned to them.

Mention of those who said that:

17474. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And it was not for the believers to go forth all together⁠﴾: it is not in reference to jihad. Rather, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ invoked against Mudar with years of drought, their lands became barren, and a tribe from them would come with all of its members until they alighted in Medina out of hardship, and they would claim Islam while they were liars. They distressed the companions of the Prophet ﷺ and burdened them, and Allah revealed informing the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that they were not believers. So the Messenger of Allah returned them to their tribes and warned their people not to do what they did. That is His saying: ﴿and that they may warn their people when they return to them, that they may beware.⁠﴾

* *

A third opinion has also been related from Ibn 'Abbas on this matter, which is that:

17475. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And it was not for the believers to go forth all together⁠﴾, to His saying: ﴿that they may beware⁠﴾: He said: A band would set out from every tribe of the Arabs, and they would come to the Prophet ﷺ and ask him about what they wanted of their religion, and they would gain understanding in their religion, and they would say to the Prophet of Allah: "What do you command us to do, and tell us what we should say to our tribes when we set out to them?" He said: The Prophet of Allah would command them to obey Allah and obey His Messenger, and send them to their people with prayer and zakat. When they came to their people, they would call out: "Whoever has embraced Islam is one of us," and they would warn them, to the point that a man would acquaint his father and mother [with Islam]. [[This sentence is as it appears in both the manuscript and the printed edition; it is of strange construction, and I fear something may have dropped from it.]] And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would inform them, and they would warn their people. When they returned to them, they would invite them to Islam, warn them of the Fire, and give them the good news of Paradise.

* *

Others said: This is only a rebuke from Allah to hypocrites who disparaged the Bedouin Muslims and others regarding their staying behind contrary to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while they were among those whom Allah had excused for remaining behind. [[In the printed edition: "among the Bedouin Muslims and they blamed them," and the correct reading is what is in the manuscript.]]

Others among them said: Rather, the meaning of that is: that the group that went forth should gain understanding, not the group that remained behind, and that the one who went forth should warn the one who remained behind.

The Interpretation of His Words: "O you who have believed, fight those of the disbelievers who are adjacent to you, and let them find in you harshness. And know that Allah is with the righteous." (9:123)

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may He be exalted, says to the believers in Him and in His Messenger: "O you who have affirmed Allah and His Messenger, fight those of the disbelievers who are near you, not those who are further away from you." [See the explanation of "wali" in the earlier indices of language, under (w-l-y).] He says to them: begin with fighting those nearest to you in dwelling, rather than the farther and farther away. The ones adjacent to those addressed by this verse at that time were the Byzantines (al-Rum), because they were the inhabitants of al-Sham (Greater Syria) at that time, and al-Sham was closer to Madinah than Iraq was. As for after Allah granted the believers conquest of the lands, the obligation upon the people of each region is to fight the enemies adjacent to them, not the farther of them, so long as the people of another region of the lands of Islam do not need them. If the people of another region need them, it becomes binding upon them to aid and support them, because the Muslims are a single hand against all others.

* *

To confirm that this is so, everyone who has interpreted this verse has taken its meaning to be the obligation upon the people of each region to fight the enemies adjacent to them.

Mention of the narrations to that effect:

17481 - Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Shabib ibn Gharqadah al-Bariqi, from a man of Banu Tamim who said: I asked Ibn 'Umar about fighting the Daylam. He said: "Stick to the Byzantines!"

[Note on the chain: "Shabib ibn Gharqadah al-Bariqi" — the well-known name is "al-Sulami," and he is a reliable Successor (tabi'i); this is how it appears in the manuscript, while the printed edition gives "from Shabib ibn Gharqadah, from 'Urwah al-Bariqi," which is not sound, since "'Urwah al-Bariqi" is 'Urwah ibn Abi al-Ja'd al-Bariqi, a known Companion. The addition of "'Urwah" appears to be an insertion into the chain, as my brother concluded, and this is supported by what occurred in this place from a copyist or editor.]

17482 - Ibn Bashshar, Ahmad ibn Ishaq, and Sufyan ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan: "Fight those of the disbelievers who are adjacent to you" — he said: the Daylam.

17483 - Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from al-Rabi', from al-Hasan: that when he was asked about fighting the Byzantines and the Daylam, he recited this verse: "Fight those of the disbelievers who are adjacent to you."

17484 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub narrated to us, saying: my brother 'Imran narrated to us, saying: I asked Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, and I said: What is your view on fighting the Daylam? He said: "Fight them and garrison against them, for they are among those whom Allah described: 'Fight those of the disbelievers who are adjacent to you.'"

[Note on the chain: Ya'qub ibn 'Abdullah al-Qummi, mentioned many times earlier, the last at no. 16960. He narrates from his two brothers, 'Abd al-Rahman and 'Imran, and I have not found a biography for his brother 'Imran.]

17485 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Rabi', from al-Hasan: that he was asked about al-Sham and the Daylam, and he said: "Fight those of the disbelievers who are adjacent to you" — the Daylam.

17486 - 'Ali ibn Sahl narrated to me, saying: al-Walid narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu 'Amr and Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz say: Every people garrisons what is adjacent to them of their frontier posts and fortresses, and the two of them interpret the words of Allah: "Fight those of the disbelievers who are adjacent to you."

17487 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: "Fight those of the disbelievers who are adjacent to you": the disbelievers adjacent to them were the Arabs, and he fought them until he was finished with them. When he had finished, Allah said: "Fight those who do not believe in Allah nor the Last Day," until His words "and they are humbled" [Surah al-Tawbah: 29]. He said: When he had finished fighting those adjacent to him among the Arabs, He commanded him to strive against the People of the Book. He said: And striving against them is the best striving with Allah.

* *

As for His words: "and let them find in you harshness," its meaning is: let these disbelievers whom you fight find in you — i.e., from you — severity against them [See the explanation of "ghilzah" earlier, vol. 7: 341 / vol. 14: 360]. "And know that Allah is with the righteous" means: be certain, when you fight them, that Allah is with you, and He is your helper against them. If you fear Allah and are mindful of Him by fulfilling His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions, then Allah is the helper and supporter of those who are mindful of Him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 124:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And whenever a surah is revealed, among them are those who say, "Which of you has had his faith increased by this?" As for those who believed, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice﴾ (9:124).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, means: When Allah sends down a surah of the Qur'an upon His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), among these hypocrites whom Allah mentioned in this surah are those who say, "O people, which of you has had his faith increased by this surah?" That is, (has had his) affirmation of Allah and His verses increased. Allah says: ﴿As for those who believed﴾, from among those to whom that was said, ﴿it has increased them﴾, the surah that was revealed, ﴿in faith﴾, ﴿and they rejoice﴾ in what Allah has given them of faith and certainty. [[See the explanation of "istabshara" (rejoice) above, 7:396.]]

* *

If someone says: Does "al-iman" (faith), in the speech of the Arabs, not mean affirmation (taṣdiq) and acknowledgment (iqrar)? [[See the explanation of "al-iman" above in the language indexes, root (a-m-n).]] It is said: Yes!

If it is said: How, then, did the surah increase them in affirmation and acknowledgment?

It is said: It increased them in faith at the time it was revealed, because before the surah was revealed, the obligation upon them to acknowledge it and act upon it specifically had not fallen on them, except within their general faith that everything their Prophet (ﷺ) brought them was from Allah and was true. When Allah sent down the surah, the obligation of acknowledging that it, specifically, was from Allah fell upon them, and the obligation of believing in what it contains of Allah's rulings, limits and obligations became binding upon them. That was the increase that the revelation of the surah brought them, at the time it was revealed, in faith and affirmation of it.

* *

Those who held the same view as we have stated on this were the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil).

Mention of those who said so:

17488 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Whenever a surah is revealed, among them are those who say, "Which of you has had his faith increased by this?"﴾ He said: Whenever a surah was revealed, they believed in it, and Allah increased them in faith and affirmation, and they would rejoice.

17489 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' regarding His saying: ﴿So it increased them in faith﴾, he said: fear (khashya).

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 125:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿But as for those in whose hearts is a disease, it adds to their filth [rijs] to their filth, and they die while they are disbelievers﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿But as for those in whose hearts is a disease﴾, meaning hypocrisy and doubt concerning the religion of God. [[See the explanation of "disease" (marad) above: 1:278–281 / 10:404 / 14:12.]] As for the surah that was sent down, ﴿it adds to their filth to their filth﴾, and that is because they doubted that it was from God, so they did not believe in it nor affirm it. Thus that was an increase in doubt, a new occurrence in the revelation of God, which obligated them to believe in it; rather, they became skeptical about it, and so that was an increase in the foulness of their deeds, added to the foulness and hypocrisy that had preceded in them of its kind. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿so it adds to their filth to their filth﴾. [[See the explanation of "filth" (rijs) above: p. 425, footnote 5, and the references there.]] ﴿And they die﴾, meaning: these hypocrites, that they perished. ﴿While they are disbelievers﴾, meaning: while they are disbelievers in God and His signs.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 126:

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿Do they not see that they are tested once or twice every year? Yet they do not repent, nor do they take heed.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The reciters differed over the recitation of His words: ﴿Awa la yarawn﴾ (Or do they not see).

The majority of the reciters of the metropolitan cities recited it: ﴿Aw la yarawn﴾, with the letter ya', meaning: Or do not those in whose hearts is a sickness of hypocrisy see?

Hamzah recited it: ﴿Aw la tarawn﴾, with the letter ta', meaning: Or do you not see, O believers, that they are tested?

Abu Ja'far said: The correct recitation in our view is the ya', as a rebuke from God to them, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters of the metropolitan cities upon it, and the soundness of its meaning.

* *

The meaning of the statement, then, is: Do not those hypocrites see that God tests them once or twice every year, meaning that He tests them once in some years and twice in others? [[See the explanation of "fitnah" (trial, test) above, p. 286, footnote 3, and the references there.]] ﴿Yet they do not repent﴾, that is: despite the affliction that befalls them from God and the trial that confronts them, they do not turn back from their hypocrisy, nor repent of their disbelief, nor do they take heed by what they see of the proofs of God and witness of His signs, so that they might be admonished by them, but they persist in their hypocrisy?

The scholars of interpretation differed over the meaning of "fitnah" (trial) by which God mentions these hypocrites are tested.

Some of them said: It is God's testing of them with drought and hardship.

Those who said this:

17490. Ibn WakI' related to us: Ibn Numayr related to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Do they not see that they are tested once or twice every year?﴾: He said: With famine and hunger.

17491. Muhammad ibn Amr related to me: Abu 'Asim related to us: Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words ﴿are tested﴾: He said: they are afflicted. ﴿Once or twice every year﴾: He said: With famine and hunger.

17492. al-Muthanna related to me: Abu Hudhayfah related to us: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Do they not see that they are tested once or twice every year?﴾ He said: They are afflicted with punishment once or twice every year.

17493. al-Qasim related to us: al-Husayn related to us: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid regarding His words ﴿are tested once or twice every year﴾: He said: With famine and hunger.

* *

Others said: Rather, its meaning is that they are tested through raids and jihad.

Those who said this:

17494. Bishr related to us: Yazid related to us: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah regarding His words ﴿Do they not see that they are tested once or twice every year?﴾: He said: They are afflicted with fighting in the way of God once or twice every year.

17495. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la related to us: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan, the same.

* *

Others said: Rather, its meaning is that they are tested by what the polytheists spread of falsehoods about the Messenger of God ﷺ and his companions, whereby those in whose hearts is sickness are led astray.

Those who said this:

17496. Ahmad ibn Ishaq related to us: Abu Ahmad related to us: Sharik related to us, from Jabir, from Abu al-Duha, from Hudhayfah regarding ﴿Do they not see that they are tested once or twice every year?﴾: He said: We used to hear a lie or two lies every year, by which a great multitude of people would go astray.

17497. Ibn WakI' related to us: my father related to us, from Sharik, from Jabir, from Abu al-Duha, from Hudhayfah, who said: They had a lie or two lies every year.

* *

The most correct of these views is that God marvels to His believing servants at these hypocrites, and rebukes the hypocrites themselves for their scant reflection and poor attentiveness to God's admonitions with which He admonishes them. It is permissible that those admonitions are the hardships He sends upon them of hunger and famine; it is permissible that they are what He shows them of the victory of His Messenger over the people of disbelief in him, and what He grants him of raising His word above theirs; and it is permissible that they are what becomes apparent to the Muslims of their hypocrisy and the corruption of their inner selves, by their inclining to what they hear of the rumours of the polytheists about the Messenger of God ﷺ and his companions. There is no report that necessitates the soundness of some of these over others, in a manner that must be accepted. No view on this is more correct than submitting to the apparent meaning of God's words: "Do they not see that they are tested once or twice every year, by what should be a deterrent to them, yet they neither refrain nor take heed?"

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 127:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And whenever a surah is sent down, they look at one another, [saying], "Does anyone see you?" Then they slip away. Allah has turned their hearts away, because they are a people who do not understand.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, He says: ﴿And whenever a surah is sent down﴾ from the Qur'an, containing the faults of these hypocrites whose description He, may His praise be exalted, has given in this surah, while they are in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): ﴿they look at one another﴾, so they exchange glances, ﴿[saying], "Does anyone see you?"﴾ — [meaning], if you speak or confide to one another about the faults of the people, which he would report to them. Then they stand up and leave the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), without listening to the recitation of the surah that contains their faults. Then He, may His praise be exalted, began with His words: ﴿Allah has turned their hearts away﴾, saying: Allah has turned the hearts of these hypocrites away from good, from success, and from faith in Allah and His Messenger [[See the explanation of "al-sarf" (turning away) above: 3:194 / 11:286 / 13:112.]] = ﴿because they are a people who do not understand﴾, meaning: Allah has done this abandonment to them and turned their hearts away from goodness, because they are a people who do not understand the admonitions of Allah, out of arrogance and hypocrisy. [[See the explanation of "al-fiqh" (understanding) above, p. 573, note 1, and the references there.]]

* *

The scholars of Arabic differed concerning what calls for the interrogative particle.

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: ﴿They look at one another, "Does anyone see you?"﴾ is as if he said: "Some of them said to others," because their looking in this place was a gesture and something resembling it. [[In the printed edition it reads "wa-tanbihan bihi" (and an alerting by it), and the correct reading is what I have established.]] And Allah knows best.

* *

And some of the grammarians of Kufa said: It is rather: "And whenever a surah is sent down, some of them said to others: Does anyone see you?" Another of them said: this "looking" does not mean "saying," but rather the kind of looking that brings about the interrogative, as the Arabs say: "They looked at one another as to which of them is more knowledgeable" and "They gathered as to which of them is more learned," meaning: they gathered in order to look. This is what brings about the interrogative.

* *

17498 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Abu Hamzah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Do not say, "We have departed from the prayer," for a people departed and Allah turned their hearts away; rather say, "We have finished the prayer."

17499 - ...... He said: my father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Umayr ibn Tamim al-Tha'labi, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Do not say, "We have departed from the prayer," for a people departed and Allah turned their hearts away. [[Report 17499: "Umayr ibn Tamim al-Tha'labi" is thus in the manuscript as well; I have not found a biography for him outside the Jarh wa-Ta'dil (3/1/378), where it reads "Umayr ibn Qumaym al-Tha'labi" with a qaf. The editor noted that in one copy it reads "Umayr ibn Qath'am al-Taghlibi." In al-Thiqat and al-Kuna of al-Dulabi it reads "ibn Tamim." Ibn Abi Hatim said: "Yahya ibn Sa'id and Abu Nu'aym said he is Abu Hilal al-Ta'i, and Waki' said he is Abu Tahallul. He narrated from Ibn Abbas, and from him narrated Abu Ishaq al-Hamdani and Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq; I heard my father say so."]]

17500 - ...... He said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Do not say, "We have departed from the prayer," for a people departed and Allah turned their hearts away; rather say, "We have finished the prayer."

17501 - ...... Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿And whenever a surah is sent down, they look at one another...﴾ to the end of the verse, that he said: They are the hypocrites.

* *

Ibn Zayd used to say concerning this:

17502 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His words: ﴿And whenever a surah is sent down, they look at one another, "Does anyone see you?"﴾, [meaning]: from among those who hear your news, has anyone seen you or has anyone informed him? When something is revealed that reports their speech. He said: They are the hypocrites. He said: and he recited: ﴿And when a surah is sent down, some of them say, "Which of you has had its faith increased by this?"﴾ up to: ﴿They look at one another, "Does anyone see you?"﴾ — Has anyone informed him of this? Was there anyone with you? Did anyone hear your speech and inform him of this?

17503 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Adam narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: Abu Ishaq al-Hamdani narrated to us, from one who narrated to him, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Do not say, "We have departed from the prayer," for Allah rebuked a people, saying: ﴿They departed, so Allah turned their hearts away﴾; rather say, "We have prayed."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 128:

The explanation of His words: ﴿Indeed there has come to you a Messenger from among yourselves; it grieves him that you suffer hardship; he is anxious over you; to the believers he is kind and merciful﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says to the Arabs: ﴿Indeed there has come to you﴾, O people, the Messenger of Allah to you, ﴿from among yourselves﴾, whom you know, not from other than you, so that you could accuse him, concerning yourselves, of insincerity in advising you [[See the explanation of "from among themselves" previously, 7:369.]] ﴿it grieves him that you suffer hardship﴾, that is: it grieves him that you suffer, and that is the onset of hardship upon them, and harm and injury [[See the explanation of "grieves" (ʿazīz) in the previous lexical indices (ʿ-z-z), and the explanation of "ʿanat" (suffering) previously, 4:360 / 7:140-144 / 8:206.]] ﴿he is anxious over you﴾, he says: he is anxious for the guidance of your error, and for your repentance and your return to the truth [[See the explanation of "ḥirṣ" (eagerness) previously, 9:284.]] ﴿to the believers he is kind﴾, that is: gentle [[See the explanation of "raʾūf" previously, 3:171; 5:251 / 14:539.]] ﴿and merciful﴾ [[See the explanation of "raḥīm" previously in the lexical indices (r-ḥ-m).]].

* *

And the people of interpretation have said in accordance with what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

17504 - Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: Ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us, from Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad, from his father, concerning His words: ﴿Indeed there has come to you a Messenger from among yourselves; it grieves him that you suffer hardship﴾, he said: nothing of polytheism touched him in his birth.

17505 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn ʿUyaynah informed us, from Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad, concerning His words: ﴿Indeed there has come to you a Messenger from among yourselves﴾, he said: nothing of the birth of the Jahiliyyah touched him. He said: and the Prophet ﷺ said: "I came forth from a marriage, and I did not come forth from fornication."

17506 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated to us, from Ibn ʿUyaynah, from Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad, from his father, with its like.

17507 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿Indeed there has come to you a Messenger from among yourselves; it grieves him that you suffer hardship﴾, he said: Allah made him from among them, so they do not envy him for what Allah gave him of prophethood and honour. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript it reads "wa-la yahsudunahu" with a waw, but the context requires what has been established.]]

* *

As for His words: ﴿it grieves him that you suffer hardship﴾, the people of interpretation differed concerning its meaning.

Some of them said: its meaning is: that you go astray.

Mention of those who said that:

17508 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Talq ibn Ghannam narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Zuhayr narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His words: ﴿it grieves him that you suffer hardship﴾, he said: that you go astray.

* *

And others said: rather, the meaning of that is: it grieves him that your believer suffers hardship.

Mention of those who said that:

17509 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿it grieves him that you suffer hardship﴾, it grieves him that their believer suffers hardship.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two sayings in this matter is the saying of Ibn ʿAbbas. That is because Allah, through the report about the Prophet of Allah, generalized that it grieves him that his people suffer hardship, and did not restrict it to the people of faith. So the Prophet ﷺ [as the report from Allah described him] was grieved by the suffering of all of them. [[In the manuscript there is a blank between "kamā" and "Allāh bihi," about the length of two words; in the printed edition the sentence is completed as: "kamā waṣafahu Allāh bihi, ʿazīzan ʿalayhi," and the addition in brackets is my own inference, the rest being as in the manuscript.]]

* *

If someone says: How is it permissible to describe him ﷺ as being grieved by the suffering of all of them, when he fights their disbelievers, takes their offspring captive, and strips them of their wealth?

It is said: Their Islam, had they embraced it, would have been dearer to him than their remaining in their disbelief and denial of him, so that they would deserve that from Allah. Allah, exalted is His praise, only described him as grieved by their suffering because it was grievous to him that they should commit what would bring them suffering, namely that they go astray and thereby deserve suffering from Allah through killing and captivity.

* *

As for the "mā" in His words: ﴿mā ʿanittum﴾, it is in the nominative case by His words ﴿ʿazīz ʿalayhi﴾, because the meaning of the statement is what I mentioned: it grieves him that your suffering occurs.

* *

As for His words: ﴿ḥarīṣ ʿalaykum﴾, its meaning is what has been explained, and this is the saying of the people of interpretation.

Mention of those who said that:

17510 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿ḥarīṣ ʿalaykum﴾, eager for their misguided ones that Allah guide them.

17510m - Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿ḥarīṣ ʿalaykum﴾, he said: eager that whoever has not embraced Islam should embrace it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 9, verse 129:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Then if they turn away, say: "God is sufficient for me; there is no god but He. In Him I have put my trust, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne."﴾ (9:129)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: If they turn away, O Muhammad, these people to whom you have brought the truth from your Lord, from your people, turning their backs on you and not accepting what you have brought them of counsel concerning God and what you have called them to of light and guidance (see the explanation of "al-tawalli" in the earlier lexical indices, under w-l-y) ﴿say: "God is sufficient for me"﴾, my Lord suffices me (see the explanation of "hasb" earlier, p. 340, note 1, and the references there) ﴿"there is no god but He"﴾, there is no one worthy of worship besides Him ﴿"In Him I have put my trust"﴾, and in Him I have placed my confidence, upon His help I have relied, and to Him and to His victory I have turned for support, for He is my helper and the one who aids me against whoever opposes me and turns away from me, among you and among others of mankind (see the explanation of "tawakkul" earlier, p. 291, note 1, and the references there) ﴿"and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne"﴾, who owns everything beyond Him, and all kings are His servants and slaves (see the explanation of "al-'arsh" earlier, vol. 12, p. 482).

By describing Himself, may His praise be exalted, as "Lord of the Mighty Throne," He intends to inform that all that is beneath Him are His servants, under His dominion and authority, because "the mighty throne" belongs only to kings. So He described Himself as "Possessor of the Throne" apart from the rest of His creation, and as the Great King apart from others, and that whoever is beneath Him is within His authority and dominion, subject to His judgment and decree.

1751. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words: ﴿Then if they turn away, say: "God is sufficient for me"﴾, meaning the disbelievers who turned away from the Messenger of God (ﷺ). And this [verse] is about the believers.

1752. Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Uyayna narrated to us, from 'Amr, from 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, who said: 'Umar (may God have mercy on him) would not confirm a verse in the Mushaf until two men bore witness to it. A man from the Ansar came with these two verses: ﴿"There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves; grievous to him is what you suffer..."﴾ and 'Umar said: "I will never ask you for evidence for these two, thus was the Messenger of God (ﷺ)!"

1753. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Yunus narrated to us, from Zuhayr, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih al-Hanafi, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Indeed God is Merciful and loves every merciful one; He places His mercy upon every merciful one." They said: "O Messenger of God, we show mercy to ourselves and our wealth." He said: [Abu Salih] said: I think he said: "and our spouses"? He said: "It is not like that, but be as God said: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves; grievous to him is what you suffer, eager for your guidance, toward the believers kind and merciful. Then if they turn away, say: God is sufficient for me; there is no god but He. In Him I have put my trust, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne.﴾" I think he recited this entire verse.

[Note on the report 1753: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Yunus al-Taymi is trustworthy; Zuhayr is Zuhayr ibn Mu'awiya ibn Hudayj al-Ja'fi, trustworthy; Abu Salih al-Hanafi is a trustworthy Successor, and this report is mursal.]

1754. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Yusuf, from Ibn 'Abbas, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The last verse to be revealed of the Qur'an was: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves; grievous to him is what you suffer﴾, to the end of the verse.

1755. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Yusuf ibn Mihran, from Ibn 'Abbas, from Ubayy, who said: The last verse revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ) was: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves﴾, the verse.

[Note on the reports 1754 and 1755: 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an has poor memory; Yusuf ibn Mihran al-Basri is trustworthy. This report was narrated by 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad in his father's Musnad, from another chain, with similar wording. al-Haythami cited it in Majma' al-Zawa'id and said: "Narrated by 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad and al-Tabarani; in its chain is 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, who is trustworthy but has poor memory, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy."]

1756. Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Yusuf ibn Mihran, from Ubayy, who said: The two most recent verses of the Qur'an in regard to God are: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves; grievous to him is what you suffer﴾, to the end of the two verses.

[Note on report 1756: a repetition of the preceding, but it is mursal from Ubayy.]

1757. Abu Kurayb narrated to me, saying: Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Aban ibn Yazid al-'Attar narrated to us, from Qatada, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The two most recent verses of the Qur'an in regard to God are: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves﴾, to the end of the surah.

[Note on report 1757: mursal; Qatada did not narrate from Ubayy ibn Ka'b.]

* *

End of the interpretation of Surat al-Tawba. [After this, the manuscript reads: "And praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. Followed, God willing, by the interpretation of the surah in which Yunus is mentioned."] The fourteenth part of Tafsir al-Tabari is complete.

Followed by the fifteenth part, beginning with:

The interpretation of the surah in which Yunus is mentioned.
